Herk Bloomi was the manager of new accounts at Bank Niro Eleven during the beginning of the Imperial reign. In 18 BBY, he was visited by Clive Flax and Astri Oddo, who were looking for information about Eve Yarrow. Concerned about his client's privacy, Herk was reluctant at first but eventually caved in, giving them Yarrow's account status and her address. He let Flax and Oddo "steal" his cruiser after Imperial stormtroopers arrived.

Bloomi was an extremely nervous man who, nonetheless, believed in his clients' utmost privacy. His lack of spine is evident when he starts sweating profusely (so much so that his collar was drenched) when stormtroopers arrive. His reluctance to help Flax and Oddo stemmed both from his respect of Eve Yarrow's privacy and the thought of the repercussions of what he was doing.

Hiem Bryl was head of operations for Verga Mer Mining Company's operations on Tilnes. He was a gaunt Sullustan with slightly sunken cheeks. He did not speak Basic well, so he tended to speak slowly. He preferred letting underlings deal with outsiders, but was not sure they would do so appropriately, so he met with those who came to the mines with questions.

Bryl was a fan of Sullustan sports, and kept images and trophies of such sporting events in his office. He was an accomplished deep-miner, with a degree from a mining school on Sullust. He was popular with his workers, and was able to motivate them easily.

Hishinu Booj was a male Rodian playwright.

Hishinu Booj's most famous work was "The Trickery of Vosdia Nooma," produced in the year prior to the outbreak of the Clone Wars. Inspiration for the drama was drawn from the Rodian senator Onaconda Farr, who assisted in writing the drama with some additional help from Ruris Plin. The play was directed by Booj himself and premiered at the Equator City First Stage on Coruscant.

enrichments.description:
Hodnar Borrum was a male human who served as an officer in both the Grand Army of the Galactic Republic and its successor, the Imperial Army of the Galactic Empire. Toward the end of the Clone Wars, a three-year-long conflict that concluded with the transition from the Republic to the Empire, Borrum reportedly led the charge against the last stand of the Jedi, personally marshaling clone troopers against a mountain fortress. Borrum became a general in the Imperial Military, and he served so long that he came to be known as "the Old Man" across the Empire.

However, perhaps because of his old age or his disregard for the Force, Borrum was never made a Grand General, an honor that went to Kenner Loring instead. After the Empire suffered a major defeat at Endor, General Borrum was given a seat in the Shadow Council, a secret military advisory council led by Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax. Borrum later commanded the Imperial ground forces during the cataclysmic Battle of Jakku, which ended the Galactic Civil War in the New Republic's favor.

Hodnar Borrum served as an officer in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars. He reportedly took part in the Great Jedi Purge and led clone troopers against Jedi who had holed themselves up in a mountain fortress on either Madar or Morad. Borrum continued serving in the army of the Galactic Empire and eventually rose to the rank of general. Borrum had earned the nickname "the Old Man" among his fellow Imperial Military officers due to his long service to the Republic and the Empire.

Despite his experience and talents as a general, Borrum was not promoted to Grand General. Instead, the position went to Kenner Loring. Some like Grand Admiral Rae Sloane speculated that he had been overlooked due to his age, practicality, and his disdain for the Force, which likely enraged Darth Vader. Borrum was one of the senior Imperial officers to survive the cataclysmic aftermath of the Battle of Endor. Due to his talents and reputation, Borrum was recruited by Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax to his secret Shadow Council, a secret advisory council that governed the remnants of the Empire from behind the scenes. Rax and his figurehead Sloane commanded Imperial forces in the Vulpinus Nebula.

Hondo Bador was an male Sullustan who worked as a starship engineer on Ord Mantell during the Galactic Civil War outfitting smuggler ships. Bador was recommended to Han Solo by Mama as a potential source of information regarding the kidnapping of Leia Organa by the bounty hunter Alfreda Goot. Although Bador had recently outfitted a "free-freighter," his client was a male human hoping to work away from Imperial attention in the Outer Rim, and Bador had no knowledge of Goot.

Bador was destroyed by the Columi brothers, Craitheus and Marvid Qreph as revenge for the shooting of their mother. They did not know if Bador had done the deed, and had several suspects, so chose to destroy them all to be sure. Bador's private property was seized, and his friends and family killed.

Hran Beling was a male Vicon Jedi Initiate studying in the Jedi Order at the Coruscant Jedi Temples academy during the final decades of the Galactic Republic.

A Force-sensitive Vicon, the diminutive Hran Beling received training in the ways of the Force at the Coruscant Jedi Temple by the Jedi Order. Initiate Beling was studying at the Temple in 89 BBY when the Dark Holocron was stolen from the Temple Archives, and Beling conveyed this news to one of his contemporaries at the Temple, Dooku, speculating that there could have been an intruder within the complex. Several days later, Initiate Beling participated in an academy competition which took students out of the Temple and into the Senate District. Competing with Initiate Dooku in a challenge against another team of Jedi trainees to secure a piece of muja fruit from a market, Beling was stunned unconscious by the other team and unable to complete the challenge.

Gespo and Hreeda went to Endregaad and ambushed the rescuers, trying to "finish the job." However, others believe that Heedron and Ormann had not died in the first place and were the ambushers at Endregaad.

Hylei Indrexu Cortess, often called just Indrexu, was the queen of Ranroon circa 25,100 BBY.

She became a legend in the Tion Cluster for her resistance to Xim the Despot's conquests. Her forces fought Xim's janissaries bravely in the fierce Battle of Ranroon but were eventually defeated.

The Ihala Spiral was renamed Indrexu Spiral by Xim in honor of the Queen, as well the Far Indrexu, the region conquered after Indrexu's defeat,

No historical figure in the Tion Cluster, not even Xim himself, was as vivid as Indrexu, and no other was more argued about. Some scholars contended she was a literary invention of later dramatists; others believe she existed, but argued about her role in Xim's empire and her ultimate fate. To some she was a minor figure, a fixture at Xim's court whose name had endured; to others she was the pivot around which the empire turned, her merest glance the spark that lit the fires of the Cronese Wars, Xim's expansion, and everything thereafter.

Ibutho 1 was the first of a group of 6 Delta-class DX-9 stormtrooper transports that were used by the Rneekii Pirates.

A group of 3 Imperial Modified corvettes Hashim and a Shuttle G'nabgib, carrying the chief scientist had fell into a trap by the Rneekii. When Tan Maarek Stele in a TIE Defender was launched to fight of the Pirate strike force consisting of the transports, R-41 Starchasers and a Strike-class medium cruiser Intombe. Ibutho 1 had docked with the G'nabgib captured the scientist and jumped into Hyperspace. Stele managed to destroy all the other transports from Ibutho and drove of the Pirate force.

Ibutho 1 was used to transfer the scientist to the Empire as part of their decision to Ransom the scientist to the highest bidder which was the Empire. However, the Pirates gravely underestimated the Imperials and were trapped by Interdictor Red Claw. The pirates were eliminated and Ibutho 1 was captured to recover the ransom.

Idryssa Barruck was a human female soldier who worked in the fight against the Galactic Empire. When Saw Gerrera took in the eight year-old girl Jyn Erso, Idryssa brought her suitable clothes and taught her about health and hygiene, including menstrual health. She first worked for Gerrera's Partisans, but over the next few years, Idryssa became distanced from Saw's group before leaving it entirely, breaking off and joining a more unified group. Later, fellow Partisan Xosad Hozem joined with Idryssa's new group.

Idryssa frequently disagreed with Saw's extremist tactics, insisting that they had to be better than the enemy and being unwilling to purposefully target civilians. She did, however, provide him with information and ideas for new missions.

Idryssa had very dark skin, and used colored makeup to give it a sparkling effect.

Idryssa was known to carry a pair of machetes strapped to her back.

An Imperial starship, a type of starfighter, was hijacked at Gordon on Aquilae by Luke Skywalker, Annikin Starkiller, Han Solo, Leia, Artwo and Threepio as they escaped from the trap set aboard the Baltarian freighter by Valorum.

It was docked in a secured area, but was accessed through subterfuge and jury rigging. Two bubble-domed turrets allowed crew to fire lazercannons at opposing craft. It was equipped with shields, which covered individual sections of the ship.

It was pursued by hunter destroyers, a type of Imperial ship. After enduring a barrage of torpedoes and laser shots, it became heavily damaged over the planet Yavin, where the crew bailed out into life pods.

"Imperial starship" was the name given to this craft in the rough draft script. It may be a Banta Four. If it had two manned turrets and room for 5-7 crew it was a rather large starfighter.

enrichments.description:
Doctor Insmot Bowen was a human male member of the Obroan Institute for Archaeology, who specialized in the history of the Pre-Republic era.

At some point prior to 1 BBY, Bowen joined the Obroan Institute for Archaeology. In 1 BBY, he met with several Imperials for a debriefing regarding Celestials and their technology. During the meeting, which was made up of Bowen, Admiral Conan Antonio Motti, Dr. Bevel Lemelisk, and General Arhul Kurumenga from the Imperial Department of Military Research, Bowen presented a theory that strange occurrences in the galaxy, including a barrier to the west of the Core Worlds, were remnants of Celestial technology dating back to the Rakatan revolt. Admiral Motti, a staunch non-believer in the supernatural, refused to believe him, and frequently mocked him throughout the debriefing.

Dr. Insmot Bowen was created for the original prologue of The Essential Guide to Warfare. However, the character was cut because Erich Schoeneweiss, the editor at Del Rey, felt that the prologue would not get people involved in the book, and that a firsthand account of a battle would be more appropriate. Jason Fry, one of the authors, begrudgingly complied, replacing Bowen's conversation with an account of the Battle of Andalia by Grand Admiral Osvald Teshik.

The character later appeared in the first part of the 12-part blog series Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut, "The Celestials," on Star Wars Blog. He, alongside the entire segment, was vetted as canon within Star Wars Legends by Leland Chee.

The Inusagian court was a group of notable individuals from the planet Inusagi.

In 6 BBY, the Galactic Empire used the sakoola blossom festival to announce a new planetary leader, Governor Cor Tophervin, a personal friend of the Emperor. However, given Inusagi's relation to Naboo, the anti-Imperial Zabrak Arane Oreida saw the party as an opportunity to send a message to the Empire, and she hired Saw Gerrera to infiltrate the festival. With invitations forged by Jyn Erso, Gerrera, Maia, and a group of Arane's partisans entered the festival in the chieftess's palace. There, they used FC-1 flechette launchers to massacre the guests, including the Inusagi court members.

The native Aqualish began to destroy droids to appease the invaders. In Imthitill, droids were exterminated all over the city using a massive fire but Jedi Knight Dorsk 82 intended to leave the planet with thirty-eight droids. He was then killed when his starship was shot down upon takeoff by security officers. Nevertheless this was ignored by Warmaster Tsavong Lah and an invasion and occupation of their planet ensued.

The Invidious was an Imperial II-class Star Destroyer. At the time of Emperor Palpatine's death at the Battle of Endor, it was part of a task force commanded by High Admiral Treuten Teradoc, and served as part of his fleet when he became a self-proclaimed warlord.

At some point before 9 ABY, the Invidious was captured by ex-Moff Leonia Tavira and became the headquarters of her pirate group, the Invids (which drew their name from the ship).

In 11 ABY, Corran Horn used a powerful mind trick to frighten Tavira into believing that a large New Republic fleet, including the Executor-class Star Dreadnought Lusankya and the Sun Crusher, was arriving in the vicinity, and she fled.

Iri Camas was a male Human Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic. Stationed on Coruscant, General Camas was placed in command of the Special Operations Brigade at the beginning of the Clone Wars; a conflict between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

A Force-sensitive male Human, Iri Camas was raised by the Jedi Order from early childhood, learning the ways of the Force at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. Eventually passing the Trials of Knighthood, Camas was made a Jedi Knight and, after further study and devotion to the Order, became a Jedi Master. Serving the Order throughout the Separatist Crisis, Master Camas dutifully took up the rank of General in the newly formed Grand Army of the Republic when the Confederacy of Independent Systems escalated the Separatist Crisis with the Republic.

Unlike most of his brother and sister Jedi, Camas was placed in an office, serving as Director of Special Forces on Coruscant and was in command of one of the two Special Operations Brigade. Camas' primary concern was the effectiveness of clone troopers, and under his command, the troopers averaged a kill-ratio of 200 Battle Droids per trooper and clone commandos were trained to target droid manufacturing and raw material plants, destroying billions more.

In the days following the fateful first battle on Geonosis, Camas attempted to have the Null-class Advanced Recon Commandos put into stasis, hoping that he could use them only when needed as they were considered too independent and hard to control. However, the commandos resisted stasis and Camas demanded to speak with their trainer, Kal Skirata. By the time Skirata had arrived, the Null commandos had taken control of the Special Ops HQ barracks, and the Coruscant Security Force was called in to quell the standoff. Camas, refusing to allow the destruction of the barracks just to contain six unruly clones, ended the standoff by reversing the suspended animation order and appointed Skirata special adviser status to keep the Nulls in line. Soon after that, due to mass casualties, Master Camas' brigade was merged with that of Master Arligan Zey.

enrichments.description:
Little was known about the organization called ISPCA, up to and including its proper name, since the only time that it was known to be mentioned was during a conversation between the amateur starship captain Lando Calrissian and Mohs, the High Singer of the Toka.

Prior to this conversation, Calrissian, his droid, Vuffi Raa and Mohs landed in the Millennium Falcon at the base of one of the Sharu pyramids on Rafa V and were ambushed by a tribe of Toka who were armed with crossbows. After the Toka warriors incapacitated Vuffi Raa, Mohs took command of them and demanded that Calrissian turn the Fabled Key over to his possession. Because they were ritually forbidden from taking the key from the custody of the Key-Bearer — a prohibition that included directly killing him — they did what they felt was the next best thing and marched Calrissian to a life-orchard. There, they tied him to a life-crystal tree, which given time, would slowly drain him of his intelligence and ultimately kill him.

However, Calrissian was unwilling to go along with their plan. After Mohs and his fellow Toka left him, Calrissian freed himself and with the help of a newly-recovered Vuffi Raa, made his way back to the Falcon original landing site. They found Mohs there, cooking a creature (alternately called a lizard, a reptile or a frog) that he had impaled upon a branch. During the course of the ensuing conversation, Vuffi Raa alerted Calrissian to the approach of Mohs's friends. Calrissian threatened Mohs with the prospect of having him trade places with "that poor uncomfortable creature you're cooking" and then entertained the prospect of turning Mohs in to the "ISPCA — or at least the Epicures Club."

Given the context of Calrissian's reference to the ISPCA, it is likely that the organization would not have looked kindly upon Mohs's treatment of the frog. Calrissian's consideration of the idea of turning Mohs in to the custody of either organization may or may not have indicated that the ISPCA was vested with some power to enforce the law. Further details regarding this mysterious organization remain elusive.

She excused her two children for staring at Chewbacca because they'd never seen a Wookiee before. Han came to purchase for Jabba Desilijic Tiure a four-millennia-old portrait bust of the Hutt's ancestor, Great Bogga, recently unearthed on Near Pando, but Imperial Customs officer Rench, who followed the Millennium Falcon from Tatooine, ordered his stormtroopers to destroy it. Fortunately, Bipsmik had carved a near-perfect replica from anvilstone using a laser pantograph, which she planned to place in her garden, and Solo successfully passed it off to Jabba as the original.

Kreel reflected on Anzio and his death during the skirmish on the Ghost Moon, considering Anzio the only friend he'd ever had.

Jaizen Suel was female Jedi Knight who served the Jedi Order as a pilot in the Jedi Starfighter Corps during the final decades of the Galactic Republic.

Discovered to be Force-sensitive at an early age, Jaizen Suel was inducted into the Coruscant Jedi Temple's academy where she was taught the ways of the Force. Eventually attaining the rank of Jedi Knight, Suel began independent studies on the path of the Jedi Guardian, studying to become a member of the Jedi Starfighter Corps. Becoming a well respected pilot ace, Jedi Suel was considered to be a maverick among the Jedi, involving herself in local matters such as piracy and slavery, while ignoring the advice of the Jedi High Council.

Despite this reputation, Jedi Suel responded to Master of the Order Mace Windu's rallying cry at the height of the Separatist Crisis and piloted her Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor above Geonosis, supporting the newly unveiled Grand Army of the Republic against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Piloting her starfighter through Geonosis' asteroid belt, Suel flew under the command of High Councilors Adi Gallia and Oppo Rancisis during the battle.

Taking up the rank of General within the army, Suel spent much of her time on the Outer Rim, participating in what came to be known as the Outer Rim Sieges throughout the war. During the final days of war, Suel traded her traditional Jedi starfighter in for a modified CloakShape fighter named Dawn Raider.

Janton Belos was a male Force-sensitive individual who served the Sith Empire during the Golden Age of the Sith. Belos attained a position as a minor Sith Lord and took the Near-Human Valik Kodank as his consort. In an effort to keep her contented and romantically interested in him, he trained Kodank in the ways of the Sith. Kodank grew in power and concealed her new strength from Belos; without his knowledge, she took another Sith Lord as her lover and founded a sect of her own followers.

Janton Belos was first mentioned as an unnamed Sith Lord in Child of Light, a Star Wars Legends roleplaying adventure written by Lee Pickler and published by RPGA in 2000 as the opening instalment of the Child of Light saga. He was subsequently mentioned in the third Child of Light saga adventure, Light and Dark, in 2002, which identified his name. Neither adventure specifies Belos' species.

Jaris Affric was the High Lord of the Sarin sector during the Galactic Civil War, Following the Battle of Yavin, Affric's loose interpretation of treason against the Empire led him to employ the bulk of the Mantis Syndicate's bounty hunters on retainer, essentially using them as a personal army to serve his own interests by posting bounties either personally, or through the myriad of companies and organizations he controlled. Affric aimed the Mantis Syndicate at criminal organizations, pirate gangs, and Alliance to Restore the Republic units operating throughout the Sarin sector, especially those that directly opposed the High Lord. A keen duellist, he frequently engaged the services of The Most Honourable Guild of Armourers to procure rare and ancient duelling swords and vibroblades.

As the war in the Sarin sector escalated, Affric deployed the Mantis Syndicate in both regular combat and special operations, where they opposed both the Alliance and Churhee's Riflemen. However, as the war turned against the Empire, Affric began to run up a debt to the Mantis Syndicate, which was not tolerated by their leader, Lady Marina Mantis, who recalled her hunters. Affric protested loudly, then immediately defected to the newly established New Republic. Although he lost power and influence, Affric remained free.

Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

Jarson Andekers was a typical cocky, brash, shuttle pilot, the likes of which you would find in any starport in the galaxy. He was captured as a slave by Consolidations Unlimited, where he was only kept alive due to his mechanical skills. Due to these and his persuasive skills, he was able to convince Tarnta Bane from killing him outright. His skills, however, failed him when it came to Nuubsal the Hutt, the slaver in charge of the slave pens on the Tarnta's Fang, and he soon found himself on the top of the Hutt's List of People to Harm.

Due to this, he tried to keep as low a profile as he could so as not to draw attention to himself. While he was a slave, he became a close friend with Ch'thoqua, forming a bond within weeks. Both he and his newfound friend were anxious to escape, but would give that up if it meant they could harm their captors. Fortunately they were able to do both when Cermack Rustill boarded the ship, and managed to incite the two friends along with the other captives to riot. Shortly after this, the ship crashed on the planet Darstell 4 where he and his friend escaped in the city of Symt.

It is not known what happened to Jarson after this, but it is thought that he probably joined Ch'thoqua in his revenge against the Empire.

Jellion Broon was a famous male holovid actor in the decades before the rise of the Galactic Empire. While in Mos Espa on the planet Tatooine as part of a race story he was acting in, Broon became obsessed with the planet's deserts and wandered off to explore the Jundland Wastes. Six months later Broon reappeared, though the twin suns of Tatooine and the wind left him looking weathered and old, with his own agent no longer recognizing him and his former studio employer not wanting to deal with him.

Annileen Calwell would later use the story of Broon as an example to Obi-Wan Kenobi about the importance of keeping his hood on when working under the twin suns of Tatooine.

The handover was scheduled to take place aboard Elwis' starship, the Masquerade, while the Galactic Costume Extravaganza was being held aboard the vessel, and Zascha transported Jennalyn to the ship aboard a shuttle. Jesha Cour was a human female who lived during the final years of the Republic Era. Originally from the planet Amaltanna, Cour lost her family during the Battle of Amaltanna. Her brother died of starvation, her mother in an explosion, and her father by friendly fire. After her village was destroyed, she was placed in a refugee camp, where she met Mother Tunenep, an elderly Atriik adherent of the Path of the Open Hand, a belief system that held that the Force must remain free, opposing the Jedi Order's use of it. Cour adopted this belief and relocated with Tunenep to Coruscant after the Galactic Republic's victory against the Confederacy of Independent Systems on Amaltanna devastated the planet.

On Coruscant, Cour and Tunenep lived in poverty while spreading the teachings of the Path near the Jedi Temple. Tunenep expressed her intent to destroy the Jedi to restore balance to the Force and carried a jogan fruit pit containing synox poison. During the Battle of Coruscant, debris destroyed their residence, killing Tunenep. Cour survived, taking the poisoned jogan pit and vowing to continue Tunenep's mission.

Following Order 66 and the destruction of the Jedi Temple, Cour encountered Ryza Ayre, a human Padawan who had escaped the Temple massacre. She offered him shelter in her residence, where he revealed that younglings had been slaughtered during the attack on the Temple. Upon hearing this, Cour resolved to kill him to fulfill the Path's belief that the Force must be free, preparing tea while holding the jogan fruit pit containing the poison.

Jesha Cour appeared in "Galactic Tales: The Failing of the Light," a short story by Adam Lance Garcia that was published in issue 233 of Star Wars Insider magazine

Jestra Andrim was a female individual who was a member of House Andrim, a Kuati noble house. At some point during the reign of the Galactic Empire, House Andrim sent an operative to the Belgaroth system, to spy on some weapons tests that were to be performed by the Star Destroyers Burning Vengeance and Legacy. To collect the data that their operative had recovered, Jestra approached a group of agents that were stopping over on Kuat and requested that they perform a courier mission for her. She then invited the agents to an evening party in House Andrim's manor on the surface of Kuat, where she discussed with them the details of the assignment, then dispatched them to the Belgaroth system.

The father of Jhaka Bakarn was a Human male native to the planet Corellia several generations before the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. A member of the prestigious Bakvalen family, the Bakvalen patriarch was furious when his eldest daughter Jhaka turned her back on her life as a Corellian noble and joined the Republic Navy as a starfighter pilot. Her father disowned her, leading Jhaka to change her surname to the more common "Bakarn," and the man's daughter went on to become a renowned fighter ace. When Jhaka was killed in battle against a dangerous warlord, her father was overcome with pride and grief, and he changed the family's name to Bakarn in her honor.

Jhaka Bakarn's father was mentioned in the Codex entry for the Bakvalen family in Star Wars: The Old Republic, a video game released by BioWare in 2011.

Jioie Ancum was a Human female who supported the Alliance during the Galactic Civil War.

Jioie was a native of Tuttin IV and she accompanied her husband, Tendis Ancum, who had taken a job as a foreman at a factory on Beltrix III when the Empire took over Tuttin IV, as his assistant. Their jobs were cover for their role in the Alliance to Restore the Republic. The two left their son, Ryley Ancum, in the care of Shran Etison. Unaware of his parents' role in the Rebellion, Ryley used his music to send codes to Keth Beamis on Beltrix III. Onjo Fegel, an Imperial spy from Tuttin IV, tried to infiltrate the Agency as a member of the Far Cry band, but Ryley Ancum managed to warn the Rebels ahead of time and foil Fegel's plans. Ryley was delighted and surprised at his audition to learn the cell leaders were his parents and Tet Tramys, his music teacher. He did nothing to show that he recognized them, preserving their cover.

During General Yiv's Nikardun campaigns, "Jixtus" met his Agbui agent Haplif on board the ship on the orbit of a planet that had been devastated by the civil war incited by Haplif and his Agbui companions. He tasked the Agbui to target the Chiss Ascendancy for inner destruction next, while their attention was directed outward due the threat posed by Yiv and his Nikardun Destiny.

However, the Chiss defeated Yiv's forces during the Battle over Primea and captured Yiv himself. About two months after Yiv's defeat Jixtus hired a Pathfinder named Qilori to navigate his ship. During the trip Jixtus interrogated Qilori about Yiv's defeat and coerced the navigator to become his agent in his plot to destroy the Chiss Ascendancy.

enrichments.description:
Jodoo Kreen was a male Quermian Jedi Knight serving the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic throughout the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive, Jodo Kreen was instructed in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order from infancy to the time he passed his Trials of Knighthood and elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight. Serving the Order faithfully during the Clone Wars, a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Jedi Kreen took up the rank of General within the Grand Army of the Republic as part of the war effort.

Near the end of the war, Jedi Kreen was stationed at the Coruscant Jedi Temple when the Jedi High Council received reports of dark side activity in the Coruscant Undercity. Sent to investigate, Kreen came across the source of the malicious energy; the Dark Jedi Garth Ezzar. Engaging Ezzar in lightsaber combat, Kreen was overpowered by the darksider and slain. Leaving his body where it lay, Ezzar fled the scene to fight another day. Two weeks later, the Heroes of Cularin discovered Kreen's decaying corpse as they tracked Ezzar across Coruscant. It was recovered and returned to the Jedi Temple to receive proper funeral rites.

enrichments.description:
Jol Bengim was a Chevin male who at one time encountered enslavers and slave labor camps on Vinsoth. He later came to live in the settlement of Reestkii on the desert planet Jakku. Sometime after the Battle of Endor, Reestkii was overun by Zygerrian slavers who rounded up Bengim and the other residents and locked them in the town hall. As the settlement residents waited to learn their fate Bengim and some of the others began complaining that they were doomed. In order to keep the children present calm, the Nu-Cosian pet-seller Bobbajo began telling a story about how he and his animal companions had escaped the Death Star during the Battle of Yavin. Part way through the story Bengim interrupted and disputed its accuracy, but the disruption meant the children were no longer distracted from the slavers and the Ottegan child Adlee became upset. Bobbajo quickly resumed his story, but Bengim soon interrupted again, this time in outrage when a stormtrooper in the tale dropped the slitherette character Mideyean into a garbage compactor. When Bobbajo then finished the tale, Bengim and the other adults approached him and complimented his storytelling, but demanded to know if the story was true. Bobbajo admitted it was just a story, and then opened to doors to the town hall and revealed that the slavers had been subdued by unknown forces, leaving the citizens of Reestkii to claim their hoarded wealth.

Jol Bengim first appeared in the short story "All Creatures Great and Small," which was written by Landry Q. Walker and published as an eBook.

enrichments.description:
Jom Barell was a human male who served in the Alliance to Restore the Republic, and later the New Republic. Bearing the rank of Sergeant major, Barell served in the New Republic Special Forces. He took part in the crisis on Akiva, making a difficult jump from atmosphere onto the planet while being shot at by turbolasers to discover what exactly the Empire was doing on Akiva. He commandeered one of the turbolasers on the planet and used it to shoot at an escaping yacht, which had many important Imperials aboard, as the planet rioted and overthrew the satrapy. After the crisis on Akiva, he joined a crew of Temmin Wexley, his mother Norra Wexley, the Zabrak bounty hunter Jas Emari, and former Imperial loyalty officer Sinjir Rath Velus to hunt Imperial fugitives.

During a mission to Vorlag to capture Vice Admiral Perwin Gedde, Jom fell in love with Jas Emari after arguing about her secret plan to "triple-cross" the crew in order to pay her debts. Jom later accompanied Norra's team on their quest to find the rebel smuggler Han Solo and to rescue his Wookiee co-pilot Chewbacca from Ashmead's Lock prison. Jom, Jas, and Sinjir later joined forces with Han and Chewie to liberate Kashyyyk from Imperial rule. Despite losing his eye, Jom and his companions manage to free the Wookiees. He later stayed behind to help the newly-freed Wookiees to rebuild their world.

For taking part in an unauthorized mission, Jom was discharged from the SpecForces. Jom managed to find work as a security guard at the Galactic Senate but longed to rejoin his comrades. He took part in an undercover mission on Nakadia which exposed an attempt by the Black Sun and Red Key crime syndicates to prolong the Galactic Civil War. Later, Jom rejoined his SpecForces unit. He perished during the Battle of Jakku but managed to save the lives of his comrades.

Before joining the Rebellion, Jom Barell grew up on a farm on the planet Juntar which bred long-legged critters for their meat, milk, and leather hides.

Tall and dignified, Jovive Centi was the governor of the Chandrilan capital of Hanna and an influential member of the democratic Chandrilan House during the years leading up to and immediately following the Battle of Yavin.

When not working, she would often stroll through the streets of Hanna, striking up conversations with the citizens and joining the impromptu political discussions that frequently cropped up near the debate rotunda. Whenever she appeared in public, she would always be accompanied by Tristan Pex, her administrative aide and personal bodyguard. Tristan would later die at the hands of the Malkite Poisoner Ratambo Gale, whom Pex believed had been attempting to assassinate Centi during a public rally. In truth, Gale had been gunning for Pex all along, but that didn't stop Centi from receiving a tremendous sympathy vote and winning reelection in a landslide victory.

Kaar was a modified Corellian YT-1300 transport used by a Rebel spy during the Galactic Civil War.

Beyond the appearance of a normal YT-1300, the transport had been modified to be fast enough to outrun Assault Gunboats.

The transport was used by a Rebel Spy who decided to take shelter in a XQ3 Platform called AZ 77 that officially was a salvage yard near Venzeiia 2 Prime. However Imperial Intelligence tracked the spy to the platform with the intention of capturing him alive. Fully aware that the transport can outrun Assault Gunboats, they send a TIE Defender, equipped with a tractor beam to hamper the ship's maneuverability and disable it. After fellow ships Lin and Ko were disabled, the Kaar along with two A-wings from Rogue Squadron left the platform and the transport attempted to make the jump to Hyperspace. However, despite the Rebel escorts the transport was disabled by the TIE Defender and a Gamma-class ATR-6 assault transport arrived to board and capture the freighter to be brought back for "processing". The platform was seized shortly afterwards for harboring criminals and fugitives by forces lead by Grand Admiral Demetrius Zaarin in his flagship, the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Glory.

The events surrounding the Kaar and its capture, along with the platform were recorded and recreated for the Combat chamber to train future pilots. Maarek Stele was one of those who took the training mission to learn how to utilize the tractor beam.

Kadara Calrissian however in 15 ABY, when she was two years old, she was kidnapped by the First Order, along with other children of former Rebel leaders.

After the tragedy of losing his daughter to the First Order and his failure in a quest with Luke Skywalker to find answers about the growing darkness in the Force, Calrissian settled on the desert planet of Pasaana to lead the life of a "hermit". At first, exiling himself and hoping to bury his painful memories, he found comfort from the modest and friendly native Aki-Aki communities and the simplified life centered him. After the Battle of Exegol, Lando's hopes for finding his daughter were renewed by an encounter with Jannah, who was a former stormtrooper herself. Having resolved to provide whatever assistance he could offer to the countless individuals that the First Order had stolen from their homeworlds, Lando, although he acknowledged it as being unlikely, hoped that he might find his daughter in the process.

Landonis Balthazar Calrissian's daughter was first mentioned in the 2019 reference books Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary by Pablo Hidalgo Calrissian referenced the kidnappings of former Rebel leaders' children by the First Order that she was a victim of in lines from a deleted scene published in The Visual Dictionary. She was first identified as "Kadara" in Adam Christopher's 2022 novel Shadow of the Sith.

Kal Brigger was a Human male freelance trader who, along with his sister, Dova Brigger, bought the YT-1300 light freighter Millennium Falcon, known at the time as YT 492727ZED, in 48 BBY. Using their newly bought ship, which they named Hardwired, the siblings illegally transported cargo between Corellia and other planets in the Core Worlds. Eventually, the Briggers became involved with the Smugglers' Confederation and its leader, Nirama, who put a price on the siblings' heads due to a broken deal in which Kal was supposed to stop his dealings with slavers. After a bounty hunter captured Dova, Kal took the Hardwired for himself and rechristened the ship as Wayward Son. Kal then went to work for the former smuggler Iaco Stark, who had gotten into an armed conflict with the Galactic Republic, during which Kal was eaten alive by carnivorous insects in an abandoned spice mine on Troiken.

Kal Brigger and his sister, Dova, a pair of freelance traders, worked in the enterprising business during their careers. In 48 BBY, the Briggers came across a YT-1300 light freighter, owned by Corell Industries, which had gone bankrupt due to the Trade Federation, who had been monopolizing various businesses. The siblings bought the ship and named it Hardwired, with the intent of making a profit by transporting cargo between Corellia and other worlds. Successful in his business, Kal used the money they made toward upgrading the ship's hyperdrive, hoping for easier travel in the Corellian system, and eventually used the hyperdrive to enable travel to other Core Worlds.

However, the Briggers' business soon turned illegal, and they began to carry different cargo, including munitions, light arms, and slaves instead of consumer goods. This illegal business caught the attention of the Smugglers' Confederacy of the Cularin system and their leader, Nirama. An Oblee crime lord opposed to slavery, Nirama struck a deal with Kal hoping the Briggers would stop business with slavers. If they complied, Nirama would loan them credits to upgrade the Hardwired in return.

After a standard year, though, Kal and Dova broke the deal, prompting Nirama to put a price on their heads. A famed bounty hunter succeeded in capturing Dova, who in turn was executed by Nirama, though Kal escaped. Alone, Kal rechristened the Hardwired as Wayward Son, and attempted to take a job with Iaco Stark's Commercial Combine. This involvement with Stark, a former smuggler who headed a group of pirates, bounty hunters, and assassins, backfired on Kal when Stark became involved in an armed conflict with the Galactic Republic because of stolen bacta. The Republic forces released carnivorous insects against the smuggler on Troiken, and Kal was eaten alive by them, trapped in an abandoned spice mine.

Kallie Calwell, was the daughter of Dannar and Annileen Calwell, two Human Merchants of the Pika Oasis. She was also the sister of Jabe Calwell.

At the age of nine Kallie was entrusted to take care of the Calwell family dewbacks.

In 19 BBY Kallie was still working with her family's dewbacks. While on a dewback named Snit the animal stampeded and headed towards the Rumbles which contained one of Tatooine's sarlaccs. Her mother Annileen attempted a rescue. This was when Obi-Wan Kenobi appeared to help the teenager before they fell into the pit of the sarlacc.

Kenobi saved Kallie and Annileen but the dewback Snit was killed by the sarlacc. Annileen who had been knocked out when Kenobi threw her off the back of the dewback with the Force and told Kallie that the money to replace the dewback would come out of her wages.

Kallin Bremen was a Human male who was the father of Colonel Jak Bremen, New Republic Director of Security for the New Republic Council.

Though his early life was unknown, by at least the time of his son's birth, Bremen was living in a small, somewhat primitive village on the world of Shiffrin. He served as the village's chief constable, something young Jak would come to admire, learning much about law and justice. When his son was a teenager, a local farmer discovered a deposit of hfredium on his land, which was an ore used in the production of weapons. Not long after the farmer reported his findings did the Galactic Empire establish a garrison in the village, confiscating the land in the process.

Before long, Imperial authorities discovered that what had once been thought to be a minor deposit was actually much larger, and so, little by little, more and more land was taken from the farmers. Angry about the unjust seizures, Bremen protested, arguing with the local authorities that the ways by which the land was being taken was in opposition to Imperial doctrine—he was ignored. Determined to seek justice, Bremen organized a group of disgruntled landowners and began a peaceful protest in order to make the sector's Moff more aware of their concerns. The garrison commander, possibly wanting to cover his own illegal actions, immediately arrested the group, accusing them of being "Rebel agitators". Without a trial or hearing, the Moff ordered the execution of the entire group, bringing an end to Kallin Bremen's life.

Kani Asari was a female Human Padawan of the New Jedi Order. Stationed at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant as of 43 ABY, she was assigned as Interim Grand Master Kenth Hamner's personal assistant as he was dealing with the crisis between the Order and the Galactic Alliance.

When Alliance fugitives-turned-liaison officers Han and Leia Solo arrived at the Temple to negotiate a working treaty of sorts between Chief of State Natasi Daala and the Jedi High Council, Apprentice Asari received the pair in the main entrance hall and escorted them to a turbolift in the Great Hall that took them to a conference chamber deep in the Temple. Later, when Daala ordered Mandalorians to besiege the Temple, Asari tried to negotiate with the Mandalorian commander, Belok Rhal. However, he simply noted that she was neither Saar nor Altamik, and shot her at point-blank range, killing her, much to the shock of the Jedi. After Asari's death, Galactic Alliance Chief of Staff Wynn Dorvan carried her body from the Temple steps after his routine lunch with Jedi Raynar Thul.

Kedar Blackgate was a male Human who served as the warden of Dorthus Tal Prison. He was a fierce upholder of Sacorrian law. He had short black hair, a trimmed beard and goatee. Blackgate had a pair of loyal massiff pets that he named Emperor and Merciless.

Kedar Blackgate was born on the planet Sacorria and was raised in a privileged family. He joined the Sacorrian military at a young age. He quickly got promoted to the rank of colonel.

During the Rebellion era, Blackgate became the warden of Dorthus Tal Prison following a prison riot that was mishandled by the facility's previous warden. Blackgate assumed command of the prison with zeal, he installed various innovative programs to prevent further riots. Although his methods were more benevolent than those of his predecessors, most prisoners lived in constant fear of him. He treated and disciplined them like they were his own children, he cared for their basic needs and was enforcing a strict regimen of diet and exercise. He didn't tolerate prisoner abuse and could put even the most hardcore criminal in his place with his icy glare. He held the position of the warden of Dorthus Tal Prison for several years following the Battle of Endor.

The data card would eventually be incorporated into The Rebel Files, a central data repository that contained physical documents and intelligence from the Alliance.

Keog Boorn was a male scout who surveyed uninhabited regions of the Sluis sector around 19 BBY. He worked for both the Galactic Republic and its successor, the Galactic Empire, noting that the latter paid better. Boorn investigated a possible signal from a beckon call emanating from the planet Dagobah; while he investigated the swamps, Boorn was scared away by a howl emanating from the swamps as he approached a cave straddled by a tree.

Keog Boorn was an old scout who, about a year after the end of the Clone Wars, had been commissioned by the Galactic Empire that had just emerged to capture the worlds of the Sluis sector. After his sensors picked up strange signals during the second round of the swamp world of Dagobah, he followed the instructions of his contract with the Empire, which in these cases prescribed landing and further research. Deep in the swamps he came across a cave in a dark, deformed tree from which the signals seemed to come. But before he could enter the cave there was a terrible scary scream that filled Boorn with fear. Terrified, he left the planet without further research and noted in his notes (the exploration report SS-176.01) that the planet was completely empty and uninhabited. Dagobah thus remained a safe exile for Grand Master Yoda, who was sought by the Empire.

Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back, Second Edition

Keth Beamis was a male Human Alliance Intelligence member who worked as a talent scout during the start of the Galactic Civil War.

In 2 BBY, Beamis was stationed on the planet Beltrix III searching for talent and was impressed by Ryley Ancum's Far Cry band. After dismissing Onjo Fegel and his band, the scout was approached by two Tuttin System Security Force officers, one of whom questioned him on Maiferri Tag, a female individual who was arrested on espionage charges. The officers then arrested Keth and Ryley.

Ryley was soon afterwards released by Shran Etison, the governor and his legal guardian, who vouched for him, while Keth remained in custody and was interrogated regarding Alliance activities in Beltrix III and Maiferri Tag. However, while he instead talked about Ryley and the Far Cry, he committed suicide by triggering an affide crystal inside a drilled tooth of his before any useful information could be extracted from him.

His death was relayed by Shran, who wanted to recruit Ryley, unaware of his loyalties to the Alliance, into trying to expose the Rebel activities on Beltrix III and was tasked to lay a trap with Onjo Fegel. Ryley managed to send a rig a comlink and use his bass vye to send a signal to warn the Rebels of the impending sting operation causing them to cover their tracks and deny Onjo his promotion.

Keturah Ambar was born and raised on the moon Neftali, where she met and married her husband, Drexler Ambar. The couple had a family of seven sons and a daughter, and ran Ambar's Big Game, Tackle, and Gear Shop. On the evening of the Ambars' sixtieth wedding anniversary, Drexler went out to check the ice pools and traps and never returned. Searches for Ambar found nothing, but Keturah refused to give up on her husband. For ten years, Keturah hiked to the top of the Orane Mountain to watch for signs of Ambar. Because of her vigil, the top of the Orane Mountain became known as Keturah's Point. Keturah's routine left her nearly blind and disabled due to overexposure to Neftali's freezing temperatures. She spent her time in the back of the family-run shop, knitting and entertaining children with stories of her husband's hunting expeditions and how the animals got their names.

Kevreb Bebo was the captain of the Misanthrope, a ship that crash-landed on D'vouran, a planet that was "created" as part of Project Starscream.

He and his friend Lonni survived the crash with eighteen other people but many of them went missing after some time. While they waited for help, the rest discovered an old Imperial laboratory, in which they stayed. When one of them went to their emergency signal he disappeared too and in the end only Bebo and Lonni remained. The native Enzeen told them that the Imperials gave Bebo the blame for the crash and now he and Lonni had to stay on D'vouran. As other settlers came to the planet, Bebo tried—and failed to warn them of the disappearance of the people. Because he found an Imperial amulet, which protected him from D'vouran and saved him for disappearing, he was safe to warn the settlers, though they thought he was a madman.

In 0 ABY Mammon Hoole, DV-9, Tash and Zak Arranda arrived on D'vouran and met Bebo. Tash wanted to hear his story and went with him to the laboratory, where he gave her his protective amulet. After she left, he was killed by a Gank killer who was following the orders of Smada the Hutt.

enrichments.description: A kiss is the touching or pressing of one's lips against another person, animal, or object. The cultural connotations associated with kissing vary significantly between different societies and contexts. Depending on the culture and circumstances, a kiss can express a wide range of emotions, such as love, passion, romance, sexual attraction, sexual arousal, affection, respect, a wish for peace or good luck, as well as numerous other meanings. In some situations, kissing takes on the function of a greeting or a ritual, formal, or symbolic gesture indicating religious devotion, institutional respect, or an act of sacramental nature.

Klerin Chekkat, a Kuranu female and daughter of Mantessa Chekkat, invented a recainium-powered four-seven nullifier that the pair hoped to sell at the Valo Republic Fair. Her mother took all the credit for the invention, but was killed at the Fair during the Battle of Valo, and Klerin was rescued by Jedi after her attempt to sell her nullifier bangle to the Nihil raiders went awry. Chekkat concealed her true intentions, telling the Republic forces that the Nihil had stolen the plans for the nullifier, and went so far as to willingly play a part of a Jedi ploy to discover the Nihil base, which saw her kidnapped by the escaped Nihil Quin Amarant and taken aboard a stolen shuttle. However, upon arriving at the Nihil base on the planet Grizal and meeting with the Nihil Tempest Runner Lourna Dee, Chekkat exposed the presence of the Jedi who had snuck aboard the stolen shuttle, and offered to sell the bangle to Dee.

Klerin Chekkat was a Kuranu female who pretended to be a less capable inventor than her mother, Mantessa Chekkat. The pair hired the Tholothian mercenary Ty Yorrick to protect them as they attended the Republic Fair on the planet Valo. En route to the fair, Klerin displayed attraction towards Yorrick while toying with the large bangle she wore on one wrist. Though it appeared to be jewelry, it was actually a four-seven nullifier, a device that disrupted energy weapons such as blasters and lightsabers, powered by the illegal substance recainium. Though Klerin had invented it, her mother posed as the true inventor when meeting with Sullustan Senator Tia Toon to discuss selling it for his Defense Force Program. Toon refused to buy the device, and had Mantessa and Yorrick imprisoned for bringing recainium onto the world. The two managed to escape and got separated when Nihil marauders attacked the Valo Republic Fair, but soon after the mother and daughter were reunited, Mantessa was killed by a hragscythe that had escaped from the Lonisa City Zoo.

Star Wars: The High Republic Character Encyclopedia

The klirun was a high-tension projectile bow that was the traditional hunting weapon of the Tunroth. It became so revered by the species that it was considered a sacred weapon.

Weighting around 3.5 kg, the powerful hunting bow was built with a recurve so that it remained bow-shaped even when unstrung. Designed for Tunroth strength, the bow had a heavy pull, and was capable of piercing stormtrooper armor. The bows used caros arrows, which were occasionally tipped with talar, a stunning agent that enabled non-lethal strikes.

Klossi Anno was a female Chalactan Padawan serving the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the final years of the Republic. A commander within the Grand Army of the Republic, she survived the Clone Wars and the execution of Contingency Order 66, unlike her master, who died during the initial stages of the Great Jedi Purge.

Discovered to be Force-sensitive near birth on Chalacta, Klossi Anno was taken to the Coruscant Jedi Temple and inducted into the academy there. Studying the ways of the Force, Anno eventually graduated after years of study and was selected by a Jedi Master for one-on-one training. During her apprenticeship, the tensions between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems came to a breaking point resulting in the start of the Clone Wars. Reporting to the Jedi High Council, Anno was given the rank of Commander in the Grand Army of the Republic and leadership of clone troopers.

After years of fighting, the war ended abruptly when the Republic's Supreme Chancellor disbanded the Jedi Order with the issuance of Contingency Order 66. When her clone troopers turned their blasters on her, Anno's master sacrificed herself so that Anno could flee. Making her way to Dellalt, Anno joined with nine other fugitive Jedi in hijacking an SX troop shuttle from the newly formed Galactic Empire. While they were pursued by a group of ARC-170s and a light cruiser, losing two of their company, Anno and the others escaped pursuit and were given sanctuary by the crew of the Drunk Dancer. In the company of smuggler Jula Shryne, the group was eventually joined by Master Roan Shryne and Padawan Olee Starstone. Given new hope by Starstone's enthusiasm and determination, Anno and her companions agreed to search for Grand Master Yoda on Kashyyyk. Giving Master Shryne her fallen master's lightsaber, the group headed out to meet their fate on the Wookiee homeworld.

Once there, Kashyyyk came under invasion by the Empire for housing Jedi. Led by Darth Vader, the Empire searched for the Jedi fugitives, eventually confronting them. Padawan Anno attacked the Sith Lord after he injured Jedi Knights Siadem Forte and Iwo Kulka, but the powerful cyborg merely sidestepped her, slashing her across the back with his lightsaber. Dragged away from the battle and taken offworld by the other surviving Jedi, Anno was able to recover and decided to sabotage the Empire in a less direct way. With the suggestions of her comrades, Anno planned to work on construction sites, or in an agricultural project, and intended to undo the Sith in more subtle ways than with a lightsaber.

A Jedi Master served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a Jedi General during the Clone Wars between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. In 19 BBY, the Jedi Master was fighting in the conflict alongside their Padawan, the Chalactan Klossi Anno. When Contingency Order 66—an order to kill the Jedi—was initiated, the Republic's clone troopers turned on their Jedi Generals, considering them traitors to the Republic. The Master was killed by the clones, though their sacrifice allowed Anno to escape. Anno later met with other fugitive Jedi—including the Jedi Master Roan Shryne—to whom she gave her Jedi Master's lightsaber.

The Jedi Master was mentioned in the 2005 novel Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, written by James Luceno.

Knights was an MC80 Star Cruiser belonging to the Rebel Alliance.

The cruiser along with a Bothan Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser called Doomer were attempting a secret meeting. However the Imperials had sent a strike force consisting of Missile Boats, one of the starfighters piloted by Tan Maarek Stele, TIE Avengers and Gamma-class ATR-6 assault transports to capture the Rebel Cruiser and destroy the Bothan Dreadnaught.

Stele cleared a minefield, destroyed all starfighter opposition, destroyed the Dreadnaught and reduced the cruiser's shields and the ship was successfully disabled and captured along with the Nebulon-B2 frigate Tarken.

Ko Bas was a male Caarite, who worked for the Metatheran Cartel trade alliance during the waning years of the Galactic Republic. Bas had responsibility for overseeing operations at a secret Cartel base on the moon Tilnes in the Cularin system. Around 21 BBY, the Believers Sith cult dispersed a test batch of a virus fatal to Caarites in the Tilnes facility as part of a plot to weaken the Cartel. Bas survived exposure to the contagion and instead of being killed was transformed into a violent, raging mutant being. Two weeks after the release of the virus, a team of Believers ventured to the Cartel base and four of their party were killed and eaten by Bas. Shortly thereafter, a team of freelance agents entered the facility to follow up a distress signal emanating from the base. Bas attacked the operatives but was defeated by them.

Ko Bas was a Caarite male who worked as a bureaucrat for the Metatheran Cartel trade alliance during latter years of the Galactic Republic. Bas was responsible for the running of a secret base operated by the Cartel beneath the surface of the moon Tilnes in the Cularin system and held the position of Overseer of Cartel Operations, Tilnes Special Detachment. Bas maintained an office in the base, within which he kept a set of personalized stationary that bore his name. the Cartel technician Celis Bol was requested to prepare some bean juice for Bas. Angered at being given such a menial task, Bol surreptitiously spat in the juice that the technician had put together for him. Bas detected the impurities in his juice via a purifier and Bol's pay was docked as punishment.

Four days after the incident with Bol and the bean juice, the Believers Sith cult secretly placed an explosive device laden with a virus fatal to Caarites within the ventilation system of the Cartel Tilnes base, close to the location of Bas' office. The cultists desired to use their pathogen to weaken the influence of the Caarite-dominated Metatheran Cartel and saw the Tilnes base as a suitable location to test their viral weapon. Bas was in his office when the bomb was detonated and the force of the explosion hurled him against the far side of the room, leaving a blast outline in his shape imprinted against the wall. The virus quickly spread throughout the base, infecting Bas and his colleagues, resulting in the sudden demise of the majority of the facility's inhabitants. By a fluke of fate, Bas and two other Caarites, "U" and "G," were not killed by the virus and were instead mutated into enlarged violent, raging beings, retaining little semblance of their old selves.

enrichments.description:
Korelei was a female Keshiri Lord of the Lost Tribe of Sith who became one of the final host bodies of Abeloth and was killed at the New Jedi Temple when Abeloth and the Lost Tribe of Sith were defeated.

By the time of the Lost Tribe of Sith emergence Korelei had ascended to the rank of Sith Lady. After Abeloth took over the Lost Tribe, and the Galactic Alliance, Korelei served Abeloth by torturing Wynn Dorvan for over a month.

Shortly after the Jedi began the Liberation of Coruscant, Korelei met with Abeloth to discuss the Lost Tribe's losses. When Abeloth learned that the Jedi had managed to kill about a thousand Sith she commanded Korelei to kill all the Jedi by the next dawn. Korelei explained that this wasn't possible as they had not captured any Jedi, and explained to Abeloth that Wynn Dorvan, who was now serving as her adviser, was hiding information about the Jedi. Korelei suggested revealing the Sith to the people of Coruscant, but Wynn disagreed as that would lead to open rebellion against the Sith. Korelei attempted to kill Wynn with her shikkar but Abeloth caught it and agreed with Wynn that civilian deaths were not in their interests. Wynn told Abeloth and Korelei that the best plan of attack would be to lure the Jedi to the Sith occupied Jedi Temple. After death of High Lord Ivaar Workan she was chosen as one of Abeloth's host bodies and became High Lord herself.

Korelei was strong enough to ascend to the rank of Sith Lord within the Lost Tribe. Korelei was skilled in Force torture, which she used against Wynn Dorvan during his captivity. She was also capable of using the Force to probe an individual's mind. Later, as Abeloth's host, Korelei was strong enough to shield herself against a mine detonation. Korelei was also skilled in the use of Force lightning, which she used against Jedi during the Liberation of Coruscant.

Korsin Bentado was a Force-sensitive Human Male. He was a well-built and bald man who had a black moustache. Korsin was a member of the Lost Tribe of Sith, the descendants of a group of Human Sith that had become stranded on the planet Kesh during the Great Hyperspace War. Korsin grew up during the Time of the Rot and became the leader of the Korsinite League, a faction which revered the Tribe's founder Yaru Korsin and his daughter Nida Korsin. In 3000 BBY, he went to Tahv to celebrate Testament Day, and to stop an attempt by the Sisters of Seelah to alter the Testament of Yaru Korsin to favor their interests. During Testament, the various Sith factions learnt that the ancestors of the Lost Tribe were not "great conquerors" but were actually slaves of the Sith Empire. This sparked a brief period of murder and unrest known as the Great Crisis. During the fighting, Korsin lost his left hand to Iliana Merko, the leader of the Sisters of Seelah.

Korsin subsequently joined forces with several surviving members of the Tribe including Edell Vrai and Neera to destroy the ancient Sith starship Omen in order to purge the "shameful history" of the Tribe. However, they were stopped by the Caretaker Varner Hilts, Iliana, and Hilt's Keshiri assistant Jaye Vuhld. During a brief skirmish, Korsin killed Jaye with his lightsaber. However, Hilts successfully convinced the other Sith to end the fighting by revealing the existence of a map which showed the existence of another continent known as Alanciar. Yaru Korsin had concealed Alanciar's existence and intended to use it as a "cause" to give his descendants a new sense of purpose. Hilt's ploy worked and the other Sith including Korsin elected Hilts as their new Grand Lord, the first since the Night of the Upside-Down Meteor which ended the life of Lillia Venn.

After Hilt's takeover of the Tribe, Bentado became a member of the Grand Lord's new Circle of Lords, and received the title of High Lord. For the next twenty-five years, the Tribe committed themselves to reaching and conquering Alanciar. The Tribe also developed a fleet of hydrogen-powered airships which were used to travel to Alanciar. Korsin's rival Edell Vrai led the vanguard force and encountered resistance from the Alanciari Keshiri, who had prepared for a Sith invasion. During the invasion of Alanciar in 2975 BBY, the High Lord commanded the Ebon Fleet which sustained heavy casualties from the Alanciari forces. The Ebon Fleet's airships were shot down, and most of the invasion force was killed.

Kosul Ayada was a male Herglic Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic faithfully for many years, dying several decades before the outbreak of the Clone Wars and the eventual rise of the Galactic Empire.

A Force-sensitive Herglic, Kosul Ayada was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, eventually attaining the rank of Jedi Master. A noted Jedi, Ayada took many Padawans during his career and successfully trained them to knighthood. His last student was a Zabrak boy named Eeth Koth, who went on to train as a Guardian of the Order and earn a seat on the Jedi High Council. When Ayada became one with the Force, Koth constructed a lightsaber hilt that resembled the Herglic's own as a way of memorializing his master.

Kunor Bann was a male Human Jedi Knight who lived around the time following the Second Galactic Civil War. In 44 ABY, Bann developed a psychosis brought on by the dark side entity Abeloth, causing him to believe that everyone he knew had been replaced by impostors. He succumbed to the psychosis while inside the Jedi Temple, although he was captured by the Jedi there and confined in the Jedi Temple detention center. Jedi Master Cilghal drew up a report that went into detail about the psychosis in Bann and another Jedi who was suffering from the same illness, Turi Altamik, putting forth her belief that the rate of Jedi succumbing to the psychosis was accelerating. Before long, however, exiled Jedi Grand Master Luke Skywalker successfully completed his mission to kill Abeloth, resulting in the immediate termination of Bann's psychosis.

Bann later participated in the rescue attempt to free both Valin and Jysella Horn from the clutches of Galactic Alliance Security. As part of "Team Saav'etu", Bann took up a defensive position outside the bunker housing the Horn siblings and helped fend off attacks by GAS personnel.

enrichments.description:
L'lacielo Sageon was an aged male Lorrdian Jedi Knight who served the Jedi Order during the waning years of the Galactic Republic. Sageon served as a General of the Grand Army of the Republic through the Clone Wars.

Born a Force-sensitive on the planet Lorrd, L'lacielo Sageon was discovered by scouts for the Jedi Order and taken to the Coruscant Jedi Temple for training in the ways of the Force. After years of study at the Temple's academy, Sageon was selected by a Jedi Master to become a Padawan and travel the galaxy for one-on-one training. During his training, Sageon grew in his knowledge of the Force and crafted for himself a blue-bladed lightsaber before passing his Trials of Knighthood and being elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight by the Jedi High Council.

Sageon served the Order as a Knight for many decades, serving the Jedi Temple as quartermaster, equipping Jedi for field missions for many years. However, once the Clone Wars erupted between the Confederacy of Independent Systems and the Republic, Sageon was called into active duty once more. Receiving the rank of General in the newly formed Grand Army of the Republic.

Stationed on Coruscant near the end of the war, Sageon was present when General Grievous launched a surprise attack on the capital world. Manning a fighter Sageon raced up into the atmosphere to join the fight, when word reached the Jedi that the cyborg had fled the planet with Supreme Chancellor Palpatine as his prisoner. Sageon joined several of his fellow Knights including Pablo-Jill as well as council members Agen Kolar and Saesee Tiin, in an attempt to rescue the Chancellor.

enrichments.description:
Lanoree Brock's father was a male Human and a Je'daii Master who taught at Bodhi, the Temple of Arts, for the Je'daii Order on Tython at the height of the Infinite Empire's reign.

Trained as a member of the Je'daii Order, Brock met his future wife met as Journeyers crossing the planet Tython on their Great Journey. Both of the young Je'daii were drawn to Bodhi Temple where the Force exposed their natural talents in the arts. A talented sculptor renowned across Masara continent, Brock was also skilled at cooking rumbat stew. Years after their Journey ended, Brock and his wife became the parents of Lanoree and Dalien Brock. Living in the Je'daii settlement surrounding the Temple of Arts, Brock taught at Bodhi, amusing his students and colleagues with his magic tricks. One of his students, Master Xiang, would later go on to teach under his watch. When his children were growing up, he would tell them tales and legends from Je'daii history, including a cautionary tale of Osamael Or and his fateful mission into the Old City.

During the war between Tython and Despot Queen Hadiya and her army, Brock served some of his time on the planet Nox where the fighting was especially vicious. Following the war and the supposed death of his son, Brock rarely saw his daughter, who had become a Je'daii Ranger by the time of Dalien's reemergence during the Stargazer Uprising.

Brock wore his hair long, usually tied up, but allowed it to fall across his shoulders when at home. Brock believed that his son's inquisitive nature was a sign that he would make a fine Je'daii in time; he always believed that Dalien would find his own way. When spending time with his children, Brock would often take them to the Edge Forest where his explorer's heart would yearn to venture into its vastness.

Lanoree Brock's grandfather was first mentioned in Dawn of the Jedi: Into the Void, a Legends novel written by Tim Lebbon. He was first mentioned as the former owner of Dalien Brock's blaster pistol.

enrichments.description:
Lanoree Brock's mother was a female Human Je'daii Master who served as instructor at Bodhi, the Temple of Arts, for the Je'daii Order on Tython at the height of the Infinite Empire's reign.

Trained as a member of the Je'daii Order, she met her future husband as Journeyers crossing the planet Tython on their Great Journey. Both of the young Je'daii were drawn to Bodhi Temple where the Force exposed their natural talents in the arts. A talented musician with a speciality for prose and poetry, she was on the track to become a Je'daii of some renown. Years after their Journey ended, she and her husband became the parents of Lanoree and Dalien Brock. Living in the Je'daii settlement surrounding the Temple of Arts, Brock taught at Bodhi, and in the evenings would read poetry to her children before they slept. When her children were growing up, she would teach them the basics of touching another's mind and the survival skills necessary to live on Tython.

During the war between Tython and Despot Queen Hadiya and her army, Brock served some of his time on the planet Nox where the fighting was especially vicious. Following the war and the supposed death of her son, Brock comforted her daughter at Dalien's memorial ritual by assuring her that not everyone completed their Journey. Afterwards, she rarely saw her daughter, who had become a Je'daii Ranger by the time of Dalien's reemergence during the Stargazer Uprising. Following the Stargazer Uprising, Lanoree returned to Bodhi Temple and to her parents' house for her brother's second Remembrance Ceremony after she had killed him in service to the Order.

Brock was a loving mother who expressed deep concern for her son. When her children were about to leave on their Great Journey, she pulled her daughter aside and asked her to look after Dalien, as she sensed his middling Force ability. Tearing up as she speaks of her fears that Dalien will be drawn away from Tython, she insisted to her daughter that her worry is genuine and that her son's interest in the distant past troubled her.

Lazlo Ardine was a male Human who served as a Colonel in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

During the conflict, Ardine was selected to command Strike Force Cularin, a strikeforce that was made up of units from the Galactic Republic, Cularin Militia and Thaereian military. He led them on a mission to the Ando system, where they captured a Separatist CR90 corvette and attacked a Separatist base on a planetoid in the system. During the attack, he overheard his second-in-command, Colonel Rast'tul, confess to an attempt to kill the Heroes of Cularin, so Ardine ordered some Clone troopers arrest him.

He was later aboard the Relentless during the Battle of Cularin.

Ardine was a career soldier and was committed to fighting and doing what he thought to be right. Although he respected the fighting abilities of the Jedi, he felt that they shouldn't have been given command of the Grand Army. Prior to the mission to the Ando system, he disliked the Cularin Militia's war against the Thaereians, as he believed that the Thaereian military was justified in being in the Cularin system. However, the mission changed his perspective on this and afterward, he was more sympathetic to the Militia.

Leanna Carella was an customs officer and later the wife of captain Dav Kathis of the Longrunner. Once he mysteriously disappeared, Carella took control of his ship to make a living and to look for him.

Leanna Carella began her career as a customs officer. She eventually left this job to marry Dav Kathis, an independent free-trader who operated his Kazellis Light Freighter Longrunner through the Enarc Run. Carella and Kathis lived on their ship along with their son.

Kathis suddenly vanished; he had been kidnapped by agents of COMPNOR who mistakenly believed him to be an informer to the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Carella began traveling Kathis' usual routes looking for him, while at the same time she tried to earn some money with the business.

One of the COMPNOR agents suffered from paranoia: When they could not link Kathis with the Alliance, he decided that Carella was probably the informer they were looking for.

Ledina Chott was a Human female who was a famous interplanetary pop singer who resided on Kuratooine. In 44 ABY, she had received various gifts from a mysterious man named Thadley Biolan, who was really known as corrupt Alliance General Stavin Thaal. Since Chott had physical similarities to all of Thaal's ex-wives, the General looked to Chott as a new mistress.

During Wraith Squadron's investigation into Thaal's guilt regarding his involvement with the Lecersen Conspiracy, they deduced that, as Biolan, he would retire from the military service and probably pick Chott as a potential wife. In response, one of the Wraiths, Trey Courser, wore a double disguise of Biolan over Thaal and he and a few of the other Wraiths kidnapped her from her home and drugged her before Thaal himself could meet her.

The next day, Courser and fellow Wraith Drikall Bessarah smuggled Chott's unconscious form to the Kuratooine warehouse where Thaal performed some of his criminal operations. From there, after the two Wraiths dealt with security, they activated Chott's emergency transponder so that the local Kura City Guard could save her; this way, Thaal could be framed for kidnapping Chott, though they weren't counting on him actually being convicted for their crime.

By the time she was kidnapped, Ledina Chott had been a pop star for about two years, yet she wasn't jaded and used to the life of a celebrity yet. She was also annoyed that her home on Kuratooine would feature holos and stills of her works only and not of works of some of the celebrities she liked. Her facial resemblance to the template that General Stavin Thaal loves made her a potential wife to him, which was why he sent her gifts as Thadley Biolan.

enrichments.description:
Leesa Chaffni was a Kessurian female who resided in Cratertown on the planet Jakku alongside her father Lubos during the New Republic Era and the following First Order-Resistance War. She also owned a skittermouse she had nicknamed Tails, which accompanied her everywhere in her pocket after she had rescued him from a predator during her childhood. After her father hurt his leg in an accident at work in the local kesium mines, Leesa began working as a help at Dai's Cafe.

Between 34 ABY and 35 ABY, when she was twelve years old, Chaffni overheard the Jakkuvian scavenger Velorie Sarcon bragging at the Cafe about a contract she had gotten to retrieve the contents of a vault on the crashed Dreadnought-class heavy cruiser Explorator of Imperial Commodore Visler Aqorian Korda III in the desert sands north of the Kelvin Ravine on Jakku. When Sarcon realized that Chafni had listened, she confronted and bullied her, but was stopped by the patrons and Resistance members Rey, Finn and BB-8, and left. Sarcon and her droid RJ-21, as well as Chaffni, who hoped to find medical supplies for her father, and the Resistance members, then each made their way to the Dreadnought. On her way to the ship through the tunnels of an abandoned kesium mine, Cafni was almost killed by a swarm of gnaw-jaws and was only saved by stumbling into the wreck were she was found by Rey and Finn and BB-8. On the Explorator, the four ultimately joined forces with Sarcon and found the vault, but came to a standoff with Sarcon's client, the First Order officer Dihun, and her stormtroopers in the hangar. During the confrontation, RJ-21 then betrayed his companions and and opened the vault door unleashing Korda's prototype nightwatcher droid from the vault, which attacked everyone in the hangar. However, Rey managed to briefly control the droid with Korda's control circlet so that they could overwrite Korda's corrupting code and calm the droid, which then rescued Rey, Finn, BB-8, Chaffni, Sarcon and Sarcon's former associate Ivrax from the ship while it sank beneath the sand dunes. Back at home Sarcon fixed the magna-cast they had found in the Explorator medical bay to Lubos's leg and Lubos and Leesa invited Sarcon to live with them in their home. Chaffni later relayed the story of her recent adventure to Dai's Cafe patron Naldri Zuvio.

Leesa Chaffni first appeared in The Jaws of Jakku, an Audible-exclusive audiobook written by Cavan Scott and narrated by Helen Sadler, In the book, the story is presented as being told in-universe by Leesa Chaffni to Naldri Zuvio who stands in for the actual real-world listener. The spelling of Leesa Chaffni's first name was confirmed by a chapter title, but due to being an audio exclusive, the spelling her last name has not yet been confirmed.
