Legacy world was a term for planets in remote regions of the galaxy that were environmentally-protected and legally exempted from exploitation. had a limited visitation and restricted industrial presences. While activities like mining were permitted on these worlds, they were regulated so to be low-impact only. Permanent settlements on Legacy worlds were not permitted. While the concept of Legacy worlds pre-dated the Galactic Empire by generations, during the Imperial Era, the Galactic Empire controlled the process of planets being granted legacy status or having their status maintained and upheld. Environmentalists and scientists sought to have planets such as Alpinn granted the legacy status. While some thought the worlds needed to be preserved, others regarded Legacy worlds as just primitive historical locations. Lyra Erso had an interest in protecting planets with legacy status and visited several of these worlds in the years before the Clone Wars.

Several planets in the Western Reaches, including Samovar and Wadi Raffa, were considered Legacy worlds. Samovar's mining conglomerate had worked to get the Legacy regulations removed, until the Empire targeted it. They hired smugglers to transport old Separatist weaponry to the planet before "exposing" the operations and using it as a means to remove Samovar's legacy status. Meanwhile, on Wadi Raffa, Turlin/Benthic Extraction had been been operating legal underwater mining operations until the Empire stepped in, using the same tactics they had on Samovar. Turlin/Benthic was framed for received illegally-trafficked weaponry, and the Empire removed Wadi Raffa's legacy status before beginning their own operations there.

Official legislation on Republic legacy worlds became stored in the Imperial Archives following the rise of the Empire. Later, the historian Beaumont Kin accessed the records.

Lidan Bleeker was a Rodian male mercenary who lived during the last decades of the Galactic Republic.

Bleeker was a professional soldier and during his career he served with the armed forces of several planets as well as within a couple of mercenary bands. However, he later found himself within job and he was enlisted by the Force Adept Dersa Welles into joining the Intarsa League, a criminal faction that she led.

Circa 31 BBY, Bleeker and the rest of the Intarsa League were attacked by a criminal rival while traveling in a shuttle close to the world Cularin and they crash-landed in the grounds of the Blue Star Centre, a philosophical research facility. In desperation, Bleeker and the other Intarsa League members seized control of the Blue Star Centre and held its' inhabitants hostage in return for a ransom, passage off Cularin and assurances that the local authorities would apprehend the criminals who had shot down their shuttle. However, the Heroes of Cularin–a band of freelance operatives that operated within the Cularin system–attacked the Intarsa League and defeated Bleeker and his companions.

Lik Ankkit was a male Neimoidian. He lived in a villa on the planet Qiilura, where he controlled the production of barq and other luxury foods, exploiting the poor farmers who couldn't afford the food that grew on their fields.

During the start of the Clone Wars, Ankkit hired the Mandalorian Ghez Hokan to enforce his dominance of the farmers. Hokan despised Ankkit, and thought of him as a "weak and decadent grocer".

When the Mandalorian was put in command of a small force of battle droids to defend a vital facility, he used Ankkit's villa to hold some of his droids. The smashing of artifacts and scratching of floors by the droids was a great frustration to Ankkit.

Ankkit appeared in the 2004 novel Republic Commando: Hard Contact by Karen Traviss.

Lin was a modified Corellian YT-1300 transport that was used by criminals that were hiding from the Galactic Empire during the Galactic Civil War. The transport was the first of three transports to try to leave a XQ3 platform that served as a salvage yard but was also responsible for being a hiding point for fugitives, including a Rebel spy.

The Lin was only able to get a relatively safe distance from the platform but was disabled by a TIE Defender that carried with it a tractor beam. The transport was boarded by an assault transport and captured bringing the criminals back into custody the rest of the transports followed suit and the platform was seized. The events surrounding the Platform's capture were recorded and recreated for the Combat chamber for training.

The transport is labeled "Lindilu" in the list of objectives in Strategy Guide, however the ship is also called "Lin" in the book and is addressed as "Lin" in the game.

Lo Bukk was a Zabrak male who served the Jedi Order as a Padawan during the final decades of the Galactic Republic. Around 67 BBY, he and his Jedi Master, Ni-Cada, were sent by the Order to the world of Abraxin to investigate the continuous killing of marsh haunts, which were being carried out by the Force-sensitive Nautolan Naat Lare. On the planet the Jedi unknowingly crossed paths with the Muun Sith Lord Darth Plagueis, who was also looking for Lare. After Plagueis managed to make contact with Lare, the Muun convinced him into taking the offense against the Jedi as proof of his worthiness to join the Sith; the resulting skirmish was short, in which Bukk's Master killed Lare.

Lo Bukk was a male Force-sensitive Zabrak Jedi Padawan of Master Ni-Cada who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic forty-five years before the Clone Wars, a series of conflicts fought between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. He and Ni-Cada were sent by the Order to the swampy planet Abraxin in the Tion Cluster, to investigate the continuous killing of non-sentient marsh haunts, The marsh haunt killings were committed by Naat Lare, a Force-sensitive Nautolan. Lare had been selected by Darth Venamis, a prospective male Bith Sith Lord of the lineage of Darth Bane, as a potential Sith apprentice.

During their stay on Abraxin, the Muun Sith Lord Darth Plagueis passed by Bukk and Ni-Cada disguised while the Jedi were bargaining with a member of the Barabel species—cold-blooded reptilians from the world Barab I— for a water skimmer. Both of them felt Plagueis' presence, though neither identified him as a Sith, an order of Force-sensitives who utilized the dark side of the Force. Later, as Bukk and his master emerged from an eatery bearing flagons of liquid, they unknowingly crossed paths with Darth Plagueis once again, and later talked with the Muun, who was also looking for Lare, as they sat at a table and discussed with the Muun about the recent killing of marsh haunts. Plagueis managed to make contact with Lare and convinced him into striking against the Bukk and his master as proof of Lare's worthiness to join the Sith. The Jedi tracked Lare with the skimmer, and a short skirmish ensued after the Nautolan attacked the two near the water, during which Lare was killed by Bukk's master.

Lo Bukk had a more of a open attitude than his master, as he easily divulged the nature of the Jedi's mission to Plagueis, though his master tried to hide the reason of their mission. When the Muun Sith Lord Darth Plagueis passed by under disguise, both Ni-Cada and Lo Bukk felt Plagueis' presence, though neither of them identified him as a Sith, a sect of Force-sensitives who utilized the dark side of the Force.

enrichments.description:
Lon Bennor was a male who lived in the city of Domaz on the planet Kolatill, located within the Kathol sector of the Outer Rim Territories. In 8 ABY, Domaz was assaulted by TIE bombers from the Imperial Ton-Falk-class escort carrier Kathol Protector. The attack was in retaliation for the population of Kolatill overthrowing their Imperial governor in the wake of the New Republic's liberation of the nearby planet of Kal'Shebbol. With the city devastated, Bennor began to organize relief efforts from a park that had been converted into an emergency aid station. He accepted help from the crew of the New Republic vessel FarStar—who had responded to a distress call from the planet—in providing medical assistance and enlisted their services to retrieve more supplies from a bombed-out hospital.

Lon Bennor was a male who resided on the planet Kolatill in the Kathol sector in the Outer Rim Territories, and lived in the capital city of Domaz. the New Republic liberated the planet of Kal'Shebbol, the sector capital. As a result, the local Imperial Moff, Kentor Sarne—who had set himself up as a warlord following the death of Emperor Palpatine at the Battle of Endor four years previously—was forced to flee his capital with the majority of his forces. When news of the New Republic's victory at Kal'Shebbol reached the population of Kolatill, they staged a popular uprising, overthrowing and imprisoning their Imperial governor, Tetrum, and reinstating the Kolatill Council to lead them.

Shortly after this act of rebellion, the Imperial Ton-Falk-class escort carrier Kathol Protector arrived in-system and used TIE bombers to assault Domaz. Bennor survived the devastation wrought on his home and immediately began to organize relief efforts from a park at the heart of the city that had been converted into an emergency aid station. He blamed the Kolatill Council for the attack, since they had publicly declared allegiance to the New Republic after being reinstated into power.

Four days after the attack, the crew of the New Republic CR90 corvette FarStar arrived to assist in relief operations. Bennor was not particularly pleased to see them, as they were representatives of the government that had indirectly been the cause of the attack on Domaz. However, he did accept their assistance and medical supplies, since his priorities were saving as many lives as possible. Bennor also requested the assistance of FarStar crew members when he went to a bombed-out hospital to retrieve much needed medical supplies. With their help, he was able to overcome collapsing floors, fires, and other hazards to recover the supplies.

After the Corsignis Property Alliance and the Jon-Tow Economic Development Group blockaded Pinett as a result of a trade dispute, the Pinett Freedom Force, a local protest movement, attempted to prevent Corsignis and Jon-Tow starships from landing on the moon. However, a number of port workers became disgruntled as a result of the Freedom Force's actions, and under the leadership of Jaeth and B'Nash, the port workers began to cause trouble for the Freedom Force.

The Lourna Dee was the flagship of Lourna Dee, Tempest Runner in the Nihil marauder organization, following the loss of her previous starship of the same name. The vessel was formerly the Restitution, a correctional ship of the Galactic Republic. The Restitution constantly journeyed between star systems, with its prisoners being taught skills to repay for their deeds. Dee was assigned to the Restitution after being captured by the Republic and Jedi Order, who were unaware of her identity. Over a month after Dee's capture, the Restitution was attacked by former Nihil Tempest Runner Pan Eyta, who sought revenge on Dee. Though Dee had begun to turn away from her Nihil past, the attack eventually drove her to take command of the prison ship, the crew of which had been near eliminated by the attackers. Dee renamed the vessel after herself, returning to the Nihil with the surviving prisoners as her new Tempest. which she had stolen during the destruction of Starlight Beacon and also renamed Lourna Dee, as her personal vessel.

Star Wars: The High Republic Character Encyclopedia

Lunar Shadow was a ship stuck on Nar Shaddaa during the Meetra Surik's visit to the planet. It was crewed by Nikto, and the captain was a Weequay who frequented the Jekk'Jekk Tarr. The Nikto were unable to leave because the captain was also their pilot, and they were unable to go fetch him due to the fact that the cantina contained fumes that were poisonous to their species.

During the game, it is possible for the Exile to convince the Weequay to return to the Lunar Shadow so that the ship can leave.

It is also possible for the exile to convince the Nikto to hire the refugee Odis as their new pilot. The crewmen are tired of having to wait around all the time while the captain wastes the group's profits on his own entertainment, so they agree quickly to hire Odis after the idea is suggested, as it solves two problems, getting them a qualified new pilot and getting rid of the incompetent existing captain.

Lastly, the Exile can choose the Dark-side action of coming to the apartment where the ship's crew are staying and killing everyone there.

Lune Banjeer was a male Admiral who served with distinction during the Ruusan campaign between the Galactic Republic and the Brotherhood of Darkness, which lasted from 1002 BBY to 1000 BBY. The Admiral was made the first commander of the Republic's Judicial Forces following the Ruusan Reformation at the end of Ruusan campaign, which created the force as a replacement for the disbanded Republic Military. Under Banjeer's leadership, and that of his successors, the Judicial Forces fought successfully in a series of Unification Campaigns in the period between 1000 BBY and 900 BBY.

Lune Banjeer was first mentioned in The Essential Guide to Warfare, a sourcebook written by Jason Fry and Paul R. Urquhart and released in 2012. Two other individuals, Llon Banjeer and Boss Banjeer, share the admiral's surname, but no connection has been established between them.

The stepdaughter of Lux Bonteri was a female individual who was the daughter of Bonteri's wife. She eventually became a loyal member of the Galactic Empire. After Bonteri had joined the Partisans, he contacted his stepdaughter asking her for specific times and locations for places where he could hand himself in to the Empire. She compiled a list of events where Bonteri could turn himself in to moderate Imperial authorities who could be trusted to honor his defection without torturing or killing him. Instead of turning himself in, however, Lux joined Staven Dreamers, and the insurgents used the information as targets for attacks.

When Imperial Captain Iden Versio of Inferno Squad confronted Bonteri, she asked him if he ever thought about turning himself in to the Empire. Lux replied that indeed he had, but he knew the Empire would eventually trace the source of his information to his stepdaughter and torture and/or kill her. He could not bear the thought of them hurting her, as he loved her very much, so he did not turn himself in.

Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy

enrichments.description: The Madman's Fortune was a museum exhibit ship that flew as part of a traveling freak show. The ship was owned by the Snivvian Goontirk and at some point during galactic history, Goontirk purchased the mummified remains of Vardovin IV, the "Lost King of Duro" from a Ryn merchant, to display aboard the Madman's Fortune. However, unknown to Goontirk, the mummy contained more than a dozen skekfish eggs and while the Madman's Fortune was passing through the Engebo system, the mummy's plasteel coffin cracked open and the skekfish eggs hatched. The creatures attacked Goontirk and in an attempt to escape from them, he ran into one of the ship's escape pods. The skekfish pursued the Snivvian in and they devoured him before he could launch the pod, and thirty seconds later the Madman automated safety systems launched the escape pod into the atmosphere of the planet Engebo V.

Mandragall was a Human male Sith Lord who ruled a region of space during the Republic Dark Age. By using mercenaries and pirates, he was able to achieve significant military success, but he was eventually murdered by the Sith Xelian.

Mandragall was a Human male who became a Sith Lord While in his youth, Mandragall discovered a holocron that had belonged to Elcho Kressh, an individual who had served the Sith during the time of the Great Hyperspace War. Mandragall eventually became the ruler of a region of space, but he came into conflict with rival Sith Lords, and he found himself without sufficient troops to defend his territories. He attempted the defend his borders using droids, but the scheme failed, so he consulted Kressh's holocron to try and find an alternative solution. The device contained records of an operation enacted by Kressh to create an army by forming alliances with mercenaries and pirates. Mandragall followed Kressh's plan word for word: eventually, three-quarters of his forces were independent operators, and he achieved significant military success against his opponents.

Mandragall knew more about the Sith of previous eras than his rivals did. Due to the fact that he allowed his forces to retain autonomy, many independent operators fleeing from enslavement by other Sith Lords were willing to fight for Mandragall.

Mandragall was mentioned in the novel Knight Errant, which was written by John Jackson Miller and published in 2011.

Mantessa Chekkat was a Kuranu female inventor. She and her daughter, Klerin, attended the Republic Fair on the planet Valo, hiring the mercenary Ty Yorrick to protect them. Chekkat intended to offer to sell the prototype of a recainium-powered four-seven nullifier, a device that disrupted energy weapons, including blasters and lightsabers, to Senator Tia Toon for his Defense Force Program. Toon refused to buy the device, having both Chekkat and Yorrick imprisoned for the inventor bringing an illegal substance onto the world. The two managed to escape after Nihil marauders attacked the Republic Fair, and Chekkat located Klerin, parting ways with Yorrick in an attempt to escape Valo. However, the elder Chekkat was killed by a hragscythe that had escaped from the Lonisa City Zoo.

A male Jedi warrior served as the Master of the Zabrak Padawan Maris Brood, teaching her aboard the starship Gray Pilgrim. Stationed in the Outer Rim Territories at the end of the Clone Wars in 19 BBY, he and Brood did not fall victim to Order 66, which saw many Jedi killed. Feeling the deaths of many of his comrades in the Force, the Master took a starfighter and set off to find out what had happened, never to return again.

A male Jedi warrior served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the Republic's waning days. The Jedi was the Master of the Zabrak Padawan Maris Brood, whom he tutored aboard the starship Gray Pilgrim. during the closing stages of the Clone Wars between the Republic's clone trooper army and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, the Jedi and Brood were stationed in the Outer Rim Territories. Because of that, they were not affected by Order 66, which dictated that the Republic's clone troopers kill their Jedi Generals. However, Brood's Master felt ripples in the Force caused by the deaths of other Jedi. After all of his transmissions to the Jedi Temple on the galactic capital of Coruscant were met with silence, the Jedi warrior took his personal starfighter and set off to find out what had happened. He discovered that the Jedi Order had been nearly exterminated by the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader and relayed this information to Brood. However, he was not seen or heard from again after that. Seeking revenge, Brood began to search for Vader, but was soon found herself by Jedi Master Shaak Ti. Ti took the young Zabrak as her apprentice and spirited her away to the planet Felucia, where they sought refuge with the native Jungle Felucian species.

Maris Brood's Master was known as a Jedi warrior, indicating that his talents laid in battle. However, he also had a deep connection to the Force, able to sense the deaths of his Jedi brethren. He was a capable pilot and possessed his own starfighter.

Maris Brood's Master was first mentioned in Brood's databank entry in the Star Wars: The Force Unleashed video game, which was released on September 16, 2008. The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia, and in Maris Brood's entry in the now-defunct Databank on StarWars.com.

Mas Missur was a Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, Mas Missur achieved the rank of Jedi Master by the end of the Separatist Crisis that plagued the Galactic Senate. When the Clone Wars erupted between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Master Missur took up the rank of Jedi General in the newly created Grand Army of the Republic, leading clone troopers against the Separatist Droid Army on several fronts.

When the Republic incited a rebellion on the planet Gaftikar, Master Missur was assigned to lead the Acclamator-class assault ship Leveler to the world to provide support against a CIS invasion. Assisting the Marit population, Missur and the 35th Infantry were successful in securing the planet's mineral wealth for the planet.

Maser voice-streams, also known as the Oswaft language, were the communications medium and weapons of the Oswaft species.

Their language was complex and highly sophisticated, with communication being performed by modulating radio-frequency waves with their brains. The vacuum-breathers were also able to "speak" a picture-message intended to convey visual reality rather than pure ideas.

Oswaft were able to employ this type of communication in the form of maser bolt. They referred to this as "shouting" at their opponent. The Oswaft were capable of destroying Imperial fighters in a single "shout", and could also destroy unshielded starships. However, maser voice-streams were generally ineffective against capital ship shielding.

Maximian Ajax was a human male who served as a grenadier and sergeant in the Rebel Alliance during its war against the Galactic Empire. He was a member of the Thirty-Second Infantry before the group was obliterated. Ajax then became a part of the Alliance's 61st Mobile Infantry, nicknamed Twilight Company. During the Alliance's Mid Rim Offensive, which began around 1 ABY, he served with the company on the planet Bamayar, where he and another soldier named Twitch helped to capture the Chenodra port.

In 3 ABY, after Imperial Governor Everi Chalis defected to Twilight Company, Ajax spoke unfavorably about the new guest with several other soldiers over a game of cards aboard the company's CR90 corvette, the Thunderstrike. Ajax also took part in Twilight Company's campaign on the planet Coyerti, in which he and a number of other rebels faced an AT-ST walker until the Coyerti natives came to their aid. Ajax later led a squad during a raid on an Imperial freighter, where they set up a choke point in a main passageway. However, during their withdrawal from the freighter, Ajax and his squad were backed into a corner by Imperial stormtroopers, who killed the grenadier while the rest of the group was rescued.

Maximian Ajax served as a grenadier in the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War against the Galactic Empire, eventually rising to the rank of sergeant. Initially a member of the Alliance's Thirty-Second Infantry, he was one of five survivors after the unit was obliterated in an event that resulted in the death of over 400 members of the infantry group.

Ajax then joined the Alliance's 61st Mobile Infantry, better known as Twilight Company, although he continued to wear the Thirty-Second Infantry's "Bleeding Roughneck" badge. When the company fought on the Mid Rim Bamayar during the Alliance's Mid Rim campaign, Ajax and another soldier named Twitch helped to secure the port of Chenodra, but their actions during the battle led Twitch to believe that she was responsible for a bad mistake.

Maxine Baytor was once a general in the Galactic Republic, during which time she participated in the Battle of Denubba. Shortly after Palpatine's declaration of a New Order, she led a group of retired troops, known collectively as the Renegade Legionnaires, against the Galactic Empire. Baytor managed to escape to Tatooine, where she spent her time collecting rumors about the former members of her company. This led her to find other tidbits of information on the Imperials, which she sold to the local syndicate. Although she was not proud of doing this, she would rather sell the information than starve on the streets. Baytor was only one of many informants working for the syndicate. By the time of the Galactic Civil War, she had become a weathered woman with gentle creases in her face, and her once brown hair had started to gain gray shots.

Sometime during the war, however, the Empire believed that some of her former soldiers were in fact moles working for the Rebellion. Because of this, they tasked the local police forces of Tatooine to imprison Maxine. A group of Rebels discovered that she had been captured and were asked by a local to rescue her. To accomplish this, they met in a cantina with Verral Kayrell, a mechanic at the police station. They made a deal with him where they would acquire a Natrilux conductor relay in exchange for him leaving the garage door to the station unlocked. Soon after this the group was approached by a Wookiee working for the local syndicate named Nilwoon who offered them 15,000 credits if they gave Maxine to him, although the group turned him down. Though stormtroopers were assigned to the police station, the group managed to free Maxine. After this they had a fight on their hands to get off planet but eventually managed to escape and delivered Maxine to a Rebel Alliance base. Maxine then decided to reform the Renegade Legionnaires to work for the Rebel Alliance, and invited the group who had rescued her to meet with them. Though they were not as young as they had once been, they still had much to contribute to the Alliance.

The Mayhem was an Imperial EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate serving as an escort to the Relentless.

The Mayhem was the ship to receive a convoy consisting of 3 BFF-1 bulk freighters; Strider, Treader and Walker near Cificap VIII. One of the freighters, the Walker, contained Habassa slaves, which was why Rebel operations rescued them before the Mayhem could arrive to convince the Habassa to join the Rebel Alliance.

Much later, the Habassa had joined the Alliance. In order to destroy the Relentless, Rebels and Habassa agreed to lure the frigate somewhere in order to capture her.

Having two CR90 corvettes, Filve and Bilbringi meet somewhere for an officers' meeting, and letting the information 'leak' with a known Imperial spy, Mayhem came to disrupt the meeting.

The Melida were a group that inhabited Melida/Daan in the Cadavine sector alongside the Daan. When the Melida took the leader of the Daan captive, a Republic senator and his eighteen year old son, Axel Greylark, embarked on a diplomatic mission with the Jedi Order to negotiate for the release of the leader. The mission however, was a trap to show all of the Daan's allies what would happen to those that helped them. During the extraction there was an explosion that buried the senator under rubble, but as the Melida were coming, a Jedi Knight pulled an injured Greylark away, forcing him to leave his father to die. Greylark told the Jedi Gella Nattai about the incident.

In the current Star Wars canon, the Melida were first mentioned in the 2022 novel The High Republic: Convergence by Zoraida Córdova.

Melo Centris was a female human, who worked as a bounty hunter during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

Centris was force-sensitive and used the Force to enhance her bounty hunting skills. She took a bounty from the Hutts to kill Jarid DeBell, a former Jedi who had incurred their wrath. DeBell was going to be marrying Senator Lavina Durada-Vashne Wren on the planet Cularin, so Centris traveled to the Cularin system. She arrived in Tolea Biqua on the gas planet Genarius, where a group of Devaronians persuaded her to let them work for her. She sent the Devaronians to acquire some cake baking materials, which she used to bake a poisoned cake. She then infiltrated the wedding in disguise as an usher and planned for DeBell to consume the cake. However, the Heroes of Cularin realized what she was planning to do and they thwarted her plans.

During the Clone Wars, Centris attempted to release a virus into the atmosphere of the planet Caarimon, in an attempt to kill off its native species, the Caarites.

Melvosh Bloor was a young Kalkal professor in Investigative Politico-Sociology from Beshka University who tried to interview Jabba Desilijic Tiure.

In the wake of Ra Yasht and Skarten's book Torture Observed: An Interview with Jabba's Cook, Bloor proposed to the university that he would interview Jabba, but his superior, Professor P'tan, stole the idea and did it himself. When P'tan failed to return from Jabba's palace, the University sent Bloor to investigate. Bloor went on his own, deciding to continue with his original plans. He made arrangements with Lady Valarian to meet with a contact of hers, Darian Gli who had also helped Ya Rasht and Scartan.

When Bloor arrived at Jabba's palace, he was greeted by Salacious B. Crumb. Impersonating Darian Gli, Crumb told Bloor that P'tan had been fed to the sarlacc. Bloor was led to Jabba, who found the idea of an interview laughable. However he consented to an interview with the requirement that Bloor make him laugh. Bloor failed, telling a joke Jabba had apparently already heard, and was fed to the rancor. As Bloor screamed, Jabba responded, "And I've heard that one before too."

Mess Boulanger was a male Human who served in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars as a quartermaster. Boulanger participated in the Battle of Praesitlyn, providing logistical support to the liberation of the Republic's Intergalactic Communications Center from a Separatist occupation force.

During the Clone Wars in 22 BBY, the male Human Mess Boulanger was assigned to the post of quartermaster within a Republic military expedition dispatched to Praesitlyn, where a Republic listening post had come under attack from a Separatist taskforce led by Admiral Pors Tonith. Traveling to Praesitlyn with a clone trooper detachment under the command of Jedi Master and General Nejaa Halcyon, Boulanger meticulously planned and prepared the necessary supplies well in advance of battle and thoroughly briefed Commander Anakin Skywalker on the importance of logistics.

While on Praesitlyn during the Republic incursion, Boulanger encountered Zozridor Slayke, the leader of a pro-Republic splinter group that had been fighting against the Separatist occupation force. Slayke mistook Boulanger for the General in charge of the relief effort, prompting Boulanger to indicate Commander Skywalker as a more suitable contact. As the fighting intensified, Boulanger took charge of the supply chain, directing the transports carrying provisions to and from Praesitlyn and having several troopships modified to serve as cargo carriers to deal with the sheer amount of supplies, which Boulanger and his staff had planned to last for the estimated week needed to unseat Tonith's grip on the communications facility. Despite the quartermaster's best efforts, persistent attacks from Tonith's forces meant that Boulanger's shuttles had to negotiate ever more hazardous conditions to land on Praesitlyn, resulting in many of the ships being destroyed.

Mess Boulanger was a logistician at heart; his dedication to ensuring that the Republic expedition to Praesitlyn was adequately supplied was absolute, and he took great pride in informing others of that fact, espousing the use of the acronym COMETS-Q to help remind others of what a military force needed to function adequately. As a quartermaster specialising in the supply and support of an organic army, Boulanger was disdainful of battle droids, though he freely admitted that managing provisions for droids, such as spare parts and lubricants, also counted as logistics. An older male Human, Boulanger had a pot belly, blue eyes and a drooping brown mustache.

Metron Besk was the founder of Dynamic Automata, a droid-manufacturing company. Besk built the company from a single firm that supplied logic-enhancement circuits to third-degree droids. Eventually, he began supplying the Empire with advanced droid circuitry aboard Sector Plexus droid vessels and Viper probe droids.

Besk was a suspicious man and grew tired of the backstabbing and bickering among his company's partners. Before his death, Besk carefully divided the company's power among them so that they would all have to answer to his daughter, Elta Besk. Besk trained his daughter in corporate and armed warfare and handed control of Dynamic Automata over to her.

Milessa Arranda was born and raised on Alderaan, and married Kalf Arranda. Milessa and Kalf eventually raised two children, Tash and Zak. In 0 BBY, she and her husband sent their children away from their world for what was intended to be a brief vacation. During the children's absence, Milessa was killed along with every other person on the planet, when Grand Moff Tarkin used the Death Star to destroy Alderaan as an example of Imperial might.

Mill Alibeth was a Force-sensitive Zabrak female who served as a Jedi Initiate in the late Republic Era. Alibeth possessed powerful empathic powers which she found difficult to control, resulting in her experiencing severe nausea whenever she was exposed to anything relating to combat or violence, even mere discussion of the subject. After attempting to cut herself off from the Force, she discovered that her unique connection could be used to provide medical and spiritual assistance to wounded Jedi fighting in the Clone Wars.

Alibeth and her friend Vivert Stag were among those in the Jedi Order that survived the Great Jedi Purge and were able to remain undetected. The pair took up the life of supposed bounty hunters, coming to work alongside hunter Mwarr Ja'Randa.

Mill Alibeth was a Jedi Initiate around the time of the First Battle of Geonosis in 22 BBY. She was a part of an Initiate Clan of eight younglings including friend Vivert Stag. While the rest of the Clan was excited for their upcoming trip to Ilum for The Gathering, Alibeth was overcome with intense feelings of nausea over the recent increase in violence across the galaxy. Although she did a good job faking it for the others, she could not bring herself to be excited at the prospect of building a lightsaber. No one could explain why her particularly connection to the Force worked this way, but Alibeth was becoming increasingly miserable. She eventually resorted to pushing away the Force entirely, something in direct conflict with her Jedi teachings.

The day before Alibeth's clan were set to fly to Ilum, Cato Neimoidia, the Purse World of the Trade Federation, was hit by a bombing, capturing the attention of most of the Temple's adults. This only increased Alibeth's growing suffering since she felt the impending war on the horizon.

Mind Walking was the process in which Mind Walkers entered and remained in the realm they called "beyond shadows." Through a specific type of meditation, their consciousnesses entered beyond shadows and left their bodies behind. The technique was learned by Jacen Solo during his five year sojourn following the Yuuzhan Vong War, and several years later by Luke and Ben Skywalker, who were retracing Solo's steps to find out what had caused his fall to the dark side. Soon after, in 44 ABY, the Skywalkers allied with the Lost Tribe of Sith for a mission to eliminate Abeloth. After traveling to Abeloth's homeworld in the Maw, the Skywalkers, along with Sith High Lord Sarasu Taalon, Sith Saber Gavar Khai, and Captain Leeha Faal, Mind Walked beyond shadows in an attempt to locate Abeloth. Skywalker would Mind Walk one more time in an attempt to stop Abeloth. Additionally, Luke was joined by Darth Krayt in this state, who allied himself with Luke in order to have the united power to overcome Abeloth.

The Mining Worlds referred to four planets—all located in the Anoat sector of the galaxy's Outer Rim Territories—that were known for their abundance of mineral resources. Burnin Konn was considered to be a Mining World, though centuries-long mining operations to harvest its chromium and dolovite destroyed the planet's indigenous plant life and created a nearly uninhabitable wasteland. During the Iron Blockade, which was established by a remnant of the Galactic Empire in an attempt to prevent news of their crushing defeat by the Alliance to Restore the Republic at the Battle of Endor from reaching the Anoat sector's populace, the Imperials locked down the Mining Worlds, capturing every transport that attempted to pass through the blockade.

The Smuggler sent several members of their crew to liberate the ships and their cargo from the Empire.

The Mining Worlds were originally created for the Star Wars Legends web article "Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin," which was written by Jason Fry, Daniel Wallace and Craig Robert Carey for Wizards of the Coast and released in 2004. They became canon when they appeared in the mobile game Star Wars: Uprising, which was developed by Kabam for iOS and Android platforms and released in 2015.

Brought into the Jedi Order early in his life, Beldun was trained at the experimental Almas Academy in the Cularin system as opposed to the academy within the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. After training one-on-one with a Jedi Master and passing his Trials of Knighthood, Beldun was elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight.

In 31 BBY, Beldun was sent to the Jedi enclave in the city Gadrin, on the planet Cularin by the Almas Academy. Ordered to represent the Almas Academy during the celebrations for Cularin's 200th anniversary since it was colonized, Beldun was to ensure that the Padawans in attendance were acting appropriately and where they needed to be. He also spoke to several Masters, directing them towards Initiates in need of a master.

The Monarch was an Imperial Star Destroyer, commanded by Captain Averen and serving under Director of Imperial Intelligence Ysanne Isard. It was one of two ships left to defend Imperial Center against the impending New Republic invasion. It surrendered and was eventually added to the New Republic fleet.

The Monarch class was never specified, but well before the battle, Admiral Ackbar stated that approximately seven Victory-class star destroyers were on station defending Imperial Center. It was also stated that both sides' Star Destroyers traded missiles during the battle, something Imperial-class Star Destroyers did not have, lending more credibility to the ship being a Victory-class Star Destroyer.

Although tasked with the defense of Imperial Center, the Monarch was not known for its illustrious reputation or crew. As a result, Isard chose it to defend the planet during the Seizure of Coruscant along with the Star Destroyer Triumph, which had a similarly unimpressive reputation.

Isard wanted Coruscant to fall to the Rebel hands so that the New Republic would find its bacta resources devastated by an outbreak of the krytos virus. Therefore, it is likely Isard knew the Monarch and Triumph would be either captured or destroyed during the battle. She essentially left them for dead, choosing to instead relocate the superior Star Destroyers Emperor's Will and Imperator.

Morga Bunna was a male Bosph who lived during the reign of the New Republic. Bunna worked as a bounty hunter, but later retired and established a depot on one of the moons of the planet Bosph, which served as a cache point for illicit items.

In 19 ABY, supplies of the spice Tempest were stored in Bunna's facility by the Hutt crime lord Mika Anjiliac Chiera. Bunna had the Tempest removed after the Jedi archivist Mander Zuma and the spacers Reen Irana and Eddey Be'ray began shutting down the Tempest trade. Bunna's depot was later raided by Zumma and the Jedi's Corporate Sector Authority arrived moments later, and Bunna was forced to surrender to them. Bunna shared his knowledge of the Tempest trade with Zuma and in return for his honesty, the Jedi Master instructed the CSA to not detain the Bosph.

Morga Bunna was a male Bosph who lived during the era of the New Republic. After making a living as a bounty hunter and traveling across the galaxy, Bunna retired and set up a depot on the outermost moon of the Bosph homeworld for storing stolen goods. The small moon was desolate and far from the planet Bosph, and Bunna's facility served both as a place for criminals to cache illicit goods and a trading post for individuals who wished to sell their wares without meeting buyers face to face. To protect the anonymity of Bunna's customers, all deliveries to his depot were arranged through blind drops with shipping schedules changing regularly. Over time, Bunna burrowed through moon to expand his depot and he built a number of halls, passages, storage rooms, as well as a translucent pleasure dome along one side.

Around 19 ABY, Bunna agreed to a number of contracts to store Tempest, a new potent form of spice produced by the Hutt crime lord Mika Anjiliac Chiera that left users prone to violent fits of rage. However, after the Jedi archivist Mander Zuma began disrupting the Tempest supply chain across Hutt Space and the Corporate Sector in an attempt to trace the source of the spice, Bunna sent on all of the Tempest stored at his depot and refused to accept any more shipments of the spice.

During the war, following the capture and enslavement of most the crew of a Republic military exploration ship on the Unknown Regions planet O'reen, Jedi General Morningfire led the clone troopers of Vornskr Company on a rescue mission to O'reen, which led to the death of the planet's ruling Magnus. Due to the Magnus' death, O'reen was eventually quarantined by the Galactic Senate in an attempt to control the planet's population, and to stop it from sharing military secrets and resources to the Confederacy.

Morningfire was mentioned in The Unknown Regions, a hardcover supplement for the Star Wars Saga Edition roleplaying game, written by Sterling Hershey, Rodney Thompson, and Daniel Wallace, Morningfire was created as a reference to freelance game designer Jonathan Stevens' fan character and forum handle, Donovan Morningfire, making it one of the few fanon elements in the Star Wars Legends continuity.

Mourne Blee was a male Twi'lek, who worked for the company Uniformal Attire during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

Blee worked for Uniformal Attire, a company that specialized in developing commercial uniforms. He wanted to become a fashion designer, so only planned to work for Uniformal Attire until he had saved up enough money to open a fashion house of his own. In 32 BBY, Uniformal Attire developed a new uniform for security staff of the pharmaceutical company Culpharm, so Blee was sent to be Uniformal's representative at the Culpharm Headquarters Building in the city Hedrett.

Blee disliked working for Uniformal Attire, as he believed that designing uniforms was very mundane and was almost embarrassed by the fact that he worked for them. He was particularly unenthusiastic about the uniform that was developed for Culpharm.

The mouth-operated gun was a ranged weapon intended for operation by the Laboi, a species of limbless mammals native to the planet Laboi II. The mouth-operated weapon required no hands to fire and was useful to Laboi who left their homeworld for the greater galaxy. Nevertheless, such technology was incredibly rare and extremely expensive; during the Galactic Civil War, it cost at least ten times the price of a comparable hand-operated weapon.

The second edition of Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races mentions the mouth-operated gun as a possible piece of equipment for Laboi characters in West End Games's Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game. The book, updated by Chuck Truett from the original edition by Troy Denning, marks the first mention of such technology. The source fails to specify whether such weapons used blaster technology, slugthrower technology, or something else.

Movac Arisster was a Human male from Lorrd City. He had a dark-haired mustache and beard, weighed 150 kilos, was well muscled, and had considered a career in wrestling. However, he became a university professor, getting a tenure with the University of Pangalactic Cultural Studies.

Arisster studied how literary cycles from different planets became merged as they entered the galactic community. He specialized in the various myths of Aayla Secura. In 40 ABY, he got an incurable form of cancer and only had six months to live. It was then that he saw a vision of Aayla (in reality a projection of Lumiya) telling him to enter himself in a mythical cycle by killing a Jedi.

Arisster took a number of people hostage at the Lorrd Academy for Aquatic Studies, and demanded that the world's Jedi show up. When Jacen Solo refused to negotiate with him, Jacen having no other option detonated Arisster's suicide bomb, killing him and his Human shield, Serom Haxan, to prevent Arisster from taunting the Jedi for their helplessness and killing other hostages with a blaster as the day went on.

However, Artoo discovered his true identity and was able to keep Brattakin occupied long enough for him to be shot by Jace Forno, his former henchwoman who objected to a droid giving her orders, even if it had a Human brain.

Moy-Ran Bostt was a man living on the same planet as the farm belonging to Armo Drane and his wife, Tso Sook Drane. Before Armo was sent to a detention moon via the Imperial prison barge Purge for committing a crime, Bostt was paid back money by the family with the profits from their farm season. In the post-post-script of a letter to Tso, to be delivered by a guard from Purge named Wembly, Armo warned his wife that Bostt was a piker and may try and swindle her into paying the money to him again. The letter was recovered aboard Purge after its occupants were decimated by a plague so it is unlikely that it reached her before it was released to the public for academic purposes in relation to the history of Purge.

The mutiny on the Advent was an incident that occurred in 48 BBY aboard the Advent, a cargo freighter tasked with delivering food to a famine stricken star system. During the mutiny, the head Jedi in charge of protecting the ship, Rael Averross, decided to confront the mutineers alongside his Padawan Nim Pianna in the cargo bay of the Advent as opposed to following normal procedure and retaking control of the bridge of the ship. The skirmish in the cargo bay between the mutineers and the two Jedi resulted in Pianna's death when she was hit by a slicer dart which caused her to briefly turn on her Master, forcing him to kill her with his lightsaber.

By the end of the mutiny, all mutineers were either defeated or arrested. Upon return to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, Averross was put on trial by the Jedi High Council who ruled that his actions were necessary to save the lives of the passengers of the Advent. After the trial, Averross was sent on an eight year assignment to mentor the planet's Princess Fanry, an assignment which he put all his energy in to to atone for his apprentice's death.

The mutiny on the Advent first appeared in a hologram in Master & Apprentice, a 2019 novel written by Claudia Gray.

Myk Bidlor was a Human male who served as the leader of the team of forensic specialists hired by Durga to perform a thorough autopsy on Aruk's corpse.

During the Galactic Civil War, Myk Bidlor served as a loyal forensic expert to the Galactic Empire, where he worked on Coruscant until he was recruited by Durga Besadii Tai. Myk and his team examined the corpse of Durga's father and searched for evidence from the murder. During the investigation, Bidlor reported frequently to Durga about the progress. Finally, they found a trace of poison, but they couldn't classify it. Durga urged them to continue.

Later, the researchers traced the poison to the planet Malkii and named the rare toxin X-1. Myk also discovered that X-1 was very expensive and that it should be administered over a long period. Thus Durga still had no clear evidence, and the researchers continued their work after Durga gave Bidlor a large payment in anticipation.

Myk Bidlor is a Tuckerization of Mike Beidler, a Star Wars military tech advisor and continuity editor.

Myra Chimor was set to appear in the comic story "Squad Goals, Part One," which was published in Star Wars Adventures (2020) 11 on October 20, 2021.

Myrran Swimmer's Club was an athletic club that existed in Myrra the capital city of the Outer Rim Territories planet Akiva.

The club was forced to define a no-go zone for training in the western edge of the Great Basin due to increased Hutt Clan activity in 3 ABY At the time a member of the club named Kin Shiff died. The club set out a notice of this news and stressed that the untimely death of Kin Shiff was not related to the Hutt activity. A copy of the notice was kept on a datapad in the Hutt Cartel District of Myrra during 3 ABY.

Myrran Swimmer's Club was mentioned in a datapad in the 2024 Massive Entertainment video game Star Wars Outlaws published by Ubisoft.

Na'daz was a male Twi'lek Sith Lord who lived near the end of the New Sith Wars who was exceptionally skilled in the art of lightsaber combat. While on a visit to Nal Hutta, Na'daz found the young Force-sensitive Twi'lek slave Kas'im and bought him. Na'daz brought the young boy to the Outer Rim planet of Ryloth and trained him as his apprentice. In 1010 BBY, Na'daz was challenged by his apprentice in a lightsaber duel and slain. Kas'im later gave Na'daz's lightsaber to his pupil, Bane.

Na'daz was a male Twi'lek Sith Lord who lived during the final years of the New Sith Wars. He was a skilled combatant with a curved-hilt lightsaber. Later during his life, Na'daz traveled to the Mid Rim world Nal Hutta and discovered a young, Force-sensitive Twi'lek slave named Kas'im. Na'daz bought the boy and took him to the Outer Rim planet Ryloth, where he trained him as his Sith apprentice.

By 1010 BBY, Kas'im had become stronger in the Force and more skilled in lightsaber combat than his Master, and he challenged Na'daz in a duel. Na'daz was defeated and killed by his pupil, who took Na'daz's lightsaber as a trophy. Kas'im eventually became one of the greatest lightsaber duelists of his time and trained many young Sith at the Sith Academy on Korriban. Kas'im later gave Na'daz's lightsaber to his student, Bane, who eventually became a Dark Lord of the Sith after defeating his rival apprentice, Sirak.

Na'daz was considered to be a great Sith Lord by his apprentice, Kas'im, and was a skilled lightsaber duelist—a trait he passed on to his apprentice. Na'daz used a curved-hilt, red-bladed lightsaber in combat, which his apprentice took after killing Na'daz. Na'daz also taught Kas'im how to use a double-bladed lightsaber.

Nalia Adollu was a female Human Jedi Padawan from the Expansion Region planet Corsin. Following the Battle of Ruusan in 1000 BBY, Adollu was chosen to be the Padawan of the Pyn'gani Jedi Master Anno Wen-Chii. For at least five years, since 995 BBY, Adollu and her Master resided on Wen-Chii's homeworld of Polus. In 990 BBY, the Sith Lord Darth Zannah used Adollu's name and persona to sneak into the Jedi Temple on Coruscant in order to research information for her Master, Darth Bane.

Adollu was born around 1010 BBY In 990 BBY, while Adollu was still on Polus, her identity was used by the Sith Lord Darth Zannah, who infiltrated the Jedi Temple on Coruscant in order to find information regarding the parasitic orbalisk organisms that plagued her Master, Darth Bane. Zannah carried out her mission successfully, as Adollu had not been seen on Coruscant for five years.

An athletic, Force-sensitive Human female of average height, Adollu had long black hair. She possessed enough Force potential to be accepted as a Jedi Padawan and trained for at least five years under Master Wen-Chii.

Nalia Adollu was first mentioned in the 2007 novel Darth Bane: Rule of Two, written by Drew Karpyshyn. She later received an entry in The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia.

The Namrelllew was a Wookiee starship which carried Republic Senator Padmé Amidala and her Head of Security Captain Gregar Typho on an undercover mission to Hebekrr Minor in 22 BBY, during the first weeks of the Clone Wars.

By the beginning of the Clone Wars in 22 BBY, the Namrelllew was already old. However, it was very well built due to its Wookiee construction and design. Its air-filtration systems in particular were noticeably superior to those that could be manufactured on Naboo, producing recycled air without any particulates and which smelled almost fresh.

The ship was luxurious, although it could seem unusual to human passengers due to its Wookiee-centric design. For example, its beds were very long, it had full-body hot-air dryers instead of towels, and some adult humans needed to use a stool to reach the back of the sinks in the refreshers. Captain Typho stated that its cabins were larger than any barracks he had lived in. The control panels on the flight deck that were within easy reach for a Wookiee would have required a human to stretch to their limits. The hull of the ship was made of cool metal, which vibrated slightly while traveling through hyperspace.

The Namrelllew was co-captained by a husband and wife team of Wookiees: Naijoh, the pilot, and Rayyne, who served as the ship's navigator. They were described as a perfect team, each relying on the other's talents for a safe arrival and never doubting their skill. Idda was a Mriss engineer on board, and G-1FY served as the ship's protocol droid.

Nanda-Ree Janoo was a Jedi Knight who served the Jedi Order during the final years of the Galactic Republic. Janoo was made a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars, serving alongside such esteemed Jedi as Master Obi-Wan Kenobi.

A Force-sensitive being, Nanda-Ree Janoo was a member of the Jedi Order, which taught Janoo the ways of the Force. After passing the Trials of Knighthood, Janoo was elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight.

When the Clone Wars erupted across the galaxy between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Janoo became a General within the ranks of the Grand Army of the Republic. At some point during the conflict, Janoo was assigned to work with Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi in leading a task force to the planet of Balamak in order to destroy an experimental communications jamming array. During the battle above the world, Janoo piloted a starfighter against the CIS fleet. After fellow Jedi Anakin Skywalker destroyed the array, the Republic forces returned to Coruscant.

Sometime after the Battle of Yavin, Balrekk and his company were sent to serve under General Vorrel in an attack on a Rebel base built on the planet Arda I.

He worked for Vago the Hutt and the Anjiliac kajidic along with a number of his clan during the reign of the Galactic Empire.

Narra was a Lambda-class T-4a shuttle used by Wraith Squadron during the campaign against Warlord Zsinj.

The shuttle was originally used by a former Imperial officer turned smuggler, but was later captured and renamed by the Rebel Alliance. The vessel was largely stock, with the addition of a sophisticated electronically shielded secret smuggling compartment, similar to other smuggler's ships, such as the Millennium Falcon. The compartment was at least big enough to fit an adult Gamorrean, as well as parts for a jury rigged laser cannon.

The smuggling compartment was used as the body for the Lunatic, a makeshift boarding craft piloted by Voort saBinring during the capture of the Night Caller and was reinstalled after. This feature was also used to hide Grinder during the mission to Revos on Storinal and by Castin Donn to sneak aboard the Iron Fist.

Naytha Alutana was a female Twi'lek escort who lived during the waning years of the Galactic Republic. Alutana began life as a slave; she was eventually purchased from a slaving pen by Thurm Loogg, a senior Metatheran Cartel official, and she entered the service of the Cartel. In about 31 BBY, Loogg sent Alutana to act as an escort for Merik Darou, the assistant of Lavina Wren, the senator of the Cularin system, as part of a plan developed by Loogg to put the senator into his debt. Alutana spent some time with Darou on the planet Cularin, and she was with him when he entered a coma as a result of consuming some tainted ryll. The Twi'lek immediately called some private medical personnel and ensured that they took care of Darou, then traveled to a Cartel officer-cruiser to report to Loogg on Darou's condition.

Lavina Wren hired the Heroes of Cularin, a group of local freelance agents, to track down the drug dealer from which Darou had purchased the tainted ryll, and the agents flew to the officer-cruiser to meet with Alutana. Loogg and the Twi'lek met with the agents in Loogg's personal office, and Loogg agreed to allow Alutana to assist the agents with their investigation. She then provided them with the address of Kelkan D'vrosh, the dealer who had sold the ryll to Darou.

Despite being forced into slavery, Alutana was genuinely helpful and willing to serve others. However, she was fiercely loyal to Loogg due to the fact that he had rescued her from slavery, so she was only willing to help the freelance agents once Loogg had directed her to do so.

Neer was a Sith Lord who was active He crafted a gauntlet as an anonymous gift to send to a powerful Jedi who served as the Jedi Watchman of the Corbos system. The Jedi had lost friends during the conflicts with the Sith, and when he received the gauntlet, he immediately appreciated the power of the gauntlet.

Neer was first mentioned in the new Star Wars canon in Nexus of Power, a 2016 Fantasy Flight Games supplement book for the Star Wars Forces of Destiny roleplaying game.

Nerrethel was a Sith Lord of the reconstituted Sith Empire. Sometime between 3645 BBY and 3642 BBY, Nerrethel grew interested in the structure known as the Dark Heart on the planet Voss, and spent two years studying the structure, comparing its architecture to that of the ancient Sith of the planet Korriban and analyzing the Dark Heart's orientation relative to Voss's constellations. His only notes from the expedition were the words "It sees"—for he had encountered the entity Sel-Makor within the Dark Heart.

Neth Bralor was a Human male Mandalorian who lived during the time of the Second Galactic Civil War. In the year 40 ABY, Bralor attended a meeting of Mandalorian clan leaders on behalf of his clan at MandalMotors Hall in Keldabe, the capital city of the planet Mandalore. Along with several other chieftains, mercenaries, and heads of Mandalorian corporations, Bralor met with reigning Mand'alor Boba Fett to discuss the place of Mandalore and its people in the course of the galaxy's latest conflict between the Galactic Alliance and the Corellian-led Confederation. Amidst the discussions, Bralor raised his hoarse voice in support of Fett's proposal of neutrality in favor of concentrating on rebuilding Mandalore's infrastructure in the wake of the devastation dealt to the Mandalorian homeworld by the Yuuzhan Vong during their invasion of the galaxy.

Neth Bralor first appeared in Star Wars canon in the fifth novel of the Star Wars: Legacy of the Force series, Sacrifice, written by author Karen Traviss and published May 29, 2007.

Nicko was a Cargo ferry used by Airam pirates during the Galactic Civil War.

The Nicko, along with Lausbee were part of an Airam pirate raid to steal Imperial munitions and Warheads. What the they didn't know was that the convoy was "leaked" to the Airam by Imperial Intelligence as bait to lure Airam members into a trap. The Cargo ferries arrived and R-41 Starchasers from Jerrid Squadron helped disabled the BFF-1 bulk freighters (Convoy (BFF-1 bulk freighters), while T-wings from Claw Squadron were to provide starfighter support. However Imperial fighters such as Avenger Squadron broke through Claw Squadron and attacked both ships warning them to power down or be threatened to be destroyed. With both ferries surrendering Stormtrooper transports from Sigma were dispatched and the Nicko and Lausbee were captured, while their remaining fighters were eliminated, compromising the location of their base and leading to its subsequent destruction.

When questioned as to why, Nobil lectured Konshi on his lack of self-control, citing his recent comments to Senator Vuub as an example.

Nikil Nobil was mentioned in the 2010 novel The Old Republic: Fatal Alliance, written by Sean Williams as a tie-in to the then-upcoming 2011 video game Star Wars: The Old Republic by BioWare. Like many of the characters from the novel, which was written early in the game's development, Nobil has not been referenced in any other part of the game's multimedia project.

NM-KO 28 was a private shuttle stolen by Jacen and Jaina Solo during the latter's rescue of the former from the CorDuro Shipping office on the orbital city Bburru Station. They landed it at the Gateway refugee camp on Duro and were told by their mother, Leia Organa Solo, to use it to escape the Duro system prior to the impending Yuuzhan Vong attack, along with Randa Besadii Diori. The two of them refused to leave without Leia, or her Noghri bodyguard Olmahk. Jaina followed her mother's example in staying at the refugee camp and eventually loaded up NM-KO 28 with refugees and sent it away without Randa, her brother, Olmahk, or her mother when the initial Yuuzhan Vong invasion force, led by Warmaster Tsavong Lah, entered the system. Upon witnessing the Yuuzhan Vong's destruction of shuttles evacuating the orbital city Orr-Om, Jaina salved her moral qualms against stealing NM-KO 28 by speculating that the shuttle would have met a similar fate had she and Jacen left it on Bburru. The shuttle was equipped with a hyperdrive, and in Jacen's opinion, could accommodate four or five passengers.

By the time following the Battle of Yavin, Bok was captured by the Corellian slavers and enslaved in the Corellian Slaver Bunker near Tyrena. a spacer infiltrated the bunker to find evidence of the slaver operations for the Corellian Security Force. Noro Bok agreed to help the spacer to access to the lower levels of the bunker. Thanks to Bok's assistance, the spacer was able to explore all the areas of the bunker and eventually broadcasted the slavers' records on the CorSec emergency request channels.

Noro Bok was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, Noro Bok was added to the game with the update named "Chapter 1: The Corellian Captives," published on June 8, 2006.

His appearance was randomly generated during each server reset, but he consistently appeared as a male. Species he could appear as included, but were not necessarily limited to, Bothans and Bith.

Noshow was a group of 16 Delta-class JV-7 escort shuttles that originally belonged to the Rebel Alliance but were stolen by Imperial Special Forces.

Originally in the Rebel Alliance, the Empire stole the shuttles and brought them to an abandoned and forgotten Asteroid Hangar Iron Mine in the Talcim Cluster. They planned to use the shuttles to unleash biological warfare operations on Rebel sympathetic worlds as part of a frame up against the Alliance. However, the plan was complicated by a Rebel strike force consisting of X-wings, B-wings and A-wings on a hit and run strike against the facility. Noshow was launched with TIE Interceptors as fighter escort as a result and the Rebels changed priorities to destroying the shuttles as they inspected the shuttles and realized their intentions not wishing to let even one escape. TIE Avengers from Avenger Squadron and Assault Gunboats were also dispatched as they attacked the Rebel fighters from behind.

The outcome depends on which side the player takes.

Nova Whisper was a modified Lantillian ShipWrights GX1 Short Hauler with a checkered history and long list of owners. The original owner was a Corellian commodities shipper by the name of Tev Driscull. He soon lost it at Elshandruu Pica to a privateer named Dharus who upgraded the weaponry to have 2 concealed concussion missile launchers and replaced the forward firing laser cannon with an ion cannon. The ship also possessed military-grade sensors and terrain-following scanners in addition to 2 shielded smuggling compartments; one hidden in engineering and the other in the starboard repulsorlift.

The ship soon was captured by the Corellian Security Forces, also known as CorSec, who determined that the Nova Whisper would make an excellent ship for sting operations against smugglers and pirates since it was a legitimate smuggling craft. The ship was used in a joint CorSec-Imperial operation where it was once again stolen, this time by the pilot, Delt Nerris, who was an Alliance sympathizer.

The Nova Whisper was used by the Alliance forces on Asher III as a medical transport until the destruction of that Rebel cell just prior to the Battle of Hoth. The Imperials did not get their hands on the ship as it was filched by a Rodian arms merchant by the name of Lernik De'Yago who used it to escape the raid on the Alliance cell.

De'Yago coded a series of credit-account access numbers into the nav computer. Since De'Yago had lost the shipment of arms he had been delivering to the Alliance before he received payment he decided to recoup his losses. Accordingly he sold the Nova Whisper to a ship dealer on the merchant station Bazaar.

Novin Bress was a scientist at Binring Biomedical Product.

Bress was a Human male, with a lean build and greying hair. A member of the special operations division at Binring's facility on Saffalore, Bress was part of Project Chubar. After discovering the possibility of escaped test subjects, Warlord Zsinj called Bress and Edda Gast to Iron Fist to explain.

Doctor Gast calmly explained to Zsinj that it was feasible for test subjects to have escaped the explosion that Tuzin Gast set. Zsinj was angered, and set two blaster pistols before Bress and Gast as if to invite them to commit suicide.

Instead, Gast fired her pistol directly against Novin Bress's chest, killing him instantly and satisfying Zsinj.

Nysis Belzara was a male Bothan Jedi Knight who served the Jedi Order during the last years of the Galactic Republic. Around 31 BBY, Belzara greeted a starship arriving on the planet Coruscant that was transporting a Mandalorian iron box on behalf of the Jedi. The Bothan was subsequently killed in an ambush by the Believers, dark side cultists who sought to steal the vessel's cargo.

Nysis Belzara was a Force-sensitive Bothan male who served the Jedi Order during the latter years of the Galactic Republic, attaining the rank of Jedi Knight. Around 31 BBY, Jedi researchers discovered the Pulas, a powerful Sith artifact, on the planet Almas. To keep the relic out of the clutches of the Believers, a dark side cult who sought to steal it, the Jedi arranged to relocate the artifact to the galactic capital Coruscant for safe keeping. A fleet of ships was assembled to ferry the relic, with each vessel carrying a Mandalorian iron box, one of which contained the Pulas and the others acting as decoys. Belzara was tasked by the Jedi Council, the ruling body of the Jedi Order, with meeting one of the starships arriving on Coruscant and accompanying the crew and their Mandalorian iron box to a safe house.

The starship that Belzara was assigned to meet docked on a Coruscant landing platform and just as the crew were disembarking, the Bothan arrived to greet them. However, one of the ship's company the, Tarasin Es'Loma, was secretly in league with the Believers. The Tarasin pretended to fall from the edge of the platform, distracting Belzara and her fellow crew members, the Wookiee Wojarra and the Human San Herrera and Nia Reston, just as a Believer strike team attacked. Belzara was shot and killed in the ambush and the Believers seized the box that the ship had been transporting, which contained a fragment of the dark side-imbued city Conkesta. Moments later, the Jedi Knight Devan For'deschel and a group of spacers arrived at the landing platform; For'deschel recognized Belzara and contacted the Jedi Council to notify them of the Bothan's demise, while Wojarra provided the spacers an account of Belzara's death.

Nysis Belzara was created by Morrie Mullins and featured in the 2002 roleplaying adventure Coruscani Dawn, which formed part of the Living Force campaign and debuted at the fan convention Celebration II. Belzara's death takes place off-scene during the adventure and only his corpse appears directly in the roleplaying module.

enrichments.description:
Nystammall was a male Vuvrian Jedi Master serving the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

Brought to the Coruscant Jedi Temple after being identified as Force-sensitive, Nystammall entered into the Temple academy and began learning the ways of the Force. After graduating, he was selected by the Eirrauc Jedi Master Puroth to study as a Padawan. Traveling the galaxy together, Nystammall constructed a blue-bladed lightsaber for his personal use for the rest of his career. Master Puroth trained the young Vuvrian for years before recommending him to the Jedi High Council as ready to take his Trials of Knighthood. Passing the Trials presented to him, Nystammall was elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight by the High Council.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Nystammall and his former Master reported to Coruscant and took up the rank of General within the Grand Army of the Republic to combat the Separatist horde. Fighting valiantly throughout the war and earning the rank of Master, the Jedi pair were stationed at Tovarskl when the world was attacked by Confederacy General, the cyborg Grievous. The former Master-Padawan duo fought bravely against the General, but both were slain. Grievous took possession of Nystammall's lightsaber, carrying it as a trophy for the rest of the war. At the end of the war, Grievous wielded Nystammall and Puroth's weapons against Master Obi-Wan Kenobi on Utapau. While Kenobi was able to kill the Kaleesh cyborg, the weapons were never recovered.

During the occupation of the Twi'lek colony on the planet of Aaloth, the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Quellus, who served as an emissary of the Sith Empire, was dispatched to conquer the world and incorporate it to the Sith dominion within the galaxy. Utilizing the power of the dark side of the Force and his gauntlet, Darth Quellus extinguished all bonfires in the settlements that were previously employed to repel Aaloth's predatory creatures. Additionally he compelled the Twi'lek population to construct a stronghold, thereby solidifying his control and asserting his authority over the planet.

In response to the Sith Lord's oppressive rule, a resistance group emerged and engaged in numerous battles against him. Despite thier efforts, the attack on the stronghold ultimately proved unsuccessful. Compelled to yield to Darth Quellus' authority, the Twi'leks reluctantly returned to their villages. However, hope was reignited when the elder Silana devised pouches containing flammable materials and distribured them to the rebellious Twi'leks. Unfortunately, her actions were discovered, and she was captured with the intention of being executed by Darth Quellus. Learing of this imminent threat, the Twi'leks rallied once more, launching a daring assault on again the stronghold. Their concentrated efforts resulted in a massive fire that forced Darth Quellus to retreat Aaloth, abandoning his hold over the planet.

Odair Bel-Opis was a human male from the planet Corellia who served as the attaché to Grand Moff Lozen Tolruck during the Imperial occupation of Kashyyyk in the months following the Battle of Endor.

Odair Bel-Opis served as Lozen Tolruck's attaché on the Grand Moff's island fortress on Kashyyyk. They ambushed Jom Barell's commando team attempting to capture a shuttle platform, and captured Barell, taking his eye.

During the Wookiee insurgency, Bel-Opis counseled Tolruck to remain within his fortress, despite the Grand Moff's desire to hunt the natives. He and Tolruck confronted Sinjir Rath Velus when the double-agent arrived in the fortress in the guise of Imperial officer Jorrin Turnbull. Odair fought Sinjir hand-to-hand while Tolruck's followers watched and cheered, and bested the New Republic agent with a choke hold. However, Rath Velus was able to disrupt the Imperial control module, resulting in a prison break. Odair attempted to kill Sinjir, but was attacked by an escaped Wookiee who struck him across the head with a saw blade. Falling, Odair was straddled by the Wookiee, and screamed as the beast ripped off his arms.

As the personal attaché to Grand Moff Lozen Tolruck, Odair Bel-Opis was a capable and trustworthy individual. Organized and straightforward, Bel-Opis had no designs on Tolruck's position, making him ideal as a servant. He proved himself to be a brutal and merciless killer, and Tolruck considered him as necessary and simple as a club. While on Kashyyyk Bel-Opis grew dark, patchy stubble over his face, reflecting his untamed environment.

Oland Barsha was a human male member of the Barsha family, serving as an executive board member for the Barsha Corporation on their executive board.

During the official ceremony for the change of CEO in the early Imperial Era in 19 BBY, all of the members of the Barsha Corp's executive board were arrested by the Galactic Empire for conspiracy. They were tried and placed under house arrest at their compound on Corellia's moon Gus Treta. During their stay, the family were de facto on holiday. At some point into their stay, Oland first encountered the BX-series droid commando ND-5, who he believed to be a replacement for one of the employed droids. Weeks after their trial, Oland along with the rest of the executive board was pardoned and in celebration, Roisem Barsha held a party with family and friends at the compound. During the night, Oland along with all of the Barsha family and their guests were assassinated by ND-5, who had actually been sent to kill everyone present. His cousin Jaylen Barsha was however able to survive by reprogramming ND-5 with the help of the compound's droid A1-A1.

Oland Barsha appeared in the 2026 novel Star Wars Outlaws: Low Red Moon, written by Mike Chen.

Olaris Rhea was a female Human Sith Lady in the Lost Tribe of Sith from the remote planet of Kesh. In 41 ABY, Rhea was appointed to be the Master of Sith Tyro Vestara Khai after Khai had encountered a Sith Meditation Sphere named Ship. Rhea and her new apprentice served in the Tribe's armada aboard the captured warship Eternal Crusader. After the members of the Tribe sensed Jedi Grand Master Luke Skywalker's presence in the Force two years later, Rhea and Grand Lord Darish Vol handpicked a strike team to bring down Skywalker and recover Ship, who had abruptly left Kesh. Using Khai's unique connection to Ship, the strike team, led by Rhea, tracked the Meditation Sphere to a planet in the Maw, where they encountered Abeloth, a female being who was able to control the world's deadly flora. She agreed to help keep the Sith safe while they searched for Ship. Meanwhile, the strike team's executive officer, Yuvar Xal, was plotting to overthrow Rhea and take command of the team for himself. Before he could execute his coup, the Meditation Sphere finally returned to the Sith.

Abeloth discovered Skywalker's location—along with his son, Ben Skywalker—to be Sinkhole Station, a small space station in the Maw, and Ship transported the surviving Sith there. Rhea led the strike team's ambush of the Skywalkers, and Xal initiated his coup during the battle. Due to Rhea's foresight, however, his betrayal failed, and he was killed by Khai, who was then captured by the Skywalkers. Khai escaped later during the battle; and as Ben prepared the Skywalkers' starship, the Jade Shadow, for flight, Rhea met up with Khai and the two remaining Sith. The other two were quickly dispatched by Luke, leaving only Rhea and her apprentice to duel him. The three fought on the turbolift that led to the hangar. As the lift's door opened, Rhea and Khai saw Ben in the Jade Shadow opening fire on Ship. Luke took advantage of their distraction and quickly killed Rhea, while Khai fled.

Olaris Rhea was a female Force-sensitive Human born on the remote world of Kesh. She was trained in the ways of the dark side of the Force with the Lost Tribe of Sith Rhea completed her training and became a respected member of the Tribe. By 41 ABY, she had achieved the rank of Lady on the Circle of Lords, the Tribe's ruling council. As a Lady, she served on the council in the Circle Chambers in the capitol building of the planet's capital city, Tahv.

In 41 ABY, Ship, a Sith Meditation Sphere, arrived on Kesh after refusing to join the One Sith, a faction of Sith who followed the Rule of One. After landing in the Temple courtyard in the Takara Mountains, it spoke through the Force with a Sith Tyro named Vestara Khai. The Circle of Lords decided that since Ship's expressed purpose was to train Sith apprentices, the Sphere's interest in Khai warranted her promotion to the rank of apprentice, and Rhea was chosen to be her Master. Ship then revealed to the Tribe that the Sith Empire had been all but destroyed, and now only a few Sith remained in hiding.

Olge Plavi-Dol was a female Human Jedi Knight, who served the Galactic Republic as a member of the Jedi Order during the Clone Wars.

A female Human, Olge Plavi-Dol was born on the planet of Commenor to a family who quickly discovered she was Force-sensitive. Sent to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, Plavi-Dol was educated in the ways of the Force before being assigned to a Jedi Master. Completing her Trials of Knighthood and ascending to the rank of Jedi Knight, Plavi-Dol explored the ways of the Consular, delving into the art of healing with the Force becoming a proficient Jedi healer.

At the outbreak of the Clone Wars, Plavi-Dol took up the rank of Jedi General in the Grand Army of the Republic. Early in the war she traveled to Argul, where she participated in a battle against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. She attended the sick and wounded who were awaiting transport offworld alongside Jedi Master Ulseh. After Grand Master Yoda left the planet to gather reinforcements, Plavi-Dol volunteered to stay behind with Master Ulseh, even though another transport may not have arrived in time, as she believed that her abilities to heal the injured were still needed.

Plavi-Dol made her only appearance in Only the Force, a scenario for the Star Wars Roleplaying Game. In that, the player playing as Plavi-Dol can choose Plavi-Dol's sex. However, she is described as female in the biographies of the other playable characters, so that can be assumed to be her canonical sex.
