Olia Choko was a female Pantoran who served in the Alliance to Restore the Republic and later the New Republic as the public relations representative between Chancellor Mon Mothma and the Galactic Senate. During a news broadcast that took place before the first official meeting of the new Galactic Senate, she spoke to the galaxy about a need for peace and reform. One angry citizen threw rotten fruit at her, but she brought him on camera and spoke to him about his needs, asking him to present his case to the Galactic Senate where they could take care of his people's needs. She also saw a New Republic soldier parading around Imperial prisoners, so she reprimanded him to show the galaxy that the New Republic would be nothing like the Galactic Empire before it.

Olia Choko was a female Pantoran who lived during the Age of the Empire and the rise of the New Republic. Choko was a member of the Alliance to Restore the Republic by the time of the Battle of Yavin. In order to turn the Alliance victory over the Galactic Empire into a propaganda campaign, Chancellor Mon Mothma wrote a report to Minister of Education Tynnra Pamlo of the assets she had at her disposal. One asset was holographic footage of the medal ceremony of Luke Skywalker and Han Solo following the battle, though permissions had to be routed to Choko in communications.

Following the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY, Choko became the public relations representative for Chancellor Mon Mothma and the new Galactic Senate. While the Rebellion on Akiva was taking place, Choko was interviewed by the Queen of the Core Network journalist Tracene Kane and the Trandoshan cameraman Lug. This was the first broadcast of the new HoloNet channel.

When Kane noted her nervousness, Choko reassured her that she would be fine as a pretty alien. Choko made sure that Lug got a good shot of Hanna City, Chandrila's capital and the current headquarters of the Galactic Senate. Choko also told Kane and Lug to get a good shot of the stormtrooper helmet art installation in the city circle. Having sorted out the surroundings, Kane commenced the interview and Lug commenced filming.

Omar Berenko was a famous and controversial human Naboo male tragic poet from the Mid Rim planet Naboo who lived during the High Republic Era. Berenko resided at Varykino, a lake retreat in Naboo's Lake Country, in an unconventional community of Naboo and Gungan outsiders. Varykino Villa's Room of Morning Mists was a favored composing spot of his, where he wrote the epic and disturbing poem "Defense of Naboo" and several other famous works.

In 232 BBY, Jedi Master Avar Kriss and Jedi Knight Elzar Mann visited the San Tekka compound near Varykino. The island caught Kriss' eye, and Mann spoke to her about Berenko, who was living there at the time. Mann noted that Berenko had a reputation for brilliance.

Eventually, Berenko was mysteriously kidnapped from the villa's terrace by unknown assailants, at the spot where Jedi Padawan Anakin Skywalker and Senator Padmé Amidala secretly married After his abduction, the poet was never seen again.

Omar Berenko was first mentioned in the current Star Wars canon in the 2016 edition of the reference book Star Wars: Complete Locations.

Omicron 1 was a Delta-class DX-9 stormtrooper transport that was carrying Imperial officers that were assigned to the Death Star. Alliance Special Forces sabotaged the transport, leaving it stranded in the Corellian system. The Alliance then sent a team consisting of Y-wings from Red Squadron, one of the pilots was Keyan Farlander, and X-wings from Blue Squadron with a Lambda-class shuttle Hunter to board and capture the transport and then bring it to the EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate Inad.

As soon as the shuttle boarded the transport Assault Gunboats arrived to intercept. The Rebel fighters intercepted and destroyed them with losses occurred. When the transport was captured and the Inad arrived to pick up the transport, the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Immortal arrived and launched TIE Fighters and Bombers and three transports arrived to intercept the captured transport. However Farlander in his Y-wing held of the attacking forces and the transport boarded the frigate, which jumped to Hyperspace.

Ordez was a Human male Sith Lord who served the Falleen Dark Councilor Darth Karrid during the Galactic War. He wielded a massive double-bladed lightsaber that produced identical beams of red-black energy.

Ordez and fellow Sith Lord Quux were assigned to the Ascendant Spear in the year 3640 BBY to serve the newly appointed member of the Dark Council, Darth Karrid.

When Jedi Master Gnost-Dural broke free from his restraints with the help of SIS Operative Theron Shan, he went to confront his former pupil, Darth Karrid in the chambers in which she could control the Spear.

When Gnost-Dural arrived, he was met with Lord Ordez, Lord Quux and Karrid's Human Male Apprentice, all of which were meditating in order to support Karrid in controlling the Ascendant Spear. When they saw Dural enter, the trio stopped their meditation and engaged the Jedi Master in a duel. Ordez and Quux together were powerful enough to hold off Gnost-Dural, the only problem being that they were not coordinated, constantly interrupting each others attacks, this allowed the Jedi to kill Karrid's Apprentice and focus on the other two.

Ormann Bomu was a male Rodian of the Bomu Clan. Along with his brother he worked for Zonnos of the Anjiliac kajidic. Onboard the light freighter Vengeance, they led raiding parties against enemy ships.

In typical Hutt fashion, there was much infighting in the Anjiliac kajidic. Heedron were dispatched by Zonnos to prevent the rescue of his brother Mika from Endregaad. The rescue was instigated by Zonnos' parent Popara, and was more than the pair could handle. In the ensuing firefight, it is believed that Ormann was killed and Heedron handed over to the Corporate Sector Authority.

The rescuers found two more Bomus on Endregaad when returning to their ships, wanting to "finish the job". It is unclear if they were Heedron and Ormann, or if they were their relatives, Gespo and Hreeda Bomu, looking for revenge.

Orn Belden was a Bakuran male senator in the Bakuran Senate, a position he held since before the foundation of the Galactic Empire and represented the Bakur RepulsorCorp in the Senate that was instrumental in the export industry that Bakura was chiefly known for. He was 164 years old by the time of the Bakura Incident.

A member of the Belden family, Orn was presumably one of the original Bakur Mining Corporation settlers of Bakura. He was described as being tall in terms of both height and courage.

He married Eppie Antruse in 97 BBY, the same year as a droid uprising on Bakura. Sometime afterward, they had their only child, Roviden. Along with his wife and son, Orn sympathized with the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War, but unlike them, he took no steps to help them.

Thus, when the Galactic Empire occupied Bakura in 1 ABY, his son was executed and his wife slated to be so; however, he convinced Governor Wilek Nereus to save her life by giving up his voice box. Nereus still punished Eppie, however, by inserting a senility-creating parasite into her brain.

Osted Alater was an officer in the Imperial Navy and captain of the Crusader's Shield. In the early days of the Galactic Empire, Alater was sent by Governor Paro Lanto to investigate the dealings of Planetary Safaris Inc., a business that specialized in providing challenging hunts across exotic worlds. On one such worlds, the planet Barab I, hunting parties were being routinely lost or decimated by the wild beasts on the planet. Under the Dangerous Species Act, it was legal for these beasts to be eliminated to prevent danger to Imperial occupation. However, when Alater began to observe these "wild beasts" he learned that they were actually a sentient race. Because the Dangerous Species Act did not apply to sentient beings, he had Planetary Safaris shut down for unscrupulous dealings.

In honor of Captain Alater's actions, the Barabels built Alater-ka, the planet's main spaceport and eventual capital.

Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races, Second Edition

The New Essential Guide to Alien Species

Ottoh Blythe was a human male miner. Living in a homestead on the Outer Rim planet Elphrona with his family, Ottoh and his wife Erika had relocated out of the Core Worlds in search of a simpler lifestyle for themselves and their children, Ronn and Bailen. However, their wealthy relatives in the Core made the Blythes targets for kidnapping at the hands of the Nihil pirates. While Ottoh's family was rescued by the Jedi Porter Engle, Indeera Stokes, and Bell Zettifar, Ottoh was captured alongside Jedi Master Loden Greatstorm, who had broken his leg while attempting to rescue Ottoh. As capturing a Jedi had been the true goal of Eye of the Nihil Marchion Ro when he had set up the raid, Ro killed Ottoh with Greatstorm's lightsaber aboard his flagship, the Gaze Electric, after Tempest Runner Lourna Dee brought the prisoners to him.

enrichments.description:
The Overtone was a planet hopper captained by the Bivall bounty hunter Quin Carree of the Tempest Breakers, along with her partner Lourna Dee. The ship was provided to a motley team of Jedi and bounty hunters by the Villarandi information broker Kradon Minst, through Greyamina Tiss, as they prepared to track down the abducted Nihil Minister of Advancement Baron Boolan in the Nihil Occlusion Zone. It was equipped with a way to circumvent the Stormwall, allowing passage into the Occlusion Zone. Though the ship was modest and with some faulty components, it saw the team through their mission, including surviving the eternal storms of Heiklet and a dogfight with one of the Nihil's She'ar. Following the mission, the ship came under the ownership of Carree and Dee. The latter attempted to change its name to the Quin, but Carree refused to have a ship named after her. Journalist Rhil Dairo interviewed Lourna Dee from within the Overtone.

The Overtone first appeared in The High Republic: Tempest Breaker, a 2024 audio drama written by Cavan Scott and published as a part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's Phase III. During the audio drama's flashbacks, the Overtone is described by Greyamina Tiss as a planet hopper. However, the drama's script, released in 2025, indicates in slug lines that the interview used as the frame story takes place in a Star Cruiser. In the dialogue of the final scene, Rhil Dairo confirms that they are in the Overtone. Given that the slug lines are out-of-universe, this article considers the descriptions of the ship in-universe to take precedence, especially as the ship is described more consistently with the typical size of a planet hopper instead of a Star Cruiser.

Pann was a male Human Jedi Knight who served the Jedi Order during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

Discovered to be Force-sensitive, Pann was taken to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant and trained at the Temple's academy in the Jedi arts. Selected as a Padawan, Pann eventually passed his Trials of Knighthood and was made a Jedi Knight by the Jedi High Council. During his studies, Jedi Pann became fascinated with the mysterious Codex, an ancient artifact created centuries in the past. Employing a protocol droid named Q4P3 to assist in his search, the droid wandered far and wide on its quest. Meanwhile, the Clone Wars erupted between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

Reporting to Coruscant, Pann served in the Grand Army of the Republic as a General fighting on many fronts until the end of the war when the Galactic Empire came to power and disbanded the Jedi Order and the Republic. Escaping the horrors of the Great Jedi Purge with his life, Pann went underground in hopes that Q4P3 would return with the Codex. Having been drawn to the volcanic world of Mustafar as of 1 ABY, the droid eventually did locate the artifact and took it back to Pann for study. After a great deal of time and effort, Pann came to understand a few of its functions before it left his possession.

Pann was created as a character example to illustrate an adventure idea in the Star Wars Gamemaster Handbook. His existence in-universe remained unclear until it was confirmed by Trials of Obi-Wan, the third expansion to Star Wars Galaxies.

Pari Bunkle was a female human who worked in the Galactic Empire's Ministry of Agriculture on the planet Lothal. She had a child named Ames Bunkle with another researcher at the Ministry, and the family lived in an apartment in Lothal's Capital City. When Ames was sixteen he enrolled in the planet's Academy for Young Imperials along with Dhara Leonis, a girl who lived in the same apartment building. The Leonis family threw a party for their daughter, but Pari and her partner were unable to attend as they were on assignment. While at the academy, Ames was chosen to specialize in stormtrooper training, and during the course was not allowed contact with his parents, a fact which Pari told Dhara's mother Tepha Leonis told her family. When Pari fell ill however, Ames was given two days leave to visit her.

Pari Bunkle was first mentioned in Servants of the Empire: Edge of the Galaxy, a novel by Jason Fry released in 2014.

Parja Bralor was a female Human Mandalorian who was the niece of former Cuy'val Dar Rav Bralor. She was a talented engineer and loved to fix things, from a broken chrono to a sick Nuna chick. She owned a successful workshop on Mandalore and was eventually responsible for the maintenance of all the machinery at Kyrimorut, the Skirata clan's home.

When clone commando Fi Skirata was brought to Mandalore following brain damage sustained at the battle of Gaftikar, she took on the job of nursing Fi back to health - caring for him, giving him physical therapy, and eventually falling in love with him. Parja was endlessly patient with Fi's loss of memory and coordination and was fiercely protective of him even after he regained some mobility and speech. Fi and Parja were married in a traditional Mandalorian wedding ceremony 998 days after the battle of Geonosis with Parja wearing her workshop overalls and Fi wearing Mandalorian armor. The wedding - which took less than a minute - occurred right before Fi, now mostly recovered, left on a mission to Coruscant with ARC trooper deserters Sull, Spar and former Jedi General Bardan Jusik.

When Clan Skirata deserted from the Grand Army of the Republic after Order 66, she lived there with them in Kyrimorut.

Parja wore armor of a deep scarlet color. Her chestnut braids were often tied with copper beads. Her name is derived from the Mandalorian word "parjiir" meaning "victory".

Parnax of Human or Sith pureblood descent who held the title of Sith Lord in the Sith Empire in the years before the Great Galactic War with the Galactic Republic. Parnax was deeply unpopular even among his own family, and he spent his brief career as a Sith betraying every one of his allies and accumulating a long list of powerful enemies.

Around 3683 BBY, Parnax, believed by some to either have been incredibly arrogant or incredibly stupid, deliberately broke into the Dark Temple, a forbidden Sith structure on the planet Dromund Kaas that had been sealed for centuries, in search of the key to the Sith Emperor's power. Parnax recorded his experiences in several journals, chronicling his descent into madness as he found himself unable to leave the Temple and discovered the Emperor's plans to extinguish all life in the galaxy. Parnax ultimately committed suicide, as he believed he could survive the coming darkness by merging with the Force.

Parnax was originally slated to be the focus of a Codex entry in Star Wars: The Old Republic, a video game released by BioWare, but the entry was removed before the game's release in 2011.

Patch Bruit was Lommite Limited's chief of field operations in 33 BBY. Although he served the company for nearly twenty years, working his way up from the lommite pits, he had long dreamed of starting over and relocating to Coruscant or one of the other Core worlds and making a new life for himself. After being ordered by Jurnel Arrant to hire the Toom clan to sabotage rival InterGalactic Ore, the Tooms betrayed him and sabotaged both LL and InterGal. Working with Caba'Zan, he led an assault on the clan's hideout on Riome. Following the clan's defeat, he was Force choked to death by Darth Maul, who went on to frame Bruit for his actions sabotaging the two companies.

The Peculiar Inspiration was a starship that was in existence during the time of the Clone Wars.

After rescuing the Tarasin Force Adepts Krizta and Trik, the Heroes of Cularin were loaned use of the Peculiar Inspiration to transport the Tarasin pair to the Cularin system. However, a group of bounty hunters sabotaged the ship, causing it to crash on the planet Holador.

In Strike III, the player characters, who role-play as the Heroes of Cularin, are only loaned the use of the Peculiar Inspiration if they lack a suitable transport of their own. If the players are traveling in a ship of their own, then it is that ship, not the Inspiration, that they travel in, and which crashes on Holador.

Pentir Bephorin was the son of Givin mathematician and cryptographer Drusil Bephorin. When Drusil was captured by the Galactic Empire and forced to work for them she was separate from Pentir, who was left with his father and other siblings. Members of the Alliance to Restore the Republic rescued Bephorin's family and kept them safe while the rebel agents Luke Skywalker and Nakari Kelen extracted Drusil from the planet Denon, where she was being held. The Alliance then arranged for Pentir and the rest of the family to reunited with Drusil on the remote world of Omereth. Skywalker and Kelen managed to bring Drusil to the meeting place, but were attacked by bounty hunters searching for the cryptographer. Kelen was killed during the fighting, but Skywalker successfully defeated the hunters, after which a CR90 corvette commanded by Major Bren Derlin arrived carrying Pentir and the rest of his family. Drusil happily greeted her husband and children and introduced them to Skywalker, whom Pentir tried to ask a mathematics question as a standard form of polite Givin greeting. Drusil informed her son there was no need for such formality, after which she and her family left in one of the bounty hunter's starships in order to find a safe location to hide from the Empire and continue aiding the Alliance.

Pentir Bephorin first appeared in the novel Heir to the Jedi, which was written by Kevin Hearne and released in 2015.

The People's Inquest was a grassroots populist Jedi-accountability watch-group active before and during the Clone Wars.

They supported Jonava Billane in the Case of "Baby Ludi". Thrynka Padaunete was president of the People's Inquest. They were known for their multiple petitions and marches on the Jedi Temple. In one particular march, several Padawans were overwhelmed and were unable to quell the angry group. Jedi Master Plo Koon easily dispatched the disruptive mob using a Jedi mind trick.

In the wake of Order 66, the People's Inquest aided the Galactic Empire by compiling a list of all known Jedi that were still at large, along with information on other Force-using sects.

enrichments.description: Phasers were a type of weapon. Phaser was an acronym for Perpetually Heat-Activated Sonic-Emmitted Ray. They differed from the usual "laser" weapons in that they did not rapidly shoot out gas-induced plasma beams, but instead shot long beams of pure radio-active heat-light rays activated by a special type of sonic conductor. Bounty hunters often preferred to use them as sniper rifles because they were lighter weight than plasma-beam sniper rifles and a lot easier to handle, but finding one was very difficult. Phaser weapons were exceedingly rare and worth a lot of money as relics.

Phis Benlip was a male Human who worked for the Hutt Riboga during the time of the Clone Wars.

Following Riboga's return to the Cularin system, he sent Benlip and a group of thugs to the moon Dorumaa, to extort money from businesses on the world. Benlip worked his way through various resorts on the world and eventually came to Greentree Pointe, where he extorted money from hotels and other tourist facilities. However, while Benlip and his men were attempting extract money from an amusement park owner, they were confronted by the Heroes of Cularin, a group of freelance agents who operated in the Cularin system. Benlip and his thugs fled the scene by jumping into cars on the Meteor Strike!! rollercoaster ride, and heroes pursued them.

enrichments.description:
Phoenix was a BFF-1 bulk freighter that bore a load of communications satellites, stolen from the Imperial base on Orron III.

The Imperials attempted to recover the satellites, sending a force of shuttles and transports to capture the fleeing freighter. However, the Rebel Alliance, worried about the rumors concerning a new Imperial secret project, planned to capture some of the Empire's own communication satellites to help them intercept transmissions and dispatched the shuttle Wilsey escorted by Keyan Farlander in a BTL Y-wing starfighter to capture the freighter.

Farlander defeated the Imperial forces, allowing the Wilsey to board and capture the Phoenix. The Phoenix escaped into hyperspace shortly before the arrival of the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Intrepid.

A week later, Phoenix was due to be recovered by the Mon Calamari Star Cruiser Maximus in a quiet sector, away from Imperial interests. However, when the Maximus was delayed, Farlander was sent in a lone R-22 Spearhead to protect the Phoenix until the Maximus arrived. When Farlander emerged from hyperspace, he was surprised to discover the Intrepid in the area, already launching TIE starfighters against the Phoenix. Coming under immediate attack, Farlander fought off the TIEs until the Maximus arrived with the freighter Ojai. The Maximus launched X-wings from Blue Squadron but the Intrepid fled quickly leading the Rebels to wonder if it was suffering from a shortage of pilots or starfighters. The Ojai then docked with the Phoenix to recover the satellites.
enrichments.short_description: Phoenix was a BFF-1 bulk freighter that bore a load of communications satellites, stolen from the Imperial base on Orron III.

Pilester Binalie was a Human male who was the father of Corf Binalie, a friend of Jedi Master Jafer Torles, and the owner of Spaarti Creations on the planet Cartao during the Clone Wars, a conflict between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

In 22 BBY, he resided in a mansion near Foulahn City and attempted to remain neutral throughout the war. However, the Confederacy of Independent Systems planned to use the factory for equipment and special purposes throughout the war. This led to a fierce battle when Jafer and the Republic arrived on the planet. Pilester and his son observed as a Republic ship destroyed the factory, blaming the Jedi and thus ending their friendship with Torles. In secret, however, it was all a fabrication by Darth Sidious and Kinman Doriana.

During the invasion of Stronghold by the alien Charon, Akarias fought with the Alliance defenders, but his small group of personnel was overwhelmed and captured. Akarias escaped but witnessed the horrors that the Charon inflicted upon their prisoners. The Plooriod Bodkin was a cruiser in the Judicial Starfleet of the Galactic Republic during the Separatist Crisis. Shortly before the start of the Clone Wars, it was dispatched to recapture the Judicial corvette Scarlet Thranta, commanded by Captain Zozridor Slayke, which had gone renegade in hopes of provoking war with the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

On that mission, the Plooriod Bodkin was crewed by thirty Judicials and twelve Jedi, and accompanied by eight Jedi Starfighters. The mission was led by Jedi Knight Nejaa Halcyon. They trailed the Thranta for weeks, finally finding it on Bpfassh. However, while searching for Slayke's crew, the pirates stole the Plooriod Bodkin after disabling the Thranta, leaving the Republic crew stranded on the world for months, disgracing Halcyon in the eyes of many. The Bodkin became Slayke's command ship.

The Plooriod Bodkin is referred to at least once, in the novel Jedi Trial, as a 'judicial corvette'. It is unclear whether the Bodkin can be correctly designated as a cruiser, as a corvette, or as either.

Po Bandis was a male Jedi Master who, in addition to being a member of the Jedi Order, served as a General of the 313th Legion during the Clone Wars, a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

Po Bandis was a Force-sensitive Zabrak male who was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order. After years of study and work with the Jedi High Council, Bandis would pass the Trials of Knighthood to reach the rank of Jedi Knight and finally made a Jedi Master.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Master Bandis dutifully took up the rank of General within the Grand Army of the Republic. Leading clone troopers against the Separatist Droid Army, Bandis was placed in command of the 313th Legion and tasked with locating a Separatist base located on Ando Prime. Discovering a massive droid production facility, Bandis led his troops to destroy it but were intercepted by General Terrus and his droid army. As they did battle, the Skakoan engineer Vylagos activated his experimental hyperspace wormhole transporter, which transported Bandis and his men off-planet to an unknown location in the Outer Rim Territories.

Detecting Bandis's disappearance, the High Council dispatched Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi to locate the Jedi and his clones. Leading Commander Vargus and Excelsior Company to Ando Prime, the Jedi encounter a medic, Gen-Goma, who helped them extract information from Vylagos about the experimental machine. Reactivating the machine, the Skakoan brought back Bandis and his troops, who then aided in shutting down the Separatist base.

Pol Andrissus was a male human who served as a member of the alliance's 61st Mobile Infantry. He defected from the Galactic Empire as a cadet along with his classmate Carver. He was nicknamed Charmer for his "good looks" and reputation for being a "ladies' man." In a campaign on Blacktar Cyst, he was badly injured which lost him his "good looks" and resulted in him developing a stutter.

Following the Battle of Hoth, the 61st initiated Operation Ringbreaker and Charmer was assigned his own squad. He died during the attack on Mardona III, when he attempted to save his squad from an armored worm vehicle, with Corbo being the lone survivor. Carver joined the team that went out to avenge him and his two fallen men, successfully catching the crew as they disembarked from the vehicle and destroyed the worm.

Pol Andrissus first appeared in the 2015 novel Battlefront: Twilight Company, written by Alexander Freed.

Precognition, known to the Chiss as "Third Sight," was an ability of the Force that allowed its use to see future events before they occurred.

Anakin Skywalker utilized precognition during his time as a Jedi Knight and Sith Lord Darth Vader to peer into the future to know where and when an attack was coming from.

Chiss individuals, nearly always females, who were born to be Force-sensitive, were born with the ability of precognition. Because of this, they were used by the Chiss to navigate and pilot their ships through the Unknown Regions, as well as finding and mapping temporary hyperlanes. Such Chiss navigators were known as ozyly-esehembo. Only Chiss children had precognitive power to safely guide their ships at the speed the Aristocras demanded, and as the Chiss grew older the ability faded, regardless of the amount of training or practice the individual undertook. The Force-sensitive child Eila could use this ability.

Precognition was first mentioned in Star Wars canon in the 2015 novel Aftermath, written by Chuck Wendig. It made its first appearance in 2017 during Zero Hour, the Star Wars Rebels Season Three finale.

Trevagg caught sight of M'iiyoom Onith, a female H'nemthe. Balu warned Feltipern to "leave the girl alone" when he was attempting to bed her. However, stubborn Trevagg didn't listen to him, and was killed during their mating ritual. Balu's surprised reaction to Wuher's fingering of M'iiyoom Onith in Trevagg's murder suggests that Balu did not know of the danger Trevagg was in.

As a security officer, Balu patrolled the streets of Mos Eisley. He wore dark blue pants and vest, gray shirt, and tan holster and belt.

In the audio dramatization of Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale, the character was voiced by Russell Horton.

The Prosperous was first mentioned in the current Star Wars canon in the "Secrets of Spaceflight" section of the fifty-eighth issue of De Agostini's Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon magazine, In the Star Wars Legends continuity, the Prosperous was introduced in the twenty-third episode of the Star Wars: Clone Wars animated series, which aired on March 26, 2005. It was then identified in the StarWars.com Databank entry for Saesee Tiin.

Prowler was the name given to two Escort carriers used by the Rebel Alliance. Prowler 1 contained B-wings, while Prowler 2 carried X-wings. The two carriers were attacked by two TIE Defenders launched from modified corvette Burke, followed by James, should the Burke be destroyed. Both fighters carried Space bombs to disable only one of them. After disabling one of them the other jumped to Hyperspace.

Soon two pairs of Corellian corvettes Sharky and Spear followed by X-wings and A-wings arrived to intercept the capture attempt. The Rebel corvettes and fighters were destroyed by the TIE Defenders, while the Interdictor Suelu arrived to prevent escape and to capture the disabled carrier. When the operation was complete, a Nebulon-B Frigate Egale arrived to launch more B-wings and X-wings, but the Carrier jumped to hyperspace to an unknown location.

The event was recreated and used in the Combat chamber to train future pilots, in particular, Maarek Stele.

The Pulsar Station was a Death Star-like system domination weapon planned by the Ciutric Hegemony.

The Pulsar Station was a drastically scaled-down version of the original Death Star battle stations, inspired by the way the Emperor utilized the second Death Star at the Battle of Endor—for the destruction of capital ships.

Along its equatorial plane were a number of gravity-well generators to halt all hyperspace traffic in and out of local space. The superlaser was also scaled down and numerous superlaser emplacements were installed, each capable of destroying a Super Star Destroyer. Its capabilities were rounded off by half a dozen TIE wings and smaller anti-ship weapons.

Though detailed schematics for the station were created, there were never any intentions to implement such a weapon, which was supposedly being built into the moon of Distna in the Corvis Minor system. The designs were allowed to fall into the hands of the New Republic at the Battle of Liinade III. The Pulsar Station was nothing more than an elaborate charade by ex-Imperial Empress Ysanne Isard to lure Rogue Squadron to aid her in her quest to destroy her rogue clone and Prince-Admiral Delak Krennel.

enrichments.description:
Quillan, a male Human Sith, was the twin brother of Dromika and one of the youngest children of Sith Lord Chagras and the younger siblings of Arkadia Calimondra. During the New Sith Wars, Byllura was controlled by the Chagras Hegemony. Following the death of Chagras, the ruler of the hegemony, Byllura became the capital of the Dyarchy and was governed by the Sith Lord twins Dromika and Quillan with Saaj Calician serving as its Regent. Their reign ended in 1032 BBY when Byllura fell to the forces of the Arkadianate.

Quillan with his twin sister Dromika were the youngest children of the Sith Lord Chagras, ruler of the Sith realm known as the Chagras Hegemony during the New Sith Wars. In 1040 BBY, Chagras died which sparked a second series of clan warfare among the Sith clan ruling the Grumani sector. At that period, Quillan and Dromika were only five years old. They became rulers of a rump state known as the Dyarchy which was governed on their behalf by their Krevaaki Regent Saaj Calician. They lived on the planet Byllura, residing on a mesa situated above the capital city of Hestobyll.

During his childhood, Quillan specialized in using the Force to manipulate their surrounding environment, making all other sentient beings and droids de-facto extensions of their will. With the assistance of Calician, Quillan and Dromika employed a network of Celegians to transmit mental suggestions which enthralled the population of Byllura in functioning like a single living organism. To maintain their control over the Dyarchy, Calician employed a force of red-clad Unifiers to enforce compliance among the population by using Force persuasion. This feat was unparalleled elsewhere within the Grumani sector since even Sith Lord Daiman, who regarded himself as the omnipresent Creator of the universe, was unable to exert the same level of direct control over the daily affairs of his own subjects.

During their rule, they stayed within their mesa as Quillan suffered from an powerful farsight ability while he was taken care of by Dromika, Calician, and a large retinue of servant droids. Quillan's Force perceptions were so strong that all other sentient beings had to address them from a dais situated at some distance from their throne, which consisted of a pile of orange pillows. Since Quillan perceived living beings as mere phantasm shining radiantly through the Force which blinded his physical senses, only servant droids were allowed to physically approach the twins. Throughout much of his life, Quillan dwelled almost entirely within his expansive mind and preferred to delegate much of his interaction with the outside world to his twin Dromika and their Regent Calician.

Quux was a Pureblood male Sith Lord who served the Falleen Dark Councilor Darth Karrid during the Galactic War. He wielded a pair of purple-bladed shotos.

Quux and fellow Sith Lord Ordez were assigned to the Ascendant Spear in the year 3640 BBY to serve the newly appointed member of the Dark Council, Darth Karrid.

When Jedi Master Gnost-Dural broke free from his restraints with the help of SIS Operative Theron Shan, he went to confront his former pupil, Darth Karrid in the chambers in which she could control the Spear.

When Gnost-Dural arrived, he was met with Lord Quux, Lord Ordez and Karrid's Human Male Apprentice, all of which were meditating in order to support Karrid in controlling the Ascendant Spear. When they saw Dural enter, the trio stopped their meditation and engaged the Jedi Master in a duel. Ordez and Quux together were powerful enough to hold off Gnost-Dural, the only problem being that they were not coordinated, constantly interrupting each others attacks, this allowed the Jedi to kill Karrid's Apprentice and focus on the other two.

Raar Anyell was a Human male Corellian TIE/LN starfighter pilot in the Imperial Navy that served as part of Alpha Squadron, under the command of Lieutenant Commander Villian Dance, that was assigned to the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Steel Talon.

Anyell was a foul-up everywhere but in the cockpit, and although he was always behind on keeping up with new intel, he was a good enough pilot for his squadron leader to give him some slack.

He was one of twelve pilots of Alpha Squadron assigned to chase down RLH-1, a stolen Lambda-class T-4a shuttle, but was instructed to hold back while the squadron leader attempted to convince the shuttle's pilot to surrender. Anyell witnessed the shuttle destroyed by his commander after the pilot refused to return. He was one of two pilots assigned to examine the wreckage for survivors, of which there were none.

The Nihil pirate organization led a raid in the Abrion sector during the High Republic Era. The Tycoon Trader, a cargo cruiser, had been shipping glitterstim from Aaloth to the Hutt Cartel. An informer within the Hutt Cartel informed Dowutin Tempest Runner Pan Eyta of a stim shipment in the sector, so he sent his Tempest to raid the ship.

The Nihil pulled the Trader out of hyperspace with a gravity mine, punctured the hull with gas torpedoes, and boarded the ship with a boarding tube. The Nihil's masks protected the marauders from the war cloud they had released. The Trader was protected by the mercenary Lourna Dee, who set up automated defenses aboard the ship to combat the Nihil, and sacrificed the pilot droid RL-18 as part of her counter-ambush.

The Storm Jinnix dispatched a boarding party of his crew including the Nikto Towl and an individual named Blackwing, both of whom Dee killed. The droid H7-09 was damaged in the skirmish. Jinnix went to confront Dee, but she defeated him by ripping out one of his fangs and stabbing him with it.

Lourna thought she had won, but Pan Eyta came and took her prisoner. She cut a deal with him to join the Nihil and help conduct a raid on Aaloth. As payment, Lourna joined the Nihil and took possession of Jinnix's former ship, the Toothspike, renaming it the Lourna Dee.

In around 3643 BBY, Coruscant Security Force officer Stansun tasked an agent of the Galactic Republic with raiding a clinic being operated by the criminal Black Sun on the planet Coruscant. The clinic was being used to surgical alter the faces of wanted criminals to help them escape arrest, and Stansun wanted for it to be shut down and for a list of its previous patients so they could be tracked down.

The agent successfully located a passkey for the clinic and then entered the structure, killing at least eight of the Human and droid medical personnel working inside and shutting the facility down. The agent then recovered the patient list from the structure's computers and returned it to Stansun.

enrichments.description:
The EX-F was an Imperial warship used as a testbed for new gunnery and engine technologies. It was part of the Black Fleet, which was captured by the alien Yevetha towards the end of 4 ABY. Renamed the Glory of Yevetha by them, she was eventually reclaimed by the Imperial Remnant in 17 ABY and renamed the Rakehell, only to be destroyed at the Battle of Anx Minor within the same year.

The EX-F was a ship that served in the Black Fleet. Outfitted for weapons and drive testing before the Battle of Endor, she attracted the attention of Alliance Intelligence. The vessel disappeared from records some time before Endor; she was next reported eight months after the battle, when she was berthed at the Black Fifteen shipyards at N'zoth in the Koornacht Cluster, a facility assigned to Black Sword Command.

Following the Yevethan seizure of the Black Fleet, the EX-F was renamed the Glory, although the Yevetha were unable to understand her engine technology even after twelve years of reverse-engineering. She accordingly missed out on the opening stages of the Yevethan Purge. She was moved afterward to Morning Bell.

In 17 ABY, she was recaptured by the Imperial survivors, who the Yevetha had retained for their technical knowledge, and along with the rest of the Imperial ships in the Black Fleet, she departed Koornacht for the Deep Core, though her crew soon after opted to join the forces of the Imperial Remnant in the Outer Rim. During the Battle of Anx Minor in 17 ABY, the EX-F, known at this time as the Rakehell, was destroyed when her antimatter containment was breached, wiping out several other Star Destroyers in the process.

enrichments.description:
The wife of Raymus Antilles lived on the planet Alderaan around 1 BBY. She had two daughters with Antilles, but raised the children for long periods of time without her husband's presence due to his dedication as a captain in service to the Rebellion. In 1 BBY, the human rebel wished to write his final, parting words to his beloved family, believing that he would die aboard the Tantive IV as the Galactic Empire pursued the rebel craft of his for the theft of the important Death Star plans.

His close collaborator Princess Leia Organa had ensured the family's wellbeing during the resistance against the Empire, yet Antilles felt sorry for having spent little time with them; however, the Tantive IV was attacked before he could write down his words. The captain was soon captured by Imperial forces and choked to death by their leader, Darth Vader, despite his and his crew's resistance. Although he knew that he would never see his wife or daughters again, Antilles, having fought to secure lives that his loved ones deserved, hoped in his final moments that the Princess would escape and help liberate the galaxy. While Alderaan was destroyed, Organa's stolen plans helped secure a rebel victory at the following Battle of Yavin, and the Rebellion toppled the Empire five years later.

Razor's Kiss was an Executor-class Star Dreadnought built at Kuat Drive Yards for the Empire.

Warlord Zsinj sent a boarding party to hijack the vessel before full completion, unaware that the party had been infiltrated by Wraith Squadron.

The captured ship broke free of the shipyard at which she was docked and left to rendezvous with Zsinj's flagship Iron Fist, unaware that Shalla Nelprin of Wraith Squadron had docked her stolen TIE/IN interceptor on her hull while escaping.

Shalla took out the Star Dreadnought's shield generators and bridge, allowing a New Republic battle group, led by the Mon Remonda and commanded by General Han Solo, to finish the job.

Recnelo Cott was a female Ugnaught who worked in the tibanna gas mines and lived apart from her clan in Cloud City on Bespin in the year 3 ABY. She had an apartment on Level 121 where Isabalia rent a room. She took part at the event led by Joy Iya to arrange a citywide work stoppage to get the attention of Calrissian and others running the city. At first they tried unsuccessfully to involve Isabalia, but later when a stormtrooper appeared and aimed a blaster at the group, she didn't think; she exchanged fire and then beat the stormtrooper unconscious. She then offered to join Iya's work stoppage, and Iya's response gave her hope of having a lifetime together.

Recnelo Cott first appeared in "Beyond the Clouds," a short story by Lilliam Rivera that was published in the 2020 anthology From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back.

The red apricot was the starship of red apricot squad, an elite squad of the Silver Knights, a prominent civil mercenary group in the Aakaash system. Attended to by the squad's mechanic, Zhuang Yuanying, as well as a team of seven worker drones of the WB-35 mechanic droid model, the red apricot was shaped like a cone lying down on its side. Its elongated contour was protected by an armored hull composed of enigmatic iron and other metals, with the hull being disposable in a maneuver known to red apricot squad as "shell shedding."

When the squad was tasked to retrieve a lost Silver Dawn shipment of enigmatic tenebrae, the squad took the red apricot to Fire and later Lake 4399 in the Heaven system.

The red apricot appeared in The Vow of Silver Dawn, a Chinese web novel written by "His Majesty the King." The ship first appeared in a chapter released in January 4, 2021, and is named 红杏号 in the original simplified Chinese text.

Red Feathers was a crippled Kuat Drive Yards Super Transport VI, which had crashed on Blood Nest, orbiting the gas giant M2398-3. This ship was used as the headquarters for a band of pirates under name Blood Nest until their defeat in 7 ABY by Wraith Squadron. It was then used by the New Republic in the Battle of Ession to deliver three starfighter squadrons and the Page's commandos. The commandos activated its self-destruct and left the ship in an escape pod, while Rogue, Blue, and Green Squadrons were released from the ship's hangar when the self-destruct charges broke apart its hull.

Red Gauntlet was an Imperial I-class Star Destroyer under the command of Warlord Zsinj. It participated in the Battle of Vahaba, attacking Admiral Teren Rogriss's Stellar Web along with Zsinj's Victory-class Star Destroyer Serpent's Smile. The attack failed due to mass fire and superior tactics on behalf of the temporarily allied New Republic and Galactic Empire, and Serpent's Smile was destroyed. Red Gauntlet surrendered shortly after, under the guns of General Han Solo's Crynyd and Skyhook, as well as Stellar Web. General Solo captured Red Gauntlet by putting a crew aboard her and discussed using her against Zsinj until she was reassigned.

Redoubtable was an early-model Imperial I-class Star Destroyer. It was later renamed the Destiny of Yevetha.

After taking significant damage in the retreat from the Battle of Endor, she was sent to the Black-15 shipyard at N'zoth. The ship was seized by Nil Spaar of the Yevetha during their uprising, and renamed the Destiny of Yevetha. After the Yevetha completed her repairs, she served in the Yevethan fleet during the Black Fleet Crisis.

Redoubtable jumped to Byss in the Deep Core along with the other Imperial-design starships which left the Yevethan fleet under the command of Sil Sorannan.

Rei'izu () was the homeworld of the Empire. Its capital city was Yojou.

During the Sith rebellion against the Empire and its Jedi clans, the Sith captured Rei'izu. The rebellion was led by a former Jedi knight who became a Dark Lord of the Sith, later known only as the Ronin, and a witch who had been a guardian alongside him. Their capture of the Imperial homeworld proved to the Empire that the Sith were a genuine threat, leading formerly feuding lords to band together.

The dark lord and the witch entered the Shinsui Temple together, and after expelling the nuns and monks who were willing to leave and killing those who would not, they approached the legendary kyber mirror of Shinsui Temple. The witch knelt before the mirror and began praying, entering a trance. After multiple days passed, the dark lord grew frustrated; without intent, he idly touched the mirror. The vision of unending war and resulting guilt for his own actions were overwhelming, and he struck the mirror with his fist and with the black current and white flare of the Force.

Rei'izu appeared in the 2021 non-canon novel Ronin: A Visions Novel, by Emma Mieko Candon. due to their historical significance, the presence of several temples and shrines, and the author's fondness for these cities. Reidi Artom was a female Near-Human space explorer that discovered and named the Reidi Artom I, Reidi Artom II, Reidi Artom III, Reidi Artom IV, and Reidi Artom V systems. Additionally, she rediscovered the Cularin system (initially Reidi Artom VI) in 232 BBY.

Reidi Artom belonged to a long-lived humanoid species. Her people generally stayed on their own planet, something a young Artom did not understand. She loved excitement, adventure, and the thrill of exploration, so she escaped her homeworld early in her life. For years, she wandered aimlessly, working whatever jobs would allow her to get from one place to another.

Artom gained her exploring vessel, the Trailblazer, in a unique manner. After she stowed away on the scout vessel, the ship came under attack. After the pilot was killed, nearly instantly, the ship was left floating in space. She made repairs and, after using the hyperdrive to get to a starport, registered the ship in her own name. In an effort to explore new systems and undiscovered space while getting paid for it, Reidi became a scout for the Galactic Republic. Although many scouts explored the Unknown Regions or the Outer Rim, Reidi surveyed the Exploration Region to find planets that had been overlooked. She was credited with the renewed interest that followed her explorations in at least eight systems.

During her first scouting in the Cularin system in 232 BBY, Artom visited the system from the outer to the inner planets. As such, she found the Almas Sith fortress in Almas; the Crystal Snare in the Cularin asteroid belt, and the mysterious lava-like creature of Rennokk in her second visit to the moon. She also befriended the Tarasin native species of Cularin to the extent that she was taken to the Sacred Ch'hala Tree Grove — a honor that was bestowed to few outworlders since.

Reina Bilass, formerly known as Reina Ganzee, was a humanoid female Jedi Initiate during the High Republic Era. Born in the Coruscant Underworld's level eleven-eighty, she was found at a young age by the Ganzee Gang, a notorious criminal group which used young children as agents, and raised on level ten-fourteen. When Reina was found to be Force-sensitive, the gang willingly handed her over to the Jedi Order, hoping that she would one day return the favor. However, the girl resisted, changing her surname to "Bilass" and reacting negatively to any perceived incursion by the gang into the Temple District. Despite only being an initiate, she became a mentor to Lohim Nara, who could not become a Jedi Knight but could study to become a guardian of the Temple.

Rel Bentin was a male captain in the Galactic Empire. After Imperial Captain Thrawn failed to comprehend the Kaleesh species' culture by studying their art, he bombarded the Kaleesh planet destroying the headquarters of the Kaleesh commander, warlord Bentilais san Sk'ar. Afterward, Bentin encountered a surrendering Sk'ar in his base, and was intimidated by the warlord's size, bringing the Kaleesh to Emperor Palpatine. Palpatine then allowed Sk'ar to serve the Imperial Military.

Rel Bentin was introduced in the 2007 article Aliens in the Empire, written by Abel G. Peña and Rich Handley for the Hyperspace website.

Releqy A'Kla was a female Caamasi who served the New Republic and the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances during the Yuuzhan Vong War. She was the daughter of Elegos A'Kla.

In 28 ABY, she was present on Mon Calamari with the majority of the Senate that had survived the Fall of Coruscant, and supported Cal Omas in his bid to become Chief of State. After the Alderaanian won the election, Omas appointed Releqy Minister of State as well as appointing her to the High Council, where she voted against the use of the biological weapon Alpha Red.

Releqy was originally planned to be introduced in the comic Specter of Thrawn, before it was cancelled.

enrichments.description:
Ren Auglu was a male Human Jedi Padawan who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a Commander in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive Human born to a family on Naboo, Ren Auglu was handed over to the Jedi Order following his father's death during the Invasion of Naboo in 32 BBY. Taken to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, Auglu underwent Jedi training in an Initiate clan for the next several years. Before reaching the age of fourteen, Initiate Auglu was selected by Jedi Master Ulseh to continue his training in the field as a Padawan.

When the Clone Wars broke out across the galaxy between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Padawan Auglu was made a Commander in the Grand Army of the Republic and assigned to several missions. In 22 BBY Auglu followed Master Ulseh to the planet Argul, where they fought side by side in the battle against the Confederacy's Droid Army. During the battle, the pair oversaw the evacuation of the injured Argullians. After an Acclamator-class assault ship was shot down over the planet, Master Ulseh rushed to assist the crash victims. While Auglu survived the battle, Master Ulseh died from a droid attack on the ship's wreckage.

Alone on the planet with several other Padawans, Auglu continued to lead troops against the forces of Commander Drogen Hosh unsuccessfully. As Hosh prepared for a final assault, he sent Auglu and the other Padawans an offer in which he would accept their surrender. Before Hosh received a decision, however, Grand Master Yoda arrived on the planet with reinforcements and defeated Hosh. Victorious, Auglu and the other Padawans returned to the Jedi Temple.

Renthal's Vigilance was a Carrack-class light cruiser in Drea Renthal's pirate fleet. Originally it had been an Imperial ship named Vigilance under Captain Darv Eldon.

It was part of the Imperial squadron present at the Battle of Nar Shaddaa in 4 BBY. When the Vigilance entered the debris field surrounding the moon, it was ambushed by ships of the smugglers' First Strike Element. After a fierce engagement with the Hutt ship Dragon Pearl commanded by Mako Spince, Vigilance became damaged to the extent that the shields on the port side went down and the lasers started to score hits on the hull. The pirate ships Too Late Now and Minestra came in to finish it off, leaving the Vigilance a crippled wreck in space and Captain Eldon dead.

Before the Vigilance was defeated, it destroyed Take That! and Bnef Nlle, though the latter ship weakened the Vigilance port shields in a ramming attack. After the battle, it was salvaged by the pirate leader Renthal. She renamed her new acquisition the Renthal's Vigilance, turning it into her flagship and the largest ship in her fleet.

The ship's size and power came in handy in subsequent raids, especially when Drea assaulted the Queen of Empire by tugging a massive asteroid into place and knocking the luxury liner out of hyperspace.

Rickert Beagle was an male Alderaanian Communications Officer on board the Sunspire, a frigate that was gifted to the Alderaan Flotilla The flotilla was made up of seven vessels carrying what remained of the planet Alderaan, which had been destroyed by the Galactic Empire. While the ships were gathered in the remains of Alderaan within the Alderaan system, the Sunspire's sensors picked up several large ships approaching. Worried, Beagle reported via hologram to the Alderaanians' Regent Administrator Eglyn Valmor, but then quickly announced that the ships had New Republic code clearance. The new ships turned out to be bringing the wreckage of the Death Star to the flotilla as a gift from the New Republic, which some then suggested should be used to build a space station for the Alderaanians to live on.

Rickert Beagle first appeared in the novel Aftermath: Life Debt, which was written by Chuck Wendig and released in 2016.

In Eastport, Coruscant, a melee erupted between Houk and Weequay immigrants who were placed in adjacent holding rooms while waiting to be processed. Cultural enemies, they verbally assaulted each other before resorting to physical violence.

Since blasters were not allowed within the processing area, no shots were fired. However, those involved made use of blades and shivs to harm each other. In the end, fifteen were left for dead with forty-five wounded.

Creterk suffered a broken arm in the incident.

The Rise of the Cortosis Battle Droids was a campaign that occurred when the Confederacy of Independent Systems began to manufacture battle droids with cortosis, a lightsaber-resistant substance. The event ended with the destruction of the C-B3 cortosis battle droid factory on Metalorn.

A number of missions and skirmishes were involved in this campaign, including a Mission to Tatooine, the Coruscant Insurrection, a Duel in Bentho's Nightclub and a mission to the world of Metalorn.

While The New Essential Chronology originally dated Star Wars: The New Droid Army to ten months after the start of the Clone Wars, "Heroes on Both Sides," which is set in 20 BBY, later established that the planet Coruscant had not been attacked until the events of that episode, moving The New Droid Army forward in the timeline.

enrichments.description:
Roisem Barsha was a human female member of the Barsha family. She was married to Nnytyl Barsha and the mother of Jaylen and, together with her husband, the co-CEO of the Barsha Corporation from Corellia. She was also the unwilling stepmother to her husband's other son, Sliro Barsha, who she consistently treated as lesser than his half-brother. When Jaylen was eight years old, she gifted him two Fathier plushies, but purposefully didn't gift one to Sliro even though he would have liked them more than Jaylen. During the Clone Wars, the parents began to groom Jaylen Barsha to become the next CEO of the family company, while Sliro became a low ranking employee of Republic Intelligence.

During the official ceremony for the change of CEO in the early Imperial Era in 19 BBY, all of the members of the Barsha Corp's executive board were arrested by the Galactic Empire for conspiracy. They were tried and placed under house arrest at their compound on Corellia's moon Gus Treta. During their stay, the family were de facto on holiday. At some point into their stay, she gave the BX-series droid commando ND-5, who she believed to be one of the employed droids a green blazer to wear. Weeks after their trial, the executive board was pardoned and in celebration, Roisem Barsha held a party with family and friends at the compound. During the night, all of the Barsha family and their guests were assassinated by ND-5, who had actually been sent to kill everyone present. Roisem and Nnytyl were among the last killed and were witnessed by Jaylen who had tried to unsuccessfully save them. He was however able to survive by reprogramming ND-5 with the help of the compound's droid A1-A1 and thought dead.

Over the following nine years, their son, now known as Jaylen Vrax tried to find their murderer and ultimately learned that it was Sliro who had betrayed them to the Empire and after their pardon had sent ND-5 to kill them all instead. Throughout his adult years, Jaylen Vrax continued to remember his mother saying "you need to know when to say something or stay quiet" and often recited it to himself.

Roisem Barsha was a stern and goal-oriented mother to Jaylen. Because she didn't see him as a "full Barsha", Roisem mistreated Sliro as lesser to his half-brother and didn't treat him as her son, with him only calling her "Lady Barsha". Over the years her relationship with her husband, Nnytyl became distant and at their stay at the Barsha compound they almost never spoke with one another. Jaylen ultimately came to also become distant to his parents and had mixed feelings about them. Meanwhile, Sliro began to hate his father and Lady Barsha and see them as corrupt and as "architects of deception".

Rynog Asokaji was a male Bith and the aide-de-camp of the Admiral Nek Bwua'tu, Chief of the Galactic Alliance Navy. When an assassination attempt left Bwua'tu in a coma, Asokaji at first blamed Chief of State Natasi Daala for the act in retaliation for Bwua'tu's attempt to make a deal with interim Grand Master Kenth Hamner to allow the Jedi Order to launch their StealthXs. Daala merely praised him for his bravery and requested that he ask permission to speak freely with her in the future, and the two came to be on good terms. Asokaji later suspected that the Jedi were behind the attack, although Daala and her Chief of Staff, Wynn Dorvan, remained dubious. Asokaji offered to send 5,000 marines against the Jedi if Daala so wished, but she declined.

When Bwua'tu regained consciousness, Asokaji was delighted to see him again and was one of the few, along with Bwu'tu's uncle Eramuth Bwua'tu, Wynn Dorvan, and Leia and Han Solo, to know that he was still fully functional. Knowing that a conspiracy had targeted him, Bwua'tu feigned brain damage. Brainstorming between Dorvan and Bwua'tu over the recent events, namely the coup that overthrew Daala, led them to deduce that Bwua'tu's replacement, Admiral Sallinor Parova, was a part of the conspiracy. With assistance from Han Solo, Asokaji kidnapped Parova and they imprisonned her in the Jedi Temple. There, Dorvan, Bwua'tu and Asokaji interrogated Parova but she refused to tell them anything. A few moments after they left her, she was killed by members of the Lost Tribe of Sith.

The Sable III, originally known as the Anto's Star, was a modified Corellian CR90 corvette used by the flamboyant pirate Drek Drednar and his crew. The ship was stolen by a group of starship thieves working for Drednar who was planning a mutiny against Captain Karn Granzor.

The Anto's Star had was a standard corvette with a normal armament of 6 double turbolasers. After Drek Drednar and his crew took over the ship and defeated the gunship Sable II, the newly-commissioned Sable III received numerous upgrades: The mechanics upgraded the hull and shields and installed two salvaged gun turret mounts from the Sable II. These mounts were later equipped with an ion cannon and a tractor beam. Additionally, a salvaged tractor beam was installed for a front turbolaser.

The docking bay carried five non-hyperdrive snubfighter, usually three Z-95 Headhunters and two Zebra starfighters, leaving one slot for emergencies.

The ship was decorated with the "Blazing Claw" symbol, which had been an icon for piracy for thousands of years in the history of the galaxy.

The Saltbarrel was a freighter originally owned by the Watith captain Fsir. During the plot to destroy the Chiss Ascendancy, the Saltbarrel sent out a distress call to Senior Captain Thrawn of the Chiss Expansionary Defense Fleet. The Saltbarrel claimed to be under attack from Vagaari pirates, but was in reality under false attack by gunboats remotely piloted from aboard itself. This skirmish was meant to delay the Chiss officer from discovering the plot against the Ascendancy. Thrawn did not fall for the ruse, and ended up arresting Fsir and commandeering the Watith gunboats and the Saltbarrel. Thrawn later employed the commandeered starships at the Hoxim incident.

Sam Brunk was a male Human moisture farmer who lived on Tatooine during the time of the Galactic Empire. He was the husband of Dama Whitesun Brunk.

Sam Brunk and his wife Dama lived in the town of Anchorhead. Along with moisture farming, the two also operated a hotel. The two occupations kept both busy to the point that they infrequently visited the family of Dama's sister, Beru Lars, who lived twenty kilometers from Anchorhead.

Around 15 BBY, the couple got a new A-1 Deluxe Floater landspeeder. Some time after, the Brunks visited the Lars homestead. There, Sam gave the recent news of Podracing being outlawed by the Galactic Empire. During the visit, Sam was surprised to find that Beru's husband, Owen Lars, had removed his relatives' headstones from their graves at the homestead.

Saral Aenet was a grizzled female free trader and the captain of a Corellian G9 Rigger-class merchant ship, the Silver Star. Though Aenet and her crew were not formally rebels, they had no love for the Empire. They dealt in various legal goods, and occasionally traded antiquities. Whenever Aenet stumbled across a holocron in a market, she remembered the device from the stories of the Jedi in her childhood, and decided to secret it away from the Empire's reach.

At some point, Aenet's actions attracted the attention of Duke Erron Irbian, the Imperial ruler of Jorra, who callously gave Nex Pavros and his group of bounty hunters an order to intercept the Silver Star and kill the seven-member crew. After the massacre, a group of Force-sensitives discovered the Suljo Warde's holocron hidden in a secret compartment installed behind a computer terminal in the ship's cockpit.

Saras Loorne was a male Jedi Master and a Jedi General during the Clone Wars. In 19 BBY, Loorne, along with five other Jedi and a clone trooper task force, was dispatched to occupy the Outer Rim planet Murkhana, a Corporate Alliance stronghold. During the battle, Order 66—an order for the clone troopers to execute their Jedi officers—was issued, and Loorne and the two Jedi Knights accompanying him were killed by the clones of the 22nd Air Combat Wing.

Saras Loorne was a male Jedi Master who lived during the last decades of the Galactic Republic. When the Clone Wars between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems broke out, Loorne served as a Jedi General with the Grand Army of the Republic. Near the end of the war in 19 BBY, Loorne, along with five other Jedi and a contingent of clone troopers under the command of Clone Commander Salvo, was dispatched to invade the Outer Rim planet Murkhana, home to the Confederacy-allied Corporate Alliance.

The Republic task force was ordered to rendezvous in the Murkhana system, and after one week, they began their attack. Upon touching down on the planet in LAAT/i gunships, the Republic troops were greeted by Confederate rocket fire, but Loorne survived the attack. When Master Roan Shryne reached out for Loorne with the Force in order to find out if the Jedi Master was still alive, Loorne answered him affirmatively. After successfully landing on the surface, Republic and Separatist troops engaged each other in combat. In the midst of the battle, the clone troopers received Order 66—a dispatch for all clone troopers to slay their Jedi officers. Loorne and the two Jedi Knights who accompanied him were ambushed and executed by clones of the 22nd Air Combat Wing. The bodies of Loorne and the two Jedi Knights were later shown to the Sith Lord and Imperial Executor Darth Vader, during his visit to Murkhana, by Commander Salvo. The Commander also gave the lightsabers of the Jedi to Vader, who then ordered Salvo to dispose of the bodies.

Saras Loorne, a Force-sensitive male, possessed the knowledge and skills required to become a Jedi Master, and was placed in command of the Murkhana mission above Masters Shryne and Bol Chatak. However, he was unable to defend himself against the clone troopers, resulting in his death.

Sarn Vals was a Quarren Jedi Knight serving the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive, Sarn Vals was discovered by the Jedi Order as an infant and instructed in the ways of the Force at the Coruscant Jedi Temple. Eventually completing training and passing the Trials of Knighthood, Vals was elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight by the Jedi High Council. Serving the Order throughout the Clone Wars, a violent and costly conflict between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Vals was able to survive an attack by the Grand Army of the Republic in 19 BBY. The Grand Army, which the Order had fought alongside and commanded during the entire conflict, turned on their Jedi leaders when Supreme Chancellor Palpatine betrayed the Jedi and initiated Contingency Order 66 in a secret scheme to destroy the Order.

Fleeing into exile, Vals escaped to the Corporate Sector and went to ground. However, when a disturbance was reported in the sector, the Inquisitorius of the newly formed Galactic Empire traced it back to the fugitive Vals and sent agents to locate and destroy the Quarren Jedi outlaw.

Sawj Luzo was a male Human Sith Saber of the Lost Tribe of Sith. Around 3960 BBY, for his devotion to the Grand Lord Lillia Venn, he was promoted, with his elder brother Flen Luzo, to the rank of Sith Lord after the events of the Korsinata. The Luzo brothers were rivals of Orielle Kitai in the Sith Saber leadership. Under Lillia Venn, they acted as executioners and took pleasure in their work, like the public execution of Dernas, the leader of the Red Faction and Pallima, who lead the Gold Faction. A few days later, they were sent to Jelph Marrian's farm to execute Ori Kitai's uvak, Shyn and give her two scrolls, which stated that her mother, Candra Kitai had plotted with the High Lords of the Red and Gold factions to assassinate Grand Lord Venn. Her mother had signed both scrolls, which also stated that Candra, now Venn's slave, pledged her eternal loyalty to the Grand Lord. The Luzo brothers confiscated Orielle's lightsaber, gave her a shovel symbolic of her new life as a slave, and returned to Tahv.

After being tipped off by Candra about her daughter's discovery of a working starship, they returned to the farm they visited a few days ago, this time accompanied by Grand Lord Venn herself, where they confronted an unexpectant Orielle. While Venn immobilized Kitai with the Force, several guards took hold of her. Venn explained that Candra had alerted Venn to the meeting, betraying her daughter in exchange for what Venn called "improved working conditions." While Venn entered Marrian's starfighter, her guards held Kitai in place. Kitai's rescue came under the guise of former Jedi Knight and Covenant Shadow, Jelph Marrian. After shooting her two captors from behind and firing blaster shots in the Luzos' direction, Marrian led her toward the river as Venn powered up the starfighter, unaware that he had used the ship's proton torpedoes and thousands of kilograms of ammonium-nitrate-based explosives—converted from common fertilizer—to create an anti-theft system for the vessel. As Venn ascended, the torpedoes detonated, killing Venn, the Luzos, and the guards. Orielle and Marrian fled the farm, which, along with the entire bank, sank into the river as a result of the explosion.

Sawj and his older brother Flen Luzo were members of the Lost Tribe of Sith, the descendants of a group of stranded Human Sith who had colonized the planet Kesh during the Great Hyperspace War. He grew up almost a millennium after the reign of Grand Lord Nida Korsin, who had ruled for 79 years. By that time, the Force-sensitive members of the Tribe had become the new ruling elite on the continent of Keshtah Minor and lorded over the native Keshiri, who had become a large serf underclass which worshiped the Sith as the a race of gods known as the Protectors. Internal divisions had also emerged within the Tribe with two important political factions being the Red and the Gold Factions, led by the High Lords Dernas and Pallima respectively.

Scar Blenner was a large Human, and a member of the Blood Raptors gang on Genarius. When the Rodian Teeloo accidentally destroyed a Blood Raptor snubfighter, Blenner went to Teeloo's docking bay and ambushed the Rodian. He had his Raptors take Teeloo's cargo, and told Teeloo he would be able to get his cargo back if he beat one of them in a race through Eskaron. If Teeloo lost, they would take his ship. Scar wrote the coordinates of the race on the Rodian's forehead to humiliate him. He was still roughing Teeloo up when some passing samaritans interfered and chased him off.

Blenner also led the group that wanted to take Teeloo's ship after the race, unless he was killed in the first scene, in which case he was replaced with Vhell Kursoc. Else, Blenner would be killed in the last scene.

Captain Scarlet Bloodhawk was a Rebel sympathizer who operated, at different times, a repairing port for starships and a smuggler starship.

Scarlet Bloodhawk was a female who owned a spaceport with repair facilities during the Galactic Civil War, which was staffed by herself, her domodroid H2-1B4, and the Ky'lessan known as "Snake-Eyes" among others. At some point, Snake-Eyes turned on Bloodhawk, locking her up in her own quarters and taking control of the spaceport. During this time, tasks such as maintaining the landing beacons were neglected.

While Bloodhawk was imprisoned, an old friend of hers arrived at the spaceport with their ship and crew needing repairs. While Snake-Eyes pretended to help them, he in fact called in the Galactic Empire to capture the Rebels in return for a reward. H2-1B4, loyal to Bloodhawk and knowing her old friend as well, relayed Snakes-Eyes' intentions to the group of Rebels. The Rebels broke into Bloodhawk's quarters and freed her. However, during the attempt, the alarm was raised and Scarlet, H2-1BA and the Rebels were forced to flee into the wilderness. With the Empire due to arrive soon, Bloodhawk and the group sneaked into the repair dock where their ship was held and succeeded in taking control of it. However, an Imperial cutter was inbound to their position, and the group discovered that the engines of their ship had been sabotaged. Bloodhawk and H2-1B4 worked to repair the ship while the spacers exchanged fire with Imperial troops outside. Eventually, the ship was repaired and lifted off, pursued by the cutter. The spacers attempted to engaged the ship's hyperdrive, but found it inoperable.

Scarlet Bloodhawk was known to not spare expenses in important tasks, including maintenance of landing beacons. She was also a trustworthy friend.

Scover Byne was a female Bivall who was the owner of the Byne Guild, an organization that handled shipping throughout the Galactic Frontier during the High Republic Era. Byne was the foster mother of the Guild pilot Affie Hollow, whom she was training to help take responsibility over the Guild. Byne often traveled on the Guild freighter Legacy Run. After the Legacy Run was destroyed in the Great Hyperspace Disaster, Hollow worried for Byne's safety. Byne was later arrested and her Guild dissolved after Hollow turned her in to Galactic Republic authorities for abusing laws regarding indentured servitude after she discovered that Byne had been forcing her indentured laborers to take on extremely dangerous work in exchange for shortened indentures.

Scover Byne appeared in the 2021 novel The High Republic: Into the Dark, written by Claudia Gray.

The Sealion was a prototype Missile Boat delivered to the Rebel Alliance.

The Sealion was a Missile Boat prototype, that was stolen by forces under the command of Rogue Grand Admiral Zaarin. When Zaarin conferred to his officers about the second Death Star and that the Rebels were actually walking into a trap at Endor but didn't intend to warn them, one of his loyal commanders Namuura Din who lead the Victory-class Star Destroyer Zeplin decided to take the information and the Sealion and defect to the Alliance. While Zaarin was unable to stop him, Loyalist forces led by Darth Vader in the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Garrett managed to intercept and capture Din's flagship, but by the time they arrived the Sealion was already transferred to the Mon Calamari Cruiser Link and the cruiser jumped to lightspeed.

The commander of the Link attempted to get the news to Rebel Command, but the ships engines overloaded forcing the ship out of Hyperspace. The Link commander sent the Sealion to a Rebel stronghold, a XQ4 Platform Enin'sd to be fully analyzed. But the Rebels never got the chance to disassemble the vessel and learn its secrets before the Imperials arrived at the base with the intention of either destroying or otherwise illicitly recovering the Sealion, as the Prophets of the Dark Side discovered when recovering it illicitly before its container was destroyed, preventing any chance of the Rebels making their own Missile Boats. Nonetheless, the Rebel's capture of the Sealion, combined with the treacherous Grand Admiral Zaarin's breakaway faction's destruction of the Missile Boat's production facilities via planetary bombardment, led to the suspension of all Missile Boats from service until further notice at Emperor Palpatine's order, with all remaining Missile Boats being placed into a secure holding area.

The Sealion only appears in Star Wars: TIE Fighter Battle 13 Combat 4. The first mission regarding the prototype shows the ship on the Link and the third and final mission about the fighter hiding in one of the Class-B cargo container group Niicee.

In 228 BBY, Jedi Masters Keeve Trennis and Avar Kriss, alongside bounty hunter and former Nihil pirate Lourna Dee, spearheaded a search for ailing Jedi Master Sskeer and Nihil Minister of Advancement Baron Boolan after the two were captured by Muglan Tarantyne's crew and brought into the custody of Eye of the Nihil Marchion Ro on the planet Heiklet. However, Sskeer and Boolan eventually escaped Heiklet on their own and traveled to Boolan's former home on the planet Dalna. There, they were recovered by the Jedi and brought to the planet Protobranch for medical attention, and so that Boolan could help the Galactic Republic researchers there find a solution for the mysterious blight spreading across the galaxy. However, Ro and the Nihil pursued Sskeer and Boolan to Protobranch, where Dee dueled and bested Ro, who warned that Boolan had created a virus that would kill all life and was pretending it was a cure for the blight. With Dee's warning, the Jedi and the Republic were able to contain the virus, provide an antidote to those already infected, and arrest Boolan.

The Second Battle of Cyclor, or as the Skirmish over Cyclor, was a Nihil attack on the Cyclor Shipyards in 231 BBY. It occurred not long after the Battle of Valo, where the Dowutin Tempest Runner Pan Eyta left his fellow Tempest Runner Lourna Dee for dead when Republic reinforcements arrived. Dee survived and returned to the Nihil base on Grizal, where she witnessed Eyta be poisoned by Marchion Ro, the Eye of the Nihil, for challenging his authority and for his previous failures. Dee seemingly saved Eyta with an injection of cypanid, a substance from Ryloth that did not cure him but instead prolonged his agony, and convinced him to launch a second attack on the Republic.

Eavesdropping on a communication from Senator Tia Toon to the Cyclor Shipyards, Eyta learned that the Jedi Order was withdrawing its forces to Hetzal Prime and Starlight Beacon, and so chose to attack the shipyards—only for him to find an entire battle fleet waiting for his cruiser, the Elegencia, when it arrived. The Republic had recently discovered that the Nihil were tapping into their communications and laid a false trail to ambush the Nihil forces, and Dee had also gone behind Eyta's back and convinced the majority of his Tempest to abandon him as he had done to them on Valo. Upon realizing that he was betrayed, the severely-ill Eyta fled the Elegencia a secret escape pod and left the rest of his forces to be wiped out by the Republic.

However, the crime lord Reegas Vance also planned to salvage the derelict and to prevent Faal and Idi-Shael from interfering with his plans, he fired upon the Seeker with his YT-2400 light freighter Blackstar, disabling the Seeker. Faal and Idi-Shael then donned space suits and abandoned the Seeker, while Vance led a boarding party over to the stricken vessel. The Separatist Coalition was an organization active by during the reign of the Galactic Empire, which Chandrilan Imperial Senator Mon Mothma was a part of and attended meetings of. In that year, the Empire had grown suspicious of Mothma's activities and supplanted individuals she regularly encountered with Imperial spies to uncover her dealings.

To that end, though many others still believed her to be just an irritation due to her fights against Imperial overreach and for Separatist sympathizers, Imperial Grand Vizier Mas Amedda began infiltrating the coalition's meetings. Aware of the Empire's spying and wanting it so they would miss her machinations, Mothma revealed the Vizier's infiltrations to Chandrilan banker Tay Kolma, whom she had sought to recruit as well as gain help from to regain access to her family accounts used to fund a secret network of anti-Imperial individuals.
