enrichments.description:
This individual served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a Jedi Knight.

A Force-sensitive, this individual received training in the ways of the Force at an academy and eventually attained the rank of Knight. Accepting the role of General at the beginning of the Clone Wars, this individual was stationed on Murkhana during the last part of the war. Participating in the battle there under the leadership of Jedi Master Saras Loorne, this Jedi was aboard a Republic gunship with Loorne and another Knight when the Republic's Supreme Chancellor betrayed the Order with the issuance of Contingency Order 66. The clone troopers under this Jedi's command obeyed the executive order and shot down the Jedi's gunship, killing all three.

enrichments.description:
A male Human Jedi Master served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive male Human was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, eventually attaining the rank of Jedi Master. Constructing a double-bladed lightsaber imbued with green crystals at its core, this Master was proficient in it use during lightsaber combat. During his years of service to the Order, the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems went to war, drawing the Jedi Order into the conflict known as the Clone Wars. The Master was stationed at the Coruscant Jedi Temple in 19 BBY when Supreme Chancellor Palpatine of the Republic betrayed the Order by issuing Contingency Order 66 to the Grand Army of the Republic. Led by Sith Lord Darth Vader, the 501st Legion marched on the Jedi Temple and began to slaughter all of its occupants, Masters, Knights, and Initiates alike.

As the forces of the 501st Legion stormed the Temple as part of Operation: Knightfall, this man came to possess a valuable holocron and attempted to escape the Temple with the artifact. While putting up a fight, this Master was slain by Darth Vader during the fighting and the holocron fell into the hands of the Dark Lord of the Sith, Darth Sidious.

This Jedi Master is killed by the player in Star Wars: Battlefront II, but the means of his execution is not standardized. He can be killed either as Vader or a clone trooper at the whim of the player.

enrichments.description:
A male Jedi Master served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars, becoming a key member of the Vaklin insurgency at the start of the Great Jedi Purge.

A Force-sensitive male was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, eventually attaining the rank of Jedi Master by the time of the Clone Wars. Taking on a Padawan, they served together in the Grand Army of the Republic and both avoided execution during the initial stages of the Galactic Empire's ascent to power. Together with his former student and Jedi Cho'na Bene they went into hiding on Vaklin, a very pro-Jedi world.

A key member of the Vaklin insurgency, he was the first to be captured by Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader. Surrendering and taken prisoner by the Sith, Vader believed that the man was far too good of a swordsman to be taken alive and dumped him out an airlock as a form of execution.

enrichments.description:
This individual was a male Human Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive, this Human received training in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, ascending to the rank of Jedi Master. Constructing two blue-bladed lightsabers, this Master was proficient in their use during lightsaber combat.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, this man took up the rank of General in the Grand Army of the Republic. Surviving three years of war, he was stationed at the Coruscant Jedi Temple when the Republic's Supreme Chancellor Palpatine betrayed the Order and issued Contingency Order 66 to the Grand Army, ordering them to kill their Jedi leaders. As the forces of the 501st Legion stormed the Temple as part of Operation: Knightfall, this man joined other masters and led a final charge against clone troopers on the Temple Veranda. While fighting valiantly against the clones under the command of Darth Vader, this Master and his companions were slain during the fighting and the Temple fell into the hands of the Dark Lord of the Sith, Darth Sidious.

This Jedi Master used two blue-bladed lightsabers in combat. He was a skilled combatant, demonstrated by the fact that he was one of the last Jedi standing during the march on the Temple.

Sometime during the Great Galactic War and the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire, the notorious pirate Harridax Kirill captured a vessel belonging to the Jedi Order that was carrying Force-sensitive children. Kirill, better known as the Voidwolf, personally led the boarding party that killed the Jedi defenders aboard the starship, and he took the children to the Sith planet of Korriban as a "gift" to the Empire. The Empire rewarded the Voidwolf by promoting him from privateer to commander in the Imperial Navy.

As Dobbs showed Zeveron the bracelet, he informed her of the rumor it had belonged to the Lord of the Sith. In response, however, the woman stated the object was not what the Path was looking for.

The Lord of the Sith was mentioned in the young-adult novel The High Republic: Path of Deceit, written by Justina Ireland and Tessa Gratton as part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's Within the novel, the Lord of the Sith was mentioned in a chapter written by Ireland.

An orange planet was located in the Earth system. Comparable in size to a gas giant, it was the second-closest planet to Earth.

Han Solo and Chewbacca of the Millennium Falcon, having entered this star system while evading the Imperial Navy sometime after the Battle of Endor, passed by this planet before being caught in the gravity well of Jones's homeworld.

The planet, alongside three other planets, including Earth, appeared in the non-canon Dark Horse Comics comic serial "Into the Great Unknown," which acted as a crossover between the Star Wars and Indiana Jones franchises. The appearance and corresponding location of Jones' homeworld (which is heavily implied but not directly stated to be Earth) implied that it was Jupiter, the largest planet in the Solar System.

According to a legend, a long time before a planet served as the home of the Wookiee species. However, they left the planet in favor of the world of Kashyyyk,

Wookiee records rarely mentioned the planet, and when they did, they only gave vague information, which included a suggestion that the Wookiees who came to Kashyyyk were pioneers or refugees. In 0 BBY, the Wookiee Attichitcuk told the story of the Wookiees' old planet to his grandson, Lumpawarrump.

The planet was first mentioned in The Wookiee Storybook, a 1978 young readers book written by Eleanor Ehrhardt.

A large, glowing planet was located in a star system with one sun, and was orbited by a set of planetary rings. The rings, consisting mostly of ice drifts, constantly shed vapor and reflected light from the planet's star, which confused most starships' sensor sweeps and made them an ideal place for smugglers to hide.

In 35 ABY, during the war between the First Order and the Resistance, Commander Poe Dameron of the Resistance, having learned of the hiding spot sometime prior, guided his fellow Resistance members to the planet's rings in the starship Bestoon Legacy following a mission to the planet Pasaana. Shortly afterward, the Resistance members departed for the planet Kijimi,

While the planet itself was not seen, its rings first appeared in the 2019 film Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker. The planet was first mentioned in the 2020 novelization of the film, written by Rae Carson.

enrichments.description:
In 0 ABY, Storm-hair Warlord Nuso Esva traveled aboard his Kazellis-class light freighter Salaban's Hope to an unknown and unremarkable terrestrial planet that orbited an unremarkable sun for more than five hours before returning to the Imperial II-class Star Destroyer Chimaera. Senior Captain Thrawn of the Galactic Empire speculated that the world was where Esva met with his commanders to finish their preparations for a battle against the Empire in the Candoras sector's Poln system, a theory the senior captain shared with the former smuggler Jorj Car'das after the battle.

The planet was mentioned in Timothy Zahn's 2011 novel Choices of One.

enrichments.description:
A Sith Lord ruled on the Outer Rim planet Athiss millennia before 0 BBY. He was betrayed by his allies, killed, and entombed in a sarcophagus deep inside his own temple. Over the following years, knowledge of the Sith Lord's tomb was hidden by his betrayers and became corrupted, leading to his name being lost to history.

Due to the incomplete records, by the time of the Battle of Yavin a group of lore-seekers had come to believe the Sith Lord's final resting place was actually a tomb of a Jedi and a source of Force-related knowledge. The group journeyed to Athiss to find the tomb. Once there, they battled Sithspawn and a dark side illusion, which, using the fears and perceptions of the explorers, adopted the Sith Lord's appearance.

The Sith Lord was first mentioned in "Lost Knowledge," a roleplaying game adventure written by John Dunn and published as part of Fantasy Flight Games' 2014 Star Wars: Force and Destiny Beta book. The discovery of the Sith Lord's tomb by the player characters forms a portion of the adventure. This article assumes the scenario plays out as described.

The ship was described by Jagged Fel as compact and sleek, and completely unknown to anything he had ever seen before. The ship could also move with "astonishing speed" and was equipped with a Laser weapon. However, it was no match for the power of the Dunelizard's Laser cannon.

A starship was owned by the hunter Riegenn Hetuu during the time of the Galactic Republic. The starship needed at least one person to operate it, and had a cargo bay equipped with life support systems. Hetuu used the ship's cargo bay to hold a live k'lor'slug queen that he had captured for a Hutt who intended to use the beast in a yearly gladiatorial tournament. He flew his ship to the planet Hutta, where the Hutt was located, but the worm-like k'lor'slug had laid eggs in the cargo bay that quickly hatched into nearly four hundred k'lorslugs. When the Hutt arrived at the ship, Hetuu opened the cargo bay to present the Hutt with his prize. However, the hoard of k'lorslugs swarmed out and devoured both Hetuu and his Hutt client.

Riegenn Hetuu's starship was indirectly mentioned in Star Wars: The Old Republic, a 2011 MMORPG produced by BioWare. The starship was mentioned as part of the k'lor'slug codex entry, which could be found by players who killed the k'lor'slug broodwatcher in the tomb of the Sith Lord Ajunta Pall on the planet Korriban.

A starship was traveling through the Kolatill system, which was located in the Kathol sector of the Outer Rim Territories, in 8 ABY. Around the same time that the escort carrier Kathol Protector—a starship serving in the military forces of the Imperial warlord Moff Kentor Sarne—attacked Domaz, the capital city of the planet Kolatill, this vessel was attacked. The assault crippled the vessel, leaving it adrift between planets. The derelict was discovered by a starfighter patrol from the New Republic CR90 corvette FarStar, which was in-system responding to a distress signal from Kolatill. The corvette's crew deployed a rescue team to investigate the wreck and see if any survivors were sealed in airtight sections.

The starship was mentioned in the roleplaying adventure "Omens," part of The DarkStryder Campaign, published by West End Games in 1995. The discovery of the ship is a possible side adventure that the players may undertake during the scenario. The players can search the ship for crew members that may still be alive, although whether they discover any is left to the discretion of the gamemaster.

During the attack, two members of the Ro family, the mothers of the cousins Marda and Yana, killed the Theelin family and took their ship. After they escaped, the ship's life-support systems began to fail and the Ros experienced days of hunger and cold.

Eventually, the family was towed by a Hutt trawler to Nar Shaddaa where the Hutts attempted to enslave the Ros. In 382 BBY, as the cousins spoke about Yana's plans to leave the Path of the Open Hand cult they had since joined, Yana mentally recalled their mothers taking the Theelin family's ship and the subsequent events involving it.

The Theelin family's ship was mentioned in the 2022 young-adult novel The High Republic: Path of Deceit, written by Justina Ireland and Tessa Gratton as part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's Within the novel, the ship was mentioned in a chapter written by Ireland.

enrichments.description:
Upulu was a male Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive, Upulu was educated in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order. Attaining the rank of Jedi Master, Master Upulu selected the young Mon Calamari Initiate Shalimin as his Padawan during the Separatist Crisis.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Master Upulu took up the rank of General in the Grand Army of the Republic. While Master Upulu was away fighting, Padawan Shalimin was selected to serve beside Jedi High Council member Kit Fisto during the Battle of Dac where the two led the Republic to victory over the Confederacy. As the report came to the Coruscant Jedi Temple, Fisto detailed how Shalimin had reveled in the victory in a way unbecoming of a Jedi. Shamed by his Padawan's actions Upulu sent Shalimin to the planet Argul to assist in the defensive there. While an initial failure, Grand Master Yoda arrived with reinforcements which ensured a Republic victory.

Vaas Ga was a Duros male Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive, Vaas Ga was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, achieving the rank of Jedi Master by the start of the Clone Wars. The war, a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, saw Master Ga pushed into the role of General within the newly created Grand Army of the Republic. Placed in command of Sarlacc Battalion A and B of the 41st Elite Corps, he saw battle on many fronts.

During the war, Master Ga and his troops were assigned to take the planet Dinlo, working closely with Senior Clone Commander Gree. Overwhelmed during the fighting, Ga and his men were rescued by General Etain Tur-Mukan and the clone troopers of Improcco Company during the skirmish. While looking a little worse for wear, Master Ga did not sustain severe injuries during the costly battle and returned to Coruscant for new orders.

enrichments.description: The Vahla homeworld was the homeworld of the Vahla, a Force-sensitive, Near-Human species with ties to the dark side. The planet was believed to have been taken over by Vahl, a Force Adept who led her followers and was later deified by the cultists of the Ember of Vahl. The ancient Vahla were regarded as twisted and decadent, and several thousand years before the Sith–Imperial War, the cult was decimated by the Jedi Knights in an attempt to quash their dark and destructive tendencies. Since then, the Vahla traveled the galaxy as nomads, searching endlessly for their lost homeworld.

Vaius Antinus was a male record keeper who lived circa 5000 BBY. He was a contemporary of several Sith Lords, such as Tulak Hord and Aloysius Kallig. In those days, bloodlines were regarded as very important, and Antinus recorded the genealogies of the greatest Sith Lords of his time. Following his passing, he was buried on the Core World of Alderaan, a fact that was well known to later archaeologists. During his life, Antinus had also trained an apprentice whose name had been lost to history by the time of the Cold War. Given that both the Reclamation Service of the Sith Empire and members of the Jedi Order took an interest in the tomb of Antinus's apprentice on Aduba-6, the record keeper was probably in some way affiliated with the Sith or the Jedi.

Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia

The Valorous was a Victory-class Star Destroyer of the Imperial Navy assigned to Black Sword Command. It was later captured by the Yevetha following an uprising led by them, and the ship was renamed the Devotion of Yevetha or simply the Devotion.

The Valorous had large numbers of weapons ports and paired starfighter bays on either side of the hull. The fighter complemment included a number of TIE/rc starfighters for long-range reconnaissance, and the ship's weaponry was capable of subjugating settlements of considerable size, such as that on Polneye.

In 4 ABY, the Valorous was assigned to Black Sword Command and based in the Koornacht Cluster. Along with the Super Star Destroyer Intimidator, she was one of two Imperial warships seized substantially intact at N'zoth by the native Yevetha in their coup eight months after the Battle of Endor. Subsequently, together with a number of Type II Orbital Repair Yards such as Black Fifteen, plus a number of ships under construction and undergoing repair, they became the nucleus of the Black Fleet.

The surviving Imperial crewers from Valorous, along with their counterparts from Intimidator, were sent to Camp Pa'aal and forced to assist their captors with the reverse-engineering and copying of Imperial technology, and the two Star Destroyers were renamed and incorporated into the fleet of the Duskhan League. However, unbeknownst to the Yevetha, the Imperial survivors they had retained for their technical skill, led by Major Sil Sorannan, secretly equipped every Imperial-designed ship in the Black Fleet with extensive slave circuitry which would eventually enable them to regain control.

Varesk Bura'lya was a male Bothan undersecretary who worked for the Bothan embassy on the planet Coruscant. Shortly after the formation of the Empire, he feared for his life and contacted the resistance movement Whiplash seeking help for safe passage offworld.

Bura'lya was escorted by former Jedi Jax Pavan and his crew which consisted of I-Five, Den Dhur and Laranth Tarak. During his extraction, their group was ambushed by a squad of stormtroopers in their final checkpoint. A brief shootout ensued where everyone from their group emerged relatively unharmed, with exception to Bura'lya who fainted and lost control of his bladder.

They eventually made it to the rendezvous point and he boarded the freighter Big Score.

Vek Alakor was a female archaeologist active after the reign of the Galactic Empire. She mentored the Lucem Sian, who adopted his mentor's surname in her honor, and was concerned with returning important artifacts to their rightful home. One such artifact was Luke Skywalker's yellow lightsaber. One of the worlds she and Sian discovered was a world with a pollen that degraded metal over time, and Vek named it Alakor after herself. She was also an associate of the Pirate Queen Maz Kanata. By 33 ABY, Alakor had died at the hands of the First Order.

Veltzz Arakyd was a male industrialist who founded the droid, starship and weapons manufacturer Arakyd Industries with his children on the planet Vulpter around nine thousand years before the Battle of Yavin. Even in the company's earliest days, Arakyd dedicated himself to eliminating competetion no matter the means. His earliest droid models were equipped with weaponry, flouting Old Republic laws that regulated the manufacture and sale such of droids. The weaponry intimidated rivals, ultimately inducing many to become subsidiaries out of fear. By the rise of the Galactic Empire, Arakyd engaged in political maneuvering, bribery and elimination of his competitors to position Arakyd Industries as the Empire's main droid manufacturer. The loyalty of Arakyd and his company eventually won Arakyd Industries contracts for weapons and vehicles as well. With the dawn of the New Republic, he briefly retired from the public view to regroup and Arakyd Industries changed to new leadership.

Veltzz Arakyd was a ruthless businessman who was willing to use any means necessary to eliminate competitors. He was known for tactics including bribery, bullying and intimidation to advance his company's interests.

Veltzz Arakyd's namesake company Arakyd Industries was first mentioned in the 1987 roleplaying game sourcebook The Star Wars Sourcebook, written by Bill Slavicsek and Curtis Smith. Arakyd was later identified as the company's founder in Del Rey's 2004 reference book The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology by W. Haden Blackman.

Although The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology stated that Veltzz Arakyd founded Arakyd Industries some nine thousand years before the Battle of Yavin, it also indicated that he lived during the Imperial and Post-Imperial eras. It's unclear whether this was an error or if other factors account for Arakyd's long lifespan.

However, the former scout Dayla Kev hijacked the conference, seeking revenge against Troper for abandoning her to die on a jungle world many years earlier. Kev and her allies released various dangerous predators aboard the ship, driving Andsof, Troper and several of their security guards deep into the jungle biosphere of the ship, while falling under constant attack from the creatures.

Vodal Kressh was a Dark Lord of the Sith who lived a thousand years before the Cold War.

A descendant of Ludo Kressh, Vodal was an Alchemist who was considered to be the greatest in the Empire. However, as his madness and power grew, he rebelled against the Sith Emperor and fled to the planet Athiss which would become his final resting place. Even after his death and burial, many of his rebellious servants remained on the planet and their descendants occupied Vodal Kressh's tomb until they were wiped out by a strike team during the Cold War a thousand years later.

By the time of the Battle of Yavin thousands of years later, it was rumored that the Republic had destroyed Kressh and his followers, but that a dark cult still protected his tomb.

The Vorantis was a starship owened by the pilot Brantis Mo Fresk. Mo Fresk participated in the Karee Blockade Clutch in his ship where he beat the starship Brightfox. Later that year, the New Republic operative Han Solo and his friend Lando Calrissian visited Frander's Bay—a space station that orbited the Core Worlds planet Chandrila—in search of an unaffiliated pilot to hire. The barker of Mo Fresk—who offered his services as a pilot at Frander's Bay—mentioned the Vorantis and Mo Fresk's victory over the Brightfox in the Karee Blockade Clutch into one of Solo's ears. Solo and Calrissian ultimately hired the pilot Taka Jamoreesa.

The Vorantis was mentioned in the 2018 novel Last Shot, written by Daniel José Older.

Wac Bur was a male Rodian who worked as a counterfeiter and forger. In 24 ABY, he sold fake art to Gebbu the Hutt who, in retaliation, sent the bounty hunter Boba Fett after him. Fett tracked Bur down on the of Coruscant. After leading Fett in a mad chase through a network of alleyways, Bur hid in a pile of crates and fruitlessly attempted to plead for his life. He was killed by Fett when he refused to surrender.

Unusually overweight for a Rodian, Wac Bur was a cowardly individual. He was also highly hypocritical, attempting to lecture Fett on morality when he himself was nothing more than a criminal.

Wac Bur first appeared in Karen Traviss' 2006 eBook Boba Fett: A Practical Man.

Walda Ceen was a Near-Human female who worked for CreedCon Construction during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

When CreedCon began construction of a race track through the jungles of the planet Cularin, Ceen was part of a group of construction workers who were tasked with building a bridge for part of the race course. However, they uncovered a mysterious cavern, which was home to an ancient creature, the t'salak, that had been imprisoned there by the Tarasin. The Dark Jedi Raik Muun traveled there and tried to free the creature, but was unable to do so, so took out her anger by capturing all the workers at the bridge construction site, including Buume.

Muun took the captured workers to TX-38, a deserted factory, located on Tilnes, a moon of Cularin. She managed to obtain the t'salak and it touched Ceen and the other workers with its tendrils, causing them all to enter a violent rage. However, they were eventually rescued by the Heroes of Cularin.

enrichments.description:
Waldan Bridger was a bald and burly male Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A male Force-sensitive, Waldan Bridger was educated in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, eventually attaining the rank of Jedi Knight. As a Knight, Bridger pursued the path of the Jedi Guardian during his independent studies, fashioning for himself a San-Ni staff which he wielded in place of a lightsaber. A ranking Jedi Weapon Master, Bridger eventually was made a Jedi Master by the Jedi High Council for his knowledge and power in the Force.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Master Bridger dutifully took up the title of General within the newly formed Grand Army of the Republic, leading clone troopers in battle against the Separatist Droid Army. 22 months after the start of the war, Bridger led a campaign to bring the war-plagued planet of Togoria back into the Republic. The Togorians had voluntarily joined the CIS, however, and viewed the Republic as invaders. When Bridger brought his landing party down on the world, the natives attacked and massacred the clone troopers under Bridger's command. The Togorians were bolstered by the leader of the Confederacy's army, General Grievous, who saw to it that he alone would face the Jedi. Bridger attacked Grievous head-on, but the duel lasted only twenty seconds. Grievous' lightsabers cut through Bridger's staff and the Jedi Master's body, killing him instantly. Grievous, victorious, left Bridger's body where it fell for the ravenous native mosgoth beasts.

Waldan Bridger was created by Daniel Wallace for the canceled guidebook known as The Essential Guide to Episode I. Along with Jedi L'lacielo Sageon, Bridger was described as serving as one of the Jedi Temple's quartermasters at the time of the Invasion of Naboo. Both Jedi's first names are anagrams of their creator's name; the letters from both names combined can be reconfigured to spell, 'Daniel Wallace.' The names Waldan and L'lacielo are older then the canceled guidebook however. Author Abel G. Peña originally intended to name one of his own creations "Waldan L'lacielo"; the name was changed during the editing of this particular text to Awdrysta Pina.

enrichments.description:
Wall Bennis was a male Human Jedi who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a member of the Agricultural Corps.

A Force-sensitive Human, Wall Bennis was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order and ultimately assigned to work as the director of the Marfa-based labs of the Agricultural Corps. Serving the AgriCorps during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire, Bennis worked with Hestizo Trace in researching flora on the planet. During their work one morning, the bounty hunter Tulkh infiltrated the facility in search for the Murakami orchid on behalf of Darth Scabrous. While Trace was tending to another sections of the facility, Tulkh impaled Trace with a spear. Trace saw Bennis' body impaled on a Malpassian squid pine and attempted to flee before being captured by Tulkh.

While Bennis was gravely injured, Jedi healers were able to treat him in time. Making a full recovery, Bennis bore a scar on his chest where he had been impaled. Bennis greeted Trace when she returned from her imprisonment with the Empire, and encouraged her when she decided to return to Coruscant.

The War on Corellia was a civil war that took place in the wake of the Nihil infiltration of the planet Corellia. Following the destruction of Starlight Beacon, the Nihil took root on the planet, and a contingent of Corellians believed the only way to prevent the planet from sharing the same fate as Starlight Beacon was to embrace the Nihil's rule. They were opposed by Corellians such as Alys "Crash" Ongwa and Svi'no Atchapat. Two Jedi—Jedi Master Conithr and her Padawan, Ruu—chose to not to return to Coruscant after the Jedi Order recalled the Jedi there, instead choosing to remain on Corellia to defend the Corellians from the Nihil. During one incident, Conithr was killed, causing Ruu to fall to the dark side of the Force and stop operating as a Jedi.

A massacre of Nihil forces occurred at the Greens

The War on Corellia was first mentioned in the reference book Star Wars: Timelines.

Waz-alem Amir was a male Cerean, who worked for Culpharm on the planet Cularin, during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

Amir worked as a biochemist for Culpharm, a pharmaceutical company that was based on the planet Cularin. He carried out research for the company from a lab that was located in his house, on the edge of the city of Hedrett. He also employed the Tarasin Ta'Mara as a cleaner.

In about 32 BBY, Amir began studying a plant that was reputed to have medicinal properties. After examining it in his personal laboratory, he wanted to study the sample using specialist equipment in the Culpharm Central Laboratory, so he called Culpharm Security and arranged for the sample to be transported there. A Human and Wookiee dressed in Culpharm Security uniforms turned up at his house and collected the sample. However, they were in fact employees of Biotherapy, a rival company of Culpharm, who hoped to discover what Amir had been developing. Two genuine Culpharm Security guards, Blut and Mien, turned up a short time later and Amir informed them that the samples had already been collected.

Culpharm hired the Heroes of Cularin to investigate the disappearance of the samples. They traveled to Amir's house and asked him some questions about the circumstances surrounding their disappearance.

Weet was a transport containing Rebel spies hiding inside a Rebel Class-D cargo container Pi, surrounded by Type A mines. The minefield was cleared by a single Assault Gunboat, Mu 1, and was inspected to see what was hiding inside. The transport was then launched from the container and attempted to escape, only to be disabled by the Gunboat. System Patrol Craft Scythis then boarded the transport and captured it.

The event was recorded and used to train future pilots on how to use a Gunboat. One of those pilots was Maarek Stele.

Wellam Adarios was a captain in the Imperial Navy of the Galactic Empire during the Galactic Civil War against the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Shortly after the Imperial attack on a Rebel base on the planet Arda I, Adarios was stationed in orbit of the planet Ord Radama as captain of the Interdictor-class Star Destroyer Eternal Wrath.

Wellam Adarios first appeared in Onslaught at Arda I, an adventure module for Fantasy Flight Games' Star Wars: Age of Rebellion roleplaying game released in 2014. It is possible for players to run into the Eternal Wrath while they travel to Ord Radama, but only if they fail to make a specified course correction. If they do they must persuade the ship's crew to let them pass despite having outdated access codes, otherwise Adarios calls for them to be brought aboard for questioning and sends TIE fighters to destroy them if they try to escape. This article assumes that players were successful and so did not encounter the Star Destroyer or its captain.

Weren Dal was a Kel Dor female Jedi Knight during the Clone Wars. Her ship was shot down by Separatist forces over the planet Dathomir.

Weren Dal was a Jedi Knight who served as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars. Near the end of the war, Dal was flying a Delta-6 when she was shot down by CIS starfighters over Dathomir under the orders of Separatist General Teaok.

Crash landing in the northern region of the world below, Dal survived the initial crash but was severely injured. Taking her astromech with her, Dal located a nearby cave to take shelter in. Constructing a cot to sleep on, Dal died in the cave. Her damaged lightsaber remained at her side, along with the disassembled droid and a lock box containing its memory core.

Werla Cayn was a human female Jedi Knight of the Jedi Order who lived during the High Republic Era. At some point, Cerean Jedi Master Char-Ryl-Roy knew Cayn as a Jedi youngling at the Jedi Temple Coruscant. In 382 BBY, Cayn was present among a convoy of four transports in the Dalnan system when they received a distress signal from Jedi Master Creighton Sun at the Outer Rim planet Dalna requesting immediate assistance. The convoy responded to the distress call and landed near the compound of the extremist Force cult, the Path of the Open Hand. During the ensuing battle, Cayn was overcome by the effects of a Nameless, a creature that could consume the life from Force-sensitives, and cried out for help, letting out screams of agony. However, help never came as she was killed by the creature and reduced to ashes. Shortly thereafter, her body was discovered by Jedi Padawan Enya Keen. Her lightsaber was taken by Jedi Master Char-Ryl-Roy, remembering her time as a Jedi youngling at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, and added it to his belt.

The Whisper was a 3-Z light freighter that was used by the Rebel Alliance scout team the Gray Griffins during the Galactic Civil War. After the Gray Griffins were assigned to perform some exploration work on the behalf of the Radell Mining Corporation, the Griffins flew the freighter to the Elrood sector and they discovered the planet Alluuvia. However, the Whisper was captured by The Scourge, a local pirate group, and the Griffins were imprisoned. The pirates then sold the freighter to the Squib crime lord Slythor, who stored the vessel in space, near to the planet Korad.

A team of Rebel Alliance agents were sent to recover the co-ordinates of Alluuvia from the Whisper computer and the agents negotiated with Slythor for access to the freighter. A pair of Slythor's Verpine hoppers escorted the agents to the Whisper location and the Rebels entered the vessel. However, during its time near Korad, the Whisper had became infested with mynocks and space mites, and the creatures attacked the agents. The Rebels defeated the creatures, then obtained the co-ordinates and departed Korad.

White Eyes was a prominent Sith Lord of the early One Sith. Alema Rar encountered him in the Valley of the Dark Lords on the planet Korriban, in 40 ABY. As he did not vouch his name to her, she so regarded him for the penetrating white eyes, the only part of him visible beneath the cowl of his cloak.

White Eyes led the interrogation of Alema Rar upon her arrival at their cloister on Korriban. Alema had originally come to Korriban in an effort to find help for Darth Caedus, who she felt was losing his way following the death of his Sith mentor Lumiya. However, White Eyes and the thirty or so Sith who gathered to examine her initially had no inclination to help, and to be told that they were operating entirely independently of Lumiya. When White Eyes was convinced by the Twi'lek Dark Jedi to render aid, he gave her the holocron of Darth Vectivus as a gift for Caedus.

During a later meeting of members of One Sith, White Eyes ordered Dician to take the Poison Moon to capture or kill Alema. He also ordered Dician to take any Sith artifacts found in Lumiya's asteroid base. His intentions with capturing Alema were to learn Darth Vectivus' Force phantom technique and capture its source of power.

Like all the members of the group, White Eyes dressed in a hooded black cloak, and also black gloves. He spoke in a deep, rough voice. In his encounter with Alema, White Eyes' firm, insistent attitude was accented by flashes of emotional intensity, and also by lapses into a dryly ironic tone, which masked the moments in which he adopted a more conciliatory attitude.

Wil Asani was a male Human who lived through the Clone Wars and into the dark times.

In 19 BBY, Asani became a resistance fighter and member of The Eleven, a group started by former Jedi Ferus Olin and Roan Lands, after Emperor Palpatine reorganized the Galactic Republic into his New Order. After Lands and Dona Telamark were arrested by the Empire, Asani and Doctor Amie Antin met with Oryon and Trever Flume where they would send in information to rescue Lands and Telemark. However, they were interrupted by stormtroopers, and Asani was forced to put the data on his computer. After fleeing through a tunnel, Asani and Antin took Flume, Solace and Oryon to a landing platform in order to escape the planet.

When Flume returned to Bellassa with Solace and Oryon, Asani and Antin helpeded to find where Telemark and Lands were being held for trial. Unable to locate the ship, the only information he could give them was that the trial was on the True Justice, a ship that traveled constantly picking up political prisoners. After leaving the planet, Asani traveled with the other opposition leaders to the Jedi asteroid where they would remain hidden from the Empire. As the transpirator the ship broke and they had to stop over, Asani and Ferus discovered a tracking device on board. While he remained on the base, it was revealed that Toma was serving as spy to the Empire and was the one who activated the tracking device which allowed Darth Vader and the Empire to find the resistance leaders. Asani perished in the Jedi asteroid's destruction.

A male Jedi Master trained Jedi Winslau Da'k. The Master was imprisoned on Morcanth by his former student, as Da'k had been corrupted to the dark side of the Force by Darth Vader. Later, the Master was released and served his rescuers as a teacher in the ways of the Force.

A Force-sensitive, the man was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order and eventually attained the rank of Jedi Master. He trained the young initiate Winslau Da'k as his student.

At the conclusion of the Clone Wars, the implementation of Order 66 killed the majority of the Jedi and effectively disbanded the Jedi Order. Da'k and his Master survived, but at some point afterward, Da'k encountered Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader, who, despite the brevity of his contact with Da'k and unbeknownst to Da'k's Master, was able to corrupt the young Jedi to the dark side of the Force. The Jedi Master was surprised and overcome by his twisted student, who imprisoned him on the planet Morcanth, deep in the Unknown Regions. The power-mad Da'k incessantly assaulted him, attempting to attain mastery over his former master and gain knowledge before destroying him.

Weakened by these assaults and desperate, the Master used the last of his diminishing power to reach out across space for help. His pleas reached the minds of a group of Force-sensitive individuals who experienced visions and dreams of the man beckoning to them from his oppressive prison. The Master was also able to communicate the name of his prison world, Morcanth; however, Morcanth had been renamed on modern star-charts, and was thus a mystery to the group until they uncovered very old charts that used the original name. Upon journeying there, the group discovered the planet was located in disputed territory in a centuries-old war being waged by three local starfaring species, none of which recognized neutrality in their conflict. The group evaded the warring parties, neutralized Da'k's bevy of guards, and finally overcame Winslau Da'k himself, freeing the Master.

Wordro's organization, run by Wordro the Hutt, suffered hijackings of its shipments during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire.

Around 3643 BBY, an individual associated with one of the two opposing governments sent a companion of theirs to guard the organization's shipments in exchange for Wordro giving them a share of his profits. The companion defeated the hijackers and exposed a traitor working within Wordo's organization. The Hutt was pleased and gave them a bonus.

Xarah Blacwood was a middle-aged female individual who served as a commander in the New Republic and was in command of the New Republic staging outpost in orbit of the planet Adelphi. She had sharp features, and had a bob of bright white hair with a metallic blue sheen. she met with Jedi Master Luke Skywalker and Lando Calrissian, who had traveled to the outpost to speak with Flight Sergeant Dina Dipurl. Blacwood told the two that she would be unable to help them and that Dipurl was unavailable, though she did not reveal why; because Dipurl had recently been killed in a pirate attack. The commander then questioned why Skywalker had traveled to Adelphi, and Calrissian informed the Blacwood that the Sith had returned and the two were attempting to stop what they had planned. Blacwood told Calrissian and Skywalker that the crew of the outpost were engaged in classified high-value missions and she would be not be able to share the details and informed Skywalker that he would need to go through the official channels. Blacwood again repeated that she would be unable to help them before she had her adjunct, Jashei Zigler, end the meeting.

Xat Hracken was a male Human Sith Lord who served as the Combat Master at a Sith academy on Odacer-Faustin. By 3645 BBY, Hracken had taught at the academy for many decades. A short time after the disappearance of the student Wim Nickter from the academy, Hracken stayed up late one night with the student Mnah Ra'at, while Ra'at practiced on the academy's combat simulator. Hracken turned off the lights in the room to test whether Ra'at could face the machine while blind.

Xat Hracken was a Force-sensitive Human male It was during that time Hracken became allied with the Sith Empire and eventually became both a Master and Lord of the Sith. His service to the Empire was given as a combat instructor, one stationed at the Sith academy on the snow-blanketed world of Odacer-Faustin. at which point the Imperial war machine chose to accelerate its output of Sith warriors and leaders, rather than decrease it. Master Hracken retained his decades-long position as combat instructor of the Odacer-Faustin Sith academy, and a measure of his skill was imparted to the enrolled learners.

Hracken survived the initial outbreak caused by Scabrous' experiment and saved Ra'at and his fellow students Hartwig, Maggs, and Kindra by blasting their attackers with Force lightning. He killed an infected Ra'at shortly after the student turned by incinerating him with Force lightning.

The surviving four Sith confronted each other over if any of them were infected. They all stripped to examine each other for infection. However, unbeknownst to all, Hracken, during the previous fight, had bitten his lip open while straining to maintain his Force lightning, and as a result, spraying infected blood got into his wound. He succumbed to the infection and killed Hartwig before being slain by Kindra.

Xavi Brightsun was a human male who lived in the settlement of Reestkii on the desert planet Jakku. When the settlement was overrun by Zygerrian enslavers sometime after the Battle of Endor, he and the other residents were rounded up and locked in the town hall. While imprisoned, the Nu-Cosian pet-seller Bobbajo kept the children calm by telling them a story about he and his animal companions escaping from the Death Star during the Battle of Yavin. Once the tale was finished, the storyteller left the town hall and revealed all the slavers had been subdued by unknown forces, allowing the residents of Reestkii to claim the Zygerrian's gathered wealth.

Xavi Brightsun first appeared in the short story "All Creatures Great and Small," which was written by Landry Q. Walker and released as an eBook in 2015.

enrichments.description:
Xiri A'lbaran was a human after a chance meeting, she proposed marrying Prince Phan-tu Zenn of Eiram at a summit hosted by the Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order during a temporary truce, hoping the marriage would help bring peace to their planets. Though the wedding was tumultuous, in the aftermath it was decided that a peace treaty would be signed on the holy moon Jedha.

When A'lbaran, Zenn, and the Jedi then discovered members of the Path of the Open Hand cult trying to frame E'ronoh for accumulating the bioweapon klytobacter, which could devestate Eiram, A'lbaran agreed to travel with the Jedi on a diplomatic mission to speak with the Path on Dalna and investigate their role in the conflict. However, the Path used it as an excuse to attack them and the Jedi, which erupted into an extensive battle that became known as the Night of Sorrow. She and Zenn managed to escape the planet and the battle in a damaged starfighter they found. The two, with the help of Supreme Chancellor Orlen Mollo, then united their planets against the Path and turned the tide of the battle in the Jedi's favor, all while hoping to bring a lasting peace to their worlds.

Xiri A'lbaran was born to Monarch A'lbaran, and was the second in line for the monarchy behind her brother Niko A'lbaran. In around 387 BBY a war between E'ronoh and its twin planet Eiram was reignited when Prince Niko accidentally drowned while on a visit to Eiram. Xiri therefore became heir to the throne and was made Captain of Thylefire Squadron, leading the E'roni starfighters into battle against the Eirami for five years. A constant at her side was her second-in-command, Jerrod Segaru, with whom she developed a close friendship.

A ship was owned by the Twi'lek rebel Xosad Hozem during the Imperial Era.

Xosad Hozem's starship was used by Hozem and his crew who were a part of Saw Gerrera's Partisans. The ship had a cockpit with room for at least two people, a back section with jump seats for passengers, and a common area with benches and seats surrounding a table that was screwed into the floor. Past the common room was a hallway that led to a room with bunks for Hozem's crew, namely Jari and Bilder. The floors of the ship were rough and dull metal, as was most of the rest of the interior.

It was compatible to dock with a CCR-class pinnace via a transport tube.

Hozem piloted the ship for a mission to gather information from a civilian transport that the Empire was using as a scout ship. Joined by Jari, Bilder, Gerrera, and Jyn Erso, they traveled from Wrea to the Western Reaches and boarded the ship, stealing datapads of intel before returning to Gerrera's outpost.

Like the rest of her family, she was a follower of the Religion of the Cosmic Balance that dictated for every good, there had to be an equal bad (or vice-versa), lest the universe fall out of alignment.

As such, when in 2 BBY Gaeriel was chosen to attend the Bakur Senatorial Academy and eventually join the Bakuran Senate, Dol and Marga gave Ylanda a golden alms bowl—since her sister would become a senator, to preserve the Cosmic Balance, Ylanda was to become a beggar.

Ylanda carried out the dictate of her parents and religion.

enrichments.description:
Yula Braylon was a female Jedi Master who initially served as a Jedi seeker, searching the galaxy for initiates to recruit into the Jedi Order. During her years as a seeker, Braylon had a son named Arath Tarrex, who became an initiate at a young age. However, his heritage was unknown to the Jedi Order for decades. Braylon had herself assigned to train Jedi younglings in order to keep a watchful eye on her son. She eventually received a seat on the Jedi Council, but lost her position when it was discovered that Arath, now a corrupt Jedi, was her son and that she had used her position to help cover his gambling debts and protect him from his debtors. Braylon then spent the interceding years trying to get back into the Jedi High Council's favor.

Yula Braylon was a renowned Jedi seeker, traveling the galaxy to find Force-sensitive children who could be recruited into the Jedi Order. However, during her time away from the Jedi Temple she conceived and gave birth to a son named Arath Tarrex, an act which would be highly controversial in an organization that forbade attachment. She therefore brought him in as an initiate, giving up her position as a seeker to train younglings at the Temple so that she could watch over her secret child. After several years she became a Jedi Master and gained a place on the Jedi Council, serving alongside famous figures such as Grand Master Yoda and Master Tera Sinube.

In 90 BBY, Braylon attended a festival on Serenno with other members of the Jedi Order. The aim of the celebration was to showcase what Outer Rim planets had to offer the Galactic Republic, but the Jedi also put on a lightsaber demonstration for the crowds, with Braylon performing with Yoda and Tera Sinube. During the course of the event, a young initiate named Dooku, also the estranged son of Count Gora of Serenno, created chaos by inadvertently causing the planetary assembly hall to collapse on himself and his sister, Jenza. Braylon and the other Jedi masters rushed to the scene, with Braylon assisting Yoda in lifting the debris off the children so that they could be rescued. Despite their efforts, an ungrateful Count Gora, angry at the reappearance of Dooku, forced the Jedi to leave the planet immediately.

Two years later, Braylon and Yoda instructed the Hawk-Bat Clan on the importance and use of the Jedi Archives. When the initiates Zang Arraira and Sifo-Dyas questioned the masters about the busts of the Lost, Braylon explained that members of the Order could become disillusioned and leave, with some going on to become leaders and teachers elsewhere. That night, Dooku and Sifo-Dyas were caught attempting to break into the Archive of Forbidden Artifacts, a Bogan Collection, an exhibit of forbidden Dark Side artifacts. Braylon harshly reprimanded the boys, despite the fact that she herself had attempted to break into the collection when she was an initiate, before clashing with Master Lene Kostana when Kostana attempted to question Dooku on the Force vision he had had while interacting with the artifacts.

Yun Baliss was a Human male duke who was a member of House Baliss, a minor family on Alderaan that remained neutral when war broke out between the major houses, during the Cold War. When the Baliss estate was overrun by Killiks, Yun decided to capitalize on the chaos engulfing Alderaan and make the Teraan estate the new Baliss home.

After the smuggler known as Ace stole a datapad from the Baliss estate to allow House Teraan to regain their lost fortune, the Duke sent his son Xin Baliss to exact vengeance against House Teraan by challenging Lenn Teraan to a blaster duel to the death. As Lenn had never mastered the blaster, he and his sister Cedonia persuaded Ace to stand as their champion, who defeated Xin in the duel.

Aggel lived on Nizon, where she was a healer and considered a "wise woman" by the other Nazren. When the Empire came to Nizon, she witnessed her people becoming slaves, so she was pleased when they rose up against the Empire. During the battle, she gave a group of Alderaanian Resistance agents shelter in her house, after they were cornered by the advancing Imperial forces. However, some LM-432 crab droids that were working for Vril Vrakth, a Zabrak bounty hunter, burrowed into her house to attack the agents.

enrichments.description:
Yush Baskalar was a scientist who worked with the Thaereian military in researching genetics and cybernetics.

As a child, Baskalar had been identified as a Force-sensitive and taken to be trained at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. He was soon sent away because of his violent tendencies. By the time he returned home, his family had died in an accident while moving to another system. He had a lasting hatred of the Jedi for that reason.

Yush Baskalar had an interest in science, and excelled in such diverse fields as droid manufacturing, cybernetics, and Near-Human genetics, partly because of his Force sensitiveness. He worked at a university doing advanced genetics research for the Galactic Republic, but was then dismissed for conducting questionable experiments. He was approached by Qar Jalunn, who offered unlimited resources to continue his research. Baskalar balked when he learned he had to work with the Thaereian military, but Jalunn convinced him to continue on.

Yush Baskalar was a short, stooped man with narrow shoulders. He was bald, with thick black eyebrows. His mouth was in a perpetual grimace, and he had a small x-shaped scar on his right forehead, which he tried to hide by turning away in conversation. Overall he moved slowly and awkwardly, which belied the nimbleness of his hands.

Recognizing her Force potential the master took Yuthura to Dantooine, to be trained as a Jedi, taking the young Twi'lek as his Padawan. The partnership would not last long, however, as Yuthura, consumed with hatred towards the slave trade, and infruiated by the Jedi's apathy toward it, left the Order, eventually joining the new Sith Empire of Darth Revan and Malak. Yuthura returned to the Jedi after being redeemed by a reformed Revan and upon seeing his old apprentice, the Jedi wept.

enrichments.description:
Zeen Afit was a craggy-faced male Human smuggler who first introduced Han Solo to Smuggler's Run. He owned a freighter named Corona.

Zeen, like many other smugglers, aided the fledgling Alliance to Restore the Republic in their fight on Ylesia. Unlike Han and many others, he, along with Katya M'Buele were not cheated by the Rebels.

Han later met up with Zeen on Skip One in the Run while investigating Kueller's Senate Hall bombings in 17 ABY. He joined Han and Chewbacca in their attempt to rescue Lando Calrissian from the crime lord Nandreeson, along with Kid DXo'ln, Wynni and Ana Blue. Unknown to Han, Afit's true loyalty lay with Nandreeson. Once the rescue party reached the pool in Nandreeson's chamber, Afit turned on Han along with Kid and Wynni. At a command from Nandreeson, Afit joined Kid, Wynni and Nandreeson's guards in attempting to kill Solo, Calrissian and Chewbacca (Blue did not help either side in the ensuing struggle). Solo dived underwater to avoid the blaster fire and the fiery breath of the Glottalphib guards and pulled Afit down with him. Afit was caught unawares and had no opportunity to draw in a lungful of air before going under. After a desperate struggle with Solo he finally succumbed to lack of oxygen. Solo released his grip on Afit and made for the surface to help Lando and Chewbacca. The unconscious Afit sank toward the bottom of the pool, drowning to death moments later.

Zeth Bresque was a Balosar female slave. She was also an addict to death sticks.

In around 20 BBY, Bresque had been captured by slaver Phylus Mon and kept in a cell in Mon's slave zoo aboard the Animiasma. Her cell had a slot and a lever so that Bresque could get a new death stick whenever she wanted. This was apparently an experiment to see how long she could survive with a constant supply of her drugs. As a result, she was not anxious to leave.

Phylus Mon surgically inserted an explosive near the heart of each of his slaves. The explosive would be activated in the case of Phylus Mon's death, but it could also be deactivated with the impact of an ion blaster. All the slaves in Phylus Mon's zoo were also regularly battered.

Zip Beeline was the pseudonym of a Drall professional speeder racer on Coruscant. He then legally assumed the name after an impressive debut with good fan reaction. His speeders, swoops, and podracers were customized for his small stature. Touring widely, Zip ended his professional career at Boonta on Tatooine, when he caused a multi-speeder pileup during a championship race. Retiring in disgrace to Coruscant, Zip acquired newfound fame and notoriety in the illegal podraces, garbage pit races, and swoop rallies of the Undercity. Even in the illegal races, Zip was known as an honest competitor who never resorted to sabotage or cheating. He was known to post low times after indulging in Corellian lum.

Zoiya Relle was a Sith Lady who ranked among the best fighters in an empire created by the Sith tradition of Force-users. To compensate for her lack of charisma and guile, Relle created a Sith talisman that allowed its wielder to dominate the minds of other individuals.

The Sith Lady subsequently became one of the few women to ever rule the Sith. it was believed that a Sith carrying the Relle Talisman had perished on the planet Ossus, a world with significant historical ties to the Jedi Order, the ideological antithesis of the Sith tradition.

Zoiya Relle was introduced in the 2015 core rulebook for Fantasy Flight Games' Star Wars: Force and Destiny roleplaying game system.

Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook

Ztenortha pilgrims were a group that existed by the Imperial Era. At least some of the pilgrims wore distinct wrappings. In 19 BBY, Imperial Senator Bail Organa visited the moon Jedha, donning the gray wrappings of a Ztenortha pilgrim and stukleather boots. The attire allowed him to blend in with the crowd of mourners in the moon's Holy City, who were mourning the recent purge of the Jedi Order.

Ztenortha pilgrims were mentioned in the 2025 novel Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear, written by Alexander Freed as the first installment of the Star Wars: Reign of the Empire trilogy.

Zyle's shuttle was a Nihil escape shuttle utilized by the Nihil marauders that was held in a hangar aboard the vessel of the captain I'nah. In 229 BBY, the shuttle was stolen by the young pirate Zyle Keem, whose mother, Tanana Keem, had stopped aboard I'nah's vessel to barter goods. Keem flew the shuttle to the planet Valo, where they had overheard there was valuable bacta aboard the sunken vessel Innovator. However, as Keem attempted to land on Valo, the shuttle's navigation system deactivated and its wings began to fall apart, forcing them to make an emergency landing. The shuttle was severely damaged in the process and exploded shortly after Keem disembarked. After meeting the Jedi Padawan Ram Jomaram and the younglings Gavi, Kildo, and Tep Tep, who were fighting back against the Nihil occupation of the planet, the group decided to raid the Innovator together. The group retrieved the wreckage of Zyle's shuttle and salvaged components from it to modify Jomaram's ship, an Eviscerator.

The .48-caliber Enforcer pistol, commonly known as the Enforcer pistol or the .48 Enforcer, was a projectile weapon developed in limited quantities by the Morellian Weapons Conglomerate, only to be used by the Morellian Enforcers. It was not sold except in the black market, commonly over six thousand credits.

The projectile equivalent to a heavy blaster pistol, the Enforcer boasted eight .48 caliber slugs and produced a cannon like crack upon firing a slug, with the slug itself carrying enormous stopping power sufficient to pierce heavy personal armors and even light vehicles; as was the case when Barosa Warren demolished a XP-38 sport landspeeder.

With its power though came extreme recoil, with specialized training needed to avoid having the weapon fly out of a users hand with each shot. However, with practice firing the weapon was possible, and with specialized military training - such as that offered to Morellian Enforcers - rapid fire was also possible; though practice was needed to ensure that shots were precise, as rapid firing could lead to erratic placement of shots.

Scoutmaster Barosa Warren used one as his weapon of choice, and due to his training as a Morellian Enforcer was capable of firing multiple shots in quick succession.

"Backstabber" was a human TIE fighter pilot in the Galactic Empire's Black Squadron who served as the wingman of Darth Vader during the Battle of Yavin. He was shot down by Han Solo when Vader was following Luke Skywalker and his X-wing starfighter who was trying to destroy the Death Star.

At the battle, during which the Rebel pilots attacked the Death Star, Vader ordered Backstabber and Mithel to be his wingman. Vader pursued Red Squadron as they targeted the thermal exhaust port, a flaw in the Death Star put in place by Imperial scientist Galen Erso, which would allow a precision shot to destroy the main reactor, destroying the station.

Vader, along with several other Imperial pilots, destroyed or disabled the attacking Rebel ships, with the exception of Luke Skywalker. As Vader and his wingmen targeted Skywalker, the Millennium Falcon, piloted by Han Solo, engaged the Imperials, shooting down Backstabber. His death caught Vader by surprise, and led Mithel to attempt to evade the attacker, clipping Vader's TIE Advanced x1 in the process before crashing into the Death Star. With Vader's ship damaged and incapacitated, he fled the battle, while Skywalker fired a proton torpedo into the thermal exhaust port, destroying the Death Star.

A male individual was a scientist who accidentally created the Triple-Zero protocol personality matrix. When they added cooperative algorithms to the matrix—including morality, empathy, equability and loyalty—they realized it was subverting them as fast as they developed, making the personality psychotic. While fascinated by his creation, the individual saw it as a reject, ordering their assistant to discard it in the trash compactor. However, the personality matrix took control of the droid assistant's body, escaping destruction. Many years later, Triple-Zero discovered his memories, and was disgusted by the circumstances in which he was created.

0-0-0's creator first appeared in flashbacks in the canon comic Doctor Aphra (2016) 30, written by Simon Spurrier, illustrated by Emilio Laiso,

1047 was a Human male stormtrooper who served as a sergeant in the Galactic Empire's Desert Sands unit by 0 BBY. In that year, he was among the Desert Sands troopers dispatched to the planet Tatooine to search for the fugitive Rebel Alliance droids C-3PO and R2-D2, who carried stolen plans for the Empire's Death Star battle station. 1047 was among Desert Sands' Zeta Squadron detachment, who conducted their search in the spaceport city of Mos Eisley. Ultimately, Desert Sands' search led 1047 and others in the unit to Mos Eisley's Docking Bay 94, where they attempted to apprehend the Millennium Falcon, the YT-1300 light freighter that the droids had boarded for escape, but the troopers were unable to prevent the ship from fleeing.

1047 he sergeant, attached to the Desert Sands unit under Captain Mod Terrik's command.

In 0 BBY, Desert Sands was dispatched to the planet Tatooine to search for the fugitive Alliance to Restore the Republic droids C-3PO and R2-D2, who were wanted for carrying the stolen plans for the Empire's first Death Star battle station. 1047 was among the Desert Sands troopers assigned to the unit's Zeta Squadron detachment, tasked with searching the planet's spaceport city of Mos Eisley for the droids, serving as the backup to fellow trooper Davin Felth.

At one point, 1047 and Felth were outside Mos Eisley's Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina when one of the cantina's patrons, Garouf Lafoe, approached to inform them of a fight that had occurred within the cantina. Felth used his comlink to inform Terrik that he would investigate the cantina disturbance, and the latter requested that 1047 back up Felth. The pair entered the cantina and left after failing to find anything out of the ordinary, not knowing that two of the occupants, Tatooine locals Obi-Wan Kenobi and Luke Skywalker, they had seen were in fact trying to sneak the droids off of Tatooine.

1137 was a clone trooper who served the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars.

Once during a mission, 1137 and their fellow clone trooper, 1139 were forgotten on a desert planet after their unit miscounted and departed. Ultimately, this proved fortuitous, for while abandoned the two soldiers learned of a CIS secret weapon project. As dutiful soldiers, 1137 and their companion resolved to destroy it. To aid in this endeavor, they built a TX-130 fighter tank, with which they destroyed the Separatist weapon. Soon thereafter, realizing their absence, a Republic gunship returned to retrieve the duo.

Having proven their competence, 1137, together with 1139, were then assigned to hunt the missing astromech droid R2-D2, their squad ordered by Supreme Chancellor Palpatine to find them before the Jedi. Travelling in a Nu-class attack shuttle, their first stop was the sector where R2-D2 was last seen, taking directions from a group of Rocket battle droids who were floating through space. Landing on an unidentified planet as their scanners picked up various droid signatures.. After struggling to find any droids, the clone squad was ambushed by various B1 and B2 battle droids, 1137's commander ordered their shuttle to give them cover fire while the other clones attacked the droids head on. The clone squad were able to quickly overwhelm them and steal the droid forces' Armored Assault Tank,only to be bombed from above by the clone forces in the shuttle, who had mistaken them for the enemy.

Knocked unconscious by the blast, 1137 dreamt of flying an Advanced TIE before being woken up by 1139. Going off to mope while their colleagues worked on rebuilding their arsenal,1137 was visited by Anakin Skywalker's Jedi Padawan Ahsoka Tano.
enrichments.short_description: 1137 was a clone trooper who served the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars.

1151 was a clone cadet who was a part of the Clone Youth Brigade during the Clone Wars.

Like all clone cadets, 1151 was created by the Kaminoans for the sole purpose of military service. By 21 BBY, 1151 was training as a cadet aboard the Venator-class Star Destroyer Endurance, which was commanded at the time by Jedi General Mace Windu and Admiral Kilian. Unbeknownst to the cadets, their unit had been infiltrated by budding bounty hunter and mercenary Boba Fett, who sabotaged the Star Destroyer in an attempt to kill Windu. After a bomb planted in Windu's quarters failed to kill him, Fett then destroyed the reactor. Seeing that the ship was beyond saving, Kilian ordered the cadets to abandon ship. Crasher, a Clone Sergeant who was conducting the tour, ordered the eight cadets to split up into two groups of four. 1151 and three other cadets got into the escape pod occupied by Crasher, while Fett and 3 other cadets got into another pod.

Clone trooper 17 served in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. During the First Battle of Geonosis in 22 BBY, they and fellow trooper Three-Five fought alongside clone commando Boss and two other clones in defending a barricade against Separatist B1-Series battle droids. Once the advancing droids were defeated, the surviving clones pushed through to a gun emplacement.

Decanted on the planet Kamino by the Kaminoan species, They served as a clone trooper in the Galactic Republic's Grand Army during the Clone Wars against the Confederacy of Independent Systems, a separatist group that attempted to secede from the Republic. 17 was deployed to the planet Geonosis, where they fought in the first battle of the Clone Wars.

On Geonosis, 17 and fellow trooper Three-Five greeted the clone commando Boss. Trooper 17 pointed out Boss to their companion, who responded by praising the highly-skilled commandos, remarking that they could defeat the Separatist forces alone. The trio then joined two other clone troopers in defending a barricade from Confederate B1-Series battle droids. The droids blew through a wall to avoid the barricade, killing one of the troopers. Despite the casualty, Boss, 17, 35, and the other surviving clone defeated the attacking droids, pushing them back to a Separatist gun emplacement.

A clone of the Human bounty hunter Jango Fett, 17 stood 1.83 meters tall like all clone troopers and had tan skin.

49AX3 was a Dreadnought-class heavy cruiser that served the navy of the Galactic Empire. the vessel was captured by the Alliance to Restore the Republic, who used it to raid Imperial Refining Platform M36, a refinery in the Outer Rim Territories. Assisted by Luke Skywalker, the team of rebels managed to steal fuel from the refinery, but their escape was blocked by an Imperial-class Star Destroyer. Skywalker landed his X-wing in the vessel's hangar, where he and the rebel major used a shuttle to draw the attention of the Imperial TIE fighters away. The tactic worked, and the rebels aboard 49AX3 were able to evacuate, escaping to a nearby world.

836-VS was a Sentinel-class landing craft that was stolen by the Alliance to Restore the Republic and used for a mission to the moon Killun 71. Crewed by members of Phoenix Cell, namely the former Imperial pilot Wedge Antilles, the former Imperial inventory droid AP-5, and the C1-series astromech droid C1-10P "Chopper," 836-VS arrived at Killun Station, where they attempted to steal Imperial clearance codes.

Following the mission, 836-VS docked with the modified VCX-100 light freighter Ghost. Soon after, Chopper, who had been reprogrammed by Imperial personnel, trapped Antilles, AP-5, and the fellow rebels Hera Syndulla, Ezra Bridger, and Garazeb Orrelios in the ship's cargo bay. Then, he detached the Ghost from 836-VS and flew away, leaving the stolen Imperial shuttle floating in space.

A'Koba, was a skilled but young Tusken Raider who lived on Tatooine during the Galactic Civil War and had cousins, A'Vor and A'Vor's twin. Shortly before the Battle of Yavin, A'Koba attacked Luke Skywalker before getting scared off by Obi-Wan Kenobi.

A'Koba lived on the Outer Rim world of Tatooine during the Galactic Civil War as part of Chieftain A'Yark's tribe. Shortly before the Battle of Yavin, A'Koba, joined by his cousins, A'Vor and A'Vor's twin, killed a juvenile krayt dragon as a rite of passage into adulthood. He then claimed to A'Yark that he would be able to kill the adult krayts as well.

After being told of a mysterious shaman by A'Yark, A'Koba, having wanted to lead a hunt, attacked Luke Skywalker, a local moisture farmer who, along with protocol droid C-3PO, was searching for his missing astromech droid R2-D2. A'Koba knocked Skywalker unconscious, and the Tusken and his cousins began searching Skywalker's landspeeder. They were scared off by Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, who mimicked the call of a krayt dragon to spook A'Koba and his fellow Tusken Raiders into fleeing. Upon seeing Kenobi, A'Koba realized he was the shaman A'Yark had warned them about.

A'Koba was played by stunt coordinator Peter Diamond, who was the only stunt person on location in Tunisia, in the 1977 film Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope. In Star Wars Legends, the character was identified as URoRRuR'R'R.

AA-23 was a Lambda-class T-4a shuttle in the service of the Galactic Empire.

AA-23 was stationed on an Imperial XQ6 Platform DX-11a in the Eidoloni system some time after the Battle of Hoth. It was one of four shuttles that attempted to flee the platform when Ace Azzameen's squadron staged a diversionary attack on the outpost. Their aim was to give Commander Zaletta, an Imperial officer who had grown sympathetic to the Rebel Alliance's cause, an opportunity to defect.

Onboard shuttle AA-23, Zaletta fled the platform after the Rebels were able to disable the platform's shields. Unsure of which of the shuttles the defector was on, Azzameen was ordered to scan each craft before contact could be established. Their attack a success, the Rebels fled to a rendezvous with the Rebel Nebulon-B Frigate Redemption. Zaletta safely docked with the vessel, but the group suddenly came under attack from an Interdictor and an escorting Star Destroyer. With Zaletta under suspicion of luring the Rebels into a trap, he was imprisoned while the Rebels attacked the Interdictor and forced it to disengage.

Before the Rebels had a chance to decode the shuttle's valuable data, however, Liberty Tactical Officer Commander Kupalo, secretly a mole for the Empire, blew his cover, breaking into the hangar. He bound the shuttle's custodian, placing a series of explosives beside him. Despite the deck officer's protests, Kupalo stole the shuttle and blasted his way out of the hangar, detonating the charges and causing huge damage to the hangar as he did so.
enrichments.short_description: AA-23 was a Lambda-class T-4a shuttle in the service of the Galactic Empire.

"Aach" was the code name of a Human male who served as a Rebel agent during the Galactic Civil War. In 2 BBY, he informed Garm Bel Iblis of the Death Star plans. Directly answerable to Bail Organa, Aach was a special messenger that was only used for top-level Alliance business.

Though he was willing to forgo his return to Alderaan and accompany Bel Iblis on his mission to Darkknell, the senator sent him back to Organa with firm belief that Aach would be needed elsewhere.

Aach appeared in the Star Wars Legends novella "Interlude at Darkknell" by Timothy Zahn and Michael A. Stackpole, which was published in the 1999 anthology Tales from the New Republic. the 2016 canon reference book Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide, a tie-in to the film Rogue One: A Star Wars Story, established that Cassian Jeron Andor, one of the film's protagonists, had used the code name "Aach" as a senatorial contact on Darkknell.

Aaida was a Human female who lived on Telos IV during the Jedi Civil War. A survivor of the Sith bombardment of the world in 3958 BBY, she was separated from her husband, Lootra, during evacuation. Seven years later, Aaida was present on Nar Shaddaa, where the Jedi Exile Meetra Surik reunited her with Lootra.

Aaida lived with her husband Lootra on the Outer Rim planet of Telos IV during the early stages of the Jedi Civil War, a conflict between the Galactic Republic and Darth Revan's Sith Empire.

In 3958 BBY, Republic Navy Rear Admiral Saul Karath defected to the Sith. Soon after, he led a fleet against Telos IV and called for the planet's surrender. When the inhabitants refused, Darth Malak ordered an orbital bombardment of the planet. Aaida and Lootra survived the assault, but the two were separated during evacuation. Aaida made it onto a civilian ship and escaped, while her husband boarded another. The Sith did not destroy the ship, and Aaida belied that it was because they wanted living witnesses to the attack. The ship, loaded with refugees, jumped from system to system, just ahead of the Sith's warships.

On the run for years, Aaida began to think she would never see her husband again. Seven years later, in 3951 BBY during the First Jedi Purge, Aaida found herself living in the Refugee Sector on Nal Hutta ecumenopolis moon, Nar Shaddaa.

Aarrba was a Hutt repairman who resided on Koros Major prior to and during the Great Hyperspace War. Owner and manager of Aarrba's Repair Dock, the Hutt enjoyed a successful business, in which he repaired spacecraft quickly and cheaply. His reputation was a good one in Cinnagar, and he was very protective of it. When two of his customers, Hok and Timar Daragon died during the Battle of Kirrek, Aarrba took it upon himself to look after their children, Gav and Jori, by giving them their parents' ship, Starbreaker 12.

The younger Daragons took it upon themselves to become hyperspace explorers—a hazardous profession, and one that required constant repair to the Starbreaker 12. Soon enough, the Daragons found themselves in Aarrba's debt, and when a shipment owned by merchant lord Ssk Kahorr used one of the "shortcuts" they had discovered and was destroyed, they were then targeted by Kahorr's assassins. They betrayed Aarrba by stealing the Starbreaker 12, and when, sometime afterward, Jori returned claiming she had discovered the Sith Empire and that Gav had been captured by them, the Hutt refused to listen. This proved costly for him, however, as he was subsequently slain by Sith warriors in the Battle of Koros Major.

Aarrba, a Hutt, owned and ran Aarrba's Repair Dock, located in Cinnagar, Koros Major. He chose to use a hoversled for personal transportation, and offered to repair starships at budget prices, discreetly, although the repairs were never guaranteed to last. Despite this, the service was usually quick, and he enjoyed success. During the Unification Wars, Aarrba's services were employed by Hok and Timar Daragon, owners of the Shadow Runner, who planned to run supplies to besieged warriors loyal to Empress Teta fighting in the Battle of Kirrek. Despite the fact that the Daragons did not have the funds to pay for a speedy repair of the Shadow Runner, Aarrba agreed to take a percentage of their profits for the work. The Daragons were grateful, but the Hutt insisted that they keep his generosity a secret from the other customers.

As collateral, he asked that they leave their other ship, the Starbreaker 12, with him on Koros Major, and they obliged. Some time afterward, Aarrba received word that Hok and Timar had been killed at Kirrek, and he then had to solemnly inform their children, Jori and Gav, of their deaths. Reasoning that the elder Daragons had paid for the repairs to the Shadow Runner with their blood, the Hutt gave the Starbreaker 12 to the younger Daragons. They chose to become hyperspace explorers, hoping to find new shortcuts for spacefarers, which they would then sell to the highest bidder. The task was dangerous, however, and the Starbreaker 12 was in constant need of repair. The expenditures of the Daragons soon outweighed their income, and, like their parents, they had to begin providing Aarrba with collateral.

Aau was a Force-sensitive Korban girl who lived on the planet Korba with her father, Abat. On Korba, Aau washed beasts near the entrance of a mine shaft where Abat worked by 19 BBY. After the Jedi Kratu visited the pair's home, they traveled to their respective workstations. Aau abandoned hers and followed her father to a tunnel, where she found a mine entrance in a mountain.

She entered it to find a cave full of kyber crystals and started to sing, purifying the crystals with her voice and destroying the cavern's spire, causing the mountain to collapse. Abat then dug a hole into the cave and rescued his daughter. However, the mountain's collapse cut a bridge the pair were using to escape; as a result, Aau and her father fell and were subsequently saved from the fall by Kratu. While the Jedi used the Force to protect them from several falling stones, Aau sang and purified the mountains' kyber crystal. Shortly after, the girl and Kratu left Korba so that the Jedi could nurture Aau's ability to purify kyber.

At some point, they learned that the girl's voice could cause kyber crystals to release energy when she sang, which her father deemed dangerous. Aau climbed a cliff with a rope and looked at the landscape's spires, singing and watching as the Jedi Kratu's starship traveled to her home, rushing there.
