Batono was a Human male and a former employee of Czerka Corporation. He disagreed with many of their practices and began to seek shelter with the Ithorians on Citadel Station. The leader of the Ithorians, Chodo Habat, put Batono in a secure apartment.

Unluckily for Batono, both Czerka and the Telos Security Force were after him. Czerka wanted to silence him while the TSF wanted him to testify against Czerka before the Telosian Council. Eventually, Dol Grenn would hire the services of Meetra Surik, who quickly found where Batono had gone.

When he was found, Batono was very resistant to leaving his apartment, though Surik persuaded him to come and testify against Czerka. Batono agreed and he left with Surik, only to run into two of Czerka's mercenaries, which Surik defeated handily. Batono was handed to the TSF safely and he thanked Surik. Grenn then gave 300 credits to Surik.

Alternatively, for the dark side choice, the player can kill Batono and go to Jana Lorso to claim the reward of 200 credits for his elimination.

Between 3 ABY and 4 ABY, Vermillion and the Galactic Empire. After becoming aware that the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Sidious was hunting her, Crimson Dawn leader Lady Qi'ra activated her spies within the various major powers of the galaxy to create chaos in order to buy her time to follow through with her plans. Qi'ra hid with the Orphans on an astronomical object aboard their ship, the Siroto, where they were eventually discovered by the Imperial Navy. The Empire deployed an Interdictor-class to prevent Qi'ra and her flagship from escaping.

As Qi'ra spoke personally with Sidious and outlined her plans to destroy him, Qi'ra sent the Vermillion to attack the interdictor. The Vermillion was attacked by TIE fighters and TIE/IN interceptors, but they were unable to prevent the ship from crashing directly into the interdictor, destroying both. Escape pods were deployed from the Vermillion, and Sidious ordered they all be destroyed, allowing for no one to escape.

The destruction of the Vermillion allowed for Qi'ra and the Oprhans to escape from the Imperials aboard the Siroto and as they left, Chanath Cha asked Qi'ra if they should pick up any potential survivors from the escape pods, Qi'ra thought for a moment before declining, adding that they could honor their sacrifice by seeing her plans through to the end.

The fact that Qi'ra survived was later inadvertently revealed to Vader by Cha. When Cha confronted Vader, he informed her that she would not avenge Qi'ra's death, which surprised the hunter. Vader sensed this and realized that Qi'ra had actually survived, adding that his Master would be fascinated to learn of this.

The battle at the Denarii Nova was fought in the Denarii system at the end of the Great Hyperspace War in 5000 BBY.

Following his defeat at Korriban, the Dark Lord of the Sith Naga Sadow set course for the Denarii system aboard his Derriphan-class battleship, the Corsair. Pursued by Galactic Republic forces, Sadow maneuvered his damaged flagship between the binary stars of the Denarii Nova. The Sith sorcerer then used his powers to manipulate the solar flares of the Denarii Nova. The resulting explosion destroyed the Republic ships in his wake and allowed him to stage his own death.

This cataclysmic event also resulted in the destruction of the entire system, which created a nebula of highly ionized gases known as the Denarii Nebula.

In the aftermath of the battle, Sadow, his Sith followers, and his Massassi crew settled on the jungle moon Yavin 4.

The ISD Ultima II under the command of Admiral Kalaxo trapped the Alliance Eleventh Division on the surface of Ab Dalis. The Rebel Ground Defense Command under Colonel Chouch organized the surface defense against Imperial walkers and tanks. Following Ground Defense Command's destruction, Starlight Squadron arrived and destroyed Ultima II by causing an eruption of the volcano directly below it.

The Battle of Aguarl 3 was a brief engagement of the Galactic Civil War approximately six months after the Battle of Yavin, in which a wing of TIE bombers struck at a sub-aquatic Rebel base on Aguarl 3.

Following intelligence provided by a Quarren spy, the Imperial Star Destroyer Ravagor swiftly deployed a wing of TIE/sa Bombers to destroy the Rebel base hidden under the seas of Aguarl 3. Assigned to the task were the pilots, Willks, Rawst, Parrot and Ranulf Trommer.

The Rebel Base under command of Leia Organa quickly detected the fighter squadron, activating the Rebel anti-air emplacements. The mines swiftly destroyed all but one target, the bomber piloted by Ranulf Trommer. Although his craft had sustained damage, Trommer successfully launched three concussion missiles, striking the base's launch bay and flooding the facility, forcing the Rebels to evacuate.

Returning to the Ravagor, Trommer and his smoking ship were recovered by the Star Destroyer's tractor beam and brought to the flight deck. Imperial Firefighting droids hosed down the craft and recovered the critically injured Trommer, rushing him to surgery and saving his life at the cost of his leg. Disgusted by his cybernetic replacement, Trommer endeavored to hide it in his return to service, seeing it as dishonorable.

There were three divisions in the battle plan: one to lead the battle and destroy the deflector shield generator, one to infiltrate the base once the shield was down, set charges inside, and destroy it, and one person who would go to Trandosha and persuade the locals not to get mixed up in the conflict. In the end, the Galactic Republic won the battle and the base was destroyed.

At some point between 2 BBY and 1 BBY but before the battle on Vir Aphshire, a battle took place between the Rebel Alliance's 61st Mobile Infantry led by Captain Micha Evon and the Galactic Empire's forces on Allst Prime led by Governor Magé. In the midst of the battle, the Forward Air Control Officer Cait was killed when directing the 61st's X-Wings and Evon had to take her place. At the same time 61st Soldier Brand rescued Lylee Anaraku from an AT-ST. Brand was distracted by Evon, standing over Cait's body and shouting orders into her comm, when Anaraku was taken down by an Imperial. Brand killed the Imperial and went to Anaraku's aid. Later in the battle Brand and Evon stormed into the governor's office and Brand stunned Magé. Brand then pointed her gun at Evon as she a had taken a bounty on him. Evon revealed what he knew about her past and convinced her to stay with the 61st and abandon her old life as a bounty hunter.

The Battle of Amaltanna was a battle between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems during the Clone Wars on the planet Amaltanna. In the end, the Republic triumphed over the Separatists, but the extent of the damage was so severe that its inhabitants were relocated as refugees to worlds such as Naboo and Alderaan.

The Battle of Amaltanna appeared in "Galactic Tales: The Failing of the Light," a short story by Adam Lance Garcia that was published in issue 233 of Star Wars Insider magazine The battle originated in the Star Wars Legends continuity and appeared in the comic story "Impregnable," which was released on January 31, 2007, as part of Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures Volume 7. In the story, the battle was a bloody affair that occurred six months into the Clone Wars and saw conflict between the clone troopers of Jedi General Bultar Swan and the battle droids of who commanded the battle from a seemingly impregnable fortress.

Garcia intended for the canon battle to have started early in the Clone War, yet he decided against outright confirming as such in "The Failing of the Light" to give other Lucasfilm creatives a chance to determine its exact timeframe. On August 2, Garcia teased that the story would feature "several events from both Legends and Canon" from a specific perspective, all without spoiling what those events were. After release, Garcia expressed joy to see story elements from "The Failing of the Light" receive their own pages in the Wookieepedia fan encyclopedia, including the canonized Battle of Amaltanna.

The Battle of Antamont occurred on the planet of Antamont during the Clone Wars, and was fought between the Grand Army of the Republic and the Separatist Droid Army.

Antamont, an nonindustrial, green planet covered in mountains, was the site of a Galactic Republic stronghold during the Clone Wars. Separatist forces targeted the base, and sent hordes of B1-series battle droids, grapple droids, dwarf spider droids, and Hailfire droids through the mountains toward the base. The path was littered with Republic landmines, which caused much damage to the onrushing droid forces.

The CIS and Republic eventually clashed in a valley. As their infantry approached each other, each side began firing missiles at each other. Though the majority of the battle was conducting with infantry and land vehicles, atmospheric combat between each force also occurred.

The battle left many destroyed battle droids strewn all over Antamont, which were often found by local farmers. One such droid, who had deserted the battle, was found in working condition and brought back to a ranch by two farmers.

The Battle of Ashas Ree was a conflict of the Great Galactic War, waged around 3660 BBY. After failed attacks on the Sith planets of Korriban and Ziost, the forces of the Galactic Republic, under the command of Jedi Master Ven Zallow, launched an attack on the Ashas Ree—a world in the heart of Sith Empire territory. The planet was defended by the Imperial Navy and Army under the command of Darth Angral and Darth Malgus. Despite the tenacity of Master Zallow and his Republic Military forces, the Jedi and his comrades lost the battle and were forced to fall back to Serenno.

Daniel Wallace, author of Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side, originally planned for the attack on Ashas Ree to be an assault on the Imperial capital of Dromund Kaas, but his first draft was vetoed by LucasArts.

The Battle of Asteroid 426 took place during the Clone Wars.

In order for Count Dooku's plan of invading the volcanic planet of Sarapin, the CIS needed to destroy the primary planetary defense grid in the asteroid maze.

Arriving with the Separatist forces, General Sev'rance Tann was instructed by Dooku to fight through the asteroid field and Republic grid defenses to Asteroid 426, located outside of Sarapin in the planet's ring. It wasn't easy as the field was filled with Heavy Anti-Air turrets, which would destroy the fighters and the rest of the force very quickly. Fortunately with Confederacy cruisers, which were brought to assist Tann, she was able to slowly make way to the asteroid with facing a little resistance from the Republic fighters. Eventually making it to the asteroid, she destroyed the supply depots, so she could get enough resources to set up a base on it. Meanwhile the Republic troops stationed on the asteroid led periodic attacks to the enemy base, though it didn't faze them at all. Then, after gathering enough troops, she devastated the rest of the Republic forces and destroyed the power relay to Sarapin's shield.

Following the collapse of the planetary shield at the hands of the Confederacy, Sarapin was then left for the taking.

The Battle of Bright Tree Village was a conflict that took place in 3 ABY between the Galactic Empire and the Ewoks of Bright Tree Village on Endor.

Doctor Raygar, an evil scientist to Emperor Palpatine, had designs on ruling the Galactic Empire and traveled to the Forest Moon of Endor to obtain the powerful Sunstar from the Ewoks' Bright Tree Village. He was attacked by the shaman Logray, who uses the Sunstar against him but Raygar's Imperial Reconnaissance droids soon overwhelmed the village and the evil doctor retaliated by swiftly stealing the Sunstar, before returning to Admiral Kazz's Star Destroyer in orbit. Back in his lab, Raygar studied the Sunstar and came to the realization that by harnessing its power, he could remove Palpatine and install himself as the Galactic Emperor. But when creating a dangerous cannon with the Sunstar's powers, Raygar discovered that Wicket Wystri Warrick, Princess Kneesaa, Latara and Teebo had come aboard Kazz's Star Destroyer with the help of a pilot droid named PD-28. Raygar planned to test his weapon on the captives—Latara and Teebo, but is thwarted by Wicket. Inadvertently, Raygar fired upon the Emperor's approaching shuttle instead. Palpatine survived, and Admiral Kazz subsequently arrested Raygar, charging him with high treason. The Emperor then oversaw the doctor's punishment personally. With PD-28, the Ewoks return safely to the Forest Moon, where Wicket, Kneesaa, Latara and Teebo say good-bye to the pilot droid as he embarked on a search for his old master.

The Battle of Cawa City was fought during the Galactic Civil War when the Alliance to Restore the Republic fought to liberate Sterdic IV from the shattered Galactic Empire. It took place seventeen days after the Battle of Endor and resulted in a Rebel victory.

Cawa City, on Sterdic IV, was occupied by the Empire, with ground forces consisting an All Terrain Armored Transport and air support from TIEs. The Alliance sent Green Group and Feral Group to liberate the city from the Imperial forces. A-wings from Green Group, which included the squadron's new acting commander, Lieutenant L'ulo L'ampar, screened the air of TIE fighters to clear a path for Feral Group's Y-wing bombers. Just as Green Group were clearing the last of the TIEs, Shara Bey's A-wing was hit by a pursuing TIE fighter, although not fatal, her ship started leaking coolant. L'ampar managed to destroy the TIE fighter before it could do any further damage.

Once the approach was clear, Feral Group made their bombing run. Their Y-wings dropped magnetising cluster bombs, which magnetized to the All Terrain Armored Transport and destroyed it instantly. Both sides suffered heavy losses, however it was a Rebel victory.

The Battle of Dac City was a conflict that occurred one year after the rise of the Galactic Empire, when Darth Vader undertook a mission to the planet Mon Cala to determine if a Jedi was hiding there and advising the Mon Calamari king, Lee-Char, in negotiations with the Empire. Moff Wilhuff Tarkin aboard the Sovereign had previously sent down ambassador Telvar to make an trade deal with Lee-Char but the king continued to deny the man and he was forced to take leave for the time being.

At that moment, Vader arrived, along with three Inquisitors and a squad of elite Purge Troopers. They were confronted by the king's chief of security Gial Ackbar who denied the possibility of there being a threat on Mon Cala. However the Lambda-class T-4a shuttle carrying Telvar exploded, killing all on board. This prompted Tarkin to deploy his forces onto Mon Cala. Lee-Char informed the Jedi of this and the Jedi said he could handle the Inquisitors and that he knew the identify of the black armored individual Ackbar had failed to get the name of.

Mon Calamari and Quarren forces under King Lee-Char battled an Imperial battalion consisting of AT-AT walkers, AT-DP walkers, and TIE fighters. Meanwhile, Darth Vader, the Inquisitors Ninth Sister, Tenth Brother, and the Sixth Brother, and Purge Troopers secured the landing platform after killing many Mon Calamari and Quarren.

The Inquisitors headed towards the palace. The Ninth Sister thought that it was folly to believe that the Jedi fugitive would be hiding near the King. Vader responded that King Lee-Char knew how to contact the Jedi fugitive. The Tenth Brother thought that Lee-Char probably fled the moment that the Imperial battalion arrived. However, Vader sensed that the king was still there. Per his previous encounter with the king , Darth Vader reasoned that the king would not abandon his city utill the battle was done.

The Battle of Daluuj was a minor skirmish preceding the Evacuation of Yavin in 0 ABY. It occurred between a small Rebel Alliance team and Imperial forces under Commander Orlok.

Following the first Imperial invasion of Mon Calamari, Admiral Gial Ackbar and his loyal Mon Calamari forces fled to meet with the Alliance Fleet. En route, they were ambushed by Imperial warships over Daluuj and forced to evacuate to the planet below in escape pods.

The pods were later rescued by Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, and Leia Organa. Despite being heavily outmanned, Admiral Ackbar came up with a plan to lure the Imperial ground-skimmers over a mud lake with gigantic worms that had previously dragged the Millennium Falcon down to the bottom upon landing, reasoning that the worms would also be attracted to Imperial machinery as well and attack. Not only were all three ground-skimmers dragged to the bottom, but the Falcon was raised and the Rebel group was allowed to leave Daluuj.

During the Galactic Civil War, the Galactic Empire discovered the location of an administrative base for the Alliance to Restore the Republic that was located on the planet Dankayo ordered the Star Destroyers Avenger, Devastator, and Relentless to bombard it. The Rebel Alliance learned of the impending assault and General Carlist Rieekan ordered the evacuation of the base. After this successful evacuation, Imperial Armored Transports Elusive and Timely recovered sensitive intelligence in the the ruins of the base. As the Imperial transports prepared to leave the Dankayo system, they were attacked by the Lambda-class shuttle Bonderium that had been stolen by the rebels. The Elusive escaped into hyperspace before it could be destroyed, dumping its garbage before it did so. Shortly, the Squib Momship Thrifty entered the star system to retrieve the rubbish. An Ugor battle-wagon soon appeared as well and engaged the Squibs over control of the garbage dump.

Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition

The Battle of Dantooine occurred during the Imperial Period when an Imperial strike force attempted to find and kill Falon Grey, who was hiding on the planet. The clone X1 spearheaded the assault, but X2 joined the rebels inside, taking a different path from his brother.

The Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader sent X1, X2, and other troops to Dantooine to root out and destroy a Jedi that the local villagers had been harboring onplanet. While en route to Dantooine, X2 decided that siding with the Galactic Empire was wrong, and opposed the Empire, as well as his clone brother, X1.

X2 then arrived on the planet, defected, and helped the villagers repel the brutal Imperial invasion. During the battle, he encountered the Jedi Falon Grey, a veteran of the Clone Wars. Grey was revealed to be his and X1's genetic father.

With the initial Imperial invasion in full swing, clone stormtroopers were sent to villages known to harbor Rebel activists, and assaulted the locales using AT-RTs.

In 3639 BBY, during the Galactic War between the reconstituted Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic, the Empire invaded the planet Denova for its baradium reserves. As the Empire lacked the ships to hold the planet's airspace, they landed an entire battalion on the surface, and the Republic was forced to hire the Trandoshan mercenary army known as the Warstalkers to fight back against the Empire. The battle raged for almost three months, but the six Sith Lords known as the Dread Masters used their powers to enslave the Trandoshans' leader, Kephess, and the Imperial army. The Republic and the Empire both investigated the disappearance of Kephess and the Imperial forces, and the battle ended with Kephess's defeat and death—albeit a temporary one, as the Dread Masters resurrected him as Kephess the Undying.

During the Galactic Civil War, a battle was fought over Derilyn. An Alliance force infiltrated Derilyn Space Defense Platform with a mission to destroy the Star Destroyer Brazen. During the mission, the Khuiumin Survivors, contacted by Alliance operative Shondra Del, arrived and assault the Imperial forces, aiding in the Alliance team's escape. The Brazen was destroyed by bombs planted by the Alliance team, which also caused extensive damage to the Derilyn Space Defense Platform.

The Battle of the Cliffs was a battle fought on the planet of Cilpar during the Galactic Civil War.

After liberating an Imperial base on Endor, Throm Loro led members of the Cilpari Resistance against Moff Boren Tascl's forces. When Loro's actions caught the attention of the Alliance to Restore the Republic, Moff Tascl responded by engaging the resistance in open warfare.

Throm Loro's last stand was in a mountainous region of the planet, where he was accompanied by Groznik, a Wookiee slave he had freed on Endor. During the battle, two Lambda-class shuttles launched a strafing run on the resistance soldiers on a rocky plateau. Throm was caught in the laser fire and killed. Groznik, having sworn a life debt to Throm, retaliated, hurling a boulder at one of the shuttles and destroying it.

The Battle of the Corridor was a conflict in the Feswe Corridor between the Rebel Alliance and Imperial forces under the House of Tagge in 0 ABY.

Baron Orman Tagge and Doctor Silas Tagge intended to use the Omega Frost, a new superweapon, to flash-freeze the Alliance Fleet as it traveled through the Feswe Corridor. However his plans were thwarted when the Rebel Luke Skywalker destroyed one of the Omega Frost's conductor towers from space with his lightsaber. With the weapon inactive, the Rebel forces led by the Millennium Falcon were able to pass through the asteroid corridor and destroy both Silas Tagge's Mining Explorer and General Ulric Tagge's battlecruiser. Ulric Tagge managed to escape the destruction of his cruiser in an escape pod.

The civilians of the settlement were slaughtered by the droid forces of the Separatists, including B2-series super battle droids and HMP droid gunships. During the attack, a number of Mandalorian warriors of Death Watch intervened, fighting back against the battle droids. The young Din Djarin, whose parents were killed in the attack, was rescued by a Mandalorian warrior and taken in as a foundling. Djarin often thought back on the battle during his adult life.

In 228 BBY, a battle on Banchii occurred when the Nihil, led by Minister of Advancement Baron Boolan attacked the planet Banchii. Boolan initially traveled there in hopes of recruiting the various Jedi there, including Jedi Knights Lily Tora-Asi and Reath Silas, fallen Jedi Azlin Rell, and Jedi Masters Savina Besatrix Malagán and Arkoff for his experiments, with the promise that he would not harm the people of Banchii if they complied. When the Jedi in charge, Tora-Asi, refused, Boolan sent his horde of Nihil pirates to attack the planet and the Jedi. As Tora-Asi fought the Nihil, the plants of the planet began to attack them too, as members of the Drengir species had triggered the plant life to protect Tora-Asi in their stead after the Jedi helped them flee Banchii.

As the Baron started to flee, not believing he could win the battle, he released Nameless creatures, which preyed on Force-sensitives such as the Jedi and inhibited them with only their presence. However, the Jedi were assisted by a large group of non-Force-sensitive Banchii natives as well as a group of Banchiians led by Shosho, a Nihil defector named Maktan Plynt, and Malagán's friend Dexter Jettster, who defeated the Nameless. Meanwhile, Boolan made one final plea to Rell to join him and study the Nameless, but Rell refused and chose to protect Jedi Initiates Viv'Nia Nia'Viv and Nima Allets instead. With the Nameless defeated, the Jedi drove the Nihil away, winning the battle and successfully protecting the planet.

Baxton was the Human male driver of Imperial Head of State Jagged Fel's limousine. In 43 ABY, he traveled with Fel to Coruscant for the Unification Summit among the three prevalent galactic governments. Later, Baxton was present during Fel's capture of psychotic Jedi Knights Yaqeel Saav'etu and Bazel Warv, after which he was confronted by Galactic Alliance Security troopers under the command of Captain Atar. Fel, however, used his diplomatic immunity to convince Atar to let Baxton go, and they left the scene in his limousine with Jedi Knight Jaina Solo. Atar, frustrated, ordered an assault speeder to block their exit. Fel told Baxton to ask the speeder's commander to let them pass, but the officer refused to move his speeder. Baxton got into a heated argument with the officer, but Fel, again using his diplomatic immunity, was able to force Atar to order the Security troops to move, and Baxton drove them away.

Baxton was a big-shouldered Human male who served under Head of State Jagged Fel in the Imperial Remnant. In 43 ABY, he traveled with Fel to the galactic capital of Coruscant There, Baxton served as the driver of Fel's limousine, an exceptionally long and heavily armored luxury speeder. Around this time, several Jedi Knights began to develop a mysterious psychosis that caused them to believe that everyone they knew had been replaced by impostors, and the Galactic Alliance decided to deal with the issue by encasing the affected Knights in carbonite.

Baxton was present in 43.5 ABY when Jedi Knights Bazel Warv and Yaqeel Saav'etu developed the psychosis. They were quickly incapacitated by Fel, Jedi Knight Jaina Solo, and her parents, Han Solo and Leia Organa Solo, outside the Jedi Temple's speeder entrance. Warv, who was hit by tranquilizer darts, fell onto Fel's limousine, severely denting the roof. Fel ordered Baxton to stay quiet about the incident, and while Han, Jaina, and the Head of State hid Saav'etu and Warv inside the Jedi Temple, Organa Solo and Baxton remained out by the limousine. There, they were accosted by a Galactic Alliance Security assault squad under the command of Captain Atar, who ordered several of his troopers to surround the limousine while four more held Baxton at blasterpoint. Atar confronted Organa Solo, who denied any knowledge of the situation. When Fel, Han, and Jaina returned, the Imperial Head of State quickly ordered Atar to have his men stand down. The captain, fearing that he would evoke a diplomatic incident, complied, ordering his men to release Baxton and the limousine. Atar then requested that the Solos hand over Warv and Saav'etu, and when he showed them a warrant for the arrest of the two psychotic Jedi, Han and Leia decided to stall for time by reentering the Temple and closing the gate behind them. Fel and Jaina then got into the limousine and Baxton drove them away.

Lord Baylan Skoll was a Force-sensitive human male mercenary who, in his past, had once acted as a Jedi Knight and Jedi General in the Grand Army of the Republic. Skoll managed to survive the Great Jedi Purge. During the New Republic Era, Skoll and his apprentice Shin Hati were allied with the forces of Morgan Elsbeth, an industrialist and Nightsister survivor who sought the return of Grand Admiral Thrawn of the Galactic Empire. The mission to find Thrawn coincided with fellow Purge survivor Ahsoka Tano and her apprentice Sabine Wren's search for Jedi Padawan Ezra Bridger, resulting in a battle between Skoll and Tano on the planet Seatos in which Tano was defeated and Wren was taken prisoner.

Shortly after arriving at Peridea and sensing its connection to the Force, Skoll met with Grand Admiral Thrawn, but he was truly unconcerned with Elsbeth and Thrawn's plans. When sent by Thrawn with Hati to hunt down and destroy Bridger and Wren, his views diverged from Hati as they started to drift in their own separate ways about the future of the force and their destinies. Upon finding Bridger, Skoll and Hati parted as the mentor no longer believed that Hati's future and destiny could be achieved if she continued to be his apprentice. He briefly confronted Ahsoka Tano again before she escaped and continuing his journey to discover his destiny on the planet.

After Thrawn and Ezra's escape during the battle of Peridea, Skoll continued his search for his destiny and came upon the monument of The Father and The Son, as well as a statue of The Daughter which had been severely damaged, unaware that his former apprentice was still on the planet, along with Ahsoka Tano, Sabine Wren, and Huyang.

Baylan Skoll was a human During his time in the Order, he learned of Peridea. He believed it to be old stories and fairy tales. Skoll was a Jedi General in the Grand Army of the Republic, but in 19 BBY, the Clone Wars ended with Supreme Chancellor and secret Sith Lord Sheev Palpatine reforming the Republic into the Galactic Empire, and ordering the execution of all Jedi.

Baylis Archan was a male Human Padawan who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as an apprentice to Jedi Knight Sha Koon.

A Human from Corellia, Baylis Archan was discovered to be Force-sensitive and taken to the Coruscant Jedi Temple as an infant. Entering into the Temple academy, Initiate Archan was encouraged to develop his naturally heightened telepathic abilities during his training there. After graduating from the academy, Archan was chosen by the Kel Dor Jedi Knight Sha Koon as a Padawan.

When the Clone Wars broke out between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Archan and his Master led the clone troopers of the Grand Army of the Republic against the forces of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, taking up the rank of Commander. Deployed to the planet Giju to lead the ongoing battle there, Archan and the men he fought alongside died in combat, leaving Koon to bring the battle to a successful conclusion. Holding him in her arms as he died, Koon sensed his passing through the Force; her connection to Archan was very strong, as she would feel a similar pain when her uncle, the esteemed High Council member Plo Koon, was killed during the first stages of the Great Jedi Purge.

Baz was a male human who served the Galactic Empire's Imperial Navy as an ensign during the early years of its reign. He was assigned to serve on Sentinel Base, a construction project under the command of Moff Wilhuff Tarkin on a moon in the Outer Rim Territories. While there he used spice, a drug which affected his performance. While traveling on board the Carrion Spike, Tarkin's personal ship, during a journey it made in 14 BBY to the planet Coruscant from Sentinel Base, Tarkin noticed signs indicating Baz's spice use and had him confined to his quarters.

The male human Baz served the Galactic Empire during the early years of its reign over the galaxy, held the junior officer rank of ensign in the Imperial Navy. During that year, he was stationed on Sentinel Base, an Imperial project on a moon in an unnamed system in the Outer Rim Territories, where construction of a superweapon was secretly taking place under the command of Moff Wilhuff Tarkin. While at the base, Baz would take spice, a type of illicit drug, while hidden in an area of Sentinel's motor pool repair bay outside the auxiliary dome, which was not covered by security cameras. On one such occasion he stood near a T-44 landspeeder in a section of the bay close to a landing platform undergoing repairs, which left a circular lubricant stain impregnated with grit on his left boot. The spice use caused Baz to arrive late to his duties several times and act inattentively when he did, which was included in his record. Some of the plugs of spice he used were not properly processed, and so stained his fingers when he pinched them.

Following a brief attack on Sentinel Base by a rebel cell led by former Republic Intelligence agent Berch Teller, Tarkin was summoned to the Imperial capital Coruscant, and Baz was selected to serve as a midshipman on board the Moff's personal starship, the Carrion Spike. Once the vessel left Sentinel Base and entered hyperspace, Tarkin summoned eighteen members of the ship's crew, including Baz, to the ship's conference room for an impromptu inspection. While he looked over the crew, Tarkin's attention was drawn to the stain on Baz's boot, which the ensign claimed was hair gel. Tarkin recognized the stain as lubricant however, and revealed that he knew about the areas of the repair bay used by spice users. After pointing out several other pieces of evidence that Baz indulged in spice, Tarkin ordered a petty officer to confine Baz to his quarters for the rest of the journey, claiming he would deal with the ensign once they reached Coruscant.

Baz had unruly brown hair cut to Imperial regulation length, which he attempted to tame with hair gel in preparation for inspections. His dipping of spice left a nascent cavity in his left eyetooth, and pinching unprocessed plugs of the substance left yellow-ochre stains on the index finger and thumb of his right hand. The spice also caused him to be unpunctual and inattentive, and during Tarkin's inspection Baz's eyes were bloodshot, his gaze unsteady and he sweated noticeably, which he blamed on hyperspace nausea.

Beam Beam was a female fathier who was born around 1 BBY. In 3 ABY, they were ridden by Vinis Karyvin and competed in a fixed fathier race for the Galactic Empire.

Beam Beam was born around 1 BBY and by 3 ABY they competed in fathier races held in the city of Canto Bight on the Outer Rim planet Cantonica. That year, the fathier was purchased by the Galactic Empire. An Imperial officer personally inspected Beam Beam and determined them to be a fine specimen. Beam Beam was then set up by the Imperial Security Bureau to win a fixed race that was sponsored by the Galactic Empire and held during the Canto Cup racing tournament on Cantonica. For the race, Beam Beam was ridden by Imperial officer and jockey Vinis Karyvin. The race was promoted on posters placed around the city Myrra on Karyvin's homeworld of Akiva prior to its start.

Kay Vess, a scoundrel and cantonica native, noticed the promotional posters while in Myrra and immediately assumed the race was going to be fixed so the Imperial jockey would win. She had her suspicion confirmed when she overheard two Imperial stormtroopers talking about the race near The Alcazar cantina in Myrra. She eventually stole a datacard from an Imperial officer in the cantina and was able to determine that Karyvin was an Imperial Lieutenant. Vess then bet on the outcome of the race at a holographic fathier-betting module located in The Alcazar and watched Beam Beam with through the betting console's hologram.

Beam Beam was a female fathier who had brown fur and black eyes. During the sponsored race, the fathier was 299 centimeters tall and weighed 915 kilograms. An Imperial officer who inspected Beam Beam considered the fathier to be a fine specimen.

Some Jedi, commonly members of the Neti species, were capable of releasing an incredible beam of light as they channeled the sum of the Force energy of the planet on which they were rooted or other large energy source at their moment of death. Such power was capable of catastrophic planetary surface destruction, as well as the obliteration of starships and other vessels. In 10 ABY, to save Jedi Knights Luke Skywalker and Kam Solusar, the ancient Jedi Master Ood Bnar released a devastating beam of light to annihilate Executor Sedriss.

More than one hundred years later, when Emperor Krayt's forces were triumphant in their assault, a female Neti Master named T'ra Saa was joined by fellow Jedi Nat Skywalker, and together unleashed a beam of light to clear an escape route for their allies using the direct energy of the Temple's detonating reactor.

Following the deaths of both Bnar and Saa, tiny saplings burst from the ground where the original Neti died, seemingly imbued with the planet's Force energy, still traveling through the engrained roots.

Bearus was a humanoid male who served as chairman of the Empress Teta system's Carbonite Guild. Bearus presided over the carbonite smelter that orbited Empress Teta, where he facilitated annual tours of progress that were conducted by Lord and Lady Keto, rulers of the Tetan worlds. Bearus oversaw his last inspection in 3997 BBY, when the children of the Ketos, Aleema and Satal, arrived on station to initiate their political takeover of the Empress Teta system under the guise of their new Sith cult, the Krath. All of the Tetan officials present were killed, and Bearus was among the casualties, having first been overcome by the Krath's Sith magic and then forced into a vat of molten carbonite.

Bearus was a humanoid male politician native to the Empress Teta star system. He obtained a position within the system's Carbonite Guild, an influential mining conglomerate that worked in close correspondence with the Tetan Monarchy. Bearus eventually rose to the title of guild chairman, and under his leadership, the guild saw great success with the production of carbonite, a mined ore that was an integral component in the manufacture of starship parts, most notably hyperdrive engines. By 3997 BBY, the guild's profit margin had risen by fifteen percent under the leadership of Bearus, which in turn provided a significant boost to the already flourishing Tetan economy.

Bearus operated from a carbonite smelter space station that orbited the system's capital world of Empress Teta. The Emperor and Empress of the Tetan worlds, Lord Keto and his sister Magda, conducted annual inspections of Bearus' smelter station and its production progress. During the inspection of 3997 BBY, the Ketos arrived as scheduled, and Bearus escorted them through his facility. In the midst of the tour, Bearus was made aware that the children of the Ketos, Aleema and her cousin Satal, were en route to the station. The chairman was reluctant to grant them permission to enter at first, knowing that their presence was a breach of protocol, and that only sanctioned officials were allowed to attend such important matters of state. However, he allowed for their entry onto the station, believing that their arrival would not detract from Lord Keto's inspection.

Bearus' efforts to improve the production of carbonite pleased Lord Keto, who noted that the significant rise in the station's net revenue directly resulted in a substantial boost in the Tetan system's overall wealth and influence. However, when Lord Keto learned of Bearus' decision to admit Aleema and Satal on board the smelter, he chastised the guild chairman for his insubordination. Bearus offered to have the children sent away, but Lord Keto relented, and instead blamed their royal tutor for the mishap. Aleema and Satal arrived at that moment, declaring themselves and their new Krath Sith cult the new governing body of the Empress Teta system, and proceeded to subdue the present Tetan officials. Lord Keto ordered Bearus to summon the authorities and have Aleema and Satal taken into custody, but when the chairman reached for a comlink, Aleema used Sith magic to transform it into a monster, and it attacked Bearus.

Beatas was a dark-green-skinned Klatooinian mercenary and the operative leader of Ploovo's Protocol Team.

Beatas began his career as a juvenile delinquent, and was lucky enough to avoid slavery for all of his life. When he was old enough, he began working as a hired thug for different criminals. It was during this time that he worked under the light of the Timja Suns, which caused the yellow color of his eyebrows. He used a heavy blaster pistol and grenades. At some time, he worked for Gotal loan shark Thar Lasan and his organization in the Corporate Sector. Lasan died unexpectedly and his organization was merged with Ploovo Two-For-One's around 5 BBY. As one of Lasan's assets, Beatas began working for Ploovo. Plovoo assigned Beatas to Ploovo's Protocol Team, collecting money from debtors. Beatas discovered that he enjoyed his new work: Should he find a debtor who had missed a payment, Beatas would hit this person until the money "miraculously" appears. In some cases, even the debtor is confused when the money appeared. Beatas also enjoyed the word "miraculous", his favorite and the longest in his lexicon. Due to his enjoyment of the job, Beatas was very loyal to Ploovo.

Bedoch was a male Human Jedi Master who served the Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order during the Cold War with the Sith Empire. A member of a sect of the Order known as the Corellian Jedi, Bedoch was renowned for both his patriotism and his paranoia. He consistently feared the end of days, and came to see the Battle of Corellia as just such an event, barricading himself in the Republic Foundation Museum, where he perished.

A Force-sensitive Corellian, Bedoch was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, achieving the rank of Jedi Master by the time of the time of the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. Like many Jedi born on Corellia, Bedoch possessed a deep-rooted patriotism for his homeworld and was a devoted member of the sect of Corellian Jedi which chose to take on missions relating to the planet and her people. Renowned throughout the Order and the ranks of the "Green" Jedi of Corellia, Bedoch was on his homeworld when the Empire invaded. Fighting valiantly, Bedoch saw the Empire's arrival and the ensuing occupation as a sign of the end of days for Corellia. Refusing to surrender or to retreat to the Jedi Enclave with his fellows, Bedoch fled to the Republic Foundation Museum to defend Corellia's history.

Proclaiming the Imperials to be an infection needing to be removed, he defiantly refused to leave the Museum when a strike team was sent in after him. Defying the Empire and without any support from the Jedi at the Enclave, Bedoch was forced to fight alone in the Museum's halls. Valiantly attacking the strike team with his lightsaber, Bedoch was swiftly outnumbered and killed. When the Imperial team searched the Jedi's body they discovered Bedoch's personal access codes to the Jedi Enclave, thus allowing them to access it without setting off the security klaxons.

Like most Jedi, Bedoch was taught the way of lightsaber combat, and became proficient in the skill once he attained the rank of Master. During the Galactic War, Bedoch wielded a double-bladed lightsaber which emitted emerald blades.

Beebox was a male bounty hunter of an unknown humanoid alien species active during the Galactic Civil War. After joining Chelli Lona Aphra, Bossk, Krrsantan, and IG-90 on the Son-tuul Pride robbery, Beebox eventually received a bounty to kill or capture Aphra. When he brought in a disintegrated body that was not Aphra to attempt to claim the bounty, he was killed by Darth Vader, who sensed his deception.

Beebox met up at a bar on Son-tuul with fellow bounty hunters Bossk and IG-90, who wanted to know where Krrsantan was. He explained that Krrsantan was fighting in the pit, confusing to others, especially Bossk, who wondered why an ex-Xonti Brothers gladiator would want to relive those moments. Beebox suggested that he got nostalgic. After Krrsantan stopped fighting, Bossk, Beebox, Krrsantan, and IG-90 had a drink in the bar. Dr. Aphra, who had recently worked with Darth Vader, explained to the bounty hunter team that Darth Vader recently killed the Son-tuul Pride leader, and the Sith Lord had taken off the Hutt credits to an Imperial light cruiser, which IG-90 explained everyone knew. Aphra told the team that she knew exactly where it was going, and she could make them rich.

The bounty hunter group headed to the Anthan system, outside the space of Anthan Prime, on Aphra's personal ship, the Ark Angel, planning to rob the ship. Aphra blew up an "asteroid," and the ship they were keeping the bounty was surrounded by debris. Aphra sent out an ion torpedo and explained that they would think that their power was cut due to the asteroid field. When Beebox and the rest of the crew broke into the ship, they deactivated the shields so Krrsantan, in his ship, could blow the ship's bridge and Aphra's astromech Beetee could magnetically pulled as many credits out as he could, although Krrsantan actually used his ship's secret magnetic feature to pull a few credits in for himself.

After the heist on Anthan Prime, Beebox and the others received their payment, but since a lot of the money "floated away," the amount was fewer than expected. The group then made plans to attack Aphra, but Aphra explained that she would not take a share in an attempt to dissuade them.

When his father lay dying, Acton secretly finished him off so that he would obtain all of his family's money. He then proceeded to roam the galaxy, causing others pain and suffering using the Force. Been was a male Otolla Gungan who was a member of the Gungan High Council at the time of the Invasion of Naboo and lived during the Galactic Civil War between the Galactic Empire and the Rebel Alliance.

Been was the keeper of the ancient records of the Gungans, and knew the locations of many secret Gungan hiding places. During the Trade Federation invasion of Naboo, Been supported Boss Rugor Nass' decision to evacuate the population of Otoh Gunga to the sacred place, and later agreed with him in forming an alliance with Queen Padmé Amidala.

During the Galactic Civil War sometime following 0 BBY, Been could still be found at the sacred place. While there, he employed the help of a spacer. The spacer, who was sympathetic to the Rebellion, was first tasked with retrieving documents from Boona Tanje. After successfully completing the task, Been gave the spacer three more missions. The next mission was to escort a Human female named Reefa Been back to the sacred place. Though the spacer was ambushed by four bandits, Reefa was returned safely. The spacer was then told to kill the bandit leader, and escort an individual named Vajoo Jinssa back to the sacred place. Once again, the spacer failed to let Been down.

In the MMORPG Star Wars Galaxies, Been appeared as a Non-Player Character (NPC) in the Gungan sacred place point of interest. Here, players could take a series of quests from Been which involved simple kill, escort, or delivery objectives. Much of his quest dialogue was bugged, and Been was eventually removed from the game.

A member of the Lightning Battalion holding the rank of sergeant, Beez served during the Icarii Campaign under Colonel Abal Karda. He notably saw action at Camp 40, where Imperial forces caught an Icarii war party attempting a sneak attack and blew them to pieces with a heavy artillery barrage.

When Boba Fett arrived on Vestar in pursuit of Karda, now an Enemy of the Empire wanted for shooting dead his commanding officer, he rescued Beez and some of his squadmates from an ill-fated bar fight with a large Wookiee and demanded information about their former commander.

Like other members of the ground forces, Beez was disdainful of the officer in charge of the overall campaign, General Nim, who never faced the Icarii in battle himself; when he learned that Nim had been murdered by Karda, he claimed that the general "had it coming". Conversely, he expressed some sympathy for Nim's murderer, Colonel Karda, who he insisted was the best officer he had ever served under.

Beez also filled Fett in on the nature of the Icarii Queen Selestrine, explaining how the wealth of her tribe was woven into her hair, her precognitive powers and her supposed death at Karda's hands. The bounty hunter would use this information to deduce the contents of the mysterious kneebshide casket carried by Karda as his pursuit progressed.

Corporal Beezer both Beezer and Carlson were selected as members of a commando strike team that was sent to the moon of Endor by the Alliance with the objective of disabling an Imperial shield generator built there to protect the Death Star II superweapon.

Using the stolen Imperial shuttle Tydirium, the team landed on the moon and proceeded to the rear of the generator, where a security bunker acted as a backdoor. Expecting the Alliance attack, the Imperials ambushed the rebels at the bunker, but they were defeated when the local Ewok population came to the aid of the strike team. The rebels then destroyed the generator, allowing the Alliance Fleet to destroy the Death Star. Beezer had light skin, brown eyes, and brown hair. She wore a green helmet, and a brown jerkin with a white shirt.

In the current Star Wars canon, Beezer was pictured in an entry for Rebel troopers on the StarWars.com Encyclopedia.

The image used in the Encyclopedia entry was a promotional photo taken for the 1983 original trilogy film, Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi, although Beezer does not appear in the film itself. The photo depicts Beezer, and other commandos stood with protagonist Luke Skywalker as their prisoner in one of the Death Star II's corridors. A card in the 1999 Endor Limited expansion set of the Decipher Star Wars Customizable Card Game then linked the name to Eddon's character. The 2008 StarWars.com Hyperspace-exclusive short story Fists of Ion provided the character's first name as Dansra. The story's author Edward M. Erdelac, stated that the name was a tuckerization of his wife's first name.

Jin-Jin subsequently was forced into stripping the ship of parts which he sold on the black market to recoup his losses. When he started his career as a smuggler and mercenary, Jin-Jin made enough money to refit the Solace and turn it from a rampaged bucket of bolts into a useful rampaged bucket of bolts. Bela Kiwiiks was a female Togruta Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the Great Galactic War, the Cold War, and the Galactic War with the resurgent Sith Empire. One of the apprentices of Ngani Zho, she fought as a Jedi Knight in the Battle of Rhen Var alongside Satele Shan, Jaric Kaedan, and Syo Bakarn. In the aftermath of the Sacking of Coruscant and the end of the Great Galactic War, all four former students of Zho were appointed to the Jedi High Council as Jedi Masters, and in the decade following the Treaty of Coruscant Kiwiiks took on a young woman named Kira Carsen as her apprentice when she discovered the teenage Human on the moon of Nar Shaddaa.

In 3643 BBY, the Council began to sense a dark presence on the Republic capital of Coruscant, and Kiwiiks was sent to the planet with her Padawan to investigate. Kiwiiks was soon joined by fellow Council member Orgus Din and his former apprentice, who discovered that the Republic's secret superweapon projects were in danger of being discovered by the Empire, and she traveled to the desert world of Tatooine at the request of the Republic general Var Suthra in order to secure the Shock Drum weapon.

A Force-sensitive Togruta, Bela Kiwiiks was discovered by the Jedi Order and trained as a Jedi by the Human Jedi Master Ngani Zho, along with Satele Shan, Syo Bakarn, and Jaric Kaedan. relationships that would continue throughout her friends' lives.

Near the end of the war, she participated in the Battle of Rhen Var alongside Zho's other former students—Satele Shan, Syo Bakarn, and Jaric Kaedan—where the four aided the Forty-fifth Battalion in the fight against the Imperial military. Between the four of them, they had fought on the ash plains of Lenico IV and against Gelpog the Tyrant on his asteroid-hives, and they were all powerful warriors in their own right. Under Shan's leadership, the Republic and Jedi forces were able to drive the Empire off of the icy planet, and Shan single-handedly defeated the Dark Councilor Darth Mekhis in a duel.

Belaya was a Human female Jedi Guardian who resided in the Jedi Enclave on the planet Dantooine during the Jedi Civil War. A student of the renowned Jedi Master Zhar Lestin, Belaya was devoted to the Jedi traditions but struggled with controlling her emotions. She became very close to Juhani, a Cathar Padawan whose emotions were similarly volatile.

A test of humility devised by Juhani's Master, Quatra, resulted in Juhani lashing out in anger and falling to the dark side when she mistakenly believed she had killed her Master. After the fallen Padawan fled to the nearby Ancient Grove, her dark emotions turned the surrounding kath hounds aggressive, but the Jedi Council would not permit Belaya to attempt to redeem her dear companion.

When Revan, a former Jedi Knight who had lost his memories, arrived at the Jedi Enclave, Belaya confronted him about not being dressed in Jedi apparel, then apologized for her behavior. In Revan's final trial to become a Jedi once again, Master Lestin instructed him to confront and cleanse the darkness in the Ancient Grove. Revan spared Juhani and convinced her to return to the light. Afterward, Belaya expressed her gratitude to Revan for his actions, and she was reunited with Juhani until the redeemed Jedi joined Revan's quest to find the Star Forge and defeat Darth Malak and his Sith Empire.

Belaya was a young, Force-sensitive female citizen of the Galactic Republic. Belaya sought a deeper knowledge of the Force and traveled to the Jedi Enclave on the Outer Rim planet Dantooine. Jedi Master Zhar Lestin, a Twi'lek male member of the Jedi Council there, trained her as a Jedi.

Beldiss was a male Human Sith Lord of the reconstituted Sith Empire living during the Galactic War with the Galactic Republic.

He was one of the most high ranking Imperial diplomats on Voss along with Darth Serevin. His plan was to take failed Voss Mystics in order to teach them the ways of the Sith, thus reducing the need for an alliance with the Voss in favor of increased quantities of Voss Sith. Lord Beldiss utilized his smooth charm to continually show the Galactic Republic in a bad light, earning a rival in Ambassador Jannik.

Eventually, when a Republic traveling hero uncovered his plans, Beldiss invited him to his base in the Ruined City to show that his new Voss acolytes willingly joined the Sith. But when his acolytes considered joining the Jedi, Beldiss refused to lose his initiates after so much effort. He attacked the hero, but was killed, with the Voss joining the Jedi Order.

Beldorion was a Force-sensitive Hutt Dark Jedi who served as a Jedi Knight under the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic roughly four hundred years before the founding of the Galactic Empire. After being sent to Nam Chorios, he fell to the dark side and established himself as the ruler of the planet, forsaking the Jedi. He was killed in a lightsaber duel with Leia Organa Solo in 13 ABY.

Discovered by the Jedi Order before 400 BBY, records indicate that Beldorion was the only known Hutt to enter into the Order. He was trained at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. During his training, he and other Jedi Initiates were taken to the Caves of Masposhani, where they ran races, and to dark worlds like Af'El and Y'nybeth to hone their Force sense. Beldorion graduated from the academy and was taken as a Padawan by a Jedi Master. Following years of travel and study, Beldorion passed his Trials of Knighthood and was elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight. Taking on missions from the Jedi High Council, Beldorion was dispatched to Nam Chorios with fellow Knight Taselda in 400 BBY.

While on the planet the two Jedi Knights failed to complete their mission when they fell to the lure of the dark side of the Force and abandoned the Order. Beldorion cast aside Taselda as the weaker half of the team and established himself as the ruler of the world. Providing his subjects with honorifics which he should be addressed by such as "Beldorion of the Ruby Eyes" and "Beldorion the Splendid," Beldorion was corrupt and enslaved many. While originally prepared as Beldorion's meal, the Droch known as Dzym came to conspire with the Hutt, helping the Dark Jedi remain strong and youthful in exchange for the freedom to access the planet's rare Tsil stones.

Due to his long abandonment of the Jedi Order, he was never hunted during the Great Jedi Purge, so it wasn't until 13 ABY that Beldorion's relatively unopposed rule was disrupted by the arrival of Jedi Callista Ming. While she was unsuccessful in getting to the Hutt and imprisoned, her disappearance drew the attention of additional Jedi: Luke Skywalker, the founder of the New Jedi Order, and his twin sister, Leia Organa. Like Ming, Organa was also captured by the Hutt who divulged stories from the past, recalling the histories of Jedi Masters Thon and Yoda. During her captivity, Organa was able to regain possession of her lightsaber and engage her captor in a duel. Though the centuries-old Dark Jedi was powerful, Organa was able to move more freely and bisected the Hutt at the mid-section.

Belia Darzu was a female Shi'ido who reigned as a Dark Lord of the Sith during the last quarter of the New Sith Wars. A born shape-shifter, Darzu typically appeared as a tall Human woman with short brown hair. In 1250 BBY, she led the revived Sith Empire at the beginning of a period called the Sictis Wars. An accomplished Sith alchemist, Lord Darzu studied an obscure Force technique known as mechu-deru, leading her to concoct a virus capable of transforming its victims into mutated cyborgs—technobeasts. Using a hidden fortress on the planet Tython, she created an army of technobeasts in a campaign against the Galactic Republic and its Jedi protectors. By 1230 BBY, the Dark Lord had fallen victim to a conspiracy to end her life. Pursued by her traitorous Sith followers and the vengeful Mecrosa Order, Darzu's reign culminated in her assassination.

Belia Darzu was a female Shi'ido who lived during the New Sith Wars, A natural-born shape-shifter like all members of her species, Darzu commonly assumed the physical form of a Human woman. By 1250 BBY, she had seized the mantle of Dark Lord of the Sith, rising to power over the resurgent Sith empire at the beginning of a period called the Sictis Wars. Around this time, she researched Sith alchemy along with the principles of mechu-deru, a Force technique granting absolute control over mechanical systems.

At some point before the end of 1230 BBY, Darzu built a secret stronghold on the Deep Core world of Tython. as well as a Sith holocron; Darzu's holocron—of which remained inside the underground inner sanctum of her fortress—would eventually contain her accumulated knowledge of mechu-deru and Sith alchemy, along with her philosophical views on the Force and instructions detailing the creation of a holocron.

Harnessing the dark side energy spread throughout the planet Tython, Lord Darzu used her fortress to research the creation of machine-organic hybrids known as technobeasts. In this pursuit, she studied the anatomy of several different species, documenting her work through a range of notes and sketches. a technovirus capable of growing metallic tumors on a victim's body. By means of a new incantation called mechu-deru vitae, she used the nanogene spore to transform living beings into Sithspawn mutants—technobeasts.

Belina was a girlfriend of Wedge Antilles when he was growing up. She had spent several nights with Wedge during their days on Tatooine. When Wedge and Wes Janson were stranded on Hoth, Wedge would reminisce about Belina and the great times he had had with her, hoping to keep his mind off the isolation. However, thinking about Belina only made Wedge more depressed.

Due to the dubious nature of this story and the contradictory backstory given to Wedge in Star Wars (1977) 78, it's unknown if Belina actually existed or was simply a fabrication of Wedge's story. The assertion that Wedge apparently met Belina when he was growing up on Tatooine, when he was actually from Corellia, may point more heavily towards the latter.

Belkan was a Human male who served in the Republic Military during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. When his squad was sent down into The Works on Coruscant to combat a group of rogue droids, they encountered an Imperial strike team that was attempting to recover an astrogation computer from the ruins of the Jedi Temple. Belkan was fatally injured in the attack, but managed to communicate his mission to a traveling hero, who successfully retrieved the computer.

A member of the Republic Military, Belkan had achieved the rank of Ensign by 3643 BBY. He served under General Wendin, who commanded the Republic forces on the Republic's capital world Coruscant. Following the Sacking of Coruscant by the Sith, the programming of many droids in The Works became corrupted and they began to attack anyone they encountered.

During the Cold War between the Republic and the Sith Empire that followed the Sacking, Belkan and his squad was sent into the Works to both aid the Republic forces there and to search for a valuable astrogation computer in the ruins of the Jedi Temple. But Belkan's unit unintentionally stumbled across part of an Imperial strike team, which was searching for the same computer, and were promptly ambushed. The Imperials decimated the squad, forcing them to retreat back to the Republic's base in the upper Works.

Ensign Belkan was critically injured in the attack, but he managed to encounter a traveling hero to whom he relayed the threat of the Imperials before he died. Thanks to Belkan's information, the hero was able to enter the Temple and recover the computer from the Sith forces within. The hero gave the computer to General Wendin, giving the Republic access to a series of secret hyperspace routes.

Bella was a female Twi'lek who served as a lieutenant to Captain Cavik Toth during the Clone Wars. In 22 BBY, she flew a personal assault transport and commanded the destroyer Reaver.

Bella was Cavik Toth's most trusted lieutenant. She oversaw the test of Toth's new weapon Trihexalon on Point Modie on the planet Maramere. Jedi Master Adi Gallia and Reti intervened to protect the innocents. Despite the results showing that the test was successful, Bella wanted to finish off the city. However, Adi Gallia managed to stop any more severe damage to the city.

Bella was then on the Sabaoth Destroyer Reaver commencing a salvage run on the Orbital Defense Cannon. However the Lok Revenants had the same idea which resulted in her forces on a Tug of War for the parts, Bella lost all of the parts but she did have a back-up plan in case of this. She sent a couple of Sabaoth Frigates to try to stop the Tritus from heading to Lok but even that had failed. She then went to Lok with Toth make a stand against the Lok Revenants but the pirates placed the Orbital Defense Cannon on one of Lok's moons known as Khons which started the Second Battle of Lok.

After the defenses failed and Nym destroyed the foundry. Lieutenant Bella decided to take the fight with Nym in her personal assault transport. Despite overwhelming firepower she was killed in a dogfight with Nym.

Bellis was a Human male who lived on the planet Ord Mantell with his wife, Lin, during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. At the time of the Separatist War started by a group of Separatists attempting to overthrow the planet's government, Bellis and Lin lived in a house in Talloran village, a small settlement on the island of Avilatan. After the Separatists captured the village, Bellis spied on them for the Republic.

In the year 3643 BBY, the Separatists stole a powerful ZR-57 orbital strike bomb from the Republic—prompting the Republic forces on the planet to ask for Bellis's help in uncovering the bomb's location. Ultimately, he was able to determine that the bomb was housed in a supply outpost on the small island of Mannett Point. After placing the information in his field box, Bellis contacted the Republic forces in order to set up a meeting so that he could give them the information. In response, the Republic Special Forces unit known as Havoc Squad sent a newly-recruited sergeant to meet with Bellis in Talloran village. However, Bellis was killed by the Separatists before the sergeant arrived, although the soldier was still able to retrieve the field box from Bellis's wife.

A Human male, Bellis was alive during the time of the Cold War fought between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. At some point during his life, Bellis married a Human female named Lin, with whom he lived in a two-story house in Talloran village, a small settlement located on Avilatan, an island on the planet Ord Mantell. While Bellis and Lin lived on the planet, a group of Separatists started a conflict in rebellion against the Republic and Ord Mantell's government in an attempt to take control of the planet. and they ultimately barricaded it to defend against Republic counterattacks.

During that time, Bellis worked as a spy for the Republic and reported on Separatist activities to Republic forces at Fort Garnik, a Republic base located near Talloran village. While working as a spy for the Republic, Bellis and his wife stayed in their home, where Bellis stored his field box, a type of container used by Republic agents to store important uncovered information. Bellis risked his life for the Republic many times in order to provide intelligence on Separatist activities. He always met with Republic forces in person, due to the fact that the Separatists could monitor nearby communications with signal tappers.

Bellow was a clone trooper who served in the 501st Legion of the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars. Bellow served under Jedi General Anakin Skywalker and Clone Captain Rex during a mission to investigate Confederacy of Independent Systems activity on the planet Benglor in 22 BBY. During the mission, Bellow discovered parts of a B1-series battle droid while trekking through jungle with Skywalker and several other clones. After searching for more clues, Bellow was attacked by a creature that caught and ate him.

The clone trooper who adopted the name Bellow served in the 501st Legion of the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Like all of the Republic's clone troopers, he was created and trained on the planet Kamino as a clone of the human bounty hunter Jango Fett. During the Clone Wars in 22 BBY, he served under Jedi General Anakin Skywalker and Clone Captain Rex on a mission to the planet Benglor in order to investigate Separatist activity there.

Bellow trekked through the hot jungle of Benglor with Skywalker, Rex, Hardcase, and another clone. As their search for the Separatists was proving unfruitful, Skywalker began considering ending the mission due to the extreme heat. Then, Hardcase discovered a green-colored slime on one of the nearby trees, which he alerted the others to as a potential clue.

Bellow then discovered a B1-series battle droid head in a sand mound, teasing Hardcase that he had found better evidence than him. As the clones discovered more parts of the droid, Skywalker realized the pieces had been purposefully left as a trail for them to find. However, before he could warn the others of the potential trap, Bellow discovered more of the slime and called out to the others.

Belos was a male Human businessman and member of the Corellian Council during both the Cold War and the Galactic War on Corellia.

Belos had a very opportunistic mind and was always looking to cut a better deal. When agents of Imperial Intelligence approached the Council with their offer to join the Empire amid promises of rich rewards, Belos, believing the Empire's superior military might would allow it to overwhelm the Republic, voted to join the winning side. But when the civil uprising against the Sith Empire gained the support of the Jedi and the Galactic Republic, Belos understood that the wind was changing and offered his secret support to the Republic Command, aiding them in eliminating many Imperial strongholds, thereby saving his life from accusations of treason.

Belos reached out to the Republic, providing them intel to help them push the Empire off Corellia, as well as orchestrating the deaths of Darth Acharon, Darth Hadra and Darth Decimus. Belos also joined the heroes of the Republic in a holoconference with Supreme Chancellor Leontyne Saresh and the Galactic Senate. Belos explained the reasons behind Corellian Council's actions and promised that, if he was allowed to stay in office, he would dedicate the rest of his term to redeeming himself. Saresh expressed hesitancy to trust him, as he could betray Corellia to the Empire again. However, a Republic hero spoke in favor of Belos, pointing out that he risked his life to help them. Thus, Saresh agreed to his request.

enrichments.description: Beltek'k was a Gatemaster of the Gree Enclave during the time of the Cold War. During that time, the planet Asation had been attacked by Kephess who served the Dread Masters as they attempted to sow fear in the galaxy. As a result, the mutated Trandoshan took control of the Grand Hypergate and created a rift in hyperspace that brought the emergence of numerous hostile lifeforms. Thus, in desperation, the Gree dispatched Gatemaster Beltek'k who held a duty to defend the Hypergate. This saw him journey to the Galactic Republic to enlist the aid of numerous spacers to undo the damage done to Asation before it became permanent. Following the completion of this task, the Gatemaster along with other Gree dignitaries decided to honor the spacers by awarding them the title of Red Rhombus.

Belth Allusis was a male Human Jedi Master serving the Galactic Republic and the Jedi High Council during the Great Galactic War between the Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. A polite and selfless individual, Master Allusis was a respected member of the Council and was liked by his peers for his sharp wit and sense of humor. In 3671 BBY, Allusis was in charge of the Republic troops and Jedi that defended the planet Bothawui against the overwhelming Sith forces. Although all of the Republic defenders, including Allusis, were killed, they managed to inflict heavy casualties upon the Sith, forcing them to retreat. Master Allusis' bravery was remembered for years to come and inspired Republic forces across the war-torn galaxy.

Belth Allusis was a Human male Jedi Master and a prominent member of the Jedi High Council active during the Great Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the resurgent Sith Empire. Since the beginning of the war in 3681 BBY, the Empire had scored many victories, and eventually established its dominance in the Outer Rim region of the galaxy. In 3671 BBY, the Sith turned their forces toward the Mid Rim and attempted to seize control of the planet Bothawui. However, a Republic fleet lay in wait above the planet, and the Sith attack was repelled. The Republic fleet was then pulled back from Bothawui, and only a small force led by Master Allusis remained behind to defend the planet against a possible Sith counterattack.

The attack soon followed; Imperial battlecruisers from all around the galaxy moved in to capture Bothawui. However, the planet was protected by a high-powered planetary shield, which prevented the Sith from using orbital bombardment and forced them to initiate a ground assault instead. Soon, a fifty-thousand-strong force of Sith landed on the planet and attacked the shield generators, which were protected only by seven dozen of the Jedi Order's Knights and four thousand Republic soldiers, all commanded by Allusis. Despite being greatly outnumbered, the Republic troops put up a valiant fight; for each Republic soldier killed, the Empire paid with ten lives. During the battle, Allusis and his men developed unorthodox tactics, which—combined with the Imperial commanders' decision to send all of their troops directly into the assault—resulted in so many Sith losses that the Empire was forced to call in reinforcements.

Eventually, however, most of the Republic defenders were killed, and only a handful of Jedi and soldiers remained. The survivors gathered near Master Allusis and prepared for a final stand. At that moment, the Imperial Grand Moff Zellos offered to spare Allusis if he and his forces surrendered. Drawing from the Force, Allusis and his soldiers refused the offer and fought to the last man. Although all of the Republic forces perished, the Empire had taken too many casualties and was forced to retreat from Bothawui.

Bemmie was a male Vorzydiak who was a member of the Freelies youth gang on his homeworld of Vorzyd V during the era of the Galactic Civil War. In 1 ABY, Bemmie was a part of a Freelie plot to kidnap Rebel leader Leia Organa for a hefty ransom, but was captured and tortured by Imperial forces who were also after the Princess. Bemmie was saved by Organa's friend Luke Skywalker, and feeling he owed the man his life, Bemmie helped Skywalker and Organa escape Imperial pursuit—an act that resulted in the young Vorzydiak's death.

A male Vorzydiak, Bemmie was a native of the world Vorzyd V, better known by the moniker "the Gambler's World." By 1 ABY, Bemmie had become a member of the Freelies, a delinquent youth gang led by a Human named Jax. One night, Bemmie and his friends happened across a pair of valuable-looking droids wandering alone: the pair, protocol droid C-3PO and astromech droid R2-D2, were attempting to track down their master, Rebel leader Luke Skywalker and his compatriot Princess Leia Organa, after they had been captured by the Empire. Although Bemmie and the gang attempted to claim the droids for themselves, R2-D2 managed to call a police droid, which chased the Freelies off.

However, Bemmie and his friends soon encountered those same droids again, after the Freelies entered a weapons shop intending to pull a caper. The droids were trying on automatic defensive weapons, which soon went haywire and damaged the store, convincing the Freelies that they'd be better served keeping their distance. Instead, they hung back and followed the droids to a starship, where the gang did a lot more than just steal a couple droids. Instead, Bemmie and his friends tricked C-3PO into letting them aboard and kidnapped Leia Organa, along with stealing R2-D2, demanding five million credits in exchange for the Princess' safe return to the Alliance. However, at some point Bemmie became separated from the rest of his gang and was captured by Imperial stormtroopers reporting to an Imperial Intelligence agent called Blackhole, who was pursuing Skywalker and Organa. The stormtroopers brutally tortured Bemmie with a mind probe, pushing him past the limits of his willpower: he was about to tell them everything he knew about Organa's location when suddenly Skywalker arrived and took the Imperial troops prisoner.

Bendu was a male Force wielder who resided on the remote planet of Atollon and claimed to represent the center of the Force, between the light side and the dark side. Bendu encountered Jedi Knight Kanan Jarrus in 2 BBY. He developed a friendly relationship with Kanan and his Padawan Ezra Bridger and helped the two Jedi repair their relationship and deal with their fears and anxieties. Despite his wisdom and powers, Bendu refused to take sides in any conflict, and was angered when Kanan called him a coward for not intervening during the Battle of Atollon, which caused him to unleash a storm against both the rebel and Imperial forces on Atollon. He was wounded by Thrawn's forces and becomes one with the Force but not before predicting Thrawn's defeat.

At some point in his life, Bendu became familiar with the Sith and the process of fusing Jedi and Sith holocrons together, witnessing the results and consequences of such a vergence.

By 2 BBY, Bendu still lived on Atollon where the Phoenix Cell maintained a base. At one point, Bendu called out to the Jedi Knight Kanan Jarrus, who was meditating outside Chopper Base. Kanan had retreated into meditation after losing his sight during a Mission to Malachor. Bendu called out to Kanan and eventually led him into a series of mesas in the wilderness. When Kanan finally arrived, Bendu told the Jedi Knight that his imbalance had awoken him from his slumber. After introducing himself, he allowed Kanan to identify himself as a Jedi Knight. Bendu listened as Kanan told him about his fear that his apprentice Ezra Bridger was falling to the dark side. When Kanan showed him the Sith holocron that Ezra had obtained on Malachor, Bendu explained that an object could not make someone good or evil. However, he stressed that only a person could choose to change themselves. Bendu then took an interest in Kanan's sensor beacon, which the Jedi had used to ward off several krykna, arachnid predators that were indigenous to Atollon.

Bendu then destroyed the sensor marker. When Kanan protested, he told the Jedi that he would never regain his sight but that he could teach Kanan to see through his other senses. When Kanan agreed to take his lesson, Bendu instructed the Jedi to empty his mind, turn around and walk forward. Kanan was quickly surrounded by two krykna which did not attack him. Bendu then explained that Kanan's bad experience with creatures stemmed from not seeing them for what they actually were. Kanan began to make peace with the krykna but was startled when he sensed that Ezra was in danger. After igniting his lightsaber, Kanan realized that the krykna had been feeding off his fear and emotions. When Kanan deduced that he had isolated himself from everyone and the Force, Bendu commented that he had finally regained his Force connection. Before leaving to rescue Ezra, Kanan left the Sith holocron with Bendu. Bendu then inspected the object and laughed.

Bene was a Force-sensitive human female Padawan of the Jedi Order who lived during the final years of the Galactic Republic. In the waning days of the Clone Wars, Bene was killed by the Sith Lord Darth Vader during the execution of Order 66 and the siege of the Jedi Temple.

Bene was a Jedi Padawan during the final days of the Clone Wars, when Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine, who was secretly the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Sidious, declared the Jedi Order traitors to the Galactic Republic. Executing Order 66 on Coruscant, the Sith Lord Darth Vader and the 501st Legion marched on the Jedi Temple to purge its occupants, including Bene. As the clone troopers stormed the Temple, Bene fought alongside Padawan Whie Malreaux and Battlemaster Cin Drallig against Vader. Despite their combined efforts, Bene, Malreaux and Drallig were killed by the new Lord of the Sith with Malreaux being the first to fall. Bene then attacked Vader in concert with Drallig, but Vader batted Bene's blade aside before grabbing her by the throat and strangling her whilst he dueled Drallig one-handed, killing the trainee Jedi before finishing off Drallig.

The duel between Bene and Vader was recorded by the Temple's surveillance system, allowing Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi to discover her fate while reviewing the security logs. Recognizing the Sith who led the attack as his one-time apprentice, Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker, Kenobi deactivated the holographic recording as he was unable to watch it through to its completion. Bene's death along with the other Jedi in the Temple led Kenobi to confront Vader on Mustafar, where the former friends fought until Kenobi emerged as the victor.

Bene was a young human female who, at the time of the Clone Wars, possessed brown hair, brown eyes, and fair skin. She rallied to the Temple's defense, opposing a former Jedi-turned-Sith and his legion of clones. She was among the Jedi who tried to defeat Vader, but ultimately died defending the Temple.
