Brand, born Lauren Mel Coelho on the planet Tangenine, was a human female member of the Alliance to Restore the Republic's 61st Mobile Infantry, commonly known as Twilight Company. Prior to her service in Twilight Company, Lauren worked as a bounty hunter under her new name Brand following the death of her family under the Malandro syndicate. She brought those skills with her to Twilight Company, serving as a sniper and tracker for the company. Brand tended to be aloof and preferred working with a higher degree of operational freedom than her fellow soldiers in Twilight Company.

Lauren Mel Coelho was born on the planet Tangenine between around 40 BBY and 39 BBY, to Remba and Kelven, who nicknamed her Lau. She attended a school on the world. Coelho's family owned a norango farm but were being extorted by the Malandro syndicate. One day her parents called her over to her farmhouse and sent her away with her infant brother, Julien, to her gran. As Coelho fled the farm with Julien on her back, Remba and Kelven were confronted and killed by the Falleen gangster Annaz, as Remba had refused to pay protection fees to the Malandro syndicate. Coelho and Julien live with their gran until she died of a fever a few years later. When Julien fell ill Coelho took a job stealing a speeder for the Malandro syndicate to pay for the cure but was caught in the process and landed in jail. By the time she got out Julien was dead.

A few years later the Galactic Empire took control of Tangenine and soon realized how embedded the Malandro syndicate was and turned to bounty hunters in order to clean up the underworld for them. Coelho then reappeared with a new name, Brand. She took jobs almost primarily on the Malandro syndicate, including Annaz herself. But as order came back to Tangenine, Brand started to witness the more corrupt side of the Empire, a thief was given a life sentence and a gang leader and dealer was pardoned after bribing a magistrate.

Brand later got sick of the corruption on Tangenine and took a job off-world. Her target was Captain Micha Evon of the Rebel Alliance's 61st Mobile Infantry, better known as Twilight Company. She tracked Twilight Company to Veron and offered to join. She then smuggled in her kit and when the company was on backwater planet Allst Prime she got her chance. She and captain Evon stormed into the governor's office and Brand incapacitated Governor Magé. She then pointed her blaster at Evon but hesitated when he revealed what he knew about her past life. He then offered her to stay with the 61st and she accepted.

Brandei was a Human male who served the Imperial Navy of the Galactic Empire during the Galactic Civil War.

Brandei was a Force-Attuned human male born on Mantooine in 45 BBY, during the last decades of the Galactic Republic. As a cadet from an Outer Rim Territories world, he had to struggle to overcome discrimination; even exemplary work gained him only marginal notice from his professors and superiors. Nonetheless, his academy training imbued him with a definite air of purpose and confidence, and he made his mark in the Imperial military in spite of this initial prejudice.

Brandei spent much of his career aboard the Star Destroyer Judicator, assigned to the area of the Core Worlds embracing Garos IV. In 6 BBY, he held the rank of Senior Lieutenant, and it was at his suggestion that his old friend Tork Winger, an administrator on Garos IV, adopted a Rebel orphan, the girl later known as Alex Winger.

By 3 ABY, Brandei had been transferred aboard the Star Dreadnought Executor, where he performed bridge duty as a Technical Services Officer with the Fleet Support Branch, holding the title of commander and the overall responsibility for the up-keep, maintenance, and combat readiness of the ship's twelve TIE squadrons. Shortly after the Battle of Hoth, however, he received notice of a transfer back the Judicator, aboard which he apparently served at the Battle of Endor. By 6 ABY, New Republic Intelligence believed that he had received a further promotion soon after Endor.
enrichments.short_description: Brandei was a Human male who served the Imperial Navy of the Galactic Empire during the Galactic Civil War.

Branno was a Human male Captain of the Galactic Republic living during the Galactic War against the resurgent Sith Empire.

During the Dread War on Oricon in 3638 BBY, Branno was among the Republic fleet send to end the threat of Dread Masters. However, the Sith overwhelmed the men with dread while the fleet was still in orbit and many ships crashed onto the moons service, while some men like Branno jettisoned in escape pods. Upon reaching surface, Branno was unexpectedly rescued by Imperials and was brought to the Dread Executioners camp. There, Sith Lord Hargrev offered Branno and other rescued Republic soldiers a temporary truce to strike against their common enemy: the Dread Masters. Branno was reluctant to the idea, but as neither side alone was strong enough to battle the Dread Host, he had no choice but to aid the Empire.

Branox was a Hrakian spacer who, in 1 ABY, made a stop at Vorzyd V. Branox was getting drunk in a spaceport cantina when he had an encounter with the Rebel droids C-3PO and R2-D2, who were on the hunt for a Hrakian pilot. Their owner Luke Skywalker, along with fellow Rebels Leia Organa, Falud, and Paxin were being held captive by Imperial troops aboard a Hrakian starship, and the droids needed a Hrakian to pose as their owner to help them get aboard. C-3PO and R2-D2 quickly identified the confused and near-unconscious Branox as a perfect candidate, and ushered the confused spacer to the starship and used him to pass security. As soon as they reached their destination, they cast Branox aside, telling him they needed to register with the "droid steward."

Branox made his first and only appearance in the Star Wars Legends continuity in Gambler's World, a comic strip story arc written and illustrated by Russ Manning and released in 1979.

Brasck was a Brubb smuggler and mercenary.

Brasck was a Brubb male native to Baros, born in 25 BBY. His homeworld, located in the Unknown Regions of the galaxy, was discovered by Imperial Grand Admiral Thrawn, who subjugated the world and taught it to fear and respect the Galactic Empire. Brasck never forgot the stories of Thrawn's time on Baros told to him as a child, or the harsh lessons the Grand Admiral taught his people, and forever feared the Empire.

Brasck eventually left Baros when he was recruited as a mercenary by Jabba Desilijic Tiure, a powerful Hutt crime lord operating out of Tatooine and Nar Shaddaa. According to Brasck, he had no choice but to work for Jabba, but he went about his job with zeal and relish, adopting some of Jabba's unscrupulous methods. Brasck acted as one of Jabba's numerous "hatchetmen," a hired gun who assassinated Jabba's personal rivals and taught lessons to any employees or business partners who displayed a lack of loyalty to the Hutt. His was considered a heartless and unsavory character, but also brutally efficient.

Brasck was considered one of the major players operating in the Trans-Hydian between the New Republic and Imperial space. Prior to the Battle of Endor, Brasck worked as a mercenary for Jabba the Hutt. When Jabba died, Brasck grabbed as many followers as he could and set up his own smuggling operation, which included kidnapping and slavery.

Brask was a Trandoshan male active during the reign of the Galactic Empire. Shortly after the destruction of the second Death Star, he operated a requisitions depot on the planet Burnin Konn, located in the Anoat sector. Riley, a human thief, was acquainted with Brask and instructed her sibling to requisition equipment from the Trandoshan. Brask offered to trade his standard stock with the sibling for requisition scrips, but also explained that he had special items available to trade for chromium. Brask then gifted the customer a case of his special stock, as he owed Riley a favor.

Brask first appeared in the 2015 mobile game Star Wars: Uprising.

Brasso was a human male who served as a Grappler and Honor guard on the planet Ferrix within the Free Trade Sector, which he had long been a citizen of. He was a close friend of Cassian Andor, willing to rescue his friend from the pitfalls of his regrettable misadventures and dubious arrangements, caring for his mother and her droid during his extended absences.

Brasso was a human male that resided on the planet Ferrix during the reign of the Galactic Empire. He served as a Grappler, tearing apart obsolete starships in the local salvage yard. In 5 BBY, his close friend Cassian Andor had been gone from Ferrix for some time, having left on a borrowed starship. His mother Maarva believed him to be out ruining his health and reputation with friends of low character, leading to Brasso to go looking for him.

Later that morning, Andor had returned from an encounter with Pre-Mor officers on Morlana One, which had resulted in a double murder, though Brasso was not aware of it. Meeting Brasso outside his workplace, a visibly-injured Andor asked Brasso to lie about where he was the night before. Creating a cover story, Andor said that they had wanted to go out drinking, but after Andor declined Brasso's suggestion to go to Cavo's, they drank nog at Brasso's home before falling asleep. Rather than question it, Brasso instead went on to embellish it further, creating a story of how they had hurt themselves when drunk at his home, a cover for Andor's injuries. He left for work soon after.

When a squad of Pre-Mor Enforcement officers arrived to arrest Andor for the two murders he had committed, Brasso wasted no time. With their Mobile Tac-Pod left unguarded, Brasso sabotaged the transport, securing it to a large piece of debris with a metal cable. When the officers engaged with Andor and Luthen Rael, who Andor had contacted to sell a stolen Imperial N-S9 Starpath Unit, one Corpo, designation North-3, attempted to get the transport airborne, Brasso's sabotage caused the subsequent crash of the ship and the death of the officer, when the attached debris got caught in a nearby structure. With blood on his hands and Andor having fled with Rael, Brasso returned to the local bar, downing a glass of alcohol.

Braum Bourne, also known as "Zakkeg", was a male Mandalorian living during the Cold War. Having been sent their way by Rally Master Merrk Kelborn on Vaiken Spacedock, he and Gen Vizla helped give tips to the future Grand Champion of the Great Hunt, becoming very impressed with the young bounty hunter.

Before the mission's removal from the game, Braum "Zakkeg" Bourne appeared in the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic as part of the Advanced Training mission for the Bounty Hunter class, wherein players were sent to him and Gen Vizla by Rally Master Merrk Kelborn in order to receive advice on whether to learn the skills of either a Powertech or a Mercenary. While Vizla preferred the Mercenary specialization, Bourne advocated for the Powertech specialization. He could be found both on Vaiken Spacedock and in the Mandalorian enclave on Dromund Kaas.

Bravo was a human male that served as the pilot of the Stinger Mantis crew during the Imperial Era. He also served as a soldier and fought alongside Saw Gerrera.

During their time together, Bravo and Jedi Knight Cal Kestis ran many successful missions together in their struggle against the Galactic Empire.

Bravo assisted Kestis and the Stinger Mantis crew to infiltrate Level 2046 on Coruscant to steal classified Imperial information aboard the yacht of Senator Daho Sejan. After capturing the Pau'an senator, the team tried to escape Coruscant, but were intercepted by the Ninth Sister of the Inquisitorius, who executed the senator for harboring Kestis. The crew's slicer Gabs, along with the Klatooinian twins Koob and Lizz, were killed during the ensuing chaos.

After Kestis bested the Ninth Sister, he reunited with Bode Akuna and Bravo. Together, they planned to escape Coruscant using Z-95 Headhunters and the Mantis, split up, and later rendezvous using locator beacons. Bravo, however, was shot down by TIE Fighters during the escape, and the Mantis received damage to its gyro systems.

While on a scouting mission for Major Anri, Brax spotted an Imperial supply drop in the area, but was pinned down by hostile Mutated Geonosians before he could reach it.

Brax first appears in the Jedi Under Siege expansion of Star Wars: The Old Republic.

In the Imperial storyline, Brax retreated to a nearby cave, where he was located and rescued by Major Anri and the Alliance Commander. After Brax expressed his excitement over meeting the famous Commander, Major Anri ordered him to return to base and tend to his wounds.

In the Onslaught expansion, if the player is a Republic Saboteur, Anri will call out Brax's name if the Commander kills Vice Admiral Dol Narlock on Mek-Sha, asking if he is still alive. This leaves his ultimate fate unknown.

enrichments.description:
Bray was a human male flametrooper who held the rank of captain in the First Order Stormtrooper Corps. During the Cold War, after a group of creatures attacked personnel in one of the tunnels on Starkiller Base, Bray served as the commanding officer of a cleaning crew deployed to remove the "infestation." Prior to the operation, one of the crew's stormtroopers, FN-2187, asked what they what be facing, but Bray had no information for the soldier.

Once they were inside the tunnel, the crew was attacked by the creatures, and Bray was overwhelmed. To save his captain, FN-2187 used Bray's flamethrower to kill the animals attacking him, although the trooper burned him in the process. When it seemed like their mission was complete, Bray ordered FN-2187 to clean up the creature's remains and, thinking that the trooper thought himself above the task, threatened to reassign the trooper to be a trash guard if he complained. However, FN-2187 ultimately discovered that the creatures were actually a native species, so the stormtrooper went to Bray and suggested moving the animals. As the Captain believed the animals were worthless and thought FN-2187 was complaining, Bray punished the trooper by ordering him to guard trash heading to the Garbage Moon of Maher. However, FN-2187 had planned to anger Bray, as he could now release some of the creatures to safety on the moon.

During the Cold War, Bray served as a captain and flametrooper in the armed forces of the First Order, aboard its Starkiller Base which was built into the Unknown Regions world of Ilum. After one of Starkiller's construction units encountered a so-called "infestation" of creatures while working on a flood chamber, Bray and a cleaning crew of stormtroopers were deployed to remedy the situation. The animals had eaten two First Order personnel, leaving only one survivor, but Bray's men were unable to get any information from him. To help Bray's operation, Captain Phasma assigned troopers FN-2187 and FN-3761 to his crew.

Upon arriving at Deck Nine, FN-2187 was confused as to why a cleaning crew was made up of troopers, but Bray, while testing his flamethrower, informed him that they were dealing with an infestation capable of eating people. As Bray had no other information for the stormtrooper, he allowed FN-2187 to speak with the only survivor of the creature's attack. By the time Bray called for the crew to go, the survivor had not said anything useful, but he then warned FN-2187 that the "infestation" had teeth.

Bre'ano Umakk was a male Mon Calamari Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order before the rise of the Galactic Empire.

A Force-sensitive Mon Calamari, Bre'ano Umakk was discovered by the Jedi at a very young age and was taken to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant where he was to learn the ways of the Force. Later, the Clone Wars broke out after the First Battle of Geonosis happened in 22 BBY after Obi-Wan Kenobi had overheard a secret meeting of various heads of major corporations, some of which represented their worlds in the Galactic Senate of the Republic, and formed the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Umakk fought side by side with clones of the Grand Army of the Republic.

In 19 BBY, the last year of the war, it became clear that the Supreme Chancellor and leader of the Republic, Palpatine, was known to be the Sith Lord Darth Sidious and had influenced the war in his favor in recent years to annihilate the Jedi. Even during the fierce battles that took hold in the Outer Rim, Palpatine and Anakin Skywalker, who had fallen to the dark side and become Darth Vader, managed to turn against the Jedi by issuing Order 66 and pull the Galactic Senate to his side in forming the Galactic Empire. Umakk survived the purge and settled on Dantooine where he trained other Jedi, who had survived the purge, in defensive combat throughout the years. He taught others the ways of the Jedi in hopes of destroying those who followed the ways of the dark side.

His helmet was similar to clone trooper helmets except that its front was foldable and the visor was more closely related to Mandalorian helmets. He was also equipped with a jetpack, a Shoulder-mounted blaster on his right shoulder and a Wrist blaster on his left gauntlet.

Breela was a female Farghul bounty hunter, and leader of Crimson Nova, a chapter of the Bounty Hunters' Guild. She was the daughter of Mika, a bounty hunter who worked during the Clone Wars and hated Jedi. She was tattooed on her face and abdomen; the lines around her navel were similar to those of a Zealot of Psusan. Years later, a grown up Breela, who along with her fellow hunters Boushh and Zuckuss, were tracking down Jedi Master Kai Justiss, a survivor who escaped Order 66 years ago and had recently sought refuge on the planet Garqi, but was betrayed by local farmers to Breela and the others. After a skirmish, during which Master Justiss was able to defeat at least two other combatants and severed the arm of one of them, Breela, Boushh and Zuckuss surrounded him and held him at blaster point.

Breela was a female Farghul from the planet Farrfin who rose to prominence as the leader of Crimson Nova, a faction operating within the Bounty Hunters' Guild during the time of the Galactic Civil War between the Galactic Empire and the Rebel Alliance. During that conflict, Mika increasingly devoted the group's efforts to hunting down Jedi, a focus that ultimately led to her capture by a Jedi Order task force led by Jedi Master Mace Windu. Following her arrest, Crimson Nova was dismantled, and its members dispersed. With the end of the Clone Wars and the rise of the Galactic Empire in 19 BBY, Mika's imprisonment came to an end, allowing her to reunite with her daughter and re-establish contact with the bounty hunting underworld.

After her release, Mika managed to restore the Crimson Nova and continued to prioritize the pursuit of surviving Jedi who had managed to evade both Order 66 and the Jedi Purge throughout the Imperial Era. During this period, Breela would adopt her mother's hostility toward the Jedi and was gradually introduced into leadership roles within the organization. Once she was considered old enough, Breela succeeded her mother as leader of Crimson Nova and directed its bounty hunters in a campaign targeting Jedi fugitives. Among the hunters with whom she collaborated were Boushh and Zuckuss. Together, they pursued the Jedi Kai Justiss after local farmers on Garqi revealed his location. The encounter escalated into a confrontation between Justiss and the bounty hunters, resulting in several members of Breela’s group being seriously wounded.

Breela was a disciplined and determined individual whose outlook had been strongly shaped by her upbringing within the bounty hunting underworld. Raised under the influence of her mother, Mika, she inherited a deep-seated hostility toward the Jedi, whom she viewed as responsible for both her family’s misfortunes and the dismantling of Crimson Nova during the Clone Wars. This resentment hardened over time into a defining motivation, guiding her decisions and priorities as she rose through the ranks of the organization. Breela was pragmatic in her approach, valuing results over ideology and focusing on the successful completion of contracts rather than personal glory.

Brehg was a male Neimoidian smuggler who lived at the time of the Cold War.

In 3643 BBY, Brehg was arrested by the Sith Empire for supplying forged documents to the Galactic Republic. He was taken to Korriban where he was held with several prisoners under the control of Jailer Knash. When the unidentified Sith acolyte arrived to meet Knash, Brehg was last one to face the trained acolyte. In spite of all the torture he underwent, Brehg still insisted that he was innocent. He admitted that he did once serve time in a Republic prison for forgery, but insisted that since his release, he had been honest ever since. Brehg begged the acolyte and Knash to let him go, but the warrior believed that he was lying and that he should be tortured even more until a confession came out, which Overseer Tremel commended.

The player can choose to torture him (Dark Side), leave him in his cell (Dark Side) or free him (Light Side).

Brejik was the leader of the Black Vulkars, a swoop gang of the Lower City on Taris that, under his direction, led a gang war against their rivals the Hidden Beks in the time of the Jedi Civil War. Formerly the lieutenant to Gadon Thek, head of the Hidden Beks, Brejik defected to the Black Vulkars when his mentor refused to retire and allow him to succeed. The war he prosecuted as head of the Black Vulkars wrecked chaos throughout the Lower City. When he captured and enslaved the Jedi Knight Bastila Shan, he provoked the intervention of two agents of the Republic, Revan and Carth Onasi, ultimately leading to his downfall.

In the days leading up to the Mandalorian attack on Taris, Brejik kidnapped the children of Sector Constable Noana Sowrs, planning to hold them for ransom and gain a profit as Gadon had taught him. Before he could make any demands, however, riots broke out on the planet. Rather than letting the children go, Brejik chose to hold them until the opportunity to contact the constable presented itself. He enlisted to the help of fellow gang member Griff Vao to help him take care of the children and keep his secret. When the Mandalorians invaded, Brejik fought with the rest of the Beks in resisting them.

Soon, Griff's sister Mission discovered her brother's covert activities, and shortly after the arrival of Zayne Carrick, she followed him with Zayne and his companion Marn Hierogryph. Not wanting his secret discovered, Brejik attacked Zayne with a vibrosword, but was stopped by Del Moomo before he could kill the former Padawan.

Though Gadon was furious that Brejik had not only kidnapped the children, but kept them secret, he recognized that they were a good opportunity to convince the Taris Resistance to ally with their gang. Brejik accompanied the rest of the Beks to the Resistance headquarters where the temporary alliance was forged. Brejik was later part of the mission to destroy the Jedi Tower, where he helped rig explosives in its foundation to bring the building down in hopes of killing Mandalorian military leader Cassus Fett. The mission was a failure, however, as Fett had already vacated the building and the Mandalorians had discovered and attacked the Resistance headquarters. Always eager to use his blaster, Brejik led Del Moomo back to the compound to fight the Mandalorians and return to the Beks' fallout point, the Pit.

Brene was one of several Ubese exiles who were part of a bounty hunter crew led by Boushh. After Boushh rescued her from a rancor, she was the first member to join him.

Brene was a Ubese female bounty hunter who was a member of the crew led by fellow Ubese Boushh. By the time of the War of the Bounty Hunters, she had been exiled from Uba IV for seven years and a member of Boushh's crew for six. Boushh and Brene met when he rescued her from a rancor and told her to run; she then became the first to join him. Fellow exiles Ilini, Hareck, and Tans also joined the group.

Boushh's crew, including Brene, were hired by Silas Tagge, the brother of Lady Domina Tagge, to kill the Tagge Corporation's Executive Board in an attempted coup. Domina and her Honor Guard successfully thwarted her brother and she hired the crew for herself. Brene and the others protected their employer from another assassination attempt by Crimson Dawn and her nephew, Ronen Tagge; Lady Domina also defended herself with the Tagge protoblade. Tans remarked that their employer was terrifying and Brene enthusiastically agreed, leading Ilini to comment that the latter had bad taste.

Brene had a fondness for puns and telling jokes in the middle of a firefight. She also enjoyed sharing the story of how she met Boushh when he rescued her from a rancor.

Brenna was a human female colonel in command of a brigade in the military of the Galactic Empire. She believed that her brigade was superior to those stationed on the Death Star.

Throughout the Galactic Civil War, Brenna and her troops engaged in multiple skirmishes with the Rebel Alliance, frequently against Alliance Major Shin and his forces.

Shortly after the Battle of Yavin, as the Rebels were evacuating their base on Yavin 4, Brenna and her troops landed and attacked the base, intending to capture data drives belonging to the Rebellion.

On Tatooine, the Imperials became privy to an elite Rebel cell operating out of Mos Eisley. Brenna led her troops in an assault on the city, attempting to prevent an evacuating Rebel U-wing from taking off. Unlike the opposing commander, Brenna did not care about civilian causalities, letting her troops know that they were "acceptable".

Brezark was a Force-sensitive Quarren male who served as a mercenary and master trapper during the High Republic Era.

At some point, he wiped out the royal family of Burundang. Eventually, Brezark was recruited into the Nihil marauder organization by Marchion Ro—the Eye of the Nihil—and was spared from the experiments of the Nihil scientist Baron Boolan by Ro.

In 228 BBY, Brezark and a group of Nihil were aboard a Nihil satellite with a kidnapped Twi'lek family in order to lure a Jedi onto the station to be killed by the Great Leveler, a Force-consuming Nameless creature. When one arrived, the Quarren learned the Jedi was in fact Grand Master Yoda, and attempted to kill Yoda with toxic Slythiant solvent, but failed. Despite, the Grand Master's desire to save Brezark, the Quarren was killed by the effects of the Great Leveler, being turned into dust.

Brezark was an experienced mercenary specialized in traps and capable of using firearms. He was also Force-sensitive and was capable of using Telekinesis.

Brianna was a Human Jedi apprentice who served as a crew member of the freighter Blind Luck during the Galactic Civil War.

By the time of the Galactic Civil War, Brianna was traveling aboard the Blind Luck, a small freighter. Despite her youth and position as a Jedi-in-training, Brianna served as a unifying presence aboard the ship.

When the Blind Luck exited hyperspace into the Elrood Sector, Brianna was among the first to recognize the transition.

Brianna exhibited the classic characteristics of a Jedi learner—disciplined, observant, and courageous—but was distinguished by her warmth and enthusiasm. Her interpersonal skills often diffused tension aboard the freighter, and even the stern Desric Fol and volatile Klag responded positively to her and she was viewed as the glue that held the crew together.

Bric was a male Siniteen bounty hunter who, along with his partner, the Arcona bounty hunter El-Les, was contracted by the Galactic Republic to train clone cadets of the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars after the death of Jango Fett. He held the rank of Master Chief.

Bric was a Siniteen bounty hunter hired by the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars to train various clone cadets As a drill sergeant under the rank of Master Chief, Bric worked to oversee clone trooper training in Tipoca City with fellow bounty hunter El-Les.

When dealing with a particular clone cadet squad called Domino Squad, Bric was very impatient with their struggles. He began to give up hope and told El-Les that they would never become competent soldiers. When Domino Squad attempted to conquer the Citadel Challenge, Bric was highly critical of their inability to function as a unit and later had to break up a fight between troopers CT-782 and CT-1409 in the barracks.

The next day Bric and El-Les rallied Domino Squad and other cadet units on a hangar deck to take a lesson from the ARC troopers of Rancor Battalion. Commander Colt addressed the troopers and watched the next attempt at the Citadel Challenge. Bric praised the first group, Bravo Squad, and told Colt that Domino Squad was inept. They watched as the group failed the test again, much to Bric's amusement. That night, he chewed out clone trooper CT-4040, saying that he was "a real cutup" and blamed him for his squad's struggles. Much to his dismay, CT-4040 took the nickname "Cutup" and drew inspiration from the criticism.

Brick was the leader of a scavenger party in the aftermath of the Second Battle of Coruscant during the Imperial Civil War.

Brick had a good deal of scavenging experience, and was fond of the scavenger lifestyle. He was known to try to convince others of its appeal. He amassed an arsenal of battle droids and other assorted tools and tricks to assist in his occupation.

When the Millennium Falcon landed on Coruscant to rescue the crew of the Liberator, Brick's team, including fellow scavenger Slag, descended on the Falcon to strip it of valuable parts. When Han Solo tried to dissuade them, Brick activated a remote to release a pack of neks from his ship. The neks were stopped by Luke Skywalker's use of the Force.

Brick and Slag were created for the Dark Empire audio drama, and based on their dialogue it can be definitively stated that they are among the scavengers atop the Millennium Falcon in the first issue of the Dark Empire comic series.

Brint was a Human male colonel who served in the Galactic Republic's military on the planet Corellia during the Galactic War against the Sith Empire.

Brint fought for the Republic during the Battle of Corellia. However, he had disagreements with Senator Jol Zackin over how to commit to the war effort. When Jedi reinforcements arrived, under the command of the Hero of Tython, Brint advocated striking at the Imperial extermination teams that have been massacring medical camps and the murderers were rewarded as a result. Zackin disagreed and advised saving Corellian citizens the Empire had enslaved. Brint reminded the senator that the citizens were taken from prison, so he designated them as criminals. Zackin insisted those people were innocent until proven guilty in court. Brint then tried offering the latest equipment from Balmorra to supply the Jedi, which an outraged Zackin viewed as bribery. To Brint's dismay, the Hero chose to follow Zackin's suggestion. Nonetheless, Brint referred the Jedi to their science adviser, revealed to be Nasan Godera.

But as the Hero went to stop fallen Jedi Master, Tol Braga, from committing mass murder, Godera was killed by an Imperial ambush. Brint presented General Var Suthra with data concerning Braga's location, which Godera managed to compile before his death. As soon as the general exited the room, Brint passed on Zackin's regards for saving Corellian "citizens". But he shrewdly reminded the Hero that by adhering to the Senator's request, the murderous Imperials the Jedi refused to strike at were laughing all the way back to Dromund Kaas. The Hero sternly stated that the Jedi had come to save lives, not take them and fulfill Brint's petty revenge. Grumbling that he'll never understand Jedi, Brint then gave the coordinates to the Republic base in the government district.

Brolis was a Clone Commander who served in the Grand Army of the Republic after the start of the Clone Wars, and was one of the few survivors in the disastrous Battle of Axion.

Created on the planet Kamino, Brolis was a Clone Commander who served the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars. During his service, Brolis participated in a battle against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. During the battle, Commander Brolis managed to lead his forces into penetrating the Fortress of Axion, but they were eventually overwhelmed by Separatist forces. Brolis and his last two squads fled into the city where they took refuge in one of the ruined buildings. Brolis requested reinforcements, but as the group waited they were eventually whittled down by battle droid forces until only Brolis remained. Commander Brolis continued to hold out in the building, knowing the droids wanted him alive so they could learn how they were able to infiltrate the Fortress of Axion. Tired, Brolis took an uneasy nap which he awoke from when his proximity alarm buzzed, alerting him of the approaching battle droids.

Commander Brolis took aim at the first battle droid he spotted but was startled after being told to put the weapon away by an unknown voice. Turning around, Brolis took sight of a diminutive, green creature who told Brolis that he was the requested reinforcements. As the short individual ignited his lightsaber, Commander Brolis realized that he was Jedi Master Yoda. Brolis watched as Yoda defeated the droids by deflecting their blaster bolts without ever moving from his spot. Shortly after, a hailfire droid arrived and shot a missile directly at Yoda. Master Yoda leaped out of the way of the missile, causing it to explode harmlessly behind him, to which the droid shot three more missiles at him. After Yoda avoided the salvo of missiles, Brolis heard calibration clicks coming from the hailfire droid. Brolis relayed to Yoda that it was a tracking lock just before the droid shot another missile. Spinning in the air, Yoda was able to confuse the missile's tracking, causing it to miss. Brolis continued to watch as the droid charged forward and sent a barrage of missiles that were evaded by Master Yoda.

Brolis appeared in "Duel," a short story written by Timothy Zahn for the Star Wars: Short Story Collection, released in August 2003. The New Essential Chronology establishes that Brolis is an outside military advisor hired by the Kaminoans to train the clones into fighting shape. Both The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia released on December 9, 2008, and The Essential Reader's Companion released on October 2, 2012 contradict this by establishing that Brolis is a Clone Commander. Since these two most recent sources identify Brolis as a clone commander, this article assumes that to be Brolis' relation to the Galactic Republic. This assumption aligns with the short story's title image, which depicts Yoda with a clone trooper.

Broon was a human male scrumrat of the White Worms gang on the Core Worlds planet Corellia. Around 13 BBY, they and the fellow human scrumrat Fixit helped prepare for a raid on a Corellia shipyard by monitoring the facility in shifts, often taking turns with the Rodian scrumrat Oggro.

In one instance, when Imperial stormtroopers exited a hangar and began scanning the area around the shipyard, Broon and their companion fled back to the den of the White Worms to tell someone, not waiting for Oggro to replace them at their posting. The pair told the older scrumrat Qi'ra of the situation, with Broon indicating they had not yet told the Rodian what they had learned. After promising to pass on the information, she dismissed the boys for dinner.

The human male Broon lived on planet Corellia during the Imperial Era. They eventually joined the White Worms criminal gang as a scrumrat thief and lived within their Coronet City den under Head scrumrat Ema's management, alongside several other orphans. the White Worms prepared to raid a Corellia shipyard to steal control boards under the orders of their leader, Lady Proxima, who hoped the endeavor would result in the deaths of several of her older scrumrats so she could thin her ranks.

As one of the group's younger scrumrats, Broon paired off with the fellow human scrumrat Fixit to monitor the shipyard as a scout. The boys took shifts at a watching post during the day, while the Rodian scrumrat Oggro would come to relieve the boys and take the night shift. One time, while waiting for the Rodian to take their place, they and their partner were surprised to see a large group of Imperial stormtroopers scanning the nearby area as they marched out of the facility's hangar. Broon and Fixit fled their post and returned to the White Worms' den to inform someone of the information, not waiting for Oggro to replace them.

Broonmark was a male Talz who served the Galactic Republic, and later the Sith Empire during the Cold War.

Born into a peaceful clan of Talz on the frozen world Alzoc III, Broonmark had an unquenchable taste for murder and death. While still young, Broonmark's father was killed by a wild beast; Broonmark would resent his father henceforth for failing to kill the beast. Developing a fascination with death, a clan elder denounced him for his violent ways and Broonmark in turn executed the elder. To escape his clan and seek out paths to destruction, Broonmark enlisted in the Galactic Republic military where he was trained and dispatched to the planet Hoth during the Galactic War. A violent leader of the Talz Commandos, Broonmark led campaigns of mass slaughter against the Sith Empire.

His violent ways earned him the disdain of many of his peers and Lieutenant Fetzellen led a mutiny against his leadership. Fleeing his attacks, Broonmark regrouped in a cave to plot the death of his squad mates. In that very cave the Jedi Padawan Sewlor took refuge from the cold as he searched for his Jedi Master Xerender. Knowing that Broonmark was hiding in the cave, Sewlor grew anxious and was unable to fight back when the Talz emerged and snapped his neck. After killing the Padawan, Broonmark confronted and dueled the apprentice of Darth Baras, the future Emperor's Wrath, ending the fight in a draw. Leaving the cave, Broonmark later confronted and executed more traitors from his squad, running into the Wrath while doing so. Eventually, the Wrath found the path to Xerender, but it was guarded by none other than Fetzellen himself. Broonmark arrived shortly afterwards and demanded to be allowed to complete his revenge by killing his old second-in-command, promising to pledge his life to the Wrath in return; the Wrath assented, and after confronting Fetzellen over his betrayal, Broonmark dueled with and finally bludgeoned his mutinous lieutenant to death. From then on, the Wrath permitted Broonmark to accompany him as his personal assassin in his never ending quest for death.

While journeying with the Wrath, Broonmark explained about his past life and how he despised the other Talz. The savage alien expressed satisfaction as he and the Wrath massacred their enemies in their wake, and eventually pledged his full loyalty, promising to train the Wrath's followers in the art of killing.
enrichments.short_description: Broonmark was a male Talz who served the Galactic Republic, and later the Sith Empire during the Cold War.

Brooser was a large, simian looking Human male born on the planet Celanon. At a height of 2.2 meters and weighing over 150 kilograms, his bulk consisted of all muscle except for a Jargridian Brandy belly around his middle. Brooser was easily provoked and had a passion for fighting and gambling. Nonetheless, he loved his girlfriend, Jezzable, above all else. However, Jezzable's flirtatious attitude toward other males aggravated Brooser's jealousy and penchant for physical violence.

Born on the planet Celanon drove him to the zenith of jealousy.

One afternoon, Brooser was present at Gularg's Libation Emporium, a local drinking establishment, when he noticed that Jezzable was assiduously flirting with a newly arrived smuggler. Having decided that he didn't like the look of the smuggler, Brooser provoked a brawl, in which the other patrons soon joined. The fracas continued until blaster weapons were drawn. At that point, Gularg, the Hutt owner of the locale—and an individual who did not condone the use of firearms in his bar—disarmed the opponents and ended the altercation.

Brooser was a strong, tough working-class man who took pleasure in fighting. Brooser was easily agitated and provoked into displays of violence, especially by Jezzable's provocative actions toward males of all species. Some individuals found Brooser's physical appearance to be anomalous in regard to a standard Human. Standing at a height of 2.2 meters and weighing over 150 kilograms, Brooser was a large man—considerably simian in appearance—whose mass consisted of all muscle, except for a protruding belly gained from the consumption of Jargridian Brandy. At one point, a freighter captain named Jorgan Blech compared Brooser to a Wookiee. What was left of the hapless captain after Brooser was finished with him was then pummeled by a Wookiee for insulting his people.

Broysc was a Human male who served as Moff during the Great Galactic War, Cold War and Galactic Wars between the Galactic Republic and resurgent Sith Empire.

Moff Broysc was Lieutenant Malavai Quinn's commanding officer at the Battle of Druckenwell during the Great Galactic War. Quinn, disobeying Broysc's orders, was able to correct his glaring oversight and achieve an Imperial victory, but Broysc court-martialed Quinn for insubordination and took credit for the victory himself. As a punishment, Broysc got Quinn assigned to Balmorra, where the lieutenant was absorbed into Darth Baras' field of operations.

Descending further into madness over the years, Broysc almost doomed the command of Major Ovech and later began sending regular transmissions to the ship where now-Captain Quinn served - the Fury-class Imperial interceptor belonging to the Sith Lord who would become the Emperor's Wrath. Eventually being put through, Broysc began to rant on the holotransmitter against Quinn. Referring to him as "Admiral Malcontent", believing it to be Quinn's actual rank and name, Broysc began blaming him for events that occurred well before Quinn, or even Broysc himself, were born, such as the Battle of Talay, Broysc's first command, and the Destruction of Taris, which had occurred three centuries earlier. He also accused Quinn of sabotaging the Glory Space Station, which Quinn had no clue what it was.

With his lord's permission, Quinn began to find ways to bring Broysc's incompetence and madness to the attention of the Imperial High Command, but to no avail; Broysc's political and military connections would not allow him to be removed through the proper channels. Thus, taking matters into his own hands, Quinn abducted Broysc from a pleasure barge where he had been holed up while battle was ongoing, and brought him to the Wrath's ship. Clearly mad, Broysc ordered the Wrath to surrender the vessel and its crew to his command and even kill themselves to everyone present. His patience stretched to breaking point, Quinn requested the Wrath's permission to execute the Moff, and the Sith granted it.

Brrang was a member of the Ranc Gang. He served under Wenda and Bett until the former stormtrooper Terex took over the group in 7 ABY. Brrang commanded the Carrion Spike and the Ranc Gang's fleet of "Uglies" during the Battle over a desert planet.

Brrang was a member of the Ranc Gang during the New Republic Era, which was led by Wenda and Bett, who ran a large ship and salvage operation based on the Outer Rim world of Kaddak. In 7 ABY, he and his fellow Ranc Gang associates including Wenda, Bett, Zumgi, and Wisper entered the Rothana Imperial Shipyards with the help of the former stormtrooper Terex.

After Terex joined the First Order, Wisper took over leadership of the gang. In 34 ABY, Terex returned to Kaddak to retake control of the Ranc Gang and use them to destroy the Resistance, an independent paramilitary faction aligned the New Republic. After Zumgi killed Wisper for contesting Terex's leadership, Brrang joined the rest of the gang in reaffirming their loyalty to Terex. Brrang and Zumgi accompanied Terex aboard his flagship Carrion Spike as they embarked on their hunt for the Resistance starfighter pilot Poe Dameron, who had escaped with the BX-series droid commando N1-ZX. While N1-ZX was purportedly carrying information about the First Order, this was a ruse created by Terex in order to track down and destroy the Resistance.

During the pursuit, Brrang informed Terex that Poe's T-70 X-wing starfighter was still generating a strong signal despite entering hyperspace. Terex thanked Brrang and instructed Zumgi to prepare the fleet and inform him when Poe had re-entered realspace. However, Poe figured out Terex's plan and exited hyperspace above a desert planet. Brrang then informed Terex that they were in the middle of nowhere and were receiving no readings from a base. Brrang realized that Poe had figured their plan and had deliberately led them away from the Resistance base. Terex then decided to kill Poe instead.

Sergeant Bruckman was a Corellian male who was picked by General Han Solo to act as point man for an Alliance to Restore the Republic strike team of commandos that was deployed to the moon of Endor in 4 ABY. The team's aim was to destroy a shield generator on the moon that was protecting the Imperial Death Star II superweapon above.

Bruckman was among the team members that entered the security bunker at the rear of the generator where they began placing charges; however, they were captured by Imperial forces that had laid a trap for them. An army of local Ewoks then attacked the Imperials, allowing Bruckman and the others to also turn on their captors. Ultimately the Alliance destroyed the generator and the Death Star.

Bruckman was a human male from the planet Corellia. During the Galactic Civil War between the Alliance to Restore the Republic and the Galactic Empire, he served as a sergeant in the Alliance Military. In 4 ABY, General Han Solo, a fellow Corellian, chose Bruckman to act as point man for a strike team of commandos he was leading during the Battle of Endor, in which the Alliance aimed to destroy the Empire's Death Star II superweapon in the Endor system. The team's role would be to disable the Death Star's shield generator, which was located on the moon of Endor.

After the team deployed to Endor in the stolen Imperial shuttle Tydirium, they landed in a clearing some distance from the generator and worked their way slowly through the dense undergrowth to the relative safety of the surrounding forest. Solo and some other leading members of the team became separated from the others, and the general ordered Major Bren Derlin to lead Bruckman and the others to regroup with them at the generator at 03:00 hours the next morning. By the time they regrouped, Solo and the others had formed an alliance with a local tribe of Ewoks. Together, the Alliance forces and the Ewoks proceeded to a security bunker that acted as the generator's rear entrance, and after the Ewok Paploo drew away most of the guards, Bruckman and several other members of the team accompanied Solo inside.

Brunson was a human female who served as a captain in the Galactic Empire's Imperial Navy. She commanded an Arquitens-class command cruiser dispatched to Geonosis, the former site of the Death Star's construction, in 2 BBY, in response to a triggered proximity sensor. There, she discovered the rebel starship known as the Ghost on the planet. Hoping to earn herself and her crew promotions, she attempted to destroy the rebels using TIE bombers, rocket troopers, and finally by trapping the rebels in an underground cavern in an attempt to bury them alive. When she used her cruiser to block their escape, the Ghost fired two proton torpedoes, resulting in the destruction of her ship.

Brunson was a young captain in the Imperial Navy who commanded an Arquitens-class command cruiser. she responded to a proximity alert on the planet Geonosis which had been triggered by a visit by the rebel cell Spectres, who were on a mission to find Saw Gerrera and investigate the disappearance of the Geonosian species. After one of her crew informed her that they had picked up live-readings on Geonosis, Captain Brunson deployed two TIE bombers to scout for intruders.

The TIE bombers soon discovered the rebel ship Ghost and strafed it. After the bomber crew transmitted a holographic image of the Ghost, Brunson recognized the ship as belonging to the Phoenix Cell, which was part of the rebellion. The Ghost managed to destroy the bombers. In response, Captain Brunson ordered her crew to pinpoint the rebel ship's last known location. She believed that they had fled into the depths of Geonosis. Brunson was proven right when they discovered that the Ghost had descended into a deep air shaft to rendezvous with their comrades, Saw, and the Geonosian Klik-Klak.

Brunson's light cruiser managed to trap the Ghost inside the air shaft. She then dispatched a squad of rocket troopers to board the rebel ship. However, the rebels managed to repel the boarders and destroy the entire squad. In response, Brunson ordered her crew to open fire on the rebel ship and to collapse the air shaft on top of them. Despite her efforts, the Spectres outwitted Brunson by using their laser cannons and proton torpedoes to blast through the Imperial light cruiser, setting it ablaze before fleeing into space. Captain Brunson survived the explosion but her light cruiser was destroyed.

Brutus was a Shistavanen male pirate captain active during the New Republic Era. He was originally the First Mate of the crew led by Captain Silvo, although the pirates fell on hard times under Silvo's leadership. Around 9 ABY, Brutus led a mutiny against the captain following a raid on a merchant freighter that had been carrying a single credit. The Shistavanen took command of the crew, and subsequently travelled to the pirate—controlled asteroid starport Port Borgo. At the starport, Brutus and his pirates captured a group of lost children from the mythical planet At Attin. However, the children escaped aboard the starship Onyx Cinder with the assistance of Silvo, who went by the name Jod Na Nawood, and Brutus had a bounty placed on the former captain.

After Na Nawood was captured, Brutus oversaw his trial and sentenced him to death by airlock. However, the former captain delayed his fate by revealing that he could grant the pirates the treasure of At Attin. Although Brutus was skeptical, the pirates embarked to the legendary planet, finding it concealed by the treacherous Barrier. When Na Nawood's claims were seemingly proven false, Brutus intended to execute the former captain once more, but was interrupted by the arrival of the Onyx Cinder, crewed by the children from At Attin. After learning the Onyx Cinder was the key to safe passage through the Barrier, Brutus and the pirates captured the ancient vessel. As Brutus boarded the Onyx Cinder, however, the children used the vessel's cargo lift to seize him. With Brutus trapped in the lift's claw, Na Nawood shot and killed the Shistavanen with his own blaster, taking command of the crew once again.

The Shistavanen male pirate Brutus served as First Mate of the crew led by Captain Silvo during the New Republic Era. The crew operated aboard a pirate frigate, seeking valuable cargo and treasure throughout the galaxy. Around 9 ABY, the pirates fell upon several lean cycles, and subsequently some of the crew lost hope in Silvo. During that time, the crew captured and breached a merchant freighter, boarding the vessel as its merchant crew attempted to fend them off. After the other pirates had began to overpower the freighter's crew, Brutus boarded the starship wielding two blasters, firing upon the remaining merchants. Once Brutus had eliminated the last of their foes, he called back to Silvo to report their success, stepping aside to allow the captain to enter.

Bry was a Hoopaloo male thief who worked with fellow criminals Jorkat and Velek during the Republic Era. At a celebration on the planet Serenno in 90 BBY, Bry stole a purse from the Serennian Lady Jenza. Although Bry and his associates restrained Jenza and her brother Ramil, the Jedi Initiate Dooku confronted the criminals. Dooku used the Force to throw the Hoopaloo through the air before revealing his presence and fighting Jorkat with an electroblade. The Jedi eventually scared Bry and his accomplices away, saving Jenza and Ramil. Dooku recounted the incident in a holo-letter to Jenza, a recording of which he later showed to his newly-recruited Sith assassin, Asajj Ventress, around 23 BBY.

The Hoopaloo Bry and his associates were present in Carannia, the capital city of the Outer Rim planet Serenno, attending a celebration for the worlds of the region. During the celebration, Bry stole the purse of the young Serennian Lady Jenza—daughter of Count Gora of House Serenno—swiping the item while roughly brushing past her. Bry fled and hid behind a repulsor tent, rummaging through the purse's contents. Jenza pursued, snatching the bag back, and the Hoopaloo reprimanded the girl for doing so. When Jenza noticed that a crystal that had belonged to her grandmother was missing, she questioned Bry, who feigned ignorance.

At that point, Jorkat and Velek approached from behind Jenza, and Bry claimed that the girl had stolen his purse. When Jenza protested, Jorkat called her selfish and asserted that the Hoopaloo had no credits to his name; the Karkarodon suggested stealing the Serennian's coat to give to Bry, who agreed that it would warm his feathers. After Jorkat grabbed Jenza to search her belongings and the girl's brother Ramil was restrained by Velek when he arrived in an attempt to defend his sister, Bry suggested kidnapping the pair and taking them to Renza, although the Karkarodon was unsure whether the Hutt would be interested. Jenza bit Jorkat and escaped his grip, and Bry attempted to catch her.

However, Bry suddenly found himself thrown through the air, having been pushed using the Force by the Jedi Initiate Dooku, who had sensed a connection with Jenza—unbeknownst to both, his sister—and followed the girl. Bry cried out, insisting that something had knocked him down when questioned by his bewildered Karkarodon accomplice. Dooku revealed his presence, wielding an electroblade against Jorkat. Bry attempted to intervene but was once again pushed back by Dooku. Velek was soon thrown into the Hoopaloo, almost crushing Bry when the Askajian stood up to run away. Although Jorkat remained aggravated at Dooku, Bry pleaded with his accomplice and the pair also fled.

Bryn was a Human male captain who served in the Special Forces of the reconstituted Sith Empire. During the Cold War, around 3643 BBY, he was stationed on the Sith capital planet of Dromund Kaas, where he performed reconnaissance on Lord Grathan, a rogue Sith Lord who had declared himself the thirteenth member of the Dark Council.

Bryn held the rank of captain within Imperial Special Forces during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. At one point during his career, he was stationed on a bridge on the Sith capital planet of Dromund Kaas between the Wall and the estate of rogue Sith Lord Grathan, At this position, he was tasked with keeping watch on Grathan while maintaining his distance. As part of his orders, he was to retrieve the plans for a prototype turret that his superiors wanted to mass-produce, but his orders also specified that he could not enter Grathan's territory. He requested the aid of a passing individual affiliated with the Sith Empire to retrieve the plans.

The Imperial individual successfully infiltrated Grathan's compound, retrieving a security badge from a member of Lord Grathan's forces in order to pass by its automated defenses. The individual broke into Grathan's weapons lab and downloaded the plans from the databanks of the droid PO-12, much to its chagrin; it wanted to destroy the schematics and ensure no more turrets could be built. Upon the individual's return, Bryn displayed an eagerness to test the efficacy of the turrets on Republic personnel.

After the individual's mission, Bryn remained posted on the bridge, continuing to keep watch over Grathan's estate.

They were stationed to move the funds onto the Republic starship, and remained there as it blasted off, journeying to an unknown destination.

Bryson first appeared in the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic, but the mission that he would have introduced on the planet Dromund Kaas was cut from the game before release. Bryson would have sent players to speak with Captain Guyvar, who they needed to convince to send one of his Chevin workers to the Diplomatic Service in order to impress visiting Chevin diplomats.

Bryti was a humanoid male that served as a butler to fugitive Jedi Master Kai Hudorra following his acquisition of The Lucky Twi'lek on Kestavel. His wide head was fitted with a Borg Construct Aj^6 headband.

When Dass Jennir, Beyghor Sahdett, and the crew of the Uhumele arrived at the casino in search of Hudorra, the Bothan told Bryti to provide the crew he was not speaking with with accommodations on the house. Following Sahdett's betrayal and subsequent report of Hudorra's Jedi status to the Galactic Empire, Bryti, along with several of Hudorra's other servants, reaffirmed that they would stand by him no matter what. Following hatching an assassination attempt on Darth Vader, who was leading the oncoming attack personally, Bryti attended the pre-fight feast, where he served Jennir drugged wine on orders of his master. Hudorra would fall in his fight against Vader, and Jennir would awake aboard the escaping Uhumele, where Bryti gave him a holodisc containing his master's final farewell to his old friend.

The BT-009S fastshot trigger was an blaster trigger that was illegally modified to reduce the amount of force or movement required to shoot. a group of pirates had stored a fastshot trigger in a cavern inside of Typhon's Rock, a rock mound in the Lost Steppe region on the moon Toshara, located in the Outer Rim Territories.

In 3 ABY, the scoundrel Kay Vess heard about the fastshot trigger stored at Typhon's Rock. She later went to the cavern and retrieved the trigger and used it to the modify her VM-19 heavy blaster pistol.

BT-009S fastshot trigger appeared in the 2024 Massive Entertainment video game Star Wars Outlaws. The player must obtain the trigger in order upgrade the light plasma module to level four.

In 3 ABY, the scoundrel Kay Vess traded a fusion engine core and two thousand credits to Entip in exchange for the ion accelerator which she later used it to the modify her VM-19 heavy blaster pistol's ion module.

Buboicullaar, or Bubo for short, was a frog-dog male that was kept as a pet by the Hutt crime lord Jabba the Hutt, who used him as a guard dog. He lived in Jabba's palace on the desert planet Tatooine and foiled many assassination despite most people thinking he was not more than an unintelligent pest. The Gran Ree-Yees was assigned to take care of the frog-dog, but on one occasion lost track of him aboard Jabba's sail barge, the Khetanna. The Gran promised Jabba that he would find his charge and clean the barge, but Buboicullaar avoided his keeper while Ree-Yees searched. Once the Gran believed he had run out of time, Jabba simply summoned Buboicullaar by calling his name.

In 4 ABY, Buboicullaar barked at the protocol droid C-3PO as the droid entered Jabba's throne room with the astromech droid R2-D2 to deliver a message to Jabba from the Jedi Knight Luke Skywalker. Later that day, the frog-dog was present for a performance of the song "Jedi Rocks" by the Max Rebo Band which ended in the enslaved dancer Oola being fed to Jabba's pet rancor, Pateesa. Buboicullaar then witnessed Princess Leia Organa, disguised as the bounty hunter Boushh, threaten Jabba and his court with a thermal detonator while trying to negotiate over the bounty on the Wookiee Chewbacca.

Buboicullaar, also known as just "Bubo," was a frog-dog male that lived in the palace of the Hutt crime lord Jabba Desilijic Tiure on the desert planet Tatooine. and protected him from many assassination attempts, The Gran Ree-Yees was tasked with unglamorous job of taking care of Buboicullaar but on one occasion lost track of the frog-dog on board Jabba's sail barge, the Khetanna, while it was out traveling on Tatooine.

Pleading for his life, the Gran promised to find Buboicullaar while also cleaning the entire sail barge so that his charge would not be tempted to wonder off again. Jabba then gave Ree-Yees the time it would take for the Khetanna to return to the palace to make good on his promises. Buboicullaar moved around the barge ignoring Ree-Yees as the Gran cleaned and called out for the frog-dog. When Ree-Yees laid out a plate of fecal worms, Buboicullaar's favorite food, as bait, the guard dog simply ate the worms when the Gran's back was turned and continued to avoid him.

Buck was a Green Forge ecoterrorist. A muscular opportunist, he would have affairs with wealthy women and use them to achieve his Green Forge ends. While the affairs' cause being information gathering for sabotage against environment-unfriendly tycoons and their installations, Buck usually made off with shares from his widowed lovers. Buck's latest target is Tibanna-mining Yorn Skot mining station and its owner, Clode Rhoden.

Becoming the illicit lover and supposed personal trainer of Madam Rhoden, Buck sneaked a core bomb aboard the Aurorient Express (which is also a property of Clode) with the intention of blowing up both the properties and owner himself. However, their plan was collided with numerous parties including pirate-infiltrator Podlong Foahl and foreknowing Clode. Podlong had activated his own time-triggered core bomb and Clode ordered the ship's captain to place Buck's core bomb in the pair's escape pod. Fortunately, they were informed by Saul Moegantz, who won the Madame's affection. After the ship had been evacuated, Podlong's bomb went off and destroyed both Aurorient and the pirate vessel.

A serial bomber himself, Buck process intimate knowledge about core bomb and were able to recognize Podlong's threat by identifying his bomb switch. He also claimed to know eight forms of the martial art Tae-Jitsu and assumed proper stance, yet he was easily overcome by young Obi-wan Kenobi.

Buggles was a male voorpak owned by Torra Doza, a resident of the Colossus platform on the planet Castilon. He remained close by his owner Torra's side though she normally kept him in her room. Buggles was involved in a few low stake adventures aboard the Colossus. During the Battle of Castilon, Buggles helped Torra find Team Colossus leader Kazuda Xiono.

Buggles was a pet voorpak owned by Torra Doza, the teenage daughter of Captain Imanuel Doza, the administrator of the Colossus station.

Later Torra, annoyed at being confined to her bedroom by her father, used Buggles to escape from the droid 4D-M1N by giving him to her, explaining that he needed to be take out or else he would have another accident indoors. After 4D-M1N left, Torra slipped out of her bedroom as she had deduced the passcode, but her presence in the hallway was given away when Buggles saw her over 4D's shoulder and reacted. The droid was prevented from chasing after Torra, however, when Buggles then urinated on the floor. When Torra later returned to her room, accompanied by Kazuda Xiono, Buggles was present while they played Flight Simulator Squadron. After Xiono left Doza Tower after a series of events, Torra cuddled her pet while wondering what he was hiding.

Sometime later Torra asked Xiono to watch Buggles at Jarek Yeager's Repair Station while she was busy. However, the Voorpak escaped Xiono, first eating the contents of a bowl before running outside and hopping onto the precarious structures at the very edge of the platform, with Xiono in pursuit. He nearly managed to catch Buggles before the pet bounded off again, to his dismay. When Torra returned in search of Buggles, Xiono evaded her question of where he was. The voorpak had gotten into the cockpit of the Fireball, and managed to launch the starship by randomly pressing buttons. Torra asked who was piloting the ship, and Xiono was forced to admit it was Buggles, to her horror.

The bugle boy was a male Human recruited into the Army of Light during the New Sith Wars.

A male Human was recruited into the Jedi Order's Army of Light during the final decade of the New Sith Wars. Charged with sounding the war bugle to rouse the Army for battle, the young boy served under Jedi Lord Hoth during the Ruusan campaign following the declaration of support from the Jedi Grand Council.

During the Seventh Battle of Ruusan, the bugle boy joined in the company of Jedi General Kiel Charny when the group of Jedi and loyal soldiers confronted the Brotherhood of Darkness in open combat. During the fighting, the Sith used the Force to destroy the forest surrounding the battlefield, leveling the Charny's forces. During the fighting, the unarmed bugle boy was slain and his body left broken on the field of battle.

Bulduga was half of a male Ithorian bounty hunter duo, alongside his brother, Onca. While Onca preferred long-range weapons, such as rifles, Bulduga preferred the quick-and-easily-accessible blaster pistols. Well-known throughout the galaxy, the two brothers gained the attention of Count Dooku, leader of the Separatists, and was given the challenge of winning the Box, a lethal bounty hunter competition. After gathering with Dooku's other assembled bounty hunters, Bulduga was killed by Cad Bane over a dispute regarding the Ithorian's wide-brimmed fedora. Onca was left to compete on his own, but died during the second challenge.

Bulduga was an Ithorian male who, alongside his brother Onca, operated as a bounty hunter during the Clone Wars. The two became regarded as a legendary duo. Preferring quick-draw blaster pistols over Onca's preference for long-range rifles, Bulduga was able to convince many targets that not all Ithorians fit the peace-loving agriculturist stereotype.

Bulduga's choice of weapons, coupled by his low-hanging holster, red-tinted goggles, and wide-brimmed hat caused bystanders to theorize that the Ithorian was nothing more than an imitator of the well-known bounty hunter Cad Bane, although no one would say such within earshot of the deadly Ithorian. Eventually, Bulduga and Onca attracted the attention of the Sith Lord Count Dooku, who was in league with the Confederacy of Independent Systems. The Count invited the hunters to the planet Serenno to compete in a lethal tournament called the Box.

In preparation for a risky mission to kidnap the Supreme Chancellor of the Galactic Republic, Dooku invited a posse of bounty hunters to his homeworld in order to test their mettle in a series of challenges designed by criminal mastermind Moralo Eval. Those who survived the challenges would take part in Dooku's operation and receive a hefty reward upon the job's completion.

Bulgeski was a Sallichen male senator who represented Salliche in the Galactic Senate during the era of the Galactic Republic.

A Sallichen male that lived in the twilight decades of the Galactic Republic era, Bulgeski served as senator for the Core Worlds planet Salliche inside the Galactic Senate. An agriworld that cultivated the crops exported to planets like the capital Coruscant, as their spokesman, Bulgeski claimed that Salliche represented the breadbasket of the Core Worlds and called for the Republic Guard to intervene when his homeworld fell beneath assault from Norkronian raiders.

In 42 BBY, not long after his request for aid, Bulgeski was present at the Senate Chamber when Jedi Master Dooku addressed him and his fellow senators to voice protest to cuts that the congress was intending to make to their trade route defense program. Though Dooku sought to intervene on behalf of the populations of worlds in the Outer Rim Territories that would be affected, Bulgeski objected to his arguments and engaged in a verbal sparring match where the senator accused the Jedi of attempting to influence the Senate. Dooku tried to use the recent request that Bulgeski had made for assistance to support his argument that the Outer Rim should receive the same benefits, but the Sallichen responded that the importance of his homeworld necessitated this intervention, as Salliche represented a vital food source for Coruscant and the other Core Worlds. When his statement prompted his opponent to theorise that Bulgeski and his constituents were afraid that the agricultural worlds of the Outer Rim would become their competitors, the senator denied this as a scandalous accusation, while Supreme Chancellor Kalpana dismissed Dooku's advice.

Bulgeski appeared in the audiobook Dooku: Jedi Lost, written by Cavan Scott and published in 2019.

Bungo Bung was a male Sullustan from the planet Sullust. Despite growing up working on his father's boaboo fungus farm, Bung harbored a desire to pilot starships. Joining SoroSuub Corporation's Transport and Supply Division, he eventually attained the command of the Chubby Gundark, a Nyubba-class cargo barge driver. Assisted by his droid co-pilot, 42-RST—known as Rusti—Bung was the pioneer of the Great Bantha Breakfast Biscuit Run between Sullust and Gastrula in the Outer Rim Territories during the Galactic Civil War. Bung transported Biscuit Baron's Bantha Breakfast Biscuits to the native Gastrulans, despite interference on the first run from Imperial Captain Wankle. Although he made a healthy profit, Bung broke even after spending much of the money on repairs to his ship after an encounter with a Giant Amorphous Bantha Breakfast Biscuit, a strange anomalous lifeform that was the result of the interaction between the preservatives in Bantha Breakfast Biscuits and the stale air in his ship. He survived by defeating the creature with blue sauce, which, as the recommended accompaniment to a Bantha Breakfast Biscuit, proved to be the lifeform's weakness.

The Sullustan male Bungo Bung was born on the planet Sullust, and grew up in the underground caverns of his homeworld, working on his father's boaboo fungus farm. Bung had few duties and spent much of his time sitting around and daydreaming. The fungus was tended to by droids, who then crushed the fungus to make boaboo juice. He was only required to clean up the mess the droids made when they eventually short-circuited in the moist environment, and transport the juice to the markets in G'rinn Go city.

However, Bung's desire was to pilot a starship, and when he was old enough, the young Sullustan signed up with the SoroSuub Corporation's Transport and Supply Division. Serving as a shipping pilot, Bung faithfully worked for SoroSuub for a number of years, eventually earning the captaincy of the Nyubba-class cargo barge driver Chubby Gundark. During his travels, Bung worked for the Mephout, and they gave him a gift—the RST Model Translator Droid 42-RST, otherwise known as "Rusti." Although Bung believed that the gift was for the services he had rendered for them, the Mephout were simply getting rid of obsolete technology. 42-RST served as co-pilot of the Chubby Gundark and was employed as a translator.

Burg was a Devaronian male who operated as a mercenary during the era of the New Republic. Burg acted as the muscle of a team recruited by Ranzar Malk to rescue the prisoner Qin from the Bothan-5, a New Republic Correctional Transport, which also included Migs Mayfeld, Xi'an, Q9-0, and the Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin, who had been recruited for the use of his gunship, the Razor Crest. After Qin was rescued, Burg and the team betrayed Djarin and trapped him inside a cell. However, the Mandalorian managed to escape and took them down, imprisoning them in a cell aboard the transport and leaving them behind to deliver Qin to Malk alone.

A male Devaronian from Devaron, Burg was recruited by the criminal Ranzar Malk as part of a team led by fellow mercenary Migs Mayfeld, which also included the droid Zero, the Twi'lek Xi'an, and the Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin, with the objective of rescuing Qin from aboard the Bothan-5, a New Republic Correctional Transport. While the Devaronian carried a crate, Mayfeld introduced Burg to Djarin, describing him as the muscle of the group. Burg then dropped the crate and approached the Mandalorian, sneering at him and stating that he thought Mandalorians would be bigger. As the team boarded Djarin's starship, the Razor Crest, Burg scoffed at his size.

During the journey, Burg strolled around inside the ship, upsetting Xi'an, who told the Devaronian to be seated. He grunted at the Twi'lek, with Xi'an snarling back in response. Burg then tinkered with the controls, opening a weapons cabinet in the process. As he inspected the weapons with glee, Djarin intervened and closed the cabinet, angering the Devaronian. Tensions rose between the two, with Burg questioning why they needed a Mandalorian on the team. Mayfeld replied stating that they were considered to be the greatest warriors in the galaxy. Burg then asked why were they all dead, causing Mayfeld and Xi'an to laugh in response. The team then questioned why Djarin never removed his helmet, with them guffawing when Mayfeld speculated if he was a Gungan. When Mayfeld suggested that he remove his helmet, Burg attempted to do so, but the Mandalorian retaliated, causing a fight to break out between the two. During the fight, the Devaronian accidentally opened the chamber where Grogu resided, revealing his existence to the team. Zero dropped the ship out of hyperspace immediately afterwards and maneuvered around the prison ship, causing everyone to stumble.

Upon landing, the team entered the prison ship and began their search for Qin, with Burg entering after Mayfeld and Xi'an. As they entered the hallway to the control room, they encountered a mouse droid. Burg toyed with the droid before shooting it, alerting a group of N5 sentry droids to their position. The team was cornered in the hallway, but watched as Djarin sneaked behind the droids and destroyed them. They then mocked his efforts, with Burg intentionally bumping into him.

Burloo, known as "Bantha" Burloo, was a burly Chagrian bouncer who worked at Miss Mylla's Saloon in Bartyn's Landing, a town on Lamaredd.

Burloo was a tall, muscled Chagrian male living in the coastal town of Bartyn's Landing in Lamaredd. He was nicknamed "Bantha" Burloo. For as far as any neighbor could remember, Burloo had been seen in the company of Miss Mylla, a Falleen who had arrived to Lamaredd at some point before 69 BBY along with several Falleen escorts.

Miss Mylla eventually bought an inn and transformed it into Miss Mylla's Saloon, an entertainment locale where customers could enjoy drinks served by scantily-clad waitresses or these women's company in private rooms. Burloo became the bouncer of the Saloon, standing always at a maximum of ten meters from the door, except when he was dealing with any problematic guest. The Saloon was always open, and Burloo appeared to be always on duty. Burloo was also partly responsible for the security of the courtesans — although most of them could take care of themselves.

At 225 centimeters of height and powerfully built, Burloo was an imposing presence in Lamaredd. He commonly carried with him a club, a combat knife and a slugthrower pistol – as blasters were uncommon in Lamaredd. He had several skills appropriate to his job, including the ability to intimidate, and was fluent in both Chagri and Basic — although he could only write Chagri.
enrichments.short_description: Burloo, known as "Bantha" Burloo, was a burly Chagrian bouncer who worked at Miss Mylla's Saloon in Bartyn's Landing, a town on Lamaredd.

Field Agent Burne was a Human male SIS operative who served the Galactic Republic during the Cold War.

During the Separatist War, he was stationed outside the entrance to the Separatist Stronghold housed inside Mount Avilatan. He received a tip that the separatists are meeting with the leaders of violent splinter groups from across the galaxy. He tasked a Republic spacer to access the separatist database in the separatist stronghold and hunt down the splinter groups' leaders.

The Mandalorian was caught, however, and frozen in carbonite as punishment by Fa'athra. Burnok then hired a spacer in the industrial town of Jiguuna to rescue his companion.

enrichments.description:
Burryaga Agaburry, was a male Wookiee Jedi Knight of the Jedi Order who was active during the High Republic Era. The apprentice of Jedi Master Nib Assek, his master learned Shyriiwook so she could communicate with him.

When Burryaga Agaburry was very young, he was afraid to climb the trees of his homeworld. His parents encouraged the young Wookiee to persevere as they climbed with him, teaching him a valuable lesson on bravery. Burryaga lived on Kashyyyk until he was five years old.

Burryaga joined the Jedi Order and became the Padawan of Jedi Master Nib Assek. In 232 BBY, Agaburry and his master participated in the rescue effort to save the Hetzal system during the Great Hyperspace Disaster. He was the one who discovered that several of the hyperspace anomalies bearing down on the worlds of the system were starship fragments with people still alive onboard. While Jedi pilots attempted to destroy the starship fragments, Burryaga felt the survivors' terror so deeply that it radiated through the Jedi Force network. Facing a language barrier, the other Jedi believed that they were feeling Burryaga's own emotions and initially attempted to remove him from the network. Burryaga's efforts ultimately made the other Jedi realize that the starship fragments had survivors aboard.

During a visit to Kashyyyk, Burryaga met the Jedi younglings Kai Brightstar, Lys Solay and Nubs.

Bursthed was the Imperial Governor of Ruten during the New Republic era. He was known to be an evil and corrupt man but also an efficient bureaucrat. He considered his appointment as governor of Rutan beneath him and hoped that an effective term would lead to promotion.

During the Galactic Civil War, Bursthed served as Governor of the planet Draenell's Point.

Bursthed's hobby was collecting exotic and unusual animals from all over the galaxy for his private menagerie. His collection included a bear spider, a dewback, a glittering mynock, and a quexius bird from Endor. His courtesans organized regular Pet Shows where the Governor would inevitably win first prize. In exchange for their support the judges of the shows would receive favors of land which were often taken from farmers later accused of treason against the Galactic Empire and evicted. Also at these shows the animals were made to do tricks that often involve violence to Humans, more than often those accused of being Rebel leaders. Members of the New Republic planned to stop these shows by arranging for the Governor to lose the contest. They planned to swap Bursthed's entry, a glittering mynock, for a Slug-rat. Native to the planet Ruten, when woken the Slug-rat would attack the nearest person.
