Toob Ancher was a male Human smuggler who worked for the crime lord Saadoon-Kauldi. He was the brother of Karl Mathieu Ancher.

Toob spent most of his time in the Ottega system. One day, a thermal detonator that was planted by a bounty hunter exploded in his face. His face was horribly disfigured, with his left eye completely blown out and his right eye had to be replaced with cybernetic prosthesis. Shortly afterward, he contracted Brekken Vinthern, more commonly known as the Bitter Winter disease, and he began to go insane. He was taken to the planet Redcap by Drake Paulsen to search out Saylor Marjan and to recover a debt owed to Saadoon-Kauldi. While on Redcap, Toob completely lost his mind and went insane. He set out to attack the Aremin, believing he could escape on his own ship. Drake Paulsen was forced to shoot him out of the sky to prevent Imperials from shooting him down.

Tophid Bruster, designated DT-4431, was a lieutenant TIE fighter pilot in the Starfighter Corps of the First Order. In 35 ABY, Bruster piloted a TIE/fo space superiority fighter as part of a group sent to destroy the YT-1300 light freighter known as the Millennium Falcon while it was on a mission to the Sinta Glacier Colony. Bruster engaged the freighter, but it ultimately escaped.

Lieutenant Tophid Bruster was a human male TIE Fighter Pilot with the designation DT-4431 who served in the Starfighter Corps of the First Order during the war against the Resistance. In 35 ABY, he flew in a TIE/fo space superiority fighter as part of a squadron sent to the Sinta Glacier Colony in order to track down the Resistance YT-1300 light freighter known as the Millennium Falcon. The TIE fighters split up into several groups, with Bruster's moving down an ice corridor within the glacier.

The group spotted the Falcon docked further down the corridor, where its crew members Finn, Poe Dameron, Klaud, R2-D2 and Chewbacca were transferring data from the Resistance sympathizer Boolio. Bruster locked on to the vessel, but it undocked and began to escape, shooting down one member of Bruster's group and then crushing two other TIE fighters by causing part of the corridor's ceiling to collapse. The Falcon ultimately escaped the colony by flying through an ice wall and hyperspace skipping away.

Tophid Bruster wore the standard black uniform and flight helmet of a First Order TIE pilot. The helmet had data projected onto its interior viewplate and the uniform's chestplate had a life support control center attached.

Torban Buck, nicknamed "Buckets of Blood," was a Chagrian male Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order as a healer during the High Republic Era. Alongside Master Yoda, Buck was stationed aboard the Jedi Padawan academic cruiser Star Hopper when the cruiser and its passengers were forced to respond to fallout from the Great Hyperspace Disaster in the Trymant system. He and Yoda intended to handle the largest pieces of debris while the apprentices assisted the civilians. However, a battle broke out against a group of Nihil pirates present on Trymant IV, which led Buck and Yoda to leap to the rescue.

Torban Buck was a male Buck joined the crew of the Padawan Academic Cruiser Star Hopper as one of two Jedi Masters teaching a class of Padawans training onboard the starship, alongside Buck had joined the crew to teach Padawans the basics of first aid.

Around this time, the Great Hyperspace Disaster occurred in the Hetzal system, when the freighter Legacy Run was destroyed in hyperspace. In its aftermath, Emergences of the debris began occurring across the Outer Rim Territories. When an Emergence occurred in the Trymant system, the Star Hopper was the only Jedi or Galactic Republic starship in range, and it was diverted to assist. With the class of apprentices assembled, Yoda had several of the students report what they had discovered on the situation, as hyperspace debris was hurtling towards Bralanak City, the most densely populated area of the planet Trymant IV. Buck told the class that he and Yoda would be handling the largest pieces of debris. He added that the Padawans' job was to help people on the ground to safety and deal with smaller chunks. The Padawans were then dispatched to their rescue speeders.

While assisting civilians in the city, Padawan Lula Talisola and several of her friends attempted to commandeer a large Spider Cruiser which had arrived in the city so it could be used as an evacuation vehicle. However, the ship belonged to the Nihil pirates, who were disinclined to acquiesce to the request. As Talisola, her best friends Farzala Tarabal and Qort, and Force-sensitive civilian Zeen Mrala, who had stepped in to telekinetically hold off a large chunk of debris, were surrounded by the pirates, Buck and Yoda arrived before the pirates could attempt to execute them.

Torkil Mux owned a HWK-290 light freighter, which he used on the planet Shinbone to mine gems.

From the outside, it appeared to be a stock HWK-290 light freighter starship.

The Arcona Torkil Mux used his HWK-290. He was skimming gems from Jabba the Hutt's criminal enterprises and storing them on a transport until he could escape the giant slug's clutches. For his mining operation, he used a number of walking plants as slave labor. When the smuggling pair of Han Solo and Chewbacca arrived with more laborers, the two smugglers became concerned with their plight. When it was discovered Mux was hoarding gems, the two smugglers hatched a plan to steal the gems and free the walking plants.

Chewbacca gathered the walking plants unto Mux's ship while Solo distracted the Arcona. Chewbacca took off with the transport and Solo ran back to the Millennium Falcon after blasting Mux's K4 security droid. The two ships docked in orbit, and Chewbacca suggested to the walking plants that they take the ship to Kashyyyk. The pair took 60 kilograms of gems to give to Jabba and went on their separate way.

The Imperial Navy special unit Black Epsilon disabled the Torton Runner engines and captured the ship, thereby securing the data.

Torul Blom was a male Pau'an politician who served as governor of Pau City on Utapau during the Clone Wars.

When Jedi Knights Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi were sent to Utapau to investigate the death of Jedi Master Tu-Anh, Blom met them to inform that their presence had upset Pau City citizens, as well as to deny the Confederacy of Independent Systems' presence on the planet.

It was later revealed that the Pau'an governor was in league with the arms dealer Endente and Separatist leader Count Dooku. As Blom awaited for Endente to arrive with a massive kyber crystal that was valuable to the CIS, he was informed of the arrival of Count Dooku's enforcer, General Grievous. He was present when Endente came empty-handed into his office and witnessed the Sugi's decapitation at the hands of Grievous for his failure. When Kenobi and Skywalker returned to Pau City to request his help, Blom had them arrested and retrieved the crystal for his Separatist allies.

His victory was short-lived as his men and B1-series battle droids were defeated and the two Jedi escaped. Grievous arrived a few moments after the duo had fled and seemed quite angered. Realizing his mistake, the governor told the cyborg warlord that he was sorry for the complication, at which Grievous stabbed Blom with a lightsaber, killing him and scornfully remarking that only now was he truly sorry.
enrichments.short_description: Torul Blom was a male Pau'an politician who served as governor of Pau City on Utapau during the Clone Wars.

Tour Aryon was the Human female who served as governor of the desert planet Tatooine under the Galactic Empire. She was a native from Treylon II.

Tour Aryon was born on the planet Treylon II. She met and married her husband, Kant, the son of a wealthy baron and baroness. He was a con artist who moved in underworld circles, but recanted the life so as not to jeopardize Aryon's political career when she was appointed as Tatooine's Imperial governor. Upon her arrival, Aryon moved her offices into a palatial house located in Bestine, and immediately appointed Orun Depp as Imperial Prefect. She placed him in charge of running Tatooine's day-to-day affairs.

Aryon's contributions to Tatooine focused on the cultural, much of which was lost on the average Tatooinian. She established a museum in Bestine, which boasted the only complete Krayt dragon skeleton on the planet, and hosted lavish garden parties with expensive, imported entertainment. Aryon did not respect the citizens of Mos Eisley, considering them to be peasants and savages.

When Darth Vader sent his own stormtroopers to the surface of Tatooine to search for R2-D2 and C-3PO, Tour objected, insisting that her own troops could handle it. When Vader was informed of her objections, he did not care. After Imperial Prefect Orun Depp was assassinated by the assassin droid IG-72, Governor Tour replaced him with Eugene Talmont.
enrichments.short_description: Tour Aryon was the Human female who served as governor of the desert planet Tatooine under the Galactic Empire. She was a native from Treylon II.

Tover Blackmoor was a Human male chemist who lived during the time of the Galactic Civil War.

After the Battle of Yavin, Tover Blackmoor worked for the Black Sun, one of the most powerful criminal syndicate in the galaxy, and operated out of a Black Sun bunker on Naboo's moon of Rori. During that time, the Black Sun discovered that the Rebel Alliance was smuggling and hoarding a new kind of spice. the Black Sun acquired a sample of this new spice after the smuggler Cal Handro crash-landed on Rori while transporting it. Tover Blackmoor analyzed the spice and discovered that it was nothing like any other spice available on the marker. The Black Sun leaders therefore decided to obtain more spice but they attracted the attention of a group of spacers who were looking for Cal Handro, the missing pilot. The spacers attacked the Black Sun bunker and eventually forced Blackmoor to reveal everything he knew about the pilot and the new spice.

Tover Blackmoor was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts. Tover Blackmoor was added to the game with the second chapter of the "Secrets of the Syren" quest line, released with the "Publish 14.1," on March 24, 2005. All the content of the "Secrets of the Syren" story arc was removed from the game with the "Chapter 1," published on June 8, 2006, due to the major changes planed for Rori with the introduction of the Battle of Restuss.

In the game, Tover Blackmoor was spelled Tovar Blackmoor in the quest objectives. During each server reset, Tover Blackmoor's appearance was randomized, but he consistently appeared as a male Human under the template "scientist_human_male".
enrichments.short_description: Tover Blackmoor was a Human male chemist who lived during the time of the Galactic Civil War.

Traavis was a Human male Jedi Knight who served as a general during the Clone Wars. In 19 BBY, during the Galactic Republic's sieges in the Outer Rim, Traavis led a campaign for five months against the Cassandran Worlds of Monhudle, New Bakstre, and Biitu.

Later in the year, he moved his troops to the Separatist world of Garqi. After securing the planet, Traavis ordered the clone commandos of Aiwha Squad to search for civilians and to take them to refugee camps. As he was inspecting the camps, the squad returned with an orphan named Evan, whose parents were killed during a skirmish between the Grand Army of the Republic's clones and the Confederacy's battle droids. Traavis met with the boy and congratulated the squad for completing their mission. As the Jedi was speaking to the other commandos, Aiwha Squad's leader, Sarge, received Order 66 from Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, commanding all clone troopers to eliminate the Jedi. The clones immediately turned against Traavis and executed him.

Traavis, a Human male, was born during the final decades of the Galactic Republic on the asteroid Skip 5, located in the Smuggler's Run. During the Clone Wars—the conflict between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems—Traavis served both the Jedi Order and the Republic as a Jedi Knight and general in the Grand Army of the Republic. In 19 BBY, during the Republic's Outer Rim Sieges, Traavis led a five-month campaign against the Cassandran Worlds of Monhudle, New Bakstre, and Biitu. Later in the year, Traavis' forces captured the planet Garqi, and the Jedi Knight began to inspect the planet's overcrowded refugee camps. He ordered the clone commandos of Aiwha Squad to search for civilians and to take them to the camps for protection. Traavis eventually received news that General Grievous, the Supreme Commander of the Separatist Droid Army, had been killed.

While Traavis was inspecting a refugee camp, Aiwha Squad's leader, Sarge, reported on the mission's success. The commando also introduced the Jedi to a boy named Evan, whose parents were killed during a skirmish between the Republic's clones and the Separatist's battle droids. Traavis told Evan that they would get the orphan a bed in the refugee camp and some food. He commended the squad on their successful mission and informed them that Grievous was dead, stating that the war was likely nearing completion. However, as Traavis conferred with the other clones, RC-1013 received Order 66 from Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, which commanded them to eliminate the Jedi Knights as enemies of the Republic. Sarge immediately ordered Aiwha Squad to execute Traavis. The Jedi attempted to reach for his lightsaber to defend himself, but he was killed by the squad's blaster fire.

Trax Bonkik was a Rodian male mechanic who, with his older brother, Pax, was a slave to the Podracer Mars Guo. Shortly before the Boonta Eve Classic of 32 BBY, Trax and Guo got into an argument that led to their owner violently beating Trax and planning to sell him after the Podrace. During the event, the Podracer Sebulba damaged Guo's Podracer and later arranged to have Guo's possessions auctioned off.

Fellow Podracer Teemto Pagalies, who had previously befriended Pax, was only able to free Pax, and Trax got sold off to Sebulba. Pax, however, was determined to save his brother and worked for Pagalies, who went on to win the Aleen Classic, with only enough money to be able to free Sebulba's slave Ann Gella, whom he had romantic interest in. However, he ended up instead ultimately freeing Trax from Sebulba and reuniting the Rodian siblings.

The Rodian male Trax Bonkik had a bond with his older brother, Pax, who hailed from Rodia, Their parents, being shiftless spice addicts, sold the Bonkik brothers into slavery.

Trax's older brother looked out for him after they became slaves, with the Rodians drifting from owner to owner, eventually learning skills to increase their worth. Working primarily as mechanics, the Bonkik brothers ended up working for a minor league Podracer, Mars Guo, who would force the siblings to work to near-exhaustion on his Podracer, a Plug-2 Behemoth.

Tren Alvar was a male Human Jedi Knight who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the decade preceding the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive Human, Tren Alvar was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order. Studying at the Coruscant Jedi Temple as an Initiate, Alvar ascended to the rank of Padawan after the Trade Federation's invasion of Naboo and the reemergence of the Sith. Assigned to a Jedi Master to continue training, Alvar constructed a blue-bladed lightsaber to wield throughout his career.

In response to the Sith's reappearance, the Jedi High Council opened several Jedi outposts across the galaxy for supplemental group training. Assigning Padawan Alvar to Kashyyyk, the High Council placed Jedi Master Mavra Zane in command of him and a number of other students to travel to the Wookiee homeworld aboard a Consular-class cruiser. Upon the group's arrival, the students were greeted by Grand Master Yoda the Watchman of Kashyyyk, along with Masters Mace Windu and Obi-Wan Kenobi. The Padawans settled in at the new outpost and quickly began classes, continuing on their path to knowledge.

During Alvar's time on the planet, the armies of the Commerce Guild, combined with Trandoshan slavers, attacked the planet and the Wookiee village near the chapter house. Rallying behind Masters Yoda and Zane, the apprentices repelled the Trandoshans with few casualties. Following Master Yoda's departure, the students were attacked again. This time, Master Zane and several students were captured while the chapter house was destroyed and most of the apprentices were killed. Alvar, among the survivors, eventually found himself above Felucia on a Commerce Guild Providence-class carrier/destroyer. After the Padawans and Zane were freed from captivity, the Jedi escaped aboard the Star Runner and made an emergency landing on the planet below. Joining Mak Pra and the Felucian resistance movement, Alvar and his companions attempted to capture Commerce Guild Presidente Shu Mai and prevent her from attacking Coruscant with trihexalon missiles. The Jedi rushed to Coruscant and smashed the Commerce Guild's fleet, ending the crisis and saving Coruscant.

Triggo Binz was a male Twi'lek thug who lived during the Galactic Civil War.

After the Battle of Yavin, former slave Kitster Banai attempted to improve the lives of the slaves on Tatooine. This led him to struggle against the slaver Drik Bandrik. In 1 ABY, Kitster Banai tasked Triggo Binz to undermine Drik's local mining business. Unaware that his boss was a slaver, Drik's employee Rakir Banai recruited a spacer to stop Binz and prevent him to blow up the mine. The spacer tracked down the Twi'lek saboteur and killed him after a brief fight. Just before dying, Triggo Binz revealed the truth about Drik Bandrik's slaver activity, and the spacer reported this information to Rakir Banai.

Triosa Broog was a human she had achieved the rank of sergeant and was stationed at the Carida Academy, where she served as training officer to Cadet Han Solo. Solo proved to be a disobedient cadet and his reckless flight behavior and repeated insubordination drew the ire of Broog's commanding officer, Captain Nettic Whain. Whain questioned Broog on why Solo had not been expelled from the academy when other cadets were kicked out for less. Broog pointed to Solo's exemplary flight record, explaining that she had never seen anyone with his reaction time or innovative problem-solving skills when piloting a ship. Whain countered that he would rather have one hundred recruits who follow orders than the best pilot in the galaxy who does not. She implored the captain to give Solo one more chance, declaring she believed she could get him to follow orders. After realizing just how impressive Solo's flight skills were, Whain relented, on the condition that she take away his flight privileges for a week—if Solo improved he could be reinstated and if he did not, he would be expelled and sent somewhere a soldier who didn't follow orders could be useful.

A double-bladed spinning lightsaber was utilized by Tualon Yaluna during his time as a member of the Inquisitorius.

The weapon featured a ringed emitter which could partially detach from the remaining hilt, allowing both blades to rotate rapidly without effort from the wielder. For a Jedi hunter like an Inquisitor, this function likely served as a way to intimidate opponents, as well as deflect any form of direct attack. However, this was also the weapon's primary weakness, as a lightsaber-wielding opponent could simply separate the emitter itself and cut the weapon in half, as was demonstrated by Kanan Jarrus during his final duel with the Grand Inquisitor aboard the Sovereign.

After the Jedi Knight Tualon Yaluna was captured by the newly formed Galactic Empire and turned to the dark side of the Force, he was given a new lightsaber, which he used during training duels with fellow Inquisitor Iskat Akaris and their master, the Sith Lord Darth Vader. During his time as an Inquisitor, Yaluna carried the weapon during a number of assignments, including a mission to Firrhana and the hunt for Eeth Koth. His last use of the lightsaber was in combat against Darth Vader, who eventually used the Force to kill Yaluna with the weapon.

Giuseppe Camuncoli's concept art for Yaluna's Inquisitor lightsaber was initially in the form of standard split saber, but soon took the form of the double-bladed spinning lightsaber typically used by Inquisitors, as seen in its official depictions.

Tulak Hord, known as the Lord of Hate and Master of the Gathering Darkness, was a Dark Lord of the Sith that ruled during the early Sith Empire, commanding great armies and possessing a mastery of the dark side of the Force and lightsaber combat which left him nearly unrivaled. During battle, Hord wore a black mask, making him a fear-inspiring sight.

A Force-sensitive male, Tulak Hord was a student of the dark side of the Force and a pupil of the early Sith Empire. Rising through the ranks, Hord was feared by his rivals even in his early days, having mastered the art of lightsaber combat and manipulation of the Force. Assembling a massive army of followers, Hord and Val led a campaign of terror against rebellious militants on the planets Yn and Chabosh, crushing them. While on the campaign, Hord was approached by a Sith known as Aloysius Kallig who sought to serve him; however, Hord dismissed him. Kallig refused to accept dismissal, however, and challenged Hord's best general and beat him. After Kallig's victory, Hord decided to accept him, and he led Hord's troops to numerous victories. During the battles, Hord employed his knowledge of Sith rituals, draining the strength from his opponents and feeding off of it. Earning the titles Lord of Hate, Master of the Gathering Darkness, and finally, Dark Lord of the Sith, Lord Hord went undefeated, slaying all who dared to challenge his might. While Kallig's military prowess gained Hord enormous success, it also intimidated the Dark Lord, who feared that Kallig could become a very dangerous rival. Hord decided to deal with the situation by having Kallig assassinated, with his family subsequently going into hiding.

Lord Hord continued his endeavors into the arts of Sith sorcery, authoring many tomes of knowledge and crafting his personal holocron. Rumored to have known the secret to eternal life, Hord scattered much of his teachings in hidden and hard to reach locations to ensure only the worthy could obtain his knowledge. Discovering and conquering the Dromund system, it was believed that the Sith Lord conquered over a hundred worlds for the Empire. One who did prove worthy during Hord's life was his only known apprentice, Ortan Cela, who came to learn much from the great Sith.

Appreciating his relationship with the honor-bound Khem Val, Lord Hord placed his servant and ally in suspended animation inside a stasis chamber deep in the heart of what would later serve as Sith Lord Naga Sadow's tomb on Korriban. Ortan Cela would kill his master not long afterwards by stabbing him through the back, and Cela's Dashade servant Veshikk Urk consumed the dying Sith Lord's Force energy.

Tunga Arpagion was a male Clawdite shape-shifter agent who was known to be a professional actor and impersonator. He was recruited by the Alliance to Restore the Republic for a mission they undertook on Mon Cala. His impersonation of Imperial Moff Tan Hubi allowed Leia Organa and her team to locate Lee-Char, former king of Mon Cala, and deliver his last words back to the Mon Calamari.

After a brief return to acting, he was once again recruited by Organa, who required his talents for a mission to Shu-Torun, with their goal to take down the Spike as an economic strike to the Empire. He impersonated the ore-duke Lord Or-Tar in order to get Organa a scan of Queen Trios' eye, which could unlock Shu-Torun's security systems. Arpagion later took the form of Queen Trios to rid the Ancestral Retreat of its staff, allowing the rebels to deactivate the security systems of Shu-Torun.

Their plan went astray when the Partisans, a rebel insurgent group recruited for the attack, sabotaged the Spike so that it would destroy Shu-Torun in revenge for the Empire's destruction of Jedha. When the rebels became trapped by both an orbital bombardment and a group of TIE fighters, Arpagion sacrificed himself, using his shapeshifting abilities to trick the Imperials into believing he was Organa, shooting down his ship. However, Arpagion survived, and was rescued by cultists of the Central Isopter, who initiated him into the cult against his will.

A Clawdite shape-shifter, Arpagion gained a reputation for the various acts of impersonation he had achieved, such as playing the role of the late Thespus-V for a week after she died before anyone noticed. He also had several connections, including many members of the Meor nobility near Encrust II. At some point, he was caught and imprisoned by Dex Acquisitions, who planned to hand the Clawdite over to the Galactic Empire in exchange for a reward.

Turon Adala was a Human male officer of the Royal Naboo Security Forces during the time of the Galactic Civil War. Sometime following the Battle of Yavin in 0 BBY, Pooja Naberrie tasked a spacer with locating Adala and escorting him back to the city of Dee'ja Peak on Naboo. Although the spacer was attacked by stormtroopers and an Imperial staff sergeant, Naberrie's mission was completed.

Turon Adala was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, prior to its closure on December 15, 2011.

Players who performed a series of quests for Pooja Naberrie had to locate Adala and escort him safely back to Dee'ja Peak. However, due to a bug, many of the NPCs in Naberrie's quests were not properly sequenced. For instance, in the quest to escort Adala, players actually encountered an individual known as Lim Paddu, who was supposed to appear in the following quest. The character model for Turon Adala likewise erroneously spawned for Naberrie's third quest, in which the player was supposed to encounter an individual named Jumis. Nevertheless, it was possible for the player to complete the mission and advance to the next quest. This article assumes that the content of Naberrie's quest dialogue is canon in the Star Wars Legends continuity, and that Adala, not Lim Paddu, actually appeared during her fourth quest.

Because Turon Adala spawned under the generic "naboo_police" template, his appearance was randomized under one of two possible depictions. He could either appear as a brown haired, brown eyed Human female, or as a brown haired, brown eyed Human male. Because the quest dialogue identified Adala as male, this article assumes that the Human male depiction is canon in the Star Wars Legends continuity. Examining the NPC also revealed his name to be Turon Idala. This article assumes "Adala" to be the correct surname, as it was consistently used in the quest dialogue.

The Twi'lek Dancer was a CEC Barloz-class freighter that had a number of owners through the years.

Originally known as the Harvest it was owned by an agricultural combine. The ship was later re-named the Venom Sting, customized and used by the Tiss'shar bounty hunter Xufal D'uat until his death. The ship was then salvaged by a mining station and sold to a cell of Thalassian slavers, who renamed it Twi'lek Dancer, re-customized it and used it in their raids. The ship was then requised by pirates and sold to a legitimate trader of used ships.

This Barloz-class freighter built by the Corellian Engineering Corporation was originally bought by an agricultural combine in the Tion Hegemony. The owners called the ship Harvest and used it for a time, until they earned enough money to buy an YT-1300 light freighter. They decided to sell the Harvest at this point.

The Harvest was bought by Xufal D'uat, a bounty hunter of Tiss'shar species. D'uat re-named the ship Venom Sting and performed several modifications first on a limited scope and later covering the whole ship, allowing him to fight any intrusion in his headquarters.
enrichments.short_description: The Twi'lek Dancer was a CEC Barloz-class freighter that had a number of owners through the years.

The Twilight was a Corellian G9 Rigger-class light freighter owned and operated by the Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker during the Clone Wars. Skywalker and his Padawan, Ahsoka Tano, used the ship to escape from a battle on Teth. When Obi-Wan Kenobi traveled to the planet Mandalore during the Mandalorian civil war, the ship was destroyed by the former Sith Lord Maul and his Shadow Collective.

The Twilight had a roomy cockpit with chairs for the pilots

The Twilight was originally owned by the Hutt crime lord Ziro Desilijic Tiure, who used it as a spice freighter. early in the Clone Wars, Ziro allied himself with the Confederacy of Independent Systems in a plot to take over his nephew Jabba Desilijic Tiure's criminal empire, as well as sabotaging relations between the Galactic Republic and the Hutt Clan. As a result, the Twilight was present on the Wild Space planet Teth, at a landing platform near a B'omarr Order Monastery where the Separatists were holding Jabba's abducted son, Rotta. During the subsequent battle at the monastery as Republic forces attempted to locate the child, the spy droid 4-A7 and several battle droids were loading cargo aboard the ship when they were discovered by Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker, his Padawan Ahsoka Tano, and Skywalker's astromech R2-D2, who had rescued Rotta and were escaping Separatist commander Asajj Ventress. Realizing that 4-A7 was not the "caretaker droid" he had claimed to be, Tano destroyed him and the battle droids before she and her master claimed the Twilight.

At first, the Twilight refused to start up, but Skywalker and R2 were able to fire up the engines and attempted to land on the nearest Jedi Cruiser. Unfortunately, the Vulture droids prevented them from landing in one of the cruiser's hangars. Thus, Skywalker and his crew were forced to take the Twilight to Tatooine. Aboard the ship, Tano activated the medical droid hologram, TB-2 to save Rotta from near death. Upon the Twilight arrival at Tatooine, the ship came under attack by a pair of IG-100 MagnaGuards using Rogue-class Porax-38 starfighters. Skywalker, Tano, and R2 were able to destroy the starfighters, but were forced to crash land in the Dune Sea.

The Tyaonon Ranger was one of only nine experimental Stathas-class freighters ever produced. At one time it was owned by Bib Fortuna who used it to smuggle spice for Jabba the Hutt until their smuggling ring was taken down by a Phraetiss system patrol cruiser which seized the ship and took the crew into custody. Somehow the vessel mysteriously disappeared from the impound yard mere days after being logged in. The only lead as to who did this was a Human near the yards just after the Ranger first arrived. He was described as being solidly built and smelled of armudu spice. Apparently this man had sold and then stolen the ship from no less than four people. Sometime before Tealo came into possession of the ship, it was upgraded to have additional hull plating.

When Tealo came into possession of the ship, it only had 10,000 light-years on it. He had received it from a quiet Sullustan who had used it to travel the Outer Rim trade routes, and was looking to sell it straight away. Though he did not know the true value of the craft, he had put a price of 25,000 credits on it, without knowing that there was 40,000 credits worth of spice inside the ship in hidden compartments. He eventually managed to sell it to a group of Rebels who discovered that the ships records had been falsified. The previous "owners" of the ship all tried to gain the ship back from the group, especially Jabba who wanted his spice back.

Tyffix was a Gand Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order during the Clone Wars. In 21 BBY, Tyffix and their Padawan, Cal, were dispatched to lead a Republic clone trooper force on the planet Thustra when the world's populace attempted to secede from the Republic. Shortly after arriving on the planet, the Republic forces were attacked by the native Sephi, and Tyffix was killed when a suicide bomber destroyed the Republic command center.

A Force-sensitive Gand, Tyffix was a member of the Jedi Order who held the rank of Jedi Master during the Clone Wars between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Tyffix selected the young Human Cal as their Padawan, training the youth to think like a warrior.

In 21 BBY, Tyffix and Cal were part of a Republic task force sent to the planet Thustra when the native Sephi population wanted to secede from the Republic. What was originally planned to be a show of force soon turned into a bloody battle, in which Sephi suicide bombers inflicted heavy casualties on the Republic troops. While discussing strategy with fellow Jedi Master Tyr and a clone officer inside the Republic command center, Tyffix was victim to the Sephi tactics when a suicide bomber destroyed the command tent, killing all present except Tyr's Padawan, Pix, whom her Master had Force-pushed out of the tent before the explosion. Cal saw the explosion from afar and called out for his master. Cal and Pix then sent a message to the Jedi and Republic on the planet Coruscant informing them of Tyffix and Tyr's deaths and calling for help.

Tyffix taught Cal that thinking like a warrior and a conqueror would be the only way to survive the Clone Wars, a lesson the Padawan took to heart but one that ultimately led to the Padawan's death later during the battle.

Tyr was a male Weequay Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a Jedi General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive Weequay, Tyr was educated by the Jedi Order in the ways of the Force, attaining the rank of Jedi Master. Because he was raised at the Coruscant Jedi Temple, Master Tyr did not worship the Quay totem that his people who grew up on Sriluur dedicated their lives to following fanatically. Wearing his long black hair in a tight braid, Master Tyr selected the young Human Initiate Pix as his Padawan.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems in 22 BBY, Master Tyr took up the rank of Senior Jedi General in the Grand Army of the Republic and contributed his lightsaber to the war effort. Assigned to the campaign on Thustra, Master Tyr and Padawan Pix joined Master Tyffix and his Padawan, Cal, in attempting to prevent the Sephi from joining the Confederacy. While Masters Tyr and Tyffix were going over strategy with their clone troopers in a battlefield command center, a suicide bomber attacked their tent. While the two Masters were killed, Master Tyr had successfully evacuated both Padawans from the tent using the Force.

As a Jedi Master, Tyr was proficient in the use of Force powers, demonstrating his skill at the Battle of Thustra when he pushed his Padawan, Pix, out of the command tent before it was engulfed by a suicide bombing. His ability to sense the imminent danger, as well as act accordingly in time to it, is testament to an aptitude for precognition.

A starship was owned by the Devaronian scoundrel Tyresius Lokai during the Cold War. Lokai became a target of the Great Hunt and his ship was shot down over Tatooine and tried to escape the planet under an alias, but was pursued by another bounty hunter across the Dune Sea desert. Eventually, Lokai was cornered at his ship's landing cite, where he persuaded the Hunter into letting him live by presenting a genetically identical clone to claim his bounty. Changing his name to Gault Rennow, Lokai left on the Hunter's D5-Mantis Patrol Craft, abandoning his ship on Tatooine.

Tyresius Lokai's starship appears in the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic during the Bounty Hunter class mission on Tatooine.

Tyrus Brokenblade was a male Mandalorian warrior and the leader of Clan Varad who lived during the third Galactic War, and represented Clan Varad in Heta Kol's organization known as the Hidden Chain.

In 3626 BBY, members of Clan Varad joined in on an attack on the Mandalorian ship the Spirit of Vengeance II alongside the Ash'ad and the Dar'manda at the behest of Heta Kol. Following this attack, after they had secured the banner of Clan Cadera, Brokenblade met with Heta Kol, Bask Sunn, and Durn Wynnward. An argument broke out between Brokenblade and Wynnward but was quickly stopped by Kol when she pulled out a thermal detonator and threw it at Brokenblade. Brokenblade managed to catch and keep it from exploding and was then stabbed twice by Kol as a demonstration of how they all relied on each other. Kol deactivated the thermal detonator, and Brokenblade was assisted by members of Clan Varad before being dismissed to fulfill the orders given to them.

Tyrus was later present in the Hidden Chain meeting when Ri'kan Kateen reunited with the group and brought his sister, the rogue Jedi Padawan Sa'har Kateen, to Heta Kol.

Following Hidden Chain's disastrous retreat from Ruhnuk, Tyrus attended a gathering of Kol's inner circle, where she revealed that Bask Sunn interfered with her duel with Shae Vizla, prompting her to expel Dar'manda from the Hidden Chain. Afterwards, she showed them Darth Nul's holocron and promised that its secrets would bring the Hidden Chain to glory, but the only ones who would know the whole plan would be just herself and Sa'har, before everyone, including Tyrus, applauded her.
enrichments.short_description: Tyrus Brokenblade was a male Mandalorian warrior and the leader of Clan Varad who lived during the third Galactic War, and represented Clan Varad in Heta Kol's organization known as the Hidden Chain.

enrichments.description:
Ubrik Adelhard was a human male officer for the Galactic Empire who served as the governor of the Anoat sector with the rank of Moff during the Galactic Civil War. Following the Battle of Endor, Adelhard reformed his forces into an Imperial remnant that quarantined the Anoat sector, and believing himself to be the next in line for the Imperial throne, ascended to the rank of Grand Moff, seeking to restore the Empire under his leadership. As a result, for the remainder of the Galactic Civil War, Adelhard refused to work with the remaining Imperial holdouts who were unknowingly carrying out the late Emperor's Contingency under the command of Counselor to the Empire Gallius Rax, while also pushing back against incursions from the newly formed New Republic. Yet still in need of forces to fulfill his plan to restore the Empire in his play for power, Adelhard allied himself with the forces of Grand General Kenner Loring, as well as those of the Acolytes of the Beyond and the Spice Runners of Kijimi, creating a coalition in doing so. Yet as Adelhard began pushing outwards from the Anoat sector against the New Republic, he was betrayed by the hired assassin from the Acolytes Reyna Oskure and was forced to escape to his presumed death and rot on the backwater planet Gallowyss with his most loyal troops. However, with many of his forces still loyal to him, Adelhard returned to his fleet, now a changed man, vowing to destroy those who had seen lesser of him and had seen him as nothing but a pawn; the New Republic and the Galactic Empire. During the Battle of Jakku Adelhard made his final bid for revenge, but was betrayed by the Spice Runners of Kijimi in his moment of victory, eventually coming being shot and killed by New Republic pilot Rynn Zenat after a brief duel with Luke Skywalker.

Born to a poor family on the lifeless Anoat sector mining planet Ripurni, Ubrik worked various mining jobs on the planet to survive until he witnessed the shooting of one of his coworkers at the hands of the Newly-formed Galactic Empire's TK stormtroopers. Amazed by the order, structure, and power that the troopers brought, Adelhard soon enlisted in the Imperial Army, himself becoming a TK trooper and later a Stormtrooper in the Imperial Stormtrooper Corps. Serving in the Storming of Abartolom and helping crush the Moraysi rebellion, Ubrik rose the ranks of the Imperial Military before eventually serving as an Imperial officer under Grand Admiral Thrawn's 7th Fleet by the time of the Battle of Atollon. Around 0 ABY, Adelhard, in command of an Imperial-class Star Destroyer, was dispatched back home to the Anoat sector to deal with a group of insurgents who had taken up a base in the sector's capital planet of Anoat. Having observed how those in the highest levels of command in the Empire held power an maintained order, Adelhard gave the order to gas the Ecumenopolis, turning the planet into a toxic waste dump, which was later framed as an industrial accident. Following the gassing, Darth Vader promoted Ubrik to the position of governor of the Anoat sector, telling the new Moff that the Empire had great plans for him, words which stuck with Adelhard long after.

Udo Barnet was male Twi'lek mercenary who lived during the time of the Galactic Civil War.

After the Battle of Yavin, Udo Barnet and his group of mercenaries were recruited by the Galactic Empire to ensure the security of a secret Imperial research facility on the planet Lok. The mercenaries were led by Udo Barnet and Kell Lapaz,

In 1 ABY, As the criminals were planning their operation, Grenz Zittoun, another lieutenant of Nym, realized that the attack on the facility could be an unique opportunity to get rid of some annoying mercenaries. A group of spacers affiliated with the Lok Revenants then assaulted the research facility. They had to fight numerous mercenaries to get access to the research complex but they finally retrieved experimental weapons and research data. During the battle, a group of Revenants attacked Kell Lapaz and Udo Barnet and killed them in the ensuring firefight.

Udo Broxin was a Herglic who was a regular at the entertainment and gambling establishment known as the Ace of Sabres on the planet Kluistar.

Udo was a fixture at the Ace of Sabres for as long as anyone could remember. The manager, Gandin T'Noull, even allowed the Herglic's large bar tab to go largely unpaid since Udo's presence always had such a positive effect on the atmosphere of the Ace of Sabers.

Udo was witty, sarcastic and outgoing. He enjoyed nothing more than a good drink, a game of sabacc and a brawl before bed. His good humor and sense of fun lifted the other patrons mood. He was loud and boisterous, and had the tendency to draw others to his mayhem and mischief.

He referred to himself as "Uncle Udo" and was always willing to dispense advice to those that were willing to listen. He also had a tendency to ramble on even when no-one was listening.
enrichments.short_description: Udo Broxin was a Herglic who was a regular at the entertainment and gambling establishment known as the Ace of Sabres on the planet Kluistar.

Ulfor Bombaasa was a male human in the year 19 BBY during a performance of the opera Squid Lake. Bombaasa was walking up the steps of the opera house with the alien Opula Deget behind Duke Teta and the Twi'lek Koyi Mateil when the Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker ran passed them on his way to meet with Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine. Bombaasa had fair skin and brown hair. He wore a black fur-trimmed coat with a light purple silk shirt and gold sash along with a pair of black boots.

Ulfor Bombaasa was portrayed by James McBryde in Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith, which was released on May 19, 2005. James McBryde also had previously appeared as an unnamed extra in Dex's Diner in Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones. The character's name was first revealed by the reference book Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars, which was written by Trisha Biggar and released on October 1, 2005. The name was then used in canon in Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia,

Star Wars: How Not to Get Eaten by Ewoks and Other Galactic Survival Skills

Ulthar Blaze was a male Human who served the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War. A secret agent, Blaze infiltrated the Galactic Empire by posing as a corporal from the Imperial Security Bureau, and he was assigned to serve as the assistant of the Imperial Admiral Grendreef on the planet Miser. After the Empire discovered the location of the Alliance-held world Isis, a group of Rebel agents were imprisoned on Miser and Blaze helped the agents to escape. By disguising themselves as stormtroopers, Blaze and the agents were subsequently able to board the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Desolator and erase Isis' co-ordinates from the vessel's computer.

Unaw Aharo was a male Bith who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a Jedi Knight during the Galactic War with the reconstituted Sith Empire. As a Jedi Padawan, Aharo discovered that the Dark Jedi Callef was leading the native Flesh Raiders of Tython against the Order, and was rescued by another Jedi learner who would become the apprentice of Master Orgus Din. Aharo passed the Jedi Trials not long after the conflict with the Flesh Raiders, and when Grand Master Satele Shan and Master Jaric Kaedan sent Jedi to aid the Republic Military in the Battle of Corellia, Aharo was among those sent to the world.

After passing the Jedi Trials, Aharo was soon recruited by Satele Shan to serve under Orgus Din's former apprentice, the Jedi Knight known as the Hero of Tython, and served as the Hero's lieutenant during the group's mission to stop the corrupted Jedi Master Tol Braga from massacring civilians on the command of the Sith Emperor. After the Hero departed Corellia to confront the Emperor himself, Aharo remained behind with the other Jedi to aid the Republic in their ultimately successful battle for control of the planet. As the Galactic War dragged on, Aharo eventually became a Master.

A Force-sensitive Bith male, Unaw Aharo was recruited into the Jedi Order and trained in the ways of the Force during the Cold War between the Republic and the Sith Empire. Aharo was training on the Order's homeworld of Tython in 3643 BBY when he encountered a group of armed Flesh Raiders—the planet's hostile natives—in the Tythonian Gnarls region. Contacting Jedi Knight Derrin Weller at the nearby Masters' Retreat, Aharo informed Weller that the Flesh Raiders were emerging from a cave nearby and were attacking the Jedi outpost in the area. However, after ending his holocall, Aharo was captured by Flesh Raiders, who injured the Bith and brought him into the cave before their Human leader.

The Dark Jedi, whose name was Callef, mocked Aharo and the Order for their weakness and prepared to execute the injured apprentice, but Aharo was saved by the arrival of another initiate. The second apprentice, who had been sent by Weller to close off the cave, asked Callef to release Aharo, but the Dark Jedi drew his lightsaber before attacking the learner. Shoved to the side, Aharo watched as the apprentice fought back against Callef and ultimately struck down the Dark Jedi in a fierce duel. As the apprentice helped Aharo to his feet, the Jedi Master Orgus Din arrived and escorted Aharo back to the Jedi Temple after collapsing the tunnel with the Force.

A capsule carried the Stranger to the Forest Moon of Endor. In 3 ABY, two moons near Endor aligned, and a rift in space opened, through which the capsule traveled. The capsule fell toward the forested moon, and the young Ewoks Wicket Wystri Warrick and Teebo saw it and mistook it for a Comet. When the capsule touched down, the Stranger emerged, and the craft was located by the two Ewoks and their friends Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka and Latara. As the Ewoks began to carry the capsule back to their village, it illuminated, spun rapidly, and vanished.

In 3 ABY, the a capsule carried the Stranger to the Forest Moon of Endor. When the capsule landed, the Stranger made his way to the Dulok swamps, but not before witnessing the Ewoks, Wicket Wystri Warrick and Teebo coming across the ship. Wicket and Teebo, with help from Latara and Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka, tried to carry the capsule back to Bright Tree Village. Wicket took a piece of it and attached it to his Belt of Honor as proof of his quest towards becoming a full-fledged Ewok warrior.

As the Ewoks walked, the capsule illuminated bright purple light and began to spin in a circle. The speed increased until the capsule was a blur, and the Ewoks stepped back. The capsule then disintegrated into a cloud of smoke, leaving no trace except for the "trophy" on Wicket's belt.

A blue-skinned, black-eyed Chagrian served as a member of the Jedi Order's High Council The Chagrian, along with their Human colleagues, grew concerned with the Jedi Padawan Exar Kun and the eagerness of the latter to study the dark side of the Force, which was shunned by the Order. The Jedi Council claimed that Kun's desire for knowledge was beginning to resemble a thirst for power, and the young Jedi indeed fell to the dark side around 3997 BBY.

In a historical record composed by Jedi Master Gnost-Dural more than three centuries later, the Chagrian member of the High Council and their colleagues were depicted against the backdrop of a high-ceilinged hall. In the record, the Chagrian was wearing dark red and dark brown robes.

The Chagrian Jedi appeared in The Exar Kun War, the tenth installment of the Galactic Timeline series of videos published on the [http://www.swtor.com official website] for Star Wars: The Old Republic,

In The Exar Kun War, the depiction of the Chagrian is identical in appearance, clothing, and pose for the 1999 prequel trilogy film, Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace, of Jerome Blake portraying Mas Amedda, Vice Chair of the Galactic Republic's Senate.

A Consular-class cruiser was owned by Noggox the Hutt during the Clone Wars. It was captured by the pirate Dool Pundar in 22 BBY.

A Consular-class cruiser was used as a freighter by Noggox the Hutt during the Clone Wars. It was painted silver, featured deflector shields. It had at least one escape pod. A Hologram emitter was on the bridge. Like other ships of its class, it was 115 meters and had three sub light Dyne 577 radial atomizer engine units.

In 22 BBY, the freighter was carrying droid brains to the Fondor Shipyards. The captain was a Klatooinian man, and other crew included a Snivvian lieutenant, a Rodian, another alien, and a Human. The freighter was intercepted near Shipwrights' Trace by Dool Pundar's pirate ship, which disabled the two of the freighter's thrusters and the primary shield generator. Pundar ordered the crew to surrender and sent B1-series battle droids to take control of the vessel. Pundar then allowed the crew to leave in an escape pod. After Pundar absconded with their vessel, the crew transmitted a distress signal to the planet Coruscant, home of the Galactic Republic. At the time of its capture, the ship was insured.

The freighter appears in 2011's The Clone Wars: Strange Allies, a comic tie-in to the Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Secret Missions young readers series.

The mummified alchemically-preserved remains of this Dark Lord were located within the Hall of Judgment in the Great Temple at the Valley of the Dark Lords on the planet Korriban.

A Force-sensitive individual served as a Dark Lord of the Sith of the Sith Empire. The deceased body of the Dark Lord, which remained untouched by time, was preserved by the Sith alchemy within the Hall of Judgment in the Great Temple at the Valley of the Dark Lords on the planet Korriban.

After Emperor Palpatine perished aboard the Death Star II, the ancient Dark Lord and at least three other deceased Sith spirits aided Palpatine in his journey out of Chaos back to the living plane of existence and into a clone body.

In 11 ABY, the reborn Palpatine visited the Great Temple, seeking counsel from the spirits of his Sith predecessors in order to restore his decaying clone body. As they traveled through the ancient Sith crypt, the Dark Side Adept T'iaz felt the dark side power emanating from the place. Palpatine explained to him that the ancient Dark Lords were preserved by the Sith alchemy that made them outcasts. The Dark Lord doubted his success and offered him Vader's tomb, but Palpatine declined and instead demanded to be healed. The spirit suggested Palpatine to gaze into the oracle stone, through which Palpatine learned that the only way for him to survive would to to transfer his spirit into Anakin Solo, the newborn son of Princess Leia Organa Solo. The other spirits gave Palpatine counsel and bid him farewell a final time.

A Ho'Din Jedi Master served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a Jedi General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive Ho'Din was educated in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, ascending to the rank of Jedi Master. Having constructed his own green-bladed lightsaber, he studied as a Consular, specializing in the art of healing and becoming one of the Order's healers. The Ho'Din selected a young Human Initiate as his Padawan.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, the Master took up the mantle of General within the ranks of the Grand Army of the Republic. Along with his Padawan, the Master was assigned to assist in the evacuation of the planet Nadiem following an invasion by the Confederacy. While ushering citizens to the rescue shuttles, he came a cross a young mother and her wounded child. Taking a moment to heal the boy's wounds, the Ho'Din Master marveled at the boy's sense of calm amidst all the turmoil. Suspicious of the boy's Force-sensitivity, the Ho'Din summoned his Padawan to take a blood sample of the boy, which came up positive for sensitivity.

Because there were limited shuttles off the planet, and the Order was in desperate need of new recruits, the Master offered to designate the boy for priority evacuation, if his mother agreed to give him over to the Order for training. Assuring the young woman that her son would reach safety at the Coruscant Jedi Temple within two days, she agreed, and her son was taken off world. Not long afterwards, the Ho'Din was forced into battle with the Separatist Droid Army to defend the refugees. Surrounded by battle droids, the Jedi was quickly overwhelmed by the superior number of droids.

enrichments.description:
A male was an alien Sith Lord who served the One Sith and Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire in 138 ABY. After the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Wyyrlok ordered the execution of the Final Protocol against the planet Dac—which was poisoned by Sith scientist Vul Isen—the Sith attempted to defend Isen's laboratory on the planet Daluuj when the former Jedi Cade Skywalker and his allies raided Isen's lair in an attempt to locate the "Butcher of Dac." The Sith Lord engaged Skywalker in a lightsaber duel on a bridge, with Skywalker gaining the upper hand and slicing off the man's legs. He was interrogated by Skywalker, who, after finding that the alien had no information as to Isen's whereabouts, left the man to die when the explosives set by Skywalker's allies in the laboratory detonated.

An alien male served the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Krayt's One Sith Order and Galactic Empire, having killed numerous Jedi Earlier, in 137 ABY, the Sith Lord Darth Wyyrlok—who, as Krayt's Voice, commanded the Empire when Krayt was incapacitated—ordered the Final Protocol's execution, causing the extermination of the majority of the planet Dac's population. During these events, the Sith Lord was stationed on the Outer Rim planet Daluuj at the laboratory of the Givin scientist Vul Isen, who created the viral spores that poisoned Dac's waters.

Early in 138 ABY, the former Jedi Cade Skywalker and his allies assaulted Isen's laboratory, in search of the scientist who had been nicknamed the "Butcher of Dac." The Sith Lord attacked Skywalker and engaged him in a lightsaber duel on the bridge leading to the laboratory, throughout which he taunted and demeaned the former Jedi. However, Skywalker evaded an attack from the Sith and cut off his legs. The wounded Sith Lord was interrogated by Skywalker about Isen's whereabouts, with Skywalker promising that the man would live if he gave them Isen's location. The Sith told him that the laboratory Skywalker had raided was indeed Isen's, but that the Givin scientist had abandoned it long ago, taking all evidence with him. He also revealed that Isen did not share his knowledge with anyone.

When Skywalker instructed his crewmate Jariah Syn to detonate the explosives that he had set in the laboratory and began to flee with his former Jedi Master Wolf Sazen, the Sith cursed Skywalker for what he believed to be a breach of the Jedi's word. However, he was reminded by Skywalker that the condition for his life was only if the Sith told him of Isen's location, and the Sith perished in the explosion after the explosives detonated.

This Humanoid male was a Jedi Guardian during the events surround the Great Hyperspace War, when the Sith Empire made their thrust for domination of the Galactic Republic.

A member of a Humanoid species, this Jedi served as a commander of the Coruscant defense force when the Sith fleet arrived prepared for war. He served alongside Jedi Knights such as Memit Nadill, Tuknatan, and Sonam-Ha'ar, and the Coruscant soldiers in pushing back the Sith threat. Once Coruscant was protected, this Jedi was part of the fleet the followed the Sith back to their region of space to ensure their forces were decimated, so that the threat they posed was unquestionably defeated.

As a Jedi Guardian, this Jedi was an expert on tactics, weapons, armor, and vehicles used in combat during his time. His weapon of choice was not a lightsaber, but rather a lightstaff imbued with the Force, whose ends both glowed with a resonant blue energy signature.

This Imperial-class Star Destroyer was a warship that served in the Imperial Navy during the Galactic Civil War.

This Star Destroyer was 1,600 meters long, the standard length for an Imperial-class Star Destroyer. However, it featured a bridge with a different interior design than the standard Imperial-class Star Destroyer. The ship also housed several laboratories.

The Star Destroyer was particularly resilient, as was shown when it was adrift during several years. Despite being near a dying star and hit by meteors, most of the ship still had operational gravity and life support systems.

The Star Destroyer carried a complement of TIE/LN starfighters and at least one TIE/sa bomber.

After learning the truth, Sevn helped the insurgents free their families.

A green-skinned individual was a male Jedi who served the Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive, this individual received instruction in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, eventually attaining the rank of Jedi Knight. Reporting to Coruscant at the start of the Clone Wars, this Jedi took up the rank of General within the Grand Army of the Republic and accepted missions from the Jedi High Council.

The Jedi was placed in command of a Jedi-clone trooper task force created to investigate the mysteriously abandoned space station known as the Brink of the Celestial Wake. Boarding the station, the Jedi and clones were quickly attacked by mass amounts of pink blobs and all perished excluding Jedi Serra Keto. When Jedi Anakin Skywalker received Keto's distress code, he boarded the ship and found the body of the unfortunate Jedi task force leader. His body would be destroyed when the space station was destroyed by the combined efforts of the two surviving Jedi.

A green-skinned humanoid, this deceased Jedi belonged to a species which had three-fingers on each hand, and two curving cranial horns which sprouted from the back of his head.

A Jedi Knight served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars, serving as a General within the Grand Army of the Republic.

A Force-sensitive, this individual was discovered by the Jedi Order sometime prior to 22 BBY and was trained in the ways of the Force. The Initiate, who had earned distinction as a promising student, proved their comprehension of the Jedi Code, self-discipline via meditation and lightsaber combat, and their strong attunement to the flow of the Force, passing the Initiate Trials. The apprentice gained the attention of a Master and was selected as a Padawan student.

At about this time, the Confederacy of Independent Systems (CIS) had united against the Republic, and the Jedi had no choice but to fight in the conflict, and like all apprentices the Padawan was given the rank of Jedi Commander. In the war room of the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, the Padawan convened with famed Jedi Yoda, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, Mace Windu, Plo Koon and Ahsoka Tano, along with clone marshal commander CC-2224 and astromech droid R2-D2. They welcomed the Padawan formally into the Jedi Order, and Windu presented them their first lightsaber.

Fighting in many early battles such as the campaign on Iceberg Three, the conflict on Umbara, the battle for Ryloth, the skirmish on Carlac and the second battle of Geonosis, the Padawan was made a Jedi Knight by the Jedi High Council and given the rank of General.

This individual was a male Human Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive, this Human received training in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, ascending to the rank of Jedi Master. Constructing a double-bladed lightsaber imbued with blue crystals at its core, this Master was proficient in it use during lightsaber combat.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, this man took up the rank of General in the Grand Army of the Republic. Surviving three years of war, he was stationed at the Coruscant Jedi Temple when the Republic's Supreme Chancellor Palpatine betrayed the Order and issued Contingency Order 66 to the Grand Army, ordering them to kill their Jedi leaders. As the forces of the 501st Legion stormed the Temple as part of Operation: Knightfall, this man joined other masters and led a final charge against clone troopers on the Temple Veranda. While fighting valiantly against the clones under the command of Darth Vader, this Master and his companions were slain during the fighting and the Temple fell into the hands of the Dark Lord of the Sith, Darth Sidious.

This Jedi Master used a blue double-bladed lightsaber in combat. He was a talented swordsman as he was one of the last Jedi standing during the attack on the Temple.

A Kel Dor Sith Lord once reigned as a Lord of the Sith. and 41 ABY, the Sith Lord engaged a group of Galactic Alliance Guard troopers in combat. The Kel Dor had orange skin and wore black robes in conjunction with armor that protected the Sith's chest. the Sith was forced to wear a set of protective goggles and an antiox breath mask. The Kel Dor was Force-sensitive, and was powerful enough to ascend to the rank of Sith Lord. The Kel Dor was additionally capable of using the Force to channel blaster fire energy and turn it against enemy forces, using Force lightning against the troopers.

The Kel Dor Sith Lord appeared in an image created for the Jedi Academy Training Manual, a 2009 resource guide for the Star Wars Roleplaying Game. The image was used to demonstrate a Force technique called "Channel energy." The Sith Lord was additionally pictured in the montage on the introductory chapter page.

enrichments.description:
A starship hailing from the region of the galaxy beyond the Unknown Regions known as "Lesser Space" carried Galactic Republic technology and held human survivors by 19 BBY. The vessel was seized by a task force of the Chiss Ascendancy's Chaf family.

Chiss Syndic Mitth'ras'safis and a human female pilot managed to steal the starship from the task force, but were unable to bring it to a refuge world from which they could give the Republic technology to the Ascendancy's Defense Hierarchy Council, as the ship was too damaged to reach its destination. The syndic and the human subsequently crashed the vessel into a valley, killing themselves in the process but saving the humans aboard the starship.

A massive starship from "Lesser Space," the region of the galaxy beyond the Unknown Regions, carried Galactic Republic technology. It was equipped with engines and carried food and supplies that could last for generations and a small vessel. The spacecraft contained a pylon.

By 19 BBY, the starship, which carried human survivors, was involved in the Vagaari pirate operations, a conflict between the forces of the Chiss Ascendancy nation and the Vagaari pirates. A task force of the Ascendancy's Chaf family obtained the vessel, and the Chiss syndic Mitth'ras'safis, core name "Thrass," and a human female pilot stole the starship. Thrass and the woman spirited the ship away in hopes of bringing it to a refuge world from which they could offer the Republic technology to the Ascendancy's Defense Hierarchy Council; however, their plan did not go as planned. The ship was far too damaged to reach the world, and the pair discovered the human survivors aboard the vessel.

enrichments.description:
A Munificent-class star frigate was created at the Gwori shipyards during the Clone Wars. In 22 BBY, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, and Ahsoka Tano stole the frigate to help them transport the slave workers in the shipyards off-world during a battle on Gwori.

The frigate was not fitted with armaments, so the Jedi were unable to fight through the blockade around the planet. They were forced to play safe; when traffic control ordered them to pass through the scanning station, they obeyed. Unfortunately Overseer Juhm, in charge of the operations on Gwori, ordered the station to activate its radiation beam, which would kill everyone on board the frigate. However, Jedi Masters Saesee Tiin and Plo Koon opened fire on the station from their interceptors, destroying it and allowing the frigate to pass safely through. Since their hyperdrive rings had been destroyed, Koon and Tiin boarded the frigate, which then flew safely to Coruscant.

A starship was utilized by a Cloud of the Nihil marauders on the planet Temerancé. The Nihil used the starship to kidnap a number of Force-sensitive children from the planet, including the Altiri Lene Kostana. The monster hunter Ty Yorrick boarded the vessel to rescue Kostana and the other children, defeating the Nihil crew. Yorrick crash-landed the ship outside the settlement where Kostana lived, returning the children home. However, after her apprentice, Drewen Qweebjillan took Yorrick's own ship on a mission, she returned to the settlement and requested the Nihil vessel. Assisted by her astromech droid R0-VR and Kostana, Yorrick repaired the Nihil ship and intended to leave Temerancé. Yorrick shortly returned to rescue Kostana from the Nihil's Children of the Storm, departing the planet to find Qweebjillan.

enrichments.description:
A lifeless planet was the site of the Jedi Mitaka's compound, where the human and several of his assistant droids resided. Within the structure, Mitaka and his assistants researched how to bring life to the planet. One day, one of the droids, T0-B1, found a skyhopper in the basement of Mitaka's compound and asked through comm if there were any Jedi present. His message reached an Inquisitor of the Galactic Empire, who landed on the lifeless world and—as T0-B1 suspected—killed Mitaka.

Shortly after, T0-B1 left Mitaka's residence and found the late Jedi's grave, putting fragments of the late Jedi's lightsaber within it. The droid resumed researching how to create life and eventually succeeded, bringing grass and rain to his homeworld. While admiring the rain with the other droids, the Inquisitor who had killed Mitaka arrived in a TIE/ad v1 to engage T0-B1, who he believed was a Jedi. The droid then reconstructed Mitaka's lightsaber and engaged the Imperial agent in a lightsaber duel, killing the Inquisitor. Soon after, T0-B1 and another droid, C03, left the planet aboard Mitaka's skyhopper, looking to populate other lifeless planets.

A settled planet was traveled to by bounty hunter Boba Fett so he could collect the bounty on criminal Bendu Fry. The son of a Twi'lek Jedi had a house here.

The planet was located near three astronomical objects, two of which were bright yellow and one of which was red. From space, the world appeared blue with streaks of white. The planet had a Type I atmosphere and a surface with plains covered in grass and trees. Clouds formed within the planet's atmosphere.

The planet had many dome-shaped buildings, some of which had spires sticking out of them. One of these buildings was the house of the Twi'lek Jedi's son, located near several buildings like it. The world also contained a cantina.

enrichments.description:
A male Jedi Knight served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars, becoming a key member of the Vaklin insurgency at the start of the Great Jedi Purge.

A Force-sensitive male, this being was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, studying under the tutelage of a Jedi Master during the Clone Wars. Serving the Order during the war as a Jedi Commander in the Grand Army of the Republic and later achieving the rank of Jedi Knight, he avoided execution during the initial stages of the Galactic Empire's ascent to power and went into hiding with his former master on Vaklin alongside Jedi Master Cho'na Bene.

A key member of the Vaklin insurgency, he watched in horror as his former master was dumped out an airlock over Shrokaan by Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader after the Master had surrendered and been taken prisoner. The Knight was taken prisoner as well and repeatedly interrogated by Vader, who claimed that he should never have been made a Knight. During an interrogation session, Vader used the Force to constrict the Jedi's heart, forcing him to reveal that Bene had holed up in the Temple of Imperfect Repose. Moments later, a band of insurgents bent on freeing the Jedi broke into the detention facility, only to be struck down by Vader and a group of stormtroopers. The Jedi managed to free himself from his restraints, but without his lightsaber he was easily killed by the Sith Lord.

The starship, piloted by Nien Nunb, was pursued by Rapier Squadron, its hyperdrive having been damaged by Commander Poe Dameron. Dameron chased the starship through the Lost Souls asteroid field, but the Resistance members disabled his T-85 X-wing to prevent him from chasing them any further. With the hyperdrive repaired, Holdo anonymously informed Dameron of the Resistance's nature before escaping into hyperspace.

enrichments.description:
At one point, an individual was a prominent Sith Lord. Centuries after his death, the Ankok cult worshiped him and the dark side of the Force while based in a city. The Sith's preserved corpse was held seated on a throne inside a structure in the settlement and was used in ceremonies by the cult. Ankok's leader, Tata, who admired the Sith Lord and viewed herself as his rightful successor, would summon tendrils that extended from the throne toward the awaiting cultists and entered their mouths.

During one gathering of the cult, Tata used the tendrils to immobilize Kako, a young woman who hated both Ankok and the dark side, and the latter person experienced a vision in which she saw the re-animated body of the Sith Lord reach out to her. At that point, the merchant Popo shot a hole into the real corpse's head with a pistol, leading to the Sith's mortal remains dissipating, not long after which Kako killed Tata with a lightsaber.

A Force-sensitive individual was at one point a major and notorious Sith Lord, a member of the Sith tradition of adherents of the dark side of the Force. Centuries after his death, human leader and messenger of the cult, admired the Sith Lord and believed herself to be the rightful successor to him and to the legacy of the Sith.

The Sith Lord's body was preserved in a towering structure in the city. It was seated in a throne that was suspended atop a pole. Ankok would use the mortal remains in a ceremony where Tata stood on a pedestal in front of the lifted seat. At a specific moment, a dark celestial body in the sky above the settlement occulted its light counterpart of the same apparent size, with the phenomenon aligning itself visually in the center of an opening in the wall of the structure behind the corpse. Directed by Tata's powers, at that point, voluminous, flesh-like tendrils began emerging from the throne and reaching toward the expectant cultists—whose mouths they then entered.

enrichments.description:
A Human male served as a Sith Lord in Dark Lord of the Sith Skere Kaan's Brotherhood of Darkness during the final years of the New Sith Wars. In 1002 BBY, the man underwent training at the Sith Academy on the planet Korriban, and was promoted with his fellow students to the rank of Sith Lord in 1000 BBY. While he was on the planet Ruusan, the man fought during the fifth battle of the Ruusan campaign and was heavily wounded after the forces of the Army of Light defeated the Sith. The Sith Lord Darth Bane, who did not participate in the battle, found the man dying and being comforted by the native Bouncers. After speaking with Bane about the preceding skirmish and the status of the Sith Order, the Sith Lord was killed when Bane used his boot to crush the man's skull against the rocks upon which he was propped.

During the New Sith Wars, in the year 1002 BBY, a Human male underwent training as an apprentice at the Sith Academy on the planet Korriban. Two years later, the man was promoted to the rank of Sith Lord in Brotherhood of Darkness, due to the increasing need for Sith Lords to combat the Jedi Order's Army of Light. He, along with most of the other apprentices at the Academy, was sent to the planet Ruusan, and eventually participated in the campaign's fifth battle, which resulted in a loss for the Brotherhood. During the conflict, the Sith Lord's lightsaber was destroyed and he was grievously injured in his stomach area, although he managed to support himself by resting on some rocks. Four Bouncers—members of a telepathic species native to Ruusan—also began projecting thoughts of peace and serenity in the injured man's mind.

The man encountered the Sith Lord Darth Bane, who had been one of his fellow students on Korriban, after the latter arrived on Ruusan near the site of the battle. Realizing that a report from Kaan stating that Bane had perished was untrue, the man expressed his delight in being able to die in what he felt was a glorious fight, a feeling with which Bane did not agree. The man tugged at Bane's heel as he turned to leave, but Bane lifted his boot and stomped the man's head in the rocks that were propping him up, revealing to the man before killing him that he had claimed the title of "Darth," which had been banned by Kaan in an attempt to prevent infighting in his organization. Bane went on to manipulate Kaan into destroying the Brotherhood of Darkness, and secretly established a new order of Sith Lords, limiting the Sith to a Master and an apprentice.

The Sith Lord was a light-skinned Human male who had a red circular tattoo which covered part of his forehead. He also had blue eyes, wore a set of Sith robes, and used a lightsaber during combat. The man believed that it was an honor to die as a result of participating in the conflict with the Jedi, and attempted to implore Bane into aiding him. In Bane's estimation, the man was so much of a lesser Sith that the former did not bother to learn the latter's name.

enrichments.description:
An Unidentified Sith Lord was present on board the Star Destroyer War Hammer during the Attack on the Hidden Temple, and acted as the Sith overseer to the crew of the War Hammer.

During the course of the battle Darth Krayt's Sith troopers arrived and began fighting, killing a large number of combatants on both sides. Also when Darth Rauder sensed the presence of Jedi younglings on a fleeing vessel, she ordered Skull Squadron to shoot it down, however Captain Gunn Yage reached a line that she would not cross and shot down Rauder instead.

Captain Yage then communicated her intentions to defect to her father Rulf Yage on board the War Hammer. The Sith Lord ordered Moff Yage to shoot his daughter down, but he had also had enough of the One Sith and decided to defect. The elder Yage pulled a blaster out and shot the Sith Lord dead. He then sent out a transmission declaring that he was joining his daughter in defecting.

A skirmish took place on a sometime after the Ronin's rupture with the Jedi clans. Amidst rain and blasterfire, a Sith known as the Ronin dueled a Jedi who would later call himself the Grand Master, near some crates and a moisture vaporator. The Ronin knocked him down onto the ground and cut off his legs and lower jaw.

The Sith blasted him for his obsession with judgment, claiming it was a denial of the balance needed between light and dark sides of the Force. The Ronin saw the young man as closer to darkness than the Sith themselves. Badly wounded, the Jedi survived and took on cybernetics, vowing revenge on his opponent. Later, the two would again meet on the planet Olcatz, where the Ronin killed the man in a duel in Tkoku Island.

enrichments.description:
At some point before 32 BBY, a starship belonging to an extra-galactic spacer was forced to land on Tatooine after colliding with an asteroid of the Dragon's Spine belt. Because of the accident, the starship was heavily damaged, but its owner managed to gather enough local Wupiupi credits to buy new parts and rebuild it. Following its refitting, the ship was equipped with a StarMark III Hyperdrive bought from Watto, a junk dealer from the Mos Espa spaceport.

Before its crash-landing on Tatooine, that starship of extra-galactic origins was equipped with a quadruple-thruster propulsion system, a pair of delta wings and a hull that looked very much like the T-06 hull manufactured by Incom Corporation. For the most part, the ship was painted in a standard gray hue, although the wings, tails and outer cockpit bore distinctive crimson markings.

However, following its forced landing, the ship was heavily damaged, and it became necessary to rebuild it from scratch with components available on Tatooine. After an extensive refitting that cost between 3,829 and 6,329 wupiupi, the ship was equipped with a StarMark III hyperdrive for hyperspace travel, three Voyager III fuel cells to store more energy, three GalaxyGuard Mk. VII shield boosters to increase the deflector shield's power, and three Polestar subZero blaster radiators to better dissipate the heat in the ship's mounted weapons. Additionally, the craft was given a brand new paint job.

In addition to the above, the starship also had to replace its original hull, its engine types, and its wings, with the spacer having chosen either the Slipstream IV hull, the T-06 hull, or the AeroMaster XI hull; the Sun-Gull 1e wing, the StarWind V wing, or the Nebula 3 wing sets; and the Thornley Space Systems-developed NovaFury MonoThrusters, the Galaxy Seven, or the Hamilton Engineering-developed Delta-C Tri-Thrusters.
