entities.name: Lowghen Badra
entities.description:
Lowghen Badra was a Human pilot and friend of the Jedi Master Niquon.

Badra worked as a technician at his shop, Badra's Engineering and Repair on the planet Yabosta. One night while at work, Niquon's Padawan, Nason Laric, arrived with the remains of an assassin droid.

Badra disassembled the droid and determined it made use of lethal Drethi venom, and that Nason should return to Skalokor with the antidote. On their way, the pair was attacked by two groups of Rodians. Badra volunteered to hold them off, laying down a wall of counter-fire so Nason could reach his Cloudjumper and escape. Immediately after, an apprentice of the Dark Jedi Von Totha appeared to eliminate the young Jedi. Laric was able to defeat the overly-confident apprentice, allowing a limping Badra to approach the hangar and return with Laric to Yabosta.

entities.name: Alexsandr Badure
entities.description:
Alexsandr Badure, also known by the nickname Trooper, was a former Imperial naval officer who in 2 BBY played a key role in the discovery of the fabled treasure of the Queen of Ranroon, the long-lost treasure ship of Xim the Despot. Once a flight instructor at the Academy of Carida, Badure was an early mentor of the future smuggler Han Solo, teaching the Corellian much of what he knew about flying and giving him the nickname "Slick."

After leaving the Imperial military, Badure fell on hard times before finding a clue to the location of the Queen of Ranroon, believing it to be somewhere on the planet Dellalt. Along with a young woman named Hasti Troujow, whom he met at a mining camp on Dellalt and with whom he shared a parental bond, Badure enlisted the help of his old friend Solo and Solo's first mate Chewbacca to uncover the treasure. After a perilous search, they eventually uncovered the haul of the Queen of Ranroon within's Xim's ancient treasure vaults, ultimately finding it to be stacks of war materiel that held little value in the present day.

A Human male, Alexsandr Badure was a long-time military man and skilled pilot who started his martial career during the last years of the Galactic Republic, seeing combat during the Twi'lek Spice Conflict, as well as the Corellian Territories Engagements and the Outer Rim Wars. While serving the Republic Military he began to serve as an instructor at the prestigious Academy of Carida, before serving as a line officer after the rise of the Galactic Empire. Badure earned several decorations in the Imperial Navy, but ultimately got in trouble for running an illegal gambling operation on his flagship, leading to his permanent reassignment as a flight instructor at Carida. Among the young pilots Badure taught at the academy was a Corellian named Han Solo, a bold and brash talent whom Badure taught almost everything he knew about flying. Badure gave Solo the nickname "Slick" after one incident during his schooling, when Solo managed a miracle landing of a malfunctioning U-33 orbital loadlifter with Badure and his entire class aboard. In exchange, Solo knew Badure by the nickname "Trooper."

Badure eventually left Imperial service to blaze his own trail in the wide galaxy, winning and spending a number of fortunes over the coming years. Badure and Solo stayed friendly, and would encounter each other again after Solo and his Wookiee partner Chewbacca entered the smuggling trade. Once, Badure saved both Solo and Chewbacca's lives during a botched Kessel spice run, earning him a life debt from the pair. Badure fell on hard times in the years to come, eventually finding himself in the Tion Hegemony, where he signed on as contract labor at a mining camp on the backwards world of Dellalt. In the squalid and dangerous conditions of the camp, Badure formed a friendship with a pair of young Human sisters, Lanni and Hasti Troujow, and the three began looking out for one another.

entities.name: Bael
entities.description:
Bael was a male Wookiee who, along with Touda, worked as a porter to Club 111, a drinking and dancing venue in the city of Depatar, in the gas giant Genarius. Bael and Touda analyzed the disguise of any prospective customer before letting him in.

At some point, Bael and Touda became indebted to Fot Ducela, a local permitor.

In 31 BBY, Bael and Touda had fun when Alec, a Jedi Knight and prospective customer of the Club, appeared disguised as an albino Wookiee Jedi. They let Alec in, even if some other people in the queue digressed about the quality of Alec's costume. Two weeks later, a team of investigators looking for the missing Alec wanted to visit the Club. As their permitor was Fot Ducela, the Wookiees let them in, paying Ducela for his previous favor.

entities.name: Baelor
entities.description:
Baelor was a male Rodian shopkeeper who operated the Baelor's Baubles and Bibelots shop in Spindlehub Square in the underworld of the planet Coruscant during the New Republic Era. He was known for his wide selection of holobooks and data-tapes, which he sold alongside numerous antiques. Although he presented himself as gruff, he softened when discussing the serial Under the Tan-Tan Sun with the human Ardent Quay, who visited his shop around 33 ABY.

Baelor sold Quay a rare holobook of the serial's last installment and secretly gave her a celestialabe with her purchase. Quay soon noticed the additional item, and upon returning to the shop, found Baelor collapsed from a blaster wound. The Rodian was shot by First Order agents in pursuit of Luke Skywalker's yellow lightsaber, which another patron, Sian Alakor, had brought to the shop. Clinging to life, Baelor pulled a hidden blaster pistol from his clothing, eliminating two of the four First Order attackers before being fatally wounded by a second blaster bolt.

entities.name: Rodin Baem
entities.description:
Rodin Baem was a Human man, who worked as a spy for the Galactic Empire during the Galactic Civil War.

Rodin Baem worked with Imperial covert operations teams as an informant and contact. He gained the confidence of Darth Vader and assisted Vader in locating several bases that were used by the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Following the formation of the New Republic, Baem continued to serve the Empire and supplied information for various Imperials, including Admiral Gaen Drommel and Moff Par Lankin. By 7 ABY, the New Republic had placed a bounty of 40,000 credits on Baem.

entities.name: Bafor
entities.description:
Bafor was a Human male and a Chief of the Wind Raider tribe on Taloraan during the Clone Wars.

In 21 BBY, two members of his clan, Jeru and Nardek, argued with Bafor over a prize—a Togruta female plucked by them from the sky when she fell. Bafor decided that the right to possess the female would be determined by a no-weapons combat between the two. Nardek quickly defeated Jeru and was going to take female as a prize. Little did he know that the female Togruta was actually a Jedi Padawan, by the name of Ahsoka Tano. With the help of the Force, she easily defeated him, after which Bafor decided that she was free to go. However, Tano attempted to convince Bafor to let his Wind Raiders join combat against the CIS forces that were trying to establish control over the planet. Bafor initially refused to help, saying that it was the matter of the Denfrandi, not the Wind Raiders. However, after the Jedi offered the Wind Raiders some supplies and goods from Taloraan City, Bafor allowed several of them to aid the Jedi.

entities.name: Baftu
entities.description:
Baftu was the leader of the Syndicat on Phindar. He was in league with Prince Beju, who had stripped his people of bacta, and was going to get some from Phindar to look like a hero to the people of Gala.

Baftu initiated his droids to kill his assistant, Terra Derida, after accusing her of stealing the Syndicat's treasury. Meanwhile, Obi-Wan Kenobi disguised himself as Prince Beju in order to expose the Syndicat's plans to the people of Phindar. When the people of Phindar got the chance to attack the Syndicat for their bacta back, Guerra Derida had Baftu jailed.

entities.name: Baggro
entities.description:
Baggro was a senior male Mon Calamari Jedi Padawan who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a Commander in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive Mon Calamari, Baggro received training in the ways of the Force at the Coruscant Jedi Temple's academy. Selected as a Padawan before the outbreak of the Clone Wars, Baggro became a Commander in the Grand Army of the Republic.

Soon after the battle at Kothlis, Padawan Baggro joined fellow apprentice Ahsoka Tano as part of Green team in a competition arranged by Jedi Master Taria Damsin. The competition, taking place in the new Sublevel Nineteen Training Dojo, ended in a tie. Baggro made it through several stages of the dojo before being defeated in the zero-gravity area. Baggro quickly exited the dojo to wait for the competition to end.

Bagitt was a Human male technician in Engine Central of Nomad City on Nkllon.

On the day of the destruction of Nomad City, he reported to Lando Calrissian the damage to drive motivators that the Empire had done during their visit. He also attempted to repair the life support systems until the evacuation order was announced.

entities.name: Gwellis Bagnoro
entities.description:
Gwellis Bagnoro was a mysterious Onodone male who rarely talked about his past. He worked as an expert forger specializing in transit documents thirty years after the Battle of Endor. He was present in the castle of the pirate Maz Kanata on the planet Takodana in 34 ABY.

Gwellis Bagnoro was born on Onod I. He was a mysterious Onodone who rarely talked about his past. At some point, Bagnoro met Han Solo.

At some point before the Galactic Civil War, Bagnoro and his protective pet barghest, Izby, lived in a cave on the planet Ogem. On Ogem, Bagnoro had the third and final droid that contained the treasure of Rane Mahal.

While Bagnoro was sleeping, Gwarm stole his valuable droid. Before he could escape, Han Solo stole it from Gwarm when Izby attacked him.

The Sullustan con artist, Dugo Bagy was solicited for information about Lando Calrissian's operations by Han Solo and Chewbacca while at Riebold's Foam and Sizzle. Bagy stated that Calrissian was mining platinum on Kerane's Folly, an asteroid in the Hoth system. This was largely a cover, however. It was primarily being used as a training ground of sorts for smugglers trying to evade Kyp Durron's Dozen-and-Two Avengers.

entities.name: Bahb
entities.description:
Bahb was a male Zeltron, who, along with three other Zeltrons—Jahn, Marruc and Rahuhl, volunteered to be attaché to Princess Leia Organa in 4 ABY. Despite Leia's dislike of Zeltrons, Admiral Ackbar felt it was essential to assign the boys to her in order to retain diplomatic ties to their homeworld. Bahb and the other Zeltrons were delighted to work with Leia, of whom they'd heard many stories, and well as Han Solo—although they initially mistook him for Lando Calrissian.

Their first assignment was to a diplomatic party on Kabray. Unfortunately, the Nagai had targeted the gathering as an opportunity to hamstring the Alliance, and captured the entire party and Leia's newly arrived group. Trapped in a room, the four Zeltrons devised a plan, hoisting Jahn up to the ceiling where he jumped on an incoming Nagai guard. The Zeltrons then turned the tables on the Nagai raiding party, capturing them all and turning their guns on them. Their fierce efforts impressed both Han and Leia, who began to warm up to the Zeltrons. Their efforts were also noticed by the Nagai leadership who would later target their homeworld.

Returning to Endor with their captured prisoners, Bahb and the Zeltrons handed them over for interrogation. They were there when the invading Nagai fleet came out of hyperspace, and were the first to detect them with Leia. Bahb and Jahn then ran off to find and warn Luke Skywalker in the forest. After warning him and returning to the tracking station to watch the fighter squadrons engaged in space, the four Zeltrons were unexpectedly caught up in a ground battle against a force of Maccabrees and Nagai who had sneaked onto the moon's surface. After repelling the first warrior, many more arrived, one grabbing Bahb around the neck. Only the timely arrival of Luke Skywalker who discovered the Maccabree's weakness, saved the lives of the Zeltrons. They then evacuated Endor along with the rest of the Alliance.

Having fled Endor, Bahb and the Zeltron boys also took part in the Battle of Zeltros. The planet had in part been identified as a target due to their efforts on Kabray. During the battle they were captured by the Tofs who mistakenly identified them as important Alliance commanders. They were then imprisoned on the Tof flagship Merriweather . Luke Skywalker, teamed up with Hoojibs and Hiromi, led a successful mission to rescue them.

entities.description:
Bahima was a male Bith bartender in the Iziz cantina during the Onderon Civil War. In 3951 BBY, he owned S-0D3-GE3, and assisted Meetra Surik during her investigation of Captain Sullio's murder. According to some of his patrons, Bahima had an ever-growing problem with keeping his droids activated and on his property.

If Surik has fallen far down the dark side, Bahima will mention that the Bith have excellent skin creams that can make Surik look like a Human in their prime.

The husband of Bahlea was a Twi'lek male who was a member of the Pilgrims on the planet Tython. The father of Rusa, Bahlea's husband went in search of manka cat teeth in hopes of healing his ailing daughter, but he was killed by Flesh Raiders.

According to the conversation files for Star Wars: The Old Republic, Bahlea's husband was originally planned to be a Mirialan.

entities.description:
Hagk Baht was a Duros smuggler who owned and operated the Singing Savrip during the height of the Galactic Civil War.

Baht attempted to smuggle blasters to agents of the Rebel agents on Tatooine aboard his ship, Singing Savrip. In the process, he narrowly avoided an Imperial customs blockade. An incredibly violent sandstorm at the rendezvous point, however, caused Baht to crash outside of Anchorhead. He was killed in the crash, but the fifty blaster rifles he was transporting remained intact.

entities.name: Bailie
entities.description:
Bailie was a Human male officer who served Galactic Empire during the Galactic Empire. Sometime following the Battle of Yavin, Captain Bailie was assigned to an Imperial space station in the Outer Rim Territories, along with Lieutenant Alin, Captain Clough, Warrant Officer Snopell, Lieutenant Farin, Colonel Sheray and Major Taison. an Imperial-class Star Destroyer captured a passenger freighter on suspicion of harboring criminals. Several spacers were apprehended and taken to the Imperial Space station. After the spacers were released, Captain Bailie processed them through the space station until they left the station.

Bailie was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts,

Captain Bailie was added to the game when the developers revamped the "New Player Tutorial" with the release of the "Publish 17," on May 26, 2005. Throughout the tutorial, Bailie and other Imperial officers directed new players through a space station in order to help them get accustomed to the game mechanics. However, Bailie was removed alongside with this tutorial when the developers introduced a completely new tutorial with the release of the "New Game Enhancements," on November 15, 2005.

entities.name: Civius Bain
entities.description:
Civius Bain was a male Rodian ryll smuggler who lived on Corellia during the time of the Galactic Civil War. He was the son of Olivia Bain.

Civius Bain resided on Corellia with his mother Olivia Bain and his fater, an accountant. After the Battle of Yavin, the young man got indebted to the spice smugglers Jaryn Minoze and Oret Sturm, two members of the ryll smuggling ring of the Chirq Council in Kor Vella. Civius Bain was forced to work for the smugglers in the Ryll Smuggler Base where they refined their ryll. His mother was desperate and wished for him to leave the smuggling ring and come home.

In 1 ABY, Olivia Bain met a spacer in the Vella plains and begged to rescue her son. The spacer accepted and headed to the Ryll Smuggler Base. The spacer found Civius Bain in the bunker but the young man explained that he could not leave the smuggling ring since he was still indebted to the smugglers. The spacer therefore killed both Jaryn Minoze and Oret Sturm, allowing Civius to finally escape. After that, Civius Bain decided to start a new life and become an accountant like his father.

Civius Bain was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, Civius Bain was added to the game with the update named "Chapter 1: The Corellian Captives," published on June 8, 2006.

entities.name: Bairn
entities.description:
Bairn was a young Human male, born and raised on the planet Ceriun about 1000 BBY.

Bairn was one of several youths who assisted Tenno steal a Holocron from the community elders after a Jedi starship crashed near their village. When the elders met to debate the matter of the holocron, Tenno and his friends armed themselves and appeared at the meeting. A brawl broke out, in which several of the adults were killed. The fight was interrupted by the appearance of a Sith Lord, who seized the holocron and departed. When Tenno tried to explain that he and his friends had kept the artifact safe for the Sith, the Sith Lord attacked and killed several of them with his lightsaber.

entities.name: Baiuntu
entities.description:
Baiuntu was a male Ansionian and a non-traditional Alwari tribesman who was the chief trader of a Qulun clan on the planet Ansion. In 22 BBY he had Jedi Masters Luminara Unduli and Obi-Wan Kenobi, their Padawans Anakin Skywalker and Barriss Offee, and their Ansionian guides Kyakhta and Bulgan drugged and held captive. He was later killed by a shanh pack during a skirmish in the Qulun camp.

Baiuntu was an obese male Ansonian of the Alwari tribes who acted as chief trader of a Qulun clan on Ansion. In 22 BBY, Jedi Masters Luminara Unduli and Obi-Wan Kenobi, along with their Padawans Anakin Skywalker and Barriss Offee, and several local companions encountered a Qulun patrol led by Baiuntu while they were searching for the Borokii, the ruling Alwari overclan. As the Qulun were always keen on company, Baiuntu invited the group to return to their camp to dine with them, an offer the Jedi accepted.

After being shown around the camp, the Jedi and their companions were brought into a large portable "trade room" structure, where they were invited to sample various goods offered by the Qulun. After they'd done so, and had been entertained by lightwick sculptures and dance pixies, the Jedi and Baiuntu discussed politics: Baiuntu felt that the Qulun had benefited from Ansion's membership in the Galactic Republic. He later invited the group to sample various intoxicating essences, including Paluruvu, which contained a powerful sedative that rendered unconscious the Jedi and their companions—along with Baiuntu, who had willingly inhaled the essence. Baiuntu later admitted the drugging was carried out because of the bossban Soergg-issued promise of a large reward to those who could delay the group's return to Cuipernam. However, the Jedi and their companions were freed by Tooqui (by way of a lorqual stampede) prior to a skirmish in the Qulun camp.

Baiuntu, while attempting to pursue the Jedi, was killed by a rabbidly agitated shanh pack shortly thereafter.

entities.name: Baj
entities.description:
Prince Baj was a human male royal during the Imperial Era.

Baj was a young man who in 3 BBY, who embarked on the maiden voyage of the luxury train Exas Jewell on the planet Tyegin. On board the train, he took part in a high-stakes, invitation-only sabacc game with the Fosh D'Lina, the reptilian Rakan, and Lando Calrissian who was impersonating the train's designer, Shen Kanton. Calrissian, who had won the game, tried to depart with his winnings, but was stopped by Rakan and D'Lina who expressed surprise as Kanton was supposed to ride until the end of the trip. This discussion upset Baj, who demanded that they either play another hand or leave. However, the card game was interrupted by pirates, who stole Calrissian's winnings and valuables from the guests in the train car. The pirates also damaged the train before making their escape.

With the train out of control, Calrissian led the other guests of the premier-class train car in unhooking the engine car and disrupting the magnetic link in order to slow it down using the furniture from the train. Baj tried to help by throwing the dealer droid into the pile but was stopped by Calrissian. As the train's magnetic field was disrupted, the train jerked, throwing Baj from the front of the train. Calrissian caught his arm and pulled him back in. Eventually Tyegin's law enforcement responded to the situation and the guests were rescued.

Baj was a small male human who had blonde hair, black eyes and tanned skin. He was a wealthy royal and wore a white dress suit, with a red sash and cummerbund and gold epaulettes. He was petulant and demanding.

entities.name: Baji
entities.description:
Baji was a male Ho'Din healer who mainly worked in the rain-forests of Yavin 4. He always spoke in rhyme, and, like almost all his species, he was a botanist. He was very peaceful but loathed the Empire. In 5 ABY, Baji met Luke Skywalker, who was searching for the Lost City of the Jedi, and Ken, who was fleeing the city. Later Trioculus arrived, searching for the city on Kadann's orders, and captured Baji. He forced him to help heal the new Emperor's blindness. Baji was forced to remain in Imperial service, serving as a staff physician. Nevertheless, at some point he made it to Barenth, where he continued his botanical research.

Baji lived in a hut buried within Yavin 4's rain-forests. His hut had very little in it, only containing a bed made out of leaves and a table with a few chairs. He would collect plant species he feared might go extinct, and when a ship came from Moltok, he would send his collection off with them for other botanists to study.

Luke Skywalker met Baji while seeking the Lost City of the Jedi. Into this encounter arrived Ken and DJ-88, both of whose presence proved temporary. Baji and Ken later met again when the Empire set the forest afire during its own search for the Lost City. Ken offered Baji shelter in the City, but Baji refused—one of Moltok's transports was scheduled to arrive the next day. This rejection ultimately proved unwise as stormtroopers soon came to arrest the Ho'Din healer, desiring him to cure the ersatz emperor Trioculus' blindness. Certain seeds were necessary to effect the cure. Baji was then drafted, at gunpoint, into the Empire as Trioculus' personal physician.

The next day, desiring to learn more about healing agents, he visited the planet Barenth, which was home to a series of unique healing plants. Discovering an ancient laboratory, he chose to explore it. He found his healing plants at last but only as an groundquake struck. He gathered some plants and left. Later he would came back only to find it in a heaping pile of rubble—on the surface at least. The plants were not destroyed; however, they were contaminated. Baji was forced to make a decision—to leave the planet with the plants that he had initially found or stay on Barenth and do what he could to help. He would eventually decide to stay and cure the contaminated plants.

entities.name: Jhaka Bakarn's father
entities.description:
The father of Jhaka Bakarn was a Human male native to the planet Corellia several generations before the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. A member of the prestigious Bakvalen family, the Bakvalen patriarch was furious when his eldest daughter Jhaka turned her back on her life as a Corellian noble and joined the Republic Navy as a starfighter pilot. Her father disowned her, leading Jhaka to change her surname to the more common "Bakarn," and the man's daughter went on to become a renowned fighter ace. When Jhaka was killed in battle against a dangerous warlord, her father was overcome with pride and grief, and he changed the family's name to Bakarn in her honor.

Jhaka Bakarn's father was mentioned in the Codex entry for the Bakvalen family in Star Wars: The Old Republic, a video game released by BioWare in 2011.

entities.name: Syo Bakarn
entities.description:
Syo Bakarn was a Human male Corellian Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a healer during the Great Galactic War against the resurgent Sith Empire. Following the Treaty of Coruscant, Master Bakarn relocated to Tython where he served as a member of the Jedi High Council during the Cold War. However, Bakarn himself was unaware that he was host to a second personality, the First Son of the Sith Emperor.

Syo Bakarn was a Force-sensitive Human male Bakarn was born during a time of turmoil, as the Galactic Republic was engaged in the Great Galactic War with the resurgent Sith Empire, led by the enigmatic Sith Emperor. Seeking to further his power base, the Sith Emperor decided to create a group of personal sleeper agents called "Children of the Emperor." The Emperor's agents, Servants of the clandestine organization Emperor's Hand, scoured the galaxy for Force-sensitive beings suited for their Master's needs. Like many infants from many different species, Bakarn was spirited away from his family on Corellia and he was taken to the Sith Academy on the planet Korriban to undergo training in a specialized group. For weeks, Bakarn and the other children underwent various rituals and processes inside the Academy, until eventually Bakarn was chosen to be the first individual to be inducted into the ranks of the Children of the Emperor. The young Bakarn was granted a personal audience with the Sith Emperor, whereupon he was infused with the Emperor's strength and was bound to his mind and will, becoming the Emperor's First Son. The First Son was essentially another persona created inside Bakarn's mind, who was unaware of its existence. A master strategist, the First Son would lay dormant inside the labyrinths of Bakarn's mind, waiting for the Emperor's command to awaken and do his Master's bidding.

After his initiation, Bakarn was returned by the Emperor's Hand to his parents, as eventually were the other Children. Thus, a network of sleeper agents was spread by the Sith Emperor throughout both the Republic and his own Sith Empire. As long as the First Son lived, the Children were undetectable by the galaxy at large. Having no memories of his experiences at the Sith Academy and unaware of the second personality inside him, Bakarn continued to live with his parents on Corellia. He and his father at one point took a walk in Axial Park, when his father told him about their family's proud past. Eventually, Bakarn's Force-sensitivity was discovered by the Jedi Order. He was taken from his homeworld and trained in the ways of the Force, becoming a Padawan to a Jedi Master. During his time as a Padawan, Bakarn gained recognition after he saved his Master from an attack by a Mandalorian Jedi hunter. Eventually attaining the rank of Jedi Knight and studying as a Consular, Bakarn focused his studies on his healing skills, eventually becoming a noted healer.

entities.description:
Bakash was a male Human who served as a colonel in the Imperial Army of the Sith Empire during the Cold War with the Galactic Republic. In 3643 BBY, Bakash and the men he commanded were stationed on the Sith world of Korriban where they were sent to the Lower Wilds region. There they were driven mad by an unknown force and became hostile to their former allies. Bakash was killed, along with his men by a Sith apprentice who was sent to wipe out the insane soldiers.

entities.name: Bakishan
entities.description:
Bakishan was a male Twi'lek constable for the Tatooine city of Anchorhead during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire.

Bakishan lived on Tatooine during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire.A constable for the city of Anchorhead, he was stymied by a string of robberies. The thieves had even stolen the state-of-the-art police surveillance holocameras that he had set up to catch them.

He asked a Republic-allied individual to help stop the group, which Bakishan suspected was actually a group of astromech droids. Astromech droids had been seen at every robbery, and no one was able to identify the thieves themselves. The individual recovered a transmitter from one of the droids and followed the trail to Izink, a Jawa outside of Anchorhead. The individual convinced the Jawa to turn himself in to Bakishan, ending the string of thefts.

Bakishan was created for Star Wars: The Old Republic, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game released by BioWare on December 20, 2011. He gives Republic players the Tatooine mission "Astromenace", where Bakishan asks the player to investigate a string of robberies.

entities.name: Bakkar
entities.description:
Bakkar, nicknamed "the Butcher," was a human who owned the restaurant Ronto Roasters in Black Spire Outpost on the planet Batuu. A big fan of podracing, Bakkar originally hailed from the planet Tatooine and came from a family that worked as butchers for four generations. Bakkar opened his restaurant with the goal of bringing his famous ronto meat to new customers after moving to Batuu with his droid, 8D-J8.

Bakkar had an unusual way of grilling his meats, utilizing a podracer engine that he purchased and modified. In 34 ABY, 8D-J8's reprogramming that was intended to make the droid man the grill had the side effect of him talking too much; in order to solve the issue, Bakkar contacted the Utai Mubo—8D-J8's original programmer—who eventually agreed to help fix the droid.

Bakkar was a fourth-generation butcher who grew up on the planet Tatooine, where his family's specialty was the ronto creature. He was a big fan of the podracing sport even after it was outlawed across the galaxy. He sold different kinds of specialty meats, but like his family, he was largely known for ronto. He left Tatooine when he came of age, dreaming of selling his family's famous meat on another Outer Rim Territories planet. Once he had earned enough credits, he bought a smelter droid, 8D-J8, who was later designated as a pitmaster droid. 8D-J8 never left his side.

Bakkar traveled to the Outer Rim planet Batuu, where he bought a podracing engine from Savi & Son Salvage at a fair price that he could use to cook his meats. With his ronto recipe ready to go, he opened a restaurant called Ronto Roasters in the Black Spire Outpost settlement in order to bring the ronto to new customers. Bakkar built a large, elaborate mechanical grill, with 8D-J8 serving as the pitmaster of the restaurant, as Bakkar had had the Utai droid scrapper Mubo reprogram him so that his sole duty was to turn the spit, making sure that the meat was cooked evenly and well.

Bakken was a male Snivvian, who worked as a Rebel privateer during the Galactic Civil War.

Bakken joined the Alliance to Restore the Republic, working as an "alien cultures consultant" for Alliance Sector Command in the Zaric sector. However, after he had worked for them for a few years, he decided that he instead wanted to be a privateer. Bakken's superiors tried to dissuade him from pursuing his new career, so they reluctantly let him go. He survived two cruises and returned with some cargo, to make a contribution to the Alliance.

entities.description:
Bakku was a male Reigat, who was a member of Sleeper Cell V-16 for the Alliance to Restore the Republic during the Galactic Civil War.

Bakku lived in Downside, a slum area in Fabrillan, the capital city of the planet Malthor. He worked as strong man for a local gang leader there and also carried out duties as a bouncer at her bar. Around 0 BBY he was the muscle for Sleeper Cell V-16, a Rebel Alliance sleeper cell.

Bakku was quiet, intimidating and anti-social. He joined the Alliance because they let him be that way, rather than imposing rules and regulations onto him, like the Galactic Empire did.

Bakku was a fearsome combatant with exceptional strength and skill in hand-to-hand combat. He was also well skilled in a variety of weaponry, including blasters, grenades, and melee weapons.

entities.description:
Bakmar was a male Selkath who lived during the Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. He sold his wares in the Republic Concourse of the Mercantile Plaza. While working he wore the blue and white robes of an adherent of the Order of Shasa, a Force-sensitive organization based on Manaan. Orloth's hairless skin was brown in color and his eyes were orange. When speaking to customers he spoke in a language other than Basic.

Bakmar was created as a character for Star Wars: The Old Republic, an MMORPG released by BioWare in 2011, although he was not added to the game until update 2.9 in 2014. The update added the planet Manaan as a location to the game as a setting for the new "Depths of Manaan" flashpoint, which Bakmar served as the Republic flashpoint vendor for, with Orloth as his counterpart for Sith Empire players. He accepts only Manaan research data as payment for his inventory, a currency earned only by playing through the flashpoint.

entities.name: Herosk Bal'far
entities.description:
Herosk Bal'far was a male Bothan who lived during the time of the Galactic Civil War. Sometime following the Battle of Yavin in 0 BBY, Pooja Naberrie tasked a spacer with locating Bal'far and escorting him back to the city of Dee'ja Peak on Naboo. Although the spacer was attacked by Imperial Army troopers and stormtroopers, Naberrie's mission was completed.

Herosk Bal'far was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, prior to its closure on December 15, 2011.

Players who performed a series of quests for Pooja Naberrie had to locate Bal'far and escort him safely back to Dee'ja Peak. However, due to a bug, many of the NPCs in Naberrie's quests were not properly sequenced. For instance, in the quest to escort Bal'far, players actually encountered an individual known as Jumis, who was supposed to appear in the following quest. The character model for Herosk Bal'far likewise erroneously spawned for Naberrie's sixth and final quest, in which the player was supposed to encounter an individual named Melloc Fitzal. Nevertheless, it was possible for the player to complete the mission and advance to the next quest. This article assumes that the content of Naberrie's quest dialogue is canon in the Star Wars Legends continuity, and that Bal'far, not Jumis, actually appeared during her second quest.

Furthermore, because Herosk Bal'far spawned under the generic "noble" template, his appearance was randomized under one of forty-two possible depictions. Species Bal'far could appear as included Bothans, Humans, Rodians, Trandoshans, Twi'leks, and Zabrak under either gender. Because the quest dialogue identified Bal'far as a male Bothan, this article assumes that the randomly generated male Bothan depiction is canon in the Star Wars Legends continuity. The questline that involved Bal'far was eventually removed from the game when Pooja Naberrie was relocated to Theed as part of the newly introduced Legacy Quest, released as part of Publish 25's New Game Enhancements on November 15, 2005.

entities.name: Bala-Tik
entities.description:
Bala-Tik was a human male who worked as a negotiator for the Guavian Death Gang. He handled a deal with the famed smuggler Han Solo by paying for Solo to haul rathtars, a deal that Solo also made with Kanjiklub.

The human male Bala-Tik served the criminal Guavian Death Gang and frontman during the reign of the New Republic. During his time with the gang, he encountered the smuggler Han Solo and managed to shake several profitable leads out of him, Bala-Tik was on the planet Kaddak on the forty-fifth level of the city known as the Sliver with three Guavian security soldiers.

Sometime after Supreme Leader Snoke's assumption of leadership within the First Order, he obtained the Smuggler's Guide previously owned by Gamma-bit 669753 from spoils of battle between Guavian Death Gang and Droid Gotra. In the book he wrote about the capabilities of the Guavian security soldiers and his own process of mechamorphosis that started with his cybernetic leg. Then he wrote how their security soldiers intercepted binary transmission from the Droid Gotra, that ordered members of Gotra and Cyban Front to strike high-value data caches on Terminus, Little Petrovi, and Corbett Cluster. Guavians then broadcast their own counteracting broadcast, that ordered to position soldiers to intercept them. Later in the book he described their plan to launch a strike on Nantoon to rule over the galaxy's underworld. However, the gang lost the Smuggler's Guide to the lieutenant Razoo Qin-Fee of the Kanjiklub during the skirmish in the Cronese Mandate.

While in the Sliver, the Guavians were approached by four members of Kanjiklub, Tasu Leech, had overheard the protocol droid C-3PO mention that Solo had borrowed money from the Guavian Death Gang, and revealed to Bala-Tik that the smuggler had also borrowed fifty thousand credits from Kanjiklub to hunt rathtar. The two groups of criminals found common ground in their hatred of Solo and agreed to confront him together over his debts, with Leech and Bala-Tik shaking hands on the agreement.

entities.name: Balahteez
entities.description:
Balahteez was a Pho Ph'eahian spice smuggler who was captured by the Galactic Empire and transported to Despayre. Balahteez developed numerous information contacts over the years, many of whom ended up on Despayre with him. He lived in Slashtown Prison Colony.

While being pursued by an Imperial patrol near Gall, Balahteez jettisoned his illegal cargo, which was packed inside a block of carbonite the size of a luggage trunk. The carbonite had been pulled down into Gall's gravity well and accidentally hit a barracks housing a large unit of TIE/LN starfighter mechanics. The impact punched a hole into the outer hull large enough to form a crater thirty meters wide in diameter, killing fifty mechanics immediately, and another thirty who were sucked out into hard vacuum during the explosive decompression. The hole was so large that another twelve mechanics who survived the initial blast and the decompression died from a lack of air before emergency droids could seal the barracks.

entities.name: Balam
entities.description:
Balam was a male figure in the religion of the Gungan species on the planet Naboo. According to legend, Balam was the first Gungan warrior, and upon his death he was taken by Oma-Oma, the chief of the Gungan guds, to the underwater city of Ossorus. Oma-Oma granted Balam immortality and turned him into the god of battles so that he could teach the other guds the art of war.

Balam went on to create the hidden paradise Otoh-D'in in the swamps of Naboo. There, the bravest Gungan militiagungs would arrive after their deaths and spend eternity distracting themselves with combat and strategy games. If Ossorus ever came under attack, the warriors of Otoh-D'in would defend it.

Balam was mentioned in the French edition of the 2001 LucasArts video game Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds in the Gungan DataBank entry.

entities.name: Baldarek
entities.description:
"Red Eye" Baldarek was a Chiss bartender who worked in Baruk's Bar on Nar Shaddaa during the Empire Reborn conflict.

Prior to the Clone Wars, Baldarek worked as a bartender in the galaxy. As the Chiss were an unusual sight in the wider galaxy, he picked up the nickname "Red-Eye", after his distinctive glowing eyes. During this period, Baldarek visited the pleasure world of Zeltros, in the Inner Rim. He partied there for a week, becoming mesmerized by the scent of Zeltron pheromones. Some of his recollections of his time there made it into the tourist guide, "Luxury on the Inner Rim."

Much later, Baldarek was employed by Reelo Baruk, a Rodian crime lord on Nar Shaddaa. He worked in Baruk's Bar, a cantina frequented by Baruk's thugs. In 12 ABY, Kyle Katarn visited the bar while trying to track down Baruk. Recommending a ruby bliel to Katarn, the Jedi instead asked for a Corellian ale. The grimy nature of the bar also prompted Katarn to specify a clean glass.

When Katarn sought information on Baruk's whereabouts from Baldarek, the bartender lured him into a trap by keeping his attention away from a group of thugs who were about to attack Katarn. The bartender succeeded in this role and activated a metal shield to seal the area behind the bar for protection. The attackers, however, were less successful and all died at the blade of Katarn's lightsaber. Katarn then unsealed the bar and threatened the bartender, who revealed Baruk's location. Katarn eventually tracked down Baruk and killed him.

Bale was a male individual who was native the planet Veroleem, in the Unknown Regions. Bales was a member of a resistance cell that opposed the Cult of Veroleem, a religious sect that ruled the planet, and the cultists eventually captured Bale and imprisoned him in a jail in the city New Promise. After spending some time in the institution, Bale encountered a group of spacers that had also been imprisoned there and he and the spacers co-operated to stage a jailbreak. Bale then led the spacers to a safe-house that the resistance maintained in New Promise.

entities.name: Balek
entities.description:
Balek was a male Human Acolyte of the reconstituted Sith Empire. He was the twin brother of Wydr.

During the Cold War, Balek and Wydr attended the Sith Academy on Korriban. During their trials, Balek and Wydr were called to meet with Overseer Harkun, who told them that they would never become Sith or beat Ffon due to how weak they were. However, if Balek and Wydr were to kill another acolyte, they would earn the right to go home. Balek didn't like the idea, however his brother believed that this would be the only way for the two brothers to leave the academy alive.

After the acolyte entered the training room, Balek and Wydr cornered the acolyte. Since he liked them, Balek apologized to the acolyte, explaining that he and Wydr had to do this in order to earn their freedom. Both of the brothers immediately engaged the acolyte, but the acolyte eventually defeated them.

entities.description:
Espan Balfed was a Lord of the noble Balfed family.

Before the rise of the Galactic Empire, the Balfed family was one of the great families in galactic society. They lost their influence and prestige and were disgraced when the rival House of Tagge framed them.

Lord Espan Balfed was the youngest descendant of the House of Balfed, but was considered a noble in title only. He had no money, political influence or significant fame and was the Captain of a small customs frigate.

Despite his reduced status the nobleman always informed a ship's crew of his lineage before inspecting a vessel. Whether the trader showed the proper respect greatly influenced the level and intensity of the inspection.

Balig was a smuggler who worked for Talon Karrde for many years. He was a turbolaser gunner on Wild Karrde during the Raid on Bilbringi.

During the Wild Karrde journey to Exocron to find the ex-smuggler Jorj Car'das, he and Chal manned the turbolasers as the crew blasted their way into Pembric II through the asteroids. He remained on the turbolasers during the battle with Rei'Kas's Corsair's on the way to Dayark, along with Griv and Shada D'ukal. He also was one of those undercover at the Ithor Loman while Karrde, Shada and C-3PO met with General Jutka.

Balig was verbose and liked to tell anecdotes even during combat, much to Karrde's annoyance. He was a skilled gunner.

He would wear flight coveralls and high spacer's boots. He wore a blaster pistol in a cross-draw holster.

entities.description:
Balisk was a male Human and a member of the Knights of Zakuul. He and his husband lived on Zakuul, and in 3631 BBY he was assigned as the replacement partner for the Knight Novo, whose previous partner Tanek had died during the pursuit of the Outlander. Novo was determined to hunt down the Outlander for Tanek's death, and so the pair tracked down the Outlander at the Razor in Breaktown and tried to arrest the fugitive, only to be defeated.

Balisk appears at the Razor encounter regardless of player choices. The Outlander can kill Novo and Balisk for dark side points or spare them for light side points. If spared, Balisk will send an encrypted e-mail to the Outlander, thanking him for sparing him and letting him return to his husband.

entities.description:
Xin Baliss was a Human male who served as a member of House Baliss, a noble family that remained neutral throughout the war between the Galactic Republic and the reconsituted Sith Empire.

After the smuggler known as Ace stole a datapad from the Baliss estate to allow House Teraan to regain their lost fortune. Xin Baliss was sent by his father, Duke Baliss, to exact vengeance against House Teraan by challenging Lenn to a blaster duel to the death. As Lenn had never mastered the blaster, he and his sister Cedonia persuaded Ace to stand as their champion. Xin impatiently waited for the Teraan's champion in their quarters at House Organa. Upon meeting Ace, he was very dismissive of the offworlder. When they began fighting, Xin believed that he could beat Ace, but he was immediately defeated.

When the Baliss estate was overrun by Killiks, Yun decided to capitalize on the chaos engulfing Alderaan and make the Teraan estate the new Baliss home.

After the smuggler known as Ace stole a datapad from the Baliss estate to allow House Teraan to regain their lost fortune, the Duke sent his son Xin Baliss to exact vengeance against House Teraan by challenging Lenn Teraan to a blaster duel to the death. As Lenn had never mastered the blaster, he and his sister Cedonia persuaded Ace to stand as their champion, who defeated Xin in the duel.

entities.name: Jonas Balkar
entities.description:
Jonas Balkar was a male Human who served the Galactic Republic as a member of the Republic Strategic Information Service during the Cold War against the Sith Empire.

While stationed on Nar Shaddaa, Balkar received a message from General Elin Garza of Republic Special Forces Division, requesting his assistance in tracking down rogue droid M1-4X. Balkar met Havoc's commanding officer in a cantina and told the lieutenant that Forex was being used to rob a bank. Havoc's commander set out and tried to stop Forex, and Balkar tapped into the bank's security holos, though he could not receive audio. After Havoc's commander defeated a team of soldiers, Balkar contacted the lieutenant and asked who the soldiers had been. Though Garza had ordered the lieutenant not to tell anyone, the lieutenant told Balkar that they were Special Forces soldiers who had defected. After Balkar helped the lieutenant defeat Forex, he had his technicians reprogram Forex to serve as a new member of Havoc Squad. He then called General Garza, angry at not having been told about the defections. Garza reprimanded the lieutenant and told Balkar that he hadn't needed to know.

Later, Havoc's lieutenant, along with sergeant Aric Jorgan, met Balkar in the same cantina on Nar Shaddaa and asked for his help finding the Deadeyes, Jorgan's old squad. Balkar was told he was not allowed to assist, though he covertly told the lieutenant that he could look in the Imperial prison on Nar Shaddaa. When the lieutenant and Jorgan returned, Senior Agent Zane of the SIS was in the middle of reprimanding Balkar. When Havoc claimed responsibility for the prison break, Zane advised them from further interference in getting the Deadeyes back by peaceful means. When Zane left, Balkar asked Havoc why they have to get him in trouble. Havoc's CO explained that they have coordinates to where the Deadeyes were shipped to decrypt. Balkar decline to aid them again with Zane breathing over his neck, but he did refer Jorgan to a contact in Signal Intelligence, but Zane later interfered.

Afterward, Balkar was stationed on Tatooine when a Republic agent crashed there, and he directed Havoc's commander, now promoted to captain, to the crash site. When the captain and his team rescued the agent, they were informed of a secret Imperial weapon called the Gauntlet, and Garza ordered Havoc to destroy it. When that had been done, Balkar sent the captain—now promoted to major—a letter congratulating him on the Gauntlet's destruction.

entities.description:
Balkin was a Human Balkin attended a strategy session aboard the Imperial I-class Star Destroyer Admonitor over the planet Quethold. During the session, he discussed alien warlord Nuso Esva's remaining forces and Quethold's native Quesoth species with Stromma Council Liaison Nyama, who insulted the bald man after he asked if the Quesoth Midli caste was loyal to their Queen. As Balkin and Thrawn had promised that the stormtroopers of the 501st would be able to defeat the Quesoth Soldiers—which Nyama considered impossible—the liaison withdrew the Stromma from the Empire's service.

Shortly after, Imperial Line Lieutenant Dramos Sanjin commented to Stromma stormtrooper Puriv that Imperial Senior Captain Voss Parck would kill them both if Balkin did not hear that Puriv and Sanjin had not followed Nyama's directive before him. Shortly after, Thrawn launched an attack on Quethold's Red City in an attempt to kill Esva, during which Balkin reported to the Grand Admiral that Sanjin had lost two of his men.

Balko was a male Human lieutenant of the reconstituted Sith Empire living during the Galactic War. At some point he became part of the Order of Revan and defected from the Empire, joining with the Revanite forces on Rishi's Sky Ridge Island under command of Lord Ivress. However, after learning the Revanites' goal he realized his mistake and began working against them. He asked an Imperial infiltrating their camp to use the provided access codes to purge the Revanites' databanks.

Lieutenant Balko appears in Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan expansion, released on December 2, 2014.

On Coruscant, he worked out of the Equipment Requisitions area of the Senate Commercial District where he trained Republic troopers.

Ballard first appeared in the MMORPG Star Wars: The Old Republic, released by BioWare in 2011, as a class trainer for the trooper class. He is only accessible to Republic players in the game as he is found on Coruscant which is a Republic-only planet.

entities.name: Corwin Ballast
entities.description:
Corwin Ballast was a male native of the Outer Rim world Mordal who lived on the world with his wife, Lynnta, and his daughter. In 4 ABY, Ballast and his family became trapped in a firefight between rebels and Imperial forces. He and Lynnta attempted to rescue their daughter, who had become immobilized amidst the fighting. However, by the end of the ensuing fighting, Ballast's wife and daughter had been killed.

Wanting to bring the memories of his family somewhere war would never reach, Ballast traveled to the planet Jakku and settled there. He became a bartender at Ergel's Bar, a local establishment. In 5 ABY, Ballast met the travelers Rae Sloane and Brentin Wexley while working in the bar, unenthused by the former's request for information. Super Star Destroyers arrived in Jakku's atmosphere during their meeting, deeply saddening Ballast.

The male individual Corwin Ballast lived on his homeworld, world Mordal, during the Imperial Era. Ballast; his wife, Lynnta; and their daughter settled in his hometown, the city Maborn, during the Galactic Civil War. While in Maborn he and his family were caught in a battle between Imperial forces and rebels and sheltered behind crates. Ballast attempted to assist Lynnta in rescuing their immobilized daughter from the middle of a street, running out from behind their cover. The man saw his wife get hit with blasterfire and then was struck himself. While unconscious, he was transported to a crawler and treated with healing bacta. Several weeks after the battle, an injured Ballast woke up in the crawler and mourned the loss of his daughter and wife after learning they had died and were buried. Grieved, he kept a picture of his family in his boot to remind him of their memory.

Ballast left Mordal to travel to Jakku, a location he considered desolate enough for war never to reach. On his way to the world, Ballast acquired a HyCor laser repeater to defend himself. After arriving at the Tuanul settlement on Jakku, he bought a dilapidated speeder from a few local anchorites, paying them more than he owed as a gesture of apathetic charity. Ballast disembarked his speeder and surveyed the terrain around him, deciding that he liked the world's bleak surroundings. A rag-man then attempted to intimidate the newly arrived Ballast, but the Mordal native quickly brandished his laser repeater and waved off the rag-man's threat.

entities.name: Hammond Ballater
entities.description:
Hammond Ballater was a male criminal. He was a member of the Black Sun syndicate on Corellia before he left the organization to work for Shalera the Hutt.

Even though Hammond Ballater left Black Sun, the criminal organization never let their members go completely. Sometime following 0 BBY, he was approached by Grobber, the Twi'lek subordinate of Zekka Thyne, who demanded certain information from him. When Ballater refused to cooperate with Black Sun, Grobber sent a well armed individual to find Ballater and bring him back to Coronet, the capital of Corellia. The individual was attacked by two thugs who were attempting to defend Ballater, but they were killed by Grobber's mercenary. Ballater then surrendered, as he did not want the situation to get even worse.

Hammond Ballater was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, prior to its closure on December 15, 2011. Due to the nature of many older quests in Star Wars Galaxies, the appearance of various characters could change each time a player performed the quest. Therefore, the canonical species of Ballater remains unidentified. However, the quest dialogue given by Grobber indicated that Ballater was a male.

entities.description:
"Shank" Ballax was a male Human guard who worked at the prison Desolation Alley during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

He was the leader of Helmet Squad. He was wanted by the Hutts because his activities stymied their flow of money. His bounty was worth 5,000 credits, dead or alive. It was claimed by Jango Fett during the bounty hunter's search for Bendix Fust, a Mordageen wanted by Dug crime lord Sebolto. Ballax' removal, whether by death or capture, broke the morale of rioters triggered by Zam Wesell, who also sought Ballax.

entities.description:
Ballon was a male Toydarian, who lived during the early years of the Galactic Empire.

Ballon worked as an arms dealer on the planet Byrsym, and had dealings with the resistance fighter Prince Torrin. After the Galactic Empire attacked the planet Daimar, a group of individuals left the world to try and locate Torrin. The individuals found Ballon in the bar Emthuul's with his employees Sskal and Tarula, and they asked Ballon to contact Torrin, to see if the prince would be willing to speak to them. However, Ballon was arrested by the Galactic Empire shortly afterwards, and under interrogation the Toydarian gave the Imperials information on how to find Torrin.

entities.name: Bendodi Ballow-Reese
entities.description:
Bendodi Ballow-Reese was the eldest member of the crew stationed on the research outpost ExGal-4 on Belkadan in 25 ABY. He had been a soldier for the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War.

Bendodi was one of four scientists that went on an expedition to scout out a large storm on the planet. As they approached it, the atmosphere, affected by the infiltrator Yomin Carr's dweebits, became increasingly toxic. The expedition had trouble returning to the base after discovering the storm, due to low oxygen rations. Realizing that not all of the team would be able to return to the base, Bendodi gave his oxygen pack to Jerem Cadmir before escaping into the jungle to die. Luther De'Ono, a friend of Bendodi, followed to beg him to not commit suicide, only to be shot by Bendodi. Moments later, Bendodi shot himself.

While on the planet, the Dark Jedi Halagad Ventor used the Force to scare Balluzikik to death.

entities.name: Balog
entities.description:
Captain Balog was a Chiss male who served the reconstituted Sith Empire as an officer in 3638 BBY. Balog was among the Imperial personnel deployed during the Conquest of Makeb, and led an Imperial strike team to raid the Makeb settlement of Tarlam for information, taking Mayor Erkens hostage for a short time.

Captain Balog was an officer of the reconstituted Sith Empire's military during the Galactic War. while drilling for Isotope-5, a mineral used as an energy source, in 3683 BBY, Balog was part of the Imperial forces dispatched in response. He led a strike team to the city of Tarlam to retrieve Isotope-5 fuel rods, containing Isotope-5, from a Hutt Cartel Isotope-5 droid Balog and his soldiers took Tarlam's residents, including Mayor Erkens, hostage.

Balog was then confronted by an individual affiliated with the Galactic Republic, the government that was fighting against the Empire in the Galactic War, who had previously been sent to Tarlam by Makeb bussines magnate and politician Shalim Avesta. This Republic operative confronted Captain Balog and gave him an Isotope-5 fuel rod rather than allow him to kill Mayor Erkens.

Balog was a male Chiss with dark hair, blue skin, and red eyes. He had two scars on his face which crossed each other directly under his right eye. Balog was willing to kill Mayor Erkens in order to secure the isotope-5 ruel rods.

entities.name: Balog
entities.description:
Balog was a Human male who served as the Chief Security Controller of the planet New Apsolon and an active Absolute. He was the one responsible for the death of Jedi Master Tahl.

Balog lived in the planet of New Apsolon, which had a social revolution at 47 BBY. In that revolution, the exploited majority Workers reclaimed equality between them and the ruling minority, the Civilized, in a bloodless campaign that saw the people's hero Ewane be elected ruler of the planet in the first ever free elections, closely supervised by the Jedi Qui-Gon Jinn and Tahl. After six peaceful years, chaos returned to New Apsolon, as Ewane was murdered shortly after being re-elected.

Balog was a Worker and at the time of Ewane's death (41 BBY) he was the New Apsolon's Chief Security Controller, but secretly he was in league with the outlawed former secret police, the Absolutes and with Ewane's twin daughters Alani and Eritha. In fact, he was an Absolute informant when they were in power. In the course of the plan to gain power and reinstall the Civilized to dominant position, Balog helped kill Ewane's successor Roan, by staging a kidnap of the twins.

He also kidnapped Jedi Master Tahl in order to retrieve a list of the Absolutes' agents that he thought she had, as she was undercover in the remnant of the disbanded secret police. That list also contained his name. Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi crossed Balog's path, as they were searching for the missing Tahl. Balog had placed her in a Sensory deprivation containment device for days, slowly torturing her in the process. When the Jedi infiltrated the Absolutes' hidden base, they set charges to the whole facility. As the explosives went off one by one, Balog set the weapons room to self-destruct and fled to Tahl's cell, seeing that he didn't need to keep her alive anymore. Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan followed him inside, where he held a transmitter that would terminate Tahl, if they came any closer. However, Qui-Gon moved so fast that he sliced off Balog's finger before he could detonate. In pain, Balog fired his blaster at the sensory deprivation device to ward the Jedi off as he made his escape.
entities.short_description: Balog was a Human male who served as the Chief Security Controller of the planet New Apsolon and an active Absolute. He was the one responsible for the death of Jedi Master Tahl.

entities.name: Baloob
entities.description:
Baloob, nicknamed "Big Nose" by Den Dhur, was an Ortolan male who worked as a pubtender of the cantina stationed on Drongar during the Clone Wars. The cantina was opened for the military and medical personnel that the Galactic Republic sent to the planet and was based at Republic Mobile Surgical Unit 7. He survived the attack of the Separatist forces against the Rimsoo, and took up again the business in the new location. When the Republic forces discovered that the Bota had no use anymore, Baloob and the rest of the personnel left Drongar.

entities.name: Dirk Balor
entities.description:
Captain Dirk Balor was a Human male who commanded an Imperial battle cruiser during the era of the Galactic Civil War. Balor's ship carried Reist, an example of an extremely rare creature known as a nightmare demon, whose telepathic abilities made it a significant threat to those around it—Balor employed a Human replica droid called Altin Wuho to keep the nightmare demon under control and allow it to be focused against Balor's enemies. 3 ABY, Balor encountered Rebel hero Luke Skywalker in the remote Lapez system, and dispatched Reist and Wuho to slay the man. However, Reist and Wuho died in the encounter, and Skywalker managed to slip away.

Dirk Balor appeared in The Empire Strikes Back Monthly 149: Death Masque, written by Steve Moore and released in 1981.

entities.description:
Narell Balrekk, also known as Balrekk the Butcher, was a male Human who served the Galactic Empire as a Captain in the Stormtrooper Corps during the Galactic Civil War against the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Balrekk served in the 84th Stormtrooper Legion as the commander of Talon Company, where he made a name for himself by using torture and other unsavory methods during interrogation of Rebel prisoners. Sometime after the Battle of Yavin, Balrekk and his company were sent to serve under General Vorrel in an attack on a Rebel base built on the planet Arda I.

entities.name: Dor Balse
entities.description:
Dor Balse was an operative working on Darkside, a repair station in the Cularin asteroid belt. He was also a member of The Cell, a criminal faction wanting to oust and replace local crimelord Nirama. He wasn't very highly placed in the Cell, neither was the Darkside faction in the general Cell scheme.

Balse was one of the few remaining members of the Darkside contingent after a raid committed by Nirama's forces in 32 BBY. Other survivors included Ahlya, Kruss Gaal, Jarrilyn, Jasper and Michael. At that point, they were trying to recruit new members, including local Wookiees, Kaarl the Ithorian and some newcomers, but the people in Darkside felt no respect for the local Cell. Shortly thereafter, they were captured by a group of spies working for Nirama.

His implication in The Cell and subsequent capture were public knowledge less than one month later.

Baltke was a male Chiss commander of the Chiss Expansionary Defense Fleet who served as a battle surgeon and interrogator.

During the Swarm War, he interrogated Jedi Knight Leia Organa Solo about her mission with her husband Han Solo, and the New Jedi Order's plans for the war. He tried using a hypoinjector on Organa Solo to force her to tell the truth but she used the Force to make Baltke inject himself.

entities.description:
Predne Balu was a male Imperial Assistant Security Officer from Tatooine. He was a coworker of Feltipern Trevagg.

Trevagg caught sight of M'iiyoom Onith, a female H'nemthe. Balu warned Feltipern to "leave the girl alone" when he was attempting to bed her. However, stubborn Trevagg didn't listen to him, and was killed during their mating ritual. Balu's surprised reaction to Wuher's fingering of M'iiyoom Onith in Trevagg's murder suggests that Balu did not know of the danger Trevagg was in.

As a security officer, Balu patrolled the streets of Mos Eisley. He wore dark blue pants and vest, gray shirt, and tan holster and belt.

In the audio dramatization of Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale, the character was voiced by Russell Horton.

Bammer was a clone trooper who served the Grand Army of the Republic as a pilot of Gold Squadron during the Clone Wars against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. In 21 BBY, he served alongside Jedi General Anakin Skywalker when they were tasked to destroy a Separatist ship during the Battle of Lanteeb. However, the Separatist ship was hijacked by General Grievous which gave him enough time to escape and fly to safety. After a short pursuit, Bammer was hit unexpectedly by a volley of lasers that destroyed his starfighter, which killed him.

entities.name: Yuthura Ban's Jedi Master
entities.description:
This male was the Jedi Master of Yuthura Ban.

Yuthura was discovered by the Jedi Master on a desolate world, having been abandoned there by the crew of a cargo ship she had stowed away on to escape from Sleheyron, and her life as a slave. Recognizing her Force potential the master took Yuthura to Dantooine, to be trained as a Jedi, taking the young Twi'lek as his Padawan. The partnership would not last long, however, as Yuthura, consumed with hatred towards the slave trade, and infruiated by the Jedi's apathy toward it, left the Order, eventually joining the new Sith Empire of Darth Revan and Malak. Yuthura returned to the Jedi after being redeemed by a reformed Revan and upon seeing his old apprentice, the Jedi wept.

entities.name: Ban-yaro
entities.description:
Ban-yaro was a male Jedi Master serving the Jedi Order during the Clone Wars as the communications chief at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant.

A Force-sensitive male, Ban-yaro was trained in the ways of the Force at the Coruscant Jedi Temple. Attaining the rank of Jedi Knight after completing his Trials of Knighthood, Ban-yaro went onto pursue independent study as a Sentinel specialized in communications. After serving the Order for some time, Ban-yaro was made a Jedi Master by the Jedi High Council. At some point as a Master, Ban-yaro was appointed to the position of communications chief at the Jedi Temple communication center.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Master Ban-yaro remained at the Temple to help coordinate Jedi Command. When Jedi Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker were appointed a secret assignment by Grand Master Yoda, Ban-yaro was advised to keep all that he heard a secret so as not to endanger the pair. As Kenobi and Skywalker sent scrambled transmissions to the Temple, Ban-yaro kept the Grand Master informed of their mission on Lanteeb. When the Jedi homed in on Confederacy General Lok Durd and his deadly nanovirus, Senator Bail Organa aided Ban-yaro and the Jedi to end the Separatist threat.

entities.name: Po Bandis
entities.description:
Po Bandis was a male Jedi Master who, in addition to being a member of the Jedi Order, served as a General of the 313th Legion during the Clone Wars, a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

Po Bandis was a Force-sensitive Zabrak male who was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order. After years of study and work with the Jedi High Council, Bandis would pass the Trials of Knighthood to reach the rank of Jedi Knight and finally made a Jedi Master.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Master Bandis dutifully took up the rank of General within the Grand Army of the Republic. Leading clone troopers against the Separatist Droid Army, Bandis was placed in command of the 313th Legion and tasked with locating a Separatist base located on Ando Prime. Discovering a massive droid production facility, Bandis led his troops to destroy it but were intercepted by General Terrus and his droid army. As they did battle, the Skakoan engineer Vylagos activated his experimental hyperspace wormhole transporter, which transported Bandis and his men off-planet to an unknown location in the Outer Rim Territories.

Detecting Bandis's disappearance, the High Council dispatched Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi to locate the Jedi and his clones. Leading Commander Vargus and Excelsior Company to Ando Prime, the Jedi encounter a medic, Gen-Goma, who helped them extract information from Vylagos about the experimental machine. Reactivating the machine, the Skakoan brought back Bandis and his troops, who then aided in shutting down the Separatist base.

entities.name: Kitster Banai
entities.description:
Kitster Banai was a human male who was enslaved and lived on the Outer Rim world of Tatooine during the Naboo Crisis. As a child, he befriended Anakin Skywalker—a fellow slave and podracing enthusiast. Banai supported Skywalker as a member of his pit team at the Boonta Eve Classic. As a result of winning the event, Banai's friend gained his freedom and subsequently departed the desert planet to join the Jedi Order. Banai was eventually freed from slavery and moved to the planet Gabredor III where he lived with other freed slaves from Tatooine in a colony.

Kitster Banai was a child enslaved on Tatooine, an Outer Rim planet that was too distant to be affected by the anti-slave laws of the Galactic Republic. Born during the final years of the Republic, he was around the same age as his friend, Anakin Skywalker. Like Banai, Skywalker was also a slave—having been sold to the Toydarian junk dealer Watto. As children, Banai and Skywalker protected each other while braving the dangerous streets of Mos Espa. Though they would sometimes argue, the two were great friends and enjoyed playing pranks on each other. When Skywalker entered his custom-built podracer in the Boonta Eve Classic podracing event, Banai supported him as a member of his pit team. Skywalker ultimately won the race along with his freedom, leading Banai and his childhood friend to part ways as Skywalker embarked on a journey to become a Jedi.

As the years went by, an older Skywalker still thought about Banai and hoped that his friend had been able to make it off of Tatooine. In the early days of the Clone Wars Skywalker reflected on his childhood memories while giving a lesson to Jedi younglings. He imparted upon the initiates that every person they would meet in their lives would have something to teach them, citing Banai as an individual who taught him how to find joy in the bleakest of times.

Banai was eventually freed from slavery by Sabé, one of the Naboo Royal Handmaidens, and the royal guard Tonra as part of a slave liberation movement they were conducting in Shmi Skywalker's honor. Banai eventually ended up on Gabredor III and lived in a colony with the other freed slaves from Tatooine, including Wald. Eventually, the Governor of Gabredor III, Sabé enlisted the help of the Sith Lord Darth Vader to help free the colony from the governor, and brought him to the colony where they met with Banai and Wald. Unbeknownst to most, Darth Vader was once Anakin Skywalker, and therefore he recognized Banai and Wald from his childhood. Due to the governor's meddling, the planet was experiencing a drought, which inadvertently caused a group of to attack the colony.

entities.name: Kitster Chanchani Banai
entities.description:
Kitster Chanchani Banai was a Human slave boy on Tatooine, and the best friend of Anakin Skywalker. After not seeing his smuggler father, Rakir Banai, in many years, Kitster gave up hopes of being rescued from Tatooine and instead hoped to one day be a majordomo for a wealthy Mos Espan estate.

Kitster Chanchani Banai was born the son of smuggler Rakir Banai, which brought them to the Tatooine city of Mos Espa.

A short time before the 32 BBY Boonta's Eve, the young Kitster, with Anakin Skywalker and their friends, narrowly avoided disaster upon hearing of children who had been captured and imprisoned by Sebulba. The Dug intended to sell the captives, including Princess Arawynne, to Gardulla the Elder. The children, disguised as Jawas, sneaked into Gardulla's estate and freed the Ghostling children.

Kitster was the best friend of Anakin Skywalker on Tatooine, During the podrace on Boonta Eve, Kitster was part of Anakin's pit crew.

entities.name: Rakir Banai
entities.description:
Rakir Banai was a male Human smuggler and the father of Kitster Chanchani Banai.

Years prior to the Invasion of Naboo, Rakir Banai was a smuggler. He had his own ship, and ran controlled medicines to Outer Rim worlds to bypass Corporate Sector surcharges. However, his job was came to an end when he and his family were captured by bounty hunters in a Hutt pirate raid. His wife and his son Kitster were sold into slavery. Rakir did not see his family anymore and, since that time, he became preoccupied with getting revenge against Hutts.

Rakir Banai eventually ended up in the small town of Wayfar on Tatooine, where he worked for a man named Drik Bandrik after the Battle of Yavin.

In 1 ABY, Rakir encountered a spacer, and asked him for his help. Rakir learned of a troublemaker in Mos Espa who was trying to undermine Drik's local mining business. Drik told Rakir that the troublemaker was accused of several murders, and was sending a saboteur to blow up his mine. When the spacer asked why the person was causing trouble, Rakir said that troublemaker was complaining of working conditions in the mine. However, Drik also told Rakir that the troublemaker was a mine owner, out to destroy the competition. Rakir asked if the spacer could stop the saboteur, who was actually a Twi'lek named Triggo Binz. The spacer set out to find Triggo, knowing fully well that he would probably not let himself be arrested. Sure enough, as the spacer approached Triggo and his associates, they began attacking. As Triggo began attacking, he shouted that the spacer would die, just like Drik's slaves. However, the spacer succeeded in killing Triggo and his associates. Following the fight, the spacer returned to Rakir to deliver the news. Rakir was surprised that Triggo yelled Drik was a slaver. Rakir did not believe that to be true, but said he needed to take the time to look into it.

entities.name: Sors Bandeam
entities.description:
Sors Bandeam was a male Human Jedi Initiate enrolled in the Jedi Order's Temple academy on Coruscant during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive Human, Sors Bandeam was given to the Jedi Order for education in the ways of the Force. Sorted into a clan at the Coruscant Jedi Temple, Initiate Bandeam remained at the Temple as many of his instructors fought and died during the Clone Wars.

When Supreme Chancellor Palpatine betrayed the Order in 19 BBY by issuing Contingency Order 66, Initiate Bandeam was present with his clan at the Temple when the 501st Legion marched up the Processional Way. Seeking refuge in the High Council Chamber high atop one of the Temple's towers, he and his peers were pleased when Jedi Anakin Skywalker walked into the chamber. Believing the famed hero was there to save them from the attacking clones, the children were caught unaware when the Jedi-turned-Sith ignited his lightsaber and slew the younglings after Sors asked Skywalker. Indeed, Skywalker had fallen to the dark side of the Force and was now known as Darth Vader.

Sors Bandeam was played by the uncredited Ross Beadman in the 2005 film Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith, the final installment of the Star Wars prequel trilogy.

entities.name: Bandi
entities.description:
Bandi was a Ewok male who was affiliated with the Alliance to Restore the Republic during the Galactic Civil War against the Galactic Empire. He stood one meter tall and was skilled in dodging, hiding, sneaking, climbing, jumping, survival, and in the use of bows and melee weapons. He wore an animal skull as headgear and carried a spear, a bow, a flute, and leather pouches.

Bandi was created for the Rebel Characters Adventure Set, a boxed set of metal miniatures released in 1989 by West End Games to be used with Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game. Bandi's character type was listed as just "Ewok" and his model came unpainted.
