entities.name: Waldan Bridger
entities.description:
Waldan Bridger was a bald and burly male Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a General in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A male Force-sensitive, Waldan Bridger was educated in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order, eventually attaining the rank of Jedi Knight. As a Knight, Bridger pursued the path of the Jedi Guardian during his independent studies, fashioning for himself a San-Ni staff which he wielded in place of a lightsaber. A ranking Jedi Weapon Master, Bridger eventually was made a Jedi Master by the Jedi High Council for his knowledge and power in the Force.

When the Clone Wars erupted between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Master Bridger dutifully took up the title of General within the newly formed Grand Army of the Republic, leading clone troopers in battle against the Separatist Droid Army. 22 months after the start of the war, Bridger led a campaign to bring the war-plagued planet of Togoria back into the Republic. The Togorians had voluntarily joined the CIS, however, and viewed the Republic as invaders. When Bridger brought his landing party down on the world, the natives attacked and massacred the clone troopers under Bridger's command. The Togorians were bolstered by the leader of the Confederacy's army, General Grievous, who saw to it that he alone would face the Jedi. Bridger attacked Grievous head-on, but the duel lasted only twenty seconds. Grievous' lightsabers cut through Bridger's staff and the Jedi Master's body, killing him instantly. Grievous, victorious, left Bridger's body where it fell for the ravenous native mosgoth beasts.

Waldan Bridger was created by Daniel Wallace for the canceled guidebook known as The Essential Guide to Episode I. Along with Jedi L'lacielo Sageon, Bridger was described as serving as one of the Jedi Temple's quartermasters at the time of the Invasion of Naboo. Both Jedi's first names are anagrams of their creator's name; the letters from both names combined can be reconfigured to spell, 'Daniel Wallace.' The names Waldan and L'lacielo are older then the canceled guidebook however. Author Abel G. Peña originally intended to name one of his own creations "Waldan L'lacielo"; the name was changed during the editing of this particular text to Awdrysta Pina.

At the same time, he used the threat of turning the planet over to the Empire to keep the New Republic at bay. However, Bridin was aware that his deceit might not last and cut a deal with the Hutt kajidics. In exchange for deflector shield technology, the Hutts gained a foothold in the sector.

entities.name: Kal Brigger
entities.description:
Kal Brigger was a Human male freelance trader who, along with his sister, Dova Brigger, bought the YT-1300 light freighter Millennium Falcon, known at the time as YT 492727ZED, in 48 BBY. Using their newly bought ship, which they named Hardwired, the siblings illegally transported cargo between Corellia and other planets in the Core Worlds. Eventually, the Briggers became involved with the Smugglers' Confederation and its leader, Nirama, who put a price on the siblings' heads due to a broken deal in which Kal was supposed to stop his dealings with slavers. After a bounty hunter captured Dova, Kal took the Hardwired for himself and rechristened the ship as Wayward Son. Kal then went to work for the former smuggler Iaco Stark, who had gotten into an armed conflict with the Galactic Republic, during which Kal was eaten alive by carnivorous insects in an abandoned spice mine on Troiken.

Kal Brigger and his sister, Dova, a pair of freelance traders, worked in the enterprising business during their careers. In 48 BBY, the Briggers came across a YT-1300 light freighter, owned by Corell Industries, which had gone bankrupt due to the Trade Federation, who had been monopolizing various businesses. The siblings bought the ship and named it Hardwired, with the intent of making a profit by transporting cargo between Corellia and other worlds. Successful in his business, Kal used the money they made toward upgrading the ship's hyperdrive, hoping for easier travel in the Corellian system, and eventually used the hyperdrive to enable travel to other Core Worlds.

However, the Briggers' business soon turned illegal, and they began to carry different cargo, including munitions, light arms, and slaves instead of consumer goods. This illegal business caught the attention of the Smugglers' Confederacy of the Cularin system and their leader, Nirama. An Oblee crime lord opposed to slavery, Nirama struck a deal with Kal hoping the Briggers would stop business with slavers. If they complied, Nirama would loan them credits to upgrade the Hardwired in return.

After a standard year, though, Kal and Dova broke the deal, prompting Nirama to put a price on their heads. A famed bounty hunter succeeded in capturing Dova, who in turn was executed by Nirama, though Kal escaped. Alone, Kal rechristened the Hardwired as Wayward Son, and attempted to take a job with Iaco Stark's Commercial Combine. This involvement with Stark, a former smuggler who headed a group of pirates, bounty hunters, and assassins, backfired on Kal when Stark became involved in an armed conflict with the Galactic Republic because of stolen bacta. The Republic forces released carnivorous insects against the smuggler on Troiken, and Kal was eaten alive by them, trapped in an abandoned spice mine.

entities.name: Slique Brighteyes
entities.description:
Slique Brighteyes was a Gulmarid native of Gulma who survived the atrocities committed by the Imperial extermination ship Azgoghk.

During the Galactic Civil War, Slique Brighteyes and other Gulmarids lived peacefully on Gulma until the planet was invaded and subjugated by the Galactic Empire several months prior to the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY. The Empire harvested all available natural resources on Gulma, transformed the planet into a barren wasteland and proceeded to relocate the planet's Gulmarid population to the Imperial starship known as the Azgoghk. While the Gulmarids were under false belief that the ship was assigned to transport them offworld, Brighteyes and his companions soon realized the truth behind the Empire's motives for transferring their species to the Azgoghk. The Azgoghk was in fact one of the three Imperial extermination ships commissioned by the genocidal Grand Admiral Danetta Pitta to eradicate Non-huMan species through the Outer Rim Territories and establish all-Human governance over the galaxy in accordance with Human High Culture, and thus the Empire strove for the deliberate and systematic extermination of the Gulmarids.

Aboard the Azgoghk the Gulmarids, like many other captive species, were frequently abused and tormented by the stormtroopers. Those Gulmarids who were considered weak, sick and feeble were killed by disintegrating them to base elements in the ship's ionization chambers. Brighteyes was separated from his unlucky family members, and they perished in the ionization chambers. Brighteyes and the survivors were used as forced labor assigned to dispose the deceased Gulmarids by incinerating their corpses in the Azgoghk fusion reactors. While most of the surviving Gulmarid slaves were kept under abysmal living conditions by the Humanocentric Admiral Mir Tork, the rest were killed in the horrific experiments conducted by the science officer Leonis Murthé. However, Brighteyes and many others eventually escaped the Azgoghk and settled on the planet Basteel. He became the spokesman of the Gulmarid refugees, planning to end the Azgoghk reign of terror once and for all.

entities.name: Kai Brightstar
entities.description:
Kai Brightstar was a human male Jedi youngling sent to the forest planet Tenoo for training during the High Republic Era.

Kai Brightstar was a human male Jedi youngling Coruscant at the Jedi Temple, where they learned under Jedi Masters Yoda and Zia Zaldor Zanna. it came time for the younglings to continue their training elsewhere, and Brightstar, Solay, and Nubs were assigned to travel to the planet Tenoo in the Outer Rim Territories. However, when Yoda announced this to the larger younglings, the three were missing, off practicing in the training course—Brightstar had had the idea of making one last attempt at their record before departing.

The trio hid behind cover while strategizing how to get beyond the training remote droids and capture a beacon. Solay decided to leap to one side of the course, drawing the droids' fire and allowing Brightstar and Nubs to make a break for the beacon. Using Nubs's paws as a jump-off point, Brightstar flipped toward the beacon and began walking backwards to it, deflecting the droids' lasers with his lightsaber. He declined when his friends offered to help but then tripped, prompting them to come to his aid anyhow. Solay reminded him that friends existed to help one another, which Brightstar affirmed—he had thought he could do it by himself. They continued blocking laserfire from the droids until Brightstar was close enough to grab the beacon, which he did—they had broken their record, much to their celebration, though Nubs's hug was too tight for Brightstar.

Master Zanna then appeared on a hologram, warning the younglings that they would need to hurry to their shuttles to Tenoo. Brightstar apologized for their tardiness. They caught the last shuttle, where the pilot, the human Nash Durango, and her droid, RJ-83, were making repairs before they left. Brightstar asked who the pilot was, and when Durango told them it was her, Solay was surprised, for she was a mere child. Durango pointed out that the Jedi, too, were kids, and she introduced herself, receiving the younglings' names in return. They boarded her starship, the Crimson Firehawk, and took off to jump into hyperspace, delighting the Jedi.

When the settlement was overrun by Zygerrian enslavers sometime after the Battle of Endor, he and the other residents were rounded up and locked in the town hall. While imprisoned, the Nu-Cosian pet-seller Bobbajo kept the children calm by telling them a story about he and his animal companions escaping from the Death Star during the Battle of Yavin. Once the tale was finished, the storyteller left the town hall and revealed all the slavers had been subdued by unknown forces, allowing the residents of Reestkii to claim the Zygerrian's gathered wealth.

Xavi Brightsun first appeared in the short story "All Creatures Great and Small," which was written by Landry Q. Walker and released as an eBook in 2015.

After learning of the Twi'leks' capture, General Obi-Wan Kenobi ordered his clone troopers to be cautious in their attacks to minimize civilian casualties. During the operation, two of the clone troopers, Waxer and Boil, encountered Brill's niece Numa who led them through the town's underground passages to a square where they rendezvoused with General Kenobi and the rest of the squad.

Kenobi, who spoke Ryl, asked Numa to lead them through the passages to the hostages, which she agreed to. This allowed the Republic forces to free the hostages and flank the Droid forces.

entities.description:
Brint was a Human male colonel who served in the Galactic Republic's military on the planet Corellia during the Galactic War against the Sith Empire.

Brint fought for the Republic during the Battle of Corellia. However, he had disagreements with Senator Jol Zackin over how to commit to the war effort. When Jedi reinforcements arrived, under the command of the Hero of Tython, Brint advocated striking at the Imperial extermination teams that have been massacring medical camps and the murderers were rewarded as a result. Zackin disagreed and advised saving Corellian citizens the Empire had enslaved. Brint reminded the senator that the citizens were taken from prison, so he designated them as criminals. Zackin insisted those people were innocent until proven guilty in court. Brint then tried offering the latest equipment from Balmorra to supply the Jedi, which an outraged Zackin viewed as bribery. To Brint's dismay, the Hero chose to follow Zackin's suggestion. Nonetheless, Brint referred the Jedi to their science adviser, revealed to be Nasan Godera.

But as the Hero went to stop fallen Jedi Master, Tol Braga, from committing mass murder, Godera was killed by an Imperial ambush. Brint presented General Var Suthra with data concerning Braga's location, which Godera managed to compile before his death. As soon as the general exited the room, Brint passed on Zackin's regards for saving Corellian "citizens". But he shrewdly reminded the Hero that by adhering to the Senator's request, the murderous Imperials the Jedi refused to strike at were laughing all the way back to Dromund Kaas. The Hero sternly stated that the Jedi had come to save lives, not take them and fulfill Brint's petty revenge. Grumbling that he'll never understand Jedi, Brint then gave the coordinates to the Republic base in the government district.

entities.name: Noa Briqualon
entities.description:
Noa Briqualon was a Human male trader and mid-level scout who, after crashing his star cruiser on Endor, spent decades living as a hermit on the surface of the forested moon. The shipwreck occurred around the year 26 BBY, when Briqualon and his friend Salak Weet set out to chart the Moddell sector. When Weet left their crash site in search of a replacement for the ship's broken crystal oscillator, he was killed by a band of stranded Sanyassan Marauders; left to his own devices, Briqualon made a home for himself inside a hollowed-out tree. With a furry Teek named Teek as his only companion, he spent years repairing the crashed cruiser, which remained grounded without a functioning oscillator.

In 3 ABY, Teek found the orphaned Human girl Cindel Towani and her Ewok friend Wicket Wystri Warrick, and welcomed them into Briqualon's home. The scout gruffly sent them away, but as the two children had no place to go, Briqualon reluctantly allowed them to sleep on his floor. He initially claimed that the invitation was for a single night, but on their third day with him, they followed him to the site of his star cruiser and prompted him to share his entire story. Briqualon grew protective of Towani and bonded with her in an almost grandfatherly way, and when she was kidnapped by the Sanyassan Marauders and taken to their castle stronghold the next morning, he immediately set out to rescue her.

Briqualon, Warrick, and Teek infiltrated the castle and rescued both Towani and a group of her Ewok friends. They also retrieved the crystal oscillator from Towani's own star cruiser, which the Marauders had stolen after killing the girl's family. Returning to the site of his crashed ship, Briqualon used the oscillator to power up the cruiser while the Ewoks held off the pursuing Marauders. He was forced to duel the sword-wielding Marauder King Terak with only a walking stick, but the fight ended when Terak was burned to death by the power of a magic ring he wore around his neck. With the star cruiser finally operational, Briqualon and Towani left Endor, and the old scout eventually retired in the galaxy's Mid Rim.

Noa Briqualon was a young Human male who worked as a mid-level scout He spent years in the profession Shortly before 26 BBY, due to interference caused by nearby stellar debris and gravity shadows. With a damaged crystal oscillator, the star cruiser was inoperable, and the two explorers hid their vessel beneath a layer of the forested moon's foliage before enacting repairs. Eventually, Weet left on a hunt for a replacement oscillator, but Briqualon remained with the ship.

Broadside was a male clone trooper who served as a member of the 501st Legion in 22 BBY, Broadside walked alongside Matchstick on board Skywalker's Acclamator-class assault ship.

During the Malevolence Campaign, Broadside and Shadow Squadron were briefed by Admiral Wullf Yularen and Jedi General Anakin Skywalker aboard the Resolute. There, Skywalker informed Broadside and their fellow pilots that their mission was to attack the Malevolence by targeting its bridge and take out the commander, General Grievous. Following the briefing, Broadside and Matchstick assured Jedi General Plo Koon that their squadron would be prepared for their mission, stating that they maintained minimal casualties and maximum effectiveness.

Following Grievous' attack on a medical convoy in the Ryndellia system, Broadside, along with the rest of Shadow Squadron, Skywalker, and Koon took the Balmorra Run in order to reach the Kaliida Shoals Medical Center before the Malevolence.

Upon arriving on Gepparin, he waited until nightfall for his accomplice Gilling to ambush her while he distracted her. entities.name: Dalien Brock
entities.description:
Dalien Brock was a Force-sensitive Human male born of two Je'daii Masters, who reluctantly trained as a Je'daii Journeyer of the Je'daii Order with his sister, Lanoree, before fleeing after having killed Skott Yun, another Journeyer. After faking his death, he joined and led a sect of the Stargazers, a cabal of fanatics dedicated to finding a way to leave Tython system and to reach the stars of their ancestors by any means.

The youngest child of Je'daii Master Brock and his wife, Dalien Brock grew up on Tython with his sister Lanoree at the Temple of Arts, Bodhi. He and his sister were encouraged to express themselves through art, and in his childhood, Dalien was particularly fond of drawing and painting. He loved fruits, and Mepples were his favorite.

Because of his Force-sensitivity, Dalien was permitted to reside on Tython and pursue studies to be a Je'daii. But he believed that the Je'daii could not be their own masters, since they served the Force and were bound by it. This belief caused him to eventually began to shun the Force, reacting furiously whenever his sister sought to connect with his mind telepathically. Every time his family visited the Edge Forest to bask in the Force energies of the teeming lives around them, the young Dalien will burst into tears due to his family's indifference towards his feelings and constant efforts to bring him to embrace the Force.Instead, he turned to history, studying the ancient cultures of Tython and pondering the stars. His mother found this concerning, worried that it will lead him to a destiny away from Tython. During his childhood, his grandfather passed down a well-used blaster pistol, a weapon that he would cherish and hold on to throughout his life.

Reaching adolescence, Dalien set out with his older sister away from Bodhi on foot to begin their Great Journey. The pair traveled first to Qigong Kesh, the Temple of Force Skills, surviving encounters with hook hawks and silik lizards along the way. There, they trained under Master Ter'cay, who took them to the Silent Desert, using Force telepathy to communicate with the pair, though Dalien was unable to hear Ter'cay in the Force. Traveling next to Stav Kesh, the Temple of Martial Arts, they were attacked by a flame tygah. Dalien attacked the creature himself with his blaster pistol without any reliance on the Force, causing his sister to intervene when his blaster misfired. Arriving at Stav Kesh with burns from the assault, the two trained with Master Tave, first learning about breathing and its importance to fighting. Throughout their training, Dalien continued to retreat from the Force despite his sister's attempts to promote its use. When he successfully landed a strike on Tave without using the Force, his sister attempted to warn him that Tave had allowed it to instill confidence, not because the Force was weak.

entities.name: Lanoree Brock's father
entities.description:
Lanoree Brock's father was a male Human and a Je'daii Master who taught at Bodhi, the Temple of Arts, for the Je'daii Order on Tython at the height of the Infinite Empire's reign.

Trained as a member of the Je'daii Order, Brock met his future wife met as Journeyers crossing the planet Tython on their Great Journey. Both of the young Je'daii were drawn to Bodhi Temple where the Force exposed their natural talents in the arts. A talented sculptor renowned across Masara continent, Brock was also skilled at cooking rumbat stew. Years after their Journey ended, Brock and his wife became the parents of Lanoree and Dalien Brock. Living in the Je'daii settlement surrounding the Temple of Arts, Brock taught at Bodhi, amusing his students and colleagues with his magic tricks. One of his students, Master Xiang, would later go on to teach under his watch. When his children were growing up, he would tell them tales and legends from Je'daii history, including a cautionary tale of Osamael Or and his fateful mission into the Old City.

During the war between Tython and Despot Queen Hadiya and her army, Brock served some of his time on the planet Nox where the fighting was especially vicious. Following the war and the supposed death of his son, Brock rarely saw his daughter, who had become a Je'daii Ranger by the time of Dalien's reemergence during the Stargazer Uprising.

Brock wore his hair long, usually tied up, but allowed it to fall across his shoulders when at home. Brock believed that his son's inquisitive nature was a sign that he would make a fine Je'daii in time; he always believed that Dalien would find his own way. When spending time with his children, Brock would often take them to the Edge Forest where his explorer's heart would yearn to venture into its vastness.

Lanoree Brock's grandfather was first mentioned in Dawn of the Jedi: Into the Void, a Legends novel written by Tim Lebbon. He was first mentioned as the former owner of Dalien Brock's blaster pistol.

Numen Brock was a Twi'lek male smuggler who became a Galactic Republic privateer during the Galactic War. He was given the rank of Commander and was working with the Balmorran resistance on Balmorra

Numen Brock was initially a hired man by the Galactic Republic who was given the rank of Commander and joined the Balmorran resistance on Balmorra. He operated as a cryptographic analysis specialist overseeing all encoded Republic Communications in the planet and also the main contact of the SIS double-agent Golden. Numen was the owner of the droid Sixer that was stationed in Farnel Outpost during the start of the Galactic War.

In 3642 BBY, Brock served as the smuggler known as Voidhound's contact when the latter came to Balmorra to disrupt Project Nebula, an Imperial operation focused in developing advanced weaponry. Brock proceeded to assign the smuggler to retrieve new info from Golden in Imperial territory. He was eventually captured by the Imperials during a patrol, but was rescued from Camp Vigil by the Voidhound.

Numen Brock can be romanced by the female Smuggler.

Brogar was a male Advozse who owned Brogar's Safe House and Cantina on the planet Lok, a cantina that doubled as a safe house for those who needed a place to lay low. Brogar used armed droid bouncers to keep the peace within his establishment.

By the year 137 ABY, some of his patrons included a compulsive gambler named Naxy Screeger and a fugitive Jedi named Hosk Trey'lis, both of whom were captured in defiance of Brogar's offered sanctuary by Cade Skywalker, Jariah Syn, and Deliah Blue.

Brogar denied to the trio of bounty hunters any knowledge that Trey'lis was a Jedi and claimed he must have been affected by a mind trick. Because of the high risks involved with harboring a Jedi, Brogar allowed the breach in protocol and told Cade that this with a gesture of good faith to Cade's employer, the dreaded pirate Rav.

entities.name: Tyrus Brokenblade
entities.description:
Tyrus Brokenblade was a male Mandalorian warrior and the leader of Clan Varad who lived during the third Galactic War, and represented Clan Varad in Heta Kol's organization known as the Hidden Chain.

In 3626 BBY, members of Clan Varad joined in on an attack on the Mandalorian ship the Spirit of Vengeance II alongside the Ash'ad and the Dar'manda at the behest of Heta Kol. Following this attack, after they had secured the banner of Clan Cadera, Brokenblade met with Heta Kol, Bask Sunn, and Durn Wynnward. An argument broke out between Brokenblade and Wynnward but was quickly stopped by Kol when she pulled out a thermal detonator and threw it at Brokenblade. Brokenblade managed to catch and keep it from exploding and was then stabbed twice by Kol as a demonstration of how they all relied on each other. Kol deactivated the thermal detonator, and Brokenblade was assisted by members of Clan Varad before being dismissed to fulfill the orders given to them.

Tyrus was later present in the Hidden Chain meeting when Ri'kan Kateen reunited with the group and brought his sister, the rogue Jedi Padawan Sa'har Kateen, to Heta Kol.

Following Hidden Chain's disastrous retreat from Ruhnuk, Tyrus attended a gathering of Kol's inner circle, where she revealed that Bask Sunn interfered with her duel with Shae Vizla, prompting her to expel Dar'manda from the Hidden Chain. Afterwards, she showed them Darth Nul's holocron and promised that its secrets would bring the Hidden Chain to glory, but the only ones who would know the whole plan would be just herself and Sa'har, before everyone, including Tyrus, applauded her.

entities.name: Brolis
entities.description:
Brolis was a Clone Commander who served in the Grand Army of the Republic after the start of the Clone Wars, and was one of the few survivors in the disastrous Battle of Axion.

Created on the planet Kamino, Brolis was a Clone Commander who served the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars. During his service, Brolis participated in a battle against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. During the battle, Commander Brolis managed to lead his forces into penetrating the Fortress of Axion, but they were eventually overwhelmed by Separatist forces. Brolis and his last two squads fled into the city where they took refuge in one of the ruined buildings. Brolis requested reinforcements, but as the group waited they were eventually whittled down by battle droid forces until only Brolis remained. Commander Brolis continued to hold out in the building, knowing the droids wanted him alive so they could learn how they were able to infiltrate the Fortress of Axion. Tired, Brolis took an uneasy nap which he awoke from when his proximity alarm buzzed, alerting him of the approaching battle droids.

Commander Brolis took aim at the first battle droid he spotted but was startled after being told to put the weapon away by an unknown voice. Turning around, Brolis took sight of a diminutive, green creature who told Brolis that he was the requested reinforcements. As the short individual ignited his lightsaber, Commander Brolis realized that he was Jedi Master Yoda. Brolis watched as Yoda defeated the droids by deflecting their blaster bolts without ever moving from his spot. Shortly after, a hailfire droid arrived and shot a missile directly at Yoda. Master Yoda leaped out of the way of the missile, causing it to explode harmlessly behind him, to which the droid shot three more missiles at him. After Yoda avoided the salvo of missiles, Brolis heard calibration clicks coming from the hailfire droid. Brolis relayed to Yoda that it was a tracking lock just before the droid shot another missile. Spinning in the air, Yoda was able to confuse the missile's tracking, causing it to miss. Brolis continued to watch as the droid charged forward and sent a barrage of missiles that were evaded by Master Yoda.

Brolis appeared in "Duel," a short story written by Timothy Zahn for the Star Wars: Short Story Collection, released in August 2003. The New Essential Chronology establishes that Brolis is an outside military advisor hired by the Kaminoans to train the clones into fighting shape. Both The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia released on December 9, 2008, and The Essential Reader's Companion released on October 2, 2012 contradict this by establishing that Brolis is a Clone Commander. Since these two most recent sources identify Brolis as a clone commander, this article assumes that to be Brolis' relation to the Galactic Republic. This assumption aligns with the short story's title image, which depicts Yoda with a clone trooper.

entities.description:
Broll was a male Human Customs Agent of the Republic Customs Office during the Galactic War. Around 3640 BBY he was stationed on Hoth Orbital Station above Hoth where he tried to inspect the XS stock light freighter of a smuggler known as Voidhound, who was smuggling Shariss Kartur off the planet with a bulk of illegal Imperial salvage.

Three ways to deal with Broll are to offer him a bribe, attempt an unconvincing lie, or attack and kill him.

entities.description:
Brollo was a Gamorrean mercenary who worked for Jerec's division of the Imperial remnants in 5 ABY. He wore a bloodsucking morrt on each bicep as a symbol of status. He was stationed on Sulon to guard the Katarn house. His cousin was Blotho, who participated in fights that the Imperials and mercenaries would bet on.

He was hired by Jerec and during his search for the Valley of the Jedi he was assigned to guard the Katarn estate along with Imperial Remnant forces. He used to participate in dueling bets with Stormtroopers. During their patrol duty in the estate, an Imperial invited him to another bet, and produced a datapad in order to choose between Kine and his cousin Blotho. Right then, the droid WeeGee broke the backdoor of the kitchen; after a moment of shock, the two were reaching for their weapons when Brollo was shot by Kyle Katarn with a blaster shot. His partner followed soon after.

entities.description:
Brolok was a male Gamorrean bounty hunter who earned the nickname "Boulder" and served the reconstituted Sith Empire during the Great Galactic War against the Galactic Republic. He supplied other hunters with equipment during the war and was stationed on board the Vaiken Spacedock space station within the Imperial fleet. Brolok wore a green and yellow set of armor including a helmet, and worked in the supplies section of the station.

Brolok was created for Star Wars: The Old Republic, an MMORPG released by BioWare in 2011. In the game he serves as an Imperial ultimate gear vendor within the Imperial fleet. He was later removed in Game Update 5.0 on November 29, 2016, which retired the PvP and PvE gear vendors in favor of the Command system.

During the Alderaan Civil War, Brom worked with Malcom to ensure the safety and tactical superiority of House Organa's forces—a difficult task, given the Organa's inexperience in military affairs and traditional pacifism.

entities.description:
Bron was a male Human who served as a representative for the Galactic Republic .

In 33 BBY, Bron was assigned to Cerea to "observe" Cerean ways and persuade the local population to technological progress to the citizens of the Republic. As he landed on Cerea, he was one of the few to be granted permission to move outside the citadel. However, he used this as an opportunity to keep public appearances about the benefits of civilized life. His speeches were particularly among the younger generation of the Cerean that were deliberately against the Cerean Elder since it was revealed that he served as an agent to Jabba the Hutt. Eventually, Bron retreated from public life, though there were rumors, that he was complicit in this plot.

entities.description:
Arly Bron was a stocky, aging Human male smuggler with a genial air and sharp tongue who frequented the Corellian Sector during the Galactic Civil War. In 1 BBY, Arly Bron was one of the captains who helped the Rebel Alliance where he piloted the Double Echo and served as one of the atmosphere guides during the Battle of Ylesia.

He was named after writer R. Lee Brown, founder and original editor of Echo Station, the original Star Wars online e-mag (itself the source of Bron's ship the Double Echo).

Bronc had white skin and eyes and white blond hair. He was sharp-tongued because of both their histories on opposite sides of the war.

entities.description:
Bronnel was a Mon Calamari bounty hunter.

During the Galactic Civil War, Bronell accepted the bounty placed on a Rebel Alliance officer by Jabba the Hutt for debts owed. After capturing the officer, Bronell allowed the Alliance, Jabba, and a group of pirates also owed money, to bid on the officer's life.

Bronell was a non-player character in the video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, prior to its closure on December 15, 2011.

entities.name: Ohh Bronna
entities.description:
Ohh Bronna was an Abyssin dejarik grandmaster who made HoloNet headlines in 22 BBY for a brawl he became involved in.

Bronna defeated the Abyssin stereotype of an aggressive thug. He was cool and collected, qualities which helped him rise to the top of the dejarik world and win the Colonies region championship at least once before.

In 22 BBY, he attended the championship again, and became the favorite to win it all once more. However, in his quarter-final match against the Siniteen Corwin Kaezeb, Bronna flew into a blind rage after Kaezeb executed what appeared to be an illegal move, and began beating and strangling his opponent before officials managed to separate them.

In the chaos, two other players attempted to cheat by resetting their gameboards while their opponents watched the brawl. D'nisenz, winner of the only match not to ultimately be nullified, thus became the champion by default.

entities.name: Maris Brood's Master
entities.description:
A male Jedi warrior served as the Master of the Zabrak Padawan Maris Brood, teaching her aboard the starship Gray Pilgrim. Stationed in the Outer Rim Territories at the end of the Clone Wars in 19 BBY, he and Brood did not fall victim to Order 66, which saw many Jedi killed. Feeling the deaths of many of his comrades in the Force, the Master took a starfighter and set off to find out what had happened, never to return again.

A male Jedi warrior served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the Republic's waning days. The Jedi was the Master of the Zabrak Padawan Maris Brood, whom he tutored aboard the starship Gray Pilgrim. during the closing stages of the Clone Wars between the Republic's clone trooper army and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, the Jedi and Brood were stationed in the Outer Rim Territories. Because of that, they were not affected by Order 66, which dictated that the Republic's clone troopers kill their Jedi Generals. However, Brood's Master felt ripples in the Force caused by the deaths of other Jedi. After all of his transmissions to the Jedi Temple on the galactic capital of Coruscant were met with silence, the Jedi warrior took his personal starfighter and set off to find out what had happened. He discovered that the Jedi Order had been nearly exterminated by the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader and relayed this information to Brood. However, he was not seen or heard from again after that. Seeking revenge, Brood began to search for Vader, but was soon found herself by Jedi Master Shaak Ti. Ti took the young Zabrak as her apprentice and spirited her away to the planet Felucia, where they sought refuge with the native Jungle Felucian species.

Maris Brood's Master was known as a Jedi warrior, indicating that his talents laid in battle. However, he also had a deep connection to the Force, able to sense the deaths of his Jedi brethren. He was a capable pilot and possessed his own starfighter.

Maris Brood's Master was first mentioned in Brood's databank entry in the Star Wars: The Force Unleashed video game, which was released on September 16, 2008. The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia, and in Maris Brood's entry in the now-defunct Databank on StarWars.com.

entities.description:
Brooks was a human male admiral in the Galactic Empire. While speaking with Commandant Brendol Hux, Hux's son Armitage was ordered to serve them drinks, but dropped the tray. Both Admiral Brooks and Commandant Hux scolded Armitage for his failure. Brooks later served as an admiral in the First Order, ranking below Armitage Hux, who had risen to the rank of General. In 33 ABY, when a shuttle transporting General Hux and Kylo Ren was sabotaged, Hux traced the attack to a radar technician working under Brooks, confronting the admiral. Brooks claimed he was not responsible for the sabotage, but Hux killed him.

entities.description:
Brooks was a male technician that worked for Senate Support Services. He was sent by the Office of the Supreme Chancellor to work on Outbound Flight prior to its departure from Yaga Minor. He was a friend of Dean Jinzler and brought Jinzler's Jedi sister, Lorana Jinzler, to meet him in the mess hall on Outbound Flight. He had recently repaired a defective line network and then addressed Jinzler to a possible connection to Dean. When the Jedi said that she did not know her relatives, he called Dean to him and introduced Dean to Lorana. After Dean then revealed that he was Lorana's brother, Brooks withdrew from the conversation, shocked by Dean's reveal.

entities.name: Cantebarius H. Broom
entities.description:
Professor Cantebarius H. Broom was a Human male who worked as a scientist at the Baobab Museum of Science in the early years of the Galactic Empire. He was part of the researchers who studied the remains of the Great Heep, an enormous self-constructing droid. After discovering that the Heep belonged to a species of advanced machines from another galaxy, Broom developed an irrational fear of droids. From then on, the professor would trap droids in his laboratory and experiment on them before turning them into scrap. Around 15 BBY, the scientist captured C-3PO, a protocol unit belonging to Jann Tosh, with the intent to deactivate him and use him for experimentation. The professor's plans, however, were foiled when the droid's master and the astromech R2-D2 intervened.

Cantebarius H. Broom was a male of the Human species who lived during the Dark Times He worked as a scientist, holding the title of professor, and he officiated at the Baobab Museum of Science, Originally, Broom was among the researchers who studied the remains of the Great Heep, a huge droid who had once manned a processing plant on the agriworld of Biitu, The researchers came to the conclusion that the Heep belonged to the Abominor, an extra-galactic species of self-constructing machines, which had forced thousands of organic sentients into slavery. Worse still, it seemed that perhaps as many as seventeen other such abominations had already infiltrated the galaxy.

Following that sensational revelation, Professor Broom developed a phobia of all mechanical life forms, which prompted him to destroy any droid that would fall into his hands.

Around 15 BBY, the professor found a new victim in the protocol unit C-3PO, who belonged to a miner named Jann Tosh. Broom threatened to deactivate C-3PO by removal of his memory diskette. Tosh, however, discovered the trapdoor to Broom's secret laboratory thanks to his other droid, the astromech R2-D2. The miner's timely arrival distracted the professor's attention. While aiming a blaster pistol at Tosh, Broom forgot to look over his shoulders. The scientist was knocked down unconscious by the protocol droid, who hit him with a piece of metal.

entities.name: Broon
entities.description:
Broon was a human male scrumrat of the White Worms gang on the Core Worlds planet Corellia. Around 13 BBY, they and the fellow human scrumrat Fixit helped prepare for a raid on a Corellia shipyard by monitoring the facility in shifts, often taking turns with the Rodian scrumrat Oggro.

In one instance, when Imperial stormtroopers exited a hangar and began scanning the area around the shipyard, Broon and their companion fled back to the den of the White Worms to tell someone, not waiting for Oggro to replace them at their posting. The pair told the older scrumrat Qi'ra of the situation, with Broon indicating they had not yet told the Rodian what they had learned. After promising to pass on the information, she dismissed the boys for dinner.

The human male Broon lived on planet Corellia during the Imperial Era. They eventually joined the White Worms criminal gang as a scrumrat thief and lived within their Coronet City den under Head scrumrat Ema's management, alongside several other orphans. the White Worms prepared to raid a Corellia shipyard to steal control boards under the orders of their leader, Lady Proxima, who hoped the endeavor would result in the deaths of several of her older scrumrats so she could thin her ranks.

As one of the group's younger scrumrats, Broon paired off with the fellow human scrumrat Fixit to monitor the shipyard as a scout. The boys took shifts at a watching post during the day, while the Rodian scrumrat Oggro would come to relieve the boys and take the night shift. One time, while waiting for the Rodian to take their place, they and their partner were surprised to see a large group of Imperial stormtroopers scanning the nearby area as they marched out of the facility's hangar. Broon and Fixit fled their post and returned to the White Worms' den to inform someone of the information, not waiting for Oggro to replace them.

entities.name: Jellion Broon
entities.description:
Jellion Broon was a famous male holovid actor in the decades before the rise of the Galactic Empire. While in Mos Espa on the planet Tatooine as part of a race story he was acting in, Broon became obsessed with the planet's deserts and wandered off to explore the Jundland Wastes. Six months later Broon reappeared, though the twin suns of Tatooine and the wind left him looking weathered and old, with his own agent no longer recognizing him and his former studio employer not wanting to deal with him.

Annileen Calwell would later use the story of Broon as an example to Obi-Wan Kenobi about the importance of keeping his hood on when working under the twin suns of Tatooine.

entities.name: Broonmark
entities.description:
Broonmark was a male Talz who served the Galactic Republic, and later the Sith Empire during the Cold War.

Born into a peaceful clan of Talz on the frozen world Alzoc III, Broonmark had an unquenchable taste for murder and death. While still young, Broonmark's father was killed by a wild beast; Broonmark would resent his father henceforth for failing to kill the beast. Developing a fascination with death, a clan elder denounced him for his violent ways and Broonmark in turn executed the elder. To escape his clan and seek out paths to destruction, Broonmark enlisted in the Galactic Republic military where he was trained and dispatched to the planet Hoth during the Galactic War. A violent leader of the Talz Commandos, Broonmark led campaigns of mass slaughter against the Sith Empire.

His violent ways earned him the disdain of many of his peers and Lieutenant Fetzellen led a mutiny against his leadership. Fleeing his attacks, Broonmark regrouped in a cave to plot the death of his squad mates. In that very cave the Jedi Padawan Sewlor took refuge from the cold as he searched for his Jedi Master Xerender. Knowing that Broonmark was hiding in the cave, Sewlor grew anxious and was unable to fight back when the Talz emerged and snapped his neck. After killing the Padawan, Broonmark confronted and dueled the apprentice of Darth Baras, the future Emperor's Wrath, ending the fight in a draw. Leaving the cave, Broonmark later confronted and executed more traitors from his squad, running into the Wrath while doing so. Eventually, the Wrath found the path to Xerender, but it was guarded by none other than Fetzellen himself. Broonmark arrived shortly afterwards and demanded to be allowed to complete his revenge by killing his old second-in-command, promising to pledge his life to the Wrath in return; the Wrath assented, and after confronting Fetzellen over his betrayal, Broonmark dueled with and finally bludgeoned his mutinous lieutenant to death. From then on, the Wrath permitted Broonmark to accompany him as his personal assassin in his never ending quest for death.

While journeying with the Wrath, Broonmark explained about his past life and how he despised the other Talz. The savage alien expressed satisfaction as he and the Wrath massacred their enemies in their wake, and eventually pledged his full loyalty, promising to train the Wrath's followers in the art of killing.

entities.name: Brooser
entities.description:
Brooser was a large, simian looking Human male born on the planet Celanon. At a height of 2.2 meters and weighing over 150 kilograms, his bulk consisted of all muscle except for a Jargridian Brandy belly around his middle. Brooser was easily provoked and had a passion for fighting and gambling. Nonetheless, he loved his girlfriend, Jezzable, above all else. However, Jezzable's flirtatious attitude toward other males aggravated Brooser's jealousy and penchant for physical violence.

Born on the planet Celanon drove him to the zenith of jealousy.

One afternoon, Brooser was present at Gularg's Libation Emporium, a local drinking establishment, when he noticed that Jezzable was assiduously flirting with a newly arrived smuggler. Having decided that he didn't like the look of the smuggler, Brooser provoked a brawl, in which the other patrons soon joined. The fracas continued until blaster weapons were drawn. At that point, Gularg, the Hutt owner of the locale—and an individual who did not condone the use of firearms in his bar—disarmed the opponents and ended the altercation.

Brooser was a strong, tough working-class man who took pleasure in fighting. Brooser was easily agitated and provoked into displays of violence, especially by Jezzable's provocative actions toward males of all species. Some individuals found Brooser's physical appearance to be anomalous in regard to a standard Human. Standing at a height of 2.2 meters and weighing over 150 kilograms, Brooser was a large man—considerably simian in appearance—whose mass consisted of all muscle, except for a protruding belly gained from the consumption of Jargridian Brandy. At one point, a freighter captain named Jorgan Blech compared Brooser to a Wookiee. What was left of the hapless captain after Brooser was finished with him was then pummeled by a Wookiee for insulting his people.

entities.name: Teso Broosh
entities.description:
Teso Broosh was a human male TIE fighter pilot who held the rank of Second Lieutenant Commander in the Squadron Five within the 204th Imperial Fighter Wing of the Galactic Empire.

Broosh was the leader of Squadron Five of Shadow Wing, appointed by Major Soran Keize. Keize approached Broosh while he was working on his TIE fighter and told him he was going to recommend that Broosh lead the rebuilt Squadron Five. He tried to decline the opportunity, saying he wasn't a natural leader and was afraid of the responsibility. Keize replied that he appreciated that Broosh viewed leadership as a duty and not a stepping stone to greater fame. Broosh claimed that other pilots might not want to follow him due to his reputation as surviving at the cost of his fellow pilots. Keize assured him that he was right man for the job and Broosh accepted the command.

Six months later, he and his squadmates attacked a Rebel cell and managed to destroy all the enemies. He returned to the Star Destroyer Pursuer and told his squad they would be getting a new mission from Commander Shakara Nuress. When he was informed that Squadron Five would be flying escort duty on the mission to recover the Star Destroyer Celerity, he expressed his opinion that it seemed strange. Nuress told Broosh that she was worried that a disabled Star Destroyer was an easy target and wanted to make sure the rescue mission was well protected.

While en route onboard the Summit, he and Lyttan Dree shared a drink and discussed the rumor that Broosh was the kind of leader that sacrificed his pilots to save himself. Broosh told Dree that he was like any other TIE fighter pilot and had only survived as long as he had due to luck. As they approached the Kudo system, Broosh conversed with the captain of the Summit about the upcoming mission. The captain was worried that they were under-staffed, but Broosh assured him that his squad would be ready. After entering the Kudo system, Broosh and the other pilots deployed from the carrier and started to approach the Celerity. Before they could get close, the carrier was disabled by an ion blast from the Star Destroyer, and Squadron Five was engaged by the TIE fighters from the Star Destroyer.

entities.name: Reeg Brosna
entities.description:
Reeg Brosna was an Arcona male pirate in the crew of the Crimson Corsair Sidon Ithano, captain of the Meson Martinet. He and the rest of the crew set out to claim the lost treasure of the Sith Lord Count Dooku from the crashed Separatist cruiser Obrexta III on the planet Ponemah Terminal. While trying to reach the cruiser in the sail barge Shrike, Brosna and his crewmates encountered a sandstorm which the Arcona fired a kinetic disruptor missile into in order to try and freeze it. Before the missile could take effect, Brosna was knocked off the Shrike and into the storm when the Weequay pirate Scorza opened fire on the sail barge. Brosna managed to survive and sometime afterwards, invited his friend Han Solo to Black Spire Outpost on Batuu to celebrate Life Day, but in actuality the invitation was a trap set up to surrender Solo over to the Kanjiklub gang.

Reeg Brosna was a male Arcona who served on board the pirate vessel known as the Meson Martinet in the crew of its captain, the Crimson Corsair Sidon Ithano. five decades after the Clone Wars ended, the pirate crew picked up an emergency broadcast on the planet Ponemah Terminal being transmitted by the long lost Confederacy of Independent Systems cruiser Obrexta III. Believing the cruiser to contain the legendary lost treasure of the Sith Lord Count Dooku, Ithano's crew set out on the retrofitted sail barge Shrike for the Sea of Sands, a dangerous region of Ponemah where the Obrexta III had crashed.

En route, Brosna questioned what the treasure on board the ancient cruiser might be, causing the first mate Quiggold to guess that it might be lightsaber crystals collected by Dooku during the Clone Wars. Before the barge could reach the source of the distress signal, it encountered a large sandstorm which threatened to destroy the vessel. After receiving silent orders from Ithano, Quiggold ordered Brosna to load a kinetic disruptor missile into the barge's torpedo system, which would freeze the sandstorm when it detonated. As Quiggold counted down, Brosna prepared the missile's targeting system and then loaded it, firing without hesitation on the count of one while whispering with his eyes closed. Brosna successfully hit his target, but before the missile could detonate, the Weequay pirate Scorza, who was also seeking to claim Dooku's treasure, opened fire on the Shrike with the cannons on board his skiff. Caught off guard, Brosna was knocked from the sail barge by the attack and immediately swept away by the sand maelstrom.

entities.name: Udo Broxin
entities.description:
Udo Broxin was a Herglic who was a regular at the entertainment and gambling establishment known as the Ace of Sabres on the planet Kluistar.

Udo was a fixture at the Ace of Sabres for as long as anyone could remember. The manager, Gandin T'Noull, even allowed the Herglic's large bar tab to go largely unpaid since Udo's presence always had such a positive effect on the atmosphere of the Ace of Sabers.

Udo was witty, sarcastic and outgoing. He enjoyed nothing more than a good drink, a game of sabacc and a brawl before bed. His good humor and sense of fun lifted the other patrons mood. He was loud and boisterous, and had the tendency to draw others to his mayhem and mischief.

He referred to himself as "Uncle Udo" and was always willing to dispense advice to those that were willing to listen. He also had a tendency to ramble on even when no-one was listening.

entities.name: Broysc
entities.description:
Broysc was a Human male who served as Moff during the Great Galactic War, Cold War and Galactic Wars between the Galactic Republic and resurgent Sith Empire.

Moff Broysc was Lieutenant Malavai Quinn's commanding officer at the Battle of Druckenwell during the Great Galactic War. Quinn, disobeying Broysc's orders, was able to correct his glaring oversight and achieve an Imperial victory, but Broysc court-martialed Quinn for insubordination and took credit for the victory himself. As a punishment, Broysc got Quinn assigned to Balmorra, where the lieutenant was absorbed into Darth Baras' field of operations.

Descending further into madness over the years, Broysc almost doomed the command of Major Ovech and later began sending regular transmissions to the ship where now-Captain Quinn served - the Fury-class Imperial interceptor belonging to the Sith Lord who would become the Emperor's Wrath. Eventually being put through, Broysc began to rant on the holotransmitter against Quinn. Referring to him as "Admiral Malcontent", believing it to be Quinn's actual rank and name, Broysc began blaming him for events that occurred well before Quinn, or even Broysc himself, were born, such as the Battle of Talay, Broysc's first command, and the Destruction of Taris, which had occurred three centuries earlier. He also accused Quinn of sabotaging the Glory Space Station, which Quinn had no clue what it was.

With his lord's permission, Quinn began to find ways to bring Broysc's incompetence and madness to the attention of the Imperial High Command, but to no avail; Broysc's political and military connections would not allow him to be removed through the proper channels. Thus, taking matters into his own hands, Quinn abducted Broysc from a pleasure barge where he had been holed up while battle was ongoing, and brought him to the Wrath's ship. Clearly mad, Broysc ordered the Wrath to surrender the vessel and its crew to his command and even kill themselves to everyone present. His patience stretched to breaking point, Quinn requested the Wrath's permission to execute the Moff, and the Sith granted it.

entities.name: Brrang
entities.description:
Brrang was a member of the Ranc Gang. He served under Wenda and Bett until the former stormtrooper Terex took over the group in 7 ABY. Brrang commanded the Carrion Spike and the Ranc Gang's fleet of "Uglies" during the Battle over a desert planet.

Brrang was a member of the Ranc Gang during the New Republic Era, which was led by Wenda and Bett, who ran a large ship and salvage operation based on the Outer Rim world of Kaddak. In 7 ABY, he and his fellow Ranc Gang associates including Wenda, Bett, Zumgi, and Wisper entered the Rothana Imperial Shipyards with the help of the former stormtrooper Terex.

After Terex joined the First Order, Wisper took over leadership of the gang. In 34 ABY, Terex returned to Kaddak to retake control of the Ranc Gang and use them to destroy the Resistance, an independent paramilitary faction aligned the New Republic. After Zumgi killed Wisper for contesting Terex's leadership, Brrang joined the rest of the gang in reaffirming their loyalty to Terex. Brrang and Zumgi accompanied Terex aboard his flagship Carrion Spike as they embarked on their hunt for the Resistance starfighter pilot Poe Dameron, who had escaped with the BX-series droid commando N1-ZX. While N1-ZX was purportedly carrying information about the First Order, this was a ruse created by Terex in order to track down and destroy the Resistance.

During the pursuit, Brrang informed Terex that Poe's T-70 X-wing starfighter was still generating a strong signal despite entering hyperspace. Terex thanked Brrang and instructed Zumgi to prepare the fleet and inform him when Poe had re-entered realspace. However, Poe figured out Terex's plan and exited hyperspace above a desert planet. Brrang then informed Terex that they were in the middle of nowhere and were receiving no readings from a base. Brrang realized that Poe had figured their plan and had deliberately led them away from the Resistance base. Terex then decided to kill Poe instead.

Vonddado Briimyo was a Neimoidian male who worked as a Mechanic during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire.

In 3643 BBY, Briimyo worked with the gangster Skavak and was forced to repair the ship, which belonged to the Smuggler Ace. He encountered Ace, who was here to find Skavak and retrieve the stolen Arkanian Hyperdrive. Briimyo was able to tell Ace where the Skavak was, and begged the smuggler to let him go. When Ace allowed to leave, Briimyo thanked the smuggler and fled.

entities.name: Bruckman
entities.description:
Sergeant Bruckman was a Corellian male who was picked by General Han Solo to act as point man for an Alliance to Restore the Republic strike team of commandos that was deployed to the moon of Endor in 4 ABY. The team's aim was to destroy a shield generator on the moon that was protecting the Imperial Death Star II superweapon above.

Bruckman was among the team members that entered the security bunker at the rear of the generator where they began placing charges; however, they were captured by Imperial forces that had laid a trap for them. An army of local Ewoks then attacked the Imperials, allowing Bruckman and the others to also turn on their captors. Ultimately the Alliance destroyed the generator and the Death Star.

Bruckman was a human male from the planet Corellia. During the Galactic Civil War between the Alliance to Restore the Republic and the Galactic Empire, he served as a sergeant in the Alliance Military. In 4 ABY, General Han Solo, a fellow Corellian, chose Bruckman to act as point man for a strike team of commandos he was leading during the Battle of Endor, in which the Alliance aimed to destroy the Empire's Death Star II superweapon in the Endor system. The team's role would be to disable the Death Star's shield generator, which was located on the moon of Endor.

After the team deployed to Endor in the stolen Imperial shuttle Tydirium, they landed in a clearing some distance from the generator and worked their way slowly through the dense undergrowth to the relative safety of the surrounding forest. Solo and some other leading members of the team became separated from the others, and the general ordered Major Bren Derlin to lead Bruckman and the others to regroup with them at the generator at 03:00 hours the next morning. By the time they regrouped, Solo and the others had formed an alliance with a local tribe of Ewoks. Together, the Alliance forces and the Ewoks proceeded to a security bunker that acted as the generator's rear entrance, and after the Ewok Paploo drew away most of the guards, Bruckman and several other members of the team accompanied Solo inside.

entities.name: Driscoll Bruhnej
entities.description:
Driscoll Bruhnej was a Human male from the planet Alderaan and the twin brother of Trey Bruhnej. In 0 BBY, Alderaan was destroyed by the Galactic Empire's first Death Star, sending Driscoll and Trey, as well as thousands of Alderaanian refugees to Alderaan's sister planet Delaya.

When Princess Leia Organa visited Delaya to help the refugees, as well as recruit soldiers for the Rebel Alliance, Driscoll and his brother were among an Alderaanian faction that resented Organa's involvement with the Rebellion, blaming her for their homeworld's destruction. Their group abducted Organa then planned to turn her over to the Empire in exchange for a new planet to settle on. However, the Imperials reneged on the deal and took Organa after killing her abductors. Driscol and his brother were the first to die, acting as guards to their group's hideout.

A prisoner exiled to Kiffex, he was hired by Gorto Zaga to defend the local settlement's walls against the attacking Anzati. His standing orders were to shoot anyone who tried to enter at night; as a result, he attempted to kill the Devaronian Vilmarh Grahrk and his Jedi companions. After entering the city, Tholme used a mind trick, causing Bruiser to forget the affair entirely.

entities.description:
Patch Bruit was Lommite Limited's chief of field operations in 33 BBY. Although he served the company for nearly twenty years, working his way up from the lommite pits, he had long dreamed of starting over and relocating to Coruscant or one of the other Core worlds and making a new life for himself. After being ordered by Jurnel Arrant to hire the Toom clan to sabotage rival InterGalactic Ore, the Tooms betrayed him and sabotaged both LL and InterGal. Working with Caba'Zan, he led an assault on the clan's hideout on Riome. Following the clan's defeat, he was Force choked to death by Darth Maul, who went on to frame Bruit for his actions sabotaging the two companies.

After having been on Despayre for many years, he managed to work his way up into a position of trust with the dirtside guards. Using his position, Brun assisted a fellow prisoner, Celot Ratua Dil, escape Despayre.

entities.description:
Danbit Brun was a human male lieutenant in the Galactic Empire who served as a shield relay systems operator onboard the Shield Gate positioned above the planet Scarif. His job required him to carefully monitor field dynamics to prevent dangerous build up from stellar wind aurorae. In 1 BBY, he was killed when the remnants of the Persecutor and the Intimidator, two Star Destroyers destroyed in the Battle of Scarif, drifted into the gate and destroyed it. Brun had fair skin and gray hair and wore a black version of the Imperial technician's uniform with a cap.

Danbit Brun first appeared in the film Rogue One: A Star Wars Story, which was released in North America on December 15, 2016. He was not identified in the film, but was named by the reference book Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide, which was written by Pablo Hidalgo and released the day after the film.

entities.description:
Deca Brun ran for governor in the Galacian Gubernatorial election He received widespread support, as he promised reform and prosperity. However, Brun had made a deal with Offworld Mining Corporation, promising them exclusive mining rights which would have caused extensive environmental damage in exchange for campaign funding. Obi-Wan Kenobi discovered this deal, and this was revealed before the election. Thus Wila Prammi, another candidate, won the election by a vast majority.

entities.name: Pemmin Brunce
entities.description:
Pemmin Brunce was an Ongidae male who was the head of security for the Canto Casino in the city of Canto Bight on the planet Cantonica.

Although Brunce and his bouncers were responsible for dealing with the day to day security at the casino, the Canto Bight Police Department could be called in to handle the most major disturbances. He and his team used silent hand signals to communicate. During the Cold War between the First Order and the Resistance, Brunce spotted the former casino employee Kaljach Sonmi inside the building and tried to throw him out; however, the Suerton gambler Dodibin helped Sonmi earn enough cantocoins in a hazard toss bet to meet the minimum amount needed for him to remain and so Brunce let him be. Brunce had pink skin and gray eyes and was the only employee in the casino permitted to scowl. He wore a pair of black pants and boots with smartly tailored black jacket that concealed a stun baton.

Pemmin Brunce was created for the film Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi, which was released on December 15, 2017; however, prior to the films release he appeared in the short story "The Ride," which was written by John Jackson Miller and released as part of the Canto Bight anthology on December 5, 2017. Brunce was portrayed by creature and droid performer Cavin Cornwall in the film, with puppeteer Mark Jefferis controlling the character's animatronic facial expressions.

entities.name: Sam Brunk
entities.description:
Sam Brunk was a male Human moisture farmer who lived on Tatooine during the time of the Galactic Empire. He was the husband of Dama Whitesun Brunk.

Sam Brunk and his wife Dama lived in the town of Anchorhead. Along with moisture farming, the two also operated a hotel. The two occupations kept both busy to the point that they infrequently visited the family of Dama's sister, Beru Lars, who lived twenty kilometers from Anchorhead.

Around 15 BBY, the couple got a new A-1 Deluxe Floater landspeeder. Some time after, the Brunks visited the Lars homestead. There, Sam gave the recent news of Podracing being outlawed by the Galactic Empire. During the visit, Sam was surprised to find that Beru's husband, Owen Lars, had removed his relatives' headstones from their graves at the homestead.

The Rebels took the workers' uniforms so they could infiltrate the Tarkin as part of a construction crew.

entities.name: Lancer Brunou
entities.description:
Lancer Brunou was a Human male doctor of archaeology at the University of Byblos during the Galactic Civil War. Loyal to the Galactic Empire, Brunou despaired for the stability of the galaxy following the death of Emperor Palpatine at the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY. Feeling helpless that he could not help in restoring order, he resigned from his post and wandered the Outer Rim Territories, visiting archaeological digs. During his travels, he heard that Moff Kentor Sarne was attempting to forge a new empire from his capital planet of Kal'Shebbol in the Kathol sector. Brunou traveled to Kal'Shebbol and joined the Moff's forces.

Welcomed by the Moff, Brunou was initially assigned to study examples of the mysterious DarkStryder technology. However, he was quickly reassigned by Sarne to lead science team MS-133 on a mission to the planet Aaris III. Brunou's objectives were to investigate a series of ruins on the planet that belonged to a long-dead civilization, with particular emphasis on what caused the society's destruction. Brunou and his team established a base camp and began excavating the ruins. On day 49 of the expedition, they discovered the Plaque of Victory—a powerful artifact that fed off organic life forces and compelled them to destroy each other—although they were unaware of its true nature.

As the influence of the Plaque began to take hold of the members of the science team, they began to experience paranoid delusions and feelings of being watched and spied on. They were subsequently attacked by the primitive descendants of the native Aaris, and Brunou sought to escape the planet. However, the destruction of their shuttle hampered his plans, and he was forced to send a distress signal to Kal'Shebbol in the hopes of a rescue. However, during his time on Aaris III, Kal'Shebbol had fallen to New Republic forces, and the transmission was intercepted by the crew of the CR90 corvette FarStar. Responding to the distress call, they rescued Brunou and his research assistant, Solla Deremot, the last survivors of the team. However, Brunou had brought the Plaque of Victory aboard the FarStar, and it began to exert its influence over the crew. Fortunately for the FarStar crew, personnel on the corvette figured out that the Plaque was responsible for the change in the behavior of the crew, and jettisoned it out of an airlock.

The Human male Doctor Lancer Brunou was an archaeologist and respected member of the faculty at the University of Byblos, during the reign of the Galactic Empire. A loyal adherent to the ideals of the Empire, Brunou felt that the stability of the galaxy was threatened when Emperor Palpatine was killed at the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY. Feeling helpless that he could do nothing to assist in restoring stability to the galaxy, he resigned his position and traveled through the Outer Rim Territories for several years, visiting archaeological dig sites and constantly looking for a purpose to dedicate his life to.

entities.name: Habbala Brupt
entities.description:
Habbala Brupt was a male Sullustan and a spy for the Galactic Empire.

Habbala was fleeing his homeworld as a passenger on a transport heading to Corellia. Unfortunately, during the trip, the ship was boarded by the Empire and subjected to a search. The boarding party found Rebel sympathizers aboard, and the Imperial officer in charge of the operation ordered the extermination of everyone on the ship. The Sullustan begged for his life and offered to do anything in exchange for mercy. The Imperial officer considered the value of a spy from a species not known to indulge in such activities. The boarding party chose to spare Habbala's life, unlike any others on the transport ship.

The Imperials assigned Habbala to N'zoth, the homeworld of the xenophobic Yevetha species. Eventually he found Werstilhere, an offworlder settlement on N'zoth, and settled there with hope to find a means to leave the planet and return to the Empire.

entities.name: Brusc
entities.description:
Brusc was a captain in the Imperial Starfleet and commanding officer of the Imperial I-class Star Destroyer Manticore in the Maw fleet.

In 0 BBY, Brusc was one of the Imperial officers assigned to protect the Maw Installation, an Imperial research center established by Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin in the midst of the Maw Cluster. As captain of the Imperial I-class Star Destroyer Manticore, he served in the fleet of four Imperial I-class Star Destroyers. Brusc and his ship were placed under the command of Admiral Natasi Daala.

In 11 ABY, Brusc and the Manticore participated in the pursuit of the experimental superweapon Sun Crusher, stolen by Han Solo, Chewbacca, Kyp Durron and Qwi Xux from the Maw Installation. However, Daala's Star Destroyers emerged in the middle of Moruth Doole's mercenary fleet and were engaged by the hostile spacecraft. In the battle, the combined fire of the Manticore and Basilisk annihilated a Strike-class medium cruiser, causing the remaining mercenary ships to flee to hyperspace. Brusc and the Manticore survived the Skirmish in the Maw, but the Sun Crusher escaped and its passengers informed the New Republic of the existence of the Maw Installation. Brusc and the Manticore accompanied with Daala in her guerrilla campaign against the New Republic. The first combat operation in which Brusc participated was the brutal massacre of the refugees and total destruction of their colony in Dantooine.

Brusc and the Manticore were charged with the destruction of the Mon Calamari orbital shipyards during the attack on Mon Calamari. As the Gorgon and the Basilisk caused heavy damage to floating cities on the surface of the planet, the Manticore approached the shipyards. However, a responding squadron of B-wing starfighters were successful in distracting the Manticore while the MC90 Star Cruiser Startide was remotely piloted by Admiral Gial Ackbar to collide with the Star Destroyer. The collision with the Startide caused a massive explosion, destroying the Manticore and killing its crew, including Brusc. Daala was enraged by the loss of the Manticore, but she was forced to withdraw as the New Republic Defense Fleet arrived to the battle.

entities.name: Tophid Bruster
entities.description:
Tophid Bruster, designated DT-4431, was a lieutenant TIE fighter pilot in the Starfighter Corps of the First Order. In 35 ABY, Bruster piloted a TIE/fo space superiority fighter as part of a group sent to destroy the YT-1300 light freighter known as the Millennium Falcon while it was on a mission to the Sinta Glacier Colony. Bruster engaged the freighter, but it ultimately escaped.

Lieutenant Tophid Bruster was a human male TIE Fighter Pilot with the designation DT-4431 who served in the Starfighter Corps of the First Order during the war against the Resistance. In 35 ABY, he flew in a TIE/fo space superiority fighter as part of a squadron sent to the Sinta Glacier Colony in order to track down the Resistance YT-1300 light freighter known as the Millennium Falcon. The TIE fighters split up into several groups, with Bruster's moving down an ice corridor within the glacier.

The group spotted the Falcon docked further down the corridor, where its crew members Finn, Poe Dameron, Klaud, R2-D2 and Chewbacca were transferring data from the Resistance sympathizer Boolio. Bruster locked on to the vessel, but it undocked and began to escape, shooting down one member of Bruster's group and then crushing two other TIE fighters by causing part of the corridor's ceiling to collapse. The Falcon ultimately escaped the colony by flying through an ice wall and hyperspace skipping away.

Tophid Bruster wore the standard black uniform and flight helmet of a First Order TIE pilot. The helmet had data projected onto its interior viewplate and the uniform's chestplate had a life support control center attached.

entities.name: Brutann
entities.description:
Brutann was a male Human Beast-Lord of Onderon and a Sith serving the reconstituted Sith Empire on the planet of Hoth during the Galactic War.

Brutann was serving as a secret weapon of the Sith Empire, controlling local predators to attack Republic expeditions. Jedi Master Heljus perished in one of such attacks, but lived long enough to ask a Republic hero for help. This Republic hero tracked and killed Brutann and many of his creatures.

In the Onslaught storyline, it is revealed that Brutann was originally from Onderon, and was from a group of people known as the Untamed. He was siblings with the Beast-Lord Akoru. According to Darth Savik, his master served Darth Jadus before the latter's disappearance.

Konur desired a lightsaber, and so got the location of Brutt's warehouse on Wayland from him.

Brutt was later spoken to by agents of Luke Skywalker who had tasked them with capturing Konur.

entities.name: Brutus
entities.description:
Brutus was a Shistavanen male pirate captain active during the New Republic Era. He was originally the First Mate of the crew led by Captain Silvo, although the pirates fell on hard times under Silvo's leadership. Around 9 ABY, Brutus led a mutiny against the captain following a raid on a merchant freighter that had been carrying a single credit. The Shistavanen took command of the crew, and subsequently travelled to the pirate—controlled asteroid starport Port Borgo. At the starport, Brutus and his pirates captured a group of lost children from the mythical planet At Attin. However, the children escaped aboard the starship Onyx Cinder with the assistance of Silvo, who went by the name Jod Na Nawood, and Brutus had a bounty placed on the former captain.

After Na Nawood was captured, Brutus oversaw his trial and sentenced him to death by airlock. However, the former captain delayed his fate by revealing that he could grant the pirates the treasure of At Attin. Although Brutus was skeptical, the pirates embarked to the legendary planet, finding it concealed by the treacherous Barrier. When Na Nawood's claims were seemingly proven false, Brutus intended to execute the former captain once more, but was interrupted by the arrival of the Onyx Cinder, crewed by the children from At Attin. After learning the Onyx Cinder was the key to safe passage through the Barrier, Brutus and the pirates captured the ancient vessel. As Brutus boarded the Onyx Cinder, however, the children used the vessel's cargo lift to seize him. With Brutus trapped in the lift's claw, Na Nawood shot and killed the Shistavanen with his own blaster, taking command of the crew once again.

The Shistavanen male pirate Brutus served as First Mate of the crew led by Captain Silvo during the New Republic Era. The crew operated aboard a pirate frigate, seeking valuable cargo and treasure throughout the galaxy. Around 9 ABY, the pirates fell upon several lean cycles, and subsequently some of the crew lost hope in Silvo. During that time, the crew captured and breached a merchant freighter, boarding the vessel as its merchant crew attempted to fend them off. After the other pirates had began to overpower the freighter's crew, Brutus boarded the starship wielding two blasters, firing upon the remaining merchants. Once Brutus had eliminated the last of their foes, he called back to Silvo to report their success, stepping aside to allow the captain to enter.

Bruzo was a Pantoran male who lived at the Barakat Outpost on the planet E'ronoh. he challenged Princess Xiri A'lbaran with an archaic E'roni rite, believing that she was not worthy of E'ronoh's throne. A'lbaran won the challenge, however, when she wasn't looking Bruzo tried to charge at her again, but he was stopped by her fiancée, Prince Phan-tu Zenn of Eiram, who punched Bruzo in the face before he could reach her.

Bruzo was created for the 2022 adult novel The High Republic: Convergence, written by Zoraida Córdova.

entities.name: Bry
entities.description:
Bry was a Hoopaloo male thief who worked with fellow criminals Jorkat and Velek during the Republic Era. At a celebration on the planet Serenno in 90 BBY, Bry stole a purse from the Serennian Lady Jenza. Although Bry and his associates restrained Jenza and her brother Ramil, the Jedi Initiate Dooku confronted the criminals. Dooku used the Force to throw the Hoopaloo through the air before revealing his presence and fighting Jorkat with an electroblade. The Jedi eventually scared Bry and his accomplices away, saving Jenza and Ramil. Dooku recounted the incident in a holo-letter to Jenza, a recording of which he later showed to his newly-recruited Sith assassin, Asajj Ventress, around 23 BBY.

The Hoopaloo Bry and his associates were present in Carannia, the capital city of the Outer Rim planet Serenno, attending a celebration for the worlds of the region. During the celebration, Bry stole the purse of the young Serennian Lady Jenza—daughter of Count Gora of House Serenno—swiping the item while roughly brushing past her. Bry fled and hid behind a repulsor tent, rummaging through the purse's contents. Jenza pursued, snatching the bag back, and the Hoopaloo reprimanded the girl for doing so. When Jenza noticed that a crystal that had belonged to her grandmother was missing, she questioned Bry, who feigned ignorance.

At that point, Jorkat and Velek approached from behind Jenza, and Bry claimed that the girl had stolen his purse. When Jenza protested, Jorkat called her selfish and asserted that the Hoopaloo had no credits to his name; the Karkarodon suggested stealing the Serennian's coat to give to Bry, who agreed that it would warm his feathers. After Jorkat grabbed Jenza to search her belongings and the girl's brother Ramil was restrained by Velek when he arrived in an attempt to defend his sister, Bry suggested kidnapping the pair and taking them to Renza, although the Karkarodon was unsure whether the Hutt would be interested. Jenza bit Jorkat and escaped his grip, and Bry attempted to catch her.

However, Bry suddenly found himself thrown through the air, having been pushed using the Force by the Jedi Initiate Dooku, who had sensed a connection with Jenza—unbeknownst to both, his sister—and followed the girl. Bry cried out, insisting that something had knocked him down when questioned by his bewildered Karkarodon accomplice. Dooku revealed his presence, wielding an electroblade against Jorkat. Bry attempted to intervene but was once again pushed back by Dooku. Velek was soon thrown into the Hoopaloo, almost crushing Bry when the Askajian stood up to run away. Although Jorkat remained aggravated at Dooku, Bry pleaded with his accomplice and the pair also fled.
