entities.name: Calder Brya
entities.description:
Calder Byra was a blue-eyed socialite connected to the planet Coruscant's high society.

Calder Brya was a young Human male socialite with connections to the highest levels of society on the Core Worlds planet Coruscant. A rich man of noble birth, he had over one million credits in his bank account and was also a shockball player.

Brya had brown hair, blue eyes, light skin, and a fit and trim build. He was also considered good-looking. Byra had the natural gift of connecting with people, and despite being the type of rich socialite people loved to hate, his worst critics walked away with a positive outlook on him. Byra's sense of humor was self-deprecating and disarming.

The socialite could speak, read, and write with the Basic, Huttese, and Ryl languages. He also spoke Rodese, though could not read or write it.

entities.name: Hawker Bryce-Kelley
entities.description:
Hawker Bryce-Kelley was a male Human smuggler who was the owner of both the medium freighter Royal Mistress and the bulk freighter Queen's Victory along with his co-pilot Rypka during the Galactic Civil War.

Hawker Bryce-Kelley and his Twi'lek co-pilot Rypka wandered Outer Rim as smugglers. The duo once met with a group of wannabe Rebels in the Mos Eisley Cantina and arranged to race their ship, the Limping Lady, with the Queen's Victory to whichever system they chose. He waited in orbit above Tatooine for them and they proceeded to race to the planet Zoma V in the Zoma system. After the race, he invited the group on board his ship for drinks and to transfer the credits.

Sometime after this, Bryce-Kelly was being pursued by Imperial Customs Frigate 517 and came to the Reginard system, following a Stellar-class starport beacon which had in fact been planted in the Rebel passive sensor array by Imperial spy Tanya Madera. He soon met with a group of Rebels on the planet who were investigating why his ship had landed so close to their sensor array. He explained to them what had happened, and that he was angry that there wasn't a starport nearby. When the group asked him where this starport was meant to be, he pointed towards the hill which the sensor array was located upon.

When the group went to investigate, they were attacked by Madera who no longer posed as a spy. Bryce-Kelly and Rypka joined in the fight, quickly killing Madera. The trouble was not over, however, as the Imperial Customs Frigate which had been chasing them soon arrived in the system also. The group of Rebels managed to convince the crew of the ship that Bryce-Kelly was not on the planet, and so they soon left, leaving Bryce-Kelly with the Rebels.

entities.description:
Gursan Bryes was a male Bothan from Kachirho, Kashyyyk. He was helping the residents of Kachirho defeat the "Enslaver of Kachirho," Lord Cyssc Blackscale. This confrontation came down to the heroes willing to help against the many space forces of Lord Cyssc. In the end, the heroes reigned supreme, and Kachirho was free of Lord Cyssc's wrath. Each was presented with a Kaminoan great staff by Bryes.

Gursan Bryes appeared as a non-player character in the video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed by Sony and published by LucasArts, prior to its closure on December 15, 2011.

entities.description:
Bryint was a male Human Republic soldier who served in the Republic Army of the Galactic Republic's during the Cold War and Galactic War against the reconstituted Sith Empire, during which he was stationed on the space station Carrick Station.

Bryint appeared in Star Wars: The Old Republic, a video game released in 2011, as the Ord Mantell Commendations Vendor on Carrick Station, though with the retirement of the planetary commendation system Bryint was relabeled as a Level 8 Equipment Vendor. He was removed along with the rest of the planetary Equipment Vendors in Game Update 4.0 on October 20, 2015.

entities.description:
Hiem Bryl was head of operations for Verga Mer Mining Company's operations on Tilnes. He was a gaunt Sullustan with slightly sunken cheeks. He did not speak Basic well, so he tended to speak slowly. He preferred letting underlings deal with outsiders, but was not sure they would do so appropriately, so he met with those who came to the mines with questions.

Bryl was a fan of Sullustan sports, and kept images and trophies of such sporting events in his office. He was an accomplished deep-miner, with a degree from a mining school on Sullust. He was popular with his workers, and was able to motivate them easily.

entities.name: Brylin
entities.description:
Brylin was a Human male who served as Spokesman for the ruling Herdessan Guild on his home planet of Herdessa during the Galactic Civil War. In 4 ABY, after the Galactic Empire's climactic defeat at Endor, Brylin led the Herdessan Guild in meeting with a delegation from the Alliance of Free Planets to establish formal diplomatic relations. Arrogant in the Herdessan Guild's control of the world and an enthusiastic participant in the Herdessan practice of slavery, Brylin and his confederates instead took Alliance leader Mon Mothma, intending to deliver her and the world to an Imperial remnant force. However, fellow Alliance diplomat Leia Organa led an armed Herdessan revolt that overthrew the Herdessan Guild's power and toppling Brylin's scheme.

entities.name: Bryn
entities.description:
Bryn was a Human male captain who served in the Special Forces of the reconstituted Sith Empire. During the Cold War, around 3643 BBY, he was stationed on the Sith capital planet of Dromund Kaas, where he performed reconnaissance on Lord Grathan, a rogue Sith Lord who had declared himself the thirteenth member of the Dark Council.

Bryn held the rank of captain within Imperial Special Forces during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. At one point during his career, he was stationed on a bridge on the Sith capital planet of Dromund Kaas between the Wall and the estate of rogue Sith Lord Grathan, At this position, he was tasked with keeping watch on Grathan while maintaining his distance. As part of his orders, he was to retrieve the plans for a prototype turret that his superiors wanted to mass-produce, but his orders also specified that he could not enter Grathan's territory. He requested the aid of a passing individual affiliated with the Sith Empire to retrieve the plans.

The Imperial individual successfully infiltrated Grathan's compound, retrieving a security badge from a member of Lord Grathan's forces in order to pass by its automated defenses. The individual broke into Grathan's weapons lab and downloaded the plans from the databanks of the droid PO-12, much to its chagrin; it wanted to destroy the schematics and ensure no more turrets could be built. Upon the individual's return, Bryn displayed an eagerness to test the efficacy of the turrets on Republic personnel.

After the individual's mission, Bryn remained posted on the bridge, continuing to keep watch over Grathan's estate.

entities.description:
Bryson was a Human male major of the Imperial Diplomatic Service who served the Sith Empire during the Cold War. Bryson worked with Vector Hyllus and Anora at one point in his career.

Bryson first appeared in the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic, but the mission that he would have introduced on the planet Dromund Kaas was cut from the game before release. Bryson would have sent players to speak with Captain Guyvar, who they needed to convince to send one of his Chevin workers to the Diplomatic Service in order to impress visiting Chevin diplomats.

entities.name: Bryti
entities.description:
Bryti was a humanoid male that served as a butler to fugitive Jedi Master Kai Hudorra following his acquisition of The Lucky Twi'lek on Kestavel. His wide head was fitted with a Borg Construct Aj^6 headband.

When Dass Jennir, Beyghor Sahdett, and the crew of the Uhumele arrived at the casino in search of Hudorra, the Bothan told Bryti to provide the crew he was not speaking with with accommodations on the house. Following Sahdett's betrayal and subsequent report of Hudorra's Jedi status to the Galactic Empire, Bryti, along with several of Hudorra's other servants, reaffirmed that they would stand by him no matter what. Following hatching an assassination attempt on Darth Vader, who was leading the oncoming attack personally, Bryti attended the pre-fight feast, where he served Jennir drugged wine on orders of his master. Hudorra would fall in his fight against Vader, and Jennir would awake aboard the escaping Uhumele, where Bryti gave him a holodisc containing his master's final farewell to his old friend.

entities.name: Errad Brytok
entities.description:
Errad Brytok was a Human male lieutenant in the Imperial Navy, and a Sergeant Major during the time of the Galactic Civil War. Sometime after the Battle of Yavin in 0 BBY, he was second in command to Captain Gilad Pellaeon, aboard the Chimaera.

Errad Brytok was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts. The game was shut down on December 15, 2011. Although not mentioned in the quest dialogue, examining Brytok (identified as Lt. Errad Brytok in the game) revealed him to also be a Sergeant Major. As Errad Brytok was repeatedly identified as a lieutenant of the Imperial Navy, this additional rank of sergeant major displayed in the examination window was likely a result of game mechanics, and may or may not be canon. It may not have been impossible, however, for Errad Brytok to have held the additional rank of sergeant major in another branch of the Military, such as the Imperial Army.

entities.name: Trypto Buball
entities.description:
Trypto Buball was an alien male agricultural baron who grew wealthy due to the vast space-fungi farming colonies that his family owned. he was a guest at the Canto Casino and Racetrack in the city Canto Bight on the planet Cantonica and was standing near a row of gaming machines when fellow patron Dobbu Scay mistook the astromech droid BB-8 for one of the devices.

Buball was later standing in the casino crowds near BB-8's companions Finn and Rose Tico when the pair spotted the gambler known as the Master Codebreaker. While at the casino, the baron wore a black suit with a white trim along with black boots, white chaps, and a white padded collar. He used a dark blue and silver cane to walk and had dark pink skin, yellow eyes, and a gray mustache.

Trypto Buball first appeared in the sequel trilogy film Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi, Concept art of the character was created by Jake Lunt Davies and during production Buball was known as "Turkey Guy." The character was portrayed by Aidan Cook and unused B-roll footage of Buball shows him on other parts of the casino floor, including a close-up of the alien looking over the shoulder of a human casino guest. The character was first identified in the reference book Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary, which was written by Pablo Hidalgo

entities.name: Buboicullaar
entities.description:
Buboicullaar, or Bubo for short, was a frog-dog male that was kept as a pet by the Hutt crime lord Jabba the Hutt, who used him as a guard dog. He lived in Jabba's palace on the desert planet Tatooine and foiled many assassination despite most people thinking he was not more than an unintelligent pest. The Gran Ree-Yees was assigned to take care of the frog-dog, but on one occasion lost track of him aboard Jabba's sail barge, the Khetanna. The Gran promised Jabba that he would find his charge and clean the barge, but Buboicullaar avoided his keeper while Ree-Yees searched. Once the Gran believed he had run out of time, Jabba simply summoned Buboicullaar by calling his name.

In 4 ABY, Buboicullaar barked at the protocol droid C-3PO as the droid entered Jabba's throne room with the astromech droid R2-D2 to deliver a message to Jabba from the Jedi Knight Luke Skywalker. Later that day, the frog-dog was present for a performance of the song "Jedi Rocks" by the Max Rebo Band which ended in the enslaved dancer Oola being fed to Jabba's pet rancor, Pateesa. Buboicullaar then witnessed Princess Leia Organa, disguised as the bounty hunter Boushh, threaten Jabba and his court with a thermal detonator while trying to negotiate over the bounty on the Wookiee Chewbacca.

Buboicullaar, also known as just "Bubo," was a frog-dog male that lived in the palace of the Hutt crime lord Jabba Desilijic Tiure on the desert planet Tatooine. and protected him from many assassination attempts, The Gran Ree-Yees was tasked with unglamorous job of taking care of Buboicullaar but on one occasion lost track of the frog-dog on board Jabba's sail barge, the Khetanna, while it was out traveling on Tatooine.

Pleading for his life, the Gran promised to find Buboicullaar while also cleaning the entire sail barge so that his charge would not be tempted to wonder off again. Jabba then gave Ree-Yees the time it would take for the Khetanna to return to the palace to make good on his promises. Buboicullaar moved around the barge ignoring Ree-Yees as the Gran cleaned and called out for the frog-dog. When Ree-Yees laid out a plate of fecal worms, Buboicullaar's favorite food, as bait, the guard dog simply ate the worms when the Gran's back was turned and continued to avoid him.

entities.name: Buck
entities.description:
Buck was a Green Forge ecoterrorist. A muscular opportunist, he would have affairs with wealthy women and use them to achieve his Green Forge ends. While the affairs' cause being information gathering for sabotage against environment-unfriendly tycoons and their installations, Buck usually made off with shares from his widowed lovers. Buck's latest target is Tibanna-mining Yorn Skot mining station and its owner, Clode Rhoden.

Becoming the illicit lover and supposed personal trainer of Madam Rhoden, Buck sneaked a core bomb aboard the Aurorient Express (which is also a property of Clode) with the intention of blowing up both the properties and owner himself. However, their plan was collided with numerous parties including pirate-infiltrator Podlong Foahl and foreknowing Clode. Podlong had activated his own time-triggered core bomb and Clode ordered the ship's captain to place Buck's core bomb in the pair's escape pod. Fortunately, they were informed by Saul Moegantz, who won the Madame's affection. After the ship had been evacuated, Podlong's bomb went off and destroyed both Aurorient and the pirate vessel.

A serial bomber himself, Buck process intimate knowledge about core bomb and were able to recognize Podlong's threat by identifying his bomb switch. He also claimed to know eight forms of the martial art Tae-Jitsu and assumed proper stance, yet he was easily overcome by young Obi-wan Kenobi.

entities.name: Torban Buck
entities.description:
Torban Buck, nicknamed "Buckets of Blood," was a Chagrian male Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order as a healer during the High Republic Era. Alongside Master Yoda, Buck was stationed aboard the Jedi Padawan academic cruiser Star Hopper when the cruiser and its passengers were forced to respond to fallout from the Great Hyperspace Disaster in the Trymant system. He and Yoda intended to handle the largest pieces of debris while the apprentices assisted the civilians. However, a battle broke out against a group of Nihil pirates present on Trymant IV, which led Buck and Yoda to leap to the rescue.

Torban Buck was a male Buck joined the crew of the Padawan Academic Cruiser Star Hopper as one of two Jedi Masters teaching a class of Padawans training onboard the starship, alongside Buck had joined the crew to teach Padawans the basics of first aid.

Around this time, the Great Hyperspace Disaster occurred in the Hetzal system, when the freighter Legacy Run was destroyed in hyperspace. In its aftermath, Emergences of the debris began occurring across the Outer Rim Territories. When an Emergence occurred in the Trymant system, the Star Hopper was the only Jedi or Galactic Republic starship in range, and it was diverted to assist. With the class of apprentices assembled, Yoda had several of the students report what they had discovered on the situation, as hyperspace debris was hurtling towards Bralanak City, the most densely populated area of the planet Trymant IV. Buck told the class that he and Yoda would be handling the largest pieces of debris. He added that the Padawans' job was to help people on the ground to safety and deal with smaller chunks. The Padawans were then dispatched to their rescue speeders.

While assisting civilians in the city, Padawan Lula Talisola and several of her friends attempted to commandeer a large Spider Cruiser which had arrived in the city so it could be used as an evacuation vehicle. However, the ship belonged to the Nihil pirates, who were disinclined to acquiesce to the request. As Talisola, her best friends Farzala Tarabal and Qort, and Force-sensitive civilian Zeen Mrala, who had stepped in to telekinetically hold off a large chunk of debris, were surrounded by the pirates, Buck and Yoda arrived before the pirates could attempt to execute them.

entities.name: Ovus Buckell
entities.description:
Ovus Buckell was a human male who lived in Coronet City on the planet Corellia during the High Republic Era. He held the position of Finance Minister. Buckell had desires to become Corellia's leader and worked with the Nihil Respriler to achieve this. Buckell requested the Nihil occasionally launch small attacks on Corellia that could be fought off easily in an attempt to rally the Corellians to have the planet closed off to outsiders. During one attack, Respriler had the city's current Father of Finances, Nomar Tralmat, disappeared and apparently murdered. Buckell was unaware, however, that Tralmat and Respriler were in fact the same person. Buckell was chosen to replace Tralmat as the Father of Finances, and he also took over Coronet's municipal police which he used to gain supremacy in the city. Buckell's bid for power was thwarted when Respriler revealed himself to be Tralmat and attempted to assassinate Buckell for not agreeing with his vision. Buckell was saved by the bodyguard Dizcaro, who sacrificed himself for the Father of Finances and was killed. After the attempt, Ovus was taken by one of Dizcaro's employees, the Lasat Powlo, to safety.

Sometime later, after the Nihil forces on Corellia were defeated, Buckell again made a move to consolidate power on Corellia. Alys Ongwa noted that Buckell had a chance of pulling it off and informed the Jedi Padawans Reath Silas and Ram Jomaram that she intended to stop him.

As part of Grand Admiral Thrawn's task force to establish XQ3 Platform NL-1 as a foothold in the Pakuuni system. During this engagement Commander Buckeye oversaw the final preparations of NL-1 prior to Thrawn's inspection, moreover repelling several attacks from Rebel and pirate forces in the system.

entities.description:
Cosweg Budeesho was a veteran holographer and cartoonist who lived on the planet Ando Prime with his wife Seeja and their pet tooka, Yari. During the Clone Wars, he produced the propaganda piece "Do Your Part!" for the Intergalactic Association of Amalgamated Droid Builders with the aim of encouraging viewers of all ages to sign up as droid technicians for the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Other works he produced were published in materials put out by TriPlanetary Press, Baobab Publishing and the Shafr Center Press as well as other small publishing houses.

Cosweg Budeesho was first mentioned in the reference book Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy, which was released on October 25, 2016 and written by Pablo Hidalgo.

entities.name: Gilker Budz
entities.description:
Gilker Budz was a male Human working for CorSec outside Kor Vella on the planet Corellia during the Galactic Civil War.

He was investigating an illegal animal poaching outside of Tyrena where the poachers were taking local wildlife for pelts, biomaterial, or sometimes as exotic pets to sell offworld. It had been an ongoing problem and the local populations were falling to dangerous levels by the time that he learned of Snee-Roos, an offworld tourist, who recorded a killing of a gronda. He hired an individual to retrieve the holorecording from the tourist and bring it to him. Though Gilker thought this would stop the poaching, he later located a secret Black Sun base who he thought were in fact responsible for the poaching. He once again hired the previous individual, this time to take out the base.

Gilker Budz appeared as a non-player character in the video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed by Sony and published by LucasArts, prior to its closure on December 15, 2011.

entities.description:
Bug-Eyes was a male pilot belonging to the sentient species native to the planet Xantar. He met Luke Skywalker after the Rebel Alliance officer destroyed an Imperial cloning facility. The pilot brought Skywalker to Xantar aboard his starship. There, he introduced the young Rebel to Indiana Jones, whose planet the pilot had visited some time earlier.

This character is meant to resemble the common image of aliens believed to visit Earth, known as Greys. He originally appeared at the end of the Indiana Jones and His Desktop Adventures video game, taking Indy away in his flying saucer. He and Indiana Jones later appeared in Yoda Stories as a reference to that earlier game.

entities.name: Buggles
entities.description:
Buggles was a male voorpak owned by Torra Doza, a resident of the Colossus platform on the planet Castilon. He remained close by his owner Torra's side though she normally kept him in her room. Buggles was involved in a few low stake adventures aboard the Colossus. During the Battle of Castilon, Buggles helped Torra find Team Colossus leader Kazuda Xiono.

Buggles was a pet voorpak owned by Torra Doza, the teenage daughter of Captain Imanuel Doza, the administrator of the Colossus station.

Later Torra, annoyed at being confined to her bedroom by her father, used Buggles to escape from the droid 4D-M1N by giving him to her, explaining that he needed to be take out or else he would have another accident indoors. After 4D-M1N left, Torra slipped out of her bedroom as she had deduced the passcode, but her presence in the hallway was given away when Buggles saw her over 4D's shoulder and reacted. The droid was prevented from chasing after Torra, however, when Buggles then urinated on the floor. When Torra later returned to her room, accompanied by Kazuda Xiono, Buggles was present while they played Flight Simulator Squadron. After Xiono left Doza Tower after a series of events, Torra cuddled her pet while wondering what he was hiding.

Sometime later Torra asked Xiono to watch Buggles at Jarek Yeager's Repair Station while she was busy. However, the Voorpak escaped Xiono, first eating the contents of a bowl before running outside and hopping onto the precarious structures at the very edge of the platform, with Xiono in pursuit. He nearly managed to catch Buggles before the pet bounded off again, to his dismay. When Torra returned in search of Buggles, Xiono evaded her question of where he was. The voorpak had gotten into the cockpit of the Fireball, and managed to launch the starship by randomly pressing buttons. Torra asked who was piloting the ship, and Xiono was forced to admit it was Buggles, to her horror.

entities.name: Bugle boy
entities.description:
The bugle boy was a male Human recruited into the Army of Light during the New Sith Wars.

A male Human was recruited into the Jedi Order's Army of Light during the final decade of the New Sith Wars. Charged with sounding the war bugle to rouse the Army for battle, the young boy served under Jedi Lord Hoth during the Ruusan campaign following the declaration of support from the Jedi Grand Council.

During the Seventh Battle of Ruusan, the bugle boy joined in the company of Jedi General Kiel Charny when the group of Jedi and loyal soldiers confronted the Brotherhood of Darkness in open combat. During the fighting, the Sith used the Force to destroy the forest surrounding the battlefield, leveling the Charny's forces. During the fighting, the unarmed bugle boy was slain and his body left broken on the field of battle.

entities.name: Builder With Vines
entities.description:
Builder With Vines was a Qom Jha who lived during the Caamas Document Crisis.

He was one of the three Qom Jha to help Luke Skywalker, Mara Jade and Child Of Winds—a young Qom Qae—find the entrance to the Hand of Thrawn. When the party found an entrance into the fortress, Builder With Vines stayed behind with the Humans and the Qom Qae while Splitter Of Stones and Keeper Of Promises, the other two Qom Jha, flew back to their nesting to bring additional help. The four of them were threatened by an advancing swarm of fire creepers while they waited for the other Qom Jha to arrive. Initially, Builder With Vines stayed away from the deadly insects, but soon decided to show off for Child Of Winds by diving at the swarm and scooping up mouthfuls of them to eat. Builder With Vines almost succeeded in goading Child Of Winds into imitating the reckless stunt, but the Qom Jha got too close to the fire creepers on one pass; he was snared, dragged to the cavern floor, and eaten alive.

entities.name: Falen Buir
entities.description:
Falen Buir was a Human male soldier who served within the Alliance to Restore the Republic during the Galactic Civil War.

Following the Battle of Yavin, Falen served as a Rebel Desert Trooper and was stationed in a prison facility within the hidden Rebel base on Corellia. the Alliance captured and imprisoned six Imperial officers in this facility. During the Empire Day festivities of the same year, Emperor's Hand Mara Jade employed a group of loyal Imperial spacers to rescue the officers. The Imperial operatives attacked the prison facility and killed Falen Buir during the assault. One of the Imperial spacers then took his Rebel battle armor so that one of the Imperial officers could sneak out of the base in the disguise.

Falen Buir was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, Falen Buir was added to the game with the release of the "Game Update 11," published on June 23, 2009, and was present in the game during the Empire Day events of 2009, 2010 and 2011.

entities.name: Lo Bukk
entities.description:
Lo Bukk was a Zabrak male who served the Jedi Order as a Padawan during the final decades of the Galactic Republic. Around 67 BBY, he and his Jedi Master, Ni-Cada, were sent by the Order to the world of Abraxin to investigate the continuous killing of marsh haunts, which were being carried out by the Force-sensitive Nautolan Naat Lare. On the planet the Jedi unknowingly crossed paths with the Muun Sith Lord Darth Plagueis, who was also looking for Lare. After Plagueis managed to make contact with Lare, the Muun convinced him into taking the offense against the Jedi as proof of his worthiness to join the Sith; the resulting skirmish was short, in which Bukk's Master killed Lare.

Lo Bukk was a male Force-sensitive Zabrak Jedi Padawan of Master Ni-Cada who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic forty-five years before the Clone Wars, a series of conflicts fought between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. He and Ni-Cada were sent by the Order to the swampy planet Abraxin in the Tion Cluster, to investigate the continuous killing of non-sentient marsh haunts, The marsh haunt killings were committed by Naat Lare, a Force-sensitive Nautolan. Lare had been selected by Darth Venamis, a prospective male Bith Sith Lord of the lineage of Darth Bane, as a potential Sith apprentice.

During their stay on Abraxin, the Muun Sith Lord Darth Plagueis passed by Bukk and Ni-Cada disguised while the Jedi were bargaining with a member of the Barabel species—cold-blooded reptilians from the world Barab I— for a water skimmer. Both of them felt Plagueis' presence, though neither identified him as a Sith, an order of Force-sensitives who utilized the dark side of the Force. Later, as Bukk and his master emerged from an eatery bearing flagons of liquid, they unknowingly crossed paths with Darth Plagueis once again, and later talked with the Muun, who was also looking for Lare, as they sat at a table and discussed with the Muun about the recent killing of marsh haunts. Plagueis managed to make contact with Lare and convinced him into striking against the Bukk and his master as proof of Lare's worthiness to join the Sith. The Jedi tracked Lare with the skimmer, and a short skirmish ensued after the Nautolan attacked the two near the water, during which Lare was killed by Bukk's master.

Lo Bukk had a more of a open attitude than his master, as he easily divulged the nature of the Jedi's mission to Plagueis, though his master tried to hide the reason of their mission. When the Muun Sith Lord Darth Plagueis passed by under disguise, both Ni-Cada and Lo Bukk felt Plagueis' presence, though neither of them identified him as a Sith, a sect of Force-sensitives who utilized the dark side of the Force.

entities.name: Bulduga
entities.description:
Bulduga was half of a male Ithorian bounty hunter duo, alongside his brother, Onca. While Onca preferred long-range weapons, such as rifles, Bulduga preferred the quick-and-easily-accessible blaster pistols. Well-known throughout the galaxy, the two brothers gained the attention of Count Dooku, leader of the Separatists, and was given the challenge of winning the Box, a lethal bounty hunter competition. After gathering with Dooku's other assembled bounty hunters, Bulduga was killed by Cad Bane over a dispute regarding the Ithorian's wide-brimmed fedora. Onca was left to compete on his own, but died during the second challenge.

Bulduga was an Ithorian male who, alongside his brother Onca, operated as a bounty hunter during the Clone Wars. The two became regarded as a legendary duo. Preferring quick-draw blaster pistols over Onca's preference for long-range rifles, Bulduga was able to convince many targets that not all Ithorians fit the peace-loving agriculturist stereotype.

Bulduga's choice of weapons, coupled by his low-hanging holster, red-tinted goggles, and wide-brimmed hat caused bystanders to theorize that the Ithorian was nothing more than an imitator of the well-known bounty hunter Cad Bane, although no one would say such within earshot of the deadly Ithorian. Eventually, Bulduga and Onca attracted the attention of the Sith Lord Count Dooku, who was in league with the Confederacy of Independent Systems. The Count invited the hunters to the planet Serenno to compete in a lethal tournament called the Box.

In preparation for a risky mission to kidnap the Supreme Chancellor of the Galactic Republic, Dooku invited a posse of bounty hunters to his homeworld in order to test their mettle in a series of challenges designed by criminal mastermind Moralo Eval. Those who survived the challenges would take part in Dooku's operation and receive a hefty reward upon the job's completion.

entities.name: Bulgan
entities.description:
Bulgan was an Ansionian, an Alwari tribal outcast of the Tasbir clan, who had a hunched back and was missing an eye due to a suubatar accident he suffered as a child. His brain was also damaged during the accident—that is, until the Jedi healer Barriss Offee fixed it.

His disabilities were the cause of him being cast out from his clan as a child to live in the cities. He became an enforcer for Soergg the Hutt, who implanted a detonator chip in his neck to ensure loyalty.

Bulgan was bald, had pale skin, but was, despite his hunched back, stronger than other Ansonians of average height and build. He and fellow outcast Kyakhta were tasked by Bossban Soergg to capture one of the Jedi Padawans recently arrived from Coruscant to help settle a border dispute; the outcasts' mission, however, was foiled by Jedi Offee, who cured them of their mental afflictions. Their loyalties then switched to the Jedi, whom they accompanied on their mission across the planet.

entities.name: Bulgeski
entities.description:
Bulgeski was a Sallichen male senator who represented Salliche in the Galactic Senate during the era of the Galactic Republic.

A Sallichen male that lived in the twilight decades of the Galactic Republic era, Bulgeski served as senator for the Core Worlds planet Salliche inside the Galactic Senate. An agriworld that cultivated the crops exported to planets like the capital Coruscant, as their spokesman, Bulgeski claimed that Salliche represented the breadbasket of the Core Worlds and called for the Republic Guard to intervene when his homeworld fell beneath assault from Norkronian raiders.

In 42 BBY, not long after his request for aid, Bulgeski was present at the Senate Chamber when Jedi Master Dooku addressed him and his fellow senators to voice protest to cuts that the congress was intending to make to their trade route defense program. Though Dooku sought to intervene on behalf of the populations of worlds in the Outer Rim Territories that would be affected, Bulgeski objected to his arguments and engaged in a verbal sparring match where the senator accused the Jedi of attempting to influence the Senate. Dooku tried to use the recent request that Bulgeski had made for assistance to support his argument that the Outer Rim should receive the same benefits, but the Sallichen responded that the importance of his homeworld necessitated this intervention, as Salliche represented a vital food source for Coruscant and the other Core Worlds. When his statement prompted his opponent to theorise that Bulgeski and his constituents were afraid that the agricultural worlds of the Outer Rim would become their competitors, the senator denied this as a scandalous accusation, while Supreme Chancellor Kalpana dismissed Dooku's advice.

Bulgeski appeared in the audiobook Dooku: Jedi Lost, written by Cavan Scott and published in 2019.

entities.description:
Bull "The Unbreakable" was a male Weequay mercenary who lived during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. In 3643 BBY, Bull was hired by Jundo Martik to recover stolen ore and drive off the Twin Suns pirate gang from a mine in the Jundland Chasm on Tatooine. When Bull and his associates failed to return after a few days, a group of Republic spacers was sent by Jundo Martik to reclaim the mine. Bull and the other mercenaries attempted to frame the spacers for the theft of the ore, but were killed by the droid ST-97.

Bull "The Unbreakable" appears in Star Wars: The Old Republic during the heroic mission "Reap the Whirlwind" on Tatooine.

entities.name: Dhar Bullwin
entities.description:
Dhar Bullwin was a dark side magician who searched for the Eye of Koda.

Dhar Bullwin studied the dark side under a master of the dark arts for nearly 30 years as part of an ancient order of dark side magicians. Bullwin had been searching for the Eye of Koda for twenty-five years. When the amulet turned up in the Varno Market on the planet Vengler, he immediately sent six Scitrok Warriors after the amulet's owners in order to recover his prize.

When the amulet's owners fled the planet, Bullwin sent both his Homonculous into their ship as well as following in his own ship, the Logrus. Although his ship was destroyed in the battle, Bullwin escaped in an escape pod and crash landed on Koda's World. While the amulet's owners fought past a garagon, Bullwin used the dark side to convince the local indigenous Tempestro that he was their ally and that they should attack the amulet's owners when they reached the Tempestro temple. While the owners fought the Tempestro, Bullwin climbed the side of the temple and entered through a tiny opening.

Inside the temple Bullwin stepped onto a raised platform that gave all the power and knowledge of the Tempestro to whomever stood there. Bullwin used the power to become invisible as he attacked the amulet's owners. The power he gained consumed him in the end and he died in the temple.

Quartermaster Bulo appears in the Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan expansion, released on December 2, 2014.

entities.name: Alasdair Bumbalough
entities.description:
Alasdair Bumbalough was a male criminal who lived on Corellia during the time of the Galactic Civil War. After the Battle of Yavin, he worked for the crime lord Olag Greck. During that time, the Greck criminals went into the investigation of the Tyrena city councilmen Lyman Zavala and CorSec Captain Dool. At some point, Lyman Zavala dispatched a group of spacers to strike the Greck headquarters. The spacers fought Alasdair Bumbalough to get access to Olag Greck's private sanctum and eventually killed Greck himself.

Dialogue pertaining to Alasdair Bumbalough appeared in the directory tree files for the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, According to these files, introduced with the "Publish 28," on April 26, 2006, Alasdair Bumbalough would have been involved in a questline named "Tyrena - Lyman Zavala." However, he is not known to have appeared on the game's live servers as a proper non-player character.

Bun'Del was a slightly overweight Human male who lived during the Galactic Civil War. he was present at Tansarii Point Station, a space station located near the planet Ord Mantell, in the Bright Jewel system. During that time, he frequented the station's cantina with his friend Mot Draken. Draken had fallen deeply in love with O'choa Detera, a dancer performing in the cantina, but the woman instead had a crush on Bun'Del.

entities.name: Bungo Bung
entities.description:
Bungo Bung was a male Sullustan from the planet Sullust. Despite growing up working on his father's boaboo fungus farm, Bung harbored a desire to pilot starships. Joining SoroSuub Corporation's Transport and Supply Division, he eventually attained the command of the Chubby Gundark, a Nyubba-class cargo barge driver. Assisted by his droid co-pilot, 42-RST—known as Rusti—Bung was the pioneer of the Great Bantha Breakfast Biscuit Run between Sullust and Gastrula in the Outer Rim Territories during the Galactic Civil War. Bung transported Biscuit Baron's Bantha Breakfast Biscuits to the native Gastrulans, despite interference on the first run from Imperial Captain Wankle. Although he made a healthy profit, Bung broke even after spending much of the money on repairs to his ship after an encounter with a Giant Amorphous Bantha Breakfast Biscuit, a strange anomalous lifeform that was the result of the interaction between the preservatives in Bantha Breakfast Biscuits and the stale air in his ship. He survived by defeating the creature with blue sauce, which, as the recommended accompaniment to a Bantha Breakfast Biscuit, proved to be the lifeform's weakness.

The Sullustan male Bungo Bung was born on the planet Sullust, and grew up in the underground caverns of his homeworld, working on his father's boaboo fungus farm. Bung had few duties and spent much of his time sitting around and daydreaming. The fungus was tended to by droids, who then crushed the fungus to make boaboo juice. He was only required to clean up the mess the droids made when they eventually short-circuited in the moist environment, and transport the juice to the markets in G'rinn Go city.

However, Bung's desire was to pilot a starship, and when he was old enough, the young Sullustan signed up with the SoroSuub Corporation's Transport and Supply Division. Serving as a shipping pilot, Bung faithfully worked for SoroSuub for a number of years, eventually earning the captaincy of the Nyubba-class cargo barge driver Chubby Gundark. During his travels, Bung worked for the Mephout, and they gave him a gift—the RST Model Translator Droid 42-RST, otherwise known as "Rusti." Although Bung believed that the gift was for the services he had rendered for them, the Mephout were simply getting rid of obsolete technology. 42-RST served as co-pilot of the Chubby Gundark and was employed as a translator.

entities.name: Ames Bunkle
entities.description:
Ames Bunkle, who later went by his operating number DX-578, was a male human who lived with his parents on the planet Lothal. When Bunkle was sixteen he enrolled in the Academy for Young Imperials on Lothal, where he ended up specializing in stormtrooper training. The process drastically changed Bunkle's personality, breaking him down and then rebuilding him as a loyal but near-emotionless servant of the Galactic Empire. Bunkle graduated into a full fledged trooper, and took part in the arrest of a group of Lothal dissidents who had bombed Imperial mining operations on Lothal.

Ames Bunkle was a male human who lived on the planet Lothal under the reign of the Galactic Empire. Born around 22 years before the Battle of Yavin, Bunkle's parents, Pari Bunkle and her partner, were researchers in the Empire's Ministry of Agriculture. Bunkle studied at the Junior Academy of Applied Sciences during his childhood, where he set the record for number of carries in the game of grav-ball while playing against the Forked River team in summer at the age of fifteen. After graduating the Junior Academy, he applied to, and was accepted into Lothal's Academy for Young Imperials during the spring alongside Dhara Leonis, a girl of the same age who lived with her family in an apartment two floors above Bunkle's home. A year after setting his grav-ball record, Bunkle attended a party held by Leonis's parents, Leo Leonis and Tepha Leonis, although his own parents could not make it as they were on assignment.

At the party, Bunkle stood alone on the apartment's balcony until he was approached by Dhara's brother Zare Leonis. The pair discussed Bunkle's apprehension about attending the academy, and how it was a shame they had been at the Junior Academy at different times, given Zare was also grav-ball enthusiast. A patrol of TIE/ln space superiority starfighters then passed the apartment and drew the boys' attention, causing them to discuss the starfighters engines. The conversation was joined by Lieutenant Piers Roddance, another guest at the party and an Imperial officer. The discussion moved on to the Empire's All Terrain Defense Pods, before Zare spotted Governor Arihnda Pryce amongst the other guests and bought Bunkle over to speak to her. Pryce was with the other members of the Leonis family, and Leo gave a speech about the pride he felt in sending his daughter to the academy, before Dhara introduced Bunkle to the governor and then left them to talk.

entities.name: Morga Bunna
entities.description:
Morga Bunna was a male Bosph who lived during the reign of the New Republic. Bunna worked as a bounty hunter, but later retired and established a depot on one of the moons of the planet Bosph, which served as a cache point for illicit items.

In 19 ABY, supplies of the spice Tempest were stored in Bunna's facility by the Hutt crime lord Mika Anjiliac Chiera. Bunna had the Tempest removed after the Jedi archivist Mander Zuma and the spacers Reen Irana and Eddey Be'ray began shutting down the Tempest trade. Bunna's depot was later raided by Zumma and the Jedi's Corporate Sector Authority arrived moments later, and Bunna was forced to surrender to them. Bunna shared his knowledge of the Tempest trade with Zuma and in return for his honesty, the Jedi Master instructed the CSA to not detain the Bosph.

Morga Bunna was a male Bosph who lived during the era of the New Republic. After making a living as a bounty hunter and traveling across the galaxy, Bunna retired and set up a depot on the outermost moon of the Bosph homeworld for storing stolen goods. The small moon was desolate and far from the planet Bosph, and Bunna's facility served both as a place for criminals to cache illicit goods and a trading post for individuals who wished to sell their wares without meeting buyers face to face. To protect the anonymity of Bunna's customers, all deliveries to his depot were arranged through blind drops with shipping schedules changing regularly. Over time, Bunna burrowed through moon to expand his depot and he built a number of halls, passages, storage rooms, as well as a translucent pleasure dome along one side.

Around 19 ABY, Bunna agreed to a number of contracts to store Tempest, a new potent form of spice produced by the Hutt crime lord Mika Anjiliac Chiera that left users prone to violent fits of rage. However, after the Jedi archivist Mander Zuma began disrupting the Tempest supply chain across Hutt Space and the Corporate Sector in an attempt to trace the source of the spice, Bunna sent on all of the Tempest stored at his depot and refused to accept any more shipments of the spice.

entities.description:
Kip Bunyea, or "The Kip," was a Human male from the planet Naboo with affiliations to data slicers and smugglers. A dead-or-alive bounty on him was posted by Aruk the Hutt no later than 32 BBY. That year, he spent time at the Outlander Club in the Uscru Entertainment District of the planet Coruscant during bounty hunter Jango Fett's pursuit of drug dealer Jervis Gloom.

Kip Bunyea, also known as "The Kip," was a Human male Naboo. He the Hutt criminal Aruk Besadii Aora had issued a bounty for him. It stated Bunyea's last known location was the Core Worlds and described him as extremely hateful and unruly. The bounty also offered a price of 2,000 credits for him alive or 1,000 for his death.

In 32 BBY, Bunyea spent time at the Core Worlds planet Coruscant. He stood at the club's bar when Mandalorian bounty hunter Jango Fett entered during his pursuit of death stick dealer Jervis Gloom. The man remained there while Fett threatened the bartender and dispatched several thugs.

Bunyea was identified as a bounty by Fett and was captured as he cowered pathetically at the bar.

entities.description: Bur'lorr was a Yuuzhan Vong subaltern. He worked for Nom Anor and contacted Goran Beviin and some other Mandalorians, after the Battle of New Holgha. Bur'lorr commanded them to hunt down the Jedi, Kubariet, who was wounded and attempting to escape the planet. Instead, the Mandalorians slipped useful intel to the Jedi to aid the New Republic against the Vong, and were forced to kill Bur'lorr to cover the Jedi's escape. The group of supercommandos jumped the Vong warrior, and Beviin laboriously strangled Bur'lorr with a pair of illegal Mandalorian crushgaunts. Beviin then took a small piece of Bur'lorr's scalp as a trophy. Mandalorian Suvar Detta took other pieces of Bur'lorr's body for bio-testing.

entities.name: Wac Bur
entities.description:
Wac Bur was a male Rodian who worked as a counterfeiter and forger. In 24 ABY, he sold fake art to Gebbu the Hutt who, in retaliation, sent the bounty hunter Boba Fett after him. Fett tracked Bur down on the of Coruscant. After leading Fett in a mad chase through a network of alleyways, Bur hid in a pile of crates and fruitlessly attempted to plead for his life. He was killed by Fett when he refused to surrender.

Unusually overweight for a Rodian, Wac Bur was a cowardly individual. He was also highly hypocritical, attempting to lecture Fett on morality when he himself was nothing more than a criminal.

Wac Bur first appeared in Karen Traviss' 2006 eBook Boba Fett: A Practical Man.

entities.description:
Varesk Bura'lya was a male Bothan undersecretary who worked for the Bothan embassy on the planet Coruscant. Shortly after the formation of the Empire, he feared for his life and contacted the resistance movement Whiplash seeking help for safe passage offworld.

Bura'lya was escorted by former Jedi Jax Pavan and his crew which consisted of I-Five, Den Dhur and Laranth Tarak. During his extraction, their group was ambushed by a squad of stormtroopers in their final checkpoint. A brief shootout ensued where everyone from their group emerged relatively unharmed, with exception to Bura'lya who fainted and lost control of his bladder.

They eventually made it to the rendezvous point and he boarded the freighter Big Score.

entities.name: Rok Buran
entities.description:
Rok Buran was a human male Jedi Master active during the High Republic Era.

He led the Republic Pathfinder team Outer Rim Expedition Two-Five-Two, the other members of which were his Padawan Maliq, Joneth, Branda, and the communications droid EX-8C. the team was betrayed and ambushed during an expedition to the planet Gloam, with Buran left as the only survivor after being left for dead due to injuries inflicted by some of the planet's monsters. Buran made his way to an old Jedi temple on the planet, where he took shelter while sending out EX-8C with a distress signal which was discovered by Master Silandra Sho's Pathfinder team.

After leaving Aubadas, Buran joined another Pathfinder team onboard the Pathfinder ship Witherbloom. He talked to Xinith Tarl about losing his previous team on Gloam. Their ship came under attack and was rammed by a craft. The collision caused both ships to crash on a nearby planet. Buran helped Tarl who had become trapped under some debris and was injured. When the pilot Pako informed the Jedi that the ship was going to explode, he questioned Pako if the planet's atmosphere was safe. Realizing the danger, Buran picked up Tarl and fled the exploding ship along with the rest of the crew.

He put Tarl down and had the medic Ambar attend to the injured Bith. The rest of the team had a meeting and decided to check out the other crashed ship to see if there were any supplies or survivors. They made their way to the crash site and decided to split into teams to search the wreckage. Buran and Padawan Coron Solstus investigated the bridge. As they worked their way deeper into the ship, Buran was questioned by Solstus about the loss of Maliq. The pair got to the controls and started to reroute the power but were overcome by something that was clouding their senses.

entities.name: Zoda Burb
entities.description:
Zoda Burb was a Human businessman and con artist who lived on the planet Corellia during the Galactic Civil War. Zoda Burb encountered the Devaronian merchant Midgoss D'labaninaph who had just arrived on Corellia. The con artist swindled the Devaronian and abandoned him in the wilderness without any money. D'labaninaph therefore tried to win the favor of Brantlee Spondoon, the greedy assistant to the Corellian Diktat Daclif Gallamby, with a gift in order to have Zoda Burb punished. The attempt of the Devaronian was unfruitful but ironically inspired Burb who was more successful. The con artist offered a container of Neonan red cheese that extremely delighted Spondoon. The woman thus included the "businessman" in the government's contacts for future reference.

Zoda Burb was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts,

entities.description:
Fez Burba was a Human male seismologist working for the Galactic Republic during the Cold War with the reconstituted Sith Empire. He tasked a Republic spacer to take the seismic readings in the Works to prove his theory that Coruscant's core was damaged by an Imperial bombardment. The readings turned out to be false and Burba went on with his next project.

Later he was a special host in a show called Mysteries of Galactic Science quickly acquiring prominence. He also claimed that the shift of the planetary crust on Knores was the cause of extinction for an entire civilization. His theory was investigated in the equatorial trench.

entities.name: Burborok
entities.description:
Burborok was a male Sedrian from the planet Sedri alive during the Galactic Civil War. During the Sedri civil war he chose to side with the bishop of war Karak and his renegades in which he served as Karak's bodyguard. Burborok accompanied Karak and five other renegades in an assault on the Sun caves in the city of Fitsay during the Siege of the Fitsay Sun Caves in an attempt to claim the power of the Golden Sun. Karak and his men were chased by a group of Rebels and Sedrian priest Pek into the caves whom Burbork, along with the rest of the group bar Karak waited to ambush within the cave. Once the Rebels came upon him, Burborok shouted a challenge to Pek to distract him and the Rebels so other renegades could attack from behind. Burborok was killed in the following fight however.

Burborok was a male Sedrian from the planet Sedri, a water world in the Sedri system secluded from most of the galaxy. During Burborok's lifetime a civil war broke out on his homeworld between the religious sect known as the Priests of the Sun, whom ruled the Sedri from the city of Fitsay, and a group of renegades, lead by the former bishop of war Karak, who opposed their control. Burborok chose to side with the renegades in this war, who opposed the priests of the Sun due to their control of the Golden Sun, a huge group of individuals of a polyp species known as Golden Sun coral. The coral formed a group minded sentient being with considerable connection to the Force including a large number of healing powers. The priests however kept it hidden within a structure known as the Great Shell Dome in the center of Fitsay and strictly controlled those who could access it. The renegades followed Karak in the belief that all Sedrians should have access to the Golden Sun, although in truth Karak simply wanted the corals power for himself.

During the War an Imperial scout ship accidentally discovered Sedri and after it's location was reported, a small Imperial garrison was set up on the world lead by commander Aban. The Imperial's in turn drew the attention of the Alliance to Restore the Republic and a Rebel dignitary named Mors Odrion and his companion Rekara also traveled to the world. The rebels however soon encountered the renegades whom captured the pair for interrogation, not use to any off-worlders. While the renegades decided to use Odrion as a potential bartering tool for use with the new Imperial presence, Rekara managed to escape and steal a small piece of Golden coral which the renegades had taken from Fitsay.

Burbu studied the jevesects on the planet Herzob. Some unknown factor caused the death of jevesects within 48 hours of being removed from their planet, and Burbu sought to isolate this factor. This would gain him personal fame. However, his work was opposed by native environmental groups, who were aware of the devastating effect jevesects had on agricultural processes and of their potential to become biological weapons against other agricultural worlds.

Whether Burbu was ultimately successful in his endeavor is unknown.

entities.name: Burg
entities.description:
Burg was a Devaronian male who operated as a mercenary during the era of the New Republic. Burg acted as the muscle of a team recruited by Ranzar Malk to rescue the prisoner Qin from the Bothan-5, a New Republic Correctional Transport, which also included Migs Mayfeld, Xi'an, Q9-0, and the Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin, who had been recruited for the use of his gunship, the Razor Crest. After Qin was rescued, Burg and the team betrayed Djarin and trapped him inside a cell. However, the Mandalorian managed to escape and took them down, imprisoning them in a cell aboard the transport and leaving them behind to deliver Qin to Malk alone.

A male Devaronian from Devaron, Burg was recruited by the criminal Ranzar Malk as part of a team led by fellow mercenary Migs Mayfeld, which also included the droid Zero, the Twi'lek Xi'an, and the Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin, with the objective of rescuing Qin from aboard the Bothan-5, a New Republic Correctional Transport. While the Devaronian carried a crate, Mayfeld introduced Burg to Djarin, describing him as the muscle of the group. Burg then dropped the crate and approached the Mandalorian, sneering at him and stating that he thought Mandalorians would be bigger. As the team boarded Djarin's starship, the Razor Crest, Burg scoffed at his size.

During the journey, Burg strolled around inside the ship, upsetting Xi'an, who told the Devaronian to be seated. He grunted at the Twi'lek, with Xi'an snarling back in response. Burg then tinkered with the controls, opening a weapons cabinet in the process. As he inspected the weapons with glee, Djarin intervened and closed the cabinet, angering the Devaronian. Tensions rose between the two, with Burg questioning why they needed a Mandalorian on the team. Mayfeld replied stating that they were considered to be the greatest warriors in the galaxy. Burg then asked why were they all dead, causing Mayfeld and Xi'an to laugh in response. The team then questioned why Djarin never removed his helmet, with them guffawing when Mayfeld speculated if he was a Gungan. When Mayfeld suggested that he remove his helmet, Burg attempted to do so, but the Mandalorian retaliated, causing a fight to break out between the two. During the fight, the Devaronian accidentally opened the chamber where Grogu resided, revealing his existence to the team. Zero dropped the ship out of hyperspace immediately afterwards and maneuvered around the prison ship, causing everyone to stumble.

Upon landing, the team entered the prison ship and began their search for Qin, with Burg entering after Mayfeld and Xi'an. As they entered the hallway to the control room, they encountered a mouse droid. Burg toyed with the droid before shooting it, alerting a group of N5 sentry droids to their position. The team was cornered in the hallway, but watched as Djarin sneaked behind the droids and destroyed them. They then mocked his efforts, with Burg intentionally bumping into him.

entities.name: Willham Burke
entities.description:
Willham Burke was the Admiral of the Fourth Battle Group of the Rebel Alliance, operating in the Outer Rim. He later served as a commander in the New Republic's Third Fleet, winning numerous victories in the years immediately following the Battle of Endor.

He was considered a very competent commander, and many Rebel pilots took it as a great honor to meet him. He was known to help train several pilot squadrons including Havoc Squadron, Vortex Squadron, Crimson Phoenix Squadron, as well as freelancers from CorSec and the Smugglers' Alliance. Soon after the Battle of Yavin he was known to be seen in a hotel in Doaba Guerfel on Corellia. While there, he assigned a single individual to battle against 30 Imperial starfighters near Kessel, and eventually a follow-up assault against the Imperial CR90 corvette Star Ravager.

In 5 ABY, Admiral Ackbar placed command of the New Republic Third Fleet temporarily in the hands of Admirals Burke and Kalback, who worked to sever the forces of Imperial warlord Treuten Teradoc from the Core Worlds. Leading the fleet from the Mon Calamari Star Cruisers Remember Alderaan and Justice, the pair bested the warlord's task force at Togoria and fought their way to the planet Lantillies on the Perlemian Trade Route, where they connected with the forces fielded by the planet Contruum. Having established a hold on the Perlemian, the two admirals headed in different directions; while Kalback headed for Corsin, Burke pressed Coreward, encountering the forces of Admiral Ledre Okins in the Chazwa system. The two engaged in a long series of feints and raids before Burke's trickery convinced Okins to send key ships to the Pindra system, where they were caught in a grav trap hidden in the system's careening asteroids. Burke was able to destroy Okins at the latter's base of operations in the Colla system.

In 6 ABY, Burke and General Brenn Tantor captured Reytha, Gyndine, and Commenor, placing him in position to move into the Core, along with Admiral Firmus Nantz of the First Fleet and Admiral Chel Dorat of the Fourth Fleet.

entities.description:
Burloo, known as "Bantha" Burloo, was a burly Chagrian bouncer who worked at Miss Mylla's Saloon in Bartyn's Landing, a town on Lamaredd.

Burloo was a tall, muscled Chagrian male living in the coastal town of Bartyn's Landing in Lamaredd. He was nicknamed "Bantha" Burloo. For as far as any neighbor could remember, Burloo had been seen in the company of Miss Mylla, a Falleen who had arrived to Lamaredd at some point before 69 BBY along with several Falleen escorts.

Miss Mylla eventually bought an inn and transformed it into Miss Mylla's Saloon, an entertainment locale where customers could enjoy drinks served by scantily-clad waitresses or these women's company in private rooms. Burloo became the bouncer of the Saloon, standing always at a maximum of ten meters from the door, except when he was dealing with any problematic guest. The Saloon was always open, and Burloo appeared to be always on duty. Burloo was also partly responsible for the security of the courtesans — although most of them could take care of themselves.

At 225 centimeters of height and powerfully built, Burloo was an imposing presence in Lamaredd. He commonly carried with him a club, a combat knife and a slugthrower pistol – as blasters were uncommon in Lamaredd. He had several skills appropriate to his job, including the ability to intimidate, and was fluent in both Chagri and Basic — although he could only write Chagri.

Burnok was a Human male and good friend of the Mandalorian Oren Ward. During the Cold War, the pair were on the planet of Nal Hutta where Oren attempted to sneak into the palace of the Hutt crime lord Voontara Fa'athra to steal treasure from the criminal. The Mandalorian was caught, however, and frozen in carbonite as punishment by Fa'athra. Burnok then hired a spacer in the industrial town of Jiguuna to rescue his companion.

Star Wars: The Old Republic Explorer's Guide

entities.name: Burnout
entities.description:
Burnout was a male Weequay criminal and a member of the notorious gang known as the Fondor Five. During the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire, the gang was spotted operating on Coruscant. Because of the gang's violent tendencies, the Coruscant Security Force placed a high bounty on their heads. The bounty was eventually collected after all five gang members were killed in a firefight in the Fartrader Lounge.

Burnout appears in the BioWare MMORPG Star Wars: The Old Republic as one of the five targets of the Heroic mission "Republic's Most Wanted".

entities.name: Buroy
entities.description:
Buroy was a male Corellian who served as an agent of Corellian Intelligence during the time of the Second Corellian Crisis. In 40 ABY, the Corellian Head of State Thrackan Sal-Solo hired the Kiffar bounty hunter Ailyn Vel—who was operating under the alias "Ailyn Harbuur"—to assassinate the family of Sal-Solo's cousin Han Solo, and Buroy was ordered by Corellian Intelligence to provide Vel with weapons and a safe house on the planet Coruscant. However, Buroy and Vel were arrested by the Galactic Alliance Guard and after Vel was killed during an interrogation by the GAG's leader Jacen Solo, who was attempting to extract intelligence from her regarding Sal-Solo's plot, Jacen ordered the GAG captain Heol Girdun to try to obtain the information from Buroy instead.

entities.name: Burr
entities.description:
Burr was a male Human Colonel of the reconstituted Sith Empire living during the Galactic War. Following the Battle of Rishi, he was part of Darth Marr's force that traveled to Yavin 4 and established the anti-Revanite coalition along with Galactic Republic forces under Jedi Master Satele Shan. There Burr engaged in a conversation with Captain Stroh of the Republic, a man who under normal circumstances would be his enemy.

Colonel Burr appears in the Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan expansion, released on December 2, 2014.

entities.name: Burra
entities.description:
Burra was a Force-sensitive Kel Dor male from the planet Dorin and a member of the Baran Do Sages, a Force-based organization on Dorin. He later became a member of the Hidden Ones, a secret sect of the Baran Do dedicated to preserving their knowledge, should the order ever be destroyed. Burra, who took that name upon joining the Hidden Ones, was one of the eldest members of the sect present in 43.5 ABY when exiled Jedi Grand Master Luke Skywalker and his son, Jedi Knight Ben Skywalker, arrived on Dorin in search of Master of the Baran Do Order Koro Ziil, hoping to find out more about why the Jedi Knight Jacen Solo had turned to the dark side.

The Skywalkers soon discovered the Hidden Ones, and traveled with senior combat instructor Charsae Saal to the system of caverns that were home to the sect. Ziil, who had recently become the Hidden One's leader, told the Skywalkers that in order to protect the sect's secrecy, they would not be allowed to leave the caverns. After Luke defeated Ziil in a duel of Force powers, Burra revealed to the Skywalkers the location of a secret turbolift chamber out of the caverns.

A male Force-sensitive Kel Dor from the planet Dorin was a member of the Baran Do Sages, a Force-based organization on Dorin. Sometime after 19 BBY, he joined the Hidden Ones, a secret sect of the Baran Do formed by Sage Tokra Hazz, dedicated to preserving their knowledge so that if the Baran Do on the surface were destroyed, the organization could be restored. He changed his name to Burra in doing so, reflecting that his former self was considered dead.

In 43.5 ABY, Jedi Grand Master Luke Skywalker was exiled from the New Jedi Order and the galactic capital of Coruscant for failing to prevent Jedi Knight Jacen Solo's fall to the dark side of the Force. Luke and his son, Knight Ben Skywalker, traveled to the Baran Do temple on Dorin to speak with Master of the Order Koro Ziil, hoping to find the cause of Solo's fall to the dark side. Upon their arrival, however, they were told that Ziil had died, and the two decided to stay and train with the Sages.

A dark-skinned Human male, he made the jump from grade-four all the way to the hitherto nonexistent grade-thirteen by helping Ysanne Isard override Mara Jade's tampering with the Imperial Palace's computer system.

entities.name: Sk'kot Burrid
entities.description:
Sk'kot Burrid was a Human male corporal who served in Bria Tharen's Red Hand Squadron of the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War.

Burrid was stationed aboard the Marauder-class corvette Retribution when the Rebels attacked the Ylesian slave ship Helot's Shackle outbound to Kessel. Originally, he was slated to board the Helot's Shackle with the rest of his squad; having developed a mild fever, however, Burrid was ordered off the mission despite his own assurances that he felt fit for duty. Later, he participated in the Battle of Ylesia as part of a squad assaulting Colony One.

Sk'kot Burrid was killed along with the rest of Red Hand Squadron on Toprawa while attempting to transmit the Death Star plans to Princess Leia Organa.

entities.name: Burrk
entities.description:
Burrk was an human male former stormtrooper who deserted the Galactic Empire after the Battle of Endor. He teamed up with two Cathar siblings, Nodon and Nonak, and hunted Wampas on Hoth even though it was illegal.

Drom Guldi booked himself on a trip to Hoth to hunt with Burrk, but while they were on the hunt, they were ambushed by Wampas. One Wampa accidentally hit the self-destruct on their ship, and Burrk and his team were left stranded on Hoth.

Eventually Luke Skywalker and Callista Ming discovered Burrk and the others on Hoth, and were once again ambushed by Wampas. Burrk and the others took shelter in the ruins of Echo Base, but Burrk was killed during the fight.

The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons

entities.name: Bursthed
entities.description:
Bursthed was the Imperial Governor of Ruten during the New Republic era. He was known to be an evil and corrupt man but also an efficient bureaucrat. He considered his appointment as governor of Rutan beneath him and hoped that an effective term would lead to promotion.

During the Galactic Civil War, Bursthed served as Governor of the planet Draenell's Point.

Bursthed's hobby was collecting exotic and unusual animals from all over the galaxy for his private menagerie. His collection included a bear spider, a dewback, a glittering mynock, and a quexius bird from Endor. His courtesans organized regular Pet Shows where the Governor would inevitably win first prize. In exchange for their support the judges of the shows would receive favors of land which were often taken from farmers later accused of treason against the Galactic Empire and evicted. Also at these shows the animals were made to do tricks that often involve violence to Humans, more than often those accused of being Rebel leaders. Members of the New Republic planned to stop these shows by arranging for the Governor to lose the contest. They planned to swap Bursthed's entry, a glittering mynock, for a Slug-rat. Native to the planet Ruten, when woken the Slug-rat would attack the nearest person.

A bounty, 4000 credits alive, 2000 dead, was posted on his head by Brine Eyes-Li. In 32 BBY, the bounty was collected on Malastare by the deadly Mandalorian-turned bounty hunter Jango Fett.

entities.name: J. K. Burtola
entities.description:
J. K. Burtola was a human male who joined the Jedi Order at a young age and as a Jedi youngling trained as a member of Bear Clan. In 22 BBY, he and his clanmates received lightsaber training from Jedi Grand Master Yoda in the Jedi Temple on the planet Coruscant. The lesson was interrupted by Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi, who sought Yoda's help in locating the planet Kamino. The Grand Master opened up the question of why the planet might be missing from the Jedi Archives to the class, and Burtola correctly guessed that someone erased it.

J. K. Burtola was a Force-sensitive human male Burtola and the rest of the Bear Clan were practicing with training lightsabers under the tutelage of Jedi Grand Master Yoda in one of the temple's classrooms when the Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi interrupted the lesson to seek Yoda's guidance.

Yoda halted the class, and Burtola and the others greeted Kenobi, who explained that he was looking for the planet Kamino, but could not find it in the Jedi Archives. Yoda asked Burtola's classmate Liam to lower the classroom's blinds so that Kenobi could show the class a holographic star map and indicate where the planet should be. The Grand Master then asked the class if they had any thoughts on why the planet might be missing, and Burtola correctly guessed that it had been erased from the archives. Satisfied with this answer, Yoda moved away from the younglings to speak briefly with Kenobi about this troubling idea.

Burtola was Force-sensitive and had fair skin, brown eyes and brown hair.

entities.name: Burtt
entities.description:
Burtt was a Rebel Alliance officer and part of a survey team under Princess Leia Organa assigned to scout out the planet Arbra in the hopes of establishing a permanent Rebel base. One of Burtt's functions included guarding the survey team's plastent quarters at night while they slept. Burtt was one of the first to discover that members of a small, indigenous species known as Hoojibs were stealing energy reserves from the team's weaponry. That same evening, an alien creature known as a Slivilith attacked the base camp. The Slivilith grabbed Burtt about the waist with its tail, and Chewbacca the Wookiee had to wrestle him from the creature's grasp. The Slivilith was soon killed, and Burtt returned to the base camp with the others.

Burtt shares his name with Star Wars sound designer Ben Burtt.

entities.name: Buryn
entities.description:
Buryn was a Togruta male who served as a member of the Republic Military during the Great Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. In 3653 BBY, he served as the theater commander for the Battle of Balmorra—a long-running conflict between the Republic and the Empire over the planet's rich resources and manufacturing capabilities. During the fight for Balmorra, the Dark Council of the Sith Empire extended an offer of peace to the Republic. Upon the acceptance of the offer and the ratification and enactment of the Great War-ending Treaty of Coruscant, all Republic Military forces were expected to stand down, including those belonging to General Buryn on Balmorra.

As the Togruta tried to gather his commanders and leave the battlefield, Jedi Knight Fortris Gall rebelled against the General and the Treaty by launching a covert rescue mission into a Sith military base. Gall's brazen attack forced Buryn and his troops to remain on-planet, turning the mire of the Balmorra battle into one of the earliest conflicts of the post-Great Galactic War political unrest.

After the Treaty of Coruscant was signed, Buryn was present at Republic Base 11A on Balmorra with several Jedi, discussing the troop withdrawal orders given after the signing of the Treaty of Coruscant. A Jedi named Fortris Gall had been planning a rescue mission to liberate Demolitions Squad 419 from captivity by the Sith Empire. After Buryn discouraged Fortris from attempting a rescue, Fortris left the room, claiming to merely be going outside to look at the stars.

In actuality, Fortris departed for the Troida Military Workshop where Squad 419 was being held. After defeating a Sith guard in a duel, Fortris succeeded in liberating the captive demolitions team.

entities.name: Busurra
entities.description:
Busurra was a male Wookiee who joined the Alliance to Restore the Republic in the Atrivis sector. There, he was an able administrator and an assistant to the sector's Chief of Staff, and on a number of occasions was himself acting Chief of Staff. Busurra was mild-mannered, despite being tortured by forces of the Galactic Empire.

Busurra was a male Wookiee. He was once captured by forces of the Galactic Empire who tortured him, blinding him in his right eye and causing him to lose three fingers on his left hand. To cover his injury, Busurra wore an eye patch. After joining the Alliance to Restore the Republic, Busurra went on to become an assistant to Loom Carplin, the Chief of Staff of the Atrivis Sector Force. The pair were based on Generis, the headquarters of the sector forces; however, Carplin was often off-world checking numerous outposts in the sector. On these occasions, Busurra was acting Chief of Staff, aiding Commander-in-Chief Travia Chan.

Despite the reputation of his species and the mutilation delivered to him by the Imperials, Busurra was a good-natured and mild mannered Wookiee. He was a very efficient administrator and organizer, and was aided in this role by his protocol droid, C3-L1, who translated his speech for the many Humans who struggled to understand him.

Busurra was skilled in combat, trained to use both a standard blaster and a bowcaster, as well as larger blaster artillery weapons. He was also skilled in unarmed combat. Busurra was knowledgeable about alien species, along with their cultures and languages, and about planetary systems. A capable administrator, Busurra was well versed in the inner workings of a bureaucracy. He was trained to navigate starships through hyperspace, and was capable of flying space transports and driving repulsorlift vehicles.

entities.name: Corinna A'Daasha
entities.description:
Corinna A'Daasha was a female Human from the planet Corellia. After growing up in an opulent household, she left to explore the galaxy before settling down with her twin sister, Kandria A'Daasha, on the planet Adarlon. The twins founded and co-owned the Glow Dome nightclub there. After meeting a member of the No-Holds-Barred underground group, Corinna became a sympathizer to the Rebel Alliance—she never formally joined, but she offered aid and safety to Rebel agents at her nightclub.

Corinna A'Daasha, nicknamed Cori by her friends, and her twin sister Kandria A'Daasha were female Corellian Humans born on the planet Corellia into a wealthy family that provided for all their needs. As children, the sisters never struggled for anything, and although Kandria enjoyed a life of luxury, Corinna became bored and restless by it. Looking for excitement and adventure, Corinna ended up taking a portion of her wealth and leaving the A'Daasha household to explore the galaxy. Separation did not suit either sister, however, and shortly afterward Kandria joined Corinna on her travels. Kandria convinced Corinna to travel to the pleasure world Adarlon, where Corinna enjoyed her stay and the two sisters decided to try their hands at business.

The twins established the Glow Dome nightclub together. Featuring elaborate sound and light displays, it became extremely successful. Even though the twins were co-owners of the nightclub and each had at the venue an office of her own, Corinna took care of the day-to-day operations, such as handling security, for the purposes of which she bought a used seeker droid. Despite her success, Corinna still felt unfulfilled by her life until she met a member of the underground group No-Holds-Barred, who introduced her to banned holomaterials concerning the Rebel Alliance and the Jedi tradition of Force-users. Shortly after her introduction to the Rebellion's cause, Corinna became sympathetic to the organization, and although she never formally joined, she allowed underground holos to be sold at her nightclub and allowed Rebel operatives to use her business as a safehouse.

Corinna A'Daasha was the antithesis of her sister. Whereas Kandria enjoyed their luxurious lifestyle, Corinna's longing for excitement and adventure caused her to reject her opulent upbringing and made her sympathetic to the Rebellion. Corinna and her sister shared a love for clothes, although Kandria took more pride in her wardrobe collection and put more care into it: Corinna, on the other hand, despite enjoying pieces that she felt accentuated her features, would often wear the same clothing.
