entities.name: Ahleazah
entities.description:
Ahleazah was a female Mon Calamari healer who served in the Alliance to Restore the Republic and later the New Republic during the Galactic Civil War.

Captured during the Galactic Empire's occupation of Dac, Ahleazah's skills as a healer earned her work with medical staff, while her family was put to forced labor. Ahleazah put her skills to use helping whomever she could as the occupation authority moved her from camp to camp. Her actions in saving a low level Imperial Starfleet officer earned her escape from the enslaved world. She was placed aboard his starship where she was able to make use of and learn from the advanced Imperial medical technologies.

While aboard the Imperial vessel, Ahleazah tended to a captured Rebel Alliance pilot who was slated to undergo interrogation. Ahleazah aided the pilot and seized the opportunity to escape the Empire. Together the pair stowed away in an escape pod and launched just as the ship exited the Anoat system. An Alliance convoy picked up the drifting pod, and Ahleazah went on to serve the Alliance and New Republic as a healer.

entities.name: Ahlya
entities.description:
Ahlya was a female Human operative who worked for the Darkside, a repair station in the Cularin system asteroid belt. She was also a member of The Cell, a criminal faction wanting to oust and replace local crimelord Nirama. She wasn't very highly placed in the Cell, neither was the Darkside faction in the general Cell scheme.

In 32 BBY, Ahlya was one of the few remaining members of the Darkside contingent after a raid committed by Nirama's forces. Other survivors included Dor Balse, Kruss Gaal, Jarrilyn, Jasper and Michael. At that point, they were trying to recruit new members, including local Wookiees, Kaarl the Ithorian and some newcomers, but the people in Darkside felt no respect for the local Cell. Shortly thereafter, they were captured by a group of spies working for Nirama.

Her implication in The Cell and subsequent capture were public knowledge less than one month later.

entities.name: Ahoec
entities.description:
Ahoec was a Mon Calamari female and the sister of Loku Kanoloa. She was an aspiring diplomat. In an effort to escape the Galactic Empire, she joined a rebel convoy transporting civilians to a hidden rebel world. The Empire ambushed the convoy, and the transport she was on managed to jump to hyperspace and escape the battle. Eventually, the hyperdrive gave out near the planet Tatooine, where the damaged ship crashed. Ahoec, along with the other survivors, set up a camp where they stayed before being attacked by Captain Terro and his forces.

Ahoec first appeared in the Star Wars: Imperial Assault companion app Legends of the Alliance, in the "Jabba's Realm" campaign. Ahoec has a chance of being one of the eight crash survivors present during the first mission, or guaranteed if the player chooses Loku Kanoloa to be in the squad. Depending upon the actions and success of the player during the missions, Ahoec's fate can vary. Ahoec can end up being enslaved by Jabba the Hutt, eaten by a rancor, left behind at Terro's camp, or successfully have escaped Tatooine with the squad.

entities.name: Aida Forte's mother
entities.description:
A female individual was the mother of the Kadas'sa'Nikto Jedi Knight Aida Forte. when Forte and Jedi Master Creighton Sun traveled to planet Dalna to investigate the Path of the Open Hand cult, they witnessed a Teevan man being brought before the Mother and the Leveler, the Path's leader and a creature which fed on Force-sensitives, respectively. As the Leveler consumed the Teevan, the two Jedi also became overwhelmed by fear.

After it was over, Forte compared the feeling of the incident to her killing her own mother. The Jedi Knight then noted she had not felt as much fear before as she had during the ordeal, and even though it felt real, it could not have been. Forte then concluded that the experience was horrible, and as she did not know her mother, it would not have made any sense.

Aida Forte's mother was mentioned in Cataclysm, a novel written by Lydia Kang and published in 2023 as part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's

entities.name: Duala Aidu
entities.description:
Duala Aidu was a Force-sensitive female Human who was a member of the Singing Mountain Clan, a clan of witches that resided on the planet Dathomir.

In about 18 BBY, the Jedi Knight Jax Pavan ventured to Dathomir on business with the Singing Mountain Clan and as he approach the clan's stronghold, he was spotted by Aidu and the Dathomirian Zabrak Magash Drashi, and the pair escorted him to their clan mother, Augwynne Djo. Pavan subsequently sought the aid of the witches to allow him to access the secrets of the holocron of the Sith Lord Darth Ramage, which would only activate after being provided with a large quantity of blood from a Force-sensitive being, and Aidu, Djo, Drashi and Pavan all donated blood to allow the Jedi open the holocron.

entities.name: Aigorn
entities.description:
Aigorn was a female Trandoshan who lived on Tatooine during the time of the Galactic Civil War. Sometimes after the Battle of Yavin, she tasked a spacer with eliminating one of the medical staff from the White Thranta Shipping Company and steal medical data from the White Thranta bunker.

Aigorn appears in the directory tree files for the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, According to these files, introduced with the 2005 "New Game Enhancements," Aigorn would have been a quest giver, giving to players two quests named "Opening Moves" and "Information Control" during the Mos Eisley part of the "Legacy Quest." However, Aigorn is not known to have appeared on the game's live servers as a proper non-player character. Nevertheless, an emulated depiction pulled from this character's Interchange File Format reveals what he would have looked like if he were added to the game.

entities.name: Ailish
entities.description:
Ailish was a Tarlafar and the mother of the Force-sensitive infant Bayrn, living with him in a mountain city on the world Caraad. After her son was witnessed using the Force to throw a pot while they were out shopping, Ailish rushed him home, but an Aqualish neighbor reported the child as the Galactic Empire had placed a bounty on Force-sensitive children. The bounty hunter Cad Bane then arrived at Ailish's home and stunned her before kidnapping Bayrn.

Ailish was a Tarlafar the pair lived in a mountain city but rumors began to spread about how Bayrn might be gifted or cursed. While out shopping on one of the city's market streets, Ailish carried her son to a flower stall and placed him on a nearby crate with his doll, stroking his head then leaving him to play while she spoke with the vendor. Bayrn began throwing his doll up in the air and catching it before accidentally throwing it into some pots.

With Ailish still distracted, Bayrn climbed down from the crate and crawled over to recover the doll, sending a pot flying through the air with the Force as he did so. This was witnessed by an Arcona and a human nearby, who pointed out Bayrn as the culprit when an angry Aqualish questioned who had thrown the pot. As the Aqualish dismissed the idea that an infant could have lifted the pot, Ailish became aware of the commotion and hurried over to collect a Bayrn, who had begun to wail. Apologizing to the trio discussing the incident, she then carried Bayrn away and returned to their home. Having listened to the Arcona speak more about Bayrn's apparent powers, the Aqualish watched the mother enter her home with interest and later reported the child from his neighboring apartment, as the Galactic Empire had placed a bounty on Force-sensitive children.

Based on the Aqualish's tip, the bounty hunter Cad Bane and his droid Todo 360 sought out Ailish's home one night. The mother was playing with Bayrn and his doll on the apartment's couch, feeding him a snack and then tickling him, when she heard Bane's footsteps outside. Seeing his silhouette passing by under the apartment's door, Ailish moved Bayrn from a table to the couch slightly further from the door and frowned as she moved over to the entryway. Worried, she glanced back at her child as Bane's silhouette returned beneath the door, prompting Ailish to pick up a shovel for defense.

entities.name: Airen
entities.description:
Airen was a Human female who served as the mayor of Espelar Settlement on the planet of Tatooine during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the resurgent Sith Empire.

A female Human, Airen lived on the Outer Rim planet during the Great Galactic War and subsequent Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the resurgent Sith Empire. By 3643 BBY, she had begun serving as the mayor of Espelar, a Human settlement near the native Jawa settlement of Camp Karnori. Espelar was located in the northern part of the Jundland Wastes, the region just south of the city of Anchorhead, and the settlement also had a small trading post to the west.

When the former Jedi Galen Besk asked a Republic-allied individual to stop a group of Imperial saboteurs at Espelar's trading post, the individual came to Airen after they eliminated the Imperials. Her settlement was constantly plagued by broken equipment, sandstorms, and attacks by pirates and the native Sand People, so the individual offered to help out by aiding Junter Galt, the head of the area's branch of the Anchorhead Guard, in training the new recruits.

Airen was created for Star Wars: The Old Republic, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game released by BioWare on December 20, 2011. She appears in the Tatooine Bonus Series of missions for Republic players, after the player has defeated the saboteurs. Airen asks the player to go speak with Junter Galt, beginning the next missions.

entities.description:
Troya Ajak was a female Ash'ad warrior and former Mandalorian who lived during the third Galactic War.

In 3626 BBY, Troya Ajak and the Ash'ad joined in on an attack on the Mandalorian ship the Spirit of Vengeance II alongside Clan Varad and the Dar'manda at the behest of Heta Kol in exchange for Mandalorian relics, which Ajak considered symbols of honor and a reminder of what the Mandalorians once were. There she encountered the Alliance Commander and Rass Ordo, who she engaged in combat. The fight ended with her death.

entities.name: Jin-Rio Akabi
entities.description:
Jin-Rio Akabi was a Human female diplomat for the Rebel Alliance from Colstev.

Jin-Rio Akabi was a Human female from Colstev. She was a student at the University of Zo-Ro before the massacre there. She joined the Alliance Special Operations as a Political Advisor to stop further such incidents. In 0 ABY she was involved with operations at the captured Whisper Base.

Jin-Rio, Zal Artha, Vendri DeRalm, Cael Hanarist, Tendaar Bel, and Arkhan Brem'tu were assigned to infiltrate Whisper Base on Onderon. Their mission was to isolate the base from any external communication, disable the shuttles and capture the base before Lieutenant Sarev called for reinforcements. Once the group landed on Onderon, they avoided stormtrooper patrols and crossed the dense jungle for a few hours before they finally arrived at Whisper Base. They entered through the garage and quickly sliced the communication line, which caused an enemy patrol to direct their attention towards the garage.

The squad of rebels hid in different areas successfully and awaited the patrol's arrival. They eliminated the patrol of soldiers in a fast and efficient manner, without alerting the rest of the base.

entities.description:
Feyra Akaris was the mother of Iskat Akaris. Once a Jedi Padawan, Feyra left the Jedi Order after failing her Jedi Trials, specifically her Trial of the Spirit, and returned to her homeworld of Pkori. After giving birth to a daughter, she gave up her child to Jedi Master Sember Vey. The Jedi Master promised Akaris to protect her daughter, and maintained possession of her yellow-bladed lightsaber in secret. The elder Akaris became depressed shortly thereafter and committed suicide out in the deserts of Pkori. Her death was felt in the Force by Vey and Jedi Master Klefan Opus.

entities.name: Thirteenth Sister
entities.description:
The Thirteenth Sister, formerly known as Iskat Akaris, was a Pkorian female Inquisitor of the Galactic Empire who served under Darth Vader. A former Jedi Knight who willingly joined the Inquisitorius, she killed three Jedi on her first hunt. She later accompanied Vader, Fifth Brother, and Tualon Yaluna, to hunt down the former Jedi Master Eeth Koth.

Vader's discovery of her relationship with Yaluna led him to attempt to kill her shortly after their return to the Inquisitorius Headquarters. Yaluna held him off while she escaped, then followed after her. Vader pursued them in a destructive chase across Coruscant until they knocked him down with a speeder. Before the Thirteenth Sister could kill him, Vader froze the couple with the Force and killed them.

Born around 40 BBY, Iskat Akaris served the Jedi Order during the waning years of the Galactic Republic. Akaris was taken in early as a child to the Jedi Order. Her birth species and origin planet were both unknown to the Jedi, a topic that would spark many awkward conversations when asked about her unique species.

She was taken as an Apprentice to Master Sember Vey, one of the order’s most prominent collectors of Jedi texts and scrolls found throughout the Galaxy. Akaris enjoyed her lightsaber training the most and dreaded meditation, but she did notice that it did improve her focus and emotional control. She relished training with Grandmaster Yoda and exploring with younger and more energetic Jedi Knights.

entities.description:
Aktropaw was a Dathomirian female Nightsister witch, and one of the Great Mothers who allied with Mitth'raw'nuruodo. she and the other Great Mothers, Klothow and Lakesis, welcomed Nightsister Morgan Elsbeth and her forces to the planet Peridea after calling Elsbeth there via her dreams.

Aktropaw first appeared in "Part Six: Far, Far Away," the sixth episode of the Ahsoka television series, portrayed by Jeryl Prescott Gallien. While not identified in the episode, the character's name was given in its credits. This is similar to how Aktropaw and the other Great Mothers claimed to be able to read and know the threads of fate and destiny.

entities.name: Kata Akuna
entities.description:
Kata Akuna was a human female who was the daughter of Bode and Tayala Akuna.

The Akuna family lived happily on the Inner Rim world of Birren. One day, Kata was out with Bode when they received a comm message from Tayala saying to flee with Kata because the Inquisitorius had found them. Bode took Kata to the Nova Garon system and struck a deal with an ISB commander and chief supervisor named Lank Denvik, his former handler in Republic Intelligence. Bode was to act on behalf of Denvik in order to keep Kata safe from the Inquisitorius. One such mission required Bode to gain the trust of Jedi Knight Cal Kestis in order to infiltrate the anti-Imperial operations of Saw Gerrera. While with Kestis, Bode learned of a hidden planet called Tanalorr, which the Empire was unaware of due to it being blocked by the Koboh Abyss.

While her father served Commander Denvik, Kata remained in the officers' quarters on the ISB station, spending significant time alone with her doll Mookie. She quickly developed a hatred for the base while living there.

Bode eventually betrayed Kestis, and stole from him a compass which served as the last remaining key to navigate the Koboh Abyss and reach Tanalorr. With Kestis in pursuit, Bode fled back to Nova Garon to fetch Kata. As her father implemented a plan to betray Denvik to the Inquisitorius and erase any record of him or Kata, the girl met Kestis, who had infiltrated the base. Kestis attempted to win the child's trust by helping Kata find Mookie who had been lost in the living quarters. Bode managed to distract Kestis and buy time for him and Kata to escape the ISB station.

entities.name: Tayala Akuna
entities.description:
Tayala Akuna was a human female who was the wife of former Jedi Knight Bode Akuna, and mother of Kata Akuna.

After becoming the wife of former Jedi Knight Bode Akuna and having a daughter with him, Kata Akuna, Tayala was killed by the Inquisitors after her executors failed to discover the location of her husband, a Jedi survivor of Order 66, in the Akuna family home in Birren. Upon their arrival, Tayala quickly sent a message to Bode warning him and her daughter not to come home. After the Galactic Empire discovered his absence, they took their frustration out on her instead, ending her life.

Following her death her husband began working for the ISB, partly because Bode wanted to know which Inquisitor killed his wife and because the ISB helped keep Kata safe. Kata realized that her father changed due to her mother's death, and perhaps she herself too. After her father's death, Kata placed her doll Mookie, the one her mother had given her, to burn along with her father's body on a funeral pyre.

Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy

entities.description:
A Chiss female was the former caregiver of sky-walker navigator Al'iastov. At some point they told Al'iastov not to complain about her feelings. Around 39 BBY, on Al'iastov's final voyage as a sky-walker on the Chiss Defense Force Transport Tomra, she met Cadet Mitth'raw'nuru, core name "Thrawn," who saw her in a state of distress and asked if she was alright. Al'iastov, remembering her former caregiver, told the cadet she was fine.

This caregiver was mentioned in flashbacks of the 2020 novel Thrawn Ascendancy: Chaos Rising, written by Timothy Zahn as the first entry in his Star Wars: The Ascendancy Trilogy.

entities.name: Vek Alakor
entities.description:
Vek Alakor was a female archaeologist active after the reign of the Galactic Empire. She mentored the Lucem Sian, who adopted his mentor's surname in her honor, and was concerned with returning important artifacts to their rightful home. One such artifact was Luke Skywalker's yellow lightsaber. One of the worlds she and Sian discovered was a world with a pollen that degraded metal over time, and Vek named it Alakor after herself. She was also an associate of the Pirate Queen Maz Kanata. By 33 ABY, Alakor had died at the hands of the First Order.

entities.name: Alani
entities.description:
Alani was a Human female who was the daughter of Ewane and twin sister of Eritha.

Alani was born in 57 BBY on New Apsolon. At this time a totalitarian system of government ruled the planet. The Civilized received all the benefits, while the Workers lived in poverty. Alani's father, Ewane, was a leader of the resistance against this social system. Due to this activity he spent many years in the prison and saw his daughters rarely. Alani and Eritha were raised mostly by friends of their father, since their mother had died around the time they were born. One of those friends was Lenz.

With the first elections after the fall of the regime in the year 47 BBY, their father was selected to be Supreme Governor of New Apsolon. At that time, the Jedi Knights were sent to supervise the election, and they were represented by Qui-Gon Jinn and Tahl, who developed a bond with Alani and her twin sister Eritha.

Ewane held the office for five years, but was murdered shortly into his second term. Roan, a close friend of their father and his successor, adopted them. At that time, Alani and Eritha conceived a plan to gain the power on New Apsolon. That plan included killing Roan and kidnapping Tahl, who died as a result of the injuries suffered. However, the plan failed with no small part due to the actions of Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi who came to New Apsolon looking for the missing Tahl. Because Alani wasn't as clever as Eritha, she had bragged to Obi-Wan that Qui-Gon would die in a trap elaborated by her sister, leading Obi-Wan to rescue Qui-Gon. After the failed plan, both Alani and Eritha, along with their associate Balog were arrested.

entities.name: Alara
entities.description:
Alara was a Human female member of the Jedi Order during the Great Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. She was present at the Jedi Temple on the Republic capital of Coruscant in 3653 BBY, when the Empire launched a surprise attack on the planet. When the Sith Lord Darth Malgus infiltrated and assaulted the Temple with a strike team of fifty other Sith, Alara joined her fellow Jedi in the defense of their home; she attacked Malgus alongside two of her comrades, but was quickly defeated—the Sith Lord severed Alara's lightsaber-wielding hand and throttled her with his own hand before slamming her into the Temple floor with Force-enhanced strength, killing her. Malgus's forces were victorious in the battle, slaughtering Alara's Jedi brethren before destroying the Temple as a whole in what would prove to be the final battle of the war.

Alara first appeared in The Old Republic: Deceived, a 2011 novel written by Paul S. Kemp.

entities.name: Xiri A'lbaran
entities.description:
Xiri A'lbaran was a human after a chance meeting, she proposed marrying Prince Phan-tu Zenn of Eiram at a summit hosted by the Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order during a temporary truce, hoping the marriage would help bring peace to their planets. Though the wedding was tumultuous, in the aftermath it was decided that a peace treaty would be signed on the holy moon Jedha.

When A'lbaran, Zenn, and the Jedi then discovered members of the Path of the Open Hand cult trying to frame E'ronoh for accumulating the bioweapon klytobacter, which could devestate Eiram, A'lbaran agreed to travel with the Jedi on a diplomatic mission to speak with the Path on Dalna and investigate their role in the conflict. However, the Path used it as an excuse to attack them and the Jedi, which erupted into an extensive battle that became known as the Night of Sorrow. She and Zenn managed to escape the planet and the battle in a damaged starfighter they found. The two, with the help of Supreme Chancellor Orlen Mollo, then united their planets against the Path and turned the tide of the battle in the Jedi's favor, all while hoping to bring a lasting peace to their worlds.

Xiri A'lbaran was born to Monarch A'lbaran, and was the second in line for the monarchy behind her brother Niko A'lbaran. In around 387 BBY a war between E'ronoh and its twin planet Eiram was reignited when Prince Niko accidentally drowned while on a visit to Eiram. Xiri therefore became heir to the throne and was made Captain of Thylefire Squadron, leading the E'roni starfighters into battle against the Eirami for five years. A constant at her side was her second-in-command, Jerrod Segaru, with whom she developed a close friendship.

entities.description:
Albea was a Human female scientist who worked for the Galactic Republic during the Cold War.

During the Cold War, Albea was imprisoned for unknown reasons by Voontara Fa'athra in his palace on Nal Hutta. At the same time, the resurgent Sith Empire placed a bounty on Albea, who hired Trandoshan bounty hunter named Rarsk to hunt her.

The prospective Grand Champion of the Great Hunt was on quest to retrieve the Great Hunt sponsorship token from Rarsk and saved her from the Trandoshan, only to later kill and claim her bounty.

The player has the option to spare Albea instead of claiming the bounty on her, as she is not a required target of the Great Hunt.

entities.name: Alcida-Auka
entities.description:
Alcida-Auka was a Lanai female who served as the matron of the Caretakers of Temple Island on the planet Ahch-To. In the year 34 ABY, she encountered the former scavenger Rey in the Jedi village on the island. The Lanai was scaling a fingerlip garpon with a knife when Rey emerged from the stone hut she was residing in while receiving training from Jedi Master Luke Skywalker, another resident of the island.

Alcida-Auka was a Lanai female who lived in the Caretaker village on Temple Island on the planet Ahch-To. She inherited the position of matron of the Caretakers from her mother, which had previously been held by many of her ancestors, and in turn would someday pass that on to her eldest daughter. The Caretakers were responsible for the upkeep of the ancient Jedi village on the island, and during Alcida-Auka's tenure as matron, the Jedi Master Luke Skywalker lived as a resident of the village. The Caretakers tolerated his presence, though he insisted on doing most of their duties to care for him himself, something which puzzled Alcida-Auka.

In the year 34 ABY, the scavenger Rey traveled to Ahch-To to recruit Skywalker to the Resistance and receive training from him. After Skywalker reluctantly agreed to train Rey, the student began sleeping in one of the stone huts of the Jedi village. After seeing a vision of her adversary Kylo Ren, Rey accidentally blew a hole in the side of the hut and then emerged to find Alcida-Auka and the other Caretakers outside. While two of the other Lanais fussed over trying to repair the hut, the matron scaled a fingerlip garpon using a fish-scaling knife on a clay chopping board in order to prepare a meal for the village as part of her daily routine. When she asked Skywalker about Rey's identity, he responded that she was his niece, though she was doubtful.

Later, Rey was training with her lightsaber on a cliff, where the young Force-user chopped a rock in half. The rock fell down the cliff and onto a wheelbarrow that Alcida-Auka and a fellow Lanai were using for transport, completely destroying their cart. Surprised, Alcida-Auka and the other Lanai spotted Rey and glared at her in dismay. Not long after this, the matron participated in the Festival of Return, a monthly ceremony in which the male Lanais returned from their fishing trips and old relationships were mended. Alcida-Auka was dancing with a Visitor when Rey burst in with her lightsaber, having been led to believe the Visitors were in fact marauders coming to pillage the Caretakers, surprising the Lanais. After a moment of awkward silence, Alcida-Auka indicated for the girl to join in, cheering and dancing when she did.

Maelrich Alde was a female Human and a member of the Alderaanian House Alde during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire.

A noble woman of the Alderaanian House Alde, Maelrich Alde resided on Alderaan during the Cold War, and her nephew Alethios served as a captain at Wardpost Landa. An opponent to House Rist, Alde sought to disable the Rists' satellite relays in the Juran Mountains and end their ability to monitor communications in the region.

entities.name: Renata Alde
entities.description:
Renata Alde was a female Human member of the Alderaanian House Alde living during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire.

In 3643 BBY, Lady Renata was confronted in her estate by a Sith Warrior sent to her by Duke Kendoh Thul. Kendoh made several advances to Renata in the past and believed she had information concerning her former handmaiden Jaesa Willsaam, he also requested the Sith to bring Renata to him. The Sith slew her bodyguard Windredd and threatened Renata, who explained that Jaesa was a handmaiden not to her, but to Gesselle Organa of House Organa and begged not to take her to Kendoh. The Warrior and FimmRess ignored her pleas and took her to the Duke.

entities.description:
Tess Alder also known as "Rogue Two" was a Human female from the planet of Corellia. During the Galactic Civil War she became a pilot for the Alliance to Restore the Republic, where she performed with enough skill and was deemed trustworthy enough to be selected by Leia Organa to be part of a team to uncover a mole within the alliance. The team worked entirely off the books, with only Mon Mothma knowing of their existence outside of the team's members. As well as discovering the mole they were also tasked with finding a suitable planet on which the alliance could set up a new base.

Tess Alder first appeared in first appeared in the Star Wars (2013) 2 of the comic book series titled simply Star Wars published by Dark Horse Comics. The issue was written by Brian Wood, illustrated by Carlos D'Anda and colored by Gabe Eltaeb. It was released on February 13 2013.

entities.name: Elarea Aldraste
entities.description:
Elarea Aldraste, also called "The Red Huntress," was a female Human living during the Galactic War. A moderately successful bounty hunter hunter operating in Wild Space, she had a reputation for preferring her targets dead instead of alive. Around 3631 BBY she took control of the Crimson Fang gang, which following the death of Empress Vaylin and formation of the Eternal Alliance took over Port Nowhere by force, planning to use the mobile space station as their base of operations. The Alliance sent a strike team on a mission to liberate Port Nowhere, who systematically rid the station of Outer Rim's most notorious villains, eventually confronting The Red Huntress and killing her.

Elarea Aldraste appears in Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne as the final boss during the "Crimson Fang" Uprising.

entities.name: Alya Aldrete
entities.description:
Lady Alya Aldrete was an Alderaanian female Human during the Imperial Era. Heiress to the business enterprise of the wealthy Aldrete family in the early years of the Galactic Empire, Alya achieved renown and celebrity status owing to her hedonistic lifestyle. Her public persona was however just a facade; Aldrete covertly established a smuggler fleet operating in the Core Worlds and Deep Core regions, using her criminal contacts to gather information and map reliable hyperlanes.

Circa 17 BBY, Aldrete attended the launch event on the world of Alderaan for her family's new luxury hovertrain. The train fell under attack from Trandoshan mercenaries and Aldrete was briefly captured, before being rescued by agents of Bail Organa, Alderaan's delegate to the Imperial Senate. Aldrete subsequently pledged her support to Organa's Alderaanian Resistance rebel group and marshalled her smuggler armada for a raid by the rebels against a prototype Super Star Destroyer under construction by the Empire in the Beshqek system. Aldrete and her forces successfully destroyed the leviathan warship, achieving one of the first victories of an insurgent group against the Imperial regime.

Lady Alya Aldrete was a wealthy Alderaanian female Human noblewoman of the affluent Aldrete family who lived during the early years of the Imperial Period. The heiress to her family's chain of casinos, hotels and passenger liners, Aldrete rose to prominence within galactic society as a result of her excessive pleasure-seeking and debauchery. She became a celebrity icon and her activities were widely reported in the media, including details of her romantic partners, her vacations and where she went clubbing.

In truth, Aldrete's public persona was just a carefully-cultivated cover. She also employed the elderly Twi'lek male Notru'denn as her personal assistant.

She may have been related to Agrippa Aldrete, an aide of Senator Bail Antilles during the time of the Invasion of Naboo, and Alya Aldrete, a noblewoman. Following Order 66, she was present when Sate Pestage and Darth Vader were in search of Fang Zar, after they paid a visit with Bail Organa.

entities.name: Tehlan Aleece
entities.description:
Tehlan Aleece was a female Human and the niece of Moff Venram Krax. She was a long time agent for Alliance Intelligence, using her connections to report vital information on Imperial procedures and activities. She fled Corellia when she suspected her cover was about to be blown.

She was fluent in Basic, Bocce, Bothese, and High Galactic. She was an experienced pilot as well.

Ducha AlGray was the head of House AlGray and the leader of the Heritage Council, which sought to assassinate the Queen Mother, Tenel Ka. She was suspected of being involved in the plot to assassinate the Queen Mother and her young daughter, Allana. This proved true when AlGray and her army attacked Tenel Ka and her Hapan forces, which escalated into the Battle of Hapes. Shortly after the conclusion of the battle, AlGray and several members of the Heritage Council were detained and questioned.

At some point she named Aleson Gray her Duch'da.

entities.name: Ali'ane
entities.description:
Ali'ane was a female Lupr'or who lived in her home on the planet Luprora. They had a great granddaughter who wore a necklace salvaged from a Lupr'or starship. Shortly after the Battle of Starkiller Base, Ali'ane's great granddaughter visited them with Captain Phasma, TN-3465, and Dar'en to speak about a necklace.

Ali'ane was the oldest living Lupr'or by the time of the Battle of Starkiller Base in 34 ABY. They were born in the stars. They gave a necklace salvaged from a Lupr'or starship to their great granddaughter. During the hunt for the First Order fugitive Sol Rivas, Captain Phasma questioned Ali'ane and their great granddaughter about where they had acquired the necklace from.

Regarding technology as evil, Ali'ane refused to reveal the location of the last Lupr'or starship, claiming that it came from the "old world". At Phasma's prompting, Ali'ane's great granddaughter claimed that Phasma had been sent by the gods to save them from the R'ora and the Tsw'ells. Ali'ane responded that the ancestors had forbidden technology, which descried as the soul killer.

Despite Ali'ane's efforts, their great granddaughter secretly revealed the location of the Lupr'or starship to Phasma. This allowed her to obtain generators which the Lupr'or used to electrocute the tsw'ells in the lake surrounding the R'ora stronghold.

entities.name: Ali'ane's great granddaughter
entities.description:
The Lupr'or Ali'ane had a great granddaughter who lived during the First Order-Resistance War. She possessed a necklace that was salvaged from an abandoned Lupr'or starship. Captain Phasma enlisted the girl's help in locating the Lupr'or starship in order to retrieve technology needed to attack the Tsw'ells guarding the R'ora stronghold. Phasma wanted to eliminate Lieutenant Sol Rivas since he was the only who knew that she had lowered Starkiller Base's shields, causing the superweapon's destruction.

This Lupr'or girl was the great granddaughter of Ali'ane, the oldest living Lupr'or who was born in the stars. The girl inherited a necklace from her grandmother, which was salvaged from an abandoned Lupr'or starship. After the First Order visitor Captain Phasma studied the R'ora stronghold, she grabbed Ali'ane and asked her where she got the necklace. The child led Phasma, the TIE fighter pilot TN-3465, and the Lupr'or guide Dar'en to the home of Ali'ane.

The girl introduced Ali'ane to Captain Phasma, who asked about the origins of the necklace. Ali'ane replied that she had obtained the necklace from the "old world". When Phasma asked where she could find more, Ali'ane replied that it was forbidden. At Phasma's prompting, the girl tried to convince her relative that Phasma had come to save them from the R'ora and the Tsw'ells. She added that Jair'i had said that the gods had sent Phasma to help them. Regarding technology as evil, Ali'ane refused to reveal the location of the ship.

Later, the girl told Phasma that she was better at climbing rocks than her companion TN-3465. Phasma replied that she had seen a world similar to Luprora and that it was a hard life. The girl agreed to take Phasma to the ship if she did not inform Ali'ane. For several hours, the Lupr'or girl led Phasma, TN-3465, and Da'ren to the last Lupr'or ship, which rested on a cliff that had not been claimed by the sea.

Around 3640 BBY she was stationed at the commando outpost on Koss Overlook in the Gormak Lands, overlooking Gorma-Koss. She informed a bounty hunter about Republic General Thelonia Redrish, who went into the Gormak territory to negotiate with the Gormak.

Ali-Le appears in Star Wars: The Old Republic during the Bounty Hunter class mission "Captive Audience" on Voss.

entities.name: Alianda
entities.description:
Alianda was a round-headed Human female slave.

By about 20 BBY, Alianda was aged between twenty and twenty-five, and she was a slave to infamous Chevin slaver Phylus Mon, who kept her onboard his ship, Animiasma. At that time, Phylus Mon was trying to repair a Sith artifact known as the Darkstaff, the semi-sentient Darkstaff was modifying the galaxy around it, namely the ship, to its image, and a team sent by Jedi Master Lanius Qel-Bertuk opposed to some of Phylus Mon's activities.

The Darkstaff possessed Alianda to negotiate with Qel-Bertuk's team as a physical being. During the possession, Alianda's scleras turned pitch black and her voice turned raspy, disconcerting her/its opponents. When the Darkstaff decided that the negotiation was over, it simply abandoned Alianda's body. The shock of having had something that horrible inside of her could have been lethal for her, although it is unclear whether she survived or not.

Alianda's voice during the possession is described as "Imagine James Earl Jones, his throat lined with sandpaper".
entities.short_description: Alianda was a round-headed Human female slave.

entities.name: Mill Alibeth
entities.description:
Mill Alibeth was a Force-sensitive Zabrak female who served as a Jedi Initiate in the late Republic Era. Alibeth possessed powerful empathic powers which she found difficult to control, resulting in her experiencing severe nausea whenever she was exposed to anything relating to combat or violence, even mere discussion of the subject. After attempting to cut herself off from the Force, she discovered that her unique connection could be used to provide medical and spiritual assistance to wounded Jedi fighting in the Clone Wars.

Alibeth and her friend Vivert Stag were among those in the Jedi Order that survived the Great Jedi Purge and were able to remain undetected. The pair took up the life of supposed bounty hunters, coming to work alongside hunter Mwarr Ja'Randa.

Mill Alibeth was a Jedi Initiate around the time of the First Battle of Geonosis in 22 BBY. She was a part of an Initiate Clan of eight younglings including friend Vivert Stag. While the rest of the Clan was excited for their upcoming trip to Ilum for The Gathering, Alibeth was overcome with intense feelings of nausea over the recent increase in violence across the galaxy. Although she did a good job faking it for the others, she could not bring herself to be excited at the prospect of building a lightsaber. No one could explain why her particularly connection to the Force worked this way, but Alibeth was becoming increasingly miserable. She eventually resorted to pushing away the Force entirely, something in direct conflict with her Jedi teachings.

The day before Alibeth's clan were set to fly to Ilum, Cato Neimoidia, the Purse World of the Trade Federation, was hit by a bombing, capturing the attention of most of the Temple's adults. This only increased Alibeth's growing suffering since she felt the impending war on the horizon.

entities.name: Alilia
entities.description:
Alilia was a Lethan Twi'lek female who was a slave to the White Maw boss Shai Tenna during the Cold War and the Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the resurgent Sith Empire.

Alilia became a slave and a wife to the White Maw Weequay boss Shai Tenna in the year 3649 BBY. She remained in this position for seven years, keeping the facade of a dim-witted woman who adored her Master. While this appearance was pleasing to Tenna, Alilia had in fact not only despised him, but did much of the work he claimed to be doing herself, such as picking up supplies at drop points and otherwise participating in the pirate gang management. When the White Maw discovered Trick, a young male Kitonak with a weak connection to the Force, they found that when frightened he could use it to disguise not only himself, but the entire fleet nearby. Trying to get him to cooperate, they bashed him in the skull, causing permanent brain damage. Alilia nursed and nurtured Trick as best she could, but his mind never came back. Because he was unable to use the Force consciously, the pirates tortured the child to keep him in a constant state of fear, a practice Alilia found disgusting, but was unable to stop.

In 3642 BBY Alilia was with the rest of the White Maw on Hoth when a smuggler later known as Voidhound approached the gang. After he survived an attempt by Shai Tenna to kill him, Alilia started to view the newcomer as a chance to escape her situation. On board of the Star of Coruscant she explained the situation with Trick and begged the smuggler for help.

After the Voidhound killed Shai Tenna, Alilia agreed to send Trick to the Jedi Order where he could be fixed and would become a Jedi.

entities.name: Alinta
entities.description:
Alinta was a Human female who served as a member of the Friends of the Republic, an organization dedicated to covertly help the Galactic Republic during the start of the Clone Wars against the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

For many years, Alinta and her allies communicated with Senator Bail Organa anonymously via a secret comlink by sending coded messages. During the Clone Wars, Alinta contacted Organa with crucial information regarding the Sith. The woman claimed that a planet called Zigoola posed a possible threat to the safety of the Republic. Organa, not knowing what to do with the information, called upon his fellow Senator and friend Padmé Amidala, who was good friends with the Jedi. Padmé convinced Master Obi-Wan Kenobi to listen to Organa's story. Reluctantly trusting Organa and his source, Kenobi and Organa set off to Zigoola. Alinta sent coordinates one at a time to Organa, as a precaution. When Organa and Kenobi arrived at the last pair of coordinates, they found themselves at a space station. At first, it seemed as if the station were abandoned, but they soon found that a battle was in progress between Alinta's allies and the Kalarba pirates.

The pirates and their battle droids had already eliminated most of Alinta's allies, leaving her the last remaining of her group. Kenobi and Organa entered the fight and managed to defeat the remaining pirates and their droids, although Alinta was mortally wounded during the fray. She was too badly hurt to be saved by Kenobi's limited healing abilities, but the woman managed to give some information to them before she died. Alinta had one request of them before they left: blow up the station so no one would be able to retrieve any information. Organa and Kenobi received a data crystal with Zigoola's coordinates and scuttled the station to preserve the group's secrets.

entities.name: Alirya
entities.description:
Alirya was a female human member of the Path of the Open Hand cult who was out on the Galactic Frontier preaching the Path's teachings at the time of its violent end on the planet Dalna in 382 BBY. At some point between the Path's collapse and around 381 BBY, she was one of the few Path members tracked down by the Evereni pirate leader and former Path member Marda Ro. She was one of the few to accept Ro's offer to join her group and Ro took Alirya aboard her ship, the Gaze Electric to introduce her to a creature known as the Great Leveler. Alirya quickly rose to a position by Ro's side as her assistant.

Around 379 BBY, Alirya, Ro and two other beings in Ro's service observed the Leveler consume a Jedi, and Alirya later conversed with Ro in the Gaze throne hall. At some point no earlier than 379 BBY, Alirya was present when the Twi'lek raider Fori Nagor presented captured refugees to Ro. Later, Alirya and Ro were alone in the throne hall and debated on the future of the group Ro led, and what Ro's goals were. When Ro managed to track down the Evereni siblings Vika and Velya Faer during her hunt for others of her species, Alirya stood by Ro's side during the initial meeting and prepared food for the three Evereni.

Feeling that her position was threatened by the two Faers, Alirya attempted to murder Vika with a dagger during a feast thrown on the Gaze a few days later. Her attack was unsuccessful however, and she was killed by the Evereni woman instead. Alirya's death was avenged by Ro, who shot Vika with a blaster. Left without Alirya, Ro offered the human's former place by her side to Vika's brother, who hesitantly accepted. Later, Ro recounted her time with Alirya in messages she recorded for her descendants, which her great-great-grandson Marchion Ro had listened to by 252 BBY.

Born around 394 BBY, In her service to the Path she ventured out onto the Galactic Frontier to spread the cult's teachings and was therefore not present for in 382 BBY and led to its dissolution. Oblivious to the Path's collapse, Alirya carried on with her mission.

entities.name: Alisande
entities.description:
Alisande was a female Human who was the wife of Aron Peacebringer, Warlord of the Calian Confederacy on Shiva IV, and mother to their children during the time of the Galactic Civil War. Alisande and Peacebringer had a happy, loving and passionate relationship for a number of years, and lived together in a palace in the city of Illyriaqüm. In 3 ABY, Alisande recognized her husband's attraction to visiting Rebel leader Leia Organa, but trusted that Peacebringer would choose their marriage in the end—ultimately, she was proven right.

A Human female native to the remote planet Shiva IV, Alisande was the wife of Aron Peacebringer, a powerful warrior who became Warlord of the Calian Confederacy. In 2 ABY, Alisande's husband signed the Concordat of Peace that ended generations of war with the Twelve Tribes of T'Syriél. By that point, Alisande and Peacebringer already been married for a number of years, having several children—their firstborn, a daughter, died in infancy—and living together in a well-appointed palace in the city of Illyriaqüm. In 3 ABY, Alisande's husband went out to investigate the sudden destruction of the city of K'avor, and returned with Leia Organa, an important Rebel leader who had recently crashed on Shiva IV.

Alisande forged a close friendship with Organa, even as her husband grew attracted to the young offworlder—an attraction that Alisande recognized, but trusted Peacebringer to not act upon. As they attempted to get to the bottom of the destruction of K'avor, they were attacked by an Imperial force led by General Bentilais san Sk'ar, coinciding with the one-year anniversary celebration for the Concordat of Peace. With the help of Alliance reinforcements Luke Skywalker and Chewbacca, along with Peacebringer's blood brother Kéral Longknife, Peacebringer and Organa managed to defeat S'kar and fight off the Imperial menace. Peacebringer returned to Alisande afterwards, having let go of his feelings for Organa, and the two happily resumed their loving marriage.

Although Alisande's marriage to Aron Peacebringer had lasted long by 3 ABY, their relationship was still extremely passionate, with the two taking every opportunity to steal away for private encounters. Their marriage brought Alisande a lifetime of happiness, and she held her husband's personal qualities of honesty and integrity in extremely high regard. However, Alisande began to notice a change in Peacebringer after her husband met Leia Organa—he became forgetful, more distant, and seemed distinctly uncomfortable around their Alderaanian guest. She quickly realized his attraction to Organa, with whom Alisande had become close during her time on Shiva IV, considering her something akin to a daughter. However, Alisande did not hold it against her husband, considering it natural to be tempted, and trusting that Peacebringer would return to her once he sorted his feelings out.

Alise Davros was a female Human citizen of the Eternal Empire of Zakuul. She fled Emperor Arcann's oppression into the Endless Swamp where she joined the Zakuulan rebels led by Pashna Veyaad.

Alise Davros sends her message only if the rebels were denied training in the Dark Side option. In this case she takes over after Pashna Veyaad was killed and thanks the Alliance for the weapons, but reveals that untrained rebels are quickly being picked off by skytroopers and that she expects to die fighting.

entities.name: Alisia
entities.description:
Alisia was a Human female musician who performed with Alitra, O'choa Detera, Mako, and Mestral in the cantinas aboard both Tansarii Point Station and Nova Orion Station in the Bright Jewel system during the time of the Galactic Civil War. During her time with the band, Alisia played the musical instrument known as the bandfill.

A Human female by the name of Alisia participated in a band during the time of the Galactic Civil War along with two other musicians, a Human named Mako, and a Zabrak named Alitra. Her band also comprised of two dancers, a Twi'lek named Mestral, and a Zabrak named O'choa Detera. Following the Battle of Yavin in 0 BBY, Alisia and her band played music and danced for the patrons of the cantina owned by a Twi'lek named Tiarsis in the Tansarii Point Station, a space station located near the planet of Ord Mantell in the Bright Jewel system. As part of the band, Alisia played the musical instrument known as the bandfill. The Twi'lek entertainer Mira T'rani enjoyed the performance of Alisia's band, which featured two popular songs from Tatooine "Mad About Me" and "Dune Sea Special".

Alisia and her band also divided their time at another space station in the Bright Jewel system known as Nova Orion Station. In addition to the music they played on Tansarii Point Station, Alisia and her band also played two other cover songs belonging to Evar Orbus and His Galactic Jizz-Wailers, including a Huttese song named "Lapti Nek". Despite the band's skill at playing these songs, their lack of original material drew criticism from at least one Nova Orion Industries employee frequenting the cantina.

Alisia had dark skin, brown hair, and amber colored eyes. She was skilled at using the bandfill to play songs such as "Mad About Me" and "Dune Sea Special".

entities.name: Alissyndrex delga Cantonica Provincion
entities.description:
Alissyndrex delga Cantonica Provincion, also known simply as The Countess, was a female Idalowd who was in the Canto Bight casino in 34 ABY. Around 34 ABY, she was the Countess of Canto Bight and was a partial owner of Zord's Spa and Bathhouse. She was a fan of the Fathier races. She wore the Onyx Bands of Cato Neimoidia. The Countess was also a rival of the Whippomorn gangster Sturg Ganna. That year she had given orders to kill Jerdon Bly aboard Yasto Attsmun's yacht. Lexo Sooger, a professional masseur who used to be an assassin was tasked with the dirty work. Sooger killed Bly, then, to cover his escape, spread a rumor that there was a fire on board, causing everyone on board to evacuate. As one of, if not the most powerful individuals in Canto Bight, it was best for the people who frequented the city and Casino not to antagonize her.

When the adopted daughter of Dor Namethian Lexo Sooger was kidnapped by Sturg Ganna, a politician and crime lord Canto Bight. Lexo, who was a humble masseur at the Zord's Spa and Bathouse was willing to do anything to get his daughter Lula back. The Countess had to sell the Zord's to Ganna himself, but thanks to an advice from Sooger, who advised her not to bet on Defancio Storsilt's stable, she won enough money to keep her share. The Countess knew Sooger well, but also Ganna, so she made him a proposal: he should kill a human named Jerdon Bly, who sold weapons to both the First Order and the Resistance. In reality, the Countess wanted to cut him out of the market to sell the weapons directly to both factions, and for personal reasons of antipathy. Also, Bly could become richer than her, and this also meant more influential, and she could not allow that. Sooger did not want to kill Bly, but he was forced to do so, otherwise the Countess would not have provided him with the favors necessary to get his daughter back. After having succeeded, he returned to her; the powerful Countess had arranged a meeting with Ganna and asked Sooger for a personal favor: to find something that particularly interested her in the Councilor's library. When Lexo managed to enter Ganna's suite and find his daughter, he also found a datapad containing the information on Ganna's plan to take over all of Canto Bight: He discovered that the Crime Lord was in league with Bly - the human he killed - and not only that; he planned to make Ubialla Gheal lose his club, to his advantage, to destroy the Canto Bight police force and replace it with his own droids, to bankrupt the Storsilt stables and to buy the Zord's to bankrupt the Countess. He sent the information to his detective friend, Neepers Panpick, who kept it aside, and in case of danger he would send it to everyone who mattered in Canto Bight. Sturg was forced to let them leave and grant several of their demands including not buying out the Countess's share of the bathhouse. Thanks to Lexo and his daughter, the Countess's continued reign over Canto Bight was assured, she went to the Zord's and toasted Lexo Sooger, while Sturg Ganna was present, although he was being massaged by others.

entities.name: Alitra
entities.description:
Alitra was a female Zabrak musician who lived during the Galactic Civil War. After the Battle of Yavin, she was part of a band that performed in the Bright Jewel system, playing the kloo horn. The band also included two other musicians, Alisia and Mako, and two dancers, O'choa Detera and Mestral. During that time, the band often played music and danced for the patrons of the cantinas of Tansarii Point Station The band was known to cover popular songs from Tatooine, including "Mad About Me", "Dune Sea Special" and "Lapti Nek". Although Alitra and the musicians were very skilled, their lack of original songs sometimes drew criticism.

Alitra was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, Alitra and her band were added to the game as part of the "New Player Tutorial," The "New Player Tutorial" featured the band in the cantina of Tansarii Point Station. Alitra and the band were also included in the cantina of the Nova Orion Station.

entities.description:
All-Terrain Attack Vehicle, or AT-AV for short, was the nickname of a female pittin that was a pet belonging to Tia Organa, one of Princess Leia Organa's adoptive aunts on Alderaan.

As a child, Leia had named the creature herself. AT-AV had a pale candy-pink color and was small enough to fit in Leia's cupped hands. She also liked to roll on her back and bat at Leia's braids and starblossom petals. AT-AV died in the destruction of Alderaan.

entities.name: Allara
entities.description:
Allara was a female Human Jedi Initiate who studied in the Jedi Order during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive female Human, Allara was a member of the Jedi Order, strong in the Force and a firm believer in the Jedi Code. Having trained at the Order's academy for years as a member of the Bergruutfa Clan, Allara and her peers were still quite young when the Clone Wars erupted across the galaxy. In an unorthodox move, Jedi Master Quarmall abducted the clan in 20 BBY and declared that each member was his Padawan. Traveling aboard a Mon Calamari starship along with her clan and new master, their ship was attacked while in transit by General Grievous and a Separatist fleet. With its engines heavily damaged, the crew could do nothing but defend their ship. Despite their efforts, the Mon Calamari crew were cut down by boarding parties of B1-Series battle droids, with Grievous following close behind.

Quarmall destroyed many of the droids who attacked him, but he was eventually surrounded and confronted by Grievous. The general discussed the possibility of dueling Quarmall, but claimed that he had grown tired of killing Jedi and ordered him killed by the droids instead. The droids turned their weapons on him and blasted the Jedi, seemingly killing him—unknown to all, Quarmall had survived, but would not resurface until years later. Grievous was brought further into the ship by his droids, stepping over the bodies of fallen Mon Calamari on the way. There he found a closed room, and within it, Allara and her fellow Padawans, including Banz and Tak-tak. Grievous ignited his lightsaber and took the Padawans as captives.

Soon after, Grievous and the Trade Federation conquered the planet of Gentes and its moon, Belsus. After a brief and one-sided battle, the native Ugnaughts were captured and forced to convert their own factories for use by the Confederacy of Independent Systems. The Padawans arrived on Belsus aboard a C-9979 landing craft, with B1's guarding them closely. Though the other Padawans worried over their fate, Allara was stoic about their situation, and Banz told the others to bury their fear and face the future with courage. The younglings were then brought to meet Grievous once more, on a balcony overlooking the city. Grievous then informed them that they were to become warriors for him, trying to convince them that this fate was not that different than that of being a Jedi. Allara, however, knew that this meant they would become servants of the Sith, and told the cyborg they would never do so.

entities.name: Allia
entities.description:
Allia was a female Twi'lek Pilgrim who lived on Tython illegally during the Cold War between the resurgent Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic.

A Twi'lek female, Allia was one of many Pilgrims who followed Matriarch Kolovish to the planet Tython in the aftermath of the Great Galactic War and the enslavement of Ryloth by the Hutt Cartels. Assisting in the establishment of Kalikori village, Allia was an advocate for Nalen Raloch and considered him a great hero of the village, defending the pilgrims from the Flesh Raiders. Allia and Keth aided Raloch in his hunt for the Fount of Rajivari, but eventually realized that Raloch himself had been corrupted by the knowledge he was seeking.

Allia was originally a blue-skinned Twi'lek named Henni in early stages of the game, but her skin was changed to green and her name to Allia by the time of the game's release. However, Henni will still appear if the player makes the dark side decision to kill Allia.

entities.name: Stass Allie
entities.description:
Stass Allie, a Force-sensitive Tholothian female, was a Jedi Master who lived during the final years of the Galactic Republic. She was also the cousin of Jedi Master and Jedi High Council member Adi Gallia. Allie became a Jedi General in the Grand Army of the Republic and gained a seat on the High Council of the Jedi Order late in the Clone Wars when Gallia was killed.

Allie would not serve on the Council long before her demise on the planet Saleucami during the waning hours of the Clone Wars. Having received the command to execute Order 66 from the Sith Lord Darth Sidious, Clone Marshal Commander Neyo and a clone trooper lieutenant opened fire on their general from their speeder bikes, killing her instantly.

Stass Allie was born on Tholoth prior to the Separatist Crisis. Allie was found to be Force-sensitive and brought to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant to start her Jedi training. She specialized in the art of healing, which would later become an invaluable resource during the long bloody years of the Clone Wars. Like her cousin, Allie would also become a consular and rising star diplomat. She was eventually granted the title of Jedi Master and became a member of the Circle of Jedi Healers, in addition to serving as an overseer of the Medical Corps.

Allie was present in Supreme Chancellor Palpatine's office along with other senators and Jedi as the issue of whether Palpatine should take emergency powers was debated.

entities.name: Harp Allor
entities.description:
Harp Allor was a human female from the planet Chandrila who lived during the era of the Galactic Empire. Sponsored by Winmey Lenz, a Chandrilan senior senator, Allor became a member of the Apprentice Legislature in 3 BBY. She was described by fellow Apprentice Legislator Princess Leia Organa as being friendly, over-prepared, and unabashedly cheerful, and was one of several Apprentice Legislators to participate Chief Pangie's pathfinding class organized by Queen Breha Organa of Alderaan.

Harp Allor was born in 20 BBY. As part of the Apprentice Legislature, Harp Allor attended a pathfinding class arranged by Queen Breha Organa of Alderaan, alongside Princess Leia Organa, Chassellon Stevis, Sssamm Ashsssen, Amilyn Holdo, Kier Domadi, and an Ithorian, among many other students under the instruction of Chief Pangie of the Chandrilan Pathfinding Corps. The group hiked for five hours before finding a hoversled. Pangie told the students that it belonged to her, and that they must find their way back to the chalet by nightfall or be kicked from the class, before she departed.

As the group slowly made their way back, and Holdo looked for snow owls, they argued over the pace they should be going. Allor rushed ahead, but slipped on ice, breaking her left ankle. This caused the group to argue, with some wanting to help Allor and others wanting to continue on, since each student had a tracker which could be used to find Allor after they had made it back. Organa, Domadi, Ashsssen, and Holdo stayed with Allor while Stevis led the rest of the class onward. The four managed to splint and bandage Allor's ankle and get her onto a travois to drag her back to the chalet. When Holdo joked they had encountered mortal peril, Allor began to cry, apologizing for slowing the group down. Domadi comforted her and they soon arrived at a snow-covered slope. Holdo came up with the idea of making a toboggan out of a tent, and Ashsssen held it together.

Stevis along with his group arrived at sunset, and when they walked into the great room, they shocked to see that the five had made it before him with the injured Allor and were resting by the hearth and drinking mocoa, Allor resting her left foot on a sleeping Ashsssen in the comfiest chair by the fire, floaty cream on the tip of her nose and a bacta bag on her foot. Pangie also lectured Stevis and the others for their abandonment of Harp.

entities.name: Allura
entities.description:
Allura was a Human female entertainer who lived on Tatooine during the Galactic Civil War. After the Battle of Yavin, she resided in Mos Eisley and used to perform in Chalmun's Cantina. Allura encountered a spacer in the cantina who was recommended and sent by one of her friend by the name Trehla Keelo. The spacer had just landed on Tatooine and was looking for work. Allura therefore agreed with teaching some of her dance moves.

Allura was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts,

Allura was added to the game with the release of the "Publish 17," on May 26, 2005. She was part of an introductory questline intended to help new players who spawned on Tatooine right after the completion of the "New Player Tutorial" to chose their "profession." Allura's quest was removed from the game upon the overhaul of the "profession" system with the release of the "Publish 25," a.k.a. the "New Game Enhancements," on November 15, 2005.

entities.name: Allya
entities.description:
Allya was, according to a commonly told story, a female Jedi whom the Jedi Council sent into exile on Dathomir, in 600 BBY. There, she allegedly trained other women in the ways of the Force, ultimately giving birth to the Dathomirians, who eventually splintered into clans of witches. However, the Jedi Council had no such records, and the Dathomirians had other, contradicting stories about their origins. Allya wrote the Book of Law, a book which portrayed the Jedi Order in a bad light, causing the Nightsisters to have little respect for the Order.

Allya was first mentioned in the new Star Wars canon in the 59th issue of the 2016 magazine, Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon. She initially appeared in the Star Wars Legends continuity in The Courtship of Princess Leia, a 1994 novel written by Dave Wolverton and published by Bantam Spectra.

entities.name: Alma
entities.description:
Alma was an innkeeper ran a bed and breakfast on the Outer Rim planet Ah Re Won. When the cloaked Sith apprentice Darth Maul arrived to her town to meditate at the ruins of a Sith temple Alma offered the Zabrak stranger a room and meals for a fair price. He took her up on the deal as long as he could have quietude.

Alma was an early settler of the area, and during her time there, the settlement grew significantly. Nestled between a beach and the ruins of the Sith temple, the town attracted enough tourism to lead the newly appointed mayor, a greedy Sullustan, to construct a flashy hotel. The mayor attempted to force Alma out of her building so he could improve his visitors' view of the ruins. He attempted stiff taxation, bothering her with noise, and, when those attempts failed, to burn down her inn. The mayor's scheming was cut short by Maul, who grew annoyed by the commotion the Sullustan was creating. The next morning, the mayor's security droids went to Alma for help when their boss went missing.

Later during Maul's visit to the ruins, Alma was accused by the Pirate King of Sector Nine for being complicit in the death of his son at the hands of local beasts. The vengeful pirate king attempted to blast the woman with a tank, but she was able to evade the blasts and get to a starship. Though the pirate king ordered his crew to fire upon the ship, they were unable due to Maul's intervention, allowing Alma to escape.

Alma appeared in the fourth issue of the Star Wars: Darth Maul – Black, White & Red comic series, written by Greg Pak, illustrated by Luca Pizzari and Will Sliney, and published by Marvel Comics

Alma was a Human female who served the reconstituted Sith Empire as a spy working for Imperial Intelligence during the Cold War, a conflict between the Empire and the Galactic Republic.

Alma was a Human female who served the Sith Empire during the Cold War as part of Imperial Intelligence. During the war Alma was sent to the Republic held planet of Ord Mantell where she acted as a spy. She went under cover as an occupant of Talloran village and spied on the nearby Republic Fort Garnik. However a Civil war broke out on Ord Mantell during her time there. The Mantellian Separatist Movement opposed the corrupt planetary government which was supported by the Republic. The separatists managed to capture Talloran village and Alma was forced to flee.

Alma ended up in a refugee camp outside of Fort Garnik where she realized in her rush to escape Talloran she had left behind a necklace which she used to communicate with Imperial intelligence.

She asked a smuggler named Ace and a member of Havoc Squad whom she met in the camp to recover the amulet claiming it was an heirloom that had belonged to her great great Grandmother.

entities.name: Alinka Aloo
entities.description:
Lady Alinka Aloo, daughter of Imperial Adviser Sim Aloo, was a Coruscant-based collector of Sith artifacts who managed the Aloo family's affairs and undertook covert missions on Emperor Palpatine's behalf. Known for her cunning and ambition, she orchestrated a dangerous expedition to retrieve an ancient dark side book from Ushruu—recruiting Chewbacca, the captive librarian Mayvlin Trillick, and an unassuming cargo droid—only for the mission to unravel when the droid proved to be the Rebel agent K-2SO and the snarler creatures of Ushruu followed the team back to Coruscant, leaving Alinka empty-handed and outmaneuvered.

A human woman from Coruscant, Lady Alinka Aloo was and the daughter of Sim Aloo, from a second marriage. She held the rank of princess and was properly addressed either as "Your Highness" or "Lady Alinka." Together with her father, she assisted in acquiring Sith artifacts from across the galaxy for the Emperor's private collection, and she oversaw the Aloo family's business interests during her father's frequent absences. She resided in a tower situated on one of the highest levels of Imperial City.

At some point during the Imperial Era, Palpatine expressed interest in an ancient dark side tome kept within a temple on the planet Ushruu. Both Sim Aloo and fellow adviser Janus Greejatus sought to retrieve the artifact, though Greejatus's attempt—conducted hastily through a hired group of Trandoshan mercenaries—ended in failure when the team was devoured by Ushruu's native snarler creatures. Seeking to ensure her father's success, Alinka devised a more deliberate plan, determining that the mission required a Wookiee guide capable of navigating Ushruu's dense forests, a librarian to recover the book, and a cargo droid to transport it.

For the librarian, Alinka selected Mayvlin Trillick, an Oktarian youth apprehended while attempting to steal from one of Sim Aloo's warehouses. Alinka coerced Trillick's cooperation by withholding the Mola Oktaro, the most sacred text of the Oktaran people. She chose the Wookiee Chewbacca—co-pilot of the smuggler Han Solo—for his strength and familiarity with hazardous terrain. The cargo droid assignment fell to a K-2SB unit that volunteered for the mission, as the Aloos paid little attention to droid personnel.

entities.name: Alora
entities.description:
Alora was a female Lethan Twi'lek Dark Jedi active during the early years of the New Jedi Order. She was the apprentice of Tavion Axmis, who led the Disciples of Ragnos cult, a cult that Alora was part of. Alora infiltrated the Jedi Praxeum on the moon Yavin 4 in an attempt to steal a list of locations with significant Force nexuses to aid the Disciples of Ragnos in their resurrection of the ancient Sith Lord Marka Ragnos.

After the Twi'lek was dispatched to the planet of Hoth to gather information, Alora encountered and dueled Jedi Initiate Jaden Korr within the former Rebel Alliance base, Echo Base. The Dark Jedi was defeated and withdrew, fleeing and traveling to Taspir III, a planet on which she encountered Korr and was killed by the initiate.

The Lethan Twi'lek Alora was a member of the Disciples of Ragnos, a Sith cult that worshipped the ancient Sith Lord Marka Ragnos. Alora was tasked with infiltrating Jedi Master Luke Skywalker's Jedi Academy on the moon Yavin 4, where Alora stole a list of locations strong in the Force by gaining access to the Jedi mainframes. By travelling to these locations, Axmis would then be able to resurrect Ragnos by siphoning the Force energies into the Sceptre.

Accompanied by support from Axmis' allies in the Imperial Remnant, Alora travelled to the planet Hoth to gather information on the Force energies located there. While they were searching Echo Base—a hideout used by the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War—a Sith cultist managed to determine from flight trajectories that Skywalker had traveled to the planet Dagobah following the Battle of Hoth. The cultist downloaded the flight information and transmitted the data to Alora before being killed by Jedi Initiate Jaden Korr, who was on Hoth as part of an investigation into the locations mentioned in Skywalker's records. Alora relayed the information to Axmis, who congratulated her apprentice and told Alora to meet her on Dagobah, when she was located by Korr in a hangar inside the base. Alora engaged Korr in a duel, but fled when she realized that she couldn't gain the upper hand. Angered, she taunted Korr as she escaped and claimed they would cross paths again.

entities.description:
Rees Alrix was a female Jedi who lived during the last years of the Galactic Republic. Alrix was the first Padawan of the Gran Jedi Master Maks Leem, and she later left her tutelage and became a Knight in the Jedi Order. When the Clone Wars broke out across the galaxy and plunged the Republic into a war, Alrix, like many Jedi, fought in the Grand Army of the Republic. she led her clone troopers in the Battle of Sullust.

Rees Alrix was first mentioned in Yoda: Dark Rendezvous, a novel written by Sean Stewart and published in 2004.

entities.description:
Altah was a female handmaiden to Queen Kylantha of Naboo during the time of the Galactic Civil War. Sometime following the Battle of Yavin in 0 BBY, Emperor Palpatine tasked a loyal subject of the Galactic Empire with safely escorting the handmaiden to the Emperor's Retreat so that Palpatine could "apologize" to her.

Altah was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, prior to its closure on December 15, 2011. While the canonical species of Altah cannot be definitively determined in the Legends continuity, the quest dialogue identified her as female. Furthermore, while the quest dialogue identified her as Altah, examining the character simply identified her as a "Royal Handmaiden."

entities.name: Turi Altamik
entities.description:
Turi Altamik was a female Human Jedi Knight of the New Jedi Order. She fell prey to a Force psychosis in 44 ABY, and the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances demanded the Jedi Order to turn her over, laying siege to the Jedi Temple. However, she and the other psychotic Knights soon recovered, and after examination by Doctor Thalleus Tharn, were pronounced sane, forcing the government to lift the siege. Later, Altamik took part in the rescue of Valin and Jysella Horn from Galactic Alliance Security Detention Center 81.

In 44 ABY, Altamik came down with a psychosis, brought on by the dark side being Abeloth, which made her believe that everyone she knew had been replaced by impostors. Altamik escaped the Jedi Temple, and although she was soon captured by the Jedi, she was caught on holocam by journalist Javis Tyrr.

Jedi Master Cilghal drew up a report that went into detail about the psychosis in Altamik and fellow Jedi Knight Kunor Bann, believing the rate of Jedi succumbing to the psychosis was accelerating. The Galactic Alliance, meanwhile, ordered that the Jedi release Altamik and Sothais Saar—a Chev Jedi who had recently succumbed to the same psychosis—to government custody. Acting Grand Master Kenth Hamner refused the directive, which resulted in Chief of State Natasi Daala ordering a Mandalorian siege of the Jedi Temple. When the Jedi Council sent Hamner's aide, Kani Asari, out to negotiate with the Mandalorians, Belok Rhal, the commander of the Mandalorian siege, noted that Kani was neither Altamik nor Saar and shot her on sight, killing her instantly. Despite the violence, the Jedi still refused to turn over the two psychotic Knights.

Before long, however, Luke Skywalker completed his mission to defeat Abeloth, apparently killing her and thus instantly ending Altamik's psychosis. However, Luke soon discovered that Abeloth had not been killed and suspected that by being wounded and weakened she had lost her control over the Jedi Knights' minds.

entities.name: Althea
entities.description:
Althea was a female member of the royal family of Isobe during the Imperial Era. She and her brother Thelan were the children of Lord Hallux. She developed a brief relationship with Jun Sato, a human from Mykapo who had joined the renowned crystal processing school on Isobe. However, it turned out that Sato was part of a smuggling ring, which led him to be banished from Isobe for life, much to Althea's dismay.

Princess Althea was a member of the royal family of Isobe during the Imperial Era, a world that became rich as one of the sole sources of the tynzo crystal, a mineral used in strengthening glass for use in hyperspace. The daughter of Lord Hallux and the sister of Thelan, she had a brief relationship with Jun Sato, a human from Mykapo who had joined the renowned crystal processing school on Isobe. However, Sato had only joined the school as a ruse, actually coming to Isobe after having been recruited to a smuggling ring that stole tynzo crystal and exported it at a lower cost than Isobe, weakening the resource's price. Sato was caught by Isobe's security forces and put on trial. He refused to tell who gave him orders and was banished for life from the planet.

Althea later died between 4 BBY and 2 BBY on Isobe. Her father had a gravestone created that he inscribed himself, carving a tynzo crystal in the shape of a heart to be placed atop her grave. During the inscription process, Hallux and her brother Thelan, accompanied by two guards, were interrupted by the gardener Levier and his droid Gee-Bee, who had apprehended Sabine Wren defacing a statue of Hallux and Sato. Sato, who faced the death penalty for returning to Isobe, revealed to Hallux that it was his son, Thelan, who ran the smuggling ring and had only kept his silence before to protect Althea. Hallux had Thelan arrested and granted Sato one hour to pay his respects to Althea before he was to leave Isobe forever.

Althea was a female Sephi who was thin and had long hair. She was not like other Sephi who held xenophobic views towards outsiders. Her father held her in great esteem, inscribing "Beloved daughter" on her gravestone.

entities.name: Altiss
entities.description:
Altiss was a female Human Moff of the reconstituted Sith Empire. In 3639 BBY she commanded the Imperial operations on Denova following the defeat of troops led by Colonel Grezor. Altiss requested the presence of the Empire's best forces to handle the situation and defeat Kephess and his Warstalkers, bringing Denova's baradium resources under Imperial control. When Grezor contacted her requesting extraction, she reprimanded him for his failure and opted to terminate him on the spot. After her assault team defeated Kephess and returned to Altiss's ship, they were interrupted by a sudden appearance of the Dread Masters, who revealed themselves to have split from the Empire and brought resurrected Kephess under their control. After the Dread Masters disappeared just as suddenly, Altiss prepared to report the incident up the chain of command.

Moff Altiss appears in the 2011 BioWare massively-multiplayer online role-playing video game Star Wars: The Old Republic during the "Explosive Conflict" operation.

A Jabiimi Human female was a cousin of the Jabiimi Nationalists commander Alto Stratus. During the Battle of Jabiim between the Jabiimi Loyalists and the Jabiimi Nationalists, she had been shot in the gut with a blaster, and then, her legs were crushed by a Republic walker. Alto Stratus witnessed his cousin as she crawled through the mud. Severely injured, she died in Stratus' arms, whose resolve to destroy the Jedi solidified. In the next week, Stratus remembered his cousin's death as he beheaded Jedi General Norcuna during the battle near the city of Choal.
