entities.name: Voe Atell
entities.description:
Voe Atell was a female senator who represented the interests of the Corporate Alliance in the Confederacy of Independent Systems during the Clone Wars.

Atell was present in the Senate chamber when Mina Bonteri made her plea to the other senators that a treaty should be proposed toward the Galactic Senate. Atell objected to the treaty on behalf of the Corporate Alliance and voted to continue the war effort. However the treaty was passed, yet the plans were foiled when Count Dooku and his allies bombed Coruscant.

Later in the war, she was sent to Mandalore to represent the Confederacy in a peace talk with the Republic, along with Amita Fonti and Separatist Congress Leader Bec Lawise. However, the talks were interrupted by Lux Bonteri, son of Mina Bonteri. He claimed that Dooku was behind the murder of his mother, and was subsequently escorted away by commando droids. Although the negotiations went on, they did not get anything done due to the interruption.

She is voiced by Catherine Taber, who also voiced fellow senator Padmé Amidala in the Clone Wars series.

Alongside Tione Zrar and Velai, Athantras attempted to protect a village led by Thissa Somori from a group of pirates. When the pirates landed to collect payments from the villagers, Athantras and her companions stood in their way, bringing the villagers into diplomatic negotiations with the pirates. While the pirates were unwilling to work with the villagers, the consulars managed to arrange a mutually beneficial agreement. Athantras wielded a staff, the end of which could be ignited into a lightsaber blade.

entities.name: Athnalu
entities.description:
Athnalu was a female Wookiee who lived in Kerritamba Village on the planet Kashyyyk during the Galactic Civil War. Shortly after the Battle of Yavin, Athnalu came under the impression that a spell had been placed on her by members of the Sayormi, a primitive species that lived in the nearby Dead Forest. Mentally unstable and in constant physical pain, Athnalu hired a passing spacer to find several objects that she thought would lift the curse. The spacer located five Sayormi voodoo dolls, shadevale eyes, mouf hair, and a Mysess blossom for Athnalu. Believing herself cured of the curse, Athnalu thanked the spacer and gave the traveler 2,200 credits and a ceremonial chair.

A female Wookiee, Athnalu lived in Kerritamba Village near the Kkowir Forest on the planet Kashyyyk during the Galactic Civil War. Shortly after the Battle of Yavin, Athnalu came under the belief that the Sayormi people—a mysterious species that lived in the Dead Forest of the Kkowir Forest—had placed a spell on her. She thought herself possessed and cursed by the Sayormi. Believing that her very soul was rotting away, Athnalu lived in constant pain and fear, which caused her to grow increasingly mentally unstable.

That same year, Athnalu was approached by a spacer who was visiting her village. Athnalu explained her situation and the curse she believed she was under and pleaded for the spacer to help her. The spacer accepted the Wookiee's request for assistance, and Athnalu tasked the traveler with collecting five voodoo dolls that she thought the Sayormi were using to possess her. By having the dolls, Athnalu hoped they would help her understand why the Sayormi had placed the curse on her. After the spacer had completed the task and returned to Athnalu, the Wookiee rewarded the being with 1,000 credits.

However, unsatisfied with the results from the dolls, Athnalu again asked the spacer for assistance. The spacer agreed, and Athnalu told the traveler to find three more items that she thought were needed to cure her: the eyes of a shadevale, snakes that lived in the nearby lakes and streams; hairs from a mouf, large, woolly creatures that wandered the forest; and finally a Mysess blossom, a flower that grew in the village. The spacer dutifully collected all she requested and brought them to Athnalu, which the Wookiee mixed together into a potion and consumed. Now satisfied that she was free of the curse's influence, she thanked the spacer and rewarded the being with another 1,200 credits and a special ceremonial chair from the village.

entities.name: Atris
entities.description:
Atris was a Human female who served as a Jedi historian, and later as a Jedi Master and Jedi Council member during the Mandalorian Wars and the Jedi Civil War. She was deeply committed to the Order and was a fierce adherent of the Jedi Code. But Atris' faith in the righteousness of the Jedi wavered when her personal hero, Meetra Surik, turned her back on the Council to join rogue Knights Revan and Malak and their faction of Jedi during the Mandalorian Wars. Atris chose not to go to war, but this decision left her bitter and conflicted.

When Surik returned to face the Council's judgment after the devastating events of the Battle of Malachor V, Atris was the first to condemn her, suggesting that she had fallen to the dark side just as Revan had. Over time, Atris grew to hate Surik for complicating her black-and-white view of the Jedi, the Sith, and the Force. During the First Jedi Purge, Atris called a secret Jedi convocation on the Miraluka world of Katarr in an attempt to find the threat that was stalking the Jedi. She then leaked knowledge of the conclave's existence in the hopes of drawing out the Sith. She succeeded, but with dire consequences; Darth Nihilus devastated the surface of the planet, wiping out all life on Katarr, including the Jedi gathered there.

However, Atris survived, and she remained in seclusion, surrounding herself with Echani Handmaidens who could not feel the Force. She planned to rebuild the Jedi Order, and established a Jedi Academy in the old irrigation system on Telos IV. However, she was heavily influenced by the many Sith holocrons she had collected in her efforts to find and understand the Sith. The holocrons fed her bitterness, and she slowly and quietly fell to the dark side. Per the machinations of her mentor, Kreia, Surik and Atris confronted each other once more on Telos, where Surik convinced Atris to turn away from the dark side. Atris then remained in the Jedi Academy, waiting to be judged for her actions by the new Jedi Council.

After the end of the Great Sith War that was started by the Sith Lords Exar Kun and Ulic Qel-Droma, the Jedi historian Atris attempted to revise the broken system of Jedi apprenticeship. She argued that there was little wonder why Kun and Qel-Droma fell to the dark side of the Force, when the Jedi had liberal instruction practices in place, such as dozens of Padawans training under a single Master, the radical bonds of reciprocal apprenticeship, and Jedi beginning their training in their teens and later. She invoked thousand-year old recommendations first suggested by the Jedi Master Simikarty, lobbying for the restriction of Padawans that a Master could have at one time, and also limiting the age of Jedi candidates.

entities.name: Atin Attan
entities.description:
Atin Attan was a Sullustan pilot who was a member of the Galactic Outdoor Survival School's Twilight Class who later joined the Alliance to Restore the Republic.

A pilot since her childhood, Attan studied Sullustan geology from SoroSuub Extension programs. After graduating, she joined the Galactic Outdoor Survival School, and was a member of the prestigious Twilight Class. Attan led one of the most dangerous parts of the final trek that led to the impressive graduation of the Twilight Class around 12 BBY.

After that, Attan joined the Rebel Alliance alongside most of the other members of the Twilight Class. She became a pilot instructor for the Alliance Fleet. Around 2 ABY, Attan was assigned to the Roche asteroid field, where she helped in some minor modifications to the prototype B-wing starfighter.

entities.name: Atuarre
entities.description:
Atuarre () was a female Trianii who served in the elite Trianii Rangers during the era of the Galactic Civil War. Atuarre joined the elite law enforcement squad after marrying a Ranger, Keeheen, with whom she had a cub, Pakka. Although she had a sheltered, higher-class upbringing, Atuarre took quickly to the life of a Ranger, which eventually took her and her mate to a posting on the Trianii frontier world of Fibuli. Her life changed significantly when the Corporate Sector Authority violently annexed Fibuli around 2 BBY: the Authority captured and imprisoned Keeheen and Pakka, and while Atuarre managed to rescue her cub, he was so traumatized that he was unable to speak.

As she searched for Keeheen, Atuarre linked up with Rekkon, an academic leading a group of concerned citizens who were also looking for family members kidnapped by the CSA. In the coming months, Atuarre was part of a crew who infiltrated a Authority Data Center on Orron III, and with the help of notorious smugglers Han Solo and Chewbacca, they managed to uncover the location of the prisoners: Stars' End, a secret prison on Mytus VII. Atuarre and Pakka subsequently joined Solo and Chewbacca in breaking into Stars' End and freeing those held within, and ultimately reunited with Keeheen.

A female member of the feline species known as the Trianii, Atuarre was born and raised on the Trianii homeworld of Trian, where she grew up dreaming of being a dancer, model or corporate executive. From her youth, Atuarre lived a life of peace and comfort, as befitting a young woman born in a higher class. But one day, she caught the eye of Keeheen, a member of the elite Trianii Ranger law enforcement force, while watching the Rangers train. Keeheen was instantly smitten—for her part, Atuarre, while interested, initially turned the young cadet down. However, they exchanged information and kept in touch over the next two years, with Keeheen proposing to her frequently. As Atuarre learned more of Keeheen and his life, the more she found herself falling for him, and eventually they wed. They soon welcomed a cub, Pakka, into the world, and not long after Keeheen asked the lithe and athletic Atuarre to join him in the Trianii Rangers.

Although the life of a Ranger was far different from the comfort she had grown up in, she soon found that she had an aptitude for the job, with her dance training helping her quickly master the intricate Trianii martial arts. After she became a full-fledged Ranger, she joined Keeheen in patrolling the planet Fibuli, a longtime flashpoint in the ongoing struggle between the Trianii and the Corporate Sector Authority. The couple's tour was originally uneventful—they spent most of their time stopping herdbeast rustlers and busting thionarx dealers—but in 2 BBY, war broke out in earnest when the Authority moved to forcefully annex Fibuli. Atuarre and Keeheen were involved in the armed Trianii resistance, but the Authority needed only three months to assume full control of the world.

entities.name: Ostan Atur
entities.description:
Ostan Atur was a a skilled Lowen saboteur who proved to be a hindrance to several key Republic installations like the Qua'Tahc meleenium mines on Af'El under the jurisdiction of the New Republic.

Ostan Atur was born on Low'n, a Mid Rim planet where she was surrounded by mercenaries and smugglers. Tempted by the amount of money she could earn, Atur decided to become a saboteur in the Lesser Plooriod Cluster and eventually began working for the Ithorian gangster Tolad Dor. She worked for Dor for close to two years, during which time she killed Imperial Colonel Sil Ompren by rigging detonators to a repulsorcraft. Atur also crippled many starships, to allow Dor's minions to collect their cargo to sell on the invisible market.

She eventually elocated to the little-known Minos Cluster and entered a partnership with the Reigat Talak. Atur was chosen by Rani Quanic to aid in the theft of 100 kilograms of meleenium from New Republic mines. During the heist, Atur disabled several of the security systems and several B1 worker droids on duty in one of the Qua'Tahc tunnels' southeast shafts enabling the criminals to escape relatively easily.

However, a group of three Republic operatives came upon the fleeing thieves. Atur and her companions sprayed the area with blaster fire, which caused the three Republic operatives to be seriously wounded. After the heist, there was a reward for her capture of 25,000 credits.

entities.name: Auben
entities.description:
Auben was a black market dealer on Korriban who lived inside the abandoned Sith Monastery.

Auben was a well-known supplier of illegal goods on Korriban when Anakin Skywalker and Ferus Olin purchased a pair of handwarmers from her while on a mission as an excuse to obtain information about Granta Omega and Jenna Zan Arbor from her outside of Dreshdae. As they were about to make a deal with her they were attacked by a Commerce Guild army. Auben led Anakin and Ferus into the Sith Academy in exchange for them having saved her life under the impression that the army would not enter the ruins.

When the army did not stop she led the Jedi deeper into the ruins and into an ancient hangar which was being used by a mysterious Sith Lord as a temporary base. A small group of B2 super battle droids were being stored in the hangar, when Auben, Ferus and Anakin entered they attacked. During the fight between the Jedi and the droids, Auben tried to sneak aboard a ship docked in the hangar to steal several valuable items she had intended to collect earlier. When she was discovered by the Sith Lord in the hangar, he stopped her heart, instantly killing her.

Auben was a paranoid woman who disliked sharing information with her customers and waited until they had spent enough time in the area for her to get a close look at them. She was motivated by credits, though she was willing to help others if they had helped her first.
entities.short_description: Auben was a black market dealer on Korriban who lived inside the abandoned Sith Monastery.

entities.name: Audila
entities.description:
Audila was a Togruta female living during the Cold War. She was the wife of Juran Reb.

Juran and Audila first met Risha when the latter, at the age of fourteen, rushed to explore the galaxy. They became both friends and business partners, and the couple stayed in touch with her after Risha went her own way.

In 3643 BBY, Audila was kidnapped by a group of assassins while her husband was at work. The kidnappers threatened to kill Audila if Risha didn't meet them at the Czerka mining complex on Tatooine. Risha appeared as expected, but the lead assassin refused to release Audila, saying that his "liege" wanted no witnesses. It was then that Risha's partner, the Voidhound, arrived and defeated the assassin leader. Audila was very angry at Risha, blaming the incident on her and asking for reasons. Risha refused to explain that the assassin was after her because of her royal status on Dubrillion. As a result, Audila threatened to sever ties with her. Risha asked Audila to trust her and then gave Audila and her husband some credits to get off Tatooine. Audila accepted them but reminded Risha that she'd want an answer to the events someday.

Juran and Audila eventually settled on Byllura, running a little frontier mercantile exchange. She sent a short note to Risha, letting her know that they were okay.

entities.name: Audra Quay
entities.description:
Audra Quay was a navigator and astrogator who served as a navigator for the Alliance to Restore the Republic before operating the Hyperlight Tours company alongside her husband, Hansifred Quay. She came from a long line of hyperspace cartographers and inherited her family's ability to navigate through hyperspace routes by intuition, an ability which she loved to use and called "wayfinding". Quay was the mother of Valor and Ardent Quay, who also inherited her abilities. She died around 23 ABY due to a miscalculation during a wayfinding hyperspace jump while en route to Ardent's eighth birthday.

Ardent Quay appeared in flashbacks in Eyes Like Stars, a 2026 young-adult novel written by Ashley Poston.

entities.name: Aunuanna
entities.description:
Aunuanna was a Human woman living on Nar Shaddaa a few years after the Battle of Naboo. She was the mother of Aurra Sing.

A poor, if not senile, old woman, she was reduced to selling her home-brewed Gizer ale on the street. After selling her wares on Kyood Vurd's turf one too many times, he decided to have the old woman killed. Luckily for her, Jedi Masters Mace Windu and Depa Billaba arrived in time to save her. She had seen the Jedi Master Quinlan Vos before they had arrived claiming, "So many Jedi! Three in one day!" Grateful, she gave the Jedi her most prized possession, her child's father's swoop bike.

Aunuanna was extremely grateful to the Jedi for saving her life and because the Jedi had taken her baby away from her, and in turn, away from the slums of Nar Shaddaa. She referred to her child only as "My Angel," but it was later revealed that her child was none other than the infamous Jedi hunter Aurra Sing.

entities.name: Odea Aurora
entities.description:
Odea Aurora was a female Human merchant who lived in Cloud City's Port Town.

Born around 13 BBY, Odea Aurora was a female Human. Her mother was a freighter captain, operating the light freighter Happy Failure. When Aurora was six, her father died. Her mother, wanting a better life for her daughter, moved them to Cloud City in the Bespin system, where she established herself as an independent shipping contractor. Unfortunately, the goods she was carrying had, unbeknownst to her, been stolen from Jabba the Hutt. One of Jabba's underlings, the Twi'lek Toln ne Yerres, dealt with the situation by having the Gamorrean Glongfurrp kill her. Aurora was playing with friends at the time, and was warned to never return to the Happy Failure; she never did, and the grounded ship was gutted by scavengers and eventually turned into a casino.

An orphan, Aurora learned to earn a living for herself making jewellery from left over electronics and scrap metal and selling them to tourists. She barely made a daily living selling to tourists at the back of loading bay 372 in Port Town, but refused all offers by other merchants to sell her wares in their shops as she preferred to cut out the middle man. She was a member of the Merchant Guild.

Sometime after the Battle of Yavin, a group of Alliance to Restore the Republic agents were directed to Aurora by a contact of hers on the planet Gerrenthum. They were tracking the Lenushaa gang, who had stolen information from an Alliance cell on the planet. Aurora met them at K'cri's Cafe, and relayed information to them that the slicer who stole the information, a vessel named Tresk, intended to transfer the information to Captain Velantia of the Imperial Security Bureau during a sabacc game at the Pair O'Dice casino.

entities.description:
Lissa Autem was a female Human who was the daughter of Sagoro and Sula, and the younger sister of Reymet.

In the year 23 BBY, Lissa accompanied her brother and his girlfriend Riao Siao at a pit race. While her father went on a mission to solve a murder case, Lissa accompanied her mother to Corellia after been separated from her father.

After the Galactic Republic and the Senate were reformed into the Galactic Empire, Lissa started a relationship with a Corellian.

entities.name: Sula Autem
entities.description:
Sula Autem was a female Human who was the wife of Sagoro and the mother of Reymet and Lissa.

Both Sula and her husband were descended from generations of Senate Guards, and lived with their children in an apartment on the planet Coruscant. When Sagoro went to work as a Guard for the Galactic Senate of the Republic, she spent much of her time at home with their children.

After the events of Sagoro's case with Simon Greyshade, and her husband's aggression towards their son as a result of his lack of interest in Sagoro's work, Sula separated from Sagoro and moved with their children to Corellia.

Sula eventually reunited with him several weeks after the Republic was reformed into the Galactic Empire under the rule of Emperor Palpatine.

entities.name: Avax
entities.description:
Avax was a female Zabrak living during the Galactic War. Formerly an assassin for Chevin Conglomerate, she and her brother Chrone eventually became top bosses of the Rishi-based Kanawyn Syndicate along with Dastid. In 3637 BBY the Syndicate went after the smuggling business of Thera Markon, demanding her routes and clients. Thera used the reputation of her bounty hunter mother Crysta Markon who coached the Grand Champion of the Great Hunt to keep Kanawyns away, and it worked for a time. Eventually, it stopped working and the Syndicate killed Crysta, which proved their undoing. Thera used her money to put a bounty on all three bosses and the Grand Champion collected, killing them and dealing a huge blow to the Syndicate.

Avax appears in Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan during the Bounty Hunter class quest on Rishi.

entities.description:
Aven was a goddess worshipped by the Neimoidian species. Alongside fellow goddess Maradaine, Aven was known for telling the Unraveled Tale. A statue of the two goddesses was a major landmark in Zarra, the capital city of the planet Cato Neimoidia. Minister Alluv Eyam of the Cato Neimoidian government mentioned the statue of Aven while ruminating about Neimoidian culture at a trial being held for Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, who had been framed for crimes relating to the destruction of Zarra's Cadesura district.

Aven appeared as a statue in the 2022 novel Brotherhood, written by Mike Chen.

entities.name: Lemda Avesta
entities.description:
Lemda Avesta was a Human female geophysicist and niece of Shalim Avesta living on Makeb during the Galactic War.

Lemba Avesta earned her doctorate in geophysics at age 16.

During the Conquest of Makeb in 3638 BBY, when the Hutt Cartel instigated a hostile takeover of the planet, she convinced her uncle to forgo their planet's independence and go to the Galactic Republic for aid. She then went to investigate the increasing number of groundquakes on Makeb's surface, and eventually discovered that they were caused by the Hutts' deep-core drilling of isotope-5. While on the Frinn Mesa, Lemda was captured by the InterStellar Regulators, Makeb's former protectors bought off by the Hutts.

She was moved to the Quake Shelter 14-K where she was guarded by Captain Kazac. Lemda was eventually rescued by a Republic strike team led by Prosk. After leaving the groundquake shelter, Lemda revealed that the seismic readings proved the Hutts had sealed Makeb's fate. The groundquakes would increase in severity and cause entire mesas to collapse, and eventually gravitational decay would destroy Makeb's atmosphere, killing all life on the surface. However, she did overhear the Regulator talking about a "Project Failsafe", which she presumed was a method to save the planet.

entities.name: Avitla
entities.description:
Avitla was a Human female member of the Jedi Order who undertook her Jedi Trials as a Padawan on the planet Tython during the Cold War. Around 3643 BBY, she accompanied fellow Padawans Mennaus and Jerridan to the Tythonian Gnarls to seek knowledge of the Jedi Code, but they were interrupted by native Flesh Raiders.

The trio fought and killed one Flesh Raider, although Jerridan was badly wounded. Although Avitla wished to keep fighting till the group's trial was finished, another Padawan arrived and told them to return to safety, giving them a signal beacon to summon a speeder.

Avitla was a Force-sensitive Human who served in the Jedi Order as part of the Galactic Republic during its Cold War against the Sith Empire. Avitla was training as a Padawan on Tython, the homeworld of the Jedi. As part of her Jedi Trials, she accompanied fellow Padawans Mennaus and Jerridan into the Tythonian Gnarls region to seek knowledge of the Jedi Code.

The trio's trials were interrupted when they were attacked by Tython's native Flesh Raiders. Having not received combat training, the three Padawans fought a lone Flesh Raider near the Tythos River Delta and killed them, although Jerridan was badly injured during the battle. While Mennaus tended to Jerridan's injury, Avitla suggested they keep fighting until their trials were complete. Mennaus disgreed, but confirmed that he could help Jerridan along if Avitla was determined to keep going.

entities.description:
Avoira was a female slave who was sold into slavery on Dromund Kaas during the Cold War. In 3643 BBY, she, along with Jurithus, Rennith, and Sathun, joined a group of slave rebels to fight against their Imperial slavers and escape the planet. However, she and her friends were all killed in the skirmish.

entities.name: Avrey
entities.description:
Avrey was a female Human communications officer who served onboard the cruiser, Indomitable, during the Clone Wars against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. During a battle on the planet Kothlis, Avrey remained on the cruiser, repairing decade-old technology as General Grievous had jammed all communications on the Indomitable, Pioneer and Coruscant Sky.

In 21 BBY, she was present with Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, and Ahsoka Tano onboard the Indomitable. She was instructed by Admiral Yularen to remain on the ship when the Republic fleet made their way to Kothlis and prepare for their defense against the Separatist fleet under the command of General Grievous. When the fleet came out of hyperspace, Avrey saw that the internal and external communication systems from the fleet were not working and discovered that it was virus which was activated by Grievous. After proposing a solution, she was able to repair the technology, allowing the fleet to successfully win the battle. After the battle ended, she asked Obi-Wan to secure a connection to the Jedi Temple.

entities.name: Cadrin Awel
entities.description:
Cadrin Awel was a female Human from the planet Vandor-3 who was romantically linked to General Stavin Thaal of the Galactic Alliance. As a teenager, Awel performed as a singer but was unable to make an impact on the galactic capital Coruscant after winning local contests on her homeworld. During the Yuuzhan Vong War, Awel and her family hid on Vandor-3 to evade notice from the Yuuzhan Vong. Before the Second Galactic Civil War, Awel established a boot camp on Vandor-3 for people to learn nature skills. Her relationship with Thaal went undocumented and she was last recorded as having married a fellow wartime survivor in 42 ABY.

entities.name: Eldon Ax
entities.description:
Eldon Ax, born Cinzia Xandret, was a Human female Sith living around the time of the Great Galactic War and the Cold War. Born the daughter of technician Lema Xandret, she was separated from her family and trained in the Sith Academy under Darth Chratis. At the age of 17, she was confronted with her past, as evidence of her family's whereabouts, now considered a traitor to the Sith Empire. Ax herself took over the search for the planet, which eventually led both the Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic to the planet Sebaddon. The two parties formed an alliance to destroy the hex droids made by Lema Xandret, who had the potential to depopulate the entire galaxy. As one of the leaders of the Empire, Ax encountered a clone of her own, taking control of the droids that could kill their master and eventually disable them.

Cinzia Xandret was stolen from her mother, a droid maker named Lema Xandret, by Darth Chratis while she was still a child. Because Lema Xandret refused to willingly give up her child to the Sith, she was sentenced to death. Lema Xandret escaped the imposed death sentence by fleeing with some of her fellow droid makers. Darth Chratis imposed a Force powered mental block in Cinzia's mind to prevent her from recalling memories of her past, and renamed her Eldon Ax.

After losing a battle against a Mandalorian named Dao Stryver, Ax was interrogated by her, who looking for information on Lema Xandret and a ship named Cinzia. It was later found that the remnants of the ship named Cinzia were found and were being auctioned off by a Hutt named Tassaa Bareesh. Prior to giving this information to the Sith Dark Council, Darth Chratis removed the memory block he imposed on Eldon Ax and told her the true story of her existence. Chratis and Ax were dispatched by the Dark Council to steal the remains of the Cinzia and execute Lema Xandret if she was found. During the attempt to steal the remnants of the Cinzia, mysterious and deadly hex droids appeared and thwarted the theft. Although the attempt to steal the artifacts was unsuccessful, Ax was able to use the remains of a hex to trace their origin back to a planet called Sebaddon. The Jedi were also able to do the same. Ax then traveled with her master to claim the planet for the Empire.

entities.name: Tavion Axmis
entities.description:
Tavion Axmis was a Human female Dark Jedi who was at large during the early years of the New Republic. Apprenticed under the Dark Jedi Desann, Axmis traveled with him to find the lost Valley of the Jedi and served alongside him in Hethrir's Empire Reborn. After her defeat at the hands of Kyle Katarn and Desann's subsequent death, she became the leader of the Disciples of Ragnos cult. She took Alora as her apprentice, and set herself upon the task of resurrecting the ancient Sith Lord Marka Ragnos.

During Luke Skywalker's search for the cult, she turned Rosh Penin, one of Katarn's apprentices and a student at the Jedi Praxeum, to the dark side of the Force. Katarn and his apprentice Jaden Korr encountered and confronted her, and Penin at Vjun. Following this, Axmis journeyed to the Sith tomb world of Korriban to resurrect Ragnos; Korr was sent to stop her, and he defeated her after a fierce duel. In desperation, Axmis let the spirit of Ragnos fill her, and he guided her body in combat. She was killed after Korr defeated Ragnos, her body unable to withstand the ordeal.

Originally an Empire Youth in Lord Hethrir's Empire Reborn movement, Tavion Axmis displayed signs of Force-sensitivity and was "purified" by the extra-dimensional being Waru. She received training in the use of her Force abilities under Desann, Hethrir's right hand and failed Jedi trainee; during this training, Axmis was selected by Desann to be his personal apprentice, and the two conceived of a scheme to discover the location of the lost Valley of the Jedi. During the Battle of Artus Prime, Desann and Axmis intercepted Jan Ors, the partner of Kyle Katarn and one of the only two people to know the location of the Valley. Axmis managed to capture her and bring her aboard their shuttle. Katarn arrived to rescue his partner, only to be quickly defeated by Desann. On Desann's order Axmis, in the shuttle and out of Katarn's line of sight, activated her lightsaber and appeared to kill Ors. Desann spared Katarn and boarded his shuttle, leaving the planet with Axmis.

However, they did not leave the system. When Katarn left in the Raven's Claw, he immediately went to the Valley of the Jedi to regain his former Force-sensitivity, with the intention of using it to exact revenge on Ors's killers. Desann and Axmis followed him there; as Desann piloted their ship to the planet's surface, Axmis contacted Admiral Galak Fyyar to alert him of the Valley's location. Soon after, Axmis and Desann brought the presumed-dead Jan Ors to Admiral Fyyar's flagship, the Doomgiver. After building up a deadly new force known as the Reborn, Axmis left her master's side to oversee Imperial Remnant forces on Bespin who were smuggling cortosis for the shadowtroopers.

entities.description:

An idealistic woman, she saw through the corruption that plagued the Galactic Senate, and was known to steal cargoes and supplies while ensuring that her victims were not harmed in any way. Her pirate fleets consisted of a number of CloakShape fighters and small transports, all of which were protected by the modified IPV-1 System Patrol Craft, the Freejack.

entities.name: Vederiat Ayon
entities.description:
Vederiat Ayon was a female Twi'lek Pilgrim who lived on Tython during the Cold War between the reconstituted Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic.

A Twi'lek female, Ayon was one of many Pilgrims who followed Matriarch Kolovish to the planet Tython in the aftermath of the Great Galactic War. Assisting in the establishment of Kalikori village, Ayon was named the Minister of Flesh and Spirit among the pilgrims and served as a healer and spiritual leader. As incursions by the native and hostile Flesh Raiders became more frequent, Ayon came to believe that a rumored elixir was indeed making the natives more aggressive. Unable to go herself, Ayon hired a visiting Padawan to destroy the elixir in hopes it would put an end to the raids. This Padawan was then asked by Odumis Mer to keep the elixir in hopes that it could be used by the pilgrims to protect from further attacks.

Vederiat appears in the mission known as "Strength of the Flesh Raiders" in the 2011 BioWare game, Star Wars: The Old Republic.

entities.name: Azalie
entities.description:
Azalie was a Human female who lived during the time period known as the Cold War. The daughter of a Corellian corporation owner, she attended a party on Nar Shaddaa hosted by her father's partner, Drooga the Hutt.

Azalie can be romanced by a male version of the Voidhound. However there is no quest marker above her head. After spending a night with her, she will leave, expecting to see him again. Later, when at the smuggler hangar, she will appear again, expressing anger that the voidhound would leave without even saying goodbye. The Voidhound then could tell her that a relationship between them would be too dangerous, to which she would understand, bid the player farewell and leave. The player would also say that there is nothing between them, which would cause her to leave heartbroken. The player can earn dark side points by lying to her about giving her presents, to which she excitedly goes to her apartment, expecting presents.

The female smuggler meanwhile has no option to start a conversation with her at all.

entities.name: Azita Cruuz
entities.description:
Azita Cruuz was a human female and smuggler who operated prior to the Clone Wars. She grew up an orphan on in Pelek Baw, the capital of Haruun Kal, living the life of a loner in which her only companion was nature. Cruuz operated as a smuggler, occasionally doing large jobs to stay financially afloat. After hearing rumors of the scientist Dr. Bishop meddling with coaxium, she came to his refinery on the moon Ro Mira to investigate a profitable opportunity. She administered a drug to Bishop to induce a six-month amnesia and stole his supply of and formula for coaxium ultra. Cruuz subsequently made a broadcast soliciting offers to purchase her exclusive supply.

Cruuz's offer garnered attention from both Ro Mira Refinery Security and numerous interested parties. One such party was the Jedi Order, who hoped to keep coaxium ultra out of the hands of criminal organizations. The Jedi Mace Windu found Cruuz at a Ro Mira hospital and convinced her to hear out his offer. The pair traversed through the moon's ice caves to reach Cruuz's hidden speeder, which they took to Ro Mira's Radial Spaceport, where her freighter waited. To survive an attack from the Anzellan bounty hunter Yaya Shram, Cruuz agreed to exclusively sell to the Jedi.

At the spaceport Cruuz and Windu were attacked by two Dusk Weavers of the Had'le Path cult. Cruuz was able to take out one. When the Had'le Path leader known as "The Shroud" attacked Windu, Cruuz took the Jedi's interceptor to destroy her own ship and save Windu. Fortunately, she still had some coaxium ultra and its formula on her person. She intended to join Windu in a visit to their shared homeworld of Haruun Kal.

entities.name: Azoora
entities.description:
Azoora was a female Wroonian who lived on the Outer Rim world of Aduba-3 during the Galactic Civil War. Known for her beauty among the residents of the spaceport Tun Aduban, Azoora frequented the town's nightlife and developed a troublesome reputation. In 0 ABY, Azoora had an encounter with Rebel Alliance hero Han Solo, although it was interrupted when Azoora's jealous "boyfriend" Warto attacked the offworlder.

A Wroonian, Azoora was a native of the Outer Rim world of Aduba-3. Well known among the local spacers, Azoora earned a reputation as "trouble"—and also earned the attention of Warto, a hulking Boltrunian who styled himself as Azoora's boyfriend. Warto was known to threaten any other men whom he saw talking to Azoora.

Azoora frequented Locru's Central Saloon in the spaceport of Tun Aduban, where in 0 ABY she encountered notorious smuggler Han Solo of the Rebel Alliance. Solo approached Azoora at the bar, and after a short flirtation, Solo accepted Azoora's offer to leave with her and take a walk. However, Solo was quickly interrupted by a stranger and Azoora slipped away in the crowd.

Solo soon found himself accosted by Warto, who attacked him for flirting with his "girlfriend," although Warto was sent packing in a barroom brawl by Solo's Wookiee friend Chewbacca. Two years later, Azoora met with Rebel historian Voren Na'al, who was trying to piece together the story of Solo's travels after the Battle of Yavin. Azoora gave Na'al information about the local swoop gangs before threats from her current boyfriend forced Na'al to cut the interview short.

Halin Azucca was a human female who led the Opposition, a performance art troupe on the moon of the Inner Rim planet Pijal. Azucca and the performers' aim was to inform the Pijali of the problems facing Pijal through political art. they were framed by traitorous members of the royal guard led by Captain Deren, who, along with Princess Fanry, initiated a revolution against the Czerka Corporation's control of the Pijal system.

Halin Azucca appeared in Master & Apprentice, a 2019 novel written by Claudia Gray.

entities.name: Tinian I'att Azur-Jamin
entities.description:
Tinian I'att Azur-Jamin was a Human female who was the heiress of I'att Armament until she later became a bounty hunter during the Galactic Civil War.

Born on the industrial planet of Druckenwell, Tinian I'att was the heiress of I'att Armament, and was in love with Force-sensitive Daye Azur-Jamin, a Second Undersupervisor at the company. Her grandparents, Strephan and Augusta I'att, as well as her protector, the Wookiee Wrrlevgebev were killed by Imperials following a demonstration of the newly-developed armor-protective field for Moff Eisen Kerioth. Daye helped her escape, but the two were separated and she believed that he was killed. From that point on, she pledged her life to bringing down the Empire and was willing to risk her life, believing that when she died she would be reunited with Daye once more.

After escaping Druckenwell, she was picked up by Chenlambec, a Wookiee bounty hunter, and the two became friends. She was appointed his Hunt-apprentice. Though small and not physically strong, Tinian's life at I'att Armaments meant that she was very knowledgeable about various forms of weaponry, explosives, and armor. She was also fluent in Shyriiwook and served as Chenlambec's translator. She stayed with him for three years before the events surrounding Bossk and Lomabu III, becoming a skilled resistance fighter and Hunter herself.

Shortly after the Battle of Hoth, the two made a plan to capture Bossk, a Trandoshan bounty hunter, for desperately needed credits, and at the same time save a slave colony of Wookiees on Lomabu III from Imperials. Tinian's life at her family's armament factory saved both her and Chenlambec, when she was able to sniff out foreign explosives aboard the ship she was using to save the Wookiee colony. She and Chenlambec managed to capture Bossk and were awarded roughly 37,000 credits. They also took the Hound's Tooth, Bossk's ship,

entities.name: Aeron Azzameen
entities.description:
Aeron Azzameen was one of four children born into the Azzameen family. The lone daughter and next-to-last child of Tomaas Azzameen, Aeron learned of the family trade and was later employed as a freighter pilot by Twin Suns Transport Services, a shipping company owned by her father and his brother, Antan. During this time, she met Olin Garn, a freelance pilot often contracted by the shipping company; the two bonded, and due to their closeness, Garn eventually became considered as an extension of the Azzameen family. When Aeron's brother, Ace, came of age, Tomaas requested that Aeron teach the youngest Azzameen how to become a freighter pilot so that he too could serve in the family business. Through the course of several of these training sessions, Aeron and Ace came upon a plot led by the rival shipping company Viraxo Industries to encroach upon Azzameen holdings by involving the Galactic Empire. Faced with these circumstances, Antan had Aeron formulate a set of plans for retribution against the Viraxo; the plan fell through, however, due to a timing failure, and the Azzameens were forced to abort, risking life and limb and losing the family's YT-1300 light freighter Selu.

Shortly thereafter, the Azzameens were forced to evacuate their home and holdings because of a botched bacta run to a Rebel Alliance outpost that left Aeron's father and oldest brother assumed to be dead and the family marked as traitors by the Galactic Empire. Aeron suggested that the surviving Azzameen children try to take refuge among the Alliance's ranks, using Garn, who had previously enlisted, as a contact to vouch for the family. The Alliance, though wary of the suspicions aroused because of the loss of their outpost, accepted their plea for refuge and sheltered the Azzameens. Ace became a pilot in the Alliance's ranks, while Aeron and her older brother, Emon, began an investigation into their former life and the Viraxo's involvement in the Azzameen's downfall. Aeron later came under fire several times while attempting to assist the Rebellion, including one occasion when she was trapped aboard the doomed Bajic Shipyards asteroid base in the Vergesso Asteroids after a successful supply mission. Ace, taking a brief leave of action from the Rebellion, rescued her before the shipyard's destruction at the hands of Darth Vader's Death Squadron. Later, she, along with Ace and Emon, were lured into an Imperial trap created by uncle Antan; though the situation looked grim for the Azzameen children, they managed to escape the close call.

Aeron was a skilled pilot and could proficiently fly both YT-1300 and YT-2000 light freighters. She was also an expert at slicing into computer systems, an ability she used on several times to gather information on the Galactic Empire. Fully dedicated to those whose missions to which she allied herself, Aeron was insistent on her beliefs; though open to new ideas, she was considered steadfast on her ideals once her mind was decided. The lone female Azzameen child was also kind; however, she reserved this quality only for family members and Olin Garn, who had become so close to the family that he was considered to be a part of it.

entities.name: Azzenaj
entities.description:
Azzenaj was an Arch Witch of the Singing Mountain Clan on the planet Dathomir during the Galactic Civil War. Her pet rancor was named Lurrexu.

She once sent out an individual to find her initiate who had gone to collect herbs and never came back. She pointed the individual towards the Nightspider Cult cave.

At some point Azzenaj's old rival, the Nightsister Nandina, had escaped from the Chamber of Banishment and, hungering for revenge, decided to settle her score with the Arch Witch. She hired an assassin to take care of Azzenaj and provided him with the proper instructions. The assassin made his move, and the Arch Witch met him with the full arsenal of her Force powers. However, the assassin possessed several lethal weapons, and Azzenaj used the Force to mask her life signs. The assassin, believing her dead, took her elaborate jewelry as the proof of his job done and left to report to Nandina.

Azzenaj was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, Arch Witch Azzenaj was added to the game with the "Publish 1" update, released on August 3, 2003. Upon the release of the revamped "Witches of Dathomir Theme Park," introduced in the Game Update 19 on December 14, 2010, Azzenaj's original dialogues were removed from the game as the character was included in the new quest series.

entities.name: B'asia
entities.description:
B'asia was a young Togruta female who resided at the orphanage of Killi and Kaya Gimm in Jedha City. During the Galactic Empire's occupation of Jedha, Imperial stormtroopers raided Gimm's orphanage in search of contraband. When stormtroopers pushed Gimm to the ground, B'asia became frightened, and she hid under her bed. When a stormtrooper tried to remove B'asia from her hiding place, he grabbed her by her montrals, and when B'asia resisted, the stormtrooper struck her. When the raid concluded, Gimm, B'asia, and the other orphans were relocated to a home near the Second Spire. Later, she and thirty-three other orphans were able to escape Jedha in a stolen Imperial shuttle.

entities.name: Anita B'ath
entities.description:
Anita B'ath was a Human female who served as a member of the Ragtags on Corellia during the Galactic Civil War. After the Battle of Yavin, she lived in Coronet City and served as a henchman for Ames Miss'd, along with Box O'Rox. In 1 ABY, Anita B'ath and hes associates used to harass new recruits of the rival Meatlump gang. Angered by this situation, a food supply clerk of the Meatlumps tasked a spacer affiliated with the Meatlumps to teach the Ragtags a lesson. The spacer therefore met Ames Miss'd outside Coronet. The former attempted to intimidate the Ragtag but Miss'd was not scared and ordered Anita and Box to attack the spacer. Eventually, the spacer managed to kill them both. Unable to defend himself, Ames Miss'd surrendered and accepted to live the Meatlumps alone.

Anita B'ath appeared as a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, Anita B'ath was added to the game as part of the "Meatlumps Theme Park," introduced with "Chapter 10: The Search for the Meatlump King," released on June 19, 2008.

entities.description:
Fema Baab was a female human senator in the Senate of the Galactic Republic. Near the end of the Clone Wars, she was a steadfast supporter of Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine. Like Mee Deechi, Ask Aak, and Halle Burtoni, she advocated in favor of expanding the Grand Army of the Republic. Claiming to be patriotic to the Republic, she would question or threaten others who did not support the war. She wore a high-necked black dress.

In Revenge of the Sith, Fema Baab was played by Olive Levi.

Herylcha Baakos believed that the Elomin people were neglecting the Elom, and ordered the Elomin to allow their neighbors equal opportunity to live on the surface of their homeworld. Baakos, however, remained oblivious to the fact that the Elom preferred living underground.

entities.name: Sula Badani
entities.description:
Sula Badani was an human female of the Jedi Order in an Outer Rim Exploration Team on the Witherbloom during the High Republic Era. She was experienced in traveling the Galactic Frontier, where she dealt with civilizations and cultures new to the Galactic Republic.

Sula Badani was in the cockpit of the Witherbloom when it nearly collided with ship that appeared unexpectedly in front of them. When the ship rammed them and forced them to crash-land on a nearby planet, she commanded Coron Solstus to assist her with using the Force to open a hatch that had buckled shut due to the crash. After escaping from the exploding ship, she and Solstus returned to the wreckage to see if they could scavenge any supplies, but were unsuccessful. Sula and the rest of the team headed to the crash site of the other ship to see if there were any supplies or survivors. Upon arrival, Sula carried the injured Xinith Tarl and joined Ambar, Pako, and EX-5A to explore the body of the ship. She entered through an open airlock and discovered three bodies that had been mauled to death. She felt uneasiness through the Force, but was unable to discern what was causing it. When the group reached a cargo bay, she ordered the rest of the group to stay behind and take care of Tarl as she continued to explore the wreckage. The Jedi was attacked by several members of the Path of the Open Hand. As she questioned them on their mission, she was overcome by an intense feeling of hunger and fell to her knees.

The members of the Path of the Open Hand fled and Sula was able to compose herself and returned to the cargo bay where Ambar, Pako and Xinith were. She explained that the creature that was banging on the hull of the ship was trying to feed on the Living Force of the Jedi. When it started attacking again, Sula tried to remain focused and to assist Xinith in resisting the effects of the beast. She suggested they move to another part of the ship to get some distance from the creature. On the way, Sula discovered a medical kit and gave it to Ambar to use on Xirith. When Pako was able to successfully route power through the outer hull of the wreck and drive off the creature, Sula recovered from its effects.

entities.name: Baeshana
entities.description:
Baeshana was a female Tarasin and a member of the Wyrd Force witch living on the planet Cularin during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

A Force-sensitive Tarasin, Baeshana lived on the planet Cularin during the final decades of the Galactic Republic. A member of the Wyrd, Baeshana was trained in the ways of the Force by the group and eventually was skilled enough to be considered a witch. During her time as a Wyrd sister, Baeshana employed a bodyguard named Veshin.

When the Clone Wars erupted across the galaxy, a conflict between the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Baeshana resided the village of the Zhadorii irstat. Residing in the camp's central tent, she was visit when the village was attacked by a band of mercenaries and freedom fighters known as the Heroes of Cularin.

In Hunting the Wyrd the identity of the Wyrd sister and bodyguard that the player characters fight in the central hut varies, depending on player level. Upper-level players fight Baeshana and Veshin, but Mid-Level players fight Naelora and Kosaa instead, while High-Level players face Torunin and Savina. It is also possible for the players to avoid the hut, so the fight against Baeshana doesn't even have to take place.

entities.name: Zoriis Bafka
entities.description:
Zoriis Bafka was a female Twi'lek with green skin, who was one of the professional swoop racers Revan met in Anchorhead in 3956 BBY. She considered swoop racing a business, and swoop racers like herself the "product." She used to race under a different name when she was younger, but her career was not spectacular at that time. Revan was successful in beating Bafka's time in a swoop race.

If the player takes the dark side path in the game, they can insult or threaten Zoriis. Insults will result in her leaving, and threats can result in her giving you credits.

Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Prima's Official Strategy Guide

entities.name: Hermione Bagwa
entities.description:
Hermione "Harmony" Bagwa was a female human who worked as a waitress alongside Wanda and FLO at Dex's Diner, an eatery owned by Dexter Jettster and located on the streets of CoCo Town, Coruscant. She grew up within Coruscant's underworld. Shortly before the onset of the Clone Wars, Bagwa was present in the diner when Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi visited Jettster regarding a mysterious saberdart.

Hermione Bagwa was portrayed by Australian actress Susie Porter in the 2002 film Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones, the second installment of the Star Wars prequel trilogy.

Early production notes for Attack of the Clones suggest that Bagwa was originally going to be Dexter Jettster's wife instead of his waitress, but this direction was ultimately abandoned. During filming, Porter delivered waitress lines as both Hermione and FLO, the latter who was the only one to have a speaking part in the finished film.

Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition

entities.description: Nana Bagwa was a female Human and the grandmother of Hermione Bagwa. However, the Besalisk chef Dexter Jettster, who later employed Hermione, thought it nice enough to serve at his restaurant on Coruscant, Dex's Diner, where he named the dish Nana Bagwa's liver and onion in honor of her.

entities.name: Bahlea
entities.description:
Bahlea was a female Rutian Twi'lek Pilgrim who lived on Tython during the Cold War between the Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic.

A Twi'lek female, Bahlea was one of many Pilgrims who followed Matriarch Kolovish to the planet Tython in the aftermath of the Great Galactic War. Assisting in the establishment of Kalikori village, Bahlea married and bore a child named Rusa.

Along with her husband, Bahlea raised their child until she fell ill with a feverish sickness. Setting out to retrieve a medicine derived from manka cat teeth, Bahlea's husband was killed by Flesh Raiders during his search. Later, her husband's final mission was completed by a young Jedi Padawan from the nearby Jedi Temple who brought Bahlea and Rusa the necessary teeth for the medicine.

entities.name: Olivia Bain
entities.description:
Olivia Bain was a female Rodian who lived on Corellia during the time of the Galactic Civil War. She was the mother of Civius Bain.

Olivia Bain resided on Corellia with her husband, an accountant, and her son Civius Bain. After the Battle of Yavin, the young man got indebted to the spice smugglers Jaryn Minoze and Oret Sturm, two members of the ryll smuggling ring of the Chirq Council in Kor Vella. Civius Bain was forced to work for the smugglers in the Ryll Smuggler Base where they refined their ryll. Olivia Bain was desperate and wished for him to leave the smuggling ring and come home. she met a spacer in the Vella plains and begged to rescue her son. The spacer accepted and headed to the Ryll Smuggler Base. The spacer found Civius Bain in the bunker but the young man explained that he could not leave the smuggling ring since he was still indebted to the smugglers. The spacer therefore killed both Jaryn Minoze and Oret Sturm, allowing Civius to finally escape. After that, Civius Bain decided to start a new life and become an accountant like his father.

Olivia Bain was a non-player character in the 2003 video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by Sony Online Entertainment and published by LucasArts, Olivia Bain was added to the game with the update named "Chapter 1: The Corellian Captives," published on June 8, 2006.

entities.name: Vitala Baize
entities.description:
Vitala Baize was a red-haired female Human police officer in the Corellian Security Force who lived on Corellia during the Galactic Civil War.

By the time following the Battle of Yavin, Vitala Baize held the rank of captain in the Corellian Security Force and was stationed in the city of Doaba Guerfel.

In 1 ABY, the Corellian Security Force started an investigation against the Chirq Council, a criminal organization also known by the CorSec as the Red Circle Gang, following the increase of ryll traffic on Corellia. After Lieutenant Lon Cope discovered that the criminal organization was based in Doaba Guerfel, Captain Vitala Baize was designated to lead the investigation.

Lilith Laughlin immediately started to work for Captain Baize and she quickly found possible connections between the Red Circle Gang and a Drall terrorist organization known as the Drall Patriots. However, after a search in the Drall Patriot Warehouse in Doaba Guerfel, it appeared that there was no connection between the two groups. Laughlin later sent the spacer talk with Gwhirrye Baric, a thug who ran a spice racket out of a small hospital in Doaba Guerfel. After the spacer helped him to deal with Rogue CorSec miscreants who harassed his business, Baric accepted to reveal a name: Trins Evnar. The man was a spice dealer with a red circle tattoo on his arm and further investigations in his house revealed that he was a member of the Chirq Council. The spacer later assumed Trins Evnar's identity towards Jzoro Quanera, a Chirq Council underboss who did not know Trins Evnar personally. The agent managed to lure the Quanera and successfully infiltrated the organization.

entities.name: Jhaka Bakarn
entities.description:
Jhaka Bakarn, born Jhaka Bakvalen, was a dark-haired and light-skinned Human female. She was the eldest daughter of the affluent Bakvalen family on their homeworld of Corellia generations before the Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. However, Jhaka shunned her noble life and instead joined the Republic Navy as a starfighter pilot, causing her furious father to disown her.

Jhaka changed her surname to the more common "Bakarn" and went on to become a renowned fighter ace in charge of her own squadron. However, she was ultimately killed leading her squadron to victory over a dangerous warlord in the Outer Rim Territories, prompting her grieving father to change the family name to Bakarn in her honor. Bakarn was memorialized by a hologram in Bakvalen Hall, the family's house on Corellia.

Jhaka Bakarn appeared in a hologram in the Jedi Consular mission "Old Blood" in the 2011 BioWare massively multiplayer online role-playing video game Star Wars: The Old Republic.

entities.name: Bakkel
entities.description:
Bakkel was a female Human Beast Rider killed by Meetra Surik in Iziz on Onderon while she was seeking holodiscs for Dhagon Ghent. Bakkel refused to give the holodiscs to Surik and became hostile forcing Surik to kill her and her companions. She and her companions were often seen in the Beast Riders' Den in the western cantina.

Bakkel and her Beast-Riders had been operating in Iziz for several months prior to the Onderon Civil War. After the doctor Dhagon Ghent was arrested in connection with the murder of Guard Captain Sullio, Bakkel and her gang looted Ghent's office and took, among other things, encrypted holodisks containing the proper protocol for contacting his political connections in the Royal Palace. After Ghent was released Meetra Surik requested his help in contacting Jedi Master Kavar, who currently resided in the Royal Palace as an advisor to Queen Talia. Ghent informed her that without the holodisks stolen by Bakkel, he couldn't meet make contact with his connections. Surik met with Bakkel in the Iziz Cantina and tried to convince her to return the holodisks, but Bakkel became belligerent and attacked her and her companions. Bakkel and her gang were killed in the battle, and Surik returned the holodisks to Ghent.

entities.name: Balada
entities.description:
Balada was a female Hutt who sponsored and ran the Hunters of the Outer Rim competition on the Outer Rim planet Vespaara, alongside Daq Dragus.

Stories told that Balada found Vespaara by accident while on a scouting journey for unique items. She established a settlement in the small inhabitable zone of the planet and constructed the Grand Arena, making Vespaara her new base of operations. Soon, a boomtown sprouted up around the arena.

Balada founded the Hunters of the Outer Rim, a competition in which contestants known as "Hunters" would face each other in combat for the entertainment of their audience. As a co-owner of the Hunters of the Outer Rim competition, Balada had ultimate authority over it. She partnered with showman and former fighter Daq Dragus, who trained Hunters and acted as the face of the competition. Dragus had influence in the recruitment of Hunters, but Balada made the final call as to who would be trained and who was added to the official Hunter roster. Despite the attention and care she paid to the competition, she spent most of her time in her ship, the Hypernova, which hovered above the Grand Arena, or traveling the galaxy in search of antiquities.

Balada was an avid collector. She traveled the galaxy in search of novel weapons, trinkets, or potential Hunters. Her finds included the lightsabers used by Hunters both Rieve and J-3DI, other weapons used in the arena, proprietary bandage tape, and even a set of old Sith armor, which had been gifted to Rieve. Balada mandated that all of the organic Hunters used the tape, which prevented injury.

entities.name: Corwin Ballast's daughter
entities.description:
The daughter of the civilian Corwin Ballast and his wife, Lynnta, resided in the city of Maborn on the Outer Rim world Mordal during the Galactic Civil War. In 4 ABY, she became immobilized during a firefight between rebels and Imperial forces in Maborn, and their parents' rescue efforts proved unsuccessful. After Lynnta and his daughter's deaths, a grieving Ballast traveled to the Inner Rim planet Jakku with a picture of his family in his boot to remember them.

A daughter was born to the civilian Corwin Ballast and his wife, Lynnta, by the time of the Galactic Civil War. Their parents settled with their child on world Mordal in the city of Maborn. In 4 ABY, she became immobilized during a firefight between rebels and Imperial forces in Maborn. Her parents attempted to rescue her from the area of contention but were downed by blaster fire before they could reach her. Ballast recovered from his injuries and woke several weeks after the skirmish to find that his daughter and wife had died and been buried.

Grieved, Ballast kept his family's picture in his boot to remember them. He left Mordal to travel to Jakku, a location he considered desolate enough for war to never reach. In the drinking establishment Ergel's Bar on Jakku, Ballast explained to the bartender Ergel that he had come to the bleak world for his family's sake because it was far from the fighting. Though the man briefly relived the memory of his daughter and wife's deaths in his mind, he broke away from the recollection to continue conversing with Ergel.

By the time of the firefight on Mordal, the daughter of Corwin Ballast was young. Ballast loved his daughter and felt emotionally distraught after her death.

entities.name: Farquil Ban'n
entities.description:
Farquil Ban'n was a female Bith from Clak'dor VII who served as Embra the Hutt's assistant in 0 BBY. When Embra participated in a competition with fellow Hutts Malta and Jabba Desilijic Tiure to see who could hire the the most effective contractors to retrieve the valuable Yavin Vassilika artifact, Ban'n was charged with organizing Embra's hirelings—the bounty hunters Zuckuss, 4-LOM, and Sardu Sallowe. The hunt commenced, with Embra's contractors pitting themselves against the likes of Boba Fett, Bossk, and Han Solo.

Ban'n, however, had other ideas, and wanted to claim the prize for herself and leave Embra's service. She decided to track Malta's assistant, Jozzel Moffet, who had originally suggested the entire escapade and was accompanying Solo and another of Jabba's contractors, Lando Calrissian, on the hunt. After Moffet collected the artifact, Ban'n tracked her to the jungle moon of Yavin 4, where Moffet received payment for delivering the Vassilika to representatives from the Alliance to Restore the Republic. A firefight broke out after the other contractors converged on the moon, but Ban'n was able to isolate Moffet, kill her, and collect the four million credits payment. Ban'n subsequently quit Embra's employ, but was tracked down by Fett, who retrieved the money on behalf of Jabba.

Farquil Ban'n was a female Bith who hailed from Clak'dor VII, She found employment in the service of Embra the Hutt. In 0 BBY, she was asked by Embra to don a Theselonian bridal gown while serving the Hutt biscuits—a task that Ban'n found to be extremely painful. A week later she accompanied Embra to the palace of another Hutt, Jabba Desilijic Tiure, who had recently won a decisive victory over the rival Besadii clan. Traveling to the palace on Tatooine, Embra and yet another Hutt, Malta paid tribute to Jabba, and joined him for a game of dejarik. Meanwhile, Ban'n joined Jabba's majordomo, Bib Fortuna and Malta's handmaiden, Jozzel Moffet in watching from the sidelines, waiting for their masters to call on them. Ban'n and Moffet spoke disparagingly of their bosses, causing Fortuna to bristle, but Moffet was adamant that she would be able to break out of her servitude to Malta and earn a living on her own, much to Ban'n's skepticism.

Ban'n and Fortuna watched as Moffet first poured wine for Malta, and then pushed the boundaries of her position by suggesting a contest between the three Hutts—the legendary and extremely valuable Yavin Vassilika artifact had recently re-emerged, a fact that intrigued the Hutts. They dictated the rules of the treasure hunt, wherein each Hutt could only hire three contractors each to locate the Vassilika and bring it to Nar Shaddaa, the Smuggler's Moon. Embra quickly put Ban'n to use collating information gathered by the Hutt's network of informants, compiling a list of the contractors hired by his rivals. Jabba had elected to hire the smugglers Han Solo and Lando Calrissian, while Malta had hired a trio of bounty hunters: IG-88B, Bossk, and Dengar. Embra elected to go down the same route, meeting with the bounty hunters Zuckuss, 4-LOM, and Sardu Sallowe at the Hutt's residence.

entities.name: Yadira Ban
entities.description:
Yadira Ban was a female Lethan Twi'lek Jedi Padawan who served the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic during the Cold War with the reconstituted Sith Empire.

A Force-sensitive Twi'lek, Yadira Ban was trained in the ways of the Force by the Jedi Order during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. A Padawan who had constructed her lightsaber, her final trial was to face a Sith in combat. She was assigned to protect an Imperial defector referred to as "The General" while he was aboard the Brentaal Star, a Republic Thranta-class corvette.

During transit, the Imperial transport Black Talon attacked the Brentaal Star. Ban was killed when Imperial boarders confronted her on the Brentaal Star engine deck.

entities.name: Yuthura Ban
entities.description:
Yuthura Ban was a Twi'lek female born on the planet Sleheyron at some point before the Jedi Civil War. Originally enslaved to Omeesh the Hutt, Ban wounded Omeesh and eventually escaped Sleheyron, although she was abandoned on an uninhabited planetoid by the crew of a cargo ship she stowed away on in order to flee her homeworld. However, the Jedi Order rescued her and began training Ban in the ways of the Force, where she reached the rank of Padawan. However, she eventually abandoned the Jedi due to her hatred for slavery, and joined the Sith at the Sith Academy on the planet Korriban, eventually becoming the apprentice of the Academy's Headmaster Uthar Wynn.

In the final year of the Jedi Civil War—a galactic conflict between the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Malak's Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic—Ban encountered the Jedi Revan who, as the reconditioned former Dark Lord, was searching for the Star Forge, a Rakatan space station under the control of Revan's former apprentice Darth Malak. Ban was convinced by Revan to approve him for enrollment in the Sith Academy, with Uthar Wynn placing her in charge of teaching Revan and the other students the ways of the Sith. However, Ban conspired with Revan to murder Wynn at the final trial, so that she could gain his position as the Academy Headmaster.

During this time, Ban also aided Revan in his quest to gain more prestige with Wynn, and Revan learned about her past as a slave and Jedi. When Revan succeeded in gaining prestige with Wynn, Ban accompanied him and Wynn to the ancient Sith Lord Naga Sadow's tomb, where Revan was tasked with reaching the Rakatan Star Map and retrieving a Sith lightsaber. After the Jedi completed the tests, Ban and Revan turned against Wynn after he ordered the former to kill the latter. Ban turned against Revan, who, after defeating her, spared her life and convinced her to return to the light side and the Jedi.

Yuthura Ban, a Force-sensitive Twi'lek female, was born on the Outer Rim planet Sleheyron She was enslaved at a young age to the slave master Omeesh the Hutt. Filled with anger over her predicament, Ban sought vengeance by strengthening her determination not to simply be "nothing." At some point, she was alone with Omeesh in his bedchambers, and Ban stabbed the Hutt, who was intoxicated, and escaped his compound. Ban fled the planet by stowing aboard a cargo ship. Upon discovering her, the ship's crew abandoned her on a desolate planetoid to die.

entities.name: Bansee
entities.description:
Bansee was a human female member of the White Worms gang on the planet Corellia. She caught the eye of the gang's leader, Lady Proxima, for being the best rat catcher amongst the scrumrats her age and was made Third Girl. In 13 BBY, she was present when the scrumrat Han escaped from Proxima in the Den of the White Worms.

Bansee was a human female from the planet Corellia who served as a scrumrat in the White Worms gang of Coronet City. As the best rat catcher out of all of the girls her age, Bansee caught the attention of the leader of the gang, Lady Proxima, who made her Third Girl.

In the year 13 BBY, Bansee was present in the den when fellow scrumrat Han was brought before Proxima by Moloch, one of the gang's lieutenants. Han, who had returned from a trade with no goods for Proxima, used a rock to break a shutter behind the gang leader and bathe her in light, which burned her skin. Using the distraction, Han then pushed through the other scrumrats and escaped.

After an individual infiltrated the White Worms in order to retrieve a client's datapad, Bansee tasked them with "sending a message" to one of the gangs enemies in order to prove their loyalty. The individual succeeded in the task, but Bansee ended up threatening them with a stun baton and questioning who they worked for. The individual managed to avoid Bansee's wrath and ultimately acquired the datapad they were after.

entities.name: Halsia Banso
entities.description:
Halsia Banso was a female Human Sith Inquisitor of the Sith Empire who was active during the Galactic War with the Galactic Republic. Banso was among the Sith who were assigned to the Dread Executioners, fighting the forces of the Dread Masters on the moon Oricon during the phase of the conflict known as the Dread War.

Halsia Banso was first added to the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel as part of Game Update 2.4: The Dread War. She appeared on Oricon, where she was the Basic Gear vendor for the Sith Inquisitor class. Banso and the rest of the class gear vendors at Oricon, along with all other Daily Areas and high-level planets, were replaced by standardized vendors in Game Update 4.0 she was replaced by Lord Turbis.

entities.name: Auren Yomm Baobab
entities.description:
Auren Yomm Baobab was a Human female from the planet Roon. The daughter of Nilz and Bola Yomm, by the age of fifteen, Auren Yomm was an accomplished athlete and served as the leader of the Umboo Racing Team during the Roon Colonial Games of 15 BBY. It was during this time that she met and befriended Mungo Baobab, whom she would later marry, and his two droids, R2-D2 and C-3PO.

A native of Umboo, a sovereign province on the Outer Rim planet of Roon, the Human female Auren Yomm was born in the year 30 BBY to Nilz Yomm, a local doctor, and his wife, Bola. An accomplished athlete by age fifteen, she specialized in the drainsweeper event, a three-stage relay race performed while riding rockhoppers, during the Roon Colonial Games of 15 BBY. While on their way to the Games, Auren and her father Nilz witnessed the crash of a cloudcraft piloted by Mungo Baobab, a merchant from the planet Manda. Rescuing Baobab and his two droids, R2-D2 and C-3PO, from a pack of meddlesome, albeit benign mudmen, Auren invited the off-worlders to accompany her and her father to the Roon Games, where they would be able to find somebody to repair their ship.

Her original team composed of her friend Gee Long and the droid BIX. Governor Bisad Koong of Tawntoom province attempted to sabotage them by eliminating Long and Bix from the competition, but Mungo Baobab and C-3PO raced in their place and won the championship with Auren. Due to a malfunction on his ship, Koong also fell ill from rooze poisoning and tasked Gaff with kidnapping Nilz Yomm, who was a doctor, and his daughter in order to create an antidote. Meanwhile, Mungo Baobab, C-3PO, and R2-D2 tracked Governor Koong to the Fortress of Tawntoom, where Auren and her father were being held captive. After their rescue, the Yomms escaped the Tawntoom as Koong's fortress froze and as Koong himself dematerialized as a result of the rooze.

Sometime after their adventures on Roon, Auren Yomm and Mungo Baobab were married and took up residence on the planet Quilken.

entities.name: Yasinda Bardak
entities.description:
Yasinda Bardak was a well-educated Human female from Coruscant who was the daughter of the owner of TranStar Construction.

She was a mainstay of the social life in Tasariq City's Paradise Square, doing whatever she wanted to do, whenever she felt like doing it. As the Imperial presence on Tasariq grew, Yasinda made more and more anti-Imperial remarks during her parties, and even openly questioned the wisdom of the Tarkin Doctrine. However, few realized that Yasinda was actually an Imperial Intelligence agent who had been recruited by Emperor Palpatine himself for special training. It was planned that she would one day become one of the Emperor's Hands, as Yasinda was found to be Force-sensitive, but her Imperial upbringing made her refuse to accept the possibility that the Force even existed, let alone was accessible to her. She was removed from the training, but continued her education with the Intelligence agency, and eagerly spent her time on Tasariq searching for Rebel cells.

The Emperor was curious as to the impact of the native tasar crystals on Force-sensitives, and sent Sarcev Quest to observe the effect on Bardak. To this end, Quest gave her an amulet containing a tasar crystal, and continued to visit her. Unfortunately for Yasinda, her proximity to the Tasar Crystals re-awakened her Force-sensitivity, and she started to hear voices in her head. This slowly drove her insane, and only her years of training kept her from completely losing her mind. The Emperor refused her transfer requests until his "experiment" was completed.

entities.name: Sansia Bardrin
entities.description:
Sansia Bardrin was the daughter of the wealthy industrialist Ja Bardrin. While running technology for her father on Makksre, she was captured by pirates, who in turn handed her over to Chay Praysh's slaver consortium.

She did not trust her father, believing (correctly) that he cared more about the fate of the luxury yacht she had been piloting, the Winning Gamble, than he did about her. However, she had no idea that he had, in fact, set her up to be captured in order to acquire prototype technology which Praysh had stolen from the Uoti Corporate.

Sansia was rescued by Mara Jade and another of Praysh's slaves, H'sishi, both of whom fought and killed a great many of Praysh's Drach'nam guards. At the same time, Sansia recovered the Winning Gamble and used it to destroy Praysh's starfighters. After returning home and learning the truth about her father's ploy from Talon Karrde, she took her revenge by gifting the ship to Mara and valuable stock options in her father's company to Karrde, as payment for their services, much to her father's dismay.

entities.description:
Trella Bare'Ah was a female Twi'lek who worked as a dancer and was romantically involved with the Rodian bounty hunter Greedo during the Clone Wars. During the blockade of Pantora, Bare'Ah was present in Jabba's Palace on Tatooine, where she was approached by Ion Papanoida and his father, Supreme Chairman Notluwiski Papanoida of Pantora, whose children had been kidnapped by Greedo. Bare'Ah claimed that the bounty hunter was not currently at the palace, however, she informed Greedo in a backroom of the palace that some Pantorans were searching for him.

Trella Bare'Ah is voiced by Jennifer Hale in The Clone Wars television series.

entities.name: Tassaa Bareesh
entities.description:
Tassaa Bareesh was a Hutt crime lord and a matriarch of Bareesh Cartel operating off of Nal Hutta.

Around 3643 BBY, Tassaa started an auction for artifact from a very precious and rare metals have been offered. She invited both the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire in order to outbid each other.

After a failed attempt, a battle between Jedi Padawan Shigar Konshi and Sith Acolyte Eldon Ax started. The battle was short until they were both arrested after large parts of the palace were stolen and destroyed by a Mandalorian named Dao Stryver. Shigar was able to convince them of his innocence, however, he had to sign a contract with the matriarch. According to the agreement, the Padawan would track down the thief and retrieve the navicomputer which was stolen.

This eventually led the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire to form an alliance together and battle against an army of hex droids on Sebaddon. However, Shigar's promise to Bareesh was not kept since he failed to retrieve what was stolen. Bareesh had no choice but to drop a bounty on the Padawan.

entities.name: Bargu
entities.description:
Bargu was a female Clawdite Jedi Padawan serving the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic as a Commander in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars.

A Force-sensitive female Clawdite, Bargu received her early education in the ways of the Force at the Coruscant Jedi Temple's academy. Selected as a Padawan after the outbreak of the Clone Wars, a conflict between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Bargu was made a Commander in the Grand Army of the Republic.

Stationed at the Temple in 19 BBY, Bargu participated in the Apprentice Tournament overseen by Jedi Master Ilena Xan. Making it through to the Round of Eight, which was held in one of the Temple refectories, Bargu was defeated in combat by a Chagrian Padawan, Lena Missa, by a blow to the arm with a training lightsaber.
