entities.name: Larisselle Chatrunis
entities.description:
Larisselle Chatrunis was a Pa'lowick female who, in 22 BBY, was a participant in the Miss Coruscant competition.

Larisselle Chatrunis was a Pa'lowick female Coruscant. Her species had just recently learned of galactic society at the time of her participation.

During the competition, she juggled whilst reciting the Founder's Day Allegiance and sang during the talent portion, impressing the judges. Afterwards, the Pa'lowick made a statement on the ongoing Separatist Crisis, where she stated separation was traumatic. She continued by saying the separation of families is sad, but when it happens to the millions of families within a galaxy, it is even sadder. Her knowledge of and sensitivity to the crisis truly impressed the judges, as it was unusual for an individual to have such comprehension when their species was new to galactic society. Chatrunis eventually won the competition, beating out the thirty-five other participants. While receiving the Miss Coruscant crown, the Pa'lowick cried with joy. Chatrunis's win was reported on the date 13:4:18 by the CoCo District Edition of HoloNet News in its 531st volume. Her crowning garnered the Pa'lowicks increased public awareness.

After the rise of the Galactic Empire Chatrunis's fame was curtailed due to the speciesist policies instated by Emperor Palpatine. The Pa'lowick, however, had joined the Alliance to Restore the Republic and used her vocal talent to tour the galaxy with a band, gathering information to provide to the Rebels. Chatrunis's purpose was to make music so that alien individuals could be freed from oppression and encouraged ideas that she was in competition with fellow Pa'lowick musician Sy Snootles to distract from her true motives. Chatrunis survived the Galactic Civil War between the Alliance and Galactic Empire and returned to homeworld, where she lived quietly with her family and friends.

entities.name: Neiya Chault
entities.description:
Neiya Chault was a Force-sensitive Human female supporter of the Galactic Republic during the Cold War. After Padawan Thoma went on a mission to investigate alien mercenaries that joined the Sith Empire, she asked a Republic spacer to search for the missing Jedi in the Mercenary Training Facility Barracks. The Republic spacer found Thoma dead, but retrieved a message he left for Neiya.

In the message, Thoma revealed that Neiya was Force-sensitive and expressed his desire that his friend receive training from the Jedi Order. After seeing the holocron, Neiya agreed to honor his wish.

entities.name: Chava
entities.description:
Chava, also known as Chava the Wise, was a female Lasat mystic who survived the fall of Lasan at the hands of the Galactic Empire. She became a refugee and, along with former Lasan High Honor Guardsman Gron, was rescued from Imperial captivity by the rebel crew of the Ghost. With the assistance of Garazeb Orrelios, a member of the Ghost crew, Chava was able to help find the way to Lira San, the ancient homeworld of the Lasat spoken of in legend. After discovering the planet, Chava remained on Lira San with the millions of Lasat who already lived there.

Chava the Wise and her traveling companion Gron, a former Lasan High Honor Guardsman, were one of the few Lasat to survive the brutal Imperial pacification of Lasan. Chava and Gron embarked on a quest to find Lira San, a legendary planet that was regarded as a sanctuary for the Lasat species. Their travels led them to smuggle themselves in a cargo container on Nixus Hub 218 where they were discovered by Imperial forces, who had been tipped off by the Weequay pirate Hondo Ohnaka. However, Ohnaka had also alerted his one-time "business partner" Ezra Bridger.

Chava and Gron were promptly detained by Imperial stormtroopers, who intended to ship them to a detention camp. However, Ezra and his rebel cell rescued the two Lasat and overpowered their Imperial captors. Chava and Gron were delighted to learn that one of their rescuers was Garazeb Orrelios, a former Captain in the Honor Guard. As the two Lasat and their rebel rescuers made their way back to the rebels' starship Ghost, Chava told her rescuers that she and Gron were searching for Lira San. On the way, they were ambushed by more stormtroopers but managed to escape due to assistance from Ohnaka. Chava and her companions then escaped into hyperspace aboard the Ghost.

Once in hyperspace, Chava informed her rebel rescuers that she did not know the location of Lira San since it was only mentioned in ancient Lasat prophecy. In order to find it, Chava told her hosts that a prophesied "child" had to first save the "warrior" and the "fool." When the astromech droid Chopper commented in Binary that she was "weird," Chava issued an angry rebuke. With the help of Ezra, Chava and Gron began a ritual designed to help them find Lira San. While Zeb was initially unwilling to help due to his lingering guilt over his failure to safeguard the Lasat royal family and Lasan, Ezra managed to convince the former Captain to help his Lasat compatriots protect their people by finding Lira San.

entities.name: Chavani
entities.description:
Doctor Chavani was a female therapist who in the treated the former Imperial prisoner Brentin Lore Wexley after he was freed from Ashmead's Lock on the planet Kashyyyk by the New Republic during the Liberation of Kashyyyk. Chavani spoke to Wexley's son Temmin and reassured that it would be normal for his father to regularly go on long walks, as a lot had likely built up in Brentin Wexley's mind during the years he was imprisoned.

Chavani was first mentioned in the novel Aftermath: Life Debt, which was written by Chuck Wendig

entities.name: Chawkroft
entities.description:
Lady Chawkroft was the Imperial Minister of Corrections in the years preceding the Battle of Yavin and co-sponsor of Stars' End.

Chawkroft began her rise within the Imperial Correctional Facilities Ministry after the death of her superior, Gervruche. As a Special Projects Consultant, Chawkroft received a message from Ilm Vaz-Weplinn, an Assistant-Deputy Viceprex of the Corporate Sector Authority's Security Division. Vaz-Weplinn proposed the joint development of an advanced prison facility in the Corporate Sector. Chawcroft was pleased with this proposal: her ministry welcomed the chance to share costs of prison development with the CSA, and Grand Vizier Sate Pestage had blocked the budget requests of the Admiralty for their own prison facilities.

Shortly after she signed on, Viceprex Mirkovig Hirken took control of the project, code-named "Stars' End." Hirken and Chawkroft continued working together on Stars' End, corresponding and visiting frequently. Chawcroft was apparently befriended by Hirken's wife Neera, who shared her recipe for oonberry pie with Chawcroft at the Hirken's anniversary banquet. While working on the project, Chawcroft's career prospered. She continued to rise through the Ministry bureaucracy, first to Assistant-Minister of Corrections and then to Minister of Corrections by 2 BBY.

After Han Solo, Chewbacca, and their associates destroyed Stars' End, resulting in the deaths of the Hirkens, Chawcroft sent her condolences to Viceprex Hirken's department. Newly appointed Viceprex Vaz-Weplinn sent a reply, arguing for continued collaboration between her ministry and the CSA despite recent setbacks.

entities.name: Che'nash
entities.description:
Che'nash was a female Geranite mercenary operative working as part of the Shrikaansi Reconnaissance Company for the reconstituted Sith Empire at the end of the Cold War.

Che'nash was a part of a mercenary team, hired by the Sith Empire and deployed to the planet Ilum at the end of the Cold War. Her team was tasked with uncovering information on a Republic operation code named "Shatterstorm," which involved the Republic's Talz commandos. However, they were unable to complete their mission alone, and were forced to seek the help of other Imperial operatives.

Che'nash first appeared in the MMORPG Star Wars: The Old Republic, released by BioWare in 2011.

She is only accessible to Imperial players in the game on Ilum.

entities.name: Che'ri
entities.description:
Che'ri was a Force-sensitive Chiss female who served as an ozyly-esehembo within the Chiss Ascendancy. Thalias was her caregiver, or "Momish" while she served on Mitth'raw'nuruodo's ship. She liked to draw on her questis and later with colored graph markers. She often drew pictures of birds, flashflies, and scenery as seen from above, as she had always dreamed of flying. Che'ri often had nightmares, which was typical of sky-walkers. She understood the trade language of Meese Caulf.

Che'ri was born around 29 BBY. At a young age, she was determined to have Third Sight, and was made part of the Chiss Sky-walker corps.

She served on multiple ships, with eight caregivers, until she fell under service to Mitth'raw'nuruodo, core name "Thrawn," aboard his ship, the Springhawk. Che'ri was sprawled across a chair making drawings/collages of pre-existing assets in her questis when her new caregiver, Mitth'ali'astov ("Thalias") arrived. Instead of introducing herself right away, Thalias, not wanting to overwhelm Che'ri, went to her private quarters to settle in. However, after a while, Thalias introduces herself and compliments Che'ri's artwork, describing it as a talent to be cherished. Che'ri reflects upon how her previous caregivers found her artwork to be "silly". Che'ri is surprised to learn that Thalias had been a sky-walker (with only four caregivers). The two talk about the incompetencies of the operation of the sky-walker/caregiver system. Eventually, Che'ri is concerned about going into a battle, but Thalias tries to soothe her by reassuring Senior Captain Thrawn's military prowess. Thalias asks Che'ri if she would like to read about Thrawn's military career. Che'ri refuses, citing her dislike of reading, but Thalias sends the file to her questis anyway. Che'ri complains about the file being too long, to which Thalias promises to create an abridged version at a later time.

After a battle over the Paataatus Hiveborn homeworld of Nettehi, Che'ri brought the Springhawk out of hyperspace in an unknown system. Che'ri was starting to feel an overload spell, but did not say any anything about it, due to being taught to not show weakness. She silently hoped that Thrawn would allow her to take a break from her duties. To her surprise, Thrawn allowed her to rest. Che'ri, while relieved, was disturbed at the thought of Thrawn knowing of Che'ri's need for a break. Thrawn orders the helm officer, Lieutenant Commander Tumaz'mor'diamir ("Azmordi") to bring the Springhawk into a high orbit over the system's planet. As Azmordi took control of the ship, Che'ri became fascinated with the ship's controls. Che'ri overheard Thalias thanking Thrawn for stopping the ship, recognizing that she too knew of Che'ri's coming overload spell. She wondered if everybody knew.

entities.name: Vokara Che
entities.description:
Vokara Che was a female Twi'lek Jedi Master and a highly accomplished Jedi healer who served the Jedi Order at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant during the time of the Clone Wars.

The female Twi'lek Vokara Che was an accomplished Jedi healer that served as the Chief Healer of the Jedi Temple's Halls of Healing. In 22 BBY, the Jedi Order suffered a great loss of Jedi on Geonosis with the outbreak of the Clone Wars. Although several Jedi survived the battle, a number were injured, and Che was set with the task of treating them. However, the Padawan Anakin Skywalker's forearm had been cut off in a duel with Count Dooku, a Jedi Master who had left the Order and become a Dark Lord of the Sith. Skywalker's Master, Obi-Wan Kenobi, had also suffered injuries, and when Master and Padawan returned to the Temple on Coruscant, Che had Skywalker put into a healing trance to counterattack the shock of his injury, while a prosthetic arm was to be given to him. In addition, Che personally sent a healer to put Kenobi into a healing trance; however, Kenobi refused, seeking to meet with his Padawan.

Senator Padmé Amidala, who had become romantically involved with Skywalker, arrived at the Halls of Healing and insisted on seeing Skywalker. Che refused to let Amidala see Skywalker, as he was already in a healing trance, and noted that Amidala herself required medical attention as well from numerous injuries. The senator, however, refused treatment from the Jedi or a medcenter, and was determined to see Skywalker. Kenobi entered the room and intervened. Che was aggravated that he had delayed his healing, but allowed Kenobi to speak with Amidala. Kenobi was able to convince the senator to receive treatment from the Jedi and return to her apartment.

Che later met with Master Yoda in her private chambers in the Halls, and brought him up to date with the Jedi being treated. The Twi'lek healer expressed her concern for Kenobi, who worried for his Padawan. Both Che and Yoda had known Kenobi from infancy, and Yoda resolved to counsel Kenobi. Che was relieved with Yoda's decision to assist Kenobi, but before Yoda departed, she informed him of Amidala's arrival at the Temple and her determination to see Skywalker, as well as the possibility of an official complaint.

entities.name: Cheelru
entities.description:
Cheelru was powerful Tarasin Force witch and a member of the Inner Circle of the Wyrd. By 19 BBY her commitment to the Dark side of the Force had driven her insane. She disagreed with the Wyrd Mother over the use of the Ritual of the Power of the Dark, as this could potentially destroy the Ch'hala, which would end all that the Wyrd stood for. The Mother responded by having Cheelru chained up in a cave and left there to be a future sacrifice. The Heroes of Cularin encountered her there while they investigated the Wyrd and she told them about the Ritual.

entities.name: Klerin Chekkat
entities.description:
Klerin Chekkat, a Kuranu female and daughter of Mantessa Chekkat, invented a recainium-powered four-seven nullifier that the pair hoped to sell at the Valo Republic Fair. Her mother took all the credit for the invention, but was killed at the Fair during the Battle of Valo, and Klerin was rescued by Jedi after her attempt to sell her nullifier bangle to the Nihil raiders went awry. Chekkat concealed her true intentions, telling the Republic forces that the Nihil had stolen the plans for the nullifier, and went so far as to willingly play a part of a Jedi ploy to discover the Nihil base, which saw her kidnapped by the escaped Nihil Quin Amarant and taken aboard a stolen shuttle. However, upon arriving at the Nihil base on the planet Grizal and meeting with the Nihil Tempest Runner Lourna Dee, Chekkat exposed the presence of the Jedi who had snuck aboard the stolen shuttle, and offered to sell the bangle to Dee.

Klerin Chekkat was a Kuranu female who pretended to be a less capable inventor than her mother, Mantessa Chekkat. The pair hired the Tholothian mercenary Ty Yorrick to protect them as they attended the Republic Fair on the planet Valo. En route to the fair, Klerin displayed attraction towards Yorrick while toying with the large bangle she wore on one wrist. Though it appeared to be jewelry, it was actually a four-seven nullifier, a device that disrupted energy weapons such as blasters and lightsabers, powered by the illegal substance recainium. Though Klerin had invented it, her mother posed as the true inventor when meeting with Sullustan Senator Tia Toon to discuss selling it for his Defense Force Program. Toon refused to buy the device, and had Mantessa and Yorrick imprisoned for bringing recainium onto the world. The two managed to escape and got separated when Nihil marauders attacked the Valo Republic Fair, but soon after the mother and daughter were reunited, Mantessa was killed by a hragscythe that had escaped from the Lonisa City Zoo.

entities.name: Mantessa Chekkat
entities.description:
Mantessa Chekkat was a Kuranu female inventor. She and her daughter, Klerin, attended the Republic Fair on the planet Valo, hiring the mercenary Ty Yorrick to protect them. Chekkat intended to offer to sell the prototype of a recainium-powered four-seven nullifier, a device that disrupted energy weapons, including blasters and lightsabers, to Senator Tia Toon for his Defense Force Program. Toon refused to buy the device, having both Chekkat and Yorrick imprisoned for the inventor bringing an illegal substance onto the world. The two managed to escape after Nihil marauders attacked the Republic Fair, and Chekkat located Klerin, parting ways with Yorrick in an attempt to escape Valo. However, the elder Chekkat was killed by a hragscythe that had escaped from the Lonisa City Zoo.

entities.description: Laneet Chekkoo was a female Rodian who lived on the planet Rodia and was a part of the Chekkoo clan. Shortly after the Battle of Yavin, she met the aspiring Jedi and pilot Luke Skywalker when he came to Chekkoo Enclave seeking to purchase weapons for the Alliance to Restore the Republic. She led Skywalker to Toopil, a secret base, and introduced him to Taneetch Soonta, sales executive for armament manufacturer Utheel Outfitters.

entities.name: Chelik
entities.description:
Chelik was a princess of the Hapan Royal House, a niece of Ta'a Chume, and the older sister of Alyssia. She was believed to harbor ambitions to usurp the throne and become Queen Mother of Hapes.

In 27 ABY, Chelik's daughter attempted to assassinate her cousin Prince Isolder. As the reigning Queen Mother, Teneniel Djo, was rapidly losing influence, Isolder's daughter Tenel Ka initially assumed that this was a desperate coup attempt by Chelik, but later reflected that this was more likely the result of scheming by her ambitious sister Alyssia, who saw the families of both Ta'a Chume and Chelik as obstacles to her own ambitions.

In the event, Alyssia's schemes failed, and Tenel Ka succeeded to the throne.

entities.name: Chelik's daughter
entities.description:
Chelik's daughter was a princess of the Hapan Royal House, the daughter of Chelik and great-niece of the Queen Mother Ta'a Chume.

During the Yuuzhan Vong War, she attempted to assassinate her cousin Prince Isolder as he returned to the Fountain Palace. Her attempt was foiled by Isolder's daughter, the Chume'da Tenel Ka Djo, and she was led away by the guard Ubris.

Although Tenel Ka's first thought was that Chelik was behind the assassination attempt, she decided on reflection that the girl had more likely been put up to the act by her scheming aunt Alyssia, and that the attempt had been intended to fail, in order to weaken Chelik and strengthen Alyssia's own ambitions to seize the throne.

Tenel Ka calmly assumed that her cousin would be promptly executed for her action.

entities.name: Tana Chellaine
entities.description:
Tana Chellaine was a female human who flew as a TIE fighter pilot for the Galactic Empire around the time of the Battle of Yavin. She flew in the Imperial Army's Nashtah Squadron, which participated in a battle on the planet Portocari where they lost three squad members. Sometime after the battle, Chellaine and the other surviving members of Nashtah Squadron drank together at the Zero Angle, a bar in the Bright Jewel Oversector Flight Base. There, Chellaine unsuccessfully tried to prevent some of her squadmates from getting into a bar fight with Imperial Navy pilots before the bar was informed by Commander Weller that the Death Star had been destroyed.

The human female Tana Chellaine served the Galactic Empire as a pilot during the Galactic Civil War against the Alliance to Restore the Republic. During the war, Chellaine flew a TIE/ln space superiority starfighter in Nashtah Squadron, a squadron of pilots in the Imperial Army who flew missions within planetary atmospheres. Around the time of the Battle of Yavin, she and her squadron were sent to the planet Portocari where they were sent to bomb Rebel artillery in the planet's hills before being reassigned to bomb an urban safehouse, which the squad were told would prevent the need for door-door fighting and civilian casualties. During the ensuing battle, Chellaine's squad-mate Muller was shot down by an anti-aircraft missile, while another named Barsay was killed by Z-95 Headhunters.

Upon bombing the safehouse, the squadron discovered it was full of munitions, which exploded and killed two more of Chellaine's comrades, Chan and Riggs. After the battle, the surviving members of the squadron traveled to the Bright Jewel Oversector Flight Base on the moon Axxila III. There, Muller was taken to be treated in bacta while Chellaine and the other surviving members of her squadron (Sully Olvar, Huck Trompo, Artur Essada, and Sax Hastur) where debriefed. The group of five then met for drinks in the Zero Angle, a bar in the flight base.

After becoming intoxicated, Trompo began singing a ground-hog anthem in an attempt to antagonize a group of Imperial Navy pilots also in the bar. Chellaine warned her squad-mate to stop, as the singing had drawn the attention of Florn, the bar's bartender, but Trompo continued and was joined by Olvar. Hastur interrupted the pair and forced them to sit. Essada tried to discuss the events on Portocari with the group, but Hastur shot down the topic of discussion and Trompo began singing again, this time successfully rallying other Army pilots in the bar to join in. The Zero Angle's navy patrons quickly retaliated with their own anthem, and a fight quickly broke out between the two groups. Chellaine stayed out of the brawl, but when a navy pilot stumbled into her and caused some of her drink to fly in the air, she was able to catch the water back in her cup and then kick the navy pilot back into the fight.

entities.name: Chem's mother
entities.description:
The mother of Kyp's Dozen pilot Chem was a wealthy diplomat. She collected pristine starfighters, and her most prized was an early T-65XJ X-wing starfighter. On Chem's fourteenth birthday, he stole the craft and went off to join the Dozen.

entities.name: Cheraama
entities.description:
Cheraama was a queen who served as the ruler of Alun and belonged to its royal family. When she ascended the throne during the Imperial Era, she was considered young and inexperienced, and genuinely wanted to serve her people but her reforms backfired. With her failed attempts at reforming trade, many in the population began to have the sentiment that a governor of the Galactic Empire would better serve their needs. This sentiment alarmed Cheraama's advisor, Faleer Ayast, as he questioned how that would affect the planet's freedoms.

entities.name: Viera Cheran
entities.description:
Viera Cheran served as Chief Technician for Rogue Squadron and crew chief, responsible for overseeing the maintenance of the squadron's starfighters and all flight deck operations.

During the Galactic Civil War, Cheran and her crew served the Rogue Squadron and followed the team from station to station throughout their missions. Around 3.5 ABY, when Slave I was spotted on Gall, her team was ordered to build a temporary base on nearby Kile.

In the same time, Prince Xizor of Black Sun intended to discredit Darth Vader before Emperor Palpatine's eyes. For that end he used his underground connections to bribe bounty hunters and anyone else who could track down and kill Luke Skywalker.

The movements of the Rogue Squadron, as well as Cheran's weariness for her position and dissatisfaction with the pilots, were known to Vigo Sprax of Black Sun, who had contacts within the Alliance. Before a Cheran moved with her crew to Kile, she was approached by someone from the fleet, who was actually one of Black Sun's moles, offering her 10,000 credits for Luke Skywalker dead by "technical malfunction", promising 40,000 afterwards. She saw killing Skywalker as a means to get enough money to buy her own light freighter and become a Free-trader, working only for herself. Cheran decided to take the bribe. Guri paid her through a net of dummy corporations, which would be traced to Saber Enterprises.

entities.name: Cheriville
entities.description:
Cheriville was a human woman who was part of the Nihil marauders with their husband, the Nihil commander Vark Tarpalin, during the High Republic Era. The wife watched historical holodramas and told Tarpalin about them, including one that included information about the Scarlet Skull Cult child assassins. By that time, the commander kept a framed painting of Cheriville hung in his city hall office on the Outer Rim planet Valo. In the artwork, the woman held a Gedonian ground weevil and donned Nihil body armor.

In 229 BBY, when Tarpalin's Dark Fair event on Valo was attacked by Jedi Padawan Ram Jomaram, who was operating under the code name the "Scarlet Skull," he was reminded of his wife's holodramas. Later, the aspiring pirate Zyle Keem and the Jedi youngling Gavi broke into Tarpalin's office and noticed the paintings of the man and Cheriville, with the former thinking the woman had fashionable hair.

Cheriville appeared in a painting in Escape from Valo, a 2024 junior novel written by Daniel José Older and Alyssa Wong as part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's On Twitter, Older confirmed that the woman in Vark Tarpalin's office painting was Cheriville.

entities.name: Cheroth
entities.description:
Cheroth was a female Mirialan who lived on Tatooine during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the reconstituted Sith Empire. A red-headed female with red eyes, they had olive-colored skin and facial tattoos, Cheroth wore their hair in a bun, and dressed primarily in green and tan desert clothing. During the Cold War, Cheroth worked in the Anchorhead cantina Junix's Joint as a waitress.

Cheroth was created for Star Wars: The Old Republic, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game released by BioWare in 2011. They appeared in Anchorhead, the Republic-only city on Tatooine, as a Cantina Vendor.

Along with fellow Beddek and Prahmin, she was kidnapped by the Sith Empire and forced to assist in stabilizing Makeb's core.

entities.description:
Chiana was a female Human wife of Tyvar, an agent of the intelligence agency of the reconstituted Sith Empire. Retired by the time of the Galactic War, Tyvar and Chiana settled on Makeb and lived there with their son Peron and daughter Syla. During the Conquest of Makeb in 3638 BBY the Empire asked Tyvar to reactivate and provide information that would help in the recovery of Isotope-5. Unfortunately the Hutt Cartel became aware of his true allegiance and set the InterStellar Regulators to eliminate him. Captain Hanthor of the Sith Empire was forced to send a retrieval team for Lurker and his family.

entities.name: Chiata
entities.description:
Chiata was a female Jedi Master who served the Jedi Order during the Clone Wars, training the Padawan Marseph. During a battle against a Separatist dreadnought, Chiata's Venator-class Star Destroyer crashed onto the planet Zeffo. Chiata and Marseph both survived the crash, along with some of their men, but were separated. Chiata was found by her clone commander, but Order 66 was executed just as he did and she was forced to kill him in self-defense before being attacked by more clone troopers. Though she reunited with Marseph and mounted a brief defense, Chiata was fatally wounded, dying of her injuries. Marseph then buried her among the wreckage before dying of his own wounds. She wielded two blue-bladed lightsabers.

Chiata first appeared, albeit only audibly, in the 2019 video game Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order, developed by EA's Respawn Entertainment. Chiata shares her character model with multiple other Jedi enemies.

entities.name: Chiba
entities.description:
Chiba was a female Human who lived on the planet Lanteeb during the Clone Wars, a galactic conflict between the Republic and the Separatists.

Around 21 BBY, Chiba and the villagers from Torbel were visited by the Confederacy of Independent Systems under the command of General Lok Durd who was planning to test his new bioweapon. However, when Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi and Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker arrived to warn the villagers and the miners about the Separatist's plan, Chiba followed their instructions and made the majority of other residents to flee the mine. In the ensuing attack, the entire village was destroyed. After the battle ended, Queen Jamillia offered the people of Torbel sanctuary on Naboo. Agreeing to leave, Chiba and the other survivors were taken off-world and traveled to their new home planet.

entities.name: Chie
entities.description:
Chie was a female individual who was an aunty by the time that twenty years had passed since the Sith rebellion. She worked as a bounty hunter and claimed to only take jobs that involved fighting Jedi knights. As a believer in the gods and the Force, she was opposed to any being who used the Force for selfish ends, whether Jedi or Sith. When she journeyed with the Traveler and Ekiya on the latter's starship, the Poor Crow, Chie was secretly spying on behalf of the Traveler's former master, the Jedi lord Hanrai.

Chie appeared in the 2021 non-canon novel Ronin: A Visions Novel, by Emma Mieko Candon. Candon likened the character to a Buddhist nun, the legendary creature tengu and Benkei, a historical warrior-monk popular in Japanese history and storytelling.

entities.name: Chilla
entities.description:
A female Imperial agent posed as Chilla, an undercover agent of the Alliance to Restore the Republic, after the latter's cover was discovered.

Soon after the Battle of Yavin, an Alliance to Restore the Republic agent known as Chilla worked as a bartender in The Rusty Bucket, a bar in the city of Takari, on Iyuta. Chilla's cover was discovered by the Empire; wounded, she hid in the planet's ancient sewer system where she eventually died.

The Empire replaced Chilla with a female impersonator, as part of a plot to discover the Rebel headquarters in the sector. This Chilla worked at The Giant Step, and was contacted by Green squad from Reekeene's Roughnecks when they were assigned to eavesdrop on a newly built Imperial Communications Center. She assisted them in their mission to maintain her cover, but Green squad discovered the real Chilla's corpse, ruining the impersonator's plan.

entities.description:
Myra Chimor was a female rebel pilot who was recruited into the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War against the Galactic Empire. She became a member of Rogue Squadron, commanded by Luke Skywalker. Chimor, however, was hot-headed and did not listen to orders, operating on her own rather than flying as part of the team.

Myra Chimor was set to appear in the comic story "Squad Goals, Part One," which was published in Star Wars Adventures (2020) 11 on October 20, 2021.

entities.name: Nimi Chireen
entities.description:
Nimi Chireen was a human female Resistance pilot from the planet Jaymir.

Nimi Chireen was recruited into the Resistance by Ello Asty alongside her brother Aarton. Chireen was held in reserve until after the Battle of Crait, when she rejoined the remaining Resistance fighters. Chireen was at the Resistance base and had just been assigned her own T-70 X-wing starfighter. Commander Poe Dameron believed she had great potential. After the Battle of Exegol and the destruction of Darth Sidious and the Sith Eternal, she joined in the victory celebrations.

Nimi Chireen first appeared in the 2019 film Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker, the third and final installment of the Star Wars sequel trilogy. She was played by British actor Mimi Ndiweni, who was credited as "Resistance Officer". The character's first name is a tuckerization to the actor's first name and was revealed in Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary, written by Pablo Hidalgo and published alongside the flim on December 19, 2019.

Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

entities.name: Chirita
entities.description:
Chirita was an Ewok female who lived in the Bright Tree Village on the Forest Moon of Endor. In 3 ABY, she participated in the fight against the Imperial Doctor Raygar's droids, although she was no match for them and was defeated.

During the Ewok Warrior Games, Chirita defeated the Ewok Weechee Warrick in wrestling. Afterward, the young Wicket Warrick, who had a crush on Chirita, attempted to talk with her, suggesting that the two go on a canoe ride. However, Chirita did not take his advances seriously.

A wokling Ewok named Malani, who had a crush on Wicket, devised a plan to make him think that she was a warrior girl just like Chirita was. However, it went awry, and Malani ended up hanging onto a tree for her life, though she was saved by Chirita. Later that day, Wicket walked up to Chirita, inquiring about the canoe ride he had discussed with her. However, Chirita went with Weechee instead.

Chirita was an Ewok female member of an Ewok tribe she attended the Bright Tree Fête carnival on the Forest Moon of Endor. She and fellow Ewok Asha stood behind the adult Ewok Paploo as he attempted to smash a circular object by launching a piece of wood into the air with a hammer. The attempt was successful.

entities.description:
Chita was a human female smuggler. During the Imperial Era, she was hired to bring Arluu, a prince being pursued by the Galactic Empire, to safety.

Chita first appeared in "The Smuggler," a non-canon short film directed by Masahiko Otsuka that released as part of the third volume of the Star Wars: Visions series. The animated short, produced by TRIGGER, released on Disney+ on October 29, 2025. The character was first introduced at the Star Wars: Visions panel at Celebration Japan on April 19, 2025. She is voiced by Ami Maeshima in the original Japanese version and by Emma Myers in the English dub.

Chloa was a human female who lived in the city of Tavuu on the planet Radhii at the time Emperor Palpatine was reported dead and the second Death Star was destroyed.

She was a mother and wife of Gorlan Seba who was an expert guide of the Zoess, a large forest. Her husband was forced to lead a team of Imperials after Rebels who escaped imprisonment through the Zoess forest.

entities.name: Nas Choka's seer
entities.description:
This Yuuzhan Vong priestess served as the warrior-seer of Warmaster Nas Choka in the prelude to the Defense of Mon Calamari. She was greatly concerned about Supreme Overlord Shimrra's order to attack Mon Calamari, openly saying that Shimrra was deranged in Choka's command grotto. While Choka himself was sympathetic, he warned the seer to be cautious about what she said outside the grotto. She also talked with the Royal Seers, saying that they would stretch the truth about when to attack to give Choka more time.

entities.name: Chokla
entities.description:
Chokla was a Human female member of the Five, a small evil-worshipping cult that lived within the remote section of space known as the Hellhoop. Chokla and her compatriots spent centuries torturing and killing visitors to the Hellhoop—notably, the Five captured and imprisoned Wutzek, the last known living Force demon. Sometime between 0 and 3 ABY, Chokla—who was romantically involved with fellow Five member Chell—and her group captured Rebel leaders Han Solo, Leia Organa and Chewbacca, preparing to kill them for their amusement as they had so many wayward travelers. However, Chewbacca managed to release Wutzek from its prison, and the demon responded in kind by slaughtering every member of the Five. Chokla witnessed the gruesome death of her lover Chell, before being killed herself.

Chokla appeared in The Pandora Effect, a 1981 comic story written by Alan Moore and published in The Empire Strikes Back Monthly 151. In the story, Chokla was drawn by Adolfo Buylla.

entities.name: Olia Choko
entities.description:
Olia Choko was a female Pantoran who served in the Alliance to Restore the Republic and later the New Republic as the public relations representative between Chancellor Mon Mothma and the Galactic Senate. During a news broadcast that took place before the first official meeting of the new Galactic Senate, she spoke to the galaxy about a need for peace and reform. One angry citizen threw rotten fruit at her, but she brought him on camera and spoke to him about his needs, asking him to present his case to the Galactic Senate where they could take care of his people's needs. She also saw a New Republic soldier parading around Imperial prisoners, so she reprimanded him to show the galaxy that the New Republic would be nothing like the Galactic Empire before it.

Olia Choko was a female Pantoran who lived during the Age of the Empire and the rise of the New Republic. Choko was a member of the Alliance to Restore the Republic by the time of the Battle of Yavin. In order to turn the Alliance victory over the Galactic Empire into a propaganda campaign, Chancellor Mon Mothma wrote a report to Minister of Education Tynnra Pamlo of the assets she had at her disposal. One asset was holographic footage of the medal ceremony of Luke Skywalker and Han Solo following the battle, though permissions had to be routed to Choko in communications.

Following the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY, Choko became the public relations representative for Chancellor Mon Mothma and the new Galactic Senate. While the Rebellion on Akiva was taking place, Choko was interviewed by the Queen of the Core Network journalist Tracene Kane and the Trandoshan cameraman Lug. This was the first broadcast of the new HoloNet channel.

When Kane noted her nervousness, Choko reassured her that she would be fine as a pretty alien. Choko made sure that Lug got a good shot of Hanna City, Chandrila's capital and the current headquarters of the Galactic Senate. Choko also told Kane and Lug to get a good shot of the stormtrooper helmet art installation in the city circle. Having sorted out the surroundings, Kane commenced the interview and Lug commenced filming.

entities.name: Aven Cholus
entities.description:
Aven Cholus was a Human Rebel infiltrator and pilot.

Aven Cholus was born on Pencael IV, daughter of a rich family. She was on good terms with her brother Senn, and both of them trained during their childhood to became pilots. The Cholus family wanted to send both of their children to the Imperial Academy. However, Aven was a firm believer in freedom, and could not stand to serve the Empire. She found a chance to join the Alliance to Restore the Republic and rejected her family to do so.

Aven became a pilot to infiltrator Scandium Team, under the leadership of lead pilot Jouffer Talamiin. During the battle of Gendrah-Narvin, Talamiin was injured and had to retire; Aven then replaced him as lead pilot.

Aven then fought against the Empire in the Battle of Fendry, and was awarded with the Alvace Star for leading her squadron out of a dangerous situation while chased by Imperial forces.

entities.name: Ledina Chott
entities.description:
Ledina Chott was a Human female who was a famous interplanetary pop singer who resided on Kuratooine. In 44 ABY, she had received various gifts from a mysterious man named Thadley Biolan, who was really known as corrupt Alliance General Stavin Thaal. Since Chott had physical similarities to all of Thaal's ex-wives, the General looked to Chott as a new mistress.

During Wraith Squadron's investigation into Thaal's guilt regarding his involvement with the Lecersen Conspiracy, they deduced that, as Biolan, he would retire from the military service and probably pick Chott as a potential wife. In response, one of the Wraiths, Trey Courser, wore a double disguise of Biolan over Thaal and he and a few of the other Wraiths kidnapped her from her home and drugged her before Thaal himself could meet her.

The next day, Courser and fellow Wraith Drikall Bessarah smuggled Chott's unconscious form to the Kuratooine warehouse where Thaal performed some of his criminal operations. From there, after the two Wraiths dealt with security, they activated Chott's emergency transponder so that the local Kura City Guard could save her; this way, Thaal could be framed for kidnapping Chott, though they weren't counting on him actually being convicted for their crime.

By the time she was kidnapped, Ledina Chott had been a pop star for about two years, yet she wasn't jaded and used to the life of a celebrity yet. She was also annoyed that her home on Kuratooine would feature holos and stills of her works only and not of works of some of the celebrities she liked. Her facial resemblance to the template that General Stavin Thaal loves made her a potential wife to him, which was why he sent her gifts as Thadley Biolan.

entities.description:
Chouch was a female human who served as a colonel within the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Following the Battle of Hoth, Chouch was in command of the Ground Defense Command protecting the Alliance Fleet Eleventh Division that was grounded on Ab Dalis. After dispatching a message for reinforcements, a corporal informed her that Starlight Squadron had come to their rescue.

entities.name: Christya
entities.description:
Christya was a Human female who met the Galactic Republic soldier Revan in the Upper City Cantina on the planet Taris in 3956 BBY. After being impressed by Revan's pazaak skills, Christya offered to buy him drinks. Revan accepted, but as Christya made her way to the bar, she met a Tarisian noble and left the cantina with him instead.

Christya was a Human female who lived around the time of the Jedi Civil War. She was present on the Outer Rim Territories planet Taris

During her time on Taris, Christya conversed with the Galactic Republic soldiers Revan and Carth Onasi in the Upper City Cantina, telling them about her interest in pazaak. Christya was impressed when Revan defeated Niklos, a local pazaak champion, in a match, praising Revan's wealth and good looks. She suggested that they go to the bar and buy some drinks for twenty credits. Revan handed her the money eagerly, and Christya began to move to the bar, telling him not to take too long. However, on her way through the cantina, Christya met a Tarisian noble, and ignoring her deal with Revan, she began flirting with him. Although Revan attempted to interrupt, she eventually left the cantina with the noble to go to his mansion, leaving Revan twenty credits short.

Christya felt exhilarated when watching pazaak, praising the game's players, depth, and stakes. She enjoyed the company of rich and prominent men, such as nobles, but found poorer men uninteresting. She was used to life's luxuries and expected men to provide her with nothing less. Christya also described herself as an impatient woman. She had blonde hair, brown eyes, and light skin.

entities.name: Chrysalla
entities.description:
Chrysalla was the near-Human Tieress of the planet Ventooine for a period during the reign of the Galactic Empire. As Tieress, Chrysalla lived a life of luxury as the favored ward of the reigning annual Satab. Despite her high station, Chrysalla languished as a captive, trapped and repulsed by the Satab's cruelty. When the mysterious offworlder Han Solo visited Ventooine and saved her life, Chrysalla fell in love with him, and the two began a brief affair. When the Satab plotted to give the Corellian his Shadeshine stone, which would grant him incredible powers but also doom him to an early death, Chrysalla intervened to stop him. She vanquished the Satab by touching the stone herself and receiving its power. When this was accomplished, she entered a state of suspended animation and never saw Solo again.

A female member of the non-Human species native to Ventooine, Chrysalla grew up a peasant on the planet, living a hand-to-mouth existence little different from the world's other oppressed inhabitants. That changed when she came to the attention of the reigning Satab. The Satabs held absolute power over the lives of everyone on Ventooine, due to the mental and physical powers derived from the stone called the Shadeshine. So when the Satab chose Chrysalla to be his Tieress, a favored ward of the ruler, she had no choice but to join him in the sprawling palace in the city of Goyoikin.

The Satab gave Chrysalla a pampered life in exchange for her companionship. She enjoyed every comfort in the palace, a position of honor at court, and the pomp of a royal entourage whenever she traveled about. These luxuries drew the ire of Ventooine's oppressed common folk, but they also made her captivity somewhat tolerable. So did the knowledge that it was temporary: the Shadeshine that gave power to the Satabs also took a toll on their bodies, resulting in an agonizing death known as "burnout." To avoid this, the Satabs ruled for only a single year, after which they would retreat to suspended animation in the Hall of Satabs. Even as Chrysalla did what she could to tolerate or enjoy her year as Tieress, she longed for freedom and for genuine love.

On one occasion, Chrysalla and her attendants were traveling through the streets of Goyoikin. Human offworlder Han Solo approached the procession, hoping to use it to escape from an crowd of angry Ventooinians chasing him from a nearby bar. Solo was threatening some of the guards with his blaster, trying to conceal himself among Chrysalla's entourage, when a pair of local insurgents dropped a bomb from a nearby rooftop hoping to assassinate the Tieress. Solo spotted the bomb as it fell and, reacting quickly, shot it in midair.

entities.name: Sowa Chuan
entities.description:
Sowa Chuan, also known as Ilka, was a female Abednedo whom Agent Terex of the First Order Security Bureau employed as a servant aboard the Carrion Spike. Ilka served Terex his drinks.

Sowa Chuan was the wife of the Resistance technician Oddy Muva. She was kidnapped and enslaved by the First Order in order to exert leverage on her husband. In order to keep Chuan alive, Muva was forced to work as a spy for Terex. Muva reported on Poe Dameron and Black Squadron's missions to Ovanis, Megalox Beta, and Kaddak. Chuan was part of a harem of slaves from various alien species who were kept as hostages by Terex aboard his personal starship Carrion Spike.

When Terex received his assignment from Captain Phasma to recover the data that Dameron had Stolen from Senator Erudo Ro-Kiintor during Operation: Sabre Strike, Chuan was present and served her master Wookiee–brewed brandy with Kessel spice. She and the other slaves withdrew when Terex requested that he have time to speak privately with Phasma. Chuan was later present at the bridge of the Carrion Spike when Terex ordered the First Order crew to attack Megalox space station and the escaping shuttles. When she tried to speak, Terex addressed her as Ilka and told her to keep his glass full.

Sowa and a female humanoid slave stood behind Terex's throne aboard the Carrion Spike bridge when his First Order crew informed him that their repairs were nearly complete. Terex then retreated to his private chamber. When the humanoid slave asked Terex if there was anything they could do for him, Terex insisted on being left alone and pointed his blaster at them.

entities.name: Riyo Chuchi
entities.description:
Riyo Chuchi was a female Pantoran politician who represented the moon Pantora in the Senates of the Galactic Republic and its successor state, the Galactic Empire, from the Clone Wars to the early reign of the Empire. Young, insecure, and timid at the start of her career, Chuchi grew into an outspoken and strong leader during the Clone Wars, upholding her ideals and challenging her enemies in efforts to maintain a fair and just government. By the time of the Empire, Chuchi resolved to use her position of power to protect the rights of the former soldiers of the Grand Army of the Republic, which had been comprised of commissioned clone troopers. Hoping to defend and represent the voiceless in the Imperial Senate, Chuchi positioned herself as a roadblock to the Empire's early plans for military expansion.

When first elected to represent her people in the Republic Senate, the idealistic Chuchi was marginalized and treated as a mouthpiece by Pantora's belligerent and militaristic Supreme Chairman, Chi Cho. When the Pantorans learned that one of their protectorate planets, Orto Plutonia, was inhabited by the primitive Talz, Chuchi was forced to balance her loyalty to the Pantoran Assembly and the Republic as Cho prepared for war with the Talz. Overcoming her fealty to Cho, who was fatally wounded in battle, Chuchi negotiated peace with the Talz tribal leader Thi-Sen, ending Cho's One-Day War. Forging a mutually respectful relationship with Cho's successor, Notluwiski Papanoida, Chuchi returned to the Senate as a stronger politician. Together with Papanoida, Chuchi later helped resolve a dispute between Pantora and the Trade Federation, culminating in her successfully forcing the Federation to lift a blockade from their world.

At the end of the Clone Wars, the Republic was transformed into the Galactic Empire, and Chuchi continued to serve in the now-Imperial Senate. As the Empire sought to transition away from Republic-era assets, Chuchi became a strong supporter for the clone troopers of the former Republic Military and opposed the Imperial Defense Recruitment Bill, which would force their discharge. Chuchi found an enemy in the bill's strongest supporter, Admiral Rampart of the Imperial Navy, however, but uncovered evidence that Rampart had taken part in the destruction of the Kamino cloning facilities to make the clones obsolete. Despite being targeted for assassination by Rampart, Chuchi was able to present evidence of Rampart's crimes to the Senate, leading to his arrest, but her efforts to stop the bill's passage backfired when Emperor Sheev Palpatine manipulated the situation to push for the replacement of the clone armies with conscripted stormtroopers. After her help in uncovering the truth about Kamino, Chuchi assisted with the Clone Underground.

At some point prior to or during the Clone Wars, Riyo Chuchi attained the rank of senator and represented her homeworld of Pantora in the Galactic Senate; though she shared her rather young age with fellow senators Padmé Amidala and Mon Mothma, she was rather timid and soft-spoken in comparison.

entities.name: Ta'a Chume
entities.description:
Ta'a Chume was the Queen Mother of the Hapes Consortium during the first part of the Galactic Civil War, the mother of Isolder, and the grandmother of Tenel Ka Djo. As the ruler of the Hapes Consortium, she was responsible for opening up the borders of the Hapes Cluster to the rest of the galaxy in 8 ABY.

As a ruler concerned only with her position, Ta'a Chume had no qualms about killing people to protect herself and/or the monarchy, including going so far as to arrange the assassinations of her firstborn son, her younger son's fiancée, and her daughter-in-law. Despite being placed under house arrest for the murder of the latter, she had arranged an assassination attempt on her newborn great-granddaughter Allana in 36 ABY. In retaliation, Jacen Solo, Allana's father, used the Force to give her a brain hemorrhage that sent her into a coma.

Ta'a Chume was the daughter of Ni'Korish, and had the company of several sisters while growing up. Details of her early life are scarce, but it was known that Ni'Korish's hatred of the Jedi was a large influence on her.

Upon the death of her mother, Ta'a Chume became the Queen Mother, the absolute monarch of the Hapes Consortium. She took a consort, and they had two sons, Kalen and Isolder. Her consort died while their children were still young.

entities.name: Chellemi Chuovvick
entities.description:
Chellemi Chuovvick was a female Jedi Knight serving the Jedi Order during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

Chellemi Chuovvick, as a Force-sensitive, was trained at the Coruscant Jedi Temple. She eventually graduated from the academy and was selected by a Jedi Master to train as a Padawan. After completing her Jedi Trials, Chuovvick was raised to the rank of Jedi Knight by the Jedi High Council.

During her time as a Knight, Chuovvick was partnered with fellow Jedi Empatojayos Brand and Bultar Swan and dispatched to the war-torn Sepan system as part of the third Jedi team sent to negotiate peace in the endless civil war. Negotiations dragged on for a month, bringing about a short-lived peace. Following the Jedi's departure however, the world erupted back into violence as debate raged on whether to secede from the Galactic Republic and join the Confederacy of Independent Systems. A fourth team was expected to replace Chuovvick and the other Jedi in order to end the fighting permanently.

entities.name: Churabba
entities.description:
Churabba was a female Hutt with a cunning business mind who led a diplomatic mission to the planet Kintan during the Xim Wars.

By the time of her mission, Hutt efforts in the Si'Klaata Cluster had already recruited the Klatooinians and the Vodrans to their side in the conflict. Convincing the more technologically sophisticated Nikto of Kintan to serve the Hutts was more challenging. However, Churabba realized that the Cult of M'dweshuu that ruled Kintan was feared by the Nikto people, and that the Hutts would be seen as saviors if the Cult's hold on the Nikto was broken. It was believed that she admired the Cult for its ability to galvanize the Nikto people, even as she sought to destroy it and bring the Nikto into the Hutt Empire. She ordered that the Cult's main headquarters be bombarded from orbit, killing off many of their leaders and leaving the Nikto people without a strong leadership. The Nikto then signed their support over to her and to the Hutts.

Most of the Riflemen, including Vlaydm, were wiped out and the survivors regrouped on Turcan III. Maydla became their new leader and she aligned the group with the Alliance to Restore the Republic.

entities.name: Chussido
entities.description:
Chussido was a Rodian female native to the planet Rodia who served as a member of Enfys Nest's Cloud-Riders gang. In 10 BBY, Chussido was amongst the Cloud-Riders who traveled to the planet Savareen with Nest in order to try and acquire coaxium fuel from a crew of criminals working for the Crimson Dawn syndicate. Nest successfully convinced all of the crew bar its leader, Tobias Beckett, to aid her and the others in stealing the coaxium from Crimson Dawn and killing the syndicate's leader, Dryden Vos.

Chussido and the other Cloud-Riders then laid a trap, while the outlaw Han Solo and his allies took the coaxium to Vos on his yacht, the First Light. Believing the coaxium Solo had brought him to be fake, Vos sent his mercenaries out to capture Nest and her allies, who he believed had the real coaxium. Chussido and the other Cloud-Riders then ambushed the mercenaries and defeated them, allowing Solo and his allies to kill Vos. Solo then returned the coaxium to Nest, Chussido and the other Cloud-Riders.

Chussido eventually joined the Bounty Hunters' Guild sometime after serving the Cloud-Riders, where she resided in a cantina on Nevarro. She was killed while attempting to reclaim The Child from The Mandalorian.

Chussido was a Rodian female who joined up with the rebellious Cloud-Riders gang under the leadership of Enfys Nest after her homeworld of Rodia was brutalized by one of the Five Crime Syndicates. In 10 BBY, Nest led a small group of the Cloud Riders in an attempt to steal a shipment of coaxium fuel from the Galactic Empire on the planet Vandor; however, their plans were thwarted by a crew of criminals led by Tobias Beckett and associated with the Crimson Dawn syndicate, who also attempted to steal the coaxium and destroyed it in the process.

entities.name: Kimmi Chyler
entities.description:
Kimmi Chyler, cousin of Tian Chyler, was the most successful female swoop racer during the Galactic Civil War.

Originally from Corellia, Chyler had outraced both Han Solo and Dengar on Agrilat Swamp Circuit. Her success on the swoop track led her to develop a certain arrogant attitude regarding her skills.

During one of the championships Chyler had hired Dash Rendar, captain of the Outrider, to provide transport for herself and her team. The Alliance to Restore the Republic had also contacted Rendar about transporting valuable cargo as he moved from race to race on different planets. After an encounter with an Imperial Security Bureau on Lok, where the first race of the season, the Lok Marathon was being held - Rendar was forced to hire an additional security for himself and his ship.

During the travel from Lok to Rori Chyler had shown her sabacc skills, when she played - and robbed every credit of Rendar's bodyguard companion. She had won the Narmle Memorial Rally, but when she and Rendar returned to Outrider landing pad, they witnessed signs of a struggle. Even though Rendar immediately became cautious about who tried to get aboard his ship, Chyler was unconcerned.

entities.name: Tian Chyler
entities.description:
Tian Chyler was a Human female who served the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Initially a member of the Galactic Empire's Sub-Adult Group, Chyler was selected by her superiors for training from the Imperial Security Bureau. After completing her training, she was tasked with rooting out Rebel Alliance sympathizers within Imperial Center's law enforcement community. She did so skillfully, and was given a more important role: the infiltration of Bespin's mining guilds, to investigate the possibility of any unregistered Tibanna gas mining.

Posing as a Corellian official fleeing from Ando, Chyler soon discovered that Bespin's Cloud City harbored a considerable amount of under-the-table mining. Reporting her findings to the Sith Lord Darth Vader, she was promised a promotion by her superiors in the Bureau. Unfortunately for Chyler, an uprising amongst Aqualish miners led her to be reprimanded for not being able to keep the employees in check. She never received her promotion, and, growing frustrated with the Empire, she defected to the Alliance.

Cousin of the famous swoop racer Kimmi Chyler, the Human female Tian Chyler was a member of the Imperial Sub-Adult Group, where she displayed a streak of ruthlessness and pragmatism that attracted the attention of the Sub-Adult Group leaders. They, in turn, sent her to the Imperial Security Bureau for training. Although most who made the transition from the Sub-Adult Group to the Imperial Security Bureau were dismissed as zealots, Chyler's results silenced her detractors. Once she had completed her training, she successfully infiltrated Imperial Center's law enforcement community, tracking down and ferreting out Rebel spies.

Her superiors were pleased, and they noticed that she had a particular skill for blending in with her surroundings. Chyler was subsequently tasked with a more significant mission: investigating unregistered Tibanna gas mining operations on Bespin. She was instructed to masquerade as a Corellian mining official from Ando who had been able to escape the Imperial occupation of the world. Chyler was to claim that she was seeking sanctuary at Cloud City alongside Andoan officials and Aqualish workers. Cloud City was more than happy to receive them, and put them to work in the Cloud City Miner's Guild,

entities.name: Cia Ferisc
entities.description:
Cia Ferisc was a Silinese warrior who, when she was between the ages of fifteen and twenty-five, participated in that year's Crowning Convocation. During the survival level of the competition, Ferisc snuck up on Jedi Padawan Yord Fandar, a fellow participant. Fandar was distracted while planning a way to get fruit from a uavin tree without being able to use the Force.

Posing as a potential ally, the Silinese tricked Fandar into letting his guard down under the false pretense of helping one another get fruit. She then stole his makeshift staff and fled. As Fandar pursued her through the forest, he was soon joined by his friend Sitia Arthyst. The latter eventually caught Ferisc, tackling her. Ferisc lost the resulting fight, effectively ending her prospects in the competition. Her supplies were subsequently looted by Fandar and Arthyst. This upset Ferisc, and she threw scathing words at Arthyst, though her insults had minimal effect on the other Silinese.

entities.description:
Cianba was a journalist during the start of the Yuuzhan Vong War and covered the creation of the Outer Rim Alliance. She belonged to a felinoid species covered with black fur, feline eyes, long ears, whiskers, and sharp teeth. She was considered a rogue journalist for questioning the New Republic's lack of action against the Yuuzhan Vong. Many refugees, like those on the Dibrook Space Station, listened to her HoloNet speeches for news about their homes and missing people.

entities.name: Cilghal
entities.description:
Cilghal was a female Mon Calamari Jedi Master who served the New Jedi Order and also a former senator of the New Republic Senate. She was one of the first students at Luke Skywalker's Jedi Praxeum and a skilled healer. Tekli, a young female Chadra-Fan, was Cilghal's Jedi apprentice. Cilghal was later a member of the Jedi High Council and the most skilled member of the Order in the healing arts.

A niece of Admiral Gial Ackbar, Cilghal was an ambassador to the New Republic. She helped Leia Organa Solo locate Ackbar when the admiral retreated to his homeworld after the disaster on Vortex in 11 ABY. She also showed Leia the Startide while it was under construction. Under the ocean, she showed Leia the Knowledge Bank. After the two women located Ackbar in his personal seapod, Imperial Admiral Daala attacked Dac.

As Ackbar led the defense, Cilghal was able to predict who would die in the battle, and during the ensuing triage, which patients were injured beyond saving. Leia identified Cilghal as a Force-sensitive and sent her to Luke Skywalker's Jedi Praxeum on Yavin 4, where Cilghal trained as a Jedi healer. Although not one of the original twelve students, Cilghal was one of the first graduating class of Jedi Knights. While there, she constructed her lightsaber with an Ultima-Pearl from her homeworld. When a poisonous drink almost killed Chief of State Mon Mothma, Cilghal healed her through the Force.

Cilghal went on to become Mon Calamari's senator. In 19 ABY, she attended the wedding of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade and supported their appeal to the Senate concerning the Diversity Alliance. Later she helped the young Jedi Knights Jacen and Jaina Solo and their friends destroy a large stash of illegal spice.

entities.name: Cimina
entities.description:
Lady Cimina was a Tholothian female who visited the Halcyon with her grandfather, Shorr Komrrin. When they arrived onboard the MPO-1400 Purgill-class star cruiser was attacked by the pirate Crimson Jack.

During the First Order-Resistance War, Cimina and her grandfather, Shorr Komrrin, took a trip onboard the Corellian MPO-1400 Purgill-class star cruiser known as the Halcyon. Once on the ship, Cimina met Deethree-Ohnine, a droid that served aboard the Star Cruiser, and asked to see the Lightsaber Training Pod before being reminded by her grandfather that they should probably go to their cabin first in order to settle in. The Halcyon was eventually attacked by a group of pirates lead by Crimson Jack. Seeing Crimson Jack's starship on her window, Cimina started to get worried but D3-O9 comfort her by telling her that the Halcyon had already faced way more dangerous situations before, the droid told the young lady about another attack on the Halcyon that occurred during the High Republic Era. After hearing the story, Cimina realized that Jack's ship started firing at them.

Despite it only being a warning shot, Cimina still expressed her fears to her grandfather. Crimson Jack contacted Captain Riyola Keevan and asked her to allow them to take a resistance spy that was inside the Halcyon. The Captain seemingly accepted when in reality she wanted the pirate ship to get closer so they could fire at it while they traveled right into a massive solar storm to avoid counter attacks. As the Halcyon approached the solar storm, Deethree-Ohnine told Cimina and her grandfather that they needed to move towards a muster station in order to avoid the radiation. The droid told Cimina another story from the Republic Era related to the star cruiser but once again all it did was confuse her.

While the Halcyon passed through the solar storm, Cimina told D3-O9 that the next story she tells should be one with action, romance and a Jedi. The droid then told the young lady a story about Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala. After the story, Cimina's grandfather told her that he'll be disembarking from the ship in order to deal with the pirates.

entities.name: Doum Cin

Doum Cin was a female Human Nightsister who lived on the planet Dathomir during the time of the Galactic Civil War. She was a follower of Axkva Min.

entities.name: Ardana Cinn
entities.description:
Ardana Cinn was a female Twi'lek. During the Galactic Civil War she became a pilot for the Alliance to Restore the Republic, where she scored the highest amongst her fellow pilots in flight simulations. She performed with enough skill and was deemed trustworthy enough to be selected by Leia Organa to be part of a team to uncover a mole within the Alliance. The team worked entirely off the books, with only Mon Mothma knowing of their existence outside of the team's members. As well as discovering the mole they were also tasked with finding a suitable planet on which the Alliance could set up a new base.

Ardanna Cinn first appeared in the second issue of the comic book series titled simply Star Wars published by Dark Horse Comics. The issue was written by Brian Wood, illustrated by Carlos D'Anda and colored by Gabe Eltaeb. It was released on February 13 2013.

Prior to the race, a racing guide that listed Cinnabar as Vermilion's dam was distributed; a copy of which was later collected by the Resistance mechanic Rose Tico and added to her diary while she was on a mission to Canto Bight in 34 ABY.

Cinnabar was mentioned in the 2018 replica journal The Last Jedi: Rose Tico: Resistance Fighter, written by Jason Fry.

entities.name: Cippa Tarko's mother
entities.description:
A female individual was the mother of the Arkanian Jedi youngling Cippa Tarko. After Jedi Master Yaddle felt a disturbance in the Force whilst on Dalna, Tarko noticed Yaddle's reaction and asked her what was wrong. After Yaddle told the youngling she was all right, Tarko remarked that she had heard about these kind of situations, and noted her mom called them doddery moments, which Tarko took to mean Yaddle was a lot older than she had realized. Sometime later, during the Night of Sorrow, Tarko saw the Leveler, a creature which consumed the life from Force-sensitives, and she became overwhelmed by fear and had several Force visions, including one of her parents screaming in torment.

entities.name: Cjaalysce
entities.description:
Lady Cjaalysce was a female colonist on Socorro and the daughter of Commander Leniel Beal who was responsible for the colonization of the planet. She fell in love with Jedi Knight Iann Doaba. However, he exiled himself into the Doaba Badlands after murdering a rival for her love. After his departure, she was filled with grief, and had a painting drawn of her which visibly showed her grief. The painting was named "Tejha Larel," which was Old Corellian for "Undying Love". She went into the Badlands to try to find Doaba, but died in the search. Doaba later found her corpse and died of grief. It was later rumored that Doaba's spirit haunted the painting.

entities.name: Taryn Clancy
entities.description:
Taryn Clancy was a Human female courier captain operating during the Galactic Civil War. Born in 16 BBY to Kal Clancy, captain of the starship Lassen, Taryn often tried to join his crew, once even resorting to stowing away, and he finally let her join as his copilot when she was sixteen. However, this led to a deterioration of their relationship. Later, she joined the Core Courier Service.

On her ship, the Messenger, Clancy regularly flew a delivery route between Coruscant and the planet Coriallis. On one such mission shortly after Grand Admiral Thrawn's campaign against the New Republic in 9 ABY, she and her first mate, Del Sato, were stranded on Coruscant during its bombardment by a newly resurgent Galactic Empire. As captain of one of several grounded civilian vessels, Clancy was brought to New Republic General Garm Bel Iblis, who had been tasked with coordinating the government's evacuation of Coruscant. Under Bel Iblis' orders, Clancy helped Colonel Jak Bremen, Director of Security for the New Republic Inner Council, to sneak past the Imperial fleet blockading the planet and bring important information to the New Republic fleet. During the eventful escape, Clancy not only had to contend with Imperial checkpoints and a homing beacon planted in her cargo hold, but the surly personality of Bremen himself.

Taryn Clancy was the daughter of Kal Clancy, a freighter pilot. From a young age, she dreamed of commanding her own ship, and constantly begged her father to let her accompany him on cargo runs. On one occasion, she stowed away in the cargo hold of Kal's ship, the Lassen, only to be discovered by a load lifter and returned home in shame.

In 0 ABY, Kal allowed Taryn, then 16, to accompany him on his trips. Despite the challenges inherent in serving aboard her father's ship, Taryn's determination eventually won her the formal position of copilot. All the while, however, her relationship with her father worsened. When she failed to live up to his expectations, he was disappointed, and made little effort to conceal his feelings. This had a profound effect on his daughter, and for years afterward she couldn't avoid judging herself the same way he had judged her.

entities.name: Randle Clanse
entities.description:
Randle Clanse was a female Brosin and a local hero on Brosi due to her role as founder and leader of the Brosin Underground.

Randle Clanse was a natural born Brosin, born between 25 BBY and 29 BBY.She was born in the rural areas north of the Shoengen Shores, in a small village near the Talbot Ridges. However, there are no official records of her birth.

When the Corporate Sector Authority decided to build three Zinsian processing plants on Brosi, displacing thousands of Brosins and "hiring" many young Brosins for dangerous mining work, Clanse decided to create the Brosin Underground: A paramilitary force using guerrilla tactics to harass the CSA facilities and troops on Brosi, attempting to force them off the planet.

The Underground began operating soon after the opening of the first plant, achieving instant popular support by the oppressed Brosins, due to Clanse's personal charisma and her decision to share with the people the profits stolen from the CSA.

entities.name: Clargod
entities.description:
Clargod was a female Trandoshan who worked as a bounty hunter during the waning years of the Galactic Republic.

During the time of the Clone Wars, Clargod and the bounty hunters Dee'Hars, Kelyan and Kiimo traveled to the city of Gadrin on the planet Cularin, planning to capture Mattenic and Kerkum, two former lieutenants of the Oblee crime lord Nirama. Clargod and the rest of the team claimed to be in the employ of the Office of Peace and Security, a law enforcement body that had placed a bounty on Mattenic and Kerkum. However, they were also working for Riboga the Hutt, who had recently seized control of crime in the Cularin system from Nirama, and the bounty hunters planned to get paid twice for capturing the pair. However, the Heroes of Cularin were also looking for Mattenic and Kerkum, and they prevented Clargod and the other bounty hunters from capturing the pair.

A short time afterward, the Heroes of Cularin destroyed Riboga's spice mining operation on the planet Kemix, so the Hutt hired Clargod, Dee'Hars, Kelyan and Kiimo to bring the heroes into a state of despair, and then kill them. The bounty hunters placed explosives aboard a starship that the heroes were traveling on and then detonated the devices, bringing the hero's craft out of hyperspace and causing it to crash on the planet Holador. The bounty hunters landed on the world and Clargod took up a position in a valley, with some sentry droids that were under her command. The heroes eventually made their way into the valley and Clargod offered to make a deal with them, whereby she would fight them all individually in unarmed combat, rather than simply attacking them all at the same time. The heroes engaged her in combat and defeated her, and they eventually made it off Holador.

entities.name: Clariah
entities.description:
Clariah was a female Nautolan and old acquaintance of Lando Calrissian. She had a son, named Jiandy.

Clariah came to visit Lando Calrissian while he was the leader of Cloud City, bringing her son Jiandy with her. She sat down to talk with Lando, and explained to him that Jiandy's recent behavior was concerning her: he had been skipping school, spending time with suspicious people, and had expressed a desire to someday lead a criminal empire like Jabba the Hutt. Clariah revealed that she had one of Lando's favorite capes, which he thought he had lost, and promised she would give it back to him if he helped Jiandy see the error of his ways. At first, Lando refused, but when he saw Jiandy cheat at a game of cards and then trick his opponents into fighting each other, he changed his mind and agreed to do it.

After Lando successfully convinced Jiandy to give up his dreams of being a gangster, Clariah came to talk to him again. As promised, she gave Lando his cape back, but expressed her concern that kids like Jiandy would continue to be tempted to a life of crime.

Clariah was a female Nautolan with blue skin and large black eyes. She had circles of darker blue around her eyes and bands of lighter blue on the tendrils on her head.

entities.description:
Claris was a member of a New Republic Intelligence team sent to aid in the liberation of Verkuyl. She worked with the Verkuylian resistance to set explosives around Verkuyls main communications transmitter to cut off the Imperials from outside aid. The transmission she sent to the New Republic fleet in waiting was captured by the Imperials resulting in her arrest. She survived the mission and was released after the fleet was contacted by Selby Jarrad and Verkuyl was liberated.

entities.name: Clarr'os'culry
entities.description:
Captain Clarr'os'culry, known by the core name Roscu and later by the appellation The One They Could Not Kill, was a Chiss female and member of the Clarr family. She served aboard the Parala in her time in the Chiss Expansionary Defense Fleet along with Senior Commander Mitth'raw'nuruodo (Core name "Thrawn") and Captain Irizi'ar'alani. Soon after the pirate attack at the Garwian world of Stivic, she resigned her post in the Expansionary Defense Fleet and joined her family's fleet as the captain of the Orisson. During her time in the family fleet, she met Generalirius Nakirre and "Jixtus," and also helped Thrawn in his efforts against the Grysk fleet, eventually receiving the offer to become the Venturous and Admiral Dy'lothe's Second Officer.

Between around 39 BBY and 19 BBY, Mid Captain Clarr'os'culry (Roscu) served alongside Senior Commander Mitth'raw'nuru Thrawn and Senior Captain Irizi'ar'alani (Ziara) aboard the Parala. At some point during Roscu's post aboard the warship, the Parala picked up an urgent distress call from Security Officer Frangelic of the Garwian Unity, stating that they were being attacked by pirates at the Garwian colony world of Stivic (specifically, the orbiting merchant-hub station). Thrawn was in temporary command of the bridge when the Parala received this message, and, convinced that the pirates were Lioaoin, decided to respond to the distress signal. Roscu verbally berated Thrawn for responding, citing the Chiss preemptive strikes protocols and stating that the Ascendancy does not interfere with aliens. After they arrived, Roscu stated that there were a couple of nice cafés on that station. Ziara sent Roscu to check the electrostatic barriers, and during Roscu's absence, Thrawn tells Ziara that he can defeat the Lioaoi pirates without causing any damage to the Parala. Ar'alani refuses to allow the Parala to engage in the battle, but, overcome by empathy, she allows Thrawn to covertly send a signal to the Garwians detailing the Lioaoi tactics and how to defeat them. She sends Thrawn off of the bridge to "check the ranging lasers". After Thrawn left the bridge, Roscu asked Ziara if she was getting Thrawn off the bridge. When Ziara responds by stating that she sent him to check the weapons sensor systems, Roscu hopes that the Parala is not able to go into battle, again citing the preemptive strike protocols. Suddenly, the battle changes. The Garwians change their tactics and are able to defeat the Lioaoin pirates. After the conclusion of the battle, Ziara asked Roscu if she was relieved, as the cafés that Roscu feared that could be destroyed were still in business.
