entities.name: Razik
entities.description:
Razik was a male Sith Lord who served the resurgent Empire during the Cold War and the Galactic War. A pale-skinned Human with red-orange eyes and short black hair in a double stripe hairstyle, Razik made use of a double-bladed lightsaber and armored robes in combat. When the Galactic Republic joined the Balmorran resistance in their attempt to drive the Empire off the planet Balmorra in 3642 BBY, Razik was stationed in the Balmorran Arms Factory during the battle to protect a cloaking device prototype.

However, the Jedi Knight known as the Hero of Tython and the medic Doc raided the factory to recover the device. When the pair copied research data from a terminal and set off an alarm, Razik and their soldiers entered the room and attacked the two in an unsuccessful attempt to stop the Hero from reaching the device, resulting in the Imperials' deaths.

Lord Razik appeared in Star Wars: The Old Republic, a video game released by BioWare and LucasArts on December 20, 2011. Razik appears in the Jedi Knight mission "Spoils of War" on Balmorra, where they attempt to stop the player and Doc from reaching the cloaking device.

Renning was a corpulent male Human Sith Lord and the Sith Master of Malora and Dominique who had many resources made available to him by the Dark Council so that he could further the Sith knowledge. During the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the resurgent Sith Empire, his apprentice thought he was wasting the Empire's time and attempted to sabotage one of his tuk'ata experiments. Renning was displeased by her action toward his experiments and tortured her by releasing a bolt of Force lightning as punishment.

Renning was killed when a Republic strike team was sent to secure Sith datacrons and artifacts on Korriban.

entities.name: Sadic
entities.description:
Sadic was a Human male Sith Lord of the reconstituted Sith Empire during the Cold War with the Galactic Republic. Born to low-class parents, Sadic's Force-sensitivity gained him admission to the Sith Academy on the planet Korriban, and he orchestrated the deaths of many rival acolytes at the Academy before he became the apprentice and personal assassin of the Sith Lord Umbriss. After Umbriss was killed by his superior Darth Angral, Sadic became Angral's apprentice, and he achieved the rank of Sith Lord alongside his fellows Praven and Nefarid. When Angral's son, Tarnis, was killed by a Jedi Knight in 3643 BBY, Sadic was sent to the moon of Nar Shaddaa to take control of the Republic's Power Guard supersoldier project as part of Angral's war of vengeance against the Republic. Willingly undergoing the Power Guard process himself in order to gain further power, Sadic planned to fashion an army of Power Guards from the throngs of refugees who made Nar Shaddaa their home, but he was killed before his plans could come to fruition by the same Jedi Knight who had killed Tarnis.

A male Human, which caused him to be sent off to the Sith Academy on the planet Korriban. Sadic was the only acolyte in his entire group to survive the trials on Korriban, as he murdered many of his fellow apprentices and other Academy residents during his time there. He was never suspected of the crimes, however, and the murders only stopped when Sadic finally left the planet to become the apprentice of the Sith Lord Umbriss. Sadic served as Umbriss's personal assassin for several years until Umbriss incurred the wrath of the more powerful Sith Darth Angral and was killed for his transgressions. Angral acquired Sadic along with Umbriss' estate and the rest of his wealth, and although Sadic pledged eternal loyalty to Angral, the elder Sith recognized that Sadic would likely kill him if given the chance and kept him on a tight leash.

In 3643 BBY, Sadic entered into a holoconference with Angral and Angral's son, Tarnis, along with the Sith Lord's other apprentices, Praven and Nefarid. Angral and his apprentices were using a secret Imperial facility on the planet Ord Mantell to contact Tarnis, while Tarnis was on the Republic capital of Coruscant, where he had abandoned his undercover assignment of posing as a Republic scientist in order to steal the Planet Prison superweapon and use it against Coruscant. Tarnis was setting up the weapon in the depths of the ruined Jedi Temple, and he was informing his father and Angral's apprentices of the success of his mission when a young Jedi Knight arrived with the Padawan Kira Carsen. Amused to see how Tarnis had failed to eliminate his Jedi pursuers, Sadic mocked Tarnis for his failure to wrap up loose ends, and he watched along with Angral and the others as Tarnis engaged the two Jedi in a duel. However, Tarnis was struck down by the Knight in the fighting, and a furious Angral declared war on the Republic as a result.

Samus was a male Human Sith Lord and Sith Inquisitor who served the reconstituted Sith Empire during the Cold War against the Galactic Republic. He resided in the Sith Academy on the planet Korriban, where he provided martial training for Sith Acolytes. Samus had pale skin, green eyes and whilst in the academy had a bald head and wore red and black robes.

One acolyte he trained, who was directed to him by Assistant Overseer Markan, went on to become the Sith apprentice of Darth Zash, and eventually became Darth Nox.

Samus first appeared in the 2011 BioWare MMORPG Star Wars: The Old Republic, in which he played a part in the quest "A Fighting Chance". The quest was for the Sith Inquisitor class only and directed them to a class trainer, a role which Samus provided in the game.

entities.description:
The Zabrak male Sanorn earned the rank of Sith Lord within the Sith Empire during the Great Galactic War against the Galactic Republic. He worked on the space station known as Vaiken Spacedock, which was located within the Imperial fleet, where he sold equipment during the war to other Imperials. Working alongside other merchants in the supplies section of the station, Sanorn wore a black and white set of armor including a mask while working.

Sanorn was created for Star Wars: The Old Republic, an MMORPG released by BioWare in 2011. In the game he serves as an Imperial classic gear vendor within the Imperial fleet, and appears again in the same room as a Basic Gear vendor. He was later removed in Game Update 5.0 on November 29, 2016, which retired the PvP and PvE gear vendors in favor of the Command system.

entities.name: Scourge
entities.description:
Scourge was a pureblood Sith male who served as a Sith Lord of the reconstituted Sith Empire and later as the Emperor's Wrath, the personal enforcer of the Sith Emperor, before he allied with the Jedi Knight known as the Hero of Tython in order to prevent the Emperor from extinguishing all life in the galaxy. Born several decades before the Jedi Civil War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire under the Sith Lord Darth Revan, Scourge excelled during his time as a student at the Sith Academy on the Imperial capital of Dromund Kaas. After two years of service in the outer reaches of the Empire, Scourge was recalled to Dromund Kaas to uncover the person responsible for the recent string of assassination attempts against Darth Nyriss of the Empire's ruling Dark Council.

Scourge battled political intrigue and rivals in his search for the truth, and after he was led to believe that Nyriss's fellow Dark Councilor Darth Xedrix was responsible, he killed Xedrix—only to learn that Nyriss had manipulated him: The assignment had been a test of his loyalties. Nyriss revealed the existence of a conspiracy against the Emperor as she showed the younger Sith how the Emperor had stripped the Force from his own homeworld of Nathema and killed millions in order to become immortal. Convinced that the Emperor needed to be stopped, Scourge allied himself with the Jedi Masters Revan and Meetra Surik while planning to confront the Emperor—but when he witnessed the future and saw that it was another Jedi who was destined to destroy the Emperor, Scourge turned on his allies to ensure his own survival.

Rendered immortal and appointed as the Emperor's Wrath, Scourge served the Emperor loyally for over three centuries, killing the Emperor's enemies and carrying out his will. Not until the Galactic War began to break out between the Empire and the Republic did Scourge encounter the Hero of Tython, the Jedi from his vision, and set in motion his plans to aid the Jedi. Scourge watched as the Hero was forced to become a servant of the Emperor when a strike team of Jedi failed to capture the Sith ruler, but when the Hero broke free from the Emperor's control, Scourge betrayed the Sith to help the Jedi escape. Pledging his loyalty to the Hero, Scourge aided the Knight and the Jedi's crew in foiling the Emperor's plans to repeat the dark-side ritual that he had used to devastate Nathema but on a galactic scale. With Scourge's aid, the Hero defeated the Emperor's servants and vanquished the Sith ruler in a final confrontation, and Scourge was awarded the Republic's Cross of Glory for his role in stopping the Emperor's plans.

Serrok was a Sith Lord loyal to the Sith Empire during the Cold War between the Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic. He was stationed on the planet Alderaan during the war and during the civil war there, which took place during the Cold War, Serrok aided the Imperial aligned Noble House of Thul. He joined Thul troops lead by General Varus Thul, in the conquest of Fort Orrus, a stronghold of the Republic aligned House of Organa. Serrok and his men successfully destroyed the Fort's defenses and killed or captured the Organa troops garrisoned there.

Serrok was killed in the year 3643 BBY by Republic forces that reclaimed Fort Orrus for House Organa.

Serrok was a male Human who was Force-sensitive and often Force choked enemies in combat. He had white skin, black hair and yellow eyes.

entities.name: Shak'Weth
entities.description:
Shak'Weth was a Human Sith Lord and the Blademaster of the Odacer-Faustin Sith academy in the years preceding, during, and after the Great Galactic War. While all students were subject to his tutelage, he often gave private training sessions to a young Sith Acolyte named Rance Lussk, the academy's premier apprentice. Eight years after the Sacking of Coruscant, a virulent outbreak overtook the student populace of the Odacer-Faustin academy, and Shak'Weth prepared to depart as mayhem rapidly consumed the planet. However, just outside the academy, the Blademaster encountered a wandering Jedi named Rojo Trace, whom he proceeded to duel. When it seemed as though he would emerge victorious, Shak'Weth was unexpectedly attacked and viciously gored to death by a victim of the plague: the reanimated corpse of one of the very students he had trained in lightsaber combat.

Shak'Weth was a Force-sensitive Human male It was during that time that Shak'Weth allied with the Sith Empire and eventually became both a Master and Lord of the Sith. He excelled in lightsaber combat and was granted the coveted title of Blademaster, a distinction that saw his service given to the Empire in the form of instruction in his field of expertise on the snow-covered world Odacer-Faustin. at which point the Imperial war machine chose to accelerate rather than decrease its output of Sith warriors and leaders. Shak'Weth retained his decades-long position as lightsaber combat instructor of the Odacer-Faustin Sith academy, and a measure of the Blademaster's wisdom was imparted to the enrolled learners.

Shak'Weth's regimen consisted of hours of drill inside the academy, followed by a trek up seventy-seven stairs to the roof for practice duels where the apprentices were armed with poison barb-covered training weapons. An especially skilled young Human adolescent named Rance Lussk showed exceptional promise, and Shak'Weth was among the many Sith Masters who granted him private instruction. On a day in 3645 BBY, after a group training lesson that left his students rather exhausted, Shak'Weth permitted them to engage in unrestricted practice combat for the first time. The highly-anticipated session commenced with a challenge—dreaded by his fellow students, nevertheless allowed by Shak'Weth—from Rance Lussk, wherein he beckoned forth the uncertain Wim Nickter. The Blademaster and his other students waited impatiently for the hesitant Nickter to accept or decline. When it became apparent that fear had stricken the apprentice, Shak'Weth demanded a response and was surprised by the boy's acceptance of his recognizably-superior opponent's summons. The Blademaster stood by silently alongside hundreds of other students as they all bore witness to the humiliating defeat subsequently suffered by Wim Nickter.

entities.name: Shalath
entities.description:
Shalath was a female Human Sith Lord and Sith alchemist who served the Sith Empire on the Sith capital planet of Dromund Kaas. During the Cold War she was camped near the rogue Sith Lord Grathan's estate where she sent several Sith Acolytes with Sith runes to bind a Sithspawn created by Sith alchemy. The acolytes were killed by the spawn and so Shalath hired several other Imperials to recover the Runes and complete the task.

According to the game files for Star Wars: The Old Republic, Shalath was originally named "Lord Sunder." She was also involved in a cut quest given by Apprentice Frun, whose master was engaged in a Kaggath with Shalath. Frun would have asked players to deliver a message to Shalath's apprentice Maraad.

entities.name: Shendan
entities.description:
Shendan was a male Human Sith Lord who served the reconstituted Sith Empire during the Cold War.

Around 3640 BBY, Shendan was sent to the planet Voss to eliminate Gaden-Ko in order for the people of Voss to join the Empire. He took his chance by stabbing Gaden-Ko, but the Jedi Consular engaged him to prevent this assassination attempt. The Consular took the upper hand, and Shendan was badly wounded. Shendan was impressed how strong the Jedi was, and he close to dying. Instead of killing him, The Jedi Consular redeemed him to release his hatred, and feel the sanctity in the light side. Shendan, for the first time in his life, felt the calmness in him, and died peacefully.

entities.name: Skar
entities.description:
Skar was a Human male Sith Lord of the Sith Empire in the Cold War. After his time at the Korriban Academy, Lord Skar was Darth Thanaton's apprentice.

During the Battle of Corellia in 3640 BBY Thanaton removed the commander of the 115th stationed at the Islands Outpost and had Skar replace him. After Thanaton's rival Kallig defeated Skar as part of the Kaggath, Skar agreed to tell Thanaton's plan. He then informed his Master's rival that Thanaton intended to destroy the fuel refinery for Kallig's fleet. When Thanaton fled a duel with Kallig in presence of multiple Sith and Imperials, Skar informed Kallig that Thanaton was headed for Korriban to enlist the assistance of the Dark Council.

entities.description:
Skatheris was a male Sith Lord of the Sith Empire during the Cold War with the Galactic Republic. Skatheris began studying the creatures known as k'lor'slugs on their native planet Noe'ha'on, in hopes of eliminating the k'lor'slug infestation on the planet Korriban. With the help of other bioanalysts, Skatheris developed a prototype anti-k'lorl'slug serum.

Skatheris was first mentioned in the Bioanalysis crew skill mission "The K'lor'slug Expedition" in the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic. With Game Update 4.1, the mission was made available to both factions, and Skatheris was referred to as faction-ambiguous "Professor Skatheris."

entities.name: Darth Soverus
entities.description:
Darth Soverus was a male Sith Dark Lord of the Sith of the reconstituted Sith Empire and a member of the Emperor's Dark Council.

At some point in his lifetime, he came across the old Sith seer Spindrall, who predicted the circumstances surrounding his death. In the year 3637 BBY, as the only member of the Council present on the planet, Soverus was killed by a Republic strike team during the Korriban Incursion as foreseen, fighting to protect the Chambers from defilement.

Darth Soverus was an expert in lightsaber combat and used the Jar'Kai form in his fight against the Republic strike force in the Dark Council chambers on Korriban. He was also capable of telekinesis, including guiding a thrown lightsaber and Force choking.

Soverus first appeared during the flashpoint Korriban Incursion.

entities.name: Sovu
entities.description:
Sovu was a Human male Sith Lord of the reconstituted Sith Empire

After the formation of the Hand of the Empire, Darth Rivix was chosen to lead the newly formed organization much to the chagrin of Lord Sovu who grew to dislike Rivix ever since.

Lord Sovu accompanied Darth Rivix to an undisclosed location regarding Darth Nul to which, upon entering, Sovu disregarded Rivix as weak when the latter had requested the help of the former, though he acknowledged Rivix "had [his] uses." When Rivix unlocked a device of Nul's which revealed a unique item, later identified as Darth Nul's lightsaber, Sovu attempted to kill Rivix after the latter teased him on the identity of the mysterious item, but when Sovu attempted to take the item from its protective field he was electrocuted by a trap. Rivix echoed Sovu's earlier words, saying the Sith Lord had his uses, before striking him down.

Lord Sovu felt that he was more powerful than others realized despite being passed over in favor of Darth Rivix leading the Hand to the extent he berated his fellow Sith Lord and attempted to kill him to achieve his desires.

entities.name: Spindrall
entities.description:
Spindrall was a male Human Sith Master adherent of the Sith Order during the Great Galactic War. By the time of the Cold War between the reconstituted Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic, Spindrall was an elder Sith prophet and Lord who had made his home on the Sith's holy world of Korriban. In the deepest reaches of the tomb of the ancient Sith Lord Ajunta Pall, Spindrall counseled new acolytes on the Code of the Sith and retrained failed students who hoped to earn re-entry into the prestigious Sith Academy of Korriban.

During the Cold War, Lord Zash, a supervisor at the academy who visited Spindrall during her own training, mandated that all of her prospective apprentices seek out the hermit during their early trials so that he might judge their worth. Around 3643 BBY, Zash's new class of students traveled into the tomb to find Spindrall in the Sacrificial Chamber. Although all seven of them successfully traversed the dangers of the tomb, only one student, a slave-turned-promising acolyte, truly impressed Spindrall. The elder Sith allowed all seven of Zash's Sith hopefuls to leave the tomb, but chose to condemn the timid acolyte Kory—a condemnation that resulted in her execution upon her return to the Academy.

Spindrall was a Human male who lived during the reign of the Old Republic and the resurgence of the Sith Empire. A Force-sensitive Spindrall was inducted into the Sith Order and eventually attained the rank of Sith Lord. Although he was renowned for his insight into the minds of young Sith Acolytes and his command of the Code of the Sith, Spindrall chose to forgo the traditional path of a Sith Lord and instead adopted the life of a hermit. In the Valley of the Dark Lords on the ancestral Sith homeworld of Korriban, he took up residence in the tomb of the ancient Lord of the Sith Ajunta Pall, and there he counseled aspiring Sith apprentices and took failed acolytes under his tutelage.

Spindrall grew old in the tomb, and although he had little contact with the surface or nearby Sith Academy, the teachers at the school knew of his expertise and began sending their students to meet with the elder Sith Lord. Within the tomb's Sacrificial Chamber, Spindrall held audience with the few young Sith who survived the crypt's dangers. He also accepted disgraced acolytes who had failed in the academy's trials and were seeking tutelage so that they might earn a second chance at becoming Sith. Spindrall's seekers included the Humans Zash and Harkun, both of whom would continue their training and ultimately achieve supervisory positions at the Sith Academy.

He and his followers were eventually eliminated by a Sith from the Academy, and his signet ring was taken from him as proof of his demise.

Tahm was a Human male Sith Lord of the resurgent Empire who fought during the Cold War and the early days of the Galactic War. Tahm wore armored robes and a neck guard while wielding his purple-bladed lightsaber into combat. The Sith Lord was an accomplished Sith sorcerer, and made great use of Force lightning and life-draining Sith magic in combat.

Tahm took on at least two apprentices during the Cold War; the Sith Warrior Mace and the assassin Harp'r. In 3642 BBY, he and his two apprentices fought during the battle on the planet Balmorra were killed on the Sundari Flatlands by Republic and Jedi forces.

Tahm appears in the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic as an antagonist on the planet Balmorra, where he can be found along with Apprentice Mace and Apprentice Harp'r in the Sundari Flatlands region.

entities.name: Parkanas Tark
entities.description:
Parkanas Tark was a male Human Jedi who lived during the Great Galactic War and the Cold War. Left behind during an expedition to Malachor III, he came under the sway of the spirit of the ancient Sith Lord Terrak Morrhage and fell to the dark side, adopting the name Lord Vivicar. Years later he would return to Republic space to get revenge upon the Jedi Order. His plans failed due to the actions of a Jedi Consular sent to stop him.

As a Jedi Padawan, Tark was the youngest of an expedition sent to Malachor III. Other members of the expedition included Yuon Par, Duras Fain, Eriz Vossan, Sidonie Garen and Cin Tykan. During their exploration of the planet, these Jedi stirred the ancient spirit of Terrak Morrhage, who had been entombed on the planet for centuries. Despite his youth, Tark refused to be influenced by the spirit while the other members succumbed to Morrhage's influence, and, as a result, indulged in their urges and become paranoid. When they realized what was happening, Sidonie Garen formulated a tactical plan to escape, but Tark was trapped after rescuing Eriz Vossan. Now left behind on the planet, Parkanas Tark was prey for Morrhage's power.

What happened during the years between the mission to Malachor Three and Tark's return is unknown. When Tark returned, little was left of his original self. While his former friends had emerged as Jedi Masters, Tark found his own mastery in darkness. Taking the name Vivicar, he had learned the secrets of Morrhage's Force plague. This dark technique induced madness into those that Lord Vivicar had known and caused them to become puppets of the Sith Lord, including Duras Fain's daughter, Laranna. As his influence spread across the members of his former team, a young Jedi Consular emerged to challenge Lord Vivicar. A Padawan of Yuon Par, this young Consular learned an ancient shielding-technique which could free any under Lord Vivicar's influence. It was later used to free the Jedi Masters from Lord Vivicar's control and made the Consular immune against the plague.

entities.name: Tarnis
entities.description:
Tarnis was a Human male Sith Lord of the reconstituted Sith Empire who lived during the Great Galactic War and the subsequent Cold War with the Republic. The son of the legendary Darth Angral, Tarnis was trained by his father's apprentice Lord Praven to the rank of Sith Lord before embarking on an undercover assignment not long after the Treaty of Coruscant ended the Great Galactic War. Posing as the Republic scientist Eli Tarnis, he infiltrated the Republic's superweapon projects and quickly became the head of the design team for the Planet Prison weapon on the Republic's capital Coruscant. While his initial purpose was to gather information from inside the Republic, Tarnis believed his cover was in danger in 3643 BBY when the Jedi Master Bela Kiwiiks arrived on Coruscant to investigate a "dark presence" the Jedi Council had sensed on the capital. He made his move and attempted to steal the Planet Prison with the help of the criminal organizations known as the Migrant Merchants' Guild and Black Sun.

Staging his own kidnapping from the Senate Building after hiring a thief to steal the design files for the Planet Prison, Tarnis fled to the territory of the paramilitary Justicars' Brigade, but was pursued by a young Jedi Knight. Tarnis' true identity was uncovered by the Jedi Knight, working with the Republic Strategic Information Service, the Coruscant Security Force, and the Padawan Kira Carsen, and the Sith was followed to the ruins of the Jedi Temple, where the Knight and Carsen faced the Sith Lord in a duel in order to stop him from using the Planet Prison against Coruscant itself. Tarnis' death was witnessed via hologram by his father, who declared everlasting vengeance upon his son's killer and embarked on a crusade to gain revenge upon the Jedi.

A Human male, Tarnis was born the son of the Sith Lord Darth Angral sometime during or before the Great Galactic War with the Galactic Republic. and Tarnis' teacher joined Darth Malgus and Lord Adraas in destroying the Jedi Temple.

When Darth Baras negotiated the Treaty of Coruscant and ended the Great Galactic War, Angral was furious to be denied the chance to crush the Republic once and for all. Tarnis inherited his father's hatred of the Republic as well, and was sent undercover on Coruscant by Angral as a scientist not long after the treaty. As Doctor "Eli Tarnis," it was not long before the Sith became the chief scientist for the entire division during the tense Cold War, and while he did contribute significantly to the other designs such as the Shock Drum and the Death Mark laser, he worked primarily on the Planet Prison—a weapon designed to ionize a planet's entire atmosphere, preventing any starships from leaving or entering the atmosphere and effectively blockading a planet without any additional naval firepower.

Tarnux wielded a red-bladed battlestaff in combat as opposed to a lightsaber and was able to utilize Force Wave against his opponents. He was also able to leap across large distances with the Force.

entities.name: Aaricetri
entities.description:
Aaricetri was a planet located on the very edge of the Imperial Outer Rim. The starport city of Penshakka was located on Aaricetri. The Aaricetrian defence fleet consists in Z-95D Headhunters and Z-95D-2 Headhunters.

Due to its relatively isolated location, the planet has only in the last few decades prior to the Battle of Yavin seen rapid industrialization.

The Empire has sent several offers to make the planet join them, but the Aaricetrians cared for their independence, and declined Empire's offers. They also refused to acknowledge the Alliance's government.

During Rekk Kashiin's kidnapping, the ISB violated Aaricetri's space to intercept the rebel ship. As a consequence, the relations between the Empire and Aaricetri cooled, whereas the relations with the Rebel Alliance warmed. A rebel embassy was later established on the planet.

entities.name: Aquilae
entities.description:
Aquilae was a Planet in the Aquilaean system that was a target of conquest by the New Galactic Empire.

Aquilae was one of the first planet-names seen in the early drafts of Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope, dating back to the first story treatment. In his story notes for the film, when discussing the theme, Lucas stated that the planet's inspiration was the communist country North Vietnam, which he claimed was a "small, independent country." In the third draft, Ben Kenobi still referenced Aquilae, along with the planet Sullust, but George Lucas cut this line when writing the fourth draft. At one point, Luke Skywalker was meant to reference these planets as well as having manageable security to evade in a conversation with Han Solo.

In the first story treatment, Aquilae, which is the Latin plural or genitive of aquila, or "eagle", was a blue-green terrestrial planet threatened by a space fortress (later to become the Death Star). It contained the starport Gordon, and is the home of an anonymous princess.

In the rough draft, the princess was first named Leia, and was the daughter of King Kayos. She succeeds to the throne of Aquilae at the conclusion of the script. It was home planet of Kane Starkiller and his sons Deak and Annikin Starkiller. The planet was renamed Townowi in the first draft; by the second draft it only appears as in the name of the Aquillian Rangers.

This planet is not mentioned in the The Essential Atlas.

entities.name: Dashaad
entities.description:
Dashaad was a planet active during the time of the Galactic Republic.

The planet of Dashaad was initially planned to appear in Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic 3, a game set in the Old Republic era with John Stafford as the lead designer of the game as well as Molly Denmark and Cory Allemeier as two of the artists. The planet was created specifically for the game. Concept art for the game shows a ship resembling the Sith fighter known as the Dashaad fighter. The game was scheduled for production, LucasArts hit a difficult period in its history which culminated in the game's cancelation. This would go unpublicized for four years, until a reference book entitled Rogue Leaders: The Story of LucasArts by Rob Smith was released. The book officially announced the game was both conceived and scratched. As the game was canceled, the planet of Dashaad is not considered to be a part of any official continuity.
entities.short_description: Dashaad was a planet active during the time of the Galactic Republic.

entities.name: Granicus
entities.description:
Granicus was the name of an Imperial throneworld, in the Granicus system, a gas giant with gray cirrus methane clouds. The galactic capital was a floating city.

Prior to 20 BBY, C-3PO served as one of 1,200 interpreter droids at the sub-embassies in the Granicus system, assigned to a "third liaison officer" He served as an interpreter for 37 years before he was eventually redesignated a protocol droid and sent to the Outlands to help welcome new systems into the Old Republic.

Granicus originally appeared only in the first draft of Star Wars, replacing Alderaan as the name for the Imperial capital. This planet's concept eventually found its way into the films as Bespin and Cloud City in Episode V.

George Lucas revived the name when writing the Expanded Universe backstory for C-3PO in 1977, but the name never made its way into any licensed projects, making it as yet non-canonical.

entities.name: Kiss
entities.description: A kiss is the touching or pressing of one's lips against another person, animal, or object. The cultural connotations associated with kissing vary significantly between different societies and contexts. Depending on the culture and circumstances, a kiss can express a wide range of emotions, such as love, passion, romance, sexual attraction, sexual arousal, affection, respect, a wish for peace or good luck, as well as numerous other meanings. In some situations, kissing takes on the function of a greeting or a ritual, formal, or symbolic gesture indicating religious devotion, institutional respect, or an act of sacramental nature.

entities.name: Rei'izu
entities.description:
Rei'izu () was the homeworld of the Empire. Its capital city was Yojou.

During the Sith rebellion against the Empire and its Jedi clans, the Sith captured Rei'izu. The rebellion was led by a former Jedi knight who became a Dark Lord of the Sith, later known only as the Ronin, and a witch who had been a guardian alongside him. Their capture of the Imperial homeworld proved to the Empire that the Sith were a genuine threat, leading formerly feuding lords to band together.

The dark lord and the witch entered the Shinsui Temple together, and after expelling the nuns and monks who were willing to leave and killing those who would not, they approached the legendary kyber mirror of Shinsui Temple. The witch knelt before the mirror and began praying, entering a trance. After multiple days passed, the dark lord grew frustrated; without intent, he idly touched the mirror. The vision of unending war and resulting guilt for his own actions were overwhelming, and he struck the mirror with his fist and with the black current and white flare of the Force.

Rei'izu appeared in the 2021 non-canon novel Ronin: A Visions Novel, by Emma Mieko Candon. due to their historical significance, the presence of several temples and shrines, and the author's fondness for these cities. Like all names in the novel, Rei'izu's name is comprised of phonemes used in the Japanese language, which, in this case, is taken from an alternate reading of the characters 黄泉,

entities.description:
An orange planet was located in the Earth system. Comparable in size to a gas giant, it was the second-closest planet to Earth.

Han Solo and Chewbacca of the Millennium Falcon, having entered this star system while evading the Imperial Navy sometime after the Battle of Endor, passed by this planet before being caught in the gravity well of Jones's homeworld.

The planet, alongside three other planets, including Earth, appeared in the non-canon Dark Horse Comics comic serial "Into the Great Unknown," which acted as a crossover between the Star Wars and Indiana Jones franchises. The appearance and corresponding location of Jones' homeworld (which is heavily implied but not directly stated to be Earth) implied that it was Jupiter, the largest planet in the Solar System.

entities.name: Unidentified planet
entities.description:
A lifeless planet was the site of the Jedi Mitaka's compound, where the human and several of his assistant droids resided. Within the structure, Mitaka and his assistants researched how to bring life to the planet. One day, one of the droids, T0-B1, found a skyhopper in the basement of Mitaka's compound and asked through comm if there were any Jedi present. His message reached an Inquisitor of the Galactic Empire, who landed on the lifeless world and—as T0-B1 suspected—killed Mitaka.

Shortly after, T0-B1 left Mitaka's residence and found the late Jedi's grave, putting fragments of the late Jedi's lightsaber within it. The droid resumed researching how to create life and eventually succeeded, bringing grass and rain to his homeworld. While admiring the rain with the other droids, the Inquisitor who had killed Mitaka arrived in a TIE/ad v1 to engage T0-B1, who he believed was a Jedi. The droid then reconstructed Mitaka's lightsaber and engaged the Imperial agent in a lightsaber duel, killing the Inquisitor. Soon after, T0-B1 and another droid, C03, left the planet aboard Mitaka's skyhopper, looking to populate other lifeless planets.

entities.name: Everon
entities.description:
Everon was a tempest planet and the homeworld of the Evereni species.

Before the High Republic Era, the Evereni put their trust in their stormy homeworld of Everon in an attempt to live in harmony with nature; however, the Great Storm came, in the form of a vortex storm that rose from the planet's core bringing strong winds and lightning, destroying the native Evereni's civilization.

A series of centuries-long conflicts in the aftermath were fought among the Evereni for the remaining resources following the Great Storm. This brought the Evereni to near-extinction, forcing those who survived to flee the planet around 500 BBY

The planet Everon and its Evereni people were created by Charles Soule, a Star Wars author who works on the Star Wars: The High Republic initiative. Everon was first indirectly mentioned in Soule's 2021 High Republic novel The High Republic: Light of the Jedi as a homeworld Marchion Ro reflected upon. It was later identified as Everon in The High Republic: Eye of the Storm 1, where it appeared for the first time via flashbacks. Soule later confirmed that the homeworld Ro reflected on in Light of the Jedi was meant to be his species's homeworld of Everon, not a separate planet the Ro family had claimed as a homeworld at some point.

entities.name: U-One
entities.description:
U-One was a legendary planet, populated solely by droids.

It could not be found on any Hyperspace map, and was entirely self-sufficient, with no need for contact with the larger galaxy. Any being who came upon the planet, or attempted to contact those on the surface, was forbidden to land.

Legends differed over the geography of the planet; some said that it was a pleasant place, with plains, gentle hills, and whispering brooks, while others claimed it was an inhospitable rock, wracked with earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

Jason Fry, co-author of The Essential Atlas, stated that U-One was excluded from The Essential Atlas Online Companion because it was an imaginary location.

entities.name: Unidentified planet
entities.description:
A settled planet was traveled to by bounty hunter Boba Fett so he could collect the bounty on criminal Bendu Fry. The son of a Twi'lek Jedi had a house here.

The planet was located near three astronomical objects, two of which were bright yellow and one of which was red. From space, the world appeared blue with streaks of white. The planet had a Type I atmosphere and a surface with plains covered in grass and trees. Clouds formed within the planet's atmosphere.

The planet had many dome-shaped buildings, some of which had spires sticking out of them. One of these buildings was the house of the Twi'lek Jedi's son, located near several buildings like it. The world also contained a cantina.

entities.description: A planet was used by Crimson Dawn members "The Archivist" and Kho Phon Farrus as the second site where they attempted to unlock the Fermata Cage. It housed at least one jungle and ocean. After their attempt failed, the Sith Lord Darth Vader arrived at the planet to retrieve the Cage and kill the two, though he was interrupted by the arrival of the Orphans led by Chanath Cha, who had been sent by Crimson Dawn leader Lady Qi'ra to rescue them and the Fermata Cage. Cha and Sear battled Vader, whilst Ladybright and Imara Vex were ordered by Cha to get the Archivist, Farrus, and the Cage to safety. Cha and Sear were both killed by Vader, and Ladybright was destroyed by the Archivist after she refused to follow Qi'ra's orders of leaving the planet. The Archivist then took control of the Orphans ship, the Siroto, and departed from the planet with Farrus and the Feramata Cage onboard.

A large, glowing planet was located in a star system with one sun, and was orbited by a set of planetary rings. The rings, consisting mostly of ice drifts, constantly shed vapor and reflected light from the planet's star, which confused most starships' sensor sweeps and made them an ideal place for smugglers to hide.

In 35 ABY, during the war between the First Order and the Resistance, Commander Poe Dameron of the Resistance, having learned of the hiding spot sometime prior, guided his fellow Resistance members to the planet's rings in the starship Bestoon Legacy following a mission to the planet Pasaana. Shortly afterward, the Resistance members departed for the planet Kijimi,

While the planet itself was not seen, its rings first appeared in the 2019 film Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker. The planet was first mentioned in the 2020 novelization of the film, written by Rae Carson.

entities.name: Vahla homeworld
entities.description: The Vahla homeworld was the homeworld of the Vahla, a Force-sensitive, Near-Human species with ties to the dark side. The planet was believed to have been taken over by Vahl, a Force Adept who led her followers and was later deified by the cultists of the Ember of Vahl. The ancient Vahla were regarded as twisted and decadent, and several thousand years before the Sith–Imperial War, the cult was decimated by the Jedi Knights in an attempt to quash their dark and destructive tendencies. Since then, the Vahla traveled the galaxy as nomads, searching endlessly for their lost homeworld.

Katiz Xemir's homeworld was first mentioned in "Preparing for War," a roleplaying adventure idea from 1998's The Far Orbit Project, by Timothy S. O'Brien. The book was a supplement to West End Games' Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game.

entities.name: Ash Worlds
entities.description:
The Ash Worlds was an Outer Rim Territories sector which contained the Iego system, home to the planet Iego and its thousand moons, and the rocky planet Sran. During the Nihil conflict of the High Republic Era, the Nihil Strike Andrik Keller visited Sran, where he was killed by former Nihil Tempest Runner Pan Eyta after unwittingly tipping Eyta off to the whereabouts of Eyta's rival, Tempest Runner Lourna Dee. Later, during the Clone Wars between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Iego was briefly occupied by the Separatists, who left behind a laser web installed in the planet's moons which kept the residents trapped there until Jedi Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker discovered the problem while visiting Iego in search of reeksa root.

The Ash Worlds was a sector located in the Outer Rim Territories of the galaxy.

In 231 BBY, Andrik Keller, a Strike of the Nihil pirates who had escaped the defeat of Lourna Dee's Tempest at the Battle of Galov, visited Sran. Commenting on Sran's propensity for dust storms, the serving droid in a cantina Keller entered suggested that the celestial body's weather was the reason for the Ash Worlds' name. In the cantina, Keller met a Dowutin, the former Tempest Runner Pan Eyta, who sought revenge upon Lourna Dee. Not knowing who he was speaking to, Keller informed Eyta of Dee's condition and whereabouts, leading Eyta to kill Keller and depart Sran.

Early in the Clone Wars, a conflict between the Galactic Republic and the breakaway Confederacy of Independent Systems, Separatist forces came to occupy Iego, installing a laser web amidst the planet's moons. The Separatists left the security system behind upon abandoning Iego, leaving its residents trapped as the laser web destroyed any starship which attempted to leave. The Iegoans began attributing the carnage to a supposed curse laid by Drol, Iego's mythical phantom ruler.

entities.description:
The Cassandran Worlds was a historical name for the region of the galaxy that, under the Galactic Empire, was divided into the Cassander sector and its two subsectors, the Tadrin sector and Tendrannan sector. a human male, hailed from Minashee which was located in the region. The hyperspace route Relgim Run was located there, and during the Imperial Era, the pirate Gunda the Terrible sought to plunder the Cassandran Worlds, at least according to the Galactic Empire.

The Cassandran Worlds were originally introduced for the Star Wars Legends brand in 2004, first seen in the Star Wars Roleplaying Game sourcebook Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds as a loose-alliance of multiple planets. In the new Star Wars canon, the Cassandran Worlds were first mentioned in the 2015 sourcebook, Ultimate Star Wars.

entities.name: Core Founder
entities.description:
The Core Founders were a group of twenty-two worlds, all located in the Core Worlds region, which founded the Galactic Republic around 25,000 BBY. Founder worlds included Alderaan, Corellia, Coruscant, and Duro. The Avenue of the Core Founders in front of the Galactic Senate Building on Coruscant, the Republic's capital, was named after the group and lined with statues representing the worlds.

The Unity Arc, built for the Valo Republic Fair was an art display made to honor the Core Founders. It was composed of twenty-two floating spheres, each representing a different Core Founder. Jedi Master Harli Cogra mentioned the Unity Arc and the Core Founders in Chronicles of the Jedi, a document that detailed the Jedi of the High Republic, written in 229 BBY.

The Core Founders were first mentioned indirectly in the current Star Wars canon in the reference book Star Wars: Complete Locations, They were later identified in the reference book Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy, which was written by Pablo Hidalgo In the Star Wars Legends continuity, the Core Founders were first mentioned in the 2000 reference book Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I, written by Kristin Lund.

entities.name: Dark Worlds
entities.description:
The so-called "Dark Worlds" was an Unknown Regions principality, located at the furthest reaches of the galaxy, which the genetic terrorist Zeta Magnus had claimed as his personal kingdom. Magnus carved out his kingdom using the followers and slaves he had gathered during his journey around the galaxy. It was composed of a group of planets ruled by Magnus, who considered the Chiss Ascendancy, the Ssi-ruuvi Imperium, the Vagaari, an Ebruchi clan, and the Rhandite nihilists as his neighbours. The terrorist's seat of power was the Rennek palace, deep within the "Dark Worlds." At some point in time before the Clone Wars, the Rhandite nihilists would "bless" these worlds.

Reference to "dark worlds", lower-case, first appeared in Kenner's aborted 1986 "The Epic Continues" product line but the worlds were not canonized until the release of SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story in 2015 in which they were capitalized as "Dark Worlds".

The Double Worlds was a phrase used to refer to the double planets Talus and Tralus, which orbited Centerpoint Station as it orbited the star Corell in the Corellian system. Double Worlders was the name given to citizens of either world.

They were two of the Five Brothers. It was believed that the Celestials moved the planets into Corell's orbit from other places in the galaxy, along with three other planets; all kept in place by the Centerpoint Station.

In 500 BBY, the Federation of the Double Worlds was founded—the government of Talus and Tralus. The Federation capital is Dearic on Talus.

During the Corellian Crisis in 18 ABY, the Tralus and Talus Liberation Party advocated independence for both worlds.

Most of the planets were at some point believed destroyed, with only At Attin said to be remaining. whereas the citizens of At Attin remained ignorant to the galaxy at large, committing themselves to the Great Work of the Galactic Republic many years after the fall of that incarnation of the Republic.

Another one of the Jewels, At Achrann, was a war-torn world that greatly resembled At Attin, with two tribes—the Troik and Hattan—fighting each other in the era of the New Republic. Four of the other Jewels were At Aytuu, At Aravin, At Arissia, and At Acoda.

entities.name: Mining Worlds
entities.description:
The Mining Worlds referred to four planets—all located in the Anoat sector of the galaxy's Outer Rim Territories—that were known for their abundance of mineral resources. Burnin Konn was considered to be a Mining World, though centuries-long mining operations to harvest its chromium and dolovite destroyed the planet's indigenous plant life and created a nearly uninhabitable wasteland. During the Iron Blockade, which was established by a remnant of the Galactic Empire in an attempt to prevent news of their crushing defeat by the Alliance to Restore the Republic at the Battle of Endor from reaching the Anoat sector's populace, the Imperials locked down the Mining Worlds, capturing every transport that attempted to pass through the blockade.

The Smuggler sent several members of their crew to liberate the ships and their cargo from the Empire.

The Mining Worlds were originally created for the Star Wars Legends web article "Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin," which was written by Jason Fry, Daniel Wallace and Craig Robert Carey for Wizards of the Coast and released in 2004. They became canon when they appeared in the mobile game Star Wars: Uprising, which was developed by Kabam for iOS and Android platforms and released in 2015.

The Six Sisters were six Inner Rim worlds dominated by the Echani species, ruled by the female council of the Echani Command. Eshan, the Echani homeworld, was one of the Six Sisters, as were Thyrsus and Begali.

In 1154 BBY, Thyrsus and Begali revolted against Echani Command, resulting in the Begali Uprising. Though Begali rejoined Echani Command less than a century later, hostilities between Thyrsus and Eshan continued until the Pact of Almera in 899 BBY.

entities.name: Vault worlds
entities.description:
The vault worlds were a collection of planets that included the worlds Muunilinst, Mygeeto, and Scipio. During the 22—19 BBY Clone Wars between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, they were protected by the InterGalactic Banking Clan's Iotran Guard. The Guard was affiliated with the Condederacy and led by Captain Tost, and was supported by IG-100 MagnaGuards and IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tanks.

Eventually by 19 BBY, Clone Commander Verd was a guest author on an edition of "Neyo's Almanac of Clankers," a survival compendium sent by Clone Marshal Commander Neyo of the 91st Mobile Reconnaissance Corps that was sent to the clone cadets of the Clone Youth Brigade. In one edition, Verd wrote the entry on the IG-227, mentioning that the droids were used to patrol vault worlds during the Outer Rim Sieges. ARC trooper Muzzle also wrote an entry on the Collections and Security Division and mentioned the Iotran Guard's presence on the vault worlds.

Vault worlds were introduced in Rise of the Separatists, a 2019 supplement to Fantasy Flight Games' series of Star Wars Roleplaying products.

entities.name: Galactic heritage world
entities.description:
A world could receive the classification of galactic heritage world by the time of the Imperial Era. The planet Eyo-Dajuritz, which had long been a fossilized ecumenopolis following its decline during the early Galactic Republic, the Galactic Empire's predecessor, eventually received this designation. Imperial Senator Bail Organa recounted a fictionalized account of his time on Eyo-Dajuritz, in which he was held hostage by guerillas led by freedom fighter Saw Gerrera, in order to promote the necessity of the Imperial Rebirth Act to the Imperial Senate. As part of his speech, he described Eyo-Dajuritz as a galactic heritage world.

The galactic heritage world of Eyo-Dajuritz appeared in the 2025 novel Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear, written by Alexander Freed as the first installment of the Star Wars: Reign of the Empire trilogy.

entities.name: Gas giant
entities.description:
Gas giants, also known as gas planets, or as a gaseous giant, were large and massive planets composed chiefly of various gases. which rendered them uninhabitable in themselves, but at least some of them had a large number of moons. Typically, gas giants harbored little life unless their atmosphere comprised a layer capable of supporting oxygen-breathing species. Atmospheres such as these could also harbor turbulent storms within, such as the case with the planet Wynkahthu. Another characteristic of those worlds was the presence of planetary rings made up of several million pieces of debris. In some cases, those debris were rocky in nature and rich in ore.

Due to their significant masses, such planets had gravity wells that created distinct, if minor, hazards for hyperspace travel. Under certain circumstances, a particularly enormous gas giant could become a star in its own right.

Ajara, Bespin, Endor, Jestefad, Lefrani, Galaan, Pujool, Cavas, Kol Iben, Golus, and Yavin were all gas giants. The feature that distinguished Bespin from most of its sister planets was the existence of its oxygen-rich Life Zone, which possessed an unusual abundance of life forms and included Cloud City.

entities.name: Legacy world
entities.description:
Legacy world was a term for planets in remote regions of the galaxy that were environmentally-protected and legally exempted from exploitation. had a limited visitation and restricted industrial presences. While activities like mining were permitted on these worlds, they were regulated so to be low-impact only. Permanent settlements on Legacy worlds were not permitted. While the concept of Legacy worlds pre-dated the Galactic Empire by generations, during the Imperial Era, the Galactic Empire controlled the process of planets being granted legacy status or having their status maintained and upheld. Environmentalists and scientists sought to have planets such as Alpinn granted the legacy status. While some thought the worlds needed to be preserved, others regarded Legacy worlds as just primitive historical locations. Lyra Erso had an interest in protecting planets with legacy status and visited several of these worlds in the years before the Clone Wars.

Several planets in the Western Reaches, including Samovar and Wadi Raffa, were considered Legacy worlds. Samovar's mining conglomerate had worked to get the Legacy regulations removed, until the Empire targeted it. They hired smugglers to transport old Separatist weaponry to the planet before "exposing" the operations and using it as a means to remove Samovar's legacy status. Meanwhile, on Wadi Raffa, Turlin/Benthic Extraction had been been operating legal underwater mining operations until the Empire stepped in, using the same tactics they had on Samovar. Turlin/Benthic was framed for received illegally-trafficked weaponry, and the Empire removed Wadi Raffa's legacy status before beginning their own operations there.

Official legislation on Republic legacy worlds became stored in the Imperial Archives following the rise of the Empire. Later, the historian Beaumont Kin accessed the records.

entities.name: Aree's ship
entities.description:
Aree's ship was a starship used by the Safari droid SF-R3 "Aree" and the cam droid CAM as they traveled the galaxy to study and document the various species of wildlife for the Galactic Society of Creature Enthusiasts.The Society's logo was featured on the ship. The ship was equipped with a hyperdrive and missile launchers.

Aree's ship a hyperdrive, The ship was capable of quickly turning around by rotating its engines. The ship could operate in extremely cold or hot conditions.

Aree piloted his ship from a chair in the cockpit at the top of the ship. The cockpit had numerous buttons and a holoprojector that could display holograms. and to show areas of the ship that were damaged. A purple button turned on the cockpit's wipers to wipe away any creatures that flew into the ship.

The interior of Aree's ship was mostly gray and it was very spacious. The ship had a room for storing a variety of foodstuff. Also, Aree had a bedroom on the ship that had a bed and plants.The ship had a room with a large power converter. There was a lever that opened and closed the ship's airlock. Aree kept a battery that could be used to restore his energy.

entities.name: Arrowhead
entities.description:
The Arrowhead was a starship built by Rowan Freemaker, who believed that it could turn the tide of the Galactic Civil War. Prior to the Battle of Endor, Rowan, his siblings Zander and Kordi, and their B1-series battle droid Roger undertook a quest to obtain the various parts needed to build the Arrowhead. After being built on Jakku, the Arrowhead was destroyed during a skirmish over Shantipole but some of its parts were incorporated into the Freemakers' starship StarScavenger just in time for the Battle of Endor.

The Arrowhead was an arrowhead–shaped starship. It was equipped with various accessories including a pair of embersteel blades, a Farium fusion conduit, a proton suspension housing, an energy matrix activator, and a large kyber crystal. The ship's embersteel blades could cut through just about anything and had a pair of blaster cannons on either side.

Following the mission to Tibalt, Rowan Freemaker experienced a Force vision of himself building the Arrowhead. Rowan later related his vision to the Mon Calamari Rebel Alliance starship builder Quarrie but was unable to accurately describe the ship. To teach Rowan a sense of style and craftsmanship, Quarrie brought Rowan and the B1-series battle droid Roger to the ancient Force Builders city of Alistan Nor. After climbing to the top of the Tower of Alistan Nor, Rowan experienced another Force vision of the Arrowhead.

After escaping an attack by the Imperial hunter droid M-OC, Rowan assembled a model of the Arrowhead. Quarrie estimated that they needed several items including embersteel blades, a Farium fusion conduit, a proton suspension housing, an energy matrix activator, and a bantha–sized kyber crystal. While Rowan's older siblings Zander and Kordi Freemaker were daunted, Rowan remained optimistic.

entities.description:
During his time as a Galactic Republic statesman, the Alderaanian noble Eckhorn Baliss owned a personal ship that could carry at least one person. Baliss, who was actually a spy for the Sith Empire during the Great Galactic War, to a list of potential Imperial sympathizers.

Sydia's husband was an Imperial operative as well, though he and Baliss were not aware of each other, and fearing his cover had been blown, the Senator's husband In 3663 BBY, Sandafar placed explosives aboard Baliss' ship and detonated them when the noble was in orbit over his homeworld of Alderaan, killing Baliss instantly. The event was ruled an accident, but was later discovered to be Sandafar's work by the astromech droid T7-O1 and the Jedi Knight known as the Hero of Tython.

Eckhorn Baliss and his ship are briefly mentioned in a series of conversations with the Jedi Knight companion character T7-O1 in BioWare's 2011 massively multiplayer online role-playing video game Star Wars: The Old Republic.

entities.name: Band Light
entities.description:
The Band Light was a vessel suspected of privateer activities during the reign of the Galactic Empire. The vessel was commanded by a captain during the Imperial period, and the crew consisted of Nix—who was second in command—Pend, and Red. The crew attempted to salvage a derelict Etti-class light transport in the vicinity of the planet Ord Mantell and they began to die in what appeared to be a series of accidents which were caused by at least one Imperial Terror Trooper. In the wake of the deaths of Nix, Pend, and Red, the Band Light captain decided to abandon the Etti-class vessel. The captain soon noticed additional problems with the Band Light—such as lights switching off and doors opening on their own—and then sent a transmission about the incident, which was intercepted.

The Band Light was mentioned in the "Terror Trooper" entry in the in-game databank of the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 versions of the LucasArts video game, Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II, which was released in 2010.

entities.name: Bantha's Charge
entities.description:
The Bantha's Charge was a starship which went missing while carrying a shipment along the Rimma Trade Route during the Galactic Civil War. Merchants blamed the disappearance on TIE attacks, and the New Republic Intelligence marked it as a possible activity of the Galactic Empire's 204th Imperial Fighter Wing. The New Republic Intelligence agent Caern Adan and his colleague Yrica Quell reviewed the Bantha's Charge disappearance in their search for the 204th but marked the event as unremarkable.

The Bantha's Charge was mentioned in the 2020 novel Shadow Fall: An Alphabet Squadron Novel, written by Alexander Freed as the second volume in his Star Wars: Alphabet Squadron trilogy.

entities.name: Base ship
entities.description: The mysterious base ship was sent to the Orellon system by an extinct alien race centuries before the Galactic Civil War. It was fully automated and manned by scout droids and collector droids whose task it was to collect 30,000 unique specimens of alien life. Eventually, it reached Orellon II where its droids brought fear to the hearts of the local Kentra. Upon its arrival on Orellon II, it had received no messages from its homeworld in three hundred years. The Kentra thought the droids were demons, and commissioned a group of Rebels with the task of eliminating them. The ship was programmed to leave the planet and move on to the next if discovered or fired upon with energy weapons.

entities.name: Bitemark
entities.description:
The Bitemark was a starship that the Trandoshan bounty hunter Bossk purchased during the reign of the Galactic Empire. Soon after he acquired it, the vessel was destroyed along with Bossk's favorite cantina during an explosive blasterfight between the bounty hunter and the fugitive smugglers Chewbacca and Han Solo on the Jurzan spaceport, after which the pair narrowly escaped Bossk. In 3 ABY, Bossk thought of the destroyed vessel when the Empire contacted him about a new bounty on Chewbacca and Solo, the former of whom had become the bane of his career.

The Bitemark was mentioned in "Tooth and Claw," a short story written by Michael Kogge and published in the From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back anthology in 2020.

Unbeknowst to Yost, the Emperor's Hand Mara Jade secretly boarded his ship as well and managed to hear where Yost and his mercenaries where holding Korlo Brightwater, one of the stormtroopers they captured.

Yost's ship was mentioned in the 2011 novel Choices of One, written by Timothy Zahn.

entities.name: Brightfox
entities.description:
The Brightfox was a starship that participated in the Karee Blockade Clutch where it was beat by the Vorantis, a ship owned by the pilot Brantis Mo Fresk. Later that year, Mo Fresk offered his services as a pilot for hire on Frander's Bay—a space station that orbited the Core Worlds planet Chandrila. When the New Republic operative Han Solo visited Frander's Bay to hire an unaffiliated pilot with his friend Lando Calrissian, Mo Fresk's barker mentioned the pilot's beating of the Brightfox in the Karee Blockade Clutch into one of Solo's ears.

The Brightfox was mentioned in the 2018 novel Last Shot, written by Daniel José Older.

entities.name: Celestine
entities.description:
The Celestine was a droid legend—a starship-droid hybrid. It was a large warship designed to be operated only by droids. It was equipped with one of the largest and most highly advanced droid brains of its era. After departing the shipyard where it was built, with a great deal of bravado, the ship jumped to hyperspace, but never arrived at its programmed destination.

There was no official record of the Celestine ever being commissioned, yet its legend was perpetuated in stories told by spacers who claimed to have seen it jumping to lightspeed. Some even boasted to have seen the vessel while they themselves were traveling through hyperspace. It was believed that seeing the warship in the midst of battle was a bad omen.

entities.name: Centennial Peregrine
entities.description:
The Centennial Peregrine was a starship stolen and crashed by Hondo Ohnaka, a pirate operating throughout the galaxy.

During the Imperial Era, Ohnaka stole the vessel following a night of drinking Sarlacc Juice and firing blaster bolts at an Imperial garrison commander's feet, though he was hazy on the details. After stealing the vessel, Ohnaka was quickly pursued by two Imperial TIE fighters. He tried to escape to the planet Galagolos V, where he was shot down and escaped into the planet's spaceport.

Shortly afterward, Ohnaka stowed away aboard the YT-1300 light freighter Millennium Falcon, hoping to steal the vessel. However, after overhearing a woman named Mahjo Reeloo pleading with the ship's owner, the smuggler Han Solo, to aid in her quest to find Novian rubies, he decided to reveal himself, surprising Solo. He described the ship as very unusual, asking for its name, and was told it. In response, he playfully referred to the vessel he had stolen as the Centennial Peregrine. Solo objected, but Ohnaka replied that he could not prove otherwise. He went on to state that having stolen and crashed it in the same day, it was a small thing to name it as well, asking if Solo wanted it to have died without a name. Solo retorted that whoever Ohnaka stole it from likely had their own name for it, which he replied was a good point.

The Centennial Peregrine appeared briefly in Pirate's Price, a junior novel written by Lou Anders, published in 2019.

entities.name: "Changeling" Mark 71NB
entities.description:
The "Changeling" Mark 71NB was a type of racing starfighter. Ace Squadron pilot Bo Keevil flew one, the Yellow Ace, during the New Republic Era.

The "Changeling" Mark 71NB first appeared in part one of the two-part episode "The Recruit," The model was identified in the 2019 reference book Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition.

The model was named by Adam Bray in reference to Mark Newbold, with "71" referencing his birth year and "NB" referencing "Newbold."

entities.name: Cormorant
entities.description:
The Cormorant was a rundown space tug ship that Annisoukaline Kalfus and her mom used to live in.

The Cormorant was designed by Aurelien Predal from the Aardman short "I Am Your Mother". This ship was mix between tugboats in the UK and various Star Wars elements to make it something utilitarian, sturdy, chunky and rusty like it hasn't been used in years. The ship's bumpers are gradually turned to bumper pads on springs which brought a vibe from one of the classic Wallace & Gromit short films "The Wrong Trousers". The challenge to create the ship to blend both the humor and quirkiness of Aardman was to apply the design rules around the characteristic designs language of Star Wars, evolving the ship towards a fish-like appearance that reflects the fish out of water situation on Anni and her mother.

In order to give a most precise blue-point to the model making department at Aardman, Predal quickly mock up the design in Maya to easily do iterations, adjust proportions & scale and check everything that would work as wanted while extracting orthographic views that could pass on to the art department, lead by art director Andy Brown and his team to built the sets and ships with 2 scales of the Cormoran being one 1:1 with the puppets and on half size for all the flying sequences of the short.

entities.name: Degarian II
entities.description: The Degarian II was one of Senator Crote's fastest starships; used in the years leading up to the Battle of Naboo. From Frego, Crote allowed Jedi Knights Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi to take the ship to Coruscant while escorting Lena Cobral there so she could testify against the Cobral family. Wary of an attack, the Jedi opted to find a different means of passage back to the capital. When the Jedi arrived on Coruscant, they learned that the Degarian II had been attacked and destroyed while en route; there were no survivors.

Dekkr and the starship were later rescued by Resistance pilot Tallissan Lintra.

entities.name: Destiny
entities.description:
Destiny was an oddly shaped starship attached to Zirtran's Anchor, a space station located in the Phosphura Belt Nebula.

It famously provided the home for the mysterious alien species called the Kalai, who rarely, if ever, left the ship, and their half-Human hybrid offspring, the Lethagoes. The ship was named using their language, but most people used the closest approximation in Galactic Basic Standard, "Destiny."

Smaller ships were housed inside the Destiny—nimble hawk-shaped vessels which had demonstrated an agility beyond that of other starfighters like the Alliance X-wing or the Imperial TIE/LN starfighter.

The Destiny inhabitants connected it to Sector Epsilon of Zirtran's Archor during the Imperial period and remained annexed since then, even during the Galactic Civil War.

Keize looked back on the destruction as one of the events that taught him about his responsibility to protect the lives of his cohorts in order to protect even more.

The Destrier was mentioned in canon in the 2021 novel Victory's Price: An Alphabet Squadron Novel, written by Alexander Freed.

entities.description:
Dindoo's Glory was the personal starship of the Rodian entrepreneur Kelko.

Once Kelko became rich, he named his ship as an homage to his long-dead stepfather and mentor, Dindoo, the one who had taught Kelko everything he knew.

Kelko, a talented pilot, would take the Dindoo's Glory for short excursions with only Weedo, his old and trusty droid, as company, while leaving his wife, Shinba, and their children behind.

entities.description:
In 0 ABY, Doss's ship, which was equipped with an engine, traveled where the Hand of Judgment stormtrooper deserter group was held prisoner by its owner, the mercenary Mikhtor Doss. Shortly after, Emperor's Hand Mara Jade killed Doss's forces and inquired the mercenary's client, the politician Bok Yost, where Hand of Judgment member Korlo Brightwater was being held. Yost then stated that the former stormtrooper was aboard his TL-1800 freighter Melnor Spear, not aboard Doss's ship.

Doss's ship was mentioned in the 2011 novel Choices of One, written by Timothy Zahn.

entities.description: The Dynamo was a starship owned by the Kuranu inventor Mantessa Chekkat and her daughter, Klerin. As Kuranu had a pathological fear of germs, the Dynamo was kept clean and sanitized by an army of small droids. The Chekkats utilized the vessel to travel to the Republic Fair on the planet Valo, where the elder Chekkat hoped to sell a four-seven nullifier that Klerin had created to the Galactic Republic senator Tia Toon. However, Toon declined to purchase the device, and the Dynamo was later destroyed by Nihil marauders when they attacked the Republic Fair.

In the current Star Wars canon, the Errant Venture was mentioned in the 2022 novel Shadow of the Sith, which was written by Adam Christopher.

entities.name: Espirion Multi
entities.description:
The Espirion Multi was a red-colored starship used by natives of the planet Espirion during the Galactic Civil War between the Alliance to Restore the Republic and the Galactic Empire. When a fleet of Alderaanian ships gathered in Espirion's orbit came under attack from an Imperial-class Star Destroyer, the Alderaanian-Espirion hybrid Beon Beonel had the ship aid the Alderaanians after hearing a speech by Princess Leia Organa broadcast from her shuttle Lord Junn. The ship's captain contacted the Alderaanians upon entering the combat and told them to stay back while they handled the Imperials. They then attacked the Star Destroyer and destroyed it.

The crew of Espirion Multi included individuals of multiple species, like Ithorian and Gand.

The Espirion Multi first appeared in the comic book Princess Leia 5, which was written by Mark Waid, illustrated by Terry Dodson and released in 2015.

entities.name: Fast Hand
entities.description:
The Submersible Mining Environment, nicknamed Fast Hand by Lando Calrissian, was exclusively designed for mining Corusca gems in the deepest reaches of the planet Yavin's lower atmosphere. It had a resemblance akin to a huge diving bell.

Fast Hand was equipped with a pair of trolling cables that could be used to retrieve Corusca gems. After a gem was captured, it would end up in an access port located in the floor of Fast Hand cockpit.

Since it needed to withstand the extreme pressures of Yavin's lower atmosphere to get the largest Corusca gems, it had been fitted with a thin layer of quantum-crystalline armor, a technology that had been pioneered in the Sun Crusher. However, Fast Hand was not invincible. A Corusca gem traveling at high speeds in Yavin's atmosphere could put at least a small dent in the vessel.

Fast Hand had no propulsion systems of its own, instead it relied on an energy tether from GemDiver Station. The energy tether's length and power could be manipulated from the cockpit. Even though it was extremely powerful, the energy tether could be severed by turbulence from Yavin's powerful storm systems. For this reason, life-support supplies and energy backups were kept aboard Fast Hand at all times. The crew of Fast Hand could survive for a relatively long time until a rescue was made.

entities.name: Fathership
entities.description:
A fathership was a type of starship operated by a species of extragalactic googly-eyed aliens. The vessel was huge, larger than an Imperial-class Star Destroyer, and its presence was capable of blocking out the stars behind it. The metal hull of the fathership was covered in winking, colored lights, and they were powerful ships capable of travelling between galaxies.

A fathership was on the final leg of a tour of the galaxy during the Galactic Civil War when they happened across a battle between an Imperial Star Destroyer and an Alliance corvette. Misinterpreting the battle as a sporting contest, the alien crew did not like the mismatch between the two ships. Dispatching droids, the crews of both ships were stunned and taken aboard the fathership to compete in a series of fairer competitions.

The Fusion Flame was a starship It once raced another ship, later called the Stellar Envoy, around the planet of Drall and was soundly defeated. The victorious pilot recorded the victory in the winning ship's SuperFlow IV droid brain. In 18 BBY, the ship that had beaten the Fusion Flame, by then given the name Stellar Envoy, was being restored by a mechanic named Bammy Decree. He discovered the pilot's record of the race against the Fusion Flame while analyzing the brain.

The Fusion Flame was mentioned in Millennium Falcon, a 2008 novel by James Luceno.

Gasgano was a starship that belonged to Galactic Society of Creature Enthusiasts Director of Creature Cartography Ardis San Tekka and her safari droid companion B8-T5. The vessel resembled a shyyyo bird, but the pair did not wish to use that as a name and instead named the vessel after their favorite podracer, Gasgano. When observing animals, B8-T5 recorded data and audio for the pair to analyze back on the Gasgano. B8-T5 then mentioned the Gasgano in an entry on whisper birds in San Tekka's journal

The Gasgano was mentioned in the 2024 reference book Star Wars Bestiary, Vol. 1: Creatures of the Galaxy, which was written by S.T. Bende.

entities.name: Gentleman Caller
entities.description:
The Gentleman Caller was an Corellian runabout owned by Tendra Risant Calrissian.

She purchased it hastily just before the onset of the First Corellian Insurrection, when she noticed a suspicious buildup of ships around Sacorria that she deduced might be part of an invading fleet assembled by the Sacorrian Triad. Unfortunately, on her voyage to Corellia to inform Lando Calrissian and the New Republic of her suspicions, she got caught in the systemwide interdiction field surrounding the Corellian system and was unable to communicate through normal means because of jamming throughout the system. She traveled through the systems in normal space for several weeks, until the field was shut off by Thrackan Sal-Solo. The Gentleman Caller was then able to make the jump and meet up with the Lady Luck.

entities.name: Good Feeling
entities.description:
The Good Feeling was a starship that was owned by the Duros Jekk Seejo.

Seejo worked for the Incom Corporation and he often persuaded his fellow workers to use the Good Feeling to test their projects on. As a result, it developed many unusual features and displayed features of both a Z-95 Headhunter and an ARC-170. Shortly after the formation of the Galactic Empire, Seejo and a group of Incom and Subpro used the Good Feeling at the Imperial Testing Grounds on the Outer Moon of Prakith where they were developing a new starship design. The Feeling was attacked by mynocks, leaving it stranded on the Inner Moon of Prakith. However, a group of Alderaanian Resistance agents came to the rescue and saved the ship.

A short time later, the ship was again attacked by mynocks. Seejo was blamed for this, so he was sacked and the Incom Corporation took control of the vessel.
entities.short_description: The Good Feeling was a starship that was owned by the Duros Jekk Seejo.

entities.description: The Good Tidings V was a starship owned by the Dressellian smuggler Has Obitt that replaced his old light freighter the Good Tidings.

entities.name: Graceful Promising
entities.description:
The Graceful Promising was a Vontorian treasure ship. At one point by 10 BBY, it became cracked apart and settled in an orbit around a dark star. The Pirate Queen Maz Kanata eventually stashed a cache of kiirium aboard the starship, which the smuggler Han Solo, assisted by Rebel Alliance Lieutenant Caluan Ematt and a few rebel Pathfinders, successfully retrieved at some point between 0 ABY and 3 ABY. The Graceful Promising and the retrieval of its treasure was documented in the logbook known as the Smuggler's Guide.

The Graceful Promising was a Vontorian treasure ship that became cracked apart at some point by 10 BBY. It settled in a close orbit around a dark star on the eastern edge of the galaxy. The Pirate Queen Maz Kanata eventually stashed a cache of relatively valuable kiirium outfitted with an antitamper sub-space alarm aboard the derelict starship. She marked its location on a map of the treasure caches she had hidden throughout the galaxy that was included in the Smuggler's Guide logbook.

At one point between 0 ABY and 3 ABY, the human smuggler Han Solo acquired the Smuggler's Guide. In order to try and earn funds needed to repay a debt to the crime lord Jabba Desilijic Tiure, Solo decided to try and access Kanata's treasure cache aboard the Graceful Promising, which he considered one of the pirate queen's more challenging caches but nevertheless worth the attempt—an opinion that the smuggler noted on Kanata's map too.

Solo recognized the difficulties lying ahead that were posed by the gravitational shear caused by the nearby dark star, however. For the mission to the Graceful Promising he also brought along the Alliance Lieutenant Caluan Ematt as well as a few rebel Pathfinders. The smuggler made an entry in the Smuggler's Guide noting his plans and included an image of the vessel—the name of which he misspelled as the Grateful Promising in one instance—with the entry.

entities.name: Grapnel
entities.description:
The Grapnel was a starship captained by Wan'yek Whett and crewed by a fishing crew.

The Grapnel was described by former first mate Skoova Stev as being large and sharp like the nose of a bony fish, and as having three claw-like legs for landing gear.

While the precise origins of the ship are unknown, the Grapnel was stolen from an unknown location and owner by the Besalisk Dread Captain Wan'yek Whett and his vile fishing crew, to serve as their spaceship and fishing vessel.

During the time of the Great Fish Famine, the Grapnel landed on the icy world of Sakavi Tar. With the crew intending to plunder the vast oceans underneath the planet's icy surface, a Sakavian fisherman named Skoova Stev struck a deal with Whett to join his crew on the Grapnel and lend him his fishing expertise, on the condition that they not fish on his starving homeworld. Whett agreed, and the Grapnel departed from Sakavi Tar with its' new crew member.

A starship was captained by Haplif, an Agbui agent of the expansionist Grysk species in the Unknown Regions. Aboard the ship, Haplif led a group of 50 members of his Agbui species conducting a plot to destroy the Chiss Ascendancy on behalf of the Grysk agent "Jixtus." During their travels, the Agbui came to host two Chiss aboard the ship: the betrothed mid-agers Yomie and Coduyo'po'nekri.

Haplif's ship first appeared in the 2021 novel Thrawn Ascendancy: Greater Good by Timothy Zahn, the second installment in Star Wars: The Ascendancy Trilogy.
