entities.name: Jixtus' ship
entities.description:
A ship was owned by "Jixtus," an agent of the Grysk warlike species during his campaign against the Chiss Ascendancy. Two months after the Battle over Primea, Jixtus hired the Pathfinder navigator Qilori to navigate the ship, where he coerced Qilori into the service of the Grysks.

Jixtus used the ship to meet with his Agbui agent Haplif on several occasions to discuss the progress of Haplif's attempts to spy and eventually goad the Chiss into a civil war. At times he also brought Qilori along.

During General Yiv's Nikardun campaigns, "Jixtus" met his Agbui agent Haplif on board the ship on the orbit of a planet that had been devastated by the civil war incited by Haplif and his Agbui companions. He tasked the Agbui to target the Chiss Ascendancy for inner destruction next, while their attention was directed outward due the threat posed by Yiv and his Nikardun Destiny.

However, the Chiss defeated Yiv's forces during the Battle over Primea and captured Yiv himself. About two months after Yiv's defeat Jixtus hired a Pathfinder named Qilori to navigate his ship. During the trip Jixtus interrogated Qilori about Yiv's defeat and coerced the navigator to become his agent in his plot to destroy the Chiss Ascendancy.

entities.name: Journeyman
entities.description: The Journeyman was a passenger starship which existed during the High Republic Era. When hyperspace routes were beginning to be opened up in the aftermath of the Great Hyperspace Disaster, the Journeyman departed Cerea with a load of mostly Cerean passengers. However, the hyperspace lane it travelled on had been prematurely opened, and it was struck by a piece of debris. The transport Vessel, carrying three Jedi passengers, happened upon the stricken Journeyman shortly after the accident, and the Jedi onboard assisted the evacuation of the starship before it exploded.

entities.name: Kintan Comet
entities.description:
The Kintan Comet was a starship that Fensi Moisk served as a crew member aboard in 22 BBY.

The Kintan Comet was first mentioned in the 2013 visual guide, Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Ultimate Illustrated Guide, which was written by Jason Fry. The book was originally written in English and slated to be published, but only found a Danish release as Star Wars: Klonernes Angreb Den Ultimative Illustrerede Guide. Jason Fry confirmed on Bluesky that the Danish caption "Kintansk Comet-mandskabsuniform" beside Fensi Moisk's picture was originally written in English as "Kintan Comet crewer's uniform" where Kintan Comet would have been the name of a starship.

entities.name: Tyresius Lokai's starship
entities.description:
A starship was owned by the Devaronian scoundrel Tyresius Lokai during the Cold War. Lokai became a target of the Great Hunt and his ship was shot down over Tatooine and tried to escape the planet under an alias, but was pursued by another bounty hunter across the Dune Sea desert. Eventually, Lokai was cornered at his ship's landing cite, where he persuaded the Hunter into letting him live by presenting a genetically identical clone to claim his bounty. Changing his name to Gault Rennow, Lokai left on the Hunter's D5-Mantis Patrol Craft, abandoning his ship on Tatooine.

Tyresius Lokai's starship appears in the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic during the Bounty Hunter class mission on Tatooine.

entities.name: Lunar Shadow
entities.description:
Lunar Shadow was a ship stuck on Nar Shaddaa during the Meetra Surik's visit to the planet. It was crewed by Nikto, and the captain was a Weequay who frequented the Jekk'Jekk Tarr. The Nikto were unable to leave because the captain was also their pilot, and they were unable to go fetch him due to the fact that the cantina contained fumes that were poisonous to their species.

During the game, it is possible for the Exile to convince the Weequay to return to the Lunar Shadow so that the ship can leave.

It is also possible for the exile to convince the Nikto to hire the refugee Odis as their new pilot. The crewmen are tired of having to wait around all the time while the captain wastes the group's profits on his own entertainment, so they agree quickly to hire Odis after the idea is suggested, as it solves two problems, getting them a qualified new pilot and getting rid of the incompetent existing captain.

Lastly, the Exile can choose the Dark-side action of coming to the apartment where the ship's crew are staying and killing everyone there.

entities.name: Madman's Fortune
entities.description: The Madman's Fortune was a museum exhibit ship that flew as part of a traveling freak show. The ship was owned by the Snivvian Goontirk and at some point during galactic history, Goontirk purchased the mummified remains of Vardovin IV, the "Lost King of Duro" from a Ryn merchant, to display aboard the Madman's Fortune. However, unknown to Goontirk, the mummy contained more than a dozen skekfish eggs and while the Madman's Fortune was passing through the Engebo system, the mummy's plasteel coffin cracked open and the skekfish eggs hatched. The creatures attacked Goontirk and in an attempt to escape from them, he ran into one of the ship's escape pods. The skekfish pursued the Snivvian in and they devoured him before he could launch the pod, and thirty seconds later the Madman automated safety systems launched the escape pod into the atmosphere of the planet Engebo V.

entities.name: Mama Tried
entities.description:
The Mama Tried was a starship that was flown by the gambler Lando Calrissian during the reign of the Galactic Empire. In 0 ABY, Calrissian stopped over on the planet Taanab whilst carrying a cargo of conner nets aboard the Mama. After Taanab was attacked by the Norulac Freebooters, Calrissian made a cantina bet that he could defeat the pirates single-handedly, and he powered up the Mama and flew into combat. After Calrissian ejected the connor nets and the pirates became entangled in the devices, and Calrissian then used the Mama tractor beam to hurl chunks of ice at the stricken freebooters.

The Mama Tried was mentioned in the 2012 guidebook The Essential Guide to Warfare, by Jason Fry and Paul R. Urquhart, and the vessel's name was intended as a reference to the song "Mama Tried," by the musician Merle Haggard.

The Mandellian Gambit was a starship active during the Great Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. Risha Drayen, the daughter of the crime lord Nok Drayen, was born aboard the Gambit in 3664 BBY. The ship's name recalled a famous incident early in Nok Drayen's career, where he massacred ten thousand pirates at the planet Mandellia.

The Mandellian Gambit was mentioned in the 2012 reference guide Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia.

entities.name: Mika Grey's ship
entities.description:
The archaeologist Mika Grey owned a ship. In 34 ABY, Grey used the ship to travel to the Outer Rim planet Ashas Ree in search of a Sith relic. Two days after she was trapped inside a Sith temple, Grey was rescued by a group of individuals. After they exited the temple, the group witnessed an explosion; Grey's ship had been destroyed by the First Order, who had tracked her to the planet. After they defeated the First Order forces, Grey, without a ship, accompanied the group back to the supertanker fuel depot Colossus.

In 34 ABY, planet Ashas Ree in search of a Sith relic for which she had spent two years searching. When she arrived on Ashas Ree, she landed her ship on the outskirts of an outpost and made her way into a Temple of the Force built over a Sith temple. After Grey raised the Sith temple and broke inside it, she became trapped. Two days later, Grey was rescued by a group of individuals consisting of the human Kel and Eila, the Resistance member Kazuda Xiono, and the astromech droid CB-23.

Once they left the temple, the group discovered that their companions, the pilots Freya Fenris and Torra Doza, had been captured by First Order Raiders, stormtroopers who sought out Sith artifacts for Supreme Leader Kylo Ren and who had also tracked Grey from the astronomical object Vargos 9. Grey suggested to her rescuers that they accompany her to her ship, though Xiono was unsure how that would be useful to their friends held captive. Xiono then added that Grey would be lucky if the First Order had not discovered her ship.

Following Xiono's remark, they witnessed an explosion; the archaeologist's ship had indeed been found and destroyed by the First Order, forcing the group to devise a new plan. They then noticed that Grey had disappeared. After the Raiders captured the group, Grey revealed herself and activated the Sith relic, which resulted in the troopers' deaths. With the troopers dead, Grey lamented that she would not be able to leave the planet as her ship had been destroyed. Eila, Doza, and Xiono invited Grey to accompany them back to the supertanker fuel depot Colossus upon which they resided. Grey accepted the offer, and they left for the Colossus.

A thief named Kay Vess overheard this conversation and later recovered old galactic credits from a container near where the smuggler claimed to have seen the Morgana.

The Morgana was first mentioned in the "A Pirate's Fortune" expansion for the Massive Entertainment video game Star Wars Outlaws, It was mentioned as part of an ambient conversation that players can listen to to start the "Ghost Ship" intel quest.

entities.name: Namrelllew
entities.description:
The Namrelllew was a Wookiee starship which carried Republic Senator Padmé Amidala and her Head of Security Captain Gregar Typho on an undercover mission to Hebekrr Minor in 22 BBY, during the first weeks of the Clone Wars.

By the beginning of the Clone Wars in 22 BBY, the Namrelllew was already old. However, it was very well built due to its Wookiee construction and design. Its air-filtration systems in particular were noticeably superior to those that could be manufactured on Naboo, producing recycled air without any particulates and which smelled almost fresh.

The ship was luxurious, although it could seem unusual to human passengers due to its Wookiee-centric design. For example, its beds were very long, it had full-body hot-air dryers instead of towels, and some adult humans needed to use a stool to reach the back of the sinks in the refreshers. Captain Typho stated that its cabins were larger than any barracks he had lived in. The control panels on the flight deck that were within easy reach for a Wookiee would have required a human to stretch to their limits. The hull of the ship was made of cool metal, which vibrated slightly while traveling through hyperspace.

The Namrelllew was co-captained by a husband and wife team of Wookiees: Naijoh, the pilot, and Rayyne, who served as the ship's navigator. They were described as a perfect team, each relying on the other's talents for a safe arrival and never doubting their skill. Idda was a Mriss engineer on board, and G-1FY served as the ship's protocol droid.

entities.description:
The Obvious Nirvana was a starship which was destroyed.

The Obvious Nirvana was one of the first ships that was to dock with the newly built Tatoo III space station outside Tatooine. Instead it rushed into and impacted the station, destroying both the ship and Tatoo III. Later investigations showed that the metals used to construct Tatoo III had been magnetic, which had dragged the Obvious Nirvana to its doom.

entities.name: Overtone
entities.description:
The Overtone was a planet hopper captained by the Bivall bounty hunter Quin Carree of the Tempest Breakers, along with her partner Lourna Dee. The ship was provided to a motley team of Jedi and bounty hunters by the Villarandi information broker Kradon Minst, through Greyamina Tiss, as they prepared to track down the abducted Nihil Minister of Advancement Baron Boolan in the Nihil Occlusion Zone. It was equipped with a way to circumvent the Stormwall, allowing passage into the Occlusion Zone. Though the ship was modest and with some faulty components, it saw the team through their mission, including surviving the eternal storms of Heiklet and a dogfight with one of the Nihil's She'ar. Following the mission, the ship came under the ownership of Carree and Dee. The latter attempted to change its name to the Quin, but Carree refused to have a ship named after her. Journalist Rhil Dairo interviewed Lourna Dee from within the Overtone.

The Overtone first appeared in The High Republic: Tempest Breaker, a 2024 audio drama written by Cavan Scott and published as a part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's Phase III. During the audio drama's flashbacks, the Overtone is described by Greyamina Tiss as a planet hopper. However, the drama's script, released in 2025, indicates in slug lines that the interview used as the frame story takes place in a Star Cruiser. In the dialogue of the final scene, Rhil Dairo confirms that they are in the Overtone. Given that the slug lines are out-of-universe, this article considers the descriptions of the ship in-universe to take precedence, especially as the ship is described more consistently with the typical size of a planet hopper instead of a Star Cruiser.

entities.description:
The Peculiar Inspiration was a starship that was in existence during the time of the Clone Wars.

After rescuing the Tarasin Force Adepts Krizta and Trik, the Heroes of Cularin were loaned use of the Peculiar Inspiration to transport the Tarasin pair to the Cularin system. However, a group of bounty hunters sabotaged the ship, causing it to crash on the planet Holador.

In Strike III, the player characters, who role-play as the Heroes of Cularin, are only loaned the use of the Peculiar Inspiration if they lack a suitable transport of their own. If the players are traveling in a ship of their own, then it is that ship, not the Inspiration, that they travel in, and which crashes on Holador.

Possibility was the name broadcast by the vessel's ID beacon during the time that Amidala piloted it, though she was unaware of its real name.

They freed the philosopher from cryofreeze and persuaded him to join their cause.

entities.description:
The Queen of Ranroon was a long-lost starship. The Crimson Dawn crime lord Dryden Vos had an ancient navi-computer dataplaque onboard his yacht, First Light, with glyphs that allegedly pinpointed the location of the vessel.

The legend of the Queen of Ranroon first appeared in the Legends continuity novels Han Solo's Revenge & Han Solo and the Lost Legacy by Brian Daley. In the novels, the vessel was a treasure ship of the powerful pre-Republic warlord, Xim the Despot. It was said to have vanished while loaded with a vast fortune, inspiring searches by treasure hunters for millennia .

Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide

entities.name: Ramid's starship
entities.description:
The spacer Ramid owned a starship around 139 ABY. The starship had a rounded rectangular shape and was equipped with three rear engines. That year, Ramid and his crew used their starship during a successful kidnapping attempt against his former lover Ania Solo, who was wanted by the Galactic Federation Triumvirate. Feigning damage to their engine systems, they waited for AG-37's freighter to dock with them. During the meeting, Ramid arranged for Ania to be separated from her companions and then imprisoned her aboard his starship. He and his crew then made a cold jump into hyperspace, which consumed a large proportion of their fuel supplies.

While orbiting a barren planet which rained acid rain, they were attacked by a another bounty hunter, who flew a modified TIE/sa bomber. During the pursuit, Ramid's starship sustained extensive damage and the ship's Twi'lek pilot was killed. Ramid then released Ania and convinced her to pilot and land the ship. Ania succeeded in landing Ramid's starship largely intact but Ramid was knocked unconscious during the landing. His Klatooinian crew mate also perished during the accident. Shortly later, the mysterious bounty hunter demanded that Ania surrender herself. After sending a medical droid to tend to Ramid, Ania confronted the bounty hunter and succeeded in knocking her unconscious with a blaster rifle. She then fled into the wilderness.

Shortly later, Ramid awoke and left in a speeder bike to rescue Ania. Ramid's ship had been damaged extensively during the crash and was unable to fly. Later, Ania's companions Jao Assam, AG-37, and Sauk found Ramid's starship. AG-37 found a lot of blood on the gangplank while Sauk found that the speeder storage section was empty.

The Rampart first appeared in the one-shot comic Beckett 1, which was published by Marvel Comics The issue was written by Gerry Duggan with Marc Laming and Will Sliney illustrating the starship. The Rampart shared its name with the Harrelson portrayed Tobias Beckett in the Anthology film Solo: A Star Wars Story, which released May 25, 2018.

entities.name: Rancor's Fist
entities.description:
The Rancor's Fist was the starship of Jabba Desilijic Tiure's cousin Graballa the Hutt. The ship also served as Graballa's mobile headquarters. It housed his henchmen and several starfighters. Following the Battle of Hoth, the Rancor's Fist was used to hunt down the Freemakers during a race for the Kyber Saber crystals.

The Rancor's Fist was a large trapezium-shaped starship with two wings on either side that are also equipped with two heavy turbo laser cannons that could tilt and fire when the vessel is commencing orbital bombardment, or when also in space, when chasing after enemy ships. The vessel served as both the flagship and mobile headquarters of the Hutt crime lord Graballa. The Rancor's Fist hosted a large complement of starfighters and could transport his henchmen. The starship also contained Graballa's throne room and a trapdoor which housed a Nexu named Smiley. The Rancor's Fist was capable of hyperspace travel but its engines could be damaged by sea water. Besides Graballa, other notable residents aboard the ship including the bounty hunters Dengar, Baash, Raam, and the Toydarian servant Yeppau.

For two centuries before the Battle of Hoth, Graballa served as the manager of a barren ore mine in the Belgaroth asteroid field. The Rancor's Fist served as headquarters and flagship. Following the Battle of Hoth, Graballa tried to borrow money from his wealthy cousin Jabba to build a beachside resort and buffet. However, Jabba was not interested and refused to loan Graballa money.

Later, Graballa's "think tank" staff Baash and Raam invited two bounty hunters aboard the Rancor's Fist. These bounty hunters turned out to be the Force-sensitive Rowan Freemaker and his B1-series battle droid companion Roger. Graballa and his entourage soon discovered Rowan and Roger's true identities. When Graballa learned about the Kyber Saber crystal, he saw an opportunity to get rich and demanded that Rowan lead him to more crystals. When he refused, Graballa ordered that Rowan and Roger be fed to his pet Nexu Smiley.

The red apricot was the starship of red apricot squad, an elite squad of the Silver Knights, a prominent civil mercenary group in the Aakaash system. Attended to by the squad's mechanic, Zhuang Yuanying, as well as a team of seven worker drones of the WB-35 mechanic droid model, the red apricot was shaped like a cone lying down on its side. Its elongated contour was protected by an armored hull composed of enigmatic iron and other metals, with the hull being disposable in a maneuver known to red apricot squad as "shell shedding."

When the squad was tasked to retrieve a lost Silver Dawn shipment of enigmatic tenebrae, the squad took the red apricot to Fire and later Lake 4399 in the Heaven system.

The red apricot appeared in The Vow of Silver Dawn, a Chinese web novel written by "His Majesty the King." The ship first appeared in a chapter released in January 4, 2021, and is named 红杏号 in the original simplified Chinese text.

entities.description: The Seeker was a starship that was used by the spacers Khedryn Faal and Marr Idi-Shael. At some point, the pair flew the ship from the planet Fhost to a star system in the Unknown Regions, where they planned to salvage a derelict ship. However, the crime lord Reegas Vance also planned to salvage the derelict and to prevent Faal and Idi-Shael from interfering with his plans, he fired upon the Seeker with his YT-2400 light freighter Blackstar, disabling the Seeker. Faal and Idi-Shael then donned space suits and abandoned the Seeker, while Vance led a boarding party over to the stricken vessel. Faal and Idi-Shael subsequently stole the Blackstar and departed the system, leaving Vance stranded aboard the Seeker.

entities.name: Ania Solo's starship
entities.description: In 138 ABY, the junk dealer Ania Solo owned a small, personal starship. She kept it with her at her junk yard, but she brought it to an ice mining platform in the rings of Carreras Minor in that year. There, she showed her friend Sauk an Imperial communications droid that she had found, and the two of them suddenly discovered a lightsaber inside of the droid. They went to Carreras Major to sell it, but their attempts led to a getaway from the law, which saw them pilot Solo's ship through a sewer system. As Sauk, an engineer, had not fixed the ship's targeting lead, they only escaped when he used the lightsaber to cut open a steam pipe and blind their speeder bike pursuers. The ship was later loaded onto a freighter that belonged to their friend AG-37, but Solo jettisoned her ship from the freighter's cargo hold in order to destroy some Carreras starfighters that were chasing them. The resulting explosion destroyed her starship as well.

entities.name: Starstream
entities.description:
Starstream Records was the record label for Starstream Communications Group, Inc., a Houston, Texas based radio promotions company (1980–1990).

It was formed as the record label supporting a national talent search, The Big Music America Contest, developed by Kenneth Kramer with support from Harold Stream, a Louisiana businessman and Dr. Donald Altfeld, a songwriter and music producer best known for co-writing "The Little Old Lady (from Pasadena)" by Jan and Dean and co-producing  "It Never Rains In Southern California" by Albert Hammond.

Originally the label was known as Nova Records and the first release was Nova Records MS7801 - The Best of Mississippi.

Later, when the contest changed from the Big Music America Contest to the Miller High Life Rock To Riches Talent Search, the operating company was changed from Big Music America to Starstream Communications Group.

Approximately 250 albums and singles were released by Starstream as part of local rock, soul and Hispanic music talent searches conducted by Starstream and local radio stations in top US markets.

Radio stations releasing LPs on the Starstream label include WCOZ, Boston; WAPP, New York, WPDH Poughkeepsie, KLOL, Houston, KLOS, Los Angeles and KSJO, San Jose.

Alumni of Starstream albums include Bon Jovi (WAPP), Twisted Sister (WAPP), Jon Butcher (WCOZ) and The Replacements & Peter Himmelman (KQDS) and WARHEAD   (WZLD - Columbia SC)  (@warhead) (www.heavenandhellrecords.com)

The Soul/R&B titles released by Starstream were part of the Budweiser Showdown Talent Search Contest.  Participating Radio Stations included WRKS, NY, WBMX Chicago, KJLH and KDAY in Los Angeles and KMJQ and KYOK in Houston.

Recording of all individual tracks was handled by the bands and occasionally the radio station.  The individual tapes to be included on the album were then sent to Starstream where they were mixed and mastered onto tape and sent off to be mastered onto disc.  Cook Sound, owned by local Houston radio personality Dwight Cook was used for most of the mastering.  The early master discs were cut by Bernie Grundman at Capitol Records and then later M.C, Rather at Columbia Records in Nashville and Carl Rowatti at Truetone in New York.  Pressing was originally done at Columbia Records Custom Pressing in Indiana and New Jersey.   Later, (early mid 80's), pressing moved to Peter Pan Industries in New Jersey where it stayed until the end.

A few of the early Budweiser Showdown discs were also pressed at Houston Record Plant.
entities.short_description: Starstream Records was the record label for Starstream Communications Group, Inc., a Houston, Texas based radio promotions company (1980–1990).

entities.description: A ship was owned by Chardri Tage and his partner and co-pilot, Tamsin, in the year after the formation of the Galactic Empire. Bail Organa sent the pair in their starship to locate a former Jedi, Ahsoka Tano, though he did not tell them whom he sought. They located her on a planet in the Thabeska system when her freighter was pursued by an agent of the Black Sun criminal syndicate. They fired upon the other ship, forcing the agent to flee, then locked Tano's in a tractor beam.

entities.name: Tarasin Dream
entities.description:
Tarasin Dream was a merchant ship that was registered on Cularin and operated during the Clone Wars.

On one occasion during the Clone Wars, the Dream was traveling as part of a convoy when it dropped out of hyperspace and entered the Cularin system. However, it was attacked by some Thaereian military Z-95 Headhunters, which claimed that it was running contraband. The Dream could not fight back, as it was unarmed, so it sent out a distress. This was detected by the Heroes of Cularin, who attacked the Thaereian Headhunters and tried to save it.
entities.short_description: Tarasin Dream was a merchant ship that was registered on Cularin and operated during the Clone Wars.

entities.name: Tarsis'Krall
entities.description: The Tarsis'Krall was a starship that crashed in the Dune Sea on Tatooine. During the Cold War, a group of prisoners escaped from the Imperial Reclamation Service with the help of Jedi, and fled into the desert. Officer Vengo activated the prisoners' shock collars, forcing them to take shelter in the ruins of the Tarsis'Krall and tend to the injured.

entities.name: TAV Prosperity
entities.description:
The TAV Prosperity was a starship that was owned by the Cularin Trade Alliance.

During the Clone Wars, the Trade Alliance held the Cularin Trade Show aboard the Prosperity while it was in the Cularin system. For the event, it was fitted with a special hyperdrive that would suposedly allow it to enter hyperspace while in the shadow of the Cularin comet cloud. However, after the CTA tried to demonstrate the hyperdrive, it failed and the ship was left floating in a dangerous area of the cloud, without any operational systems. However, Osten Dal'Nay and the Heroes of Cularin, who had visited the show, were able to save the ship by flying out and towing it to safety.
entities.short_description: The TAV Prosperity was a starship that was owned by the Cularin Trade Alliance.

entities.name: Tazca's Flare
entities.description:
The Tazca's Flare was a rumored ghost starship with solar sails that was said to have lost souls clinging to it trying to get back to a starport. While on Hauler's Keep in 3 ABY, a Mon Calamari told the story of the Tazca's Flare to fellow guests only to be called out for sharing those types of ghost stories and that they should save them for the younglings. While telling the story, a Quarren interjected who claimed to know an individual named Konal that also saw the Tazca's Flare.

The Tazca's Flare was first mentioned in the "A Pirate's Fortune" expansion for the Massive Entertainment video game Star Wars Outlaws, It was only mentioned as part of an ambient conversation that players can overhear while on Hauler's Keep.

After the Trustworthy crashed, an Ewok stowaway caused havoc throughout the ship, and discovered a comlink that revealed Kreven's betrayal to Reen.

entities.name: Twilight Explorer
entities.description: The Twilight Explorer was a starship affiliated with the Jedi Order that was lost at the bottom of Lake Paonga, on the Mid Rim planet Naboo. Between around 232 and 230 BBY, the droid 0G-LC and his associates discovered the long-lost wreckage of the ship, and sought the valuable Jedi star compass within for historical research. 0G-LC tasked Jedi Initiates Nubs, Kai Brightstar, and Lys Solay, along with the Gungan explorer Kluurt to recover the artifact. News of the ship's location made its way to the Gungan thief Tooba Jinx, who hoped to obtain the star compass and sell it. The Jedi and Jinx raced to the wreckage of the ship, and found the star compass on the ship's bridge.

entities.name: Unidentified capsule
entities.description:
A capsule carried the Stranger to the Forest Moon of Endor. In 3 ABY, two moons near Endor aligned, and a rift in space opened, through which the capsule traveled. The capsule fell toward the forested moon, and the young Ewoks Wicket Wystri Warrick and Teebo saw it and mistook it for a Comet. When the capsule touched down, the Stranger emerged, and the craft was located by the two Ewoks and their friends Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka and Latara. As the Ewoks began to carry the capsule back to their village, it illuminated, spun rapidly, and vanished.

In 3 ABY, the a capsule carried the Stranger to the Forest Moon of Endor. When the capsule landed, the Stranger made his way to the Dulok swamps, but not before witnessing the Ewoks, Wicket Wystri Warrick and Teebo coming across the ship. Wicket and Teebo, with help from Latara and Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka, tried to carry the capsule back to Bright Tree Village. Wicket took a piece of it and attached it to his Belt of Honor as proof of his quest towards becoming a full-fledged Ewok warrior.

As the Ewoks walked, the capsule illuminated bright purple light and began to spin in a circle. The speed increased until the capsule was a blur, and the Ewoks stepped back. The capsule then disintegrated into a cloud of smoke, leaving no trace except for the "trophy" on Wicket's belt.

entities.name: Unidentified Faer ship
entities.description:
A ship housed members of the Evereni family known as Faers during the High Republic Era. Created around 679 BBY, long before the High Republic Era, the Faers came to inhabit the ship during the next three centuries. Ro, wanting to know more about species, asked them about the Evereni. Among the things they told her was about the ship on which most of their family resided.

Ro later recounted her encounter with the Faers and mentioned the ship in a message she recorded for her descendants. during his youth, Ro's great-great-grandson Marchion Ro had listened to her journal, including the message where the ship was mentioned.

The ship was mentioned in the short story "A Closed Fist Has No Claws," written by Tessa Gratton and published in the 2023 young-adult anthology The High Republic: Tales of Light and Life as a part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project.

However while on route the galleon was attacked by pirates and left a drift. Its captain, a Rodian named Baloch, was taken by the pirates to be ransomed. While its one remaining crew member, a human named Kreth, was found and rescued by the crew of the Ravenstar.

entities.name: Unidentified Galleon
entities.description:
A galleon, according to legend, was a starship that participated in a competition to map a safe route to the planet Batuu and back during the early days of space travel. Captained by a human named Phillian the galleon was initially leading the search for Batuu. However the crew had begun to strip the derelict remains of starships that had previously failed to make the journey for their treasures and resources.

When the smaller Ravenstar caught up to the galleon, captain Phillian proposed a race for the final approach to Batuu. While initially faster, Phillian miscalculated the added weight for their salvaged treasure with their fuel consumption and the galleon became a drift. After winning the race the crew of the Ravenstar returned to render assistance.

entities.name: Unidentified hauler
entities.description:
The anti-Nihil operative Cair San Tekka owned a hauler during the High Republic Era. The vessel was equipped with at least one engine and a hyperdrive and could be crewed by a pilot. San Tekka hid the hauler in a spaceport on Jafan and bribed several mechanics to hide it for him.

By the time the spaceport was partially abandoned due to the Nihil presence in the sector that year, San Tekka returned and collected his hauler. Afterward, he traveled off Jafan via hyperspace, jumping to the nearby Chommell sector planet Naboo. Among the swampy cliffs on the south side of the world's capital, Theed, San Tekka swapped the hauler for his luxury yacht for the rest of the trip to his family's nearby compound.

The Jedi Hunters are going after Kara, but the ship has been destroyed by the abandoned ship's self destruct setting up by a droid Teto, which means that they're too late to escape from the close range of the abandoned ship's self destruct and the Jedi Hunters have been killed, that Kara's hunt is over. The ship's hull was red, and it was equipped with blaster cannons and deflector shields.

entities.name: Unidentified Lesser Space starship
entities.description:
A starship hailing from the region of the galaxy beyond the Unknown Regions known as "Lesser Space" carried Galactic Republic technology and held human survivors by 19 BBY. The vessel was seized by a task force of the Chiss Ascendancy's Chaf family.

Chiss Syndic Mitth'ras'safis and a human female pilot managed to steal the starship from the task force, but were unable to bring it to a refuge world from which they could give the Republic technology to the Ascendancy's Defense Hierarchy Council, as the ship was too damaged to reach its destination. The syndic and the human subsequently crashed the vessel into a valley, killing themselves in the process but saving the humans aboard the starship.

A massive starship from "Lesser Space," the region of the galaxy beyond the Unknown Regions, carried Galactic Republic technology. It was equipped with engines and carried food and supplies that could last for generations and a small vessel. The spacecraft contained a pylon.

By 19 BBY, the starship, which carried human survivors, was involved in the Vagaari pirate operations, a conflict between the forces of the Chiss Ascendancy nation and the Vagaari pirates. A task force of the Ascendancy's Chaf family obtained the vessel, and the Chiss syndic Mitth'ras'safis, core name "Thrass," and a human female pilot stole the starship. Thrass and the woman spirited the ship away in hopes of bringing it to a refuge world from which they could offer the Republic technology to the Ascendancy's Defense Hierarchy Council; however, their plan did not go as planned. The ship was far too damaged to reach the world, and the pair discovered the human survivors aboard the vessel.

entities.description:
During the time of the Cold War, a proxy conflict between the Sith Empire and Galactic Republic, the Selkath discovered an ancient pre-hyperdrive vessel and revived its captain from suspended animation. Eventually someone was sent to meet with the captain, resulting in a bond between the envoy and the captain—who was still confused by the revivification—discussing the officer's native era. Ultimately, the captain provided the envoy with a gift from the ship.

A gigantic, planet-sized probe was created millions of years ago by an ancient race from an unknown galaxy with the mission to examine all evolved life forms in the universe and to suppress those which endangered the balance established by the Force.

The probe eventually made its way to the galaxy of the Galactic Empire where it was discovered by a group of pathfinders. The group ventured inside the probe where they faced all manor of traps and danger. They eventually made it to the center of the probe where they met an old man named God.

entities.name: Unidentified starship
entities.description:
A starship was traveling through the Kolatill system, which was located in the Kathol sector of the Outer Rim Territories, in 8 ABY. Around the same time that the escort carrier Kathol Protector—a starship serving in the military forces of the Imperial warlord Moff Kentor Sarne—attacked Domaz, the capital city of the planet Kolatill, this vessel was attacked. The assault crippled the vessel, leaving it adrift between planets. The derelict was discovered by a starfighter patrol from the New Republic CR90 corvette FarStar, which was in-system responding to a distress signal from Kolatill. The corvette's crew deployed a rescue team to investigate the wreck and see if any survivors were sealed in airtight sections.

The starship was mentioned in the roleplaying adventure "Omens," part of The DarkStryder Campaign, published by West End Games in 1995. The discovery of the ship is a possible side adventure that the players may undertake during the scenario. The players can search the ship for crew members that may still be alive, although whether they discover any is left to the discretion of the gamemaster.

entities.name: Unidentified starship
entities.description:
At some point before 32 BBY, a starship belonging to an extra-galactic spacer was forced to land on Tatooine after colliding with an asteroid of the Dragon's Spine belt. Because of the accident, the starship was heavily damaged, but its owner managed to gather enough local Wupiupi credits to buy new parts and rebuild it. Following its refitting, the ship was equipped with a StarMark III Hyperdrive bought from Watto, a junk dealer from the Mos Espa spaceport.

Before its crash-landing on Tatooine, that starship of extra-galactic origins was equipped with a quadruple-thruster propulsion system, a pair of delta wings and a hull that looked very much like the T-06 hull manufactured by Incom Corporation. For the most part, the ship was painted in a standard gray hue, although the wings, tails and outer cockpit bore distinctive crimson markings.

However, following its forced landing, the ship was heavily damaged, and it became necessary to rebuild it from scratch with components available on Tatooine. After an extensive refitting that cost between 3,829 and 6,329 wupiupi, the ship was equipped with a StarMark III hyperdrive for hyperspace travel, three Voyager III fuel cells to store more energy, three GalaxyGuard Mk. VII shield boosters to increase the deflector shield's power, and three Polestar subZero blaster radiators to better dissipate the heat in the ship's mounted weapons. Additionally, the craft was given a brand new paint job.

In addition to the above, the starship also had to replace its original hull, its engine types, and its wings, with the spacer having chosen either the Slipstream IV hull, the T-06 hull, or the AeroMaster XI hull; the Sun-Gull 1e wing, the StarWind V wing, or the Nebula 3 wing sets; and the Thornley Space Systems-developed NovaFury MonoThrusters, the Galaxy Seven, or the Hamilton Engineering-developed Delta-C Tri-Thrusters.

entities.name: Unidentified starship
entities.description:
A starship was owned by the hunter Riegenn Hetuu during the time of the Galactic Republic. The starship needed at least one person to operate it, and had a cargo bay equipped with life support systems. Hetuu used the ship's cargo bay to hold a live k'lor'slug queen that he had captured for a Hutt who intended to use the beast in a yearly gladiatorial tournament. He flew his ship to the planet Hutta, where the Hutt was located, but the worm-like k'lor'slug had laid eggs in the cargo bay that quickly hatched into nearly four hundred k'lorslugs. When the Hutt arrived at the ship, Hetuu opened the cargo bay to present the Hutt with his prize. However, the hoard of k'lorslugs swarmed out and devoured both Hetuu and his Hutt client.

Riegenn Hetuu's starship was indirectly mentioned in Star Wars: The Old Republic, a 2011 MMORPG produced by BioWare. The starship was mentioned as part of the k'lor'slug codex entry, which could be found by players who killed the k'lor'slug broodwatcher in the tomb of the Sith Lord Ajunta Pall on the planet Korriban.

entities.description:
This was a light, black transatmospheric ship that came to the aid of Pharika on Sakuub and was intent on taking the Sakuub Holocron after being led to it by Jaina Solo and Jagged Fel. It killed Pharika after she was defeated but was then destroyed by an Unidentified Hutt in his G1-M4-C Dunelizard fighter. Its occupants were unknown.

The ship was described by Jagged Fel as compact and sleek, and completely unknown to anything he had ever seen before. The ship could also move with "astonishing speed" and was equipped with a Laser weapon. However, it was no match for the power of the Dunelizard's Laser cannon.

The vessel first appeared in "Chronicles of Corellia: Cracking the Mask," the second installment of the The High Republic: Chronicles of Corellia short stories. The story was written by Alyssa Wong and published in Star Wars Insider 228th issue

entities.name: Unidentified Xantar starship
entities.description:
The unidentified Xantar starship was a saucer-like starship operated by a "Bug-Eyes" who brought Luke Skywalker to his home planet of Xantar. Some time earlier, the pilot brought the starship to the homeworld of Indiana Jones, then brought Jones back to Xantar.

The spaceship was patterned after the popular image of alien spacecraft, flying saucers. The ship's pilot was meant to resemble the common image of aliens believed to visit Earth, known as Greys. The ship appeared at the end of the Indiana Jones and His Desktop Adventures video game, taking Indy away to the pilot's home planet. The ship, the pilot and Indiana Jones later appeared in Yoda Stories as a reference to that earlier game.

entities.name: Vector Bundle
entities.description:
The Vector Bundle was a starship owned by the Starros Clan that was kept at their ancestral home on Hosnian Prime. when the house was attacked by Imperial captain Cerasus Ehllo in order to retrieve his wife Aryssha, Thea Starros, Mevera Starros, and Sana Starros used the Vector Bundle to escape from the building.

The three Starroses flew the Vector Bundle to the Hosnian sector where they were ambushed by Marl Jibs. Mevera used an ion cannon to disable the bounty hunter's ship. The ion cannon was a weapon that Mevera had confiscated from a group of Soikans after they failed to pay her from some freelance work. The Starroses then flew the Vector Bundle to the Dalnan sector.

entities.name: Vorantis
entities.description:
The Vorantis was a starship owened by the pilot Brantis Mo Fresk. Mo Fresk participated in the Karee Blockade Clutch in his ship where he beat the starship Brightfox. Later that year, the New Republic operative Han Solo and his friend Lando Calrissian visited Frander's Bay—a space station that orbited the Core Worlds planet Chandrila—in search of an unaffiliated pilot to hire. The barker of Mo Fresk—who offered his services as a pilot at Frander's Bay—mentioned the Vorantis and Mo Fresk's victory over the Brightfox in the Karee Blockade Clutch into one of Solo's ears. Solo and Calrissian ultimately hired the pilot Taka Jamoreesa.

The Vorantis was mentioned in the 2018 novel Last Shot, written by Daniel José Older.

Mandalore the Avenger seized the ship after her forces discovered it involved in a smuggling operation in Mandalorian space. Her technicians further improved the ship's stealth systems and scanners. and also used to rescue Darth Malgus from Carrick Station.

entities.name: The wreck
entities.description:
The wreck was the name given to a crashed alien starship of unknown origin that was beneath the waves of the planet Spira. Discovered on the planet when Galactic Republic scouts scanned the planet around 1000 BBY, the derelict had been stripped of engines, instruments, bodily remains, and any indication as to who had built or piloted the vessel, leaving a hollowed out hole. The wreck became a popular tourist spot on Spira, with divers exploring the ship.

Possessed of organic-looking lines, the wreck's passages were ribbed and oddly curved. Only one safe entrance, a large break in the hull on the port side, granted entry to the derelict, and several doors had been welded shut to prevent tourists from entering unsafe areas.

entities.name: Xosad Hozem's ship
entities.description:
A ship was owned by the Twi'lek rebel Xosad Hozem during the Imperial Era.

Xosad Hozem's starship was used by Hozem and his crew who were a part of Saw Gerrera's Partisans. The ship had a cockpit with room for at least two people, a back section with jump seats for passengers, and a common area with benches and seats surrounding a table that was screwed into the floor. Past the common room was a hallway that led to a room with bunks for Hozem's crew, namely Jari and Bilder. The floors of the ship were rough and dull metal, as was most of the rest of the interior.

It was compatible to dock with a CCR-class pinnace via a transport tube.

Hozem piloted the ship for a mission to gather information from a civilian transport that the Empire was using as a scout ship. Joined by Jari, Bilder, Gerrera, and Jyn Erso, they traveled from Wrea to the Western Reaches and boarded the ship, stealing datapads of intel before returning to Gerrera's outpost.

entities.name: Shadow Bird
entities.description:
Shadow Bird was an alias that the freighters Millennium Falcon and Sureshot flew under in the months following the Battle of Duro during the Yuuzhan Vong War.

When he landed the Millennium Falcon on Corellia in order to ensure that his wife, Leia Organa Solo, received treatment for injuries inflicted during the First Battle of Duro, Han Solo identified the Falcon as Shadow Bird to Corellian Control so that their arrival would not attract unwanted attention. After they were forced to leave Corellia by Thrackan Sal-Solo, Han attempted to remain discreet by using the alias when requesting clearance to depart. However, Corellian Control had been informed by Corellian Security Force that the Shadow Bird was in fact the Millennium Falcon and broadcast the freighter's true name over an open channel, alerting several bounty hunters to the Falcon location.

Later, when Han and Leia traveled to Coruscant in order to undermine support for the Peace Vote by accusing Senator Viqi Shesh, its chief proponent, of corruption and to find a nervesplicer to help Leia heal her injuries, they arranged for Jedi Knight Izal Waz's YT-1300 light freighter Sureshot to be cosmetically altered to look like the Millennium Falcon and equipped it with a slave circuit to allow Waz to remotely pilot the Sureshot from the freighter Jolly Man on their approach to Coruscant. In order to further sell the illusion that the Sureshot was the Falcon, it flew under the alias Shadow Bird. This gambit resulted in the destruction of the Sureshot, but allowed Han and Leia to fulfill their goals, albeit not without some difficulty.

entities.name: Starbird
entities.description:
The starbird, also known as the Wren Phoenix crest, was a stylized depiction of a legendary bird rising up in the air, with its wings spread and its head turned to the right. The Mandalorian weapons expert and graffiti artist Sabine Wren used that symbol as her personal signature.

The design was based on the starbird of ancient legend. The legend stated that a starbird could never die and that if it seemed to be gone, it was renewing itself in the heart of a nova.

At some point, the symbol was adopted by Sabine Wren, a Mandalorian warrior who put her own artistic spin on the design, drawing inspiration from Janyor's protest paintings on Bith. During her time with the rebels from the planet Lothal, led by former Jedi padawan Kanan Jarrus, she painted the symbol wherever the small band would strike. She also painted it on her breastplate. Eventually, it became her trademark,

One such victory occurred on Lothal, when Wren sabotaged one of the planet's key air fields. She used the symbol again when she blew away a good part of the Lawbringer during the concurring skirmish. Again, on the rebels' mission to steal Imperial weapons, she painted her trademark on crates in a hangar bay on Garel, killing or distracting the pursuing stormtroopers to allow the Ghost, flown by rebel captain Hera Syndulla, to escape. Wren's sign, however, was not made using ordinary paint, but, instead, was a concoction of her own making that resulted in an explosion. She utilized her explosive symbol again at the Spire on Stygeon Prime.

entities.name: 49AX3
entities.description:
49AX3 was a Dreadnought-class heavy cruiser that served the navy of the Galactic Empire. the vessel was captured by the Alliance to Restore the Republic, who used it to raid Imperial Refining Platform M36, a refinery in the Outer Rim Territories. Assisted by Luke Skywalker, the team of rebels managed to steal fuel from the refinery, but their escape was blocked by an Imperial-class Star Destroyer. Skywalker landed his X-wing in the vessel's hangar, where he and the rebel major used a shuttle to draw the attention of the Imperial TIE fighters away. The tactic worked, and the rebels aboard 49AX3 were able to evacuate, escaping to a nearby world.

entities.name: 836-VS
entities.description:
836-VS was a Sentinel-class landing craft that was stolen by the Alliance to Restore the Republic and used for a mission to the moon Killun 71. Crewed by members of Phoenix Cell, namely the former Imperial pilot Wedge Antilles, the former Imperial inventory droid AP-5, and the C1-series astromech droid C1-10P "Chopper," 836-VS arrived at Killun Station, where they attempted to steal Imperial clearance codes.

Following the mission, 836-VS docked with the modified VCX-100 light freighter Ghost. Soon after, Chopper, who had been reprogrammed by Imperial personnel, trapped Antilles, AP-5, and the fellow rebels Hera Syndulla, Ezra Bridger, and Garazeb Orrelios in the ship's cargo bay. Then, he detached the Ghost from 836-VS and flew away, leaving the stolen Imperial shuttle floating in space.

entities.name: AA-23
entities.description:
AA-23 was a Lambda-class T-4a shuttle in the service of the Galactic Empire.

AA-23 was stationed on an Imperial XQ6 Platform DX-11a in the Eidoloni system some time after the Battle of Hoth. It was one of four shuttles that attempted to flee the platform when Ace Azzameen's squadron staged a diversionary attack on the outpost. Their aim was to give Commander Zaletta, an Imperial officer who had grown sympathetic to the Rebel Alliance's cause, an opportunity to defect.

Onboard shuttle AA-23, Zaletta fled the platform after the Rebels were able to disable the platform's shields. Unsure of which of the shuttles the defector was on, Azzameen was ordered to scan each craft before contact could be established. Their attack a success, the Rebels fled to a rendezvous with the Rebel Nebulon-B Frigate Redemption. Zaletta safely docked with the vessel, but the group suddenly came under attack from an Interdictor and an escorting Star Destroyer. With Zaletta under suspicion of luring the Rebels into a trap, he was imprisoned while the Rebels attacked the Interdictor and forced it to disengage.

Before the Rebels had a chance to decode the shuttle's valuable data, however, Liberty Tactical Officer Commander Kupalo, secretly a mole for the Empire, blew his cover, breaking into the hangar. He bound the shuttle's custodian, placing a series of explosives beside him. Despite the deck officer's protests, Kupalo stole the shuttle and blasted his way out of the hangar, detonating the charges and causing huge damage to the hangar as he did so.

entities.description:
The smuggler more commonly known as Ace owned an XS stock light freighter during the Cold War and the Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. Having owned it for a while already, the smuggler had the freighter stolen by the criminal Skavak. Ace followed Skavak to the planet Coruscant, where he had taken the vessel, and eventually retrieved it.

During Ace's search for Nok Drayen's lost fortune, the starship was modified several times. It had its hyperdrive and engine replaced and a new sensor computer was installed.

entities.name: Adamant
entities.description:
The Adamant was a New Republic bulk cruiser under the command of Admiral Gial Ackbar.

In 23 ABY, she fell under attack by an Imperial insurgency group known as the Second Imperium in the Coruscant system while transporting hyperdrive cores and turbolaser emplacements to Kuat Drive Yards.

This raid was lead by ex-TIE pilot Qorl under the command of the fallen Jedi Brakiss who operated the Shadow Academy, an ally of the Imperium. Qorl utilized a modified assault shuttle to board the cruiser, jettison the Republic crew in escape pods, and stole the Adamant and her cargo.

entities.name: Admiral Ackbar
entities.description:
Admiral Ackbar was a Victory-class Star Destroyer that served as the flagship of Admiral Nek Bwua'tu of the Galactic Alliance Defense Force following the Yuuzhan Vong War.

Admiral Ackbar, named in memory of the deceased Mon Calamari Admiral, was one of the new generation of Victory-class Star Destroyers commissioned by the Galactic Alliance to aid in the fight against pirate forces. Admiral Ackbar was known as a famous pirate hunter, and its crew was said to feel privileged to serve under Admiral Bwua'tu. The ship's Tactical Salon contained a larmalstone bust of Ackbar.

These updated Victory-class Star Destroyers were fitted with a turret on the upper hull, almost as large as the bridge itself. Mounted inside each was one of the asteroid-tug tractor beams sold to the Defense Force by Lando Calrissian. Admiral Ackbar participated in the blockade of the Murgo Choke during the Dark Nest crisis. The Star Destroyer was later commandeered by UnuThul and Alema Rar's forces during the Battle of the Murgo Choke in the beginning of the Swarm War.

This ship would later become a part of the Killik fleet during the war. Because of its presence in the Killik fleet, the Chiss assumed that the Galactic Alliance had sided with the Killiks. During the Battle of Tenupe, near the end of the war, Luke Skywalker and a squad of YVH 5 Bugcruncher war droids, managed to recapture the vessel.

The frigate had been stationed by the Nikardun at the Paccosh homeworld Rapacc in the Rapacc system, but was captured by the Paccosh after the downfall of General Yiv of the Nikardun Destiny. The vessel was placed under the command of Uingali foar Marocsaa of the Marocsaa subclan, the symbol of which—the chimaera—was painted on the underside of the frigate.

entities.name: Alliance
entities.description:
The Alliance, originally known as the Imperious, was a large, powerful warship built by the Galactic Empire ruled by Darth Krayt. It was the prototype of the Imperious-class Star Destroyer, a Star Destroyer design larger and more powerful than the Pellaeon-class. It was a personal flagship of Galactic Alliance Admiral Gar Stazi.

Darth Krayt, Dark Lord of the Sith and Emperor of the new galactic empire, had made a demand for a new class of warship that could overpower any type of ship used by the Empire's numerous enemies. With this demand, Moff Rulf Yage, the head of the Imperial Navy, proposed the idea of the Imperious-class Star Destroyer, an upgrade of the Pellaeon-class.

The Imperious was constructed in the Mon Calamari Shipyards in 137 ABY, at the time under control of the usurper faction of the Empire. It was one of the largest ships in the Empire, as well as the pride of the Imperial Navy. For its maiden voyage, the Imperious was to be operated by skeleton crews.

Meanwhile, the Galactic Alliance Remnant was one of the major opponents of Krayt's empire. Admiral Gar Stazi, the Alliance's leader, heard of the Imperious, and knew this was something they couldn't pass up. Stazi made plans to steal it, asking his old friend Gial Gahan to assist with it.

The ship was named in memory of Jedi Master Belth Allusis,

The Allusis was the setting for a battle between Republic, Sith, and Mandalorian forces after Clan Varad hijacked the ship out of the Republic shipyards at Fondor.

entities.name: Almost Authentic
entities.description:
The First Edition was a Surronian L19 heavy freighter bought by Moff Aricos Dreleene under the erroneous assumption that it was an exclusive model that he could show off in parties. Discovering that it was a mass-production ship, Dreleene spent a fortune modifying it for his pompous purposes.

The ship and the Moff later ended up in the custody of the Rebel Alliance, where Moff Dreleene was imprisoned and the First Edition was renamed the Almost Authentic for use as a transport.

The First Edition was one of the first Surronian L19 heavy freighters built for its second production. Imperial Moff Aricos Dreleene mistakenly believed it was an "L19a" luxury, exclusive model, and bought the ship to show it in important meetings on Coruscant he was invited to.

Discovering it was not what he had thought, Dreleene spent 220,000 credits to customize it, faking any ID. He then introduced his new ship as the only Surronian ship big enough for his collection of furniture and trophies.

entities.name: Antara Satrap
entities.description: Antara Satrap was a starship that once visited the lost planet Endelaan. As such, navigational information concerning the planet's location was located in its logs. The Antara Satrap was boarded by the Wookiee criminal Renarra, who wanted information on the location of Endelaan. Eventually, the ship was stolen, leading the ship Spiral Dancer on a chase through the Outer Rim.

entities.name: Aramadia
entities.description:
Aramadia was an Imperial Super Star Destroyer used by the Duskhan League.

Like all Super Star Destroyers, the Aramadia was a wedge-shaped warship and at least several kilometers in length. The vessel was fitted with a secret slave circuit system that linked it to other Imperial ships captured by the Yevethans. When activated, the vessel's controls were overridden and the craft could be remotely controlled.

After Nil Spaar used the lead ship of the Aramadia-class on his diplomatic journey to Coruscant, one of the captured Black Fleet Super Star Destroyers was used during the Battle of N'zoth, going by this name as well.

The ship, along with the Pride of Yevetha and seven other Imperial vessels, was retaken by Imperial personnel led by Sil Sorannan when they rebelled against their Yevethan masters. After reaching the Deep Core, the vessel was seemingly abandoned by Sorannan and his forces.

entities.name: Arkanoid
entities.description:
The Arkanoid was a Zeta-class long-range shuttle in service to the Galactic Empire.

Scavenged by the Zabrak P'laang Ri from the Empire, the Zeta-class shuttle was borrowed by the Human Han Solo shortly after the Battle of Yavin to infiltrate and steal an Imperial shipment from Zoma Station. Having left his personal starship the Millennium Falcon with the indebted Ri on Siskeen for safekeeping, Han Solo, accompanied by the Wookiee Chewbacca and fellow Human smuggler Avik Lore, piloted the Arkanoid to Zoma Station.

As it departed from Siskeen, the Zeta-class shuttle—noted by Solo to be far smaller than the Millennium Falcon—had its hydraulics conduit burst at the beginning of the hyperspace voyage to Zoma Station, leading to a cabin filled with what Solo thought was the unpleasant scent of "wet Wookiee fur."

Eager to leave the Imperial shuttle, Han Solo beamed a transmission via comlink to Zoma Station upon the Arkanoid return to realspace, attempting to secure permission to board with authorization codes obtained by Avik Lore on the black market prior. Without any Imperial entanglements, the Arkanoid was allowed to land on the station as the latter's tractor beam activated and led the Zeta-class into its docking bay.
entities.short_description: The Arkanoid was a Zeta-class long-range shuttle in service to the Galactic Empire.

entities.name: Ars Opus
entities.description:
Ars Opus was a BFF-1 bulk freighter that was carrying R2-series astromech droids to the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Invincible when it apparently broke down in the Rudrig system.

The Ars Opus was discovered by a Rebel R-22 Spearhead reconnaissance flight and, following a recent warning from Ordnance and Supply about a shortage of astromech droids, the Rebels decided to mount a capture operation.

However, the carriage also lured pirates that attempted to hijack it and claim the units. A pirate force of transports and Y-wings battled briefly against Rebel R-22 Spearheads from Red Squadron led by Keyan Farlander. The Rebels were able to hold off the pirates while the crew of the Lambda-class T-4a shuttle Rescue Riker boarded and captured the freighter. More R-22s from Blue Squadron arrived to escort the newly captured freighter and the pirates were unable to get close enough to prevent its escape.

The Rebels later discovered that the Ars Opus and its cargo had been used as bait by the Galactic Empire as part of a plan to capture some Rebel X-wings and their pilots. The R2 units had been deliberately programmed to hijack any X-wings they were used in. Three X-wings from Blue Squadron fell into the trap and were hijacked during a mission.
entities.short_description: Ars Opus was a BFF-1 bulk freighter that was carrying R2-series astromech droids to the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Invincible when it apparently broke down in the Rudrig system.

entities.name: Asaari Wind
entities.description:
The Asaari Wind was a SoroSuub Personal Luxury Yacht 3000 owned by the Bimm crime lord Ritinki around 0 ABY. The vessel was heavily modified by the Bimm, and featured luxurious appointments and offensive capabilities far in excess of its original specifications.

During a summit held by Ritinki and the Rodian kingpin Vop on the Ithorian Herdship Song of the Clouds, the Asaari Wind was commandeered by the thief Cecil Noone and his partners-in-crime, with Ritinki being killed in the course of the theft. Under Noone's ownership, the yacht operated under the aliases Hieroglyph, Spiraling Shape, Tailchaser, and Voona's Dream II. The vessel sustained severe damage amid the crew's frantic escape from the planet Kabal after Noone's dealings with the Krish business magnate Tyro Viveca went awry.

The Asaari Wind was a Personal Luxury Yacht 3000 manufactured by the SoroSuub Corporation. While in the ownership of the Bimm crime lord Ritinki, the Asaari Wind had been modified. Its armaments included two light laser cannons and two medium ion cannons, all of which were linked and front-mounted and could be fired from the bridge, and twin heavy laser cannon turrets, as well as a rear-facing turbolaser mounted in place of the external observation platform typical of most yachts.

The Asaari Wind could reach sublight speeds of 1,000 kilometers per hour, and was equipped with shields and sensors, as well as primary and secondary hyperdrives. The latter, and the yacht's standard repulsorlifts and ion engines, were replaced with components used in much larger ships, including state-of-the-art Sienar Fleet Systems drives. A slave circuit paired with a beckoncall transmitter enabled Ritinki to summon the Asaari Wind remotely; having been designed exclusively for Ritinki by a moonlighting Industrial Automaton engineer, the transmitter activated the yacht's engines and used the ignition command as a homing signal, which guided the ship to the Bimm's location. Measuring fifty meters in length, the Asaari Wind could carry seventy metric tons of cargo, and accomodated two crewmembers and three gunners for basic operations, with a skeleton complement of between one and ten. The yacht also had capacity for ten passengers, and toted a month's worth of consumables.

entities.name: Asagov Raider
entities.description:
The Asagov Raider, formerly known as the Cekbar Servant, was a Corellian Engineering Corporation Action IV transport operating during the early years of the New Republic. Originally a merchant vessel registered to Nalroni businessmen on the trading world of Celanon, the ship was captured by the Saurton pirate Miktiss around 7 ABY. Miktiss had the vessel heavily modified and renamed as the Asagov Raider, using the medium bulk freighter as his flagship and as the command base of the Des'maric Pirates. The Asagov Raider was a mobile headquarters for the organization while they operated in the Kathol sector in 8 ABY.

The Asagov Raider was a Corellian Engineering Corporation Action IV transport. and measured 100 meters in length. Although standard models came unarmed, the Asagov Raider was heavily modified to serve as a pirate vessel by the Saurton Miktiss. The ship boasted eight ion cannons and twelve double laser cannons. The ion cannons were placed evenly around the medium bulk freighter for maximum coverage, while the laser cannons were concentrated to the fore, with some weapons covering the port and starboard fire arcs. Other modifications included stronger shield generators, increased sublight speed, and detention cells on the lower level.

The ship was equipped with a navigation computer for plotting hyperspace jumps, and a Class 3 hyperdrive, with a Class 15 as a backup. Crewed by fifteen beings, the Asagov Raider also required a complement of forty gunners to operate effectively. A skeleton crew of eight personnel and ten gunners could run the ship, but at a cost of efficiency. The vessel could carry 60,000 metric tons of cargo, and store consumables for the crew to last 3 months.

Commissioned as a medium bulk freighter, the Cekbar Servant was originally owned by a consortium of Nalroni merchants from the planet Celanon, Around 7 ABY, the Saurton pirate Miktiss, head of the Des'maric Pirates, captured the vessel shortly after acquiring a trio of Skipray Blastboats from the planet Elshandruu Pica. Realizing that, in its current state, it was not a vessel fit for piracy, Miktiss forced a former Sienar Fleet Systems engineer—through a combination of blackmail and bargaining—to modify the ship to his specifications. The engineer complied, fitting the ship out with extra weapons, stronger shield generators, and a faster sublight drive.

entities.name: Ataraxia
entities.description:
In 90 BBY, the Ataraxia was used to transport a number of Jedi to the Outer Rim planet Serenno, in order for Jedi initiates to attend a celebration of the planets and cultures of the galactic region. When one initiate, Dooku, was insulted by fellow initiate Arath Tarrex, he suggested fighting back, but his friend Sifo-Dyas told him that they would be punished as a result, and forced to remain on the Ataraxia for the duration of the event.

The Ataraxia was first mentioned in the audio drama Dooku: Jedi Lost, written by Cavan Scott The spelling of the starship's name was confirmed by the script release of the audiobook on October 1 of that year.

The vessel subsequently featured in the Star Wars: The High Republic publishing initiative. It was first pictured, albeit not identified as the Ataraxia, in a preview released on StarWars.com on December 1, 2020 for the second issue of the Marvel Comics series of the same name, written by Scott and illustrated by Ario Anindito. while the release of The High Republic 2 on February 3, 2021 connected the name to the ship depicted in the preview.

entities.description:
Atron's Mistress was a custom Zuraco Cargo Hauler owned by the Karazak Slavers Cooperative and used to transport slaves around the galaxy. The ship was commandeered by the Red Moons while on Gabredor III after destroying the Karazak base there and freeing the slaves.

entities.name: Auberge
entities.description:
The Auberge, formerly known as the Glitterstim Shine, was a war cruiser owned by a spice dealer from Kijimi until it was confiscated by the Nihil after the formation of the Stormwall. It eventually became the flagship of General Abediah Viess, with the heavy cruiser serving at the Battle of Eriadu.

entities.name: Azure Queen
entities.description:
The Azure Queen was an Action IV transport that was used during the time of the Galactic Republic.

The Azure Queen once sent to transport a cargo of bacta and medical supplies that was worth at least 500,000 credits to the planet Rutan. However, while en route there, the Queen received a distress call from someone who was claiming to be a Republic ambassador, so it diverted it's course, to investigate. However, the call had actually been sent by a group of Black Sun pirates from their YU-410 light freighter Cutting Strike. The Strike ambushed the Queen on the edge of an asteroid field and the pirates jammed the transport's hyperwave transmitter, although the captain of the Queen was able to send out a distress call moments before. The pirates then fired on the Queen, taking its hyperdrive off-line and leaving the ship stranded. A Black Sun boarding party took control of the vessel and began carrying out repairs, so that they could move the ship to Black Sun territory.

The distress call was picked up by the Republic and they sent an ILH-KK Citadel-class cruiser to retake the Queen. The cruiser ambushed the Cutting Strike and then sent Republic troops over to the Azure Queen, to recapture it.

entities.name: Bastion
entities.description:
Bastion was an ancient refueling tanker Wraith Squadron captured on Halmad during a mission disguised as the Hawk-bat Independent Space Force. Wraith pilot Kell Tainer rigged the tanker to blow upon a signal from him, which the Wraiths planned to use in demolishing a newly constructed starfighter base near the city of Hullis on Halmad.

Their plan failed however, when Warlord Zsinj's flagship Iron Fist used its tractor beams on the Bastion. Improvising, Tainer and his group escaped by flying the Narra out of Bastion hold, and then detonating the tanker as it approached Iron Fist hangar bay.

entities.name: Beauty of Yevetha
entities.description:
The Beauty of Yevetha was the name given to a corvette captured by the Duskhan League from the Galactic Empire's Black Sword Command circa 4 ABY. The vessel was subsequently used by Nil Spaar to scout the Koornacht Cluster, and then formed part of Yevethan fleet.

The Beauty was a small capital ship. Airlock doors on the underside of the hull concealed a compact docking berth, designed to carry a pinnace, but capable of accommodating a small starfighter such as a Recon-X. A tractor beam was used to pull ships towards the bay, but mechanical docking clamps deployed at close range to pull them inside.

The original name of this Imperial corvette is not known, and the circumstances of the ship's takeover by the Yevetha are unclear. The vessel was presumably captured intact in one of the twelve Duskhan League systems when the Imperial occupation forces were overthrown in 4 ABY, in a similar way to the much larger Star Destroyers Intimidator and Valorous.

Renamed the Beauty of Yevetha, the vessel was probably the first ship with a hyperdrive to be brought into active service by the Yevetha. Nil Spaar took command, and used the vessel to explore the surrounding systems, with a crew including his loyal second, Dar Bille. The Yevetha were shocked to discover that the Empire had allowed other sentient species to establish settlements in the outer systems of the Koornacht Cluster, which they considered to be their own sacrosanct territory.

entities.name: Beggar's Solace
entities.description:
Beggar's Solace was a Starlight-class light freighter owned by the smuggler Jin-Jin, who stole it from the hangar bay at the academy on Carida where he served as a TIE pilot. His original plan was to steal an advanced TIE fighter, but he was caught in the process. He managed to escape in the Solace, but unfortunately its hyperdrive motivator initiated prematurely and the ship went off on a wild trip through hyperspace. Jin-Jin subsequently was forced into stripping the ship of parts which he sold on the black market to recoup his losses. When he started his career as a smuggler and mercenary, Jin-Jin made enough money to refit the Solace and turn it from a rampaged bucket of bolts into a useful rampaged bucket of bolts. The ship was crewed by Jin-Jin and his R2 unit, which served as a navigator, and was used on smuggling runs, for transport of personnel and also as an escape vehicle on various sabotage and theft missions.

entities.name: Bestoon Legacy
entities.description:
The Bestoon Legacy was a modified WTK-85A interstellar transport and the personal starship of the assassin Ochi of Bestoon.

Ochi used the Bestoon Legacy throughout his assassin career, including during the quest to find the child Rey, granddaughter of the resurrected Sith Lord Darth Sidious. During the quest, Ochi allied with the Corporate Sector Authority and their liaison Enric Pryde, a former Imperial officer. The craft was briefly stolen by Rey's parents, Miramir and Dathan, to return Rey to the planet Jakku, only for a drunken Ochi to kill them and reclaim his ship. Traveling to the planet Pasaana on a false lead on Rey's location, Ochi died after sinking in the Shifting Mires, leaving his ship behind. For years the ship the intakes and thrusters began to fill with sand-clogs and nomadic solif-spiders left tons of silk strands.

During the First Order-Resistance War, the ship was used by Poe Dameron, Finn, Rey, C-3PO, and BB-8 after the First Order captured the Millennium Falcon. After Rey apparently killed Chewbacca by accident, the group escaped Pasaana in the ship, with Poe hiding the ship in an asteroid belt. Though they lost the dagger, its inscription was in C-3PO's memory. So, the group decided to head to Kijimi so that Babu Frik can perform a memory bypass, unaware that the Night Buzzard, the Knights of Ren's ship, was following them. The ship made planetfall and landed in Kijimi City, which was cracking down under the First Order's occupation.

After Babu Frik successfully retrieved the translation at the cost of C-3PO's memories, the group returned to the Bestoon Legacy and flew to the Steadfast hovering above the city to rescue Chewbacca. Poe used Zorii Bliss' First Order Captain's Medallion to get clearance to land aboard one of the ship's hangars, Hangar 12. Allegiant General Pryde, the very same former Imperial whom had met Ochi and seen his ship up close, and a detachment of stormtroopers went into the hangar, where Pryde was surprised to see the vessel and asked one of his subordinates who the ship belonged to. Poe Dameron's group later recovered the Falcon and rescued Chewbacca, and the First Order met its demise soon after.

entities.name: Binder
entities.description:
Binder was an Imperial Interdictor-class Star Destroyer given to the command of Admiral Delak Krennel by Ysanne Isard for use in the evacuation of Ciutric. Its captain was Phulik.

The Binder was severely damaged by Aggressor Wing during the battle, but was later repaired and served in the fleet of the Ciutric Hegemony, when the self-proclaimed "Prince-Admiral" took control of the region. In the Battle of Ciutric, the Binder surrendered to the New Republic after Krennel was killed and his flagship Reckoning was destroyed. When the Hegemony entered the New Republic, the ship and its crew were integrated into its defense force and remained at Ciutric IV.

The Binder makes an appearance in Star Wars: Empire at War as a Sienar Immobilizer 418 cruiser. The ship's name is listed to appear randomly when the player uses one of these ships during gameplay.

entities.name: Bixby
entities.description:
Bixby was a Corellian Corvette that served in the Imperial Navy during the Galactic Civil War.

During a hit and fade strike against an Imperial convoy leaving the Dellalt system as part of a resupply operation ahead of a suspected Imperial offensive, Blue Squadron reported that the crew of Bixby wanted to defect. Captain Hamo Blastwell and Lieutenant Keyan Farlander were scrambled to destroy the convoy, consisting of BFF-1 bulk freighters Arreis, Orcim, Esorp, Nigiro and Murtceps while Y-wings guarded Bixby. The transport Dagger docked with the corvette and transferred an Alliance team to secure the ship. The Imperial Nebulon-B escort frigate Gorgon arrived too late to prevent the now captured ship from returning with the Alliance team. Bixby's commander, Captain Nogdra, revealed that the Empire was planning a major offensive called Operation Strike Fear, beginning in that system.

entities.name: Black Ice
entities.description:
Black Ice was the name of a train of two Field Secured Container Vessels containing nine linked force-field fuel spheres that was used by the Galactic Empire's Imperial Navy. Black Ice was manufactured by Rendili StarDrive and was assigned to the Imperial Replenishment Fleet DK-209 as a key part of the support fleet. Black Ice was roughly five Imperial-class Star Destroyers in length, and each fuel sphere could hold 110 million tons of fuel each, in total nearing one billion tons of starship fuel. The quantity was enough to supply a full Imperial battle fleet for one year.

Black Ice was stolen by the Alliance to Restore the Republic after the destruction of the Choah Belt fuel refinery by the Empire, although Black Ice was later destroyed in a collision.

entities.name: Blackguard
entities.description:
The Blackguard was an Imperial-class Star Destroyer, that was captured by the rogue Imperial Captain—and self-proclaimed Grand Admiral—Andal Sait, with intention of selling it to the criminal organization Black Sun.

In the Township of Aurilia there were contact persons from both the Galactic Empire and the Rebel Alliance, but also an independent investor called Hirael Chindiaye, who, unlike both the Rebel Alliance and the Galactic Empire, who sought to capture/reclaim the rogue Star Destroyer for military purposes, wanted to capture the Star Destroyer for personal interests.

All three factions managed to recruit a team of spacers, who managed to intercept the Star Destroyer when it was stationed in the Ord Mantell system, and, with some assistance of surviving crew still loyal to the Empire, managed to force their way into the Hangar Bay of the ship, and fought their way through the Star Destroyer, and even though most of the crew that had remained loyal to the Empire had either fled, or been "taken care of". It proved to be a tough fight, as Admiral Sait had managed to gather several sympathizers among the crew, along with Black Sun members.

The final fate of the Blackguard was unknown, which one of the factions that managed to wrestle the control of the ship, was quickly covered up by the Empire, information about the Empire losing one of their mightiest warships was nothing they would wished to see on the Imperial HoloVision. It was however known that Admiral Sait most likely perished in the ensuing combat aboard the bridge, along with other highly ranked rogue Imperials and Black Sun members, present to make sure that Sait did not break the deal.
