entities.name: Whip Hand
entities.description:
Whip Hand was a Lancer-class frigate that was initially operated by the Galactic Empire before it was captured. Later put to use by the New Republic during the Yuuzhan Vong War, Whip Hand participated in a battle in 28 ABY against Yuuzhan Vong forces in the Obroa-skai system before being assigned to guard the crippled cruiser Far Thunder as it made its way to the planet Kashyyyk. However, both ships were ambushed by enemy coralskippers, and, despite managing to repel the starfighters with the help of two New Republic squadrons, Whip Hand was forced to destroy the crippled Far Thunder to prevent the enemy from acquiring it.

Whip Hand was a Lancer-class frigate produced by Kuat Drive Yards and was designed to battle swarms of starfighters. Equipped with a hyperdrive and sublight engines, the 250-meter-long frigate was armed with turbolasers and possessed a bridge.

During the early part of the Galactic Civil War, which pitted the Galactic Empire against the Rebel Alliance, Whip Hand served as an Imperial vessel until it was captured. The Lancer-class frigate ended up in the hands of the New Republic, the Alliance's successor state, and a refurbished Whip Hand was operational in the New Republic Defense Fleet during the Yuuzhan Vong War, in which the extra-galactic Yuuzhan Vong species invaded the galaxy. Whip Hand participated in an attack on a Yuuzhan Vong fleet in the Obroa-skai system. The frigate and the rest of a New Republic task force waited until the captured Yuuzhan Vong frigate Trickster signaled them before jumping in-system to make it appear as if they were tailing the Trickster and were caught unawares by the Yuuzhan Vong fleet there. The enemy forces fell for the ruse, and the resulting battle ended in the destruction of the majority of the Yuuzhan Vong fleet.

Directly following the Obroa-skai battle, the New Republic's base was shifted to the planet Kashyyyk, and Whip Hand was assigned to guard the Republic-class cruiser Far Thunder as it limped to the Kashyyyk system. The cruiser had been seriously damaged in the fighting at Obroa-skai, and the majority of Far Thunder personnel were evacuated to leave the cruiser with a skeleton crew on its journey. However, after the pair of capital ships met up with a tender that contained spare parts for Far Thunder, the three ships were attacked in deep space by around sixty coralskippers launched from a pair of Yuuzhan Vong tenders. Although designed as an anti-starfighter frigate, Whip Hand could not protect both itself and the crippled Far Thunder from the attacking coralskippers, prompting Hannser, the cruiser's captain, to issue a call for help after the Far Thunder hyperdrive engines were destroyed.

entities.name: Whisper
entities.description:
The Whisper was a 3-Z light freighter that was used by the Rebel Alliance scout team the Gray Griffins during the Galactic Civil War. After the Gray Griffins were assigned to perform some exploration work on the behalf of the Radell Mining Corporation, the Griffins flew the freighter to the Elrood sector and they discovered the planet Alluuvia. However, the Whisper was captured by The Scourge, a local pirate group, and the Griffins were imprisoned. The pirates then sold the freighter to the Squib crime lord Slythor, who stored the vessel in space, near to the planet Korad.

A team of Rebel Alliance agents were sent to recover the co-ordinates of Alluuvia from the Whisper computer and the agents negotiated with Slythor for access to the freighter. A pair of Slythor's Verpine hoppers escorted the agents to the Whisper location and the Rebels entered the vessel. However, during its time near Korad, the Whisper had became infested with mynocks and space mites, and the creatures attacked the agents. The Rebels defeated the creatures, then obtained the co-ordinates and departed Korad.

entities.name: World Devastator
entities.description:
This World Devastator was a former Imperial starship used by the New Republic.

The Devastator survived the sabotage of the collective system of the deadly factory ship fleets at the conclusion of the Battle of Calamari in 10 ABY. It was reprogrammed by the New Republic, who used it to devour and recycle derelict space craft in orbit of Da Soocha V. However, the ship, and any other World Devastators that the New Republic captured, ended up scrapped after a public outcry.

Dark Horse Comics editor Bob Cooper indicates that this World Devastator was scuttled above Da Soocha V.

entities.name: Yissira Zyde
entities.description:
The Yissira Zyde was an NK-Witell-class freighter that operated as a free trader during the New Republic Era. The starship was valuable to the First Order, so they entered the Mirrin sector of New Republic space and hijacked the vessel. Rapier Squadron of the Republic received a distress signal from the freighter, and engaged the First Order's forces. However, the Republic responded too late and the stolen ship entered hyperspace. Intent on locating the commandeered freighter, Poe Dameron of Rapier Squadron began an unsanctioned mission to find the vessel and prove the First Order's involvement. Determining the Yissira Zyde possible trajectories, he tracked the ship to OR-Kappa-2722 and encountered First Order forces. Once Dameron detected the Yissira Zyde was aboard a Resurgent-class Star Destroyer, he retreated back into New Republic territory.

The Yissira Zyde first appeared in Before the Awakening, a junior novel written by Greg Rucka and published in 2015.

entities.name: Zeplin
entities.description:
The Zeplin was a Victory-class Star Destroyer in the service of the Galactic Empire. It was commanded by Namuura Din, an Imperial captain who followed Admiral Demetrius Zaarin's defection from the Empire shortly before the Battle of Endor.

Namuura Din had grown sympathetic to the cause of the Rebel Alliance, so the two sides met to discuss his defection. The Zeplin met with the Mon Calamari Star Cruiser Link, and as part of their deal, Din delivered Missile Boat Sealion to the Rebel vessel. The Imperials, unwilling to lose such valuable technology to the Alliance, sent a strike force to stop the Zeplin and the Link.

Unfortunately for the Empire, the Link escaped into hyperspace with the newly acquired Missile Boat. Darth Vader pursued the vessel while ace pilot Maarek Stele and his force attacked the Zeplin. Flying a Missile Boat, Stele brought down the Victory Star Destroyer's shields so Assault Gunboats could disable it. Imperial transports and the Imperial-class Star Destroyer Garrett soon overtook the Zeplin, and Namuura Din was captured. The Zeplin was then taken to an Imperial shipyard so that it could be inspected.

entities.description:
The Hutt crimelord Zodoh's military forces included a twin-seater starfighter. It was a twin-seater version of the Intruder-class starfighter.

These starfighters were kept aboard Zodoh's fighter carrier and flagship Voracious during the Republic Dark Age. Following the Aquilaris campaign, the Grace Command Captain Jenn Devaad stole one of these fighters during her escape from Zodoh. Later, she flew the starfighter to Aquilaris where she picked up Jedi Knight Kerra Holt and disembarked for Darkknell.

entities.name: Zorba Express
entities.description:
The Zorba Express, also known as Zorba's Express, was an ancient starship that belonged to Zorba the Hutt, shady businessman and father of the famous crime lord Jabba Desilijic Tiure.

A typical bell-shaped Huttian starship, When standing upright, the starship resembled a domed building distinguished by several spires. Its boarding hatch was shaped like a diaphragm shutter and could be accessed by a ramp. The cockpit of the Zorba Express was roomy enough to fit a Hutt, an astromech-sized droid and at least another passenger.

During the second month of 22 BBY, Zorba was imprisoned on the muddy planet of Kip for the illegal removal of ulikuo gemstones, and the Zorba Express was abandoned on a cliff immediately after the Hutt's capture. However, the native inhabitants of Kip never figured out how to fly that spaceship. As a consequence, the Zorba Express was still waiting for its owner, when Zorba was freed by a group of pirates in 5 ABY. By that time, the Zorba Express was very much in disrepair; some observers believed that the vessel would not even be able to break the sound barrier after several more trips if it was not serviced.

Despite that, Zorba still used his personal transport to get to Tatooine, a desert planet that had been the fiefdom of his son, Jabba. After discovering that Jabba had been murdered by Princess Leia Organa, Zorba laid claim to much of his son's properties throughout the galaxy. He took off in the Zorba Express, bound for the floating metropolis of Cloud City, in which Jabba once owned a casino.

entities.name: Zyle's shuttle
entities.description:
Zyle's shuttle was a Nihil escape shuttle utilized by the Nihil marauders that was held in a hangar aboard the vessel of the captain I'nah. In 229 BBY, the shuttle was stolen by the young pirate Zyle Keem, whose mother, Tanana Keem, had stopped aboard I'nah's vessel to barter goods. Keem flew the shuttle to the planet Valo, where they had overheard there was valuable bacta aboard the sunken vessel Innovator. However, as Keem attempted to land on Valo, the shuttle's navigation system deactivated and its wings began to fall apart, forcing them to make an emergency landing. The shuttle was severely damaged in the process and exploded shortly after Keem disembarked. After meeting the Jedi Padawan Ram Jomaram and the younglings Gavi, Kildo, and Tep Tep, who were fighting back against the Nihil occupation of the planet, the group decided to raid the Innovator together. The group retrieved the wreckage of Zyle's shuttle and salvaged components from it to modify Jomaram's ship, an Eviscerator.

entities.name: Darkfire
entities.description:
The Darkfire was the name of the starship captained by Flandon Sweeg in Rogar Farnoster's The Slug Named Grendel.

The work the Darkfire appeared in bears strong similarities with the 1851 novel [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moby_Dick Moby Dick], authored by [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Melville Herman Melville]. Such similarities includes the formatting of the first line and the narrative of the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishmael_(Moby-Dick) protagonist] who has joined a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pequod_(Moby-Dick) crew] upon a quest led by a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_Ahab captain] of questionable morals after a sizable limbless, ship-destroying [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moby_Dick_(whale) creature] colored white.

entities.description:
The Millennium Fist was a freighter with two giant green gloves on its front. It was allegedly an old ship of Han Solo's that Lando Calrissian kept lying around on Cloud City. However, the Millennium Fist was in fact just a parody of the Millennium Falcon, invented by Han Solo while telling a story to his son Anakin.

entities.name: Pulsar Station
entities.description:
The Pulsar Station was a Death Star-like system domination weapon planned by the Ciutric Hegemony.

The Pulsar Station was a drastically scaled-down version of the original Death Star battle stations, inspired by the way the Emperor utilized the second Death Star at the Battle of Endor—for the destruction of capital ships.

Along its equatorial plane were a number of gravity-well generators to halt all hyperspace traffic in and out of local space. The superlaser was also scaled down and numerous superlaser emplacements were installed, each capable of destroying a Super Star Destroyer. Its capabilities were rounded off by half a dozen TIE wings and smaller anti-ship weapons.

Though detailed schematics for the station were created, there were never any intentions to implement such a weapon, which was supposedly being built into the moon of Distna in the Corvis Minor system. The designs were allowed to fall into the hands of the New Republic at the Battle of Liinade III. The Pulsar Station was nothing more than an elaborate charade by ex-Imperial Empress Ysanne Isard to lure Rogue Squadron to aid her in her quest to destroy her rogue clone and Prince-Admiral Delak Krennel.

entities.name: 13X
entities.description:
13X was the name of a Victory-class Star Destroyer of the Galactic Empire's Imperial Starfleet which was under the overall command of the self-styled High Admiral Treuten Teradoc some eight years after the Battle of Endor.

After the final death of Palpatine, Teradoc maintained a whole flotilla of Victory-class Star Destroyers under his command, all with their hulls armored with a red-colored alloy, earning them the name Crimson Command. When Admiral Daala attacked Teradoc's forces under the flag of another warlord, Supreme Warlord Harrsk, Crimson Command was under the leadership of then-Vice Admiral Gilad Pellaeon with the 13X as the flotilla's flagship.

When Daala asserted full control from many of the warlords of the Deep Core, Pellaeon was given command of forty-five of the larger Imperial-class Star Destroyers and Crimson Command was given over to Colonel Cronus. From the bridge of the 13X, Cronus successfully conducted a series of attacks and raids throughout the New Republic before rejoining Daala's fleet at Yavin 4.

There, in pitched battle against a New Republic fleet, a damaged Corellian gunship rammed the bridge of the 13X, killing Cronus and annihilating the warship.

entities.description:
Abrogator was an Imperial Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser that acted as the flagship of the fleet sent to Saloch 2 to quell a group of Lortans during the Reslian Purge.

The sixth squadron of the 37th Imperial Fighter Wing was assigned to the Abrogator, under the command of Captain Lun Tessra. Lieutenant Soontir Fel was posted to the squadron after graduation from the Imperial Academy, and eventually rose to command the unit.

entities.name: Acidity
entities.description:
The Acidity was a Star Destroyer in the Imperial Navy during the Galactic Civil War. It served as the personal Star Destroyer and flagship of Grand Moff Randd, who commanded the Imperial fleet from the bridge of the Acidity during the Battle of Jakku.

The Acidity was first mentioned in the 2017 reference book Star Wars: On the Front Lines, written by Daniel Wallace.

In Aftermath: Empire's End, it is established that Randd commanded Imperial forces from the Super Star Destroyer Ravager. However, the newer book Star Wars: On the Front Lines conversely states that Randd commanded Imperial forces from the Acidity.

entities.name: Admiral Korvin
entities.description:
Admiral Korvin was an ex-Trade Federation Captor-class heavy munitions cruiser, assigned by Wilhuff Tarkin as the command ship of Raith Sienar's small fleet for his mission to Zonama Sekot in 29 BBY. It is not known who the ship was named after, or indeed if it was named after anyone. Its commander was Captain Kett.

The Admiral Korvin was regarded by "Commander" Sienar as an old, small, and poorly-equipped ship. She was markedly smaller and less powerful than the Rim Merchant Einem, which was selected by Tarkin as his own command ship, and the Einem was in turn a smaller cousin of the militarized LH-3210 cargo haulers which had formed the backbone of Nute Gunray's attack on Naboo.

Like that of many Trade Federation ships, the Admiral Korvin main strength was concentrated in automated systems—including B1-series battle droids, a force of at least thirty droid starfighters, three landing craft, and a contingent of E-5 battle droids, new models that looked like walking tanks. Nevertheless, the Admiral Korvin also carried a hundred Human troops, and a two-seater Taxon-class probe ship with a living pilot.

entities.name: Admonitor
entities.description:
The Admonitor was an upgraded Imperial-class Star Destroyer under the Empire of the Hand and had served as the command vessel of Grand Admiral Thrawn during the Galactic Empire exploration and conquest of the Unknown Regions. Thrawn had use of this capital ship during periods of his service in the Imperial Navy.

The Admonitor first reported commander was Dagon Niriz. When Grand Admiral Thrawn was assigned to the Unknown Regions, it was this ship which he departed on; his longtime associate, Voss Parck, was assigned as the ship's first officer.

One of the Admonitor first encounters on this mission was with Ebruchi pirates, which Thrawn was able to deal with effectively.

Later, the Admonitor returned briefly to the Galactic Empire so Thrawn could assist Darth Vader in the removal of Zekka Thyne, and thus Black Sun's influence, from Corellia.

entities.name: Aggressor
entities.description:
The Aggressor was an Executor-class Star Dreadnought in the service of the Galactic Empire. Commanded by Admiral Roek, the Aggressor and a force of five Imperial-class Star Destroyers were part of the fleet that patrolled the Inner Rim. Six months after the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY, the Aggressor and its escorts were recalled to the Imperial shipyards at Corellia, where they defended the Imperial withdrawal from the system as the New Republic—formerly the Rebel Alliance—began conquering planets in the Core Worlds.

By 5 ABY, the Aggressor was in the hands of Grand Admiral Josef Grunger, one of the first Imperial warlords and a man loyal only to himself. Grunger bullied Imperial officers into turning over their ships to his command, gathering a sizable armada of Star Destroyers and smaller cruisers. The Grand Admiral led this flotilla from the Aggressor and plotted to use his fleet to seize the Imperial capital world of Coruscant, utilizing the Corellian sector as a launch point. However, the sector had already been taken by fellow Grand Admiral Danetta Pitta; when Grunger's forces arrived in the Corellian system, Pitta took command of a Torpedo Sphere siege platform and began decimating his rival's fleet. Grunger, faced with the likelihood of defeat, rammed his flagship into the Torpedo Sphere, an act that killed both Grand Admirals and destroyed both vessels.

The Aggressor was the third Executor-class Star Dreadnought manufactured for the Galactic Empire, and the second warship of that class built at Kuat Drive Yards. The Aggressor was one of many such capital ships serving the fragmenting Empire in the years following the death of Emperor Palpatine at the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY. The warship served as a flagship and command vessel.

The third Executor-class warship to be manufactured, the Aggressor was the flagship of Admiral Roek, a cunning Imperial commander. Assigned an escort of five Imperial-class Star Destroyers, the Aggressor patrolled the Inner Rim. Approximately six months following the Battle of Endor, the Aggressor and its escorts were recalled to guard the Imperial-held shipyards at Corellia. Information on this reassignment, sent from the Imperial capital of Coruscant, was intercepted by the New Republic and utilized in preparations for an eventual New Republic assault on the capital planet. The Aggressor defended the Imperial withdrawal from the Corellian system as the New Republic began its conquest of the Core Worlds.

entities.description:
The Agonizer was an Imperial-class Star Destroyer and the flagship of Admiral Teren Rogriss's Anti-Zsinj Task Force. It housed the 181st Imperial Fighter Group and was sent to Adumar to open negotiations with the Adumari.

After Adumar decided to join the New Republic, the Agonizer was ordered to subjugate the planet. The New Republic sent a defensive fleet to drive the Imperials off, and the Agonizer took heavy damage during the battle, but managed to escape.

entities.name: Agrelcu Haalta
entities.description:
The Agrelcu Haalta, which could be translated as the Aggressive Defender in Basic, was a Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser that served as the flagship of Troonol. It was the command ship of a Qunaalac fleet that patrolled the Bootana Hutta region of Hutt Space.

During the Galactic Civil War, Troonol's fleet protected the Bootana Hutta region of Hutt Space. His fleet consisted of ten Qunaalac warships which he led from his command ship, the Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser Agrelcu Haalta. The rest of his fleet was a collection of Corellian gunships.

Troonol's fleet heavily patrolled the Pabol Hutta hyperspace route through the Bootana Hutta, where outlanders were not allowed to travel. His fleet regularly patrolled the route between the guardian worlds of Gos Hutta and Mulatan and, more periodically, the routes to Elgit and Varl.

entities.name: Albedo Brave
entities.description:
The Albedo Brave was a Venator-class Star Destroyer in the navy of the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars. It served as the command ship of Jedi General Jaro Tapal and his 13th Battalion of clone troopers, who led a campaign to defend the Bracca system from the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Shortly after the campaign, Order 66 was executed, forcing Tapal and his Padawan, Cal Kestis, to escape from their clone troopers. Tapal sabotaged the reactor of the Albedo Brave to conceal their escape, but was fatally wounded before he could board an escape pod. Kestis escaped the Albedo Brave before its destruction, landing on Bracca, where he would remain for the next five years.

The Albedo Brave first appeared in the 2019 video game Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order, developed by Respawn Entertainment. Concept art for the Venator-class Star Destroyer was done by artist Theo Stylianides.

entities.name: Allegiance
entities.description:
The Allegiance was an Imperial Allegiance-class battlecruiser that participated in the Battle of Calamari in 10 ABY. When the Allegiance began transmitting images of Calamari's destruction to the Deep Core, the New Republic Star Destroyer Emancipator intercepted the transmissions and tracked the Allegiance location. Once the Emancipator dropped out of hyperspace above Calamari, it attacked and destroyed the Allegiance.

The Allegiance was a Super Star Destroyer that served the Galactic Empire after the rebirth of Emperor Palpatine. where it transmitted images of Calamari's destruction to the Deep Core through a hyperspace communications channel. The Allegiance was also equipped with deflector shields.

In 10 ABY, the Allegiance commanded a fleet orbiting the world Calamari. It transmitted images of Calamari's subjugation by the Emperor's latest superweapons, the World Devastators, through a hyperspace communications channel to the Imperial fortress world Byss in the Deep Core. These transmissions were intercepted by the New Republic Star Destroyer Emancipator under the command of Generals Wedge Antilles and Lando Calrissian. The Emancipator, already on its way to Calamari with a fleet of its own, recalculated its exit from hyperspace two degrees from the source of the transmissions.

As the Emancipator and its fleet dropped out of hyperspace, a crew member aboard the Allegiance attempted to contact the World Devastator Silencer-7, but his transmission was cut off mid-sentence as the Emancipator opened fire on the Super Star Destroyer. The Allegiance, caught with its deflector shields down, was easily destroyed, alongside its two Procursator-class Star Destroyer escorts, by concentrated fire from the Emancipator forward weapons, manned by Zevulon Veers, and its wreckage was left to drift in space above Calamari.

entities.name: Anakin Solo
entities.description:
The Anakin Solo, also known as the Anakin for short or Black Annie to its crew, was a modified Imperial II-class Star Destroyer that served as the command ship of the Galactic Alliance Guard during the Second Galactic Civil War—a pan-galactic conflict between the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances and the Confederation. Serving as the personal flagship of Colonel Jacen Solo, the Anakin Solo was named after Solo's deceased brother. The commissioning of a GAG Star Destroyer reflected the Guard's expanding influence and responsibilities; by then the Guard had taken a more active role in the war, whereas their original purpose as a covert police force was to enforce domestic security on the capital world of Coruscant.

Commissioned in 40 ABY at the General Crix Madine Military Reserve of Coruscant, the Anakin Solo secured its first victory at the Battle of Hapes. It was also deployed to Corellia alongside the Galactic Alliance Defense Fleet as a result of the Alliance's decision to blockade the Corellian homeworld in response to the Corellian terrorist attacks on Coruscant. The Anakin Solo would continue to have an active part in the conflict following the withdrawal of Alliance forces from Corellia, participating in several battles across the galaxy at Gilatter VIII, Kuat, Kashyyyk, and Centerpoint Station.

The Anakin Solo also played a role in Jacen Solo's plans as an aspiring Dark Lord of the Sith. Solo, who had secretly renounced his role as a Jedi Knight in favor of becoming the Sith Lord Darth Caedus, tortured his cousin, Ben Skywalker, aboard the Anakin Solo in an effort to convert the young Jedi to the dark side of the Force. The attempt failed, however, leading Caedus to shift his attention to another potential Sith apprentice—the Jedi Knight Tahiri Veila. Veila joined the Galactic Alliance Guard as a junior lieutenant and demonstrated her willingness to become Caedus' apprentice by ordering the Anakin Solo gunners to destroy a squadron of Fondorian starfighters. During the Second Battle of Fondor, the Anakin Solo participated in a joint-fleet operation between the Galactic Alliance and the Imperial Remnant. It was at Fondor where the partnership between Caedus and Admiral Cha Niathal broke apart, resulting in the Anakin Solo return to Coruscant where Caedus secured his position as the sole Chief of State.

The Anakin Solo went on to fight Caedus' enemies at the Battle of Uroro Station in 41 ABY. In the course of the battle, the GAG battleship sustained heavy damage and was boarded by the forces of the Jedi Coalition, resulting in the deaths of many GAG troopers. At the same time, Caedus was confronted by his twin sister, Jaina Solo, who killed the Dark Lord in single combat. With Caedus' death and the fall of the Anakin Solo, the Galactic Alliance reconciled with the New Jedi Order and agreed to a ceasefire with the Confederation, hence marking the end of the Second Galactic Civil War.

entities.name: Arlionne
entities.description:
The Arlionne was a Galactic Republic Victory I-class Star Destroyer that was a part of the Victory Fleet during the Clone Wars. It served as the flagship of Republic Captain Terrinald Screed, and during the Battle of Anaxes it delivered the decisive blow against the Confederacy of Independent Systems battlecruiser Unrepentant that ended the Confederate Admiral Dua Ningo's campaign in the Core Worlds. However, the explosion of the latter starship also damaged the Arlionne, with Screed receiving near-mortal injuries in the process.

The Arlionne was a Victory I-class Star Destroyer, a part of a line of Star Destroyers manufactured by Kuat Drive Yards and Rendili StarDrive. It was 900 meters long and was equipped with a hyperdrive and weapons.

As part of the Clone Wars, in 20.1 BBY, the Confederacy of Independent Systems Admiral Dua Ningo and the Bulwark Fleet of Bulwark Mark I battlecruisers waged a campaign against the Galactic Republic's Core Worlds star systems. In response, the Republic launched the Victory Fleet, consisting of two task forces of new Victory I-class Star Destroyers under the command of Republic Navy captains Terrinald Screed and Jan Dodonna.

Eventually, Dodonna cornered the Bulwark Fleet and ending the Bulwark Fleet's campaign. However, the close range of the attack led to the Arlionne bridge being ripped open by the Unrepentant explosion, with Screed receiving near-mortal injuries in the process that necessitated cybernetic reconstruction.

entities.name: Aut-O's flagship
entities.description:
A Providence-class Dreadnought served in the Confederacy of Independent Systems's naval forces and served as the flagship of a Separatist fleet commanded by the ST-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid Commander Aut-O during the Clone Wars. In 20 BBY, the dreadnought was infiltrated by a squad of Galactic Republic droids, who had been sent to retrieve an encryption module located aboard. The squad later escaped the vessel with the encryption module, but not before Aut-O was destroyed in a brief incursion with the droids.

As a Providence-class Dreadnought, the vessel had a main Hangar bay and a command bridge. The dreadnought was also equipped with a tractor beam projector, and had a passenger complement of B1-series battle droids and B2-series super battle droids.

During the Clone Wars in 20 BBY, the ST-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid Aut-O was in command of a large fleet of Separatist warships in an area of space. The dreadnought which flagged the fleet became targeted by a squad of Galactic Republic droids led by the Zilkin Colonel Meebur Gascon, who were sent by the Republic to board the dreadnought and steal an encryption module located aboard it. The encryption module would allow the Republic to decipher an intercepted and encoded transmission of Separatist General Grievous and discover what the Confederacy was planning.

After arriving at the fleet's location aboard a stolen Maxillipede shuttle, the DUM-series pit droid WAC-47 set the squad's shuttle on a collision course with the dreadnought. However, the dreadnought, alerted by their arrival, instead pulled the shuttle into its main hangar bay with a tractor beam, where several B1 battle droids proceeded to search the vessel.

entities.name: Avenger
entities.description:
Avenger was a Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer in the service of the Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire.

In 137 ABY Avenger was commanded by Captain Furske and served as the flagship of the Coruscant Third Fleet commander Admiral Peto Kelsan. Avenger, along with the rest of the fleet was tasked with protecting the planet Ralltiir, when the Galactic Alliance Remnant and the Empire-in-exile launched a surprise attack on the planet, intending to seize as many Imperial ships as possible.

When Admiral Peto Kelsan realized that his forces were overwhelmed, he agreed to Admiral Edouard Fenel's ultimatum and ordered the fleet to surrender. However, Captain Vaclen Tor of the Ardent-class fast frigate Steadfast persuaded him to change his mind and stick to his duty. After that Kelsan ordered his men to set their ships for self-destruct and then leave them in the escape pods. Peto Kelsan himself choose to stay aboard the Avenger when the ship perished along with rest of the fleet.

entities.name: Bail Organa
entities.description:
The Bail Organa was a New Republic Star Destroyer.

The vessel served as flagship of Fleet Group Two, one of three major battle groups organized to defend Coruscant in 27 ABY. Under the command of Garm Bel Iblis, the Bail Organa and the ships it commanded went head-on into a massive Yuuzhan Vong fleet, losing virtually all of their ships in the battle.

After the Battle of Coruscant, Bel Iblis transferred command to the Mon Calamari Cruiser Harbinger.

entities.name: Ballarat
entities.description:
The Ballarat was an Endurance-class fleet carrier assigned to the New Republic Fifth Fleet.

The Ballarat was the flagship of a task force consisting of twenty-one warships. The Majestic-class heavy cruiser Mandjur served as its escort.

During the Battle of N'zoth, seven warships under its command ‒ Aboukir, Banshee, Fulminant, Garland Thunderhead, Yakez and Werra ‒ were destroyed. While the Ballarat moved forward to cover the gaps, it was attacked by a Yevethan Aramadia-class thrustship. It was hit by a salvo of proton torpedoes in the forward section of Flight Deck Four and the ensuing chain reaction of detonations destroyed three squadrons of launching X-wings and E-wings.

The Ballarat survived the battle of N'zoth, albeit heavily damaged.

entities.name: Battalion
entities.description:
The Battalion was an Imperial Praetor-class battlecruiser that operated shortly after the rise of the New Order.

In 19 BBY, the Battalion was part of the 12th Sector Army and functioned as Admiral Adar Tallon's Command ship during the Sy Myrthian Insurrection. It destroyed the Separatist flagship Defiance's Banner at the Battle of Trasemene.

The Battalion was later assigned to the Dalchon sector and tasked with protecting the area from pirates. When the hero of the Clone Wars Adar Tallon, found himself more and more opposed to the way of the new Empire, he decided to fake his death and go into exile. To achieve this, Tallon chose the Battalion and manned the ship with a loyal crew. Responding to a faked distress signal from a medium freighter that was supposedly attacked by pirates, Tallon entered the Dalchon system. There he and his crew transferred over to the freighter, while the pirate pinnace, commanded by Tallon's childhood friend Quist, destroyed the Battalion.

Later investigations would report that Tallon and his crew died as heroes, protecting the innocent from pirates. No traces of the ship or its crew were found. Tallon, officially mourned as a hero of the New Order, and his crew lived undercover on Tatooine, while Quist continued his career as a pirate.

entities.name: Berea-3
entities.description:
Berea-3 was a "combination ship" that consisted of a stripped-down Quasar Fire-class cruiser-carrier that had been coupled to a mining rig. The vessel was used by the company Imperial Mining, Ltd. and during the Galactic Civil War, the Berea-3 acted as the command ship of an IML fleet that was dispatched to deliver supplies to an IML base on the planet Alluuvia, in the Elrood sector. However, shortly after arriving in the Alluuvian system, the Berea-3 and the rest of the fleet were attacked and defeated by a Rebel Alliance ship and the Shepherd-class Herdship Varnay.

In 43 ABY, the Black Wave was among the ChaseMasters taken to Dathomir in order to confront Jedi Grand Master Luke Skywalker and convince him to join the Sith in an alliance to eliminate Abeloth. After Taalon's death in battle on Pydyr, the vessel fell under Sith Saber Gavar Khai's command. In 44 ABY, when Abeloth attacked the Sith capital city of Tahv, Khai commanded the Black Wave to support Abeloth.

When the Yuuzhan Vong warmaster ordered an occupation of Ebaq 9, Blood Sacrifice landed on the moon's surface. entities.name: Bloodfin
entities.description:
The Bloodfin was a Turbulent-class Star Destroyer that began its service in the naval forces of the Imperial Remnant in 41 ABY. It was built to serve as the flagship of Grand Admiral Gilad Pellaeon. By 44 ABY, the ship was commanded by Admiral Vitor Reige and Head of State Jagged Fel, who succeeded Pellaeon as leader of the Remnant after the Second Galactic Civil War came to an end.

The Bloodfin was smaller in comparison with other Star Destroyers of the time. Despite its physical deviation from the traditional design of Star Destroyers, the vessel possessed a greater capacity for maneuverability. Although it was meant to perform as a "pocket destroyer," the Bloodfin still retained much of the impressive weaponry that could be found on the more common destroyers.

The Bloodfin entered its first military engagement at the Second Battle of Fondor in 41 ABY. When Gilad Pellaeon refused to comply with the Sith Lord Darth Caedus' orders to ignore the ceasefire and attack Fondor, Tahiri Veila assassinated him with the support of the Moff Council, including Quille and Rosset. Although they ensured that the Remnant remained loyal to Caedus, the Bloodfin was boarded by Mandalorian Protectors, which then resulted in the deaths of most of the ship's crew. After the battle, the Bloodfin was added to Natasi Daala's Maw Irregular Fleet, under the command of Admiral Vitor Reige. After the conclusion of the Second Galactic Civil War, the Bloodfin returned to the service of the Imperial Remnant while still under Reige's command. In 44 ABY, it was part of a large task force that was led by Jagged Fel in a preemptive strike on Daala's insurrectionist fleet. During the Battle over Exodo II, the destruction of the Gilad Pellaeon forced Fel to transfer the status of flagship over to the Bloodfin as the fighting intensified between the Remnant armada and the Maw Irregular Fleet.

entities.name: Blue Diver
entities.description:
The Blue Diver was a Mon Calamari heavy carrier operated by the Galactic Alliance out of the Second Fleet in the years following the Yuuzhan Vong War.

In 40 ABY, it was recalled from its annual mission to the Tingel Arm, where it was searching for remaining pockets of Yuuzhan Vong resistance, in order to take part in Operation Roundabout during the Second Galactic Civil War. Gray Squadron was stationed onboard Blue Diver, as was Lieutenant Baradis. Following the breaking of the Alliance blockade by combined Corellian, Commenorian, and Bothan forces, the Blue Diver withdrew from Corellian space to Coruscant. Following heavy damage sustained by the Galactic-class battle carrier Dodonna, the Blue Diver became the new flagship for Second Fleet commanding officer Admiral Tarla Limpan.

The Blue Diver, with Admiral Tarla Limpan commanding and Syal Antilles assigned to one of her Aleph-class starfighter squadrons led a task force of Alliance reinforcements in a ambush set by Corellian forces. With Alliance forces fully committed to the battle, Corellians fired Centerpoint Station with the intention of destroying the Anakin Solo and thereby killing Jacen Solo. The blast failed in this but succeeding in destroying both Corellian and Alliance fleets, including the Blue Diver with all hands. The only known survivors were Syal Antilles and Zueb Zan, along with their astromech.

It, along with its escort, the Adamantine, was infected by the Death Seed plague in 13 ABY. The Borealis was lost with all hands.

entities.name: Alderaanian refugee convoy
entities.description:
Following the Disaster, a convoy of Alderaanian survivors aboard three GR-75 medium transports traveled to Fostar Haven in the hopes of evading the Galactic Empire, which was under orders from Darth Vader to destroy all remainders of Alderaan.

The convoy was discovered, and Commodore Rae Sloane sent Captain Lindon Javes of Helix Squadron alongside a blockade to Fostar Haven to eliminate the refugees. Javes, however, refused to kill innocent lives when he learnt about the Disaster and resolved to aid their escape.

The convoy was evacuated by Javes and Echo Squadron of the Alliance to Restore the Republic.

entities.description:
The Alnarian Collective was a group the Colonies Alnaria system. By 382 BBY, a delegation from the Collective was set to meet Jedi Master Fitan and her Padawan, Oliviah Zeveron. When the two parties greeted, Fitan farted vociferously, using the Force to simulate flatulence-caused air flow in her Jedi robes. Fitan and Zeveron then giggled like younglings in front of the Collective. In that year, Zeveron recounted the toot to fellow Padawan Matthea Cathley.

entities.name: Anzellan Droidsmiths
entities.description:
The Anzellan Droidsmiths were a legendary crew of four (originally three) Anzellan droidsmiths living on the planet Nevarro. By the time of the New Republic, they found great commercial success when Nevarro was thriving, as they had precise and affordable expertise to keep automated excavation equipment used for belt mining running under extreme conditions. High Magistrate Greef Karga tasked them to keep his administrative droids and foot droids operational. They were requested by Din Djarin to fix IG-11, who previously self-destructed. The Anzellans could not fix the droid, because his memory circuit was broken, a component that was very hard to find at that time as they were not being made anymore.

The crew initially consisted of a trio named Minch, Keeto and Bai. The four helped Djarin make modifications on his new ship, the Razor Crest 2.0. Although one night Embo and his anooba Keibu came to Nevarro and kidnapped Djarin and by accident Minch. The other three left with Grogu in their Anzellan Starship to Nal Hutta, where they rescued both but Djarin was too big to fit in their starship and so he and Grogu stayed behind but the droidsmiths came back with Adelphi Rangers lead by Colonel Ward to rescue Djarin, Grogu, and Rotta.

entities.name: Aquaris Freeholders
entities.description:
The Aquaris Freeholders were a group who were involved with the smugglers Chewbacca and Han Solo on a job delivering spice. Silver Fyre was affiliated with them. During the job, the Aquaris Freeholders hijacked their spice cargo, which earned them Solo's ire. When Solo was planning a new job to pay off a debt he owed Jabba the Hutt, Chewbacca mentioned Silver Fyre and the Aquaris Freeholders as possible clients, which Solo dismissed. Solo recorded the information about the Aquaris Freeholders in the Smuggler's Guide.

In between 34 ABY and 35 ABY, Strono Tuggs's food freighter was boarded by the Aquaris Freeholders who were looking for spice. When they realized he didn't have anything except for food onboard, they demanded he make them a gourmet meal.

entities.name: Aquillian Ranger
entities.description:
An Aquillian Ranger was a type of individual who was active during the Imperial Era. While starship spotting on Alderaan in 9 BBY, Princess Leia Organa spotted a Tri-Wing S-91x Pegasus Starfighter, and hypothesized that it was an Aquillian Ranger scouting for the Merson pirates.

The Aquillian Rangers originated in George Lucas' second draft of the original Star Wars film, apparently in reference to the planet Aquilae that had appeared in the previous rough draft and the first draft. Deak Starkiller was conceptualized as a Jedi and an Aquillian Ranger; elements of his character would later be given to Princess Leia. In the third draft, the Aquillian Rangers are present with the Rebels on Yavin 4.

The backstory of the Aquillian Rangers as allies of the Jedi would be partially incorporated into that of the Antarian Rangers, in the Star Wars Legends continuity. However, the name itself would not be introduced to canon until Leia's mention in Part I of Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi.

entities.description:
Arva Pars was an organization active during the Imperial Era. the group's leaders entered into negotiations with the Tagge Corporation over a sale. During the discussions, Arva Pars' leaders expressed their readiness to negotiate with the Tagge Corporation, which—the secretary of the Tagge Corporation's leader, Lady Domina Tagge—informed Domina of. In response, she told Lapin to not send a reply, expecting it to cause Arva Pars to question their offer before they reduced their asking price by twenty percent the following day.

entities.name: Biological Athletes Union
entities.description:
The Biological Athletes Union was an organization active by 22 BBY. After the growth in popularity experienced by the Nuna-Ball League's matches of nuna-ball, a sport that involved teams of droids using a nuna creature as a ball and therefore required little sentient involvement other than that of repair technicians, the Biological Athletes Union, along with the Committee Against Non-Sentient Abuse, protested against the matches. Their objections, however, did not gain traction with the public, which was noted on the date 13:4:4 in an issue of the CoCo District Edition of the HoloNet News.

The Biological Athletes Union was first mentioned in HoloNet News Vol. 531 #50, an in-universe issue of the HoloNet News and published on the HoloNet News website on April 4, 2002.

In response, Ongwa stated she would have the money sent to the Bonbrak Protection Society.

entities.description:
The Botsini crew was a crew of individuals that operated at some point after the fall of the Galactic Empire. The crew was known for a strategy where the captain gave each member of the crew a specific job, withholding the full details of their plans, so that if a mistake was made it would be clear who was at fault. The Batuuan resident Julen Rakab thought that the strategy could only work if there were backup plans.

The Botsini crew was first mentioned in the 2019 novel A Crash of Fate, written by Zoraida Córdova.

entities.name: Caamasi Remnant
entities.description:
The Caamasi Remnant was the term given to an association of individual communities of Caamasi refugees who survived the orbital bombardment of Caamas during the Galactic Civil War. The term "Caamasi Remnant" could also be used to describe the collective remnant communities, although they were only loosely affiliated.

Each Remnant community was headed by a Trustant. The largest Remnant community, under Trustant Ylenic It'kla, was established on Alderaan; however it was destroyed along with the planet in 0 BBY.

Another was established under Trustant Elegos A'Kla in the city of Morymento on Kerilt. It was later relocated to Susevfi. After A'Kla was murdered during the Yuuzhan Vong War, his daughter, Releqy A'Kla, succeeded him as trustant.

During the time of the New Republic, a Remnant community established Refuge City on Caamas itself.

entities.description:
The Calamasthon Defiance was a group with whom the Draag criminal Slaag Lado had ties. In 32 BBY, Lado was wanted by the Mon Calamari Civil Authority for allegedly creating a huge seismic attack that led to immense environmental damage in the Salinrerian Sea and resulted in constant rain on the site. In the bounty posted for Lado, the Civil Authority noted the Draag's ties to the Calamasthon Defiance.

The Calamasthon Defiance was first mentioned in the 2002 LucasArts video game Star Wars: Bounty Hunter. The organization is mentioned in the bounty information for Slaag Lado, who appears in the game's second chapter, "Lowlifes In High Places."

entities.name: Celestial
entities.description:
Celestials were a group known for their singing. During a job on Kullgroon, in 10 BBY Lando Calrissian compared the singing voice of Naaruu, a individual who threatened Lando, who Lando subsequently killed and took his hide as a cape, to the sweetest of Celestials.

Celestials where introduced into canon with a mention in the 2018 comic Lando - Double or Nothing 2, and pencilled by Paolo Villanelli. In the Star Wars Legends continuity, Celestials were first mentioned, albeit unnamed, in the 1983 novel Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu, written by L. Neil Smith. Celestials were first named by Troy Denning in his 2005 novel Dark Nest I: The Joiner King. In the Legends continuity, the Ones, who made their first appearance in Overlords, a 2011 episode of Season Three of the TV series Star Wars: The Clone Wars, were identified as Celestials in the Star Wars Blog article "Galactic Architecture 101 and the History of Centerpoint Station," but no canonical connection has been made between the Ones and Celestials.

entities.name: Chokee & Chokee
entities.description:
Chokee & Chokee was an independent polling agency.

During the early stages of the Clone Wars, the agency could report an approval rating of 81% for Chancellor Palpatine among citizens of the Inner Core. This was the lowest point since the start of the conflict.

Mas Amedda used the polls to suggest the Chancellor was being tied up in bureaucratic red-tape by the Galactic Senate, to which he received boos and jeers from the attending Senators. As an upside for the Chancellor, the same polls showed the approval rating for the Senate holding at only 31%.

The Coruscant Patrol was a patrol organization that shared its name with the Core Worlds planet Coruscant. The organization was active during the High Republic Era and had a number of starfighter cadets. At some point, Jedi Padawan Reath Silas met some of the Coruscant Patrol's cadets and felt that they spoke with an aura of firm conviction. While on a mission to the ancient Amaxine Space Station Silas met the young Nihil Nan—who had been previously disguised as a refugee. As Nan told him details about her life and how she was proud to be a Nihil, the Jedi reflected that the sureness in her voice was comparative to some Coruscant Patrol starfighter cadets he had encountered, as well as some other Padawans.

entities.description:
The D'Armin Syndicate was an organization that operated during the Imperial Era. the syndicate attacked a supply ship of the Tagge Corporation. By the following day, news of the attack led to a drop for the Tagge Corporation in the Hadi system, which the corporation's leader—Lady Domina Tagge of the House of Tagge—noticed and questioned her Lapin Tagge about. In response, Lapin informed Domina of the attack, to which she ordered her secretary have a battleship cut the syndicate off at the celestial body Feriae Junction. Domina then instructed to have their engines and weapons taken out before pushing them into the sun the next day.

The D'Armin Syndicate was mentioned in flashbacks in the sixth issue of the 2020 comic series Star Wars: Doctor Aphra. The issue was written by Alyssa Wong and published by Marvel Comics

entities.name: Daan
entities.description:
The Daan were a group that inhabited the Cadavine sector's Melida/Daan alongside the Melida. After the Melida took the leader of the Daan captive, the Jedi Order and Republic senator Lexxir Greylark and his eighteen year old son, Axel Greylark, embarked on a diplomatic mission to negotiate with the Melida for the leader's release. During the extraction of the leader however, there was an explosion, as the mission was a trap to show all of the Daan's allies what would happen to those that helped them. With the trap triggered and the Melida on their way, the senator was buried under rubble in an explosion, while a Jedi Knight pulled an injured Greylark away, forcing him to leave his father to die. Greylark told the Jedi Gella Nattai about the incident.

In the current Star Wars canon, the Daan were first mentioned in the 2022 novel The High Republic: Convergence by Zoraida Córdova.

Raise the Death Star II!, a poster made for the fund, was collected by Poe Dameron in a vehicle guidebook.

The Death Star II Restoration Fund was mentioned in the 2022 non-canon reference book LEGO Star Wars Awesome Vehicles.

entities.name: Friends of the Republic
entities.description:
The Friends of the Republic were a group of individuals dedicated to the preservation of the ideals of the Galactic Republic, which many believed had begun to crumble in the wake of the Clone Wars.

One year prior to the First Battle of Geonosis, the Friends of the Republic contacted Senator Bail Organa when the government of Alderaan had entered negotiations with Chandrila for a joint mining venture on Aridus. Bail's wife, Breha Antilles Organa, had several connections with the Corporate Sector via her family, and some of those connections were involved in the project, which it appeared would have been successful. The information provided by the Friends of the Republic helped avert a diplomatic and humanitarian disaster that would have engulfed not only Alderaan and Chandrila, but the rest of the Republic, as well.

The negotiations that followed occurred on such a lofty political scale that not even the Jedi Order was informed of the proceedings.

During the Clone Wars the Friends of the Republic contacted Senator Bail Organa, warning him of a potential Sith assault on the Jedi Order and a dangerous temple on Zigoola. Using fellow Senator Padmé Amidala as a go-between, Organa used the information to get in touch with Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, who accompanied the Senator on an arduous mission, which ended in the destruction of the temple and all of its Sith artifacts.

That year, the Jedi Padawan Joc Sah and his squad of clone troopers attacked the outcasts in order to use the world as a staging planet for an attack on a Separatist base.

The group appeared in the short story "The Order of Outcasts," which was one of four stories compiled in the fifth volume of the Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures trade paperbacks

entities.name: Inusagian court
entities.description:
The Inusagian court was a group of notable individuals from the planet Inusagi.

In 6 BBY, the Galactic Empire used the sakoola blossom festival to announce a new planetary leader, Governor Cor Tophervin, a personal friend of the Emperor. However, given Inusagi's relation to Naboo, the anti-Imperial Zabrak Arane Oreida saw the party as an opportunity to send a message to the Empire, and she hired Saw Gerrera to infiltrate the festival. With invitations forged by Jyn Erso, Gerrera, Maia, and a group of Arane's partisans entered the festival in the chieftess's palace. There, they used FC-1 flechette launchers to massacre the guests, including the Inusagi court members.

entities.name: ISPCA
entities.description:
Little was known about the organization called ISPCA, up to and including its proper name, since the only time that it was known to be mentioned was during a conversation between the amateur starship captain Lando Calrissian and Mohs, the High Singer of the Toka.

Prior to this conversation, Calrissian, his droid, Vuffi Raa and Mohs landed in the Millennium Falcon at the base of one of the Sharu pyramids on Rafa V and were ambushed by a tribe of Toka who were armed with crossbows. After the Toka warriors incapacitated Vuffi Raa, Mohs took command of them and demanded that Calrissian turn the Fabled Key over to his possession. Because they were ritually forbidden from taking the key from the custody of the Key-Bearer — a prohibition that included directly killing him — they did what they felt was the next best thing and marched Calrissian to a life-orchard. There, they tied him to a life-crystal tree, which given time, would slowly drain him of his intelligence and ultimately kill him.

However, Calrissian was unwilling to go along with their plan. After Mohs and his fellow Toka left him, Calrissian freed himself and with the help of a newly-recovered Vuffi Raa, made his way back to the Falcon original landing site. They found Mohs there, cooking a creature (alternately called a lizard, a reptile or a frog) that he had impaled upon a branch. During the course of the ensuing conversation, Vuffi Raa alerted Calrissian to the approach of Mohs's friends. Calrissian threatened Mohs with the prospect of having him trade places with "that poor uncomfortable creature you're cooking" and then entertained the prospect of turning Mohs in to the "ISPCA — or at least the Epicures Club."

Given the context of Calrissian's reference to the ISPCA, it is likely that the organization would not have looked kindly upon Mohs's treatment of the frog. Calrissian's consideration of the idea of turning Mohs in to the custody of either organization may or may not have indicated that the ISPCA was vested with some power to enforce the law. Further details regarding this mysterious organization remain elusive.

The backbone of the navy was made up of at least eight Marauder-class corvettes, and the fleet was considered obsolete by the Galactic Empire, and of little threat. The fleet was commanded by Hendric Faile.

Two corvettes, including the Bravado III, engaged forces allied to Moff Kentor Sarne posing as a New Republic vessel in 8 ABY.

entities.name: Leresai Assembly
entities.description:
The Leresai Assembly was an organization active during the High Republic Era. the Assembly intercepted several garbled transmissions of which it passed on to the Jedi Order and Galactic Republic, who were attempting to hunt down the Nihil pirates.

Unaware of Ro's identity or that he had been the Eye all along, Jedi Master Stellan Gios presented the Leresai Assembly's images of Ro at a briefing where the Jedi were attempting to deduce who might have taken over as Eye after the presumed death of Nihil Tempest Runner Lourna Dee, who had been mistakenly assumed to hold the position, during the Battle of Galov.

The Leresai Assembly was mentioned in the ninth issue of the 2021 comic series Star Wars: The High Republic. The issue was written by Cavan Scott and published by Marvel Comics as part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's Phase I. The Assembly shares its name with the Leresai, a sentient species from the Star Wars Legends continuity that originated in Timothy Zahn's 1997 novel Specter of the Past, the first installment of Star Wars: The Hand of Thrawn Duology.

entities.description:
The Manifold Mollusk Matrix and Matrimony Association was an organization for which the alien Skreen served as a technical director. An author and a member of the Gaalt Sky Rowing team, Skreen personally performed over four hundred anaerobic couplings and at some point planned to participate in a seminar along with mOKDAR 15, Regalia Sub-space station-12 Director of Nasal Infusions and member of the Society for the Refusal of Astrophysics; author and University of Desultori staffmember Aanxi Raanxi Laanxi; the horticultural educator Kaat Thrick-Thrick; and the being known as 26-424.

The Manifold Mollusk Matrix and Matrimony Association was mentioned in the 1993 book Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas, a publication that combines creature designs and photographs from various projects of George Lucas, creator of the Star Wars franchise, with original text by Bob Carrau.

entities.name: Melida
entities.description:
The Melida were a group that inhabited Melida/Daan in the Cadavine sector alongside the Daan. When the Melida took the leader of the Daan captive, a Republic senator and his eighteen year old son, Axel Greylark, embarked on a diplomatic mission with the Jedi Order to negotiate for the release of the leader. The mission however, was a trap to show all of the Daan's allies what would happen to those that helped them. During the extraction there was an explosion that buried the senator under rubble, but as the Melida were coming, a Jedi Knight pulled an injured Greylark away, forcing him to leave his father to die. Greylark told the Jedi Gella Nattai about the incident.

In the current Star Wars canon, the Melida were first mentioned in the 2022 novel The High Republic: Convergence by Zoraida Córdova.

The Breaddown care service informed the customer that the service could pick them up but was unable to retrieve the speeder from the pit. However the service did offer to supply the customer with a replacement vehicle and driving lessons if they upgraded to the premium service plan.

In 3 ABY the scoundrel Kay Vess found a datapad in the capital city Mirogana with the message regarding the speeder crash in the Kashùda Pit. Vess also retrieved the valuables from a container next to the speeder wreck in the pit.

Mirogana Breakdown Care was mentioned in the 2024 Massive Entertainment video game Star Wars Outlaws published by Ubisoft. It is part of an optional intel quest and the items can be retrieved from the pit before reading the datapad.

Myrran Swimmer's Club was an athletic club that existed in Myrra the capital city of the Outer Rim Territories planet Akiva.

The club was forced to define a no-go zone for training in the western edge of the Great Basin due to increased Hutt Clan activity in 3 ABY At the time a member of the club named Kin Shiff died. The club set out a notice of this news and stressed that the untimely death of Kin Shiff was not related to the Hutt activity. A copy of the notice was kept on a datapad in the Hutt Cartel District of Myrra during 3 ABY.

Myrran Swimmer's Club was mentioned in a datapad in the 2024 Massive Entertainment video game Star Wars Outlaws published by Ubisoft.

entities.description:
After the Battle of Jakku the New Republic pilot Captain Nath Tensent retired from service and started his own freelancing crew, wishing not to be bound by the New Republic's high expectations in abiding with the law. Tensent began tracking down members of the fallen Galactic Empire who had served the 204th Imperial Fighter Wing, a unit he had fought against. He eventually recruited the TIE mechanic Creet and the TIE fighter pilot Nord Kandende before traveling to the planet Freerock to offer the TIE pilot Bansu Ro a place in his crew.

Nath Tensent's crew first appeared in Victory's Price: An Alphabet Squadron Novel, the third novel in Alexander Freed's Star Wars: Alphabet Squadron trilogy, which was published in 2021.

entities.description:
The People's Inquest was a grassroots populist Jedi-accountability watch-group active before and during the Clone Wars.

They supported Jonava Billane in the Case of "Baby Ludi". Thrynka Padaunete was president of the People's Inquest. They were known for their multiple petitions and marches on the Jedi Temple. In one particular march, several Padawans were overwhelmed and were unable to quell the angry group. Jedi Master Plo Koon easily dispatched the disruptive mob using a Jedi mind trick.

In the wake of Order 66, the People's Inquest aided the Galactic Empire by compiling a list of all known Jedi that were still at large, along with information on other Force-using sects.

entities.name: Sana Starros' crew
entities.description:
After rogue archaeologist Doctor Chelli Lona Aphra was possessed by the Spark Eternal, the smuggler Sana Starros and archaeologist Kho Phon Farrus assembled

The crew then made their way to the Vermillion, the Fortress-Flagship of Crimson Dawn, where the Spark had gone to acquire technology of the Ascendant. The crew were ultimately unsuccessful in their attempt to save Aphra from the Spark Eternal, and the Spark took control of the two droids and also convinced Farrus to defect from the crew to join Crimson Dawn. As the Spark left the Vermillion aboard the Ark Angel IV, the crew attempted to follow in Starros' starship, the Volt Cobra, but the Spark destroyed the Cobra and fled.

The crew were rescued from the wreckage of the Volt Cobra by Just Lucky and Ariole Yu who took them to the penthouse of Ronen Tagge in Canto Bight where Tagge had Starros and her crew placed in bacta tanks. After they recovered, he attempted to recruit the crew to his services in return for the cost of operating the tanks to heal them. Starros rejected Ronen's offer as she did not want to cross Ronen's aunt, Domina. Ronen revealed his alliance with Crimson Dawn, and his desire to overthrow his aunt and take over control of the Tagge Corporation. Believing Crimson Dawn and its leader, Lady Qi'ra, to be the probable winning side, Starros reversed her decision and accepted Ronen's offer, though she suggested to Ronen that they instead kill Domina as merely overthrowing her would result in her becoming a problem for him in the future.

Unbeknownst to the rest of her crew, however, Starros was secretly working for Domina, trying to acquire proof for her of her nephew's treachery. The crew, along with Lucky and Yu, then made their way to Domina's flagship, the Acquisitor, where they saw the Tagge's at war. They eventually made their way to the ship's bridge, where they fought against the crew of the bounty hunter Boushh and Domina herself. Ronen then arrived, and declared himself the leader as the leader of the company. After Ronen drew a blaster and pointed it at his aunt, Starros asked Domina if that was good enough evidence for her, to which she replied she supposed it was. Domina then executed Ronen. Following this, Starros told Domina she had held up her side of their agreement, and told her to pay up, asking for all of their debts, including Chelli's, to be cleared, the release of Korin and Okka, who Ronen had held hostage to ensure the crew would help him, and finally, a new Volt Cobra. Domina agreed to clear their debts, and then offered them a job, stating that she paid very well. The crew rejected the offer as they had a place to be, people to see, and scores to settle. The group then reunited with Korin and Okka, who had been released, before they made their way to find Farrus. When they arrived at Farrus' location, Yao approached them, telling Farrus they had a lot to answer for, but they cut off the group, telling them they knew where Aphra, the Spark Eternal, and Crimson Dawn was. Farrus then informed the crew they knew what Crimson Dawn leader Lady Qi'ra was planning, what she had already done, and that it would kill them all.

entities.name: Separatist Coalition
entities.description:
The Separatist Coalition was an organization active by during the reign of the Galactic Empire, which Chandrilan Imperial Senator Mon Mothma was a part of and attended meetings of. In that year, the Empire had grown suspicious of Mothma's activities and supplanted individuals she regularly encountered with Imperial spies to uncover her dealings.

To that end, though many others still believed her to be just an irritation due to her fights against Imperial overreach and for Separatist sympathizers, Imperial Grand Vizier Mas Amedda began infiltrating the coalition's meetings. Aware of the Empire's spying and wanting it so they would miss her machinations, Mothma revealed the Vizier's infiltrations to Chandrilan banker Tay Kolma, whom she had sought to recruit as well as gain help from to regain access to her family accounts used to fund a secret network of anti-Imperial individuals.

The Separatist Coalition was mentioned in "Announcement," released on Disney+ on October 19, 2022.

entities.name: Sisters of the Ninth Plane
entities.description:
The Sisters of the Ninth Plane were a group that ran a children's medcenter on the astronomical object Novor during the High Republic Era. Ola Hest—an enforcer of the Hutt Clan—was sent to collect protection money from the medcenter, which the Sisters refused to pay and told her to leave. Afterward, Hest turned the thrusters of her frigate on the medcenter, bringing it down and killing all inside. The enforcer later claimed that it had been an accident and was eventually captured by

In 231 BBY, while imprisoned aboard the Galactic Republic prison ship Restitution, the prisoner Sestin Blin told Nihil Tempest Runner Lourna Dee—who was also imprisoned on the Restitution—about the incident involving Hest at the children's medcenter. Blin also informed Dee of her belief that it had not been an accident and that the enforcer had known what she was doing and wanted people to know what she was doing.

The Sisters of the Ninth Plane were mentioned in The High Republic: Tempest Runner, a 2021 audio drama written by Cavan Scott and published as a part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's Phase I. The spelling of the group's name was later confirmed with the release of the audio drama's script in 2022.

entities.name: Skeleton Crew
entities.description:
The Skeleton Crew was a crew active from around 9 ABY. but did so in order to steal the mint on At Attin.

At first, the four younglings divided amongst themselves into two distinct groups. The boys, Wim and Neel, as one group and the girls, Fern and KB, as the other. However, during their adventures, the four, who had initially fought over who had "claimsies" on the ship and who got to be captain, learned to trust one another and became a single crew. During their trip to At Achrann, Wim, who had previously wished to be captain of the Onyx Cinder instead of Fern, asserted that Fern was the right choice for captain after all. He then added that, had he been captain, they would never have gotten as far as they had under Fern's leadership.

During the Mission to Skull Ridge Mountain, after Jod Na Nawood betrayed the Skeleton Crew over his greed and Wim saved KB's life when her prosthetics failed, the four grew even closer to each other. Fern then learned to take into account the limitations posed by both KB's prosthetics and Neel being a Myykian. As Neel was a member of an elephantine species, he was less capable of climbing than humans, such as Fern. KB and Neel, in turn, learned to assert their needs and desires, and all four learned to further appreciate each other. Fern came into her own, as captain, when both her leadership skills and her ability to delegate under pressure were tested as the crew narrowly escaped from a trash compactor while aboard the Onyx Cinder. A challenge that required the crew to both engage the emergency hull demolition sequencer while relying on the individual skills of each member of the crew.

The committee met periodically on the moon of Sojourn, to assure the swift passage of corporate-friendly legislation, fix the price of commodities such as Tibanna gas, transparisteel and several other materials. While, keeping senators in the Galactic Republic's capital of Coruscant. In 52 BBY, killed at an attack on the Lodge of the Order of the Canted Circle by Maladian assassins.

The steering committee appeared in the 2012 novel Darth Plagueis, written by James Luceno.

entities.name: Techno-lord
entities.description: The Techno-lords were a group of Arkanian scientists who created an army for the Arkanian Dominion during the Arkanian Revolution. In response to the Arkanian Renegades' Assimilator cyborgs, the techno-lords created the Accelerated Transgenic Heuristic Abhorers through genetic manipulation and cybernetic enhancement. Following the conclusion of the revolution, the Arkanian Dominion attempted to systematically destroy all the Abhorers. Zeta Magnus, the prime clone of the Abhorers, managed to evade capture and proceeded to hunt down and eat his techno-lord creators out of revenge.

On one occasion, after she had won a big sales bonus, the woman decided to take her husband, Reezo, and Tsuulo with her on one of her business trips—a sales conference at the Buckell Center in Coronet City on the Core Worlds planet Corellia. On the second morning of the conference, both parents were inadvertently killed by a Besalisk factory worker when he swerved off a road and hit them. That year, Tsuulo, now a scrumrat in the White Worms criminal organization on Corellia, mentioned the freighter company and his mother's employment within it to fellow scrumrats Han and Qi'ra.

The freighter company was mentioned in the 2018 young-adult novel Most Wanted, written by Rae Carson.

entities.name: Clan
entities.description:
A clan was the familial and often political organization that made up a society. Clan-based cultures included Rodians, Bothans, Witches of Dathomir, Mandalorians, Noghri, Ugnaughts, Wookiees, Codru-Ji, and Twi'leks.

Since ancient times, Rodians were a tribal society. A clan was ruled by a Chief Protector, and associated with some land and/or enclave; enclaves grew later into cities, and some absorbed other smaller enclaves as they grew. Clan members were sometimes wholly dedicated to some profession, organization or criminal syndicate.

In later times, clans were also political entities, and were often allies or enemies with each other; their skirmishes sometimes escalated to planetary war. Affiliation was often a private matter that was not usually obvious or publicly shared; Rodians who revealed their clan risked being exposed to Rodians of enemy clans that could be present. Warfare, geography and other factors shaped the development of each clan; some weaker clans remained isolated in their ancestral lands in the jungle, and limited to older technology. Newer clans were usually small groups that split from traditional clans, often supporting radical views; as these emerged in the cities, they possessed no lands.

The Chattza Clan emerged dominant after the Rodian Clan Wars.

entities.name: Imperial holdouts
entities.description:
Imperial holdouts, also known as Imperial remnants or as Imperial hideouts, were various fractured political and military remnants of the Galactic Empire which emerged following its collapse and prevailed throughout the first few years of the New Republic Era.

Without a ruler to hold them together after the death of the Galactic Emperor Sheev Palpatine during the Galactic Civil War, who left behind no instructions of succession, the Empire began to fragment across the galaxy, while the Imperial Navy retreated as the Alliance to Restore the Republic reorganized into the New Republic. The Battle of Jakku saw the final defeat of the Empire, forcing a surrender to the New Republic.

With strict disarmament treaties and reparations in place following the signing of the Galactic Concordance, the Empire collapsed as a unified polity. Chancellor Mon Mothma also issuing a further declaration designating members of the Imperial Military as war criminals while granting conditional pardons to non-combatant functionaries. Following this, many of its soldiers, officials, warlords and other holdouts fled to the fringes of the galaxy.

By 9 ABY, Imperial holdouts remained active in the galaxy with one faction lead by Moff Gideon being active in the Outer Rim Territories on planets like Nevarro During this time, Gideon and his remnant sought after the Force-sensitive child Grogu as part of their cloning experiments and succeeded in capturing him on Tython, but was later rescued by the Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin and his allies that saw Moff Gideon arrested and brought into New Republic custody afterwards.

entities.name: Law enforcement agency
entities.description:
A law enforcement agency, also referred to as a planetary security force, police force, or security force, was an organization charged with enforcing laws, maintaining order, and protecting life and property. They were staffed by police officers or some cases soldiers and were generally structured as a paramilitary force or militia though they were rarely armed for full scale war. Sometimes police droids were utilized to supplement sentient peacekeepers in larger agencies or for smaller outposts and space stations.

A law enforcement agency, also called a police force or security force, was an organization charged with maintaining order, enforcing laws, and protecting life and property. Some law enforcement agencies also served as a military for their local governments, however they simply kept the peace and were not armed for full scale war.

Law enforcement was generally conducted on a local or planetary level but their size, functions, and training could vary greatly. They could be a small, volunteer local security force, or responsible to protect a whole, densely urbanized planet such as the Coruscant Security Force. Some served primarily as bodyguards and elite security forces, such as the Senate Guard; others were volunteer security and policing corps such as the Royal Security Forces on the planet Naboo. During the Invasion of Naboo, several hundred Royal Guards and police formed an underground resistance effort against the Trade Federation Droid Army.

The Jedi Order had policing authority under the Galactic Republic and could conduct criminal investigations and make arrests. Some even became experienced in local criminal and policing matters. However, the Jedi served the Republic as a whole as keepers of the peace and guardians of justice, leaving most planetary matters to local police. Jedi Master Dooku took notice of how many of the Republic's politicians saw the Jedi as little more than their personal, glorified police during the later years of the Republic, something that greatly upset him.

entities.name: Rebel cell
entities.description:
Rebel cells were networks of Alliance operatives, agents, and informants active on a planet or in a star system. These cells often employed secrecy so that members of the network only knew a handful of other operatives at any time. The goal of a Rebel cell was to gather information and provide it to Alliance Intelligence, rally resistance elements, and to undermine the local Imperial presence.

Rebel cells were undercover Alliance units operating throughout the galaxy at the planet and system level. The Alliance relied on these cells of operatives to gather intelligence, and to strike from hidden bases, deploying soldiers and starfighters to needed battle zones. Rebel cells were often intentionally set up by the Alliance, deploying operatives to targeted systems to build the network from the ground up.

Ahead of setting up a cell network in a star system, the Alliance provided the operatives with instructions on how to establish their cell. General Airen Cracken briefed some of these teams personally, imparting his knowledge and experience to the operatives. Although the Alliance attempted to give their operatives as much detail as possible before sending them into the field, the sheer number of systems within the galaxy made it impossible for up-to-date information and specific conditions to be provided for all systems. Because of this, the operatives were expected to thoroughly learn about their assigned system themselves and not to rely solely on the provided data. Operatives deployed to set up the cell were instructed to study the system's people, customs, and background. The Alliance knew that operatives would have difficultly attempting to operate in cultures that were completely alien to them so attempted to deploy their operatives to systems with a population that was similar to their own species.

A syndicate was a type criminal organization that had a large sphere of operation and typically defined by territory or goods. Syndicates were led by crime lords, with a layer of underbosses beneath them.

entities.name: Oviedo Engineering
entities.description:
Oviedo Engineering was a large research-and-development organization that manufactured military vehicles and weapon systems. Led by Director General Lorca Oviedo, it expanded its corporate portfolio years before 22 BBY. Around 21 BBY, during the Clone Wars between the Confederacy of Independent Systems and the Galactic Republic, Oviedo allied himself with the Confederacy.

While Oviedo traveled to the Republic's Core Worlds capital planet, Coruscant, his Consular-class cruiser and clone commando escorts were shot down by Separatist forces over the Expansion Region moon Asturias, crashing on the moon. While the Director General spoke with Separatist Wat Tambor via hologram, planning to return to the Republic and use its Senate's rearmament bill to task his industries with equipping the Republic's Army with weaponry, the commandos captured Oviedo. They brought him to Coruscant, where he died of respiratory failure. The Director General's treason resulted in the dismantling of Oviedo Engineering's operations.

Oviedo Engineering was a vast research-and-development organization that manufactured military vehicles and weapon systems.

Oviedo Engineering was founded years before the beginning of the Clone Wars, of 22 BBY, Wat Tambor sought to use the assignment to extrapolate the army's strength and deployment patterns to ambush the military's clone trooper forces.
