entities.name: Lorca Oviedo
entities.description:
Lorca Oviedo was a Human who served the Galactic Republic as the director of Oviedo Engineering, a corporation that built military weaponry, holding the title of Director General. Around 21 BBY, the director allied himself with the Separatist Confederacy of Independent Systems, the Republic's opponent in the Clone Wars. As the Republic Senate's members believed the Director General was a Separatist, he and Separatist Foreman Wat Tambor prepared an assassination attempt on the director in an attempt to establish that Oviedo was not a Separatist.

After a conference on the astronomical object Aviles Prime, a group of Republic clone commandos was tasked with escorting Oviedo's cruiser to the Republic capital planet Coruscant; however, while traveling to Coruscant, the Director General executed his crew and brought his vessel out of hyperspace as Separatist warships shot down the Republic vessels.

After the cruiser and its escort crashed on the Expansion Region moon Asturias, Oviedo spoke with Tambor via hologram. Several clones who had survived the crash located the director and Tambor commanded his forces to leave no witnesses. The commandos captured the Director General and escaped Asturias with Oviedo's cruiser, bringing him to Coruscant, where he died of respiratory failure.

A Human, Lorca Oviedo was the Director General of the Oviedo Engineering. Wat Tambor and Oviedo designed a plot to establish that the Director General was loyal to the Republic by executing a Separatist assassination attempt on Oviedo in an attempt to prompt the Senate to task Oviedo Engineering with equipping the Republic's Grand Army with vehicles and munitions. Tambor sought to use that task to extrapolate the Republic's military strength and deployment patterns.

entities.name: Class-D detonator
entities.description:
Class-D detonators were one of the most devastating pieces of disruptor technology in the galaxy. Invented by the mysterious fatalists of Plootark IX, Class-D detonators used Class-D disintegration to annihilate a target. Class-D disintegration, also known as transcendental annihilation, was the epitome of disruptor technology. Class-D devices disintegrated all organic and non-organic matter by shattering their chemical bonds at an atomic level. They were considered the ultimate affront to life and the Living Force because they targeted midi-chlorians and created a wound in the Force. Class-D detonators did not detonate in a fiery explosion and instead produced a rippling bubble that annihilated all matter in a five-meter radius in a single zeptosecond. Because of their cataclysmic-level of destruction, Class-D detonators were outlawed across the galaxy.

During a mission to capture the rogue genetic terrorist Zeta Magnus on the planet Skye, a squad of Sun Guards disguised as clone commandos infiltrated the Jedi task force. They secretly carried Class-D detonators and used them against a horde of Oskan blood eaters. The detonation disintegrated the oskans, created a perfect ten-meter wide crater in the floor, and collapsed the cavern ceiling. Sensing the wound in the Force the detonator created, Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi berated the commandos. When the commandos later turned on the Jedi in Zeta Magnus' castle, they used another Class-D detonator against them. The detonator was triggered by Jedi Padawan Halagad Ventor with the Force and detonated in the clone's hand. The destructive bubble that formed engulfed the commandos and the cloning cylinders holding the clones of Anakin, Obi-Wan, and Halagad.

A compact charric was a compact charric ranged weapon which was silent when it fired used by members of the Chiss Ascendancy government. Chiss Mitth family Caregiver Mitth'ali'astov "Thalias" obtained Mitth family Senior Aide Thivik's compact charric after the aide to his Patriarch, Mitth'urf'ianico "Thurfian," gave it to Thalias. Both Chiss entered a tube car with Thurfian's armed guards, however, Thalias and Thurfian were in a separated compartment, where the Chiss Caregiver threatened Thurfian with death if he did not listen to her request about Senior Captain Thrawn. After the Chiss woman's request was heard, she gave the charric to Thurfian.

A compact charric appeared in the 2021 novel Thrawn Ascendancy: Lesser Evil, the final volume in Timothy Zahn's Ascendancy Trilogy.

entities.name: Cybernetic Weapon Enhancement Mod VII
entities.description:
The Cybernetic Weapon Enhancement Mod VII was a model of cybernetic weapon implant available in the period following the Battle of Yavin during the Galactic Civil War between the Galactic Empire and the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Designed by BlasTech Industries, the Mod VII was the seventh–and first successful–attempt made by the company to create a realistic limb that also functioned as a long-range weapon. The enhancement cost 4000 credits, and was made using outsourced limb components combined with BlasTech's own design of light blaster pistol. The device looked and functioned like a normal limb most of the time, but could split open to reveal the weapon component at a speed quick enough to surprise most opponents. The weapon was favored by bounty hunters and assassins and could not be dropped or removed.

The Cybernetic Weapon Enhancement Mod VII was first mentioned in the Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook released by Fantasy Flight Games in 2013 and written by Sterling Hershey.

Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

Commander Kimmund of the First Legion later informed his superiors of the weapons after the battle was over and speculated that they had been purchased locally.

entities.name: Grim Rose
entities.description:
The Grim Rose was a dark artifact that could kill when given a sample of the target's genetic material. The Rose worked by scanning people across the galaxy who have been affected or influenced by the target, over time finding people who have a progressively stronger and stronger connection to the target until it finds the target themselves. Once the Rose finds the target, it kills target along with every person the Rose scanned on its path to find the target.

The Rose could not be turned off and was durable enough to deflect a lightsaber. The only way possible to stop the Rose from killing its target and everyone along that target's path is by switching the target to a different person where it would begin a new path. If the Rose's target is killed by the Rose or is already dead, the Rose will turn off with its objective completed.

The Rose was briefly in the possession of the Rebellion who attempted to use the Rose to kill Emperor Palpatine, but stopped the Rose before it was able to, saving the lives of thousands of people scanned by the Rose.

The Grim Rose was a black cube inscribed with identical golden markings on each of its sides, which included a large star-like pattern in the center, with circles of ancient writing on the edges of the sides surrounding the central star-like pattern. The writings contain the name of the Grim Rose and its function.

entities.name: Superweapon
entities.description:
Superweapons or megaweapons were weapons of extremely devastating power, ranging from the capacity to destroy a city to entire planets.

A superweapon (also spelled super-weapon) or megaweapon referred to a weapon of great power, capable of bringing varying degrees of massive destruction. Some may level whole cities and continents, whilst some could even destroy planets.

A type of superweapon was the superlaser, which were laser-based superweapons. These weapons often required large power-sources, such as the first Death Star, which took massive amounts of Kyber crystals to fire.

An ancient walker and a superweapon created by the culture of the Ancients eons before the founding of the Jedi Order was a massive, four-legged vehicle, armed with a head-mounted energy weapon capable of significant amounts of destruction.

Cedrax later gave the weapon to the Jedi Consular who tried to infiltrate the Guiding Hand. The Jedi used the weapon to prove their expertise to the Red Light Lancers tech gang, a part of the Guiding Hand.

entities.name: The Spike
entities.description:
The Spike was a massive, cylindrical pulse hammer initially intended to be used against sub-crustal military bunkers. Built by Galactic Solutions Industries, the weapon was deemed unfit for this purpose due to the immense and violent pressure unleashed on its occupants when its payload would fire. The costly weapon proved less than desirable for prospective buyers but found a new rationale when the organization, The Hyland Organization for Rakghoul Neutralization (THORN), discovered the use of underground warrens by rakghouls. The CEO of G.S.I and founder of THORN, Addalar Hyland, quickly adapted the machine to displace soil and rock to allow the entry of a temporary shaft equipped with a turbolift into subterranean rakghoul territory. Upon entry into the hollow lairs beneath the ground, the apparatus would then release a bevy of navigational markers that scanned the tunnels for expeditionary use by THORN.left|thumb|The Spike on Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan

The Spike was deployed in King's Pass on Alderaan during the Alderaan Rakghoul Resurgence, in order to create an access to the rakghoul tunnels.

It was also deployed in the Dune Sea on Tatooine and in Labor Valley on Corellia when the rakghoul plague resurfaced on both planets.

entities.name: Automated defense system
entities.description:
An Automated Defense System was a defense computer program, using any combination of laser cannons, turbolasers, or other weapons to defend a ship, space station or planetary fortress from attack without the need of a manual controller. They could be routed through to exterior weapons to defend against enemy vessels or vehicles, or interior automatic turrets to defend against infiltrating soldiers.

Exterior Automated Defense Systems were in use before the New Sith Wars, but the programming was basic and could only follow predictable attack patterns. Most pilots could predict after one or two runs and overcome with minimal difficulty. As a result, manually operated lasers were preferred and became the norm, as an operator could match a pilot's unpredictability whereas these early systems could not.

One such system was that defending the fortress of Belia Darzu on the legendary dark side planet of Tython. When Darth Bane traveled to the world seeking Darzu's knowledge of constructing Sith holocrons, he was attacked by a pair of laser turrets working on one such system. Evading the initial attacks, Bane noticed the turrets followed an identical attack pattern as the first attempt to shoot him down on his second pass. Avoiding the turrets predictable fire, he decimated the two towers.

Due to the restricted space inside a fortress or ship, Interior defense systems were used to a much wider extent, including inside capital starships as used during the Clone Wars and the Galactic Civil War.

entities.name: Blaster
entities.description:
A blaster, also called a gun, was any type of ranged weapon that fired bolts of intense plasma or particle-based energy, often mistaken for lasers.

Operating under the same principles as laser weaponry and firing at least partially by means of magnetic induction, blasters converted energy-rich gas, to a glowing particle beam that could pierce and melt through targets. called a "blaster bolt," which carried the shard of energy to the target.

Blasters came in a variety of sizes and shapes, including stun blasters, blaster pistols, blaster rifles, reconfigurable blasters, scatterblasters, shock blasters, ion blasters, ion rifles, percussive cannons,

Blaster artillery could also be attached on droids and vehicles. They could deliver variable levels of damage intensity, from stun to kill settings. Blaster muskets were a type of blaster pistol that was used by the Shistavanen pirate Brutus during the New Republic Era. Captain Brutus was captured while welding a blaster musket by the Onyx Cinder's Cargo-lifting arm while approached its landing ramp after it was tractored into the hanger of his frigate. After being grabbed by the lift arm he fired a single blast before dropping the blaster. The former pirate captain Silvo picked up Brutus' blaster musket after approaching the restrained Brutus. Avenging his previous mutiny, Silvo killed Brutus with a single shot from the blaster musket and retook his pirate crew.

Blaster muskets were first identified in the Disney+ audio descriptions of "We're Gonna Be In So Much Trouble," the seventh episode of the live–action series Star Wars: Skeleton Crew which was released on January 7, 2025.

entities.name: Blaster pistol
entities.description:
The blaster pistol was a common weapon used by both military personnel and civilians. Pistols came in a variety of shapes, sizes, and capabilities.

Some were augmented for other functions, such as ascension guns that fired grappling hooks and ascension cables. Many blaster pistols contained stun settings which were used to incapacitate a target instead of dealing lethal damage. Like all blaster technology, the blaster pistol fired cohesive bursts of plasma or particle-based energy called "bolts." Blaster bolts could be repelled by magnetic seals and deflector shields. A lightsaber-blaster hybrid is a lightsaber with a blaster pistol built in the hilt. So far it only fires stun bolts. Types of blaster pistols included Heavy blaster pistols, Blaster muskets, Hold-out blasters, Snub-blasters, Bryar pistols, Defender sporting blaster pistols, and BH-4 Double Blasters.

Two-barreled blaster pistol designs included the Blurrg-1120 holdout blaster, RSKF-44 heavy blaster, S-195 blaster pistol, and the "Snubble special" pistol. The A-180 and A280-CFE were blaster pistols that could be reconfigured into an assault blaster rifle and a sniper rifle. Blaster pistols could also have unique loading mechanisms as the S-195 had as hinged assembly that allowed for faster loading of reactant gas capsules or power plugs, the DG-29 heavy blaster pistol could be loaded from the side,

The Royal Naboo Security Forces primary wielded S-5 blaster pistols and CR-2 heavy blaster pistols. Bounty Hunter Zam Wesell carried a KYD-21 blaster pistol. The bounty hunter Jango Fett was proficient at wielding twin WESTAR-34 blaster pistols, at the same time.

entities.name: Blaster rifle
entities.description:
Blaster rifles were weapons more powerful and larger than other types of blasters, such as blaster pistols. It was used in various factions.

Pulse cannons were powerful blaster rifles. Assault rifles were modular versions of the blaster rifle. Longblasters had high precision and power over long ranges. Boiler rifles were illegal weapons. Stun rifles were a type of blaster rifle and stun weaponry. The Relby-v10 micro grenade launcher, blaster spear, bo-rifle, and the SP-B50 blaster rifle were blaster/hybrids.

Blaster rifle length ranged from the short E-11 and DC-15A blaster carbine to the longer A280 and DC-15A blaster rifle. Rifles almost always had a scope, a fully automatic firing mode, and some kind of stock. Other forms of blaster rifles included blaster carbines, heavy blaster rifles, light repeating blasters, and sniper rifles.

Caltrops first appeared in the mobile game Star Wars: Uprising, which was released in 2015 by Kabam for iOS and Android platforms. In Uprising, caltrops are a defensive ability which can be purchased from a trainer.

Another such weapon, the ion cannon, could be used to fire focused particles or plasma. The All Terrain Tactical Enforcer and the AT-AP both have a large heavy projectile cannon.

entities.name: Disruptor
entities.description:
Disruptors were a type of particularly dangerous energy weapon which was banned by Imperial law,

One model of disruptor was the T-7 ion disruptor rifle, The Aqualish weapon designer Amda Wabo later tried to sell a large supply of the weapons to Imperial Minister Maketh Tua, but was prevented from doing so by the crew of the starship known as the Ghost. the Amban phase-pulse blaster, and the DX-2 disruptor blaster pistol.

T-7 ion disruptor rifles were capable of disabling an All Terrain Defense Pod with a single shot, and were capable of short-circuiting an entire ship.

When fired upon a biological target, the victim was disintegrated atom by atom, resulting in a slow, painful death. After T-7's were used against the Lasat during the fall of their homeworld, the weapons were banned by the Imperial Senate. The mere sight of a T-7 was enough to cause surviving Lasat to recoil in shock.

entities.name: Flamethrower
entities.description:
Flamethrowers were weapons that fired streams or bursts of fire.

A millennia-old infantry mainstay, flamethrowers were modernized by Mandalorian super commandos and Republic-era clone troopers during the Clone Wars.

Mandalorian warriors often integrated flamethrowers into their vambraces as one of their many anti-Jedi tools, as the flames could not be blocked by the single beam of a lightsaber, forcing the defender to either retreat. A Force wielder with sufficient skill, strength in the Force and time to react could shield themselves from the flames with the Force, though this required considerable effort. Mandalorian plasma shields could also be used to defend against flamethrower attacks.

At the Boonta Eve Classic, Sebulba equipped his podracer with flamethrowers. He use them as weapon against other podracers to help him win the the podrace. Bounty hunters such as Jango Fett and Cad Bane used flamethrowers against the Jedi.

She typically loaded it with different gases, ranging from stun gas to poison and contact neurotoxins.

An Aqualish bounty hunter fought with a grenade launcher during a skirmish on the planet Omereth, killing Nakari Kelen in process. A notably powerful type of grenade launcher was the Relby-v10 micro grenade launcher, the favored weapon of the Trandoshan bounty hunters Cradossk and Bossk.

entities.name: Grenade mortar
entities.description:
The grenade mortar was a powerful weapon that was designed to lob grenades over long distances. Many were fitted with repulsorlift platform, meaning that they could easily be transported across the battlefield quickly, laying down barrages and relocating before counter-battery fire could be called down. The market leader could shoot grenades at a rate of one every 1.2 seconds at a range of over one kilometer. A sound dampener was often added to give the weapon a degree of stealth, while it boasted a sophisticated targeting computer in order to compensate dark or foggy conditions.

The grenade mortar could also be loaded onto a two-person repulsorlift platform, increasing the ammo capacity to five hundred grenades and the top speed to 250 kilometers per hour. To reach these speeds the platform was powered by an X-7a repulsorlift engine and four thrust vectors. The main disadvantage of this platform though was its weakness, a simple blaster shot could do considerable damage and the pilot and gunner were left dangerously open. The grenade launcher could, however, be exchanged with an E-Web heavy repeating blaster if the situation called for it. Four or more platforms normally worked together to lay down light ordnance.

entities.name: Heavy blaster rifle
entities.description:
Heavy blaster rifles were a larger and more powerful variant of the blaster rifle. They were often only distributed to one or two infantry members per squad, and inflicted more damage from greater distances than anything else used within a squad. With barrels that were often exceptionally long, heavy rifles tended to be very accurate. They could easily pierce plastoid and heavy combat armor, and could even pose a threat to lightly armored speeders.

Heavy blaster rifles employed a powerful, sometimes concentrated blaster gases, advanced XCiter technologies, upgraded Galven circuitry, and precision-ground focusing crystals to achieve their longer range, beam cohesion, and energy output. A key divider between standard rifles and heavy rifles was the option to make them fully automatic, however, over the course of galactic history, a number of semi-automatic weapons, often high-powered sniper rifles, were classified as heavy blaster rifles, and were regulated as such.

A hold-out blaster was a type of blaster pistol, used as a personal sidearm for easy concealment, often employed when other weapons or equipment were not viable or were simply unavailable.

Hera Syndulla used a Blurrg-1120 holdout blaster whenever she fought outside the Ghost. The deactivator hold-out pistol could be fired to deactivate droids. entities.name: Ion blaster
entities.description:
Ion blasters, were handheld weapons used by the Jawas of Tatooine while hunting for salvage. These customized blasters fired particles of ionized energy to disable the electrical systems of droids, rendering them powerless. When used against living creatures, they could be used as stun weapons.

The ion blasters carried by Jawa scavengers of Tatooine were handcrafted, and the PK-32 droid blaster was a model of droid blaster. The species typically began with a stripped-down blaster power pack, and added components such as an accu-accelerator, scrounged from a starship's ion engine, and a restraining bolt from a droid. These pieces were added to the weapon's firing mechanism, giving the blaster pistol an accurate range of up to twelve meters. The blasters were fitted with a safety button located above the trigger, and discharged blasts of ionized particles that disrupted the electronic systems of droids, causing the units to shut down. They could also be employed to stun living beings, in order to keep enemies alive.

Ion weapons were a long-established technology in the galaxy, ranging from larger ranged weapons such as the T-7 ion disruptor rifle to massive planet-based ion cannons. The Jawa ion blasters were created using the same principle, and were carried by the scavengers during salvage runs on the desert planet of Tatooine.

A group of Jawas used their ion blasters to defend themselves against the Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin after he attempted to board their sandcrawler. While Djarin would succeed in climbing on top of the sandcrawler, he was almost instantly stunned by a series of ion blasters firing simultaneously, causing him to fall onto the ground below.

The Nanite Launcher was a type of projectile launcher which fired nanite payloads, projectiles that could use nanotechnology to either heal or harm targets. The Twi'lek bioengineer Tuya developed a prototype while working at Medtech Industries, which she later stole after she learned they had nefarious plans for the weapon, taking it with her when she became a participant in the Hunters of the Outer Rim competition on the planet Vespaara. It could be temporarily modified for long-range usage.

entities.description:
A nuclear weapon was a device that caused widespread destruction and left behind large concentrations of radiation. Brendol Hux hypothesized that a nuclear weapon's detonation could be responsible for the "poisoning" of the dead lands on Parnassos, although he was unsure whether the detonation had been the result of deliberate usage or a factory accident for nuclear weapon production.

entities.name: Scatter gun
entities.description:
The scatter gun was a powerful slugthrower weapon that was used by the Galactic Republic, Confederacy of Independent Systems, Alliance to Restore the Republic, Galactic Empire, and the New Republic. It was lethal when fired from close range, and it could penetrate through deflector shields.

The scatter gun was introduced in Star Wars: Battlefront first major expansion pack, The Outer Rim DLC. It is bought through the use of Hutt Contracts, and will only unlock after the player has achieved 40 kills using the CA-87 shock blaster and by using 20 Focus Fire charges.

In 2025, during the Star Wars season Galactic Battle in the video game Fortnite Battle Royale, the weapon was added under the name "ACP Scatter Blaster." Unlike its canon counterpart, the change was made to accommodate gameplay and the complete removal of ammos for the season.

entities.name: Seismic charge
entities.description:
Seismic charges, also known as a seismic bomb, were devastating weapons that drew sound in from their immediate vicinity and exploded in concussive waves of brilliant blue light, shattering everything in their wake. A Charge Core was a component used in seismic charges. Jango Fett launched several Void-7 seismic charges from a deployer aboard his starship, Slave I, while trying to kill Obi-Wan Kenobi during their dogfight in the asteroid field that orbited the planet Geonosis.

Years later, during the Galactic Civil War, Luke Skywalker acquired Utheel Rockcrusher Compact charge during his mission to extract the Givin operator Drusil Bephorin. He deployed one to destroy an Immobilizer 418 cruiser.

In 9 ABY, Jango's son Boba Fett flew Slave I to the Great Pit of Carkoon to look for his lost armor. The Sarlacc inside the pit attempted to draw in the ship with its tentacles, but Fennec Shand dropped a seismic charge into the sarlacc's mouth, destroying it. Some time afterwards, Boba picked up Din Djarin and Migs Mayfeld following their raid on an Imperial refinery on Morak. Two TIE fighters pursued the ship as it escaped, but Boba quickly obliterated the fighters with a charge.

Sound designer Ben Burtt describes the sound of a seismic charge as an "audio black hole," where the sonic blast follows a moment of silence. Burtt had wanted to implement this sound design, which he called "Space Ether Explosions," since Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope. When he first presented the sound effect for exploding TIE Fighters, George Lucas did not like it, so he halted work on it until Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones.{{WebCite|url=http://filmsound.org/starwars/starwars-AQ.htm|text=Ben Burtt answers questions about sound design of Star Wars

entities.name: Shoulder-mounted armament
entities.description:
Shoulder-mounted armaments were a diverse style of weapon configurations utilizing shoulder and often back attachments that fired some form of over-the-shoulder weaponry intended to free the hands of the user. These armaments were generally autonomous, and sometimes had built-in blaster technology, while others allowed for the attachment and removal of external blaster pistols. The projectile types of these blasters could vary widely, with some firing lasers while others could even launch micro-missiles.

The Parwan bounty hunter Derrown, also known as "the Exterminator," sported a shoulder-mounted blaster and 19 BBY. Mercenary Migs Mayfeld used a pseudocybernetic automated weapon mounting armor attachment equipped with a DT-12 heavy blaster pistol prior to and during the Bothan-Five incident That same year, two participants in the Hunters of the Outer Rim utilized shoulder-mounted weaponry as part of their kits. Hunter Imara Vex wore a shoulder-mounted micro-missile launcher, while the KX-series security droid K-A0S was equipped with a back-mounted SE-14r light repeating blaster.

entities.name: Slugthrower
entities.description:
Slugthrowers were a type of handheld projectile range weapon that used kinetic energy to fire solid projectiles (known as slugs), as opposed to the energy bolts fired by a blaster. Slugs could be fired by weapons such as a slugthrower pistol, slugthrower rifle, and scatter gun. Shotguns were similar to scatter gun slugthrowers.

Carnelion IV inhabitants, the Open and Closed, used a variety of slugthrower weapons in their war against each other, some gatling gun variants are vehicle mounted on Open's large bipedal walkers. Natives from Haruun Kal used crude slugthrowers. These were ineffective against stormtrooper armor.

Typically, Force sensitive lightsaber users were able to successfully parry slugs without issue.

Jas Emari used a custom made slugthrower rifle in the months preceding the Battle of Jakku. Marauders on Hetzal Prime used slugthrower rifles and scatter guns. Cyn's team used slugthrower pistols.

A slugthrower rifle, also known as a projectile rifle, was a type of slugthrower.

Pav-ti Tano used a slugthrower when she took Ahsoka Tano hunting.

Tusken Raiders used cycler rifles to snipe at podracers during the Boonta Eve Classic.

Zam Wesell used a KiSteer 1284 projectile rifle to destroy her ASN courier droid after discovering Obi-Wan Kenobi was hanging on it.

entities.name: Sniper rifle
entities.description:
The sniper rifle, also called a sniper blaster rifle or assassin rifle, was a type of blaster rifle used to shoot targets at long range. Though some rifles were built as sniper rifles, many other models could be used as one with the addition of a scope and other accessories like a stock.

Just before the Clone Wars, Zam Wesell used a flying assassin droid in an attempt to assassinate Senator Padmé Amidala on Coruscant. The plan failed, and Zam Wesell saw the assassin droid returning to her with Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi hanging onto it. To avoid being caught by the Jedi and having her plans exposed, Wesell retrieved her sniper rifle from her airspeeder. Using the targeting scope on her KiSteer 1284 projectile rifle to zoom in on her target, she fired at the incoming droid and destroyed it. This sent Kenobi plummeting toward the planet surface, but he was quickly rescued by Anakin Skywalker. Realizing things had gone south, Wesell immediately stowed her sniper rifle and took off in her Koro-2 all-environment Exodrive airspeeder.

During the Clone Wars, a BX-series droid commando used a BX Sniper Rifle at the Battle of Saleucami to wound Clone Captain Rex and a Death Watch assassin used a BX sniper rifle in a failed attempt to assassinate Satine Kryze on Coruscant. Bounty hunters such as Aurra Sing, Rumi Paramita, and Rako Hardeen used these rifles in their jobs. Onderon rebels' leader Steela Gerrera used one in her fight to liberate Onderon.

The defective clone Crosshair used a 773 Firepuncher rifle during the Clone Wars and continued to use the weapon to deadly effect in service to the Galactic Empire. During the Assault on Cymoon, Chewbacca used a sniper rifle to attack Darth Vader, who deflected all of his shots before using the Force to topple the building Chewbacca was perched upon. Han Solo used a DLT-20A blaster rifle as a sniper rifle during the Battle of Vrogas Vas. Ochi of Bestoon, an assassin working for Crimson Dawn, used a sniper rifle to fire a poison dart, coated in Yurfloo, that grazed the neck of Major Erstin Deez, a member of the Emperor's Royal Guard.

entities.name: Sonic pistol
entities.description:
A sonic pistol was a type of sonic weapon similar to a blaster pistol. It created a high-intensity sonic blast powerful enough to shatter solid objects and cause devastating injuries.

Designed as civilian's response to Jedi and Sith using lightsabers to deflect their attacks, the sonic pistol fired compressed bolts of pure sound at its target. Though slightly less powerful than standard energy weapons such as blasters and pulse-wave weapons, the sonic pistol was particularly effective against Jedi and Sith because the weapon's sonic bolt bent around the lightsaber, making deflection impossible. Additionally, the sonic energy was sometimes able to disrupt a target's equilibrium, causing disorientation.

While this standard version of sonic pistol did not have a dedicated stun setting, other sonic weapons such as Pacnorval's Sd-77 sonic pistol did have a stun setting.

A slightly larger version of this weapon was the heavy sonic blaster, while an even larger rifle version was also produced. A notable model of sonic rifle was the Geonosian sonic blaster, which operated on similar principles as the pistol.

entities.name: Sonic rifle
entities.description:
Sonic rifles were the sonic analog to the blaster rifles, capable of striking targets from a greater range than the heavy sonic blaster while still maintaining the same damage.

Sonic rifles tended to be less powerful than conventional blasters, but they compensated for this by being more likely to pierce less advanced personal energy shields and disorienting their targets with sensory overload.

Like all sonic weapons, the sonic rifle was particularly effective against Jedi and Sith because the weapon could not be deflected by a lightsaber. Additionally, the sonic damage was sometimes able to disrupt the target's equilibrium, causing disorientation.

Variants of the sonic rifle included the SonoMax 100, the SWE/2 sonic rifle, the Arkanian sonic rifle, and the Sg-82 sonic rifle.

During a period of war on the planet Geonosis, the Geonosian hives used sonic weapons in their battles for the planet's resources as well as dominance over each other. Sonic cannons, including the LR1Ks manufactured by Gordarl Weaponsmiths, could be set to forces of varying degrees to smash bones while leaving the Geonosians' rock tunnels unharmed.

entities.name: Sporting blaster rifle
entities.description:
The sporting blaster rifle was a less lethal version of the blaster rifle that was popular with the galactic elite as well as among fringers living in isolated colonies.

The sporting blaster rifle was the rifle version of the sporting blaster pistol. It was very similar to the hunting blaster. They were primarily intended for game-hunting on frontier worlds with high wildlife populations. They were light, easy to carry, and very accurate. Sporting blaster rifles had a shorter range and packed less power than a standard blaster rifle, though they had the advantage of being more affordable and required less bureaucratic hassle to obtain. As a result of this, the weapon became common with assassins and bounty hunters who were able to circumvent the legal restrictions against heavier rifles. Sporting blaster rifles often had a targeting scope mounted on them.

Luke Skywalker kept a sporting blaster rifle in his landspeeder on Tatooine. He had also used it to "bullseye womp rats in his T-16."

entities.name: Tensor weapon
entities.description:
Tensor weapons were a class of weaponry that used tractor beam energy to harm living targets. Such weapons shot rapid pulses of compressed tractor beam waves that affected their target with an unrelenting stream of energy, the result of which caused cell disruption and eventually death. The Squib tensor rifle, manufactured by Amberlandrax Armaments, was a tensor weapon.

Although the tensor rifle is the only known example of a tensor weapon, Galladinium's Fantastic Technology establishes that the rifle is part of a more generalized class.

Wrist lasers typically cost 2,000 credits and 100 credits for a power pack.

Variants of this weapon included the LG-5 laser gauntlet manufactured by Prax Arms, and similarly wrist-mounted wrist blaster.

Wrist rocket launchers were miniaturized missile launchers capable of being worn on the wrist. They fired various types of wrist rockets, including darts and small missiles. They were a favorite of bounty hunters due to their discreet nature, versatility, and power. Bounty hunter Mira used a wrist rocket launcher as her trademark weapon. Another model of wrist rocket launcher was the Kelvarex Consolidated Arms MM9 rocket system, which was used by bounty hunter Boba Fett.

entities.name: Bacca's Ceremonial Blade
entities.description:
Bacca's Ceremonial Blade was a sacred Wookiee sword, created by the legendary Wookiee warrior Bacca from the debris of the first starship to land (or in this case crash) on Kashyyyk.

Bacca passed on the sword to the next chieftain, as it had become a symbol of the strength and courage of the Wookiee Chieftain. The sword was passed from generation to generation until it came into the possession of the Chieftain Rothrrrawr. The blade was broken at the hilt when the Chieftain was fighting a terentatek in the Shadowlands. The blade became lodged in the beast's hide, and Rothrrawr fled with the hilt. From then on, the hilt was seen as the symbol of leadership, and was passed from chieftain to chieftain until Revan found the blade at the behest of Freyyr.

Revan offered it to the exiled Freyyr as a means to help him reclaim his throne from his usurper son, Chuundar. After the defeat of Chuundar, the two parts of the sword were once again reunited, but Freyyr did not keep the sword. At the request of his younger son, Zaalbar, Freyyr allowed him to take possession of the sword, thereby signifying that Zaalbar would become chieftain upon his return.

The Ceremonial Blade first appeared in the Legends video game Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic,

entities.description: The Blade of Zakata Par was an artifact Phee Genoa claimed to have found. On a journey to the Kaldar Trinary system between 19 BBY and 18 BBY, Genoa offered to tell the young clone Omega the story of how she had found the blade, which Omega was interested in. As she began, Genoa described the tale as "exciting" and advised Omega to strap in.

entities.name: Cirra Mace
entities.description:
The Cirra Mace was a ceremonial weapon that was very important to the Cirra akia, the most warlike clan of the Aramandi people in the Brak sector.

The Cirra Mace was 80 centimeters long, made of black obsidian. It was adorned with emeralds and rubies. It was not said to have any strange powers or curses, but was central to Cirra religious ceremonies.

The mace was stolen in about 9 BBY by heretics and sold to an unknown party outside the Aramand Cluster. It turned up fifteen years later on the black market in Brenn, but the Cirra were unable to recover it. It was rumored to have ended up in the Nalroni city of Celanon.

entities.name: Dagger of Mortis
entities.description:
The Dagger of Mortis, simply referred to as the Mortis Dagger, was a mystical weapon that resided on the Altar of the Wild Space world of Mortis. The weapon was kept hidden on the realm of Mortis by the Father, who kept it as a means that could control his children, the Daughter and the Son. The weapon was capable of controlling the sibling pair of powerful Force wielders, and it was also capable of killing them, if necessary. When used on the Father, however, his death at the hands of the dagger would rob his children of their immortality.

When the Father learned that the Chosen One, a prophesied Jedi legend, had appeared in the galaxy, he lured the Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker, believed to be the Chosen One, to his realm on Mortis. However, despite passing the Father's test to prove himself as the Chosen One, Skywalker refused to remain on Mortis in the Father's place, who was dying. The Son then attempted to lure Skywalker to the dark side of the Force, forcing the Daughter and Obi-Wan Kenobi, Skywalker's former Jedi Master, to retrieve the dagger from the Altar of Mortis in an effort to gain control over the Son.

The Son, however, was able to take the dagger from the Jedi, killing Skywalker's Padawan, Ahsoka Tano. When the Son attempted to kill the Father next, the Daughter intervened and was instead killed. A distraught Son left the dagger behind, and the Daughter's remaining life force was used to resurrect Tano. In a final effort to stop the Son, the Father used the dagger on himself, robbing the Son of his immortality and allowing Skywalker to deliver a mortal wound with his lightsaber. The act brought balance in the Force back to Mortis, and the dagger, along with the entire planet, disappeared in a blinding white light from the Father's monastery.

entities.description:
Ap'lek's Mandalorian executioner vibro-ax was an antiquated Mandalorian executioner's vibro-ax that was the weapon of choice for the Knight of Ren Ap'lek. Ap'lek fought with the vibro-ax against Ben Solo on Exegol, but it availed him naught and he perished at the hands of his former leader.

A Mandalorian executioner's vibro-ax forged in ancient times, the weapon was equipped with ultrasonic transmission plates that enhanced its cutting power, turning the ax into a vibro-ax. It was also made of beskar, which resisted the blade of a lightsaber. There were gore channels carved into the face of the blade, as well as vibro-insulator plates to protect the handle of the ax from the vibrations.

The vibro weapon was used by Ap'lek, a member of the Knights of Ren, in conjunction with his smoke canister, incorporated so for his preference for stealth. The ax was once used long ago by a Mandalorian executioner.

In 35 ABY, Ap'lek used his ax to battle Ben Solo, former leader of the Knights of Ren, within the Sith Citadel on the planet Exegol. The ax was left on the battlefield as its wielder dropped it when he was Force pushed to his death.

entities.name: Beskad
entities.description:
A beskad was a traditional Mandalorian sword, forged from beskar. Comprised of a broad, single-edged blade about the length of a grown human's arm that widened toward the tip before tapering to a point, the beskad was a heavy single-handed short sword, designed to crack armor and capable of delivering short, powerful slashes—similar to machete. Two metal guards protected the wielder's hand at the top and base of the hilt. The weapon was based on a design from the ancient Taung. Traditionally, it was accompanied by the kal dagger in the wielder's off hand.

The beskad was first named by author Karen Traviss in her now-Legends e-novella Boba Fett: A Practical Man.

entities.name: Beskar spear
entities.description:
A beskar spear was wielded by the Magistrate Morgan Elsbeth on Corvus during the New Republic Era. The staff was made of pure beskar, a metal alloy tied with Mandalorian culture.

Between 9 BBY and 2 BBY, Morgan used the spear to defend herself and fight the Noghri assassin Rukh, defeating him.

After the fall of the Galactic Empire, between 5 ABY and 9 ABY, the New Republic Ambassador Nadura traveled to Corvus in hopes for the planet to join the Senate. After a heated argument in which Morgan refused to join the Senate and turn herself in, she ordered her guards to kill Nadura and her delegation, using the spear to kill one of them.

By 9 ABY, Morgan used the spear to fight the Force-sensitive Ahsoka Tano, but was defeated by the former Jedi. Tano gifted the staff to the Mandalorian Din Djarin. The staff was durable enough to be able to block and deflect lightsaber blows

entities.description:
Crushgaunts, also called shuk'orok in Mando'a, were a type of strength-enhancing gauntlets created by the Mandalorians centuries before the Clone Wars. They were made of a reactive, polymer-enhanced material reinforced by beskar plates. They could increase their wearer's grip strength to the point that they could shatter bones, crush durasteel, and deflect weapons, even lightsaber blades. Captain Phasma wore a pair of crushgaunts as part of her armor.

entities.description:
The Dark Trooper phase 4 was the fourth iteration and the culmination of the Dark Trooper, though it was a battle armor developed in the Mandalore Imperial base as an upgrade over the third-generation Dark Trooper to be worn by Moff Gideon and his planned clone army. Forged from beskar alloy collected from Mandalore, the fourth-generation design borrowed heavily from Mandalorian armor philosophy design, and incorporated a visored helmet, vambraces with integrated weaponry, and a jetpack. Additionally, the armor enhanced Gideon's strength, allowing him to deliver powerful blows and to crush the Darksaber in one hand.

It resembled the classic stormtrooper armor, and was made with an alloy of beskar, like that of Mandalorian armor, along with jetpacks, and vambraces, which were equipped with flamethrowers and whipcord launchers. Two commandos that escorted Moff Gideon had red-painted vambraces, leg armor, and red stripes on the sides of their helmets.

entities.description:
The kal was a short dagger used by Mandalorians. It was typically wielded in one's off hand as an accompaniment to the beskad sword. The kal, forged of beskar, consisted of a hexagonal blade with a rectangular cutout along its center. The hilt was bare metal and had no crossguard, though the notch where the blade met the hilt did provide some protection for the user's hand. While not as deadly as the beskad, the kal was still a formidable weapon in the hands of a skilled user.

entities.description:
Shinbone blade was a dagger forged from beskar owned by the bounty hunter Beilert Valance. It was an effective last resort in case Valance's cyborg systems were incapacitated.

Shinbone was the town where Liberty Valance from the classic John Ford western The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance lived.

entities.name: Cortosis
entities.description:
Cortosis was a metal that could be found on the planets Dinzo, Mokivj, and Bal'demnic, where the Sith known as "the Stranger" resided.

Cortosis was an extremely rare metal that had a very high energy absorption rate and transmission coefficients, which allowed even the energy of a blaster bolt to be dissipated upon contact. One of the strongest minerals in the galaxy, cortosis could even withstand the blow of a lightsaber and briefly short out its blade. It could also redirect the heat of explosions, as discovered when General Anakin Skywalker attempted to collapse the entrance of a cortosis mine, and the resulting explosion breached through Mokivj's crust. Apart from its physical properties, cortosis could also affect a Force-sensitive's ability to use the Force, as helmets made from the material isolated the wearer's thoughts and prevented others from sensing them.

Despite these advantages, cortosis was very fragile in its natural state, making it normally useless as armor. However, it was possible to, with effort, turn cortosis into an armor. When faced with an example of cortosis armor, the Chiss tactician Mitth'raw'nuruodo ("Thrawn") theorized that the cortosis was woven into the armor network as part of a defense matrix, thereby ensuring any incoming energy weapon—such as a blaster shot or the swing of a lightsaber—was dissipated throughout the whole of the armor network. Nonetheless, cortosis armor had difficulties with prolonged energy attacks, such as those of lightning guns, which would overload the material,

Many of the best suits of Mandalorian armor utilized cortosis weave, an energy-resistant mesh composed of cortosis ore. Cortosis could also be forged into a cortosis staff or cortosis sword, melee weapons that retained the defensive properties of cortosis, while cortosis weave was additionally used in the creation of the cortosis shield. Cortosis was stronger than similar materials like phrik.

The weapons existed in numerous styles and contained varying amounts of cortosis, but the practice of making them may have been as old as the practice of making lightsabers itself. The weapons cost 1,350 credits.

entities.name: Cortosis weave
entities.description:
Cortosis-weave was a swordsmithing technique commonly used on high-quality vibroblades and other melee weapons when combat with opponents wielding lightsabers was considered to be likely. It also was a descriptor for equipment that had been crafted utilizing cortosis ore. Cortosis-weave was employed primarily because it made the weapon able to withstand lightsaber blows. They could also be fashioned into armor or other gear. Weapons needed very little cortosis to be effective but armor required a substantially larger amount. The greater quantity provided an additional benefit to wearers though—a lightsaber would deactivate after contact was made with cortosis armor. Cortosis was extremely rare though and, thus, extremely expensive, resulting in few weapons and armor made with it. Several cultures developed various techniques for insulating traditional melee weapons against such sparring damage, but the art of bonding cortosis to blades in such a manner was first perfected by Echani weaponsmiths sometime prior to the Mandalorian Wars.

Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Prima's Official Strategy Guide

Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords: Prima Official Game Guide

Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide

entities.name: Cortosis-weave armor
entities.description:
Cortosis-weave armor was an armor which was resistant to lightsabers. It contained traces of cortosis, an ore prized for its ability to create an energy feedback loop which would temporarily shut down a lightsaber.

As cortosis weave contained only trace amounts of the ore woven into it, the armor lost the ability to short out an opponent's energy blade. Instead armor containing the cortosis weave would merely be resistant to lightsaber strikes.

Cortosis weave was in use as early as 4000 BBY as both an armor underlay and for the tempering of traditional melee weapons against lightsabers. At this time cortosis ore seemed to be much more common, later, however it would become a rarer, more valuable material that would give the user an unexpected edge against a force-sensitive opponent.

The armor was known to have been used by the Yinchorri in the 33 BBY Yinchorri Uprising. A variation was also used by the Jensaarai Corran Horn and Luke Skywalker fought in 11 ABY on the planet Susevfi. The Jensaarai customized their armor with cortosis weave patterns for decoration, although it retained the more pragmatic abilities of the armor. The cortosis used in their armor was smuggled from the gas planet Bespin. Shadowtrooper armor worn by the force sensitive troops of the Empire Reborn battled by Kyle Katarn and the members of the Yavin 4 Jedi academy in 13 ABY also contained cortosis weave.

entities.name: Null Blade
entities.description:
The Null Blade was a sword forged with cortosis alloy by Miril, the leader of the anti-Sith Ascendant cult during the era of the Sith. As a cortosis weapon, the blade could short out a lightsaber for a brief time if the lightsaber blade made contact with the Null Blade. However, as the weapon was not reinforced by Miril by the time of the fall of the Ascendant, the Null Blade itself would be cut by the lightsaber: in effect, Miril had a weapon that could be cut down by a lightsaber, only for that lightsaber to then fail. Centuries later, the Spark Eternal—a creation of Miril and the Ascendant—resurfaced and possessed the body of Doctor Chelli Lona Aphra, who it used to wield the Null Blade after rediscovering the weapon. With the blade able to take on lightsaber strikes by that time, the Spark-possessed Aphra wielded the Null Blade against the Sith Lord Darth Vader during the Battle at Amaxine Station, where the possessed doctor shorted out Vader's blade once their weapons struck each other. In response, Vader unleashed a Force push that separated Aphra and the Spark.

The Null Blade was a type of sword created by the Chadra-Fan Miril, the leader of the Ascendant, to kill the Sith. It had a cortosis alloy, which allowed it to neutralize a lightsaber, though it only worked temporarily. As of a result of Miril lacking the materials to finish the Null Blade, it was not reinforced, so, if the weapon was struck by a lightsaber, the blade broke. All the same, the Null Blade did succeed in temporarily shorting out the lightsaber that hit it. and the Null Blade was left unfinished.

Between 3 ABY and 4 ABY, after possessing the body of the archaeologist Doctor Chelli Lona Aphra, the Spark Eternal, another creation of Miril's, traveled to the the Vermillion, the Fortress-Flagship of Crimson Dawn, in search of other Ascendant technology, and drew the Null Blade from an altar in the office of "The Archivist," which it used to attack Just Lucky and Ariole Yu, though they both escaped.

entities.name: Sith war sword
entities.description:
The Sith war sword was a melee weapon used by Sith and Sith minions during the Dark Wars. Their double-edged staff-like appearance may have been the forebearer of the double-bladed lightsabers preferred by many Sith warriors.

Most Sith after the fall of the ancient Sith Empire wielded lightsabers in combat, though some still preferred ancient Sith war swords. Sith warriors used them for the feeling of hard metal cutting through soft flesh. They were forged with cortosis-weave metal.

Also, around the time that the Dark Jedi Exiles met with the original Sith on the planet of Korriban, Dark Jedi/Sith Lord Ajunta Pall used a Sith War Sword to kill the former Sith King by decapitation.

Another type of Sith war sword existed that was not a double-bladed sword, but rather a traditional-looking sword. Instead of cortosis, the blade was treated with Sith alchemy to produce the lightsaber-impervious effect. This Sith alchemical weapon was not only able to block lightsaber attacks, but also deflect and redirect blaster bolts in much the same way as lightsabers.

entities.name: The Stranger's helmet
entities.description:
The Stranger's helmet was a helmet worn by the Sith Lord known as the "the Stranger" during the High Republic Era. It was made of twisted cortosis metal that formed a sinister smile on the helmet as it masked the identity of the Stranger and kept Force-sensitives from peering into his thoughts. The cortosis metal also acted as sensory deprivation, allowing the Stranger to feel only the Force. In 132 BBY, Verosha Aniseya wore the helmet on Bal'demnic.

The helmet's final design and creation was done by Neal Scanlan's creature department by designer/ modeller Nick Tyrrell.

entities.name: .48-caliber Enforcer pistol
entities.description:
The .48-caliber Enforcer pistol, commonly known as the Enforcer pistol or the .48 Enforcer, was a projectile weapon developed in limited quantities by the Morellian Weapons Conglomerate, only to be used by the Morellian Enforcers. It was not sold except in the black market, commonly over six thousand credits.

The projectile equivalent to a heavy blaster pistol, the Enforcer boasted eight .48 caliber slugs and produced a cannon like crack upon firing a slug, with the slug itself carrying enormous stopping power sufficient to pierce heavy personal armors and even light vehicles; as was the case when Barosa Warren demolished a XP-38 sport landspeeder.

With its power though came extreme recoil, with specialized training needed to avoid having the weapon fly out of a users hand with each shot. However, with practice firing the weapon was possible, and with specialized military training - such as that offered to Morellian Enforcers - rapid fire was also possible; though practice was needed to ensure that shots were precise, as rapid firing could lead to erratic placement of shots.

Scoutmaster Barosa Warren used one as his weapon of choice, and due to his training as a Morellian Enforcer was capable of firing multiple shots in quick succession.

entities.name: Blastsword
entities.description:
The blastsword was a melee weapon favored by the Adumari noblemen for use in their frequent honor duels. The weapon closely resembled a conventional sword, except for one significant difference. The end of the sword contained an energy outlet which, when turned on, emitted a blaster shot upon contact being made with the tip. This emitter also left light trails in the air where it traveled, an effect which was used for comic purposes by New Republic pilot Wes Janson, who took a fancy to the weapon while on a diplomatic mission to Adumar. The Adumari had several variants of the weapon, including a polearm version used by guards of the perator, or ruler, of the nation of Cartann. The weapons were considered fit for polite company, and Adumari duelists, such as Cheriss ke Hanadi, often wielded them single-handedly while holding a shorter knife or dagger in the off hand.

Adumari culture afforded a certain significance to the blastsword, and they were carried by nobility and commoners alike. Over the years, Adumari nobility developed a stylized form for use of the weapon, which included lowering the lethality of the blaster charge to only stun instead of kill, as well as make certain blows illegal for use, though some fighters ignored those rules. Successful competitive blastsword fighters could even make a living off of endorsements from manufacturers of blastswords, such as Ghephaenne Deeper-Craters Weaponmakers. Though most honor duels fought on Adumar were lethal before the Adumari Civil War, there was a growing trend toward nonlethal blastsword duels after the Adumar joined the New Republic. The blastsword eventually found its way offworld and became popular on several other worlds as well.

The blastsword was a long metal sword that was about as long as a Human man's arm The hilt featured a pommel and was covered by a curved metal guard to protect the hand of the user, while the blade's edge began a few centimeters above the guard. The guard was also described by New Republic pilot Wes Janson as useful for bludgeoning. Unlike other sword designs, which featured a sharp tip, the blastsword had a flared nozzle at its tip. The tip was connected to a blaster mechanism powered by a cell located in the hilt that, when activated by means of a switch at the pommel, would discharge an energy blast upon contact with a solid object. When the blaster was activated, the blastsword's tip made a humming noise and glowed with energy, leaving behind colorful lines as it was moved. Due to its exotic design and function, a user required training to wield the weapon proficiently.

While many Adumari carried standard blastswords, polearm versions of the weapon did exist. These were used on at least one occasion by the honor guard protecting the perator, or ruler, of the nation of Cartann.

entities.name: Bo-rifle
entities.description:
The bo-rifle was a type of weapon that uniquely combined the functions of an electrostaff and a blaster rifle, intended for exclusive use by the Honor Guard of Lasan. It was considered a great insult if it was used by anyone else. The only known exception to this was if the individual in question had defeated a guardsmen and been presented with their weapon, in accordance with the Boosahn Keeraw, the warrior way of the Lasat species.

It consisted of a staff that could be collapsed to a length roughly equivalent to a standard blaster rifle. When extended, the weapon's tip(s) were electrified, up to 11,000 volts, either purple or yellow in color and were the primary contact points of the weapon during melee combat. The number of tips on the weapon depended on the model (AB-75 and J-19 had two, the CJ-9 had one). The weapon functioned as a quarterstaff when used in melee combat. When retracted or folded, the weapon functioned as a blaster rifle.

The bo-rifle was the exclusive weapon of the Lasan High Honor Guard. It was an insult to Lasat culture for anyone else to wield the weapon Following the devastation of Lasan, bo-rifles were rarely seen in the galaxy, although some CJ-9 bo-rifles would later fall into the hands of both the Alliance to Restore the Republic and the Galactic Empire by the time of the Galactic Civil War.

Agent Alexsandr Kallus, a member of the Galactic Empire's Imperial Security Bureau who took part in the siege of Lasan, acquired his J-19 bo-rifle via the Boosahn Keeraw. During the battle, he defeated a Honor Guard, who gifted Kallus his rifle as a sign of the agent's superior ability in combat. Kallus was surprised by the action but accepted.

entities.name: Capturing stick
entities.description:
The Lizard Warriors, a sentient species of the Forest Moon of Endor, used individually unique weapons that consisted of a long, thin, wooden stick and a rope looped around the stick. It was used to capture beings that intruded into the reptilians' territory, the Valley of the Lizard Warriors, and keep the interloper from escaping. The stick was a relatively close-range weapon that worked well during an ambush. Once the enemy was snagged, the rope pulled tight around their body, allowing the weapon's user to control the captive, for example to force them to march.

In 3 ABY, the Lizard Warriors captured the Ewoks Teebo and Wicket W. Warrick, who had wandered into the Valley of the Lizard Warriors. The reptilians then marched the Ewoks to meet Graak, an outcast Ewok and the leader of the Lizard Warriors.

The weapon appeared in Ewoks 4, the fourth issue of the Ewoks comic series, which was written by David Manak, illustrated by Warren Kremer,

entities.name: Darkstick
entities.description:
The darkstick was a weapon unique to the Kerestian people. Wickedly curved to aid slicing, the darkstick was used by the struggling Kerestians to hunt game along their barely hospitable home planet's equator.

Though developed by a spacefaring species, the darkstick was surprisingly primitive in construction and design; weaponsmiths employed lightweight metal to individually craft darksticks, though evidence exists that extinct hardwoods were once used. As a result of their independent creation, darksticks varied significantly in size—some were fifteen-centimeter blades concealable in a sleeve, while others were massive, two handed weapons primarily used for bashing and chopping. The typical design, however, was twenty centimeters long and could fit between a Kerestian's enormous knuckles. Light absorbing cells were also used in darksticks.

Attacks consisted primarily of slashing, as the darksticks fit into Kerestian hands like claws. Hunters were armed with several in each hand, transforming into unstoppable killing machines. The darkstick's sweeping curve opened the possibility of throwing the weapon. This was extremely difficult and only the most experienced hunters attempted this; however, a master of this technique could execute powerful assaults from a range of twenty meters. Even harder to learn was the ability to throw the darkstick in such a fashion that it returned to the user's hand. The tactical value of this skill was not underestimated by the Kerestian weaponsmiths, who experimented with metallic systems that automatically recalled a dispatched darkstick to the user's hands. Darksticks could be further modified to explode, and poison was frequently applied to the blade's hollow tip.

Kerestian legends played into both the application and function of the darkstick. Mythology held that following the death of the body, souls were doomed to wallow in the Great Darkness for all eternity. Kerestians were unafraid of such torment; indeed, they welcomed it by attaching symbolism to darksticks. The weapons were silent and deadly, sometimes painted black to constantly remind the wielder of their fate. Through modern technological advances, weaponsmiths built upon the shadowy image by implanting webs of light-absorbing cells into darksticks. Upon activation, a shroud of blackness descended upon the weapon, its bearer, and anyone else close enough and unfortunate enough to face a Kerestian warrior. The victim was blinded, but the warrior was not; they wore infrared goggles to remain at top efficiency.

entities.name: Felucian Skullblade
entities.description:
The Felucian Skullblade was a primitive weapon used by Felucian shamans in ceremonies and combat alike.

Felucian Skullblades were constructed from the skull and teeth of specific native creatures. These creatures grew trace amounts of Force-reactive crystals, similar to those used in the construction of lightsabers, in their bones allowing weapons constructed from them, when imbued with the Force, to block lightsabers and blaster fire. Skullblades were rarely seen off of Felucia but were sometimes sold on the black market.

A variation of the Felucian Skullblade was the rancor-bone blade. The rancor-bone blade was the traditional weapon used by Felucian warriors on the jungle world of Felucia. Like the Skullblades, the rancor-bone blades were resistant to a lightsaber, as discovered by Galen Marek, who encountered several Felucians wielding such weapons during his second visit to the jungle world, when the balance of the Force on the planet had shifted to the dark side.

The Art and Making of Star Wars: The Force Unleashed

entities.name: Fi'lang
entities.description:
Featuring a curved blade, the fi'lang was the traditional combat knife of the reptilian Trogodile species. In 22 BBY the Trogodile Swyy'm-Ee wielded a pair of fi'langs during a gladiatorial match in the Cauldron, a fighting arena on the planet Rattatak. However, Swyy'm-Ee was killed midway through the match by the Dark Jedi Asajj Ventress.

The fi'lang was a curved-blade combat knife that was augmented with a pair of sharpened points: the first at the end of the blade, and the second on the inside of the blade's curve. However, the prominence and size of the spike inside of the blade's curve varied between fi'langs. The fi'lang could be wielded with one hand, allowing the user to handle a pair of the blades at the same time. The weapon's strapped hilt was brown, and its blade was white and light blue.

The fi'lang was the traditional weapon of the Trogodiles, a sentient reptilian species. the first year of the Clone Wars, the Trogodile Swyy'm-Ee was forced to compete in a gladiatorial match in the Cauldron, a large fighting pit located on the planet Rattatak. During the match, Swyy'm-Ee brandished a pair of fi'langs, and at one point, he faced off against fellow gladiator Flalios. However, the Dark Jedi Asajj Ventress entered the match midway and dropped a large boulder on Swyy'm-Ee using her Force powers, killing the Trogodile.

The fi'lang first appeared, albeit unnamed, in the sixth chapter of the Star Wars: Clone Wars animated television series. The episode originally aired on Cartoon Network The weapon was later identified as the fi'lang in the Ultimate Sticker Book: Star Wars: Clone Wars, published in 2004.

entities.description:
The Fira was the traditional weapon of Selkath warriors belonging to Order of Shasa on the planet Manaan. The Fira was a curved sword able to inflict grievous wounds, every one forged by each member of the Order.

Members of the Order of Shasa were required to construct their Fira sword from metals found in the wreckage of a kolto harvester located in the Hrakert Rift. The harvester's hull plating contained cortosis ore, making the Fira blade invulnerable to a lightsaber. The cortosis metal had to be shaped in the heat of underwater volcanic vents, making the construction of the Fira a dangerous and time-consuming task.

entities.name: Gaderffii stick
entities.description:
A gaderffii stick, also known simply as a gaderffii or gaffi stick, was a bladed club used by the Tusken Raiders. They were used to jab and pummel their victims. The bent end of a gaderffii, called the traang in Tusken, could be doused with sand bat venom, which had paralyzing properties. Though a primitive weapon, it could be extremely deadly in the right hands. The weapon also served as a tool for more mundane tasks, such as cleaning the teeth of a bantha.

While Luke Skywalker was searching for the wandering astromech droid R2-D2 in the Jundland Wastes, he got a close look at the gaderffii of a bellicose Tusken named A'Koba.

In 5 ABY, while on Tatooine, former bounty hunter Boba Fett trained in the use of the gaderffii stick after he joined the ranks of a Tusken tribe. After leading the raid on a Pyke repulsortrain, Fett earned the right to wield a gaderffii stick of his own, which he crafted himself in the Gaderffii stick workshop. He used a branch of a wortwood tree that he found in the desert and made it with the help of a craftsman, who utilized a Tusken Adze.

He carried this stick on his back as Din Djarin left Mos Pelgo following his exploits in aiding the townspeople. Later, he used the weapon to kill Cad Bane.

entities.name: Icehead club
entities.description:
The Icehead club was a wooden bludgeon used by members of the Icehead species, who served as guards and soldiers for the Snow King, a powerful being who lived in the Snow Palace on the Forest Moon of Endor. The weapon was long and thin at its cord-wrapped handle, but it curved forward and widened into a paddle-like surface used to strike at a target. When used on ice, the club was able to swat an object a long distance across the slippery surface. In 3 ABY, Icehead clubs were used by both Ewok infiltrators and Icehead soldiers during a skirmish at the Snow Palace.

The Icehead club was a melee weapon that had a narrow, two-handed grip wrapped in cord that extended for a distance roughly equal to half the height of its Icehead wielder, and curved backward. The club then curved forward acutely and widened into a paddle-like shape at the striking end. Thicker wrappings in orange separated the weapon's tip, handle, and striking surface. Attackers were able to wield the Icehead club both over- and underhanded to strike objects within short distances. In the latter technique, Icehead clubs were able to swat objects long distances across icy surfaces.

In 3 ABY, each Icehead guard outside the Snow Palace—home to a powerful being known as the Snow King—kept watch with an Icehead club slung over the shoulder. Icehead soldiers in the Snow King's throne room also employed the weapon. That summer, three Ewoks from Bright Tree Village—Latara, Teebo, and Wicket Wystri Warrick—used snow to disguise themselves as Iceheads and sneaked into the Snow Palace, where they hoped to rescue their friend, Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka, from the Snow King and his mistress, the Frost Sprite Odra, and to recover the season scepter, which the enchanted monarch used to cause perpetual winter on Endor.

When they reached the Snow King's throne room, a skirmish erupted between Icehead forces and the Ewoks. During the fracas, Teebo used an Icehead club to bat away Iceheads who attacked him while sliding on their heads. The Ewoks reclaimed the season scepter and broke the enchantment placed on the Snow King by Odra. As a reward, the king gave Warrick an Icehead club to adorn his Belt of Honor.

The klirun was a high-tension projectile bow that was the traditional hunting weapon of the Tunroth. It became so revered by the species that it was considered a sacred weapon.

Weighting around 3.5 kg, the powerful hunting bow was built with a recurve so that it remained bow-shaped even when unstrung. Designed for Tunroth strength, the bow had a heavy pull, and was capable of piercing stormtrooper armor. The bows used caros arrows, which were occasionally tipped with talar, a stunning agent that enabled non-lethal strikes.

entities.name: Maser voice-stream
entities.description:
Maser voice-streams, also known as the Oswaft language, were the communications medium and weapons of the Oswaft species.

Their language was complex and highly sophisticated, with communication being performed by modulating radio-frequency waves with their brains. The vacuum-breathers were also able to "speak" a picture-message intended to convey visual reality rather than pure ideas.

Oswaft were able to employ this type of communication in the form of maser bolt. They referred to this as "shouting" at their opponent. The Oswaft were capable of destroying Imperial fighters in a single "shout", and could also destroy unshielded starships. However, maser voice-streams were generally ineffective against capital ship shielding.

entities.name: Mouth-operated gun
entities.description:
The mouth-operated gun was a ranged weapon intended for operation by the Laboi, a species of limbless mammals native to the planet Laboi II. The mouth-operated weapon required no hands to fire and was useful to Laboi who left their homeworld for the greater galaxy. Nevertheless, such technology was incredibly rare and extremely expensive; during the Galactic Civil War, it cost at least ten times the price of a comparable hand-operated weapon.

The second edition of Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races mentions the mouth-operated gun as a possible piece of equipment for Laboi characters in West End Games's Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game. The book, updated by Chuck Truett from the original edition by Troy Denning, marks the first mention of such technology. The source fails to specify whether such weapons used blaster technology, slugthrower technology, or something else.

entities.name: Shyarn
entities.description:
Shyarns were light, curved swords employed by the ancient Cereans during their traditional honor duels.

These primitive looking blade weapons were magnetically attracted to one another, making the weapons lock onto one another during parries. The two duelists remained linked until one was able to free himself and maneuver for another attack. As such, these honor duels were quite breathtaking to behold but were also deadly dances between life and death. Cerean blacksmiths forged the blades from unique metals found on Cerea in a process that resulted in a weapon that had no magnetic pull on other metals; they were magnetically attracted only to each other. Shyarns were small blades that were sometimes difficult to upgrade with technology designed for more conventional swords and vibroblades.

The blades were named shyarn after the old Cerean word for "dancer." Hundreds of Shyarn-Ado Training Schools on Cerea taught the art of swordplay with the shyarn, which took a lifetime to master. In any case, because of its exotic design and function, a user required training before he could wield the weapon properly.

Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords: Prima Official Game Guide

entities.name: Swiftcut foil
entities.description:
A Swiftcut foil was a foil—a type of sword—that was used by the Nagai, a warfaring species whose members favored the use of bladed weapons in combat. Along with Tehk'la blades and longswords, Swiftcut foils were employed in a number of fighting exercises that were daily customs in Nagai society. These exercises were both a form of meditation and a sign of social status; success in them could allow the victor to ascend societal ranks.

entities.name: Tensor rifle
entities.description:
Amberlandrax Armaments' tensor rifle, often referred to as the Squib tensor rifle, was a weapon of Squib design that used tractor beam technology to generate damaging waves of tensor energy. The rifle fired an invisible yet noisy burst of compressed tractor beam waves; the constant barrage affected a biological target at the cellular level and eventually resulted in death. Variants of the tensor weapon used either power generators or standard power packs as an energy source. The device was small enough to fit in Squib hands, although it was difficult to aim and fire correctly without specialized skill.

The tensor rifle was available for sale in the galaxy during the time of both the Galactic Empire and the New Republic. Although retailers such as Galladinium Galactic Exports offered the weapon in their datalog, use of the tensor rifle was strictly regulated and even illegal in most jurisdictions. The weapon's rarity also curtailed its widespread adoption.

Amberlandrax Armaments' tensor rifle was designed with a handle and trigger for one of the user's hands, with a foregrip for the other hand and a flared muzzle at the fore. The weapon drew upon Squib engineering and manufacturing to harness the species' mastery of tractor beam technology. The resulting rifle was part of a general class known as tensor weapons, which emitted quick pulses of compressed tractor beam waves to pummel a target with a constant barrage of cell-destroying tensor energy from a distance. Upon hitting a mark, the rifle's wielder was able to focus the beam on the adversary; the injury caused increased with time until the victim finally died. Nevertheless, Amberlandrax's rifle shot a beam that was invisible to the naked eye, a design that made it difficult to aim accurately. The weapon had a maximum range of 250 meters, but the unwieldy beam made rapid firing impossible. The gun created a din so loud that Squibs who owned the weapon learned to use it to get the attention of beings who might otherwise dismiss them.

The tensor rifle was small enough to be wielded by a single combatant, even one the size of a typical one-meter, twenty-two-kilogram Squib. The weapon itself weighed 7.2 kilograms. Non-Squibs found the tensor rifle difficult to use without specialized training, but Squibs took to it naturally. At least two variants of the weapon were available: one drew energy from conventional power packs of the type used to power other energy weapons and squeezed out fifteen shots before recharge. Another model instead used a power generator for energy and provided fifty shots without power replacement.

entities.name: Phasma's baton
entities.description:
Phasma's baton was a quicksilver baton used by Captain Phasma during the First Order-Resistance War.

The quicksilver baton compacted within a containment field owned and carried by Captain Phasma, served essentially for close-quarters combats, like the one she had aboard the First Order's flagship Supremacy. When the baton was activated, it extended to full length, boasting spearpoints at both ends.

The baton had different forms depending on its state: when the baton was inactive, it condensed down to a small baton; but when it was active, it instantly expanded to its full length.

During her service as stormtrooper Captain of the First Order, Phasma chose a quicksilver baton as her personal weapon as it resembled a tribal spear made of quicksilver like the ones that were used by the tribe where she grew up in a mountain range located on the planet Parnassos. In fact, Phasma's skill with traditional melee weapons was a marker of her primitive past.

entities.name: Phasma's blaster rifle
entities.description:
Phasma's blaster rifle was the personal Sonn-Blas F-11D blaster rifle used by Captain Phasma. The blaster featured a buttstock, chromium finish, and a recurved trigger guard for a two-handed grip.

Captain Phasma carried her customized blaster rifle while performing her duties for the First Order. The blaster rifle was clad in salvaged chromium to match its owner's distinctive armor. However, Phasma's blaster rifle lacked the full trigger guard standard for an F-11D blaster. The barrel of Phasma's blaster rifle had heat dispersal vents, while it also had an extended stock which contained a gas reservoir.

By the time she returned to her homeworld of Parnassos to create her armor a year after joining the First Order, Phasma had secretly ordered the blaster and it was already tuned to her gloves.

In 34 ABY, Phasma carried her blaster at Jakku and used it under the orders of Kylo Ren to execute some of the remaining villagers that survived the attack of the stormtroopers following Lor San Tekka's death. She also carried it when she was thrown into the trash compactor of Starkiller Base.
