entities.name: Pyre's blaster
entities.description:
Pyre's blaster was the personal F-11D blaster rifle of Commander Pyre of the First Order. Crafted by the Sonn-Blas Corporation, the blaster featured an electrum finish that gave it a golden shine. It featured a J20 electroscope and enlarged heat dispersal vents. Pyre used the blaster rifle throughout 34 ABY. Aboard the refueling station Colossus on the planet Castilon, he utilized the weapon's stun setting while hunting for the orphans Eila and Kel from the planet Tehar. When the Colossus Resistance cell submerged the station and brought down the communications jamming, the commander carried the rifle to investigate the device on Doza Tower. He entered a blaster fight with Resistance members Kazuda Xiono and Jarek Yeager, grazing Xiono with a shot and arresting Yeager. The gold-armored stormtrooper utilized the blaster in the Battle of Castilon, once again exchanging fire with Xiono and Yeager atop Doza Tower. Pyre then fled the Colossus with his rifle aboard a shuttle.

Later in 34 ABY, Pyre discovered mechanic Neeku Vozo and Xiono infiltrating the First Order refueling station Titan. He fired at the Resistance infiltrators with his rifle in section 1305 and later in the Titan main hangar, where the duo, along with the droid CB-23, escaped aboard a stolen AAL-1971/9.1 Troop Transport. The commander re-encountered Xiono with his blaster in hand on the planet Varkana. Though Xiono quickly stunned him, he recovered and engaged Xiono and his cohorts again outside Vargo Spaceport. Pyre subsequently used the blaster during Team Colossus attempt to help former Colossus resident Tamara Ryvora defect from the First Order. He was knocked unconscious during the battle and then perished when the Thunderer was destroyed in the Barabesh system.

Pyre's blaster was a slightly improved, customized version of a standard F-11D blaster rifle. The two-handed weapon featured an electrum finish to match Pyre's gold-colored armor The blaster was equipped with an adjustable J20 electroscope for higher zoom and increased precision. Enlarged heat dispersal vents prevented the gun from overheating. Pyre's blaster was keyed to only function when paired with the gloves of his armor. and red-colored blaster bolts.

entities.name: Teroj's blaster
entities.description:
Teroj's blaster was a blaster pistol owned by the First Order operative Teroj Kee. In 34 ABY, he wielded the weapon on the supertanker fuel depot Colossus while stealing a phase connector mining device from the platform's Office of Acquisitions. At the Colossus loading docks, he threatened the mechanic Kazuda Xiono with the blaster before returning to the Office of Acquisitions and firing repeatedly at Xiono's droid, BB-8. Aboard his freighter, he fired several shots at the gorg Bitey after the creature sabotaged the vessel.

Teroj's blaster was a blaster pistol owned by the First Order operative Teroj Kee. The weapon could be wielded single- or double-handedly for use in ranged combat and fired red blaster bolts. Teroj's blaster featured a teal blue finish and gray and silver elements on its handle, barrel, and chamber. The blaster pistol also featured brown paneling on its grip, which was fastened by two screws, and red-and-yellow lights.

In 34 ABY, Kee kept the blaster in a holster on his hip while visiting the supertanker fuel depot Colossus. Posing as a member of the Mining Guild, he sought to steal a rare phase connector mining device from the platform's Office of Acquisitions while its owners, Flix and Orka, were away. Upon approaching the mechanic Kazuda Xiono, who was helping manage the store for Flix and Orka, Kee kept his hand on his blaster as he impatiently conversed with Xiono. Upon being informed that the Office of Acquisitions could not sell him its phase connector, he was bitten by the gorg Bitey, prompting him to remove his hand from his blaster. Angrily, Kee ordered several other items to be delivered to loading dock 23 in the Colossus loading docks and left.

When Xiono delivered the requested items to the loading dock, Kee confronted the mechanic at blaster-point and locked him in the dock's storage locker. With Xiono out of the way, Kee returned to the Office of Acquisitions and used a tool to cut through its door. Wielding his blaster, he entered the store, unaware that Xiono's astromech droid—BB-8—was still inside. When BB-8 shifted behind a crate, Kee swung in the droid's direction with his blaster, though he turned away after not seeing further movement. Kee then used his blaster to fry the store's back room door controls, finding his coveted phase connector. BB-8 attacked Kee as he left with the phase connector, prompting the latter to shoot at the droid with his blaster. Kee chased BB-8 through the Office of Acquisitions, firing off several shots, though not managing to hit the droid. However, Kee eventually managed to trap BB-8 beneath a shelf and left with his stolen prize, blaster re-holstered.

entities.name: Elrik Vonreg's RK-3 blaster
entities.description:
A customized red-accented RK-3 blaster was utilized by First Order Major Elrik Vonreg. The pistol was manufactured by Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc. and Sonn-Blas Corporation. In 34 ABY, after the First Order hired pirate Kragan Gorr and his Warbird gang to abduct the pilot Torra Doza, Vonreg employed the weapon to betray the pirates aboard their sail barge, the Galleon. The pilot shot the pirates Drell and Skreek during the blaster fight and retrieved Doza from her captors.

Major Elrik Vonreg's Imperial-era RK-3 blaster was customized and featured a red finish to match his crimson armor. The one-handed weapon featured white indicator lights at the back of the pistol to indicate the weapon's power levels. Vonreg's pistol had pinpoint precision and discharged red blaster bolts.

The blaster was manufactured by Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc. and Sonn-Blas Corporation and was utilized by the First Order Special Forces pilot Elrik Vonreg. the First Order secretly hired the pirate Kragan Gorr and his Warbird gang to abduct the pilot Torra Doza from the Colossus refueling station on the planet Castilon to entice Imanuel Doza—the station's captain and Torra's father—into hiring the First Order to protect the station from raids from the very same pirates. After the Warbirds successfully captured Torra, the pirate leader contacted Commander Pyre of the First Order to inform him of the mission's success. Pyre then arranged for Vonreg to deliver the pirates' payment to their sail barge, the Galleon.

When the major arrived and disembarked from a shuttle, he was welcomed by the pirates Drell, Skreek, and Valik with a captured Doza. Vonreg greeted Gorr before revealing his pistol and opening fire on the Warbirds. The major successfully shot Drell, knocking unconscious, and Skreek, knocking into the ocean of Castilon—though both survived the attack. Vonreg then escorted Doza to the shuttle while continuing to fire at Gorr's pirates. After leaving the skirmish, the shuttle returned to the Colossus station, where Vonreg returned Torra to her father.

entities.name: Eighth Brother's lightsaber
entities.description:
The Eighth Brother's lightsaber was a double-bladed spinning lightsaber wielded by the Jedi hunter known as the Eighth Brother, similar to other double-bladed spinning lightsabers wielded by Imperial Inquisitors, though it uniquely included a buzzsaw-like feature. It was destroyed by Kanan Jarrus on Malachor.

The weapon featured a ringed emitter, allowing the twin blades to rotate rapidly without effort from the wielder. For a Jedi hunter like an Inquisitor, this function likely served as a way to intimidate opponents, as well as deflect any form of frontal attack. However, this was also the weapon's primary weakness, as a lightsaber-wielding opponent could simply destroy the emitter itself and cut the weapon in half, as was demonstrated by Kanan Jarrus during his final duel with the Grand Inquisitor aboard the Sovereign.

It could also be used to fly, spinning in a helicopter-like motion strong enough to lift the wielder off the ground.

Additionally, the Eighth Brother's lightsaber was distinct among other double-bladed spinning lightsabers used by his fellow members of the Inquisitorius in that it had the unique ability to convert into a buzz-saw-like weapon that employed the handle while the blades were deactivated. This mechanism appears in place of the hinges on the emitter rails of other Inquisitors' lightsabers, disallowing the Eight Brother from folding the guard into a crescent shape.

entities.name: Eleventh Brother's lightsaber
entities.description:
A double-bladed spinning lightsaber was utilized by the Eleventh Brother during his time as an Inquisitor of the Galactic Empire. It was similar in appearance to other double-bladed spinning lightsabers wielded by Inquisitors.

The double-bladed spinning lightsaber was used by the Eleventh Brother, a member of the Galactic Empire's Inquisitorius. It could switch between crescent mode, for a single blade, or disk mode, for one or two blades and the ability to spin. The weapon had a cylindrical hilt with an emitter ring, forming a disc-hilt, with filigree near both emitters. It contained two kyber crystals that emitted red blades.

Sometime between 17 BBY and 13 BBY, the Eleventh Brother journeyed to the planet Janix to assist the First Brother in the hunt for the Zabrak Maul, a former Sith. The two Inquisitors traveled aboard an Imperial Low Altitude Assault Transport to locate Maul. Upon cutting the former Sith's path off on a facility bridge, the Eleventh Brother leaped from the transport, alongside comrade, with his lightsaber in hand. Maul ignited his lightsaber and charged the two Inquisitors, and the Eleventh Brother responded in kind with the ignition of both his blades. After the Inquisitors deflected Maul's strikes, the Zabrak jumped to a broken bridge below with the First Brother and Eleventh Brother following suit, while Maul's associates engaged in battle against Imperial Stormtroopers.

On the bridge Maul drove the Inquisitors back, forcing them to retreat to a nearby roof. The Eleventh Brother blocked Maul's attacks, after the Zabrak followed them. The masked Inquisitor went on the offensive, but Maul blocked his attacks as well and then pushed his hilt against the Inquisitor's, shoving him back. Maul retreated into a cave behind a waterfall, where the pair followed. As the Inquisitors searched for the Zabrak, the Eleventh Brother anticipated an attack from behind, whipping around and blocking Maul's strike. The two clashed blades, with Maul rolling to dodge one of the Eleventh Brother's swings, before eventually the Zabrak Force pushed the Inquisitor away, with the First Brother taking his place in the duel.

entities.name: Fifth Brother's lightsaber
entities.description:
The Fifth Brother's lightsaber was a double-bladed spinning lightsaber wielded by the Jedi hunter known as Fifth Brother, similar to other double-bladed spinning lightsabers wielded by Imperial Inquisitors.

The weapon featured a ringed emitter which could partially detach from the cylindrical handgrip in the center, allowing the twin blades to rotate rapidly without effort from the wielder. For a Jedi hunter like an Inquisitor, this function likely served as a way to intimidate opponents, as well as deflect any form of frontal attack. However, this was also the weapon's primary weakness, as a lightsaber-wielding opponent could simply destroy the emitter itself and cut the weapon in half, as was demonstrated by Kanan Jarrus during his final duel with the Grand Inquisitor aboard the Sovereign.

It could also be used to fly, spinning in a helicopter-like motion strong enough to lift the wielder off the ground.

The Fifth Brother was trained in the use of this lightsaber alongside his fellow Inquisitors in The Works on Coruscant under the tutelage of the Grand Inquisitor.

entities.name: Fourth Sister's double-bladed spinning lightsaber
entities.description:
The double-bladed spinning lightsaber was wielded by the Inquisitor known as the Fourth Sister. It was similar in appearance to the double-bladed spinning lightsabers wielded by other Imperial Inquisitors. She utilized the lightsaber during her mission to capture Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, on Daiyu. The lightsaber was abandoned in a cave.

When Lina Graf, a commander within the Alliance to Restore the Republic, infiltrated Fortress Vader on Mustafar wearing the Fourth Sister's stolen armor, the attendant Vaneé eventually realized that Graf was, indeed, not the Inquisitor because she lacked her lightsaber.

The lightsaber was a double-bladed spinning lightsaber owned by the Fourth Sister, a Nogratu member of the Galactic Empire's Inquisitorius. The saber possessed a cylindrical hilt with an emitter ring, forming its disc-hilt. The ring featured a notch with a dull spike in the middle near the ring's blade emitters. The notches were opposite to each other.

In 19 BBY, the Fourth Sister carried the lightsaber on her back in crescent mode within a partially constructed Fortress Inquisitorius, the headquarters of the Inquisitors. There, she walked through through a hallway into the fortress's audience chamber after being welcomed in by the Grand Inquisitor, the leader of the Inquisitors. Inside the audience chamber, along with fellow Inquisitors the First Brother, Eleventh Brother, and Barriss Offee, she met the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader, the Inquisitors' new Master.

entities.name: The Grand Inquisitor's lightsaber
entities.description:
The Grand Inquisitor's lightsaber was the personal double-bladed spinning lightsaber of the Jedi hunter known as the Grand Inquisitor, similar to those wielded by the other Imperial Inquisitors.

The weapon featured a ringed emitter which could partially detach from the cylindrical handgrip in the center, allowing the twin blades to rotate rapidly without effort from the wielder. For a Jedi hunter like the Inquisitor, this function likely served as a way to intimidate, or frighten opponents, as well as deflect any form of direct attack. On some occasion this function is known to catch opponents off balance. However, this was also the weapon's primary weakness, as a lightsaber-wielding opponent could simply permanently separate the emitter itself and sever the weapon in half, as was demonstrated by Lord Vader during his first duel with the Inquisitor and Kanan Jarrus during his final duel with the Inquisitor aboard the Sovereign. This is due to the hilt consisting of non-lightsaber resistant alloy or metal. The handgrip could be removed entirely from the ring-shaped emitter, allowing the Force-imbued circlet of metal to be used as a throwing disc.

The Grand Inquisitor wielded his lightsaber against Darth Sidious's new apprentice, the Sith Lord Darth Vader. During their fight, Vader was able to damage the Inquisitor's lightsaber. though at one point he utilized another lightsaber which was broken when he fought against Naq Med.

The Grand Inquisitor wielded his lightsaber in several battles against Kanan Jarrus and Ezra Bridger. It was also used to execute Imperial officers Cumberlayne Aresko and Myles Grint both at once on Moff Tarkin's orders, after their repeated incompetence in capturing the rebels. In a final battle against the Inquisitor, after his rescue, Jarrus split the Inquisitor's weapon in two, causing the pieces to fall down a shaft. The two halves fell into the Sovereign reactor and ruptured it, causing a chain reaction of explosions that destroyed the pieces, killed the Inquisitor when he chose to fall into the blasts, and eventually obliterated the entire Sovereign.

entities.name: Marrok's lightsaber
entities.description:
Marrok's lightsaber was the red double-bladed spinning lightsaber owned by the Inquisitor Marrok, once known as the First Brother. Marrok continued to use the lightsaber after becoming a mercenary by 9 ABY. The saber was capable of switching between crescent mode, single-bladed, and disk mode double-bladed. While not in use, Marrok hooked the lightsaber on the upper back of his armor. Marrok used the lightsaber against Jedi Ahsoka Tano on the Core Worlds planet Corellia and for the final time on the planet Seatos, where the former Inquisitor fell to Tano in battle.

In 19 BBY, the First Brother, a member of the Galactic Empire's Inquisitorius, carried the saber on his back, partially under his cloak, within Fortress Inquisitorius, Darth Vader, master of the Inquisitorius.

Marrok made use of his lightsaber during his hunt for Maul. Fighting off Eeko-Dio Daki and Devon Izara in Brender Lawson's home. Devon left Daki at Daki's order to assist Brender and his son, Rylee, in escaping the house. Marrok's lightsaber eventually lit the house on fire after a strike hit a wall causing it spark. Marrok came close to defeating Daki, though Daki dropped a light down on Marrok and escaped, following Devon and the Lawson's route to the roof of the home. Once Devon stole one of the TK trooper's ships, Marrok reappeared with his lightsaber and continued to duel Daki, though Devon opened fire with the ships weapons on Marrok. Marrok attempted to block the bolts to little success, which allowed Daki time to board and for Devon, Daki and the Lawson's to escape.

Despite that, Marrok continued his pursuit and found Devon and Rylee, split off from Daki and Brander, at a train station. Marrok and Devon clashed blades at the station platform and the duel soon moved onto a train. Passing a station, Maul got onto the train and revealed himself once Marrok asked where Maul was. Marrok handled both Devon and Maul, eventually kicking Devon away and igniting his second blade when Maul grabbed his arm, beginning the spin the blades. Maul ignited his own second blade and the two continued to duel until Maul threw his lightsaber, causing Marrok to leap back onto another flatbed, where Devon cut the coupling connecting Marrok's flatbed to Maul, Devon and Rylee's with her lightsaber, leaving Marrok stranded in the tunnel.

entities.name: Ninth Sister's lightsaber
entities.description:
The Ninth Sister utilized a double-bladed spinning lightsaber during her time as an Inquisitor of the Galactic Empire.

The Ninth Sister originally utilized a similar design to the Grand Inquisitor's lightsaber, the only difference being a spike was present on each side of the wheel. It was briefly used by Darth Vader during a skirmish on Cabarria after his weapon was destroyed by the Chas, a family of bounty hunters.

At some point in between 18 BBY and 14 BBY, the Ninth Sister replaced her original lightsaber with one that had a more robust hilt, a wider emitter and a thicker wheel. She wielded the blade during the hunt for surviving Padawan-turned-Jedi Knight Cal Kestis and the hunt for surviving Jedi Knight Tensu Run. In her final moments in 9 BBY, the Ninth Sister used her lightsaber to stab Utapau Senator Daho Sejan, believing he helped Kestis, later killing Klatooinian twins Koob and Lizz. During their final duel, Cal managed to wound Ninth Sister by slashing her chest before decapitating her, leaving her lightsaber by her corpse.

The Ninth Sister's lightsaber design in the video game was based on the idea of a heavy axe, having also been inspired by its initial comic appearance.

entities.name: Reva's lightsaber
entities.description:
Reva's lightsaber also known as Reva's double-bladed Inquisitor Lightsaber, and the Third Sister's lightsaber, was a lightsaber wielded by the Jedi hunter known as the Third Sister, also known as Reva, during her service to the Galactic Empire. It was similar in appearance to other double-bladed spinning lightsabers wielded by Imperial Inquisitors. As the hunt for Obi-Wan Kenobi came to an end, Reva would lay down her lightsaber, seeking to turn her back on the dark side of the Force.

While many Inquisitors carried their lightsabers on their backs, the Third Sister kept hers hang on her right side. The saber was able to be split into two separate blades with the ringed emitter retracting at the sides so the hilt can extend and split apart. This allowed Reva to utilize her Jar'Kai skills, which she perfected under the Grand Inquisitor's tutelage. The saber's kyber crystals once belonged to Jedi who were killed during the Great Jedi Purge and were bled by Reva herself.

In 9 BBY, the Third Sister utilized the lightsaber during the Inquisitors' pursuit of the Jedi Nari, which led them to a saloon in Mos Eisley on the planet Tatooine. When Nari attempted to escape, the Third Sister drew her lightsaber and struck at him, but the Grand Inquisitor used the Force to stop her blade, leaving only Nari's left shoulder injured. As Nari fled the scene, the Grand Inquisitor chastised the Third Sister for her recklessness to kill a Jedi he had planned to interrogate. As the Inquisitors searched for information on the Jedi's whereabouts, the Third Sister threatened to cut off the hands of those who would not speak, making example of a woman who claimed that the Galactic Empire had no authority over the Outer Rim Territories. The Third Sister then turned her attention to moisture farmer Owen Lars and threatened him with her lightsaber, but the Fifth Brother ordered her to stand down.

Later, the Third Sister would brandish her lightsaber on the planet Daiyu, where she had kidnapped Princess Leia Organa in order to lure Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi out of hiding. As she cornered Kenobi in a shipyard, the Third Sister was stopped by the Grand Inquisitor, who ordered her aside to avoid her losing their quarry. The Third Sister instead used her lightsaber to stab the Grand Inquisitor in the abdomen. Although Kenobi escaped with Organa, the Third Sister was able to capture the young princess on Mapuzo, bringing her to Fortress Inquisitorius on the moon Nur. She would then use her lightsaber to defend against an attack on the fortress, deflecting cannon fire from two T-47 airspeeders flown by members of the Hidden Path.

entities.name: S-Mine Detonator
entities.description:
S-Mine Detonators, or Photon Grenades, were detonators used by the Eighth Brother, an Imperial Inquisitor. He was equipped with the small detonators on multiple occasions, including early in the Imperial Era and on a search for the former Sith Lord Maul on the planet Malachor in 3 BBY. When the Eighth Brother encountered the Jedi Kanan Jarrus, his apprentice Ezra Bridger, and the former Jedi Ahsoka Tano on Malachor, the outnumbered Inquisitor threw three S-Mine Detonators at them, allowing himself to retreat.

S-Mine Detonators, also known as Photon Grenades, were small, disk-shaped explosives carried by the Imperial Inquisitor Eighth Brother. Gray and black in color, the detonators could be attached to a belt for easy access. The Eighth Brother typically carried several of them at once. The detonators glowed red when armed, and upon detonation, they exploded into various colors.

In 19 BBY, the Eighth Brother wore the detonators on Coruscant. in 14 BBY. In 3 BBY, the Eighth Brother brought several S-Mine Detonators to the planet Malachor as he tracked down the former Sith Lord Maul. When the Eighth Brother came across the Jedi Kanan Jarrus, his apprentice Ezra Bridger, and the former Jedi Ahsoka Tano, he hurled three S-Mine Detonators at the trio as they charged forward. The explosions collapsed the ground below Bridger, causing him to fall through and providing the outnumbered Inquisitor an opportunity to flee.

The Sith Lord Darth Sidious later depicted S-Mine Detonators in a visualization of the Inquisitors, including the Eighth Brother, in The Secrets of the Sith, a book that he wrote before his death during the Battle of Exegol in 35 ABY.

entities.name: Second Sister's lightsaber
entities.description:
A double-bladed spinning lightsaber was utilized by the Second Sister during her time as a member of the Inquisitorius.

After Trilla Suduri was captured by the Galactic Empire and turned to the dark side of the Force, Suduri became known as the Second Sister and used the lightsaber as her primary weapon. She used it to hunt down Padawan Cal Kestis during the Great Jedi Purge. During their third duel on Bogano, Kestis disarmed Suduri, grabbed the lightsaber, and was forced to relive Suduri's capture and conscription into the Inquisitorius through his psychometry, allowing her to steal a Jedi holocron and escape. Kestis gave the saber to his master, Cere Junda, the Second Sister's former Master, who knighted him with it. Junda used the lightsaber as her primary weapon during the Mission to Nur. By the time Kestis faced the Second Sister in their fourth and final duel at Fortress Inquisitorius, she had replaced this lightsaber with a new one.

The Second Sister's lightsaber design had a particular circular visual design that was based on the idea of fencing and elegance.

The inscription on the wheel of the Second Sister's lightsaber reads "MASDFGHJKLQWERTYUIOPZXCVBNMAASDFGHJKLQWERTYIONMASDFGHJKLQWERTYIOPZXCVBNMASDFGHJKLQWERTYUIOPZ" in Aurebesh.

entities.name: Seventh Sister's lightsaber
entities.description:
The Seventh Sister wielded a double-bladed spinning lightsaber during her career as a Jedi hunter. It is similar to other double-bladed spinning lightsabers wielded by Imperial Inquisitors.

The weapon featured a ringed emitter which could partially detach from the remaining hilt, allowing both blades to rotate rapidly without effort from the wielder. For a Jedi hunter like an Inquisitor, this function likely served as a way to intimidate opponents, as well as deflect any form of direct attack. However, this was also the weapon's primary weakness, as a lightsaber-wielding opponent could simply separate the emitter itself and cut the weapon in half, as was demonstrated by Kanan Jarrus during his final duel with the Grand Inquisitor aboard the Sovereign.

The handgrip could be removed entirely from the ring-shaped emitter, allowing the Force-imbued circlet of metal to be used as a throwing disc.

It could also be used to fly, spinning in a helicopter-like motion strong enough to lift the wielder off the ground.

entities.name: Sixth Brother's lightsaber
entities.description:
The Sixth Brother's lightsaber was utilized during his time as an Inquisitor of the Galactic Empire. The weapon would be destroyed slightly over a year after the formation of the Empire on the Outer Rim moon Raada, causing the Sixth Brother's death, when the Inquisitor fought the former Jedi Padawan Ahsoka Tano. Tano claimed the kyber crystals from the Sixth Brother's lightsaber for use in her own newly-constructed pair of lightsabers, after purifying them of the taint of the dark side.

The Sixth Brother's lightsaber design was based on that of the Grand Inquisitor's. It seemed to have some differences, such as the absence of the two spikes around the emitter. However, it did have protrusions around the handle guard during crescent and disc mode.

One feature that set it apart from other Inquisitor lightsabers was that this one had the capability of being a split saber, being able to disconnect the hilt so the user was able to use two lightsabers instead of one.

The weapon was powered by two kyber crystals, forcibly attuned to the dark side of the Force through the process known as bleeding. Ahsoka Tano believed that the crystals had been looted from the Jedi Temple following the Great Jedi Purge.

entities.name: Tenth Brother's shoto lightsabers
entities.description:
The Tenth Brother's shoto lightsabers were two shoto lightsabers used by the Tenth Brother, an Inquisitor in the Galactic Empire's Jedi-hunting organization, the Inquisitorius. Previously using a green-bladed lightsaber during his time as a Jedi in 22 BBY, he wielded the shoto lightsabers as an Inquisitor in 18 BBY during a mission to the planet Mon Cala, where he met his end. The lightsabers featured a handguard and produced red-colored blades from their kyber crystals.

The Tenth Brother's shoto lightsabers were two shoto lightsabers owned by the Tenth Brother, a member of the Galactic Empire's Inquisitorius—an organization responsible for hunting Jedi. Both hilts contained a kyber crystal, which produced short, red-colored blades. The black cylindrical hilts featured a gray handguard that ran from the top to the pommel. When not being used, the Tenth Brother carried the lightsabers on either hip. In combat, he wielded the sabers in a reverse grip.

Previously using a green-bladed lightsaber when he was a Jedi the Tenth Brother utilized two shoto lightsabers in The Inquisitor brought the lightsabers with him when he joined fellow Inquisitors Sixth Brother and Ninth Sister, Darth Vader, and a group of Purge Troopers on the planet Mon Cala to investigate the presence of a Jedi. Shortly after they arrived in Dac City on Mon Cala, a shuttle carrying the Imperial diplomat Telvar exploded,

The Inquisitor returned the lightsabers to his hips as he followed Vader towards a nearby palace to interrogate the King of Mon Cala, Lee-Char, on the location of the Jedi. The Tenth Brother cut down Mon Cala's military personnel as the group advanced into the palace, while Ferren Barr, the Jedi in question, reviewed their progress on a datapad. After confronting the King, the Ninth Sister attempted to extract the location of Barr from Lee-Char. but before she could share the information, giant waves crashed across Mon Cala's surface, an attempt by the king to repel the Imperial invaders. With his lightsabers holstered, the Tenth Brother attempted to hold back the water with help from the other Inquisitors and Vader by creating a Force barrier, though they ultimately failed. The Tenth Brother kept his lightsabers on his person while the Inquisitors acquired an Imperial submarine and rescued Vader from the Great Ungeness Trench.

entities.name: Tualon Yaluna's double-bladed spinning lightsaber
entities.description:
A double-bladed spinning lightsaber was utilized by Tualon Yaluna during his time as a member of the Inquisitorius.

The weapon featured a ringed emitter which could partially detach from the remaining hilt, allowing both blades to rotate rapidly without effort from the wielder. For a Jedi hunter like an Inquisitor, this function likely served as a way to intimidate opponents, as well as deflect any form of direct attack. However, this was also the weapon's primary weakness, as a lightsaber-wielding opponent could simply separate the emitter itself and cut the weapon in half, as was demonstrated by Kanan Jarrus during his final duel with the Grand Inquisitor aboard the Sovereign.

After the Jedi Knight Tualon Yaluna was captured by the newly formed Galactic Empire and turned to the dark side of the Force, he was given a new lightsaber, which he used during training duels with fellow Inquisitor Iskat Akaris and their master, the Sith Lord Darth Vader. During his time as an Inquisitor, Yaluna carried the weapon during a number of assignments, including a mission to Firrhana and the hunt for Eeth Koth. His last use of the lightsaber was in combat against Darth Vader, who eventually used the Force to kill Yaluna with the weapon.

Giuseppe Camuncoli's concept art for Yaluna's Inquisitor lightsaber was initially in the form of standard split saber, but soon took the form of the double-bladed spinning lightsaber typically used by Inquisitors, as seen in its official depictions.

entities.name: CryoBan cell
entities.description:
CryoBan cells were cells made using CryoBan technology. A number of CryoBan cells were smuggled onto the planet Alderaan by a smuggling ring during the Cold War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. On Alderaan the cells were illegal, but were used by troops loyal to the House of Thul, one of the Great Houses of Alderaan, during the Alderaan Civil War. House Thul used the cells in it's fight against he rival House of Organa, who had Republic backing. A private in the Republic Army named Aza Gundo, however became aware of the smuggling ring bringing in the CryoBan goods due to criminal connections he had and the ring was shut down. The Thul troops already had large amounts of CryoBan cells and CryoBan rifles to hand though which had been previously delivered, and continued to use them.

Several days after the ring was shut down, Aza Gundo asked a Republic aligned individual to find and destroy the remaining CryoBan rifles. The individual traveled to the Organa Vinerium where they successfully destroyed the weapons carried by Thul troops, but also took it upon themselves to claim thirty CryoBan cells from Thul storage lockers where they were being kept. The individual then used these cells to sabotage dropships used by the House of Thul, which they did by throwing the cells into the engine of the ship.

CryoBan cells first appeared in 2011 in Star Wars: The Old Republic an MMOPRG released by BioWare. They appeared in the Republic bonus mission "Revenge Served Cold" which was part of the "Frozen Assets" quest.

entities.description:
Holsters were accessories used to carry weapons, typically blaster pistols.

Holsters first appeared in the 1977 film Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope, the first installment of the Star Wars original trilogy.

In the Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi television series, the propmakers were assigned with designing a holster that could fit young Leia Organa and the adult Tala Durith. Propmaster Brad Elliott found this to be challenging because of the actors' height differences and it had to hold Lola, Organa's droid, and Durith's SE-14r blaster. Durith's holster was designed as a drop holster. For Organa, the team took the drop portion off of the gun belt and it fit her perfectly. To fill the space needed to accommodate Lola, a Han Solo-style scope was added to Durith's blaster.

entities.name: Shockstun mist
entities.description:
Shockstun mist was a chemical used by bounty hunters to help immobilize targets that needed to be taken alive. Capable of quickly numbing and paralyzing exposed skin, shockstun mist was most effective when inhaled; resulting in paralysis that could last for hours. The chemical was best known for being introduced in the GRS-1 snare rifle, which had the ability to fire shockstun mist to a distance of about 150 meters. Immediately following the mist was a liquid spraynet which hardened after exposure to the air and helped restrict all movement of the paralyzed target.

A shockstun mist canister for the GRS-1 cost 75 credits and could fire up to twelve shots before the cartridge must be replaced.

entities.name: Accu-accelerator
entities.description:
An accu-accelerator was a component used in blasters, engines, and speeders. Accu-accelerators were used in starship ion engines. Some were scrounged by Jawa scavengers to construct their ion blasters; the components, along with a droid restraining bolt, were added to the blaster's firing mechanism. The accelerators were also used in Moll K-19T power generators.

Accu-accelerators were first mentioned in the canon continuity in the 2015 Dorling Kindersley reference book Ultimate Star Wars. They later appeared as upgrade materials in the 2024 video game Star Wars Outlaws developed by Massive Entertainment and published by Ubisoft.

Accu-accelerators were first mentioned in Star Wars Legends continuity in the 1991 roleplaying supplement, Cracken's Rebel Field Guide.

entities.name: Actuating diffuser module
entities.description:
An actuating diffuser module was an blaster component that destabilized energy particles, causing blaster bolts to explode on impact. it was illegal to own a diffuser module in the Galactic Empire. However, Rodian scavenger Namda Eaakee came into possession of one of the modules.

In 3 ABY, the scoundrel Kay Vess traded with Eaakee for the module in exchange for ten direct-energy circuits. She later used it to the modify her VM-19 heavy blaster pistol's plasma module.

Actuating diffuser modules appeared as an upgrade item in the 2024 video game, Star Wars Outlaws, developed by Massive Entertainment and published by Ubisoft. The player must obtain the trigger in order upgrade their blaser's heavy plasma module to level four.

entities.description:
An actuating module was a modification that could be added to a blaster for 500 credits. Mercenaries, bounty hunters, and others used the modules because it provided extra power to a weapon, although it also increased the weapon's recoil.

In 3 ABY the scoundrel Kay Vess used actuating modules to modify the firing rate and power of her VM-19 heavy blaster pistol.

Actuating modules were first mentioned in the canon continuity in Special Modifications, a roleplaying supplementary sourcebook published by Fantasy Flight Games in 2016. They first appeared as blaster upgrade components in the 2024 Massive Entertainment video game Star Wars Outlaws.

The modules first appeared in the Star Wars Legends continuity in Rescue at Glare Peak, a roleplaying adventure module for Star Wars: Age of Rebellion published by Fantasy Flight Games in 2014.

entities.name: Amplification crystal
entities.description:
Amplification crystals were a type of crystal used in the construction of the superlaser. The superlaser was powered by a massive reactor at the core of the Death Star, which used the amplification crystals to generate eight individual beams of turbolaser pulses that converged over the central focus lens.

Eight amplification crystals were used for the superlaser aboard the DS-1 Orbital Battle Station, and each crystal required a separate gunnery station to calibrate and modulate the pulses. Fourteen gunners manned each individual station, with an additional four additional amplification crystals held in reserve.

The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology

entities.name: Augmented vibro-motor
entities.description:
Augmented vibro-motors were an attachment used to modify vibro-weapons. Modifying vibro weapons with augmented vibro-motors could make the weapon more powerful, capable of cutting through armored plating with ease. However, this augmentation also resulted in the weapon being more difficult to handle. Augmented vibro-motors cost 500 credits.

Vibro-motors that were installed alongside a gene-lock—which kept weapons from activating without their owner's use by reading DNA—would be disabled. They could also be utilized in tandem with an "Accu-Strike" integrated targeting computer in order to improve a user's accuracy. Usage of vibro-motors with the targeting computers involved installing them into the gauntlets or gloves of the user, then connecting them to the helmet system of the armor.

Augmented vibro-motors were introduced in Rise of the Separatists, a 2019 supplement to Fantasy Flight Games' series of Star Wars Roleplaying products.

entities.name: Blaster module
entities.description:
Blaster modules also referred to as blaster cartridges were a type of blaster component that could be quickly swapped in order to alter the firing mode of a blaster pistol. The thief Kay Vess used a light plasma module for her VM-19 heavy blaster pistol during the reign of the Galactic Empire Vess constructed additional modules including an ion module configured for burst firing and a power module configured for firing a single bolt while preparing for a heist on the casino planet Cantonica. Following the heist, the pirate Hondo Ohnaka gave Vess a power regulator which she used to construct another ion module that was configured to discharge a powerful shockwave when its ion bolt impacted a target.

During the same year, Vess constructed five other blaster modules for her heavy blaster pistol. These included two more plasma modules, one configured to fire rapidly and the other which fired heavy bolts at a slower rate, one additional ion module who's ion bolts surged on impact, and two additional power modules, the first caused its bolts to detonate on impact and the second which dealt more damage the longer it was charged.

Several types of blaster modules appeared in the 2024 video game Star Wars Outlaws which was developed by Massive Entertainment and published by Ubisoft. The components were first identified as both "blaster modules and blaster cartridges" in the digital art book Star Wars Outlaws: Visual Guide,

As part of the game's main quests player is required to construct the burst ion module as part of the "New Tricks" mission and later must construct the bolt power module after completing the first of either "The Heavy", "The Safecracker" or "The Droidsmith" quests. Players will unlock the key parts in order to construct the other modules by completing main quests but they are not required to actually construct these to complete the game's story. The player receives the shock ion module as part of the main quest of the "A Pirate's Fortune" story expansion for the game.

entities.name: Capacitor
entities.description:
A capacitor was a device used in the galaxy to store energy. Capacitors were used in a variety of machines, including weapons, starships, and even droids.

The scientist Galen Walton Erso hoped to generate outbursts of raw power that could be harvested and stored in capacitors for use on worlds in need. Capacitors were also used in droids like B1-series battle droids. In these models of battle droids their capacitors were a weak point, and clone snipers could hit between the droid's capacitors to take out the unit. The ends of electrostaffs contained a discharge capacitor. Shortly after the rise of the Galactic Empire, the Bad Batch had their ship's capacitor stolen by an Ordo Moon Dragon.

In 3 ABY, ND-5 gave a power capacitor to Kay Vess after she recovered a stolen artifact for the Ashiga Clan from their rivals Crimson Dawn. Vess used the capacitor to create a powerful blaster module for her VM-19 heavy blaster pistol.

Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition

entities.name: Code breaker chip
entities.description:
A code breaker chip was a computer chip designed to bypass algorithmic security processes. it was illegal to own the chip in the Galactic Empire.

In 3 ABY, the scoundrel Kay Vess learned that the Starfallers pirate gang had stored one of the chips at their workshop in the Southern Falls region of Toshara, a moon of Toshaal in the Outer Rim Territories. She later visited the workshop and stole the chip and used it to upgrade her slicing unit.

Code breaker chip appeared as an upgrade item in the 2024 video game, Star Wars Outlaws, developed by Massive Entertainment and published by Ubisoft. The item was used to unlock "the slicer" expert upgrade which increased the amount of energy of the slicer kit.

entities.name: Energy envelope projector
entities.description:
An energy envelope projector was a specialized energy shield generator that was installed on proton torpedos and concussion missiles. The projectors encased the projectiles in an energy shroud during flight.

Projectiles such as the Krupx Munitions MG7-A proton torpedo and the Arakyd Industries ST2 concussion missile had multiple energy envelope projectors. When launched, the projectiles were sheathed in a protective energy shroud by the projectors. This weak energy shield protected the projectile from being prematurely detonated by collisions with space debris or near misses from laser cannons.

The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology

The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels

entities.name: Energy overclock setting
entities.description: An energy overclock setting was a type of precision analog system that, when applied, increased the lethality of vibro weapons. By replacing several internal components with such systems, a technician could increase both the speed and frequency of a vibro weapon's blade action, and as a result, a vibro weapon could be charged for amplified cutting power, but at the expense of unpredictable power fluctuations. While there was little fear of the weapon falling apart, power fluctuations could cause the weapon's internal electronics to break down or disconnect during use, which rendered it useless until repaired.

entities.name: Adiabatic shield
entities.description:
Adiabatic shield was a Force power. The user manipulated the air around them to function as a shield of sorts. While this shield did not protect the user from blaster fire or impact with solid objects, it could disperse gases and airborne chemicals that could affect the user. A user could use this power to disperse smoke, poisonous vapors like chlorine, or more subtle chemicals like airborne pheromones.

Jax Pavan and Laranth Tarak used this to disperse the pheromones Dejah Duare released in an attempt to secure their services.

entities.name: Alchemy
entities.description:
Alchemy was a Force technique practiced by alchemists. It concentrated the Force into a physical form. Unlike the Jedi, the Nightsisters used alchemy, along with magick, to consolidate and collect power. The Nightsisters use an ancient creature known as the Sleeper to create the Water of Life, a form of healing alchemy. Among the Sith, there were Sith alchemists which utilized Sith alchemy to create of amazing feats of metallurgy and biology.

Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

entities.name: Alchemy of flesh
entities.description: The alchemy of flesh was a Je'daii form of alchemy practiced at Anil Kesh, the Temple of Science. The Je'daii Ranger Lanoree Brock studied the practice in her spare time under the guidance of Master Dam-Powl. In a compartment of her Peacemaker starship, Brock was working on crafting a living being from cells. Checking on it, she noticed that blood dribbled from forming veins, vestigial limbs flapped around and it had milky eyes. Brock had created it from her own flesh. In the early stages, it had no mind and Lanoree wondered if it could feel pain.

entities.name: Ayna-seff
entities.description:
Ayna-seff or Dead–brain in Basic was a Force technique in the hassat-durr family taught by the Baran Do sages on Dorin. Like other techniques of the family, ayna-seff suffused the user's body with a low level of electromagnetic radiation. The radiation was produced as an interaction between the Force and ones own mental influence over their nervous system.

Ayna–seff made the user's brain activity undetectable. It could also be used to disabled the user's own prosthetics or electronic implants. It could also interfere with shock shackles and could provide a range–boost for com–links. It was also capable of changing how animals senses percieved the user.

To learn it, a small, two-piece device was used: a durasteel sphere and a charged plate. Attuned to the precise intensities and frequencies of the technique's energy output, the goal was to raise the ball in the air and keep it steady.

It was recommended that a user perfect the technique entirely before using it in the field as the electromagnetic radiation produced by a student early in their training was a magnet for lightning. If not perfected the user would be struck by lightning repellent and killed.

entities.name: Beam of light
entities.description:
Some Jedi, commonly members of the Neti species, were capable of releasing an incredible beam of light as they channeled the sum of the Force energy of the planet on which they were rooted or other large energy source at their moment of death. Such power was capable of catastrophic planetary surface destruction, as well as the obliteration of starships and other vessels. In 10 ABY, to save Jedi Knights Luke Skywalker and Kam Solusar, the ancient Jedi Master Ood Bnar released a devastating beam of light to annihilate Executor Sedriss.

More than one hundred years later, when Emperor Krayt's forces were triumphant in their assault, a female Neti Master named T'ra Saa was joined by fellow Jedi Nat Skywalker, and together unleashed a beam of light to clear an escape route for their allies using the direct energy of the Temple's detonating reactor.

Following the deaths of both Bnar and Saa, tiny saplings burst from the ground where the original Neti died, seemingly imbued with the planet's Force energy, still traveling through the engrained roots.

entities.name: Force call
entities.description:
Force call was a powerful Force technique utilized by only a few Force-sensitives, due to the amount of energy required to use this power.

Utilizing the Force, a Jedi could call other Jedi to his or her position; this amounted to a shout that echoed throughout the Force itself. For those who heard this summons, it would be nearly impossible to resist. Raynar Thul used this to summon the survivors of the Myrkr strike team at the beginning of the Dark Nest Crisis, while Luke Skywalker used this technique on Ossus for a Convocation of the New Jedi Order shortly before the end of the war.

entities.name: Cleanse
entities.description: This was an application of the Force performed by Jaden Korr in 41.5 ABY. After taking the defeated Kam Solusar clone Alpha's unstable red lightsaber, Jaden decided to make it his own. Reluctant to use a red crystal, and not wanting an inadequate blade, Korr removed the crystal and cleansed it of all impurities, fixing the blade and changing the color from red to yellow. Jaden was especially pleased with the color change, due to the fact that a yellow blade was traditionally associated with Jedi Sentinels, who balanced Force powers with lightsaber combat; something that fit Jaden's style just perfectly. When showing his success to Marr Idi-Shael and Khedryn Faal, they were completely amazed, Faal even asking him why Jaden couldn't purge the Community clones of imperfections, just like he did with the crystal. Korr explained that people were far to complex to change with this power.

entities.name: Cry of the Broken King
entities.description:
The Cry of the Broken King was a Force power. the murder of the Sarravi V'Kara the Sephi thief Tey Sirrek was spotted standing next to the Sarravi's corpse by the Kiffar Vildar Mac, who had chased Sirrek after seeing him steal from a Bpfasshi Truthsayer. Thinking Sirrek had killed V'Kara, Mac confronted him, attempting to strike him down with his lightsaber. After Sirrek managed to dodge all of Mac's stikes, the annoyed Jedi asked how he was doing so.

Sirrek then claimed to have mastered many Force powers, including the Cry of the Broken King, Vitali and Morichro. Mac dismissed that as nonsense, stating that Morichro was nothing more than a myth. The Sephi then used biological pheromones his ancestors had developed for usage against predators to temporarily knock out Mac, while claiming that he was using Morichro on the Jedi.

The Cry of the Broken King was mentioned in the first issue of the 2022 comic series Star Wars: The High Republic published as part of the Star Wars: The High Republic multimedia project's The issue was written by Cavan Scott, and published by Marvel Comics on October 12, 2022.

entities.name: Force Dash
entities.description:
Force Dash, or speed burst was an ability of the Force that allowed its user to increase their speed for a brief time. While powerful in short bursts, overexertion of the ability could quickly drain the Force-user of their energy for a brief period of time.

While aboard the Trade Federation starship Saak'ak, Jedi Master Qui-Gon Jinn and his Padawan Obi-Wan Kenobi used Force Dash to escape from droidekas. and later to slice through Boba Fett’s blaster carbine with his lightsaber.

entities.name: Endure
entities.description:
Endure was a Jedi Force power used to endure physical pain. During the Battle of Nar Shaddaa, Jedi Master Crucitorn used the technique to mitigate the pain of being immolated. Jedi Master Lene Kostana taught the technique to the Jedi Dooku at some point between 102 BBY and 68 BBY, and he later passed on this knowledge to his two Padawans: first Rael Averross, and later Qui-Gon Jinn.

Endure was a Force power used by several Jedi to endure physical pain. Masters of the ability could resist otherwise-deadly injuries and pain. It was also possible to use Endure to make others resist pain.

Jedi Master Crucitorn endured the pain of being immolated during the Battle of Nar Shaddaa between the Jedi Order and the Flame-Wielders through the Force. Jedi Master Lene Kostana taught the technique to fellow Jedi Dooku. Dooku taught it to his two Padawans: Rael Averross, and, after taking him on in 68 BBY, Qui-Gon Jinn. To show the technique to Jinn, Dooku placed a metal band that the Heltraxi used as a torture device on his own chest.

Dooku later told his sister, Jenza, about his conversation with Jinn in a holo-letter. Dooku gave several data disks containing his messages to Jenza to his recently recruited Sith assassin—Asajj Ventress—for her investigation into his sister's location, and she listened to the holo-disk that mentioned Endure.

entities.name: Force familiar
entities.description:
A Force familiar was an animal that could share a bond with its owner in the Force. Vjun fox Miss Vix was a Force familiar for Viscountess Whirry Malreaux on the Force-steeped Outer Rim world of Vjun on which the connection with a familiar was considered an art. She stayed close to her mistress, often following her around Château Malreaux, and died along with the Countess following Dooku's occupation of the Château during the Clone Wars.

The concept of a Force familiar made its first appearance in the 2004 novel Yoda: Dark Rendezvous by Sean Stewart.

entities.name: Farsight
entities.description:
Farsight (also called clairvoyance, far sight, or farseeing) was a Force ability that allowed the user to "see" their targets or any event happening without actually needing their eyes, enhancing the bearer's visual and spatial perception even in the dark or behind walls. Users could then acquire information using sight outside the normal range of detection about an object, person, location, or physical event.

Farsight, also known as clairvoyance, far sight, or farseeing, a power of the Force that allowed the user to "see" their targets or any event happening without actually needing their eyes, enhancing the bearer's visual and spatial perception even in the dark or behind walls. Users could then acquire information using sight outside the normal range of detection about an object, person, location, or physical event.

In 132 BBY, the Jedi Order taught its students to use this power as part of their training. The Sith Lord who used the fake identity "Qimir" wore a helmet in this time, which blocked most of his senses and made him resistant to mind-reading, such that he had to use the Force while wearing it.

In 22 BBY, Jedi Padawan Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi could sense what was happening in the room nearby where Padmé Amidala rested. Anakin arrived just in time to cut two venomous kouhuns in half, just a few centimeters from the senator's face. Both Jedi could actually sense and identify the danger without being physically in the room, and Anakin managed to eliminate it in the dark right away.

entities.name: Floating Meditation
entities.description:
Floating Meditation, also known as Rising Meditation, was a Jedi meditation technique where one meditated while using the Force to float several inches off the ground. Often, surrounding objects would revolve around the Force-sensitive. Sometimes someone used Battle Meditation would perform this act at the same time.

This technique was used by Revan when he was being re-trained at the Jedi Enclave on Dantooine, where he floated himself, and several objects (chairs and a datapad) during meditation. Bastila Shan would use this power during her Battle meditation. Barriss Offee also used this technique often. Galen Marek used this meditation in order to find Darth Vader. Luke Skywalker accidentally discovered this technique years ago when he was roused by Han Solo and found that he was a meter off the ground. He also used this technique while being imprisoned by the Joiners on Woteba. Jacen Solo meditated this way, believing that contact with the ground could prove distracting.

The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force

entities.name: Force deflection
entities.description:
In 232 BBY, during the High Republic Era, Jedi Master Porter Engle fought a pair of Nihil on Elphrona when a party of the raiders attempted to kidnap the wealthy Blythe family for ransom. During the skirmish, Engle temporarily parted with his lightsaber when he threw it to eliminate one of the raiders. Before he could retrieve his weapon, the other raider fired at him, forcing Engle to deflect the shots with the Force.

In 40 BBY, Qui-Gon Jinn contemplated employing this power, but ultimately rejected the idea as too hard, for plasma responded poorly to being commanded by the Force.

In 22 BBY, Jedi Grand Master Yoda confronted his former Padawan learner Dooku, secretly the Sith Lord Darth Tyranus, in a hangar on Geonosis during the First Battle of Geonosis. Tyranus, who had previously defeated Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker, exclaimed his superiority over his former Master and fired a blast of Force lightning at Yoda. Yoda deflected the blast back at Tyranus, who in turn used the Force to deflect the blast into the ceiling of the hangar. The Jedi Master then absorbed another bolt of the Sith's lightning into his body without any harm, prompting Dooku to turn to his lightsaber for combat.

In 19 BBY, Yoda also was able to deflect melee attacks.

entities.name: Force drain
entities.description:
The ability to drain life Force energy from other beings was utilized by various Force-sensitives throughout galactic history.

The draining of Force energy from an individual into oneself was an ability associated to the dark side of the Force and practiced by various figures. This process consisted of the summoning of life energies from others by the practitioner, who then absorbed it.

According to the Imperial adviser Yupe Tashu, some Sith Lords of old drained Force energy from other individuals. By siphoning life from others, the ancient Sith strengthened their connection to the dark side of the Force and extended their own lives by centuries.

The Nightsister shaman Mother Talzin's spirit was able to emerge from the spirit world and into a stone monolith to directly possess the Dark Lord of the Sith Count Dooku, allowing her to drain his life energy and regain her physical form in the process. Green-colored mist emmitted from Dooku's body initially, and at a later phase, the substance flowed from the Count's oral and nasal cavities, as the life force was forcefully taken by Talzin. The victim collapsed screaming in pain.

entities.description: Force Illusion was a Force ability that allowed the user to generate illusions. This power was useful in combat, allowing a Force-sensitive individual to make copies of themselves to make it harder to find them or cause their opponent to lose focus by making them see things they feared. When Jedi Knight Cal Kestis faced the fallen Jedi Dagan Gera at the Koboh Observatory, both used this ability, with which Kestis destabilized Gera by making him see something he feared: his former friend and colleague, the Jedi Master Santari Khri, judging him and disapproving of his actions. This allowed Kestis and his ally to kill him.

entities.name: Force in Balance
entities.description:
Force in Balance referred to a Force ability whereby a user healed his or her wounds by inflicting injury upon enemies. A more advanced application of this technique involved employing it in conjunction with Force suppression to weaken a target's resistance against the Force, ensuring greater potency of the power.

During the Cold War, Jedi Sages and Jedi Shadows were trained in this power.

Force in Balance is a Force power of the Jedi Consular class in the massively multiplayer online role-playing game Star Wars: The Old Republic. As the Republic and Sith Empire characters have parallel abilities in the game, Force in Balance serves as the Jedi Order's counterpart to the dark side technique of the Sith, Death Field. For this reason, the power's gameplay mechanics is identical to that of Death Field, such that the user essentially "drains" the life of his or her targets. However, since not all abilities with identical effects are meant to be the same power (e.g. Telekinetic Throw and Force Lightning) and since Death Field is an infamous dark side power, it is quite possible that Force in Balance and Death Field are not one and the same, achieving similar effects through different means. The game does not provide descriptions of the powers other than their technical gameplay effects, however, so it remains unknown how Force in Balance actually achieves its effects in non-gameplay terms or whether it is merely a light side variant of Force drain after all. The passive ability "Mental Scarring" that supplements the power may indicate a psychological component to the technique.

entities.name: Force jump
entities.description:
Force jump, was an ability of the Force that allowed a Force-sensitive to perform an extended leap across extensive distances. Moreover, Force-users could use this Force-falling power to endure great falls and decent.

The feat was helpful for Jedi to emply since they may frequently fall off surfaces. During the High Republic one form of Jedi training was flinging a student off a cliff to impel the Padawan to learn the technique.

The Jedi Tarados Gon, Nicanas Tassu, and Kanan Jarrus were all noted users of the Force jump. When Luke Skywalker dueled his estranged father Darth Vader on Cloud City, he made use of the ability to escape from the carbon-freeze chamber. The action made him feel like the air itself was moving him. Skywalker's jump was as high and fast as those of Gon, Tassu, and Jarrus.

entities.name: Force kick
entities.description:
Force Kick was a Force power that enabled the practitioner to perform a kick towards a target and thereby interrupt their actions through the Force, even if they were several meters apart. Some Jedi Knights were skilled in the ability. Luke Skywalker once used this ability against one of Jabba the Hutt's henchmen during the Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon.

"Force kick" first appeared in Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi, in which Mark Hamill as Luke Skywalker kicks one of Jabba the Hutt's henchmen in the head, causing him to fall into the sarlacc pit while Boba Fett is flying helplessly by in the background.

The choreography blooper consists of the stuntman reacting to the impact of the kick too late, when Hamill is already lowering his leg. The shooting 'flaw' consists of the camera being placed at an angle making it obvious that the kick did not actually hit the stuntman. The sequence is referred to as the "Force kick", which jokingly speculates that Luke uses Force telekinesis to make the henchman fall into the sarlacc pit rather than the physical impact of the kick.

The Force kick was mentioned in Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel, albeit as a joke, and appears in Star Wars: The Old Republic as a Jedi Knight ability.

Although the Force Orb worked initially, Naboo Representative Jar Jar Binks' saliva proved to be a more effective method of sealing the helmet.

entities.name: Force projection
entities.description:
Force projection, also known as Similfuturus, was a Fallanassi Force technique recorded in the sacred Jedi texts and utilized by Jedi Master Luke Skywalker during the Battle of Crait. The technique allowed a Jedi or other user of the art to create an illusory doppelgänger of themselves that could be transmitted through the Force across vast distances.

Force projection required extreme concentration and focus. It was also possible to project several simulacra at the same time in the immediate vicinity of the caster.

Using this power was extremely taxing; Kylo Ren noted that Rey, whose power in the Force rivaled his own immense powers as a Skywalker, would die just by trying. Although Luke Skywalker maintained a projection for several minutes, giving all of himself to the Force to allow him to physically interact with his surroundings, the strain cost him his life.

The simulacrum, being only a projection and devoid of a body, allowed one to appear to perform seemingly impossible feats, such as being unscathed after taking a barrage of blaster bolts, stabbed at with a weapon, or disappearing from one position and reappearing in another. It also allowed one to project something other than one's true physical appearance, such as making oneself appear younger, or appearing to have an object not currently in one's possession, such as conjuring the image of possessing a specific lightsaber. Despite being otherwise immaterial, the user was at least capable of physical contact with others and could even fool advanced sensors and droids.

entities.name: Force sense
entities.description:
Force sense was among the most basic of Force abilities. It could be used to feel another being's feelings, the future, ripples in the Force caused by momentous or traumatic events, impending danger and the presence of the dark side. A more concentrated form of this ability was how Jedi were able to see others without relying on their physical senses. Closely related to Force sense and Force sight was precognition, the ability to hear direction and whispered promptings from the Force about what lay ahead in the immediate future.

The ability to heighten the senses with the Force was usually one of the first things taught to a Jedi when they begin their training. A Jedi student would learn how the Force binds all living things together, and learns to recognize these bonds and how they interact. This enables them to feel their environment, detect danger and the location of hidden beings or enemies even through barriers, as well as see in complete darkness, characteristics that Kanan Jarrus developped with blindness. However, as stated by Ahsoka Tano to Riyo Chuchi, a Force users ability to sense through the Force was never fully under their control.

Jedi and other Force-users would use this ability to sense impending danger, allowing the Force to warn them of a threat. This ability to sense danger would often come naturally to Force-sensitives and allowed the user to escape a potentially deadly situation, as when Yoda thwarted the attempt on his life at the hands of his clone troopers on Kashyyyk. This danger sense was often described as tingling feeling in the back of the mind that foretold danger, though it was known only to warn a Jedi of danger and wouldn't provide any information as to where the danger would come from. The danger sense would usually flare up just before an attack or some other threat occurred, giving the Force-user time to react to the danger.

Jedi could sense the location of hidden beings or enemies from a distance, and through barriers, allowing them to find, engage or avoid a being. Kylo Ren did so with his father, Han Solo, on Starkiller Base. Rey could locate near hidden enemies with the Force.

entities.name: Force Stasis
entities.description:
Force Stasis was a telekinetic Force power used to restrain and immobilize people or objects.

Force Stasis was an ability of the Force to forcibly restrain and immobilize people or to halt objects headed in a Force-user's direction. The ability allowed its users to cancel out the motion of a target, not only reducing its speed but even suspending it in place. The effect could at times be temporary, allowing the target to regain its motion, but could also be so powerful that, unlike normal applications of telekinesis, continuous conscious effort and physical gestures were not always necessary to maintain it. Additionally, the most skilled or powerful users could even exert this paralyzing grip on non-material objects, such as blaster bolts.

During the Night of Sorrow in 382 BBY, the Wookiee Jukkyuk, a bodyguard for Mother Elecia Zeveron, was stirred into a frenzy by Guide Marda Ro, who convinced the Wookiee to battle with the Jedi Order so she could get through to Zeveron. Rushing through the tunnels, Jukkyuk soon encountered and fired upon three Jedi, Padawan Matthea Cathley, Jedi Knight Azlin Rell, and fellow Knight Oliviah Zeveron. Zeveron responded to the attack with an act of Force Stasis: with a simple raise of her hand, Zeveron stopped the incoming blaster bolt in its tracks and then pushed it back towards Jukkyuk, who fell to his own blast but survived.

Twin sisters Verosha and Mae-ho Aniseya used Force Stasis on a Brendoki flutterby on the planet Brendok in 148 BBY. Yoda used the power to freeze Asajj Ventress in place as she tried to kill King Katuunko in 22 BBY.

entities.name: Force form
entities.description:
Force forms, or Jedi stance disciplines, were meditative battle stances that served as alternatives to the various forms of lightsaber combat. While all Jedi were taught to connect with the Force, and while most lightsaber styles relied on this connection to at least some degree, the Force forms enhanced a Jedi's power to feel and control the Force, allowing one to reach beyond what most could in the midst of combat, at the expense of physical ability. They were popular among Jedi Consulars and others who relied more on the Force than on lightsabers, even in battle. These disciplines included Center of Being, Shii Cho, Niman, Makashi, Soresu, and Shien.

Around the time of the First Jedi Purge, there were four major Force forms:

The different Force forms appeared in Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords, and most of them only appear if the player follows the class of the Jedi Consular, Jedi Master, or Sith Lord. Within the game itself, the Force forms seem to be an afterthought; they do not appear in the game manual alongside the lightsaber forms, and dialogue in the game will have a dark-sided Jedi Exile learn the Jedi Masters' "lightsaber" techniques, even if they are using Force forms.

entities.name: Hyperspace tunneling
entities.description:
Hyperspace tunneling was a Force power that was a means of transport similar to traveling through hyperspace that the loth-wolves of Lothal used to pass between distant points in the familiar world, as well as accessing other realms. The White Loth-wolf helped to transport Ezra Bridger and his companions across Lothal on two occasions.

Hyperspace tunneling was a Force power that allowed the user to create a hyper tunnel to transport themselves and others across great distances. The tunnel itself was blue and was visually similar to traveling through hyperspace.

The White Loth-wolf was capable of using hyperspace tunneling. While it appeared to have no effect on the White Loth-wolf, individuals that were transported were rendered momentarily unconscious and awoke dazed.

In 1 BBY, when the rebels Ezra Bridger, Kanan Jarrus, Sabine Wren, Zeb Orrelios, and Ryder Azadi were fleeing Imperial forces following the theft of the TIE Defender Elite, they followed the White Loth-wolf and two other Loth-wolves into the mountains, eventually ending up in their den. As Imperial TIE/sa bombers began to bomb the mountains, the group realized that they had to leave before the caves collapsed. However, trusting the Loth-wolves, Bridger implored his companions to join hands and follow them. Then, the White Loth-wolf created a hyper tunnel, and the three Loth-wolves walked into it. The rebels were rendered temporarily unconscious before waking up in a cliff dwelling. Wren then realized that while they had previously been in the northern hemisphere, readings indicated that they were now in the southern hemisphere.

entities.name: Kyber crystal building
entities.description:
The power to build with kyber crystals was a rare Force power known only to the Jedi Master Baird Kantoo who used the power to forge the Kyber Saber. He locked the secret away in a holocron inside a temple on an planet. Rowan Freemaker eventually found the holocron after passing the challenges of the temple and after he learned the power from the holocron used it to forge the kyber crystal necessary for his starship the Arrowhead.

This lead to Rowan and Naare hunting for many Kyber Crystals, until Rowan found out about Naare's true identity where they raced to find the crystals. Naare kept stealing the crystals from them, until Rowan found one on Hoth. Needing to escape, Rowan created a plan so he, his sister Kordi, his brother Zander Freemaker, and RO-GR surrendered a piece of ice to Naare, tricking her into trying to forge the Kyber Saber, only for the ice to melt and the Freemakers to escape.

Palpatine grew furious at the Kyber Saber's disappearance and so built a hunter droid, M-OC to hunt down Rowan Freemaker, so that he could reveal where the Kyber Saber was.

This lead Rowan to find many pieces to construct the Arrowhead, eventually crash landing on the planet where Baird Kantoo had left his holocron millennia ago. Following a series of challenges inside the temple he learned from the holocron and created the kyber crystal necessary to power the Arrowheads shields. and became a great success for the Rebellion.

entities.name: Metamorphosis
entities.description:
Metamorphosis was a form of shapeshifting based not on species biology, but the Force. Through primitive magic or Force-imbued artifacts, a being could change its shape into that of another person, creature, or entity through the use of the Force.

Apart from the masquerade technique, metamorphosis was uncommon among Force-using traditions like the Jedi and the Sith, but not among the mysterious witches known as the Nightsisters of Dathomir, who utilized Talismans of Transformation and traditional Dathomiri illusions to metamorphose.

On the planet Dathomir, Nightsister shamans were known to craft various Talismans of Transformation, rings or pendants enchanted through Allyan Magic to allow their wearer to metamorphose. Each of those talismans only allowed to turn into one specific creature by tapping into the energy of its "ur-spirit"—the single representative spirit for each species in the spiritual realm. The arcane powers of such artifact were a mystery to both Sith and Jedi scholars, who tried to explain their effects to no avail.

Charal, the self-appointed Witch-Queen of Endor, possessed such an enchanted ring, lost on Dathomir under Talzin's rule, which gave her the ability to turn into a raven. Charal was known to use it extensively, as she did during the Ewok–Sanyassan conflict of 3 ABY. On one such occasion, she transformed into a beautiful princess-like young woman in order to capture Cindel Towani. In this case, however, it is possible that her ring was not involved, so either she used traditional illusion, her cloak was Force-imbued, or she transformed through some other means.

entities.name: Mind trick
entities.description:
A mind trick, also known as the mind touch or the mindform, was an ability of the Force in which the practitioner influenced and controlled the thoughts, behavior, and actions of the affected, generally to the user's advantage. During the High Republic Era, it was more commonly referred to as a mind touch. Dark-side Force users used mind control.

When using the mind trick, the practitioner generally adopted a suggestive tone of voice and used a distinctive gesture, waving their hand in front of the target's face. If successful, the affected individual would absent-mindedly repeat the practitioner's exact words and then act accordingly, and Hutts, Exploiting and refining the power in order to survive after Order 66, the surviving Jedi Knight Grandea displayed such skill with the mind trick that she was able to deceive even Toydarians and members of the Galactic Empire's Inquisitorius. The latter usage took so much out of her it nearly killed her, leaving her bleeding from the nose. To Grandea, while she was unsure of how she had refined the skill to such an extent, her usage of the ability had evolved beyond a mere "trick."

Additionally, as exemplified by Prime Minister Almec's Mandalorian Guards, it was also possible to train individuals to resist mind tricks. Mind trick could affect simultaneously different targets, sometimes without the target necessarily hearing what the user had commanded them to do. In some cases, a simple wave of the hand from the user was enough to make it work. In others, it could work without even making a gesture. For the stormtrooper TD-110, being mind tricked by Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi had a lasting effect for the man, leaving him with a headache and persistent thoughts that kept him from noticing the droids C-3PO and R2-D2, even as he encountered them a second time aboard the Death Star, were two droids he needed to look for.

The mind trick could also be used by a group of Force-users on the same side simultaneously, speaking in unison to exert a greater collective influence on those who would normally be able to resist a single Force-sensitive's attempt alone, as demonstrated by Jedi Anakin Skywalker, Obi-Wan Kenobi, and Mace Windu upon the bounty hunter Cad Bane. However, it was shown that concentrating on and attempting to forcibly compel a strong mind into cooperation risked damaging or even destroying the mind of the subject, with Bane experiencing overwhelming pain during the attempt by the three Jedi to influence him. The living world of Planet X had an effect similar to the mind trick on those who visited it, instilling a sense of euphoria in visitors, who found it difficult to leave the world behind.

entities.name: Mind Walking
entities.description:
Mind Walking was the process in which Mind Walkers entered and remained in the realm they called "beyond shadows." Through a specific type of meditation, their consciousnesses entered beyond shadows and left their bodies behind. The technique was learned by Jacen Solo during his five year sojourn following the Yuuzhan Vong War, and several years later by Luke and Ben Skywalker, who were retracing Solo's steps to find out what had caused his fall to the dark side. Soon after, in 44 ABY, the Skywalkers allied with the Lost Tribe of Sith for a mission to eliminate Abeloth. After traveling to Abeloth's homeworld in the Maw, the Skywalkers, along with Sith High Lord Sarasu Taalon, Sith Saber Gavar Khai, and Captain Leeha Faal, Mind Walked beyond shadows in an attempt to locate Abeloth. Skywalker would Mind Walk one more time in an attempt to stop Abeloth. Additionally, Luke was joined by Darth Krayt in this state, who allied himself with Luke in order to have the united power to overcome Abeloth.

entities.name: Mindscape
entities.description:
A mindscape was a Force power that generated an environment within one's mind, used by powerful Force-sensitives to haunt and corrupt another's mind while seeing the world before them as mere illusions, such as when the soul of Tenebrae infected the Outlander after his own demise.

Some time before 3627 BBY, Tenebrae again infected others, locking Jedi Master Satele Shan within her own mind and feeding off it. In 3626 BBY, a task force led by the Eternal Alliance's Commander—formerly known as the Outlander—were able to enter Shan's mind, release her, and kill Tenebrae for good.
