entities.name: Attack on Bright Sun Hill
entities.description:
This attack on Bright Sun Hill took place in 43.5 ABY. In that year, the Raining Leaves and the Broken Columns Clans came together in a conclave to unite the clans into one clan. However, after multiple Nightsister attacks, they moved their conclave to a hill, which was claimed by Ben Skywalker and Dyon Stadd for the Jedi Order, so that the Clans it could remain neutral ground for the Clans.

The two Clans merged, but at nightfall, the Nightsisters attacked the hill. The Clans' Witches took part in the battle, and those without "The Arts" used spears and blasters to protect their hilltop. The hill was also attacked by the Nightsisters' Rancors, which were controlled by the control web spell. The battle at first went badly for the members of the Bright Sun Clan as they were not well organized. Though they did severely injure a few rancors, quite a few clan members were lost or too severely hurt to participate in the battle. Ben Skywalker eventually helped the people to devise a plan that would better defend them, by acting as if the hill was a Star Destroyer. The spearmen acted like shields and held back the enemies, allowing the blasters to act like turbolasers and concentrate fire on their assailants. The Witches then act like special weapons, such as ion cannons and proton torpedos, firing from deep behind their lines to help weaken the rancors. Using this technique, with the help of Luke Skywalker weakening the witches by using other Force techniques, such as seeking the Nightsisters with the Force then killing his cousins with showers of rocks, the Bright Suns were able to repel the Nightsisters.

entities.name: Battle of Bright Tree Village
entities.description:
The Battle of Bright Tree Village was a conflict that took place in 3 ABY between the Galactic Empire and the Ewoks of Bright Tree Village on Endor.

Doctor Raygar, an evil scientist to Emperor Palpatine, had designs on ruling the Galactic Empire and traveled to the Forest Moon of Endor to obtain the powerful Sunstar from the Ewoks' Bright Tree Village. He was attacked by the shaman Logray, who uses the Sunstar against him but Raygar's Imperial Reconnaissance droids soon overwhelmed the village and the evil doctor retaliated by swiftly stealing the Sunstar, before returning to Admiral Kazz's Star Destroyer in orbit. Back in his lab, Raygar studied the Sunstar and came to the realization that by harnessing its power, he could remove Palpatine and install himself as the Galactic Emperor. But when creating a dangerous cannon with the Sunstar's powers, Raygar discovered that Wicket Wystri Warrick, Princess Kneesaa, Latara and Teebo had come aboard Kazz's Star Destroyer with the help of a pilot droid named PD-28. Raygar planned to test his weapon on the captives—Latara and Teebo, but is thwarted by Wicket. Inadvertently, Raygar fired upon the Emperor's approaching shuttle instead. Palpatine survived, and Admiral Kazz subsequently arrested Raygar, charging him with high treason. The Emperor then oversaw the doctor's punishment personally. With PD-28, the Ewoks return safely to the Forest Moon, where Wicket, Kneesaa, Latara and Teebo say good-bye to the pilot droid as he embarked on a search for his old master.

entities.name: Raid on Bright Tree Village
entities.description:
In 3.5 ABY, the Sanyassan Marauders raided the Bright Tree Village on the forest moon of Endor, under the lead of King Terak and the Nightsister Charal. Terak and his Marauders used to raid the native Ewoks, searching the planet for the "power of the stars," an elusive entity that would allow them to leave Endor for good. Arriving at Bright Tree village, Terak and his goons found the stranded starcruiser of the Towani, a family of marooned Humans who sought shelter from the Ewoks. The king mistook the starcruiser for the source of the "power", and he killed its crew to obtain it. Meanwhile, the two-meter tall Marauders were taking prisoners and setting the huts on fire. At the end of the skirmish, multiple Ewoks had been deprived of their liberty, others had been killed, and three of the four Towani had fallen under the Marauders' blows. The family's youngest member, Cindel Towani, had just returned from a long walk in the woods when the raid began. Having witnessed the death of her whole family, the girl was caught by the Marauders and put in wagon en route to Terak's Keep. With the help of the Ewok warrior Wicket W. Warrick, Cindel Towani managed to get free of the vehicle inconspicuously.

entities.name: Attack on Brighthome
entities.description:
In 19 BBY, the newly-christened Darth Vader attacked the Jedi Order's space station Brighthome that was under Imperial control, with the Sith Lord wiping out all the clone stormtroopers in his way. While Vader could have had his droid transmit docking codes and enter the station without bloodshed, he elected to fight the station's personnel.

Vader came to the station to access its archives, as his Sith Master, Darth Sidious, ordered him to take a Kyber crystal from a Jedi he defeated in combat, Using the archives, Vader's droid located Kirak Infil'a, who had survived the Great Jedi Purge by taking the Barash Vow.

The attack on Brighthome was first depicted in Darth Vader (2017) 2, a 2017 canon comic written by Charles Soule and penciled by Giuseppe Camuncoli.

entities.name: Destruction of Burnin Konn
entities.description:
The destruction of Burnin Konn took place three months after the Battle of Endor, when Operation: Cinder was carried out on the world of Burnin Konn was by the Galactic Empire. During the attack, General Valin Hess's forces planted bombs on the geothermal reactors within the cities which generated power from the planet's magma shifts. The city Chakonnis and its entire population were destroyed within moments. Former Imperial sharpshooter Migs Mayfeld was present on Burnin Konn during the attack as part of a division which was lost, an event that seemed to mark his split from the Empire.

Some time after the event, while undercover with Din Djarin, Mayfeld was confronted by his old commanding officer during the battle, Valin Hess. During a tense drink that followed, Mayfeld pointedly reminded Hess of the battle and the slaughter that took place, to which Hess responded with derision and indifference. Overwhelmed with the traumatizing memories of the battle as well as Hess' callousness, Mayfeld shot him dead.

entities.name: Hunt for Caleb Dume
entities.description:
During the Great Jedi Purge, Jedi Padawan Caleb Dume was hunted by the newly formed Galactic Empire as a fugitive. In particular, he was pursued by his former comrades in arms Clone Captain Grey and Clone Captain Styles. Having joined with smuggler Janus Kasmir, Dume managed to stay one step ahead of the clone trooper officers until their journey to the planet Lahn, where they were to meet with former Separatist General Kleeve. After Dume was captured and about to be executed in the Kaller system, as Styles hoped to savor the death of Dume instead of simply killing him on Lahn, he was rescued by his allies. He had also managed to break through to Grey, who, instead of obeying his behavioral modification biochip, managed to sacrifice himself by destroying their own Gozanti-class cruiser to save Dume. With Grey and Styles dead, Dume parted ways with Kasmir and Kleeve, changing his name to "Kanan Jarrus" to move on from his past.

entities.description:
The attack on Cartao occurred during the early stages of the Clone Wars over the use of a secondary cloning facility owned by Spaarti Creations. Coming across a planet called Cartao, Palpatine "discovered" Spaarti cloning cylinders, and sent a force led by Kinman Doriana there. It was a victory for the Galactic Republic.

During the battle, General Fyefee Tiis used his ship, the Whipsaw, to disable the Separatist Droid Control Ship orbiting Cartao, thus giving the Republic's ground forces advance time before the Separatist Droid Army could be activated. Kinman Doriana managed to ram remotely-controlled Republic assault transport into the Spaarti facility, destroying the majority of it—and pinning the civilian loss of life on the Jedi Order. The planet of Cartao was left ravaged by the battle. Several thousand of the cloning cylinders survived, because they were stored in a warehouse away from the main complex. Palpatine had Doriana take the surviving cylinders to Wayland

entities.name: Hunt for Cassian Andor
entities.description:
The hunt for Cassian Andor was a hunt took place in 5 BBY. ISB Supervisor Dedra Meero organised the hunt for the criminal Cassian Jeron Andor for his role in the ambush on Ferrix and his links to the rebel operative Axis.

When she arrived, she set up an active base in the Ferrix main city. Before she arrived, Dedra Meero had questioned former Preox-Morlana Deputy Inspector Syril Karn to find out any information about Andor. The Imperial forces were initially unaware that Andor was already incarcerated under a false name on the moon Narkina 5.

Following the death of Andor's adopted mother, Maarva, Meero organized trap to catch Andor during Maarva's funeral procession. However, the subsequent riot resulted in Meero's failure, allowing Andor to evade capture and formally join the Axis network.

By 3 BBY, newly-promoted Supervisor Avril Heert was assigned the Axis desk while Meero was reassigned to the Ghorman project. Unwilling to give up her search for Andor, and by extension Axis, Meero stressed to Heert the importance of finding Andor. Unbeknownst to the ISB, Andor was in fact hiding under their noses on Coruscant.

entities.name: Assault on Cato Neimoidia
entities.description:
Prior to the Battle of Anaxes, in the final year of the Clone Wars, the 212th Attack Battalion and 501st Legion of the Republic Military undertook an assault on Cato Neimoidia. the incident saw Jedi Generals Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi again teaming up as part of the effort to capture the Trade Federation's leader, Nute Gunray. The viceroy's stronghold in the western hemisphere of the planet Cato Neimoidia was marked as the prime target for the attack. While the campaign nearly ended in disaster, with Gunray indeed escaping capture and instead fleeing into the Outer Rim, the Republic was able to capture his mechno-chair, which gave the Republic's intelligence services important clues about the Sith behind the war.

Skywalker claimed to have saved Kenobi's life at some stage of the operation. to a mission on Cato Neimoidia from much earlier in the war.

The "Anakin Skywalker" issue of Star Wars Encyclopedia stated that Skywalker claimed that he had saved Kenobi's life during the incident on Cato Neimoidia towards the end of the war, explaining Skywalker's line in Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith about saving Kenobi's life during "business on Cato Neimoidia." Within Star Wars Legends, the business was described in the Battle of Cato Neimoidia seen in James Luceno's novel Labyrinth of Evil. However, the canon novel Brotherhood by Mike Chen later featured a mission to Cato Neimoidia from much earlier in the war said to be the "business" mentioned in Revenge of the Sith. Being a large fan of Labyrinth of Evil, Chen made sure that his book did not contradict the other account, telling fans that they were free to continue to view Labyrinth of Evil as the business on Cato Neimoidia if they preferred.

The 2017 Japanese reference book Sutā Wōzu Batoru Taizen I EPISODE I・II・III had previously canonized details from the Labyrinth of Evil portrayal but stopped short of confirming the incident was what both Kenobi and Skywalker were making specific reference to in Revenge of the Sith, instead suggesting only Kenobi and Skywalker themselves could understand what was being referenced between them in that moment. As such, this article reflects the Brotherhood mission as "that business on Cato Neimoidia" based on StarWars.com describing it as such, yet this article still reflects that Skywalker claimed to have saved Kenobi in the later battle based on Chen's comments and Sutā Wōzu Batoru Taizen I EPISODE I・II・III.

entities.name: Conquest of Cato Neimoidia
entities.description:
During the Clone Wars, the planet Cato Neimoidia was conquered by the Galactic Republic

The base-of-operations for the Trade Federation, the Cato Neimoidian government had previously tried to take a neutral stance in the war, but the planet instead became a hotly contested battleground for both the Republic and CIS. The Federation's importance to the war made the Republic seek control over the planet; After the Republic's conquest, the Separatists sought to take Cato Neimoidia back

The conquest of Cato Neimoidia was first mentioned in the Databank A-Z section of Star Wars Helmet Collection 9, for a December 9, 2014, release. Further detail, such as the planet having been under Separatist control before the Republic attack, was established by the Droid Directory segment of Star Wars: Build Your Own R2-D2 44 The 2022 novel Brotherhood by Mike Chen would go onto feature Cato Neimoidia in a heavy capacity, establishing it as a neutral world during the early Clone Wars. As such, how Cato Neimoidia fell to the Separatists before the conquest—such was whether the world willing joined the Confederacy at some point after Brotherhood events or if it had been annexed by the Separatists via a conquest or invasion of their own—has not yet been confirmed as of the present.

entities.name: Battle of Cawa City
entities.description:
The Battle of Cawa City was fought during the Galactic Civil War when the Alliance to Restore the Republic fought to liberate Sterdic IV from the shattered Galactic Empire. It took place seventeen days after the Battle of Endor and resulted in a Rebel victory.

Cawa City, on Sterdic IV, was occupied by the Empire, with ground forces consisting an All Terrain Armored Transport and air support from TIEs. The Alliance sent Green Group and Feral Group to liberate the city from the Imperial forces. A-wings from Green Group, which included the squadron's new acting commander, Lieutenant L'ulo L'ampar, screened the air of TIE fighters to clear a path for Feral Group's Y-wing bombers. Just as Green Group were clearing the last of the TIEs, Shara Bey's A-wing was hit by a pursuing TIE fighter, although not fatal, her ship started leaking coolant. L'ampar managed to destroy the TIE fighter before it could do any further damage.

Once the approach was clear, Feral Group made their bombing run. Their Y-wings dropped magnetising cluster bombs, which magnetized to the All Terrain Armored Transport and destroyed it instantly. Both sides suffered heavy losses, however it was a Rebel victory.

entities.name: Skirmish aboard the Celestial Crow
entities.description:
During the Hunt for the treasure of Nok Drayen, Feylara Raed lured a smuggler to her starship, the Celestial Crow, to kill them. She hoped doing this would persuade her former lover, the smuggler's rival Skavak, to get back together with her. Responding to a fake distress call, the smuggler and a companion boarded the Celestial Crow, fighting past many droids. They found Feylara in the ship's cargo bay, behind a shield.

In the year 3643 BBY, Feylara Raed, a woman who had previously been in a relationship with Skavak, believed that she could win him back by killing his rival.

Feylara sent the Captain's ship a distress call. The Captain, along with their crew members Bowdaar and Corso Riggs, listened as Feylara claimed that she needed help. She said her starship, the Celestial Crow, was experiencing severe malfunctions —the engines had burned out, the power cells were fading, and she was losing life support—and was now drifting into a sun.

entities.name: Attack on Cerberon
entities.description:
The attack on Cerberon, also referred to as battle above Troithe, battle over Troithe and Battle against the Lodestar, was a battle initiated by the 204th Imperial Fighter Wing, led by Colonel Soran Keize, to attack General Hera Syndulla's New Republic forces within the Cerberon system.

The attack started when the Quasar Fire-class cruiser-carrier Aerie and a squadron of training drones led by Colonel Soran Keize, lured New Republic starfighters into a Battle above Catadra, forcing the Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship Lodestar to remain near Troithe and engage the Imperial II-class Star Destroyer Edict alone, albeit with limited support from X-wing starfighters launched from the Troithe Garrison. En route to Catadra with Meteor Squadron, Wyl Lark received a message from Palal Seedia with a warning to return to Troithe, which in reality was a distraction. The Edict emitted system-wide jamming that prevented all ships from communicating or using their sensors and cut off Seedia. On realizing that Shadow Wing was the enemy, Lark raced back to warn the Lodestar, with Nath Tensent following right behind him.

Keize's original plan was for Shadow Wing to destroy the Lodestar and escape to hyperspace on the Aerie, however a freighter flown by Yrica Quell caused catastrophic damage to the hangar bay's magnetic field, so Keize adapted his plan, to stay and fight.

Once all of the New Republic starfighters above Catadra were no longer a threat, all six Shadow Wing squadrons launched out of hiding, hidden by the debris field and the sensor jamming from the Edict, which dropped as soon as the TIEs attacked the Lodestar and started destroying X-wings that protected it.

entities.name: Hunt on Chandar's Folly
entities.description:
In 14 BBY following the Berch Teller campaign, Governor Wilhuff Tarkin repaid a debt to the Sith Lord Darth Vader by having himself and nineteen other men hunt Vader on the planet Chandar's Folly. Vader had asked Tarkin to hunt him as he had learned of Tarkin's past hunting on Eriadu. In the second day of the hunt, the group tracked Vader to a copse of thurian trees and surrounded him with flamethrowers before letting loose on the Sith. As they engulfed him with flames, Vader attacked the flamethrowers, resulting in the loss of four hunters. By the time of the ninth day of the hunt, the group had lost eight more hunters.

On the final day of the hunt, Vader killed all the hunters except Tarkin, who lured the Sith into storm ground. As a result, Vader was severely injured by a lightning strike, and Tarkin called in his ship to pick them both up.

While Tarkin presents Darth Vader learning about Tarkin's past during their time working together during the Berch Teller campaign, Star Wars: Timelines distinctly retconned Vader's knowledge of Tarkin's youth and the Hunt on Chandar's Folly to predate the events of the novel.

Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy

entities.name: Capture of the Chelator
entities.description:
The Scourge captured the Imperial I-class Star Destroyer Chelator

Amidst the debris in the space station was a spider-droid that was an ancient intelligence merged with the Spark Eternal, and it was able to corrupt other droids into vessels of its own, beginning with a KX-series security droid that had been deployed from the Chelator as part of the recovery mission. Afterward, the Scourge spread from the security droid to astromech droids and protocol droids. The 2,518 droids were quickly corrupted, catching the humans by surprise, and killed the organic beings in various ways when the Star Destroyer was in space. The MSE-6 series repair droid Petyr, who worked undercover aboard the Chelator for the Second Revelation group of independent droids, reported the tragedy to the Colony of the Second Revelation before he too was corrupted by a Scourge spider-droid.

Having conquered the Imperial starship, the Scourge renamed it the Scourge 01 and deployed spider-droids encased in the chasis of MSE-6 units, including Petyr, throughout the galaxy in order to spread its own consciousness. The Scourge 01 gradually transformed into a monstrous vessel that was black on color and featured many irregular spikes.

Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy

entities.description:
In the aftermath of the skirmish on the planet of Batuu, Grysk prisoners broke out from their detention cells and had an encounter with Commander Kimmund and his legion, aboard the Chimaera.

After breaking into one of the Grysk heavy freighters, Kimmund and his legion found some surrendering Grysk warriors. Chiss Grand Admiral Thrawn ordered Kimmund to take the prisoners for examination aboard the Chimaera. With the prisoners safely aboard the Chimaera, Thrawn had the prisoners put in an area reserved only for TIE pilots. Kimmund felt uncomfortable with this, because of how close it was to the hangar bay if they were to break out.

Because of this, Kimmund and a few others spent the night aboard the Darkhawk. After a brief hangout, they heard a thud, which turned out to be Rukh, Thrawn's Noghri bodyguard and assassin.

entities.name: Attack on Chortose
entities.description:
During the High Republic Era, the Nihil marauder organization attacked Agricultural Hub 42, a factory on the Rseik sector astronomical object Chortose. The marauders, whose forces were led by a Storm, wished to steal the factory's sprayer droids for their own purposes. Two Chortose workers were present in the factory at the time; while one, Pango, attempted to send a distress signal to the Jedi Order, his brother, Gru, resolved to defend the factory, believing the Jedi would not arrive. After the Nihil entered Agricultural Hub 42, the Jedi Knight Keeve Trennis, having been dispatched as a result of the signal, arrived to defend the Chortose. Though she struck one of the Nihil with a deflected blaster bolt, the Storm knocked her down. At that moment, a Force vision of the Sith Lord Darth Krall taking the Storm's place prevented her from fighting back; however, the Jedi Wayseeker Orla Jareni, who had been led by the Force to assist Trennis, incapacitated the Storm. Jareni placed the remaining Nihil in binders, intending to signal the Republic Defense Coalition to collect them.

entities.name: Assault on Christophsis
entities.description:
The assault on Christophsis was a brutal ground and air campaign launched by the Confederacy of Independent Systems as an invasion of the planet Christophsis in 22 BBY, shortly after the First Battle of Geonosis, specifically coming after the mission to Kudo III. General Whorm Loathsom led the Separatist Droid Army on the ground. The invasion included a siege of the capital city, Chaleydonia. A fleet of warships under Admiral Trench also established a blockade around the planet. A Galactic Senate relief effort under Senator Bail Prestor Organa was thus trapped on the ground and even was targeted by the Separatists. As the invasion entered its final stages, forces under Jedi Generals Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker arrived in the Christoph system.

By the time of the destruction of Trench's blockade, the Separatist invasion had claimed the planet, but pockets of resistance still remained that prevented the assault from being a total victory. Rather than focus on those rebels, Loathsom was forced to redirect his forces to counter the arrival of the Grand Army of the Republic on the ground. As the battle dragged on, another droid army was dispatched to Christophsis, which the Separatists hoped would wipe out the Republic's forces and formally claim the planet for the Confederacy.

Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy

entities.name: Liberation of Clak'dor VII
entities.description:
The liberation of Clak'dor VII was fought at Clak'dor VII between the New Republic and the forces of Warlord Sander Delvardus in 5.5 ABY.

After the unsuccessful attack of Delvardus on Sullust, the New Republic led by the Sullustan captain Sien Sovv launched a counterattack campaign for the control of territories of the Eriadu Authority. The New Republic fleet dispatched to Lwhekk to deal with the Ssi-ruuvi was ordered by Mon Mothma to aid in the liberation of Clak'dor VII; the fleet included the Shriwirr, twelve Nebulon-Bs, and smaller support ships. The battle was subsequently described as a "merciless assault".

entities.name: Battle of the Cliffs
entities.description:
The Battle of the Cliffs was a battle fought on the planet of Cilpar during the Galactic Civil War.

After liberating an Imperial base on Endor, Throm Loro led members of the Cilpari Resistance against Moff Boren Tascl's forces. When Loro's actions caught the attention of the Alliance to Restore the Republic, Moff Tascl responded by engaging the resistance in open warfare.

Throm Loro's last stand was in a mountainous region of the planet, where he was accompanied by Groznik, a Wookiee slave he had freed on Endor. During the battle, two Lambda-class shuttles launched a strafing run on the resistance soldiers on a rocky plateau. Throm was caught in the laser fire and killed. Groznik, having sworn a life debt to Throm, retaliated, hurling a boulder at one of the shuttles and destroying it.

Star Wars Handbook 1: X-Wing Rogue Squadron

entities.name: Crisis on Cloud City
entities.description:
The Crisis on Cloud City was an incident during the New Republic Era that saw the Nagai Garlev crash onto Cloud City on the planet Bespin, where he demanded to speak to his old comrades Landonis Balthazar Calrissian and Han Solo, former smugglers with major ties to the New Republic, Joined by the bounty hunter Beilert Valance, Solo arrived on Bespin and met with Calrissian, but, by that point, a mysterious assassin—secretly the Anzati Reyna Oskure—had already killed Garlev. The assassin then managed to escape aboard a new model of cloud car.

The Crisis on Cloud City appeared in Star Wars (2025) 3 and was identified on its cover. The storyline was first revealed via the issue announcement at Celebration Japan.

entities.name: Campaigns of the Cloud-Riders
entities.description:
The Cloud-Riders, a crew of rebels who sought to bring down the Galactic Empire, fought a series of campaigns against the Empire and the Five Crime Syndicates, including Crimson Dawn. Under the leadership of Enfys Nest, the rebels, riding into battle on swoops, engaged in heists like the raid on Gargon and the heist on Hovun IV. The Cloud-Riders also often encountered the gang led by the smuggler Tobias Beckett, who himself often worked with Crimson Dawn. The Cloud-Riders secured a major victory during the showdown on Savareen, which occurred when the Cloud-Riders set their sights on securing a shipment of coaxium. The public leader of Crimson Dawn, Dryden Vos, was killed during the showdown, and a former Imperial corporal named Han Solo killed Beckett.

entities.name: Capture of Coh Veshiv
entities.description:
Imperial Advisor Coh Veshiv was captured in 0 ABY by Rebel allied privateers at the planet Esseles. The Rebel affiliated crew led by Dhas Fenoep Vedij of the former Imperial EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate Far Orbit, managed to convince Veshiv that they were present to take him to his next destination. Veshiv agreed and left his ship, the Empire Forever, and was captured, being turned over to the Rebels eventually. It was in large part due to Veshiv's capture as well as the failure to stop it that Palpatine orchestrated the Battle of Andalia, which resulted in Grand Admiral Osvald Teshik's cyborgification.

entities.description:
A battle on the planet Colla IV was a major engagement in the New Republic liberation campaign after the Battle of Endor.

A large New Republic fleet went from Kashyyyk and defeated Warlord Teradoc in the Togoria system. After this costly victory, the New Republic forces attacked the fortress world Colla IV. The battle was a major victory for the New Republic. This battle allowed the New Republic to return to Brentaal, in the Core Worlds. The Imperial abandoned the Chazwa system due to the progress of the New Republic forces.

entities.name: Combined Clans Center Building riot
entities.description:
In 19 ABY, agents of the Imperial Remnant fomented a riot in the area of Merchant's Square in the Bothawui city of Drev'starn, playing off civil unrest caused by the Caamas Document Crisis. After a large crowd gathered in the square, Imperial agents fired several sniper shots, which ignited a panic which drove the crowd into the nearby Combined Clans Center Building. Bothan guards responded by firing shots into the mob, which was only prevented access to the building's upper floors through the efforts of famed New Republic hero Han Solo. In the chaos, twenty-seven rioters lost their lives, and about forty more were injured.

Among the casualties were two unarmed Leresen, whose people retaliated by sending a task force to destroy a small space station in orbit over Bothawui, killing twenty-one innocent Bothans (according to their own laws, twenty innocent lives were an acceptable proxy for two guilty persons of the same "tribe"). This spurred the Mon Calamari and Diamalan governments to send task forces to protect Bothawui from further aggression, precipitating the build-up of warships in orbit that eventually sparked the second Battle of Bothawui.

entities.description:
The Battle of Commenor took place during the Second Galactic Civil War.

The Galactic Alliance objective was to contain Commenorian forces, not to occupy the world.

During the battle, elements of the Galactic Alliance Third Fleet launched a cloaked asteroid at Commenor. Pilots Caregg Oldathan and Danen of Grayfeather Squadron investigated and discovered it.

Realizing they could not hope to prevent it from colliding with their world, they pursued the ships responsible for the attack, hoping to exact vengeance and prevent the tactic from being used again.

entities.name: Attack on Corellia
entities.description:
A Nihil attack occurred in Coronet City on Corellia in the Core Worlds in 230 BBY as part of the infiltration on Corellia. The attack was only launched when the bodyguard Prybolt Garavult grew suspicious of the meeting his client, Father of Finances Nomar Tralmat, was involved in and feared for the man's life. In reality, Tralmat was having a meeting with his Nihil allies, only for Garavult's entry to risk the public learning of his secret alliance. As such, Tralmat ordered Sabata Krill to kill the bodyguard. Because Garavult was able to get a hologram message about the Nihil out to his boss and friend Alys Ongwa, kicking off a series of events that made the Jedi Order and Supreme Coronet City Diplomat Protection aware of the Nihil's infiltration on Corellia. Tralmat also used the incident as a chance to fake his death. During the Battle of the Corellian Shipyards, Tralmat revealed himself to be alive, only to be killed later in the battle by Mother Fastidima when she learned he was behind Garavult's death.

entities.name: Infiltration on Corellia
entities.description:
The infiltration on Corellia was an operation launched by the Nihil cell commanded by Krix Kamerat on the orders of the Eye of the Nihil, Marchion Ro. Aided by the Father of Finances Nomar Tralmat, the Nihil were able to hide hundreds of themselves on the Core World of Corellia amongst the Coronet municipal police, with Tralmat hiring the undercover marauders on the claim they would help with security for new starships being built in the Santhe Shipyards of Coronet City. In reality, the Nihil intended to use the opening to steal Longbeam cruisers and MPO-1400 Purgill-class star cruisers with which they could assist in the destruction of Starlight Beacon. The Nihil also helped to escalate a union dispute on Gus Talon to distract Corellia's Jedi planetary defense forces, even arranging for a bombing at Gus Talon University.

Kamerat was prevented from playing an active role in the theft of the starships when he was captured by the Jedi during a raid on his base of operations at Dol'har Hyde. When Tralmat faked his death with clear signs of Nihil involvement, a team of Jedi—including Jedi Masters Cohmac Vitus and Kantam Sy, joined by Padawans Reath Silas and Ram Jomaram—were dispatched to Coronet City from Starlight Beacon to assist the Supreme Coronet City Diplomat Protection agency. Meanwhile, Tralmat's political pawn Ovus Buckell, who became the new Father of Finances after Tralmat's supposed death, was deceived into believing there would only be several small-scale Nihil attacks to make the Corellians distrustful of outsiders, only for hundreds of Nihil, joined by armored support, to march towards the shipyards as the operation neared its end. Ultimately, the Jedi, Diplomat Protection agency, and other allies which they managed to rally defeated the Nihil plot.

Nonetheless, the other pieces of Ro's wider plot were successful, with Starlight being destroyed before he unleashed the stormseeds. Additionally, Corellia erupted into a civil war after the Nihil infiltration.

entities.name: Occupation of Corellia
entities.description:
During the First Order-Resistance War, Corellia was subject to an occupation after it was conquered by the First Order, which wanted to claim the planet, its shipyards, and its factories in 34 ABY. Most Corellians displayed scorn at being subject to the occupation but quickly accepted the new reality. The First Order at some point had also annexed control over the Corellian Engineering Corporation.

In 35 ABY, after the First Order joined with the Sith Eternal and its fleet, the Final Order, and were defeated in the Battle of Exegol, Corellia was in open rebellion against the First Order.

entities.name: Second duel on Corellia
entities.description:
To bring the Kaggath to an end, Darth Thanaton invited Lord Kallig to face him directly, in front of the crowds assembled.

Kallig arrived as Thanaton was making a speech to high ranking Imperial and Sith observers, about his adversaries corruption both by association with the presumed dead Darth Zash, and her murder. As Kallig prepared to face Thanaton, the Dark Lord ordered a subordinate Sith and then his Guardians to instead kill his foe.

After Kallig dispatched Thanaton's allies, the two Sith finally fought directly.

After a drawn out duel, Thanaton became frustrated with his inability to defeat the young and inexperienced Sith Lord. Eventually Kallig disarmed Thanaton, who responded by fleeing the field, much to Kallig's surprise and dismay.

entities.name: War on Corellia
entities.description:
The War on Corellia was a civil war that took place in the wake of the Nihil infiltration of the planet Corellia. Following the destruction of Starlight Beacon, the Nihil took root on the planet, and a contingent of Corellians believed the only way to prevent the planet from sharing the same fate as Starlight Beacon was to embrace the Nihil's rule. They were opposed by Corellians such as Alys "Crash" Ongwa and Svi'no Atchapat. Two Jedi—Jedi Master Conithr and her Padawan, Ruu—chose to not to return to Coruscant after the Jedi Order recalled the Jedi there, instead choosing to remain on Corellia to defend the Corellians from the Nihil. During one incident, Conithr was killed, causing Ruu to fall to the dark side of the Force and stop operating as a Jedi.

A massacre of Nihil forces occurred at the Greens

The War on Corellia was first mentioned in the reference book Star Wars: Timelines.

entities.description:

entities.name: Skirmish aboard the Coronet
entities.description:
A skirmish occurred aboard the Coronet, the personal starship of Duchess Satine Kryze, during the Clone Wars.

Following an attack on one the Galactic Republic's cruisers, the Jedi Council had one of its member, Obi-Wan Kenobi, investigate rumors that Duchess Satine Kryze of Mandalore was amassing an army to fight for the Confederacy of Independent Systems.

In truth, the Death Watch, under Concordia's governor, Pre Vizsla, had aligned with Count Dooku and his Confederacy. After Vizsla revealed himself as Death Watch's leader, Kryze along with Senator Tal Merrik and others went aboard the Coronet to speak to the Republic Senate in order to convince them of Mandalore's neutrality. Kenobi, along with Anakin Skywalker and detachments of clone troopers from the Grand Army of the Republic's 212th Attack Battalion and the 501st Legion accompanied Kryze and her party to protect them from Death Watch and a force of B2-series super battle droids.

Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles

entities.name: Battle of the Corridor
entities.description:
The Battle of the Corridor was a conflict in the Feswe Corridor between the Rebel Alliance and Imperial forces under the House of Tagge in 0 ABY.

Baron Orman Tagge and Doctor Silas Tagge intended to use the Omega Frost, a new superweapon, to flash-freeze the Alliance Fleet as it traveled through the Feswe Corridor. However his plans were thwarted when the Rebel Luke Skywalker destroyed one of the Omega Frost's conductor towers from space with his lightsaber. With the weapon inactive, the Rebel forces led by the Millennium Falcon were able to pass through the asteroid corridor and destroy both Silas Tagge's Mining Explorer and General Ulric Tagge's battlecruiser. Ulric Tagge managed to escape the destruction of his cruiser in an escape pod.

entities.name: Rise of the Cortosis Battle Droids
entities.description:
The Rise of the Cortosis Battle Droids was a campaign that occurred when the Confederacy of Independent Systems began to manufacture battle droids with cortosis, a lightsaber-resistant substance. The event ended with the destruction of the C-B3 cortosis battle droid factory on Metalorn.

A number of missions and skirmishes were involved in this campaign, including a Mission to Tatooine, the Coruscant Insurrection, a Duel in Bentho's Nightclub and a mission to the world of Metalorn.

While The New Essential Chronology originally dated Star Wars: The New Droid Army to ten months after the start of the Clone Wars, "Heroes on Both Sides," which is set in 20 BBY, later established that the planet Coruscant had not been attacked until the events of that episode, moving The New Droid Army forward in the timeline.

entities.name: Skirmish at the Coruscant Livestock Exchange and Exhibition
entities.description:
This skirmish took place in 43.5 ABY, during the Coruscant Livestock Exchange and Exhibition at the Grand Event Center on Coruscant. Han Solo and Leia Solo, their daughter, Jaina, granddaughter Allana, and Jedi Knights Natua Wan and Radd Minker attended the show a few days into its running. After ditching the journalist Javis Tyrr as they entered the Dangerous Animals level, the group was viewing the animals when the Solo women felt a disturbance in the Force.

They found that Wan was missing, and the lights in the area suddenly went out. Wan, who had become afflicted with the same psychosis that had overcome Valin Horn, Seff Hellin, and Horn's sister Jysella—a psychosis that caused the affected being to believe that every un-afflicted being they knew had been replaced by an impostor—hoped to kill the "impostors" and cover her escape by releasing the animals present from their cages. Leia was forced to kill all five boarwolves to save a young boy who had fallen into their pen, before the mother nexu had clamped down on an Ithorian's leg. Organa Solo stabbed the beast just as the ramps stopped retracting.

While pandemonium flooded the facility, Jaina Solo began a lightsaber duel with Wan, who was emptying a bordok cage. Organa Solo and Minker soon joined in the fight, with Minker ending it with a head-butt which left Wan unconscious. Wan was taken into custody in the Jedi Temple, but increased Galactic Alliance pressure on the Jedi to turn their captive psychotic Knights over to the government led to the Knights being evacuated from the Temple and taken off-world to Shedu Maad.

entities.description:
In 3661 BBY, during the Great Galactic War, riots broke out on the Galactic Republic's capital world of Coruscant. The contention was the result of the Mandalorian blockade of the Hydian Way, which prevented resources from traveling along the super-hyperroute. As starvation spread across the lower levels of Coruscant's Galactic City, panicked citizens began protesting and rioting against the Galactic Senates inability to break the blockade. The riots ended in 3660 BBY, when the smuggler Hylo Visz successfully led a group of fellow vagabonds against the Mandalorian cruisers.

entities.name: Attack on Coruscant's Verity District
entities.description:
The attack on Coruscant's Verity District was a mission undertaken by Colonel Soran Keize of the Galactic Empire's 204th Imperial Fighter Wing. Keize had learned of an extensive databank situated beneath the upper level Verity District of the capital planet Coruscant; the databank, maintained by the late Emperor Palpatine and cataloguing every criminal act and atrocity that Imperial personnel committed, had been used by the Messenger droids to provide orders for Operation: Cinder in the aftermath of the Emperor's demise at the Battle of Endor. Believing that the nascent New Republic would use the data bank's records to prosecute former Imperials in the event that it won the Galactic Civil War, Keize intended to destroy it by destroying its supports and dropping it onto the district's lower levels. Yrica Quell, former TIE pilot of the 204th, deduced Keize's plan, and the New Republic dispatched her and the U-wing pilot Kairos to stop him.

The attack, which occurred simultaneous to the Empire's last stand at the Battle of Jakku, saw Keize abandon his unit on his mission to destroy the databank. After breaking his way through the Imperial blockade in the Coruscant system, Keize descended toward the planet, and was later followed by Quell and Kairos. Though Imperial forces attempted to defend Coruscant, they were destroyed by both Keize and Quell, who proceeded to duel one another. With TIE fighters in pursuit, Kairos ejected from her U-wing shortly before it exploded, destroying many of her pursuers and damaging Keize's starfighter. Keize crashed, sustaining severe injuries, but intended to destroy the databank using proton warheads. Quell landed and confronted the dying Keize, preventing him from completing his mission. At the same time, the New Republic defeated the Empire at Jakku, subsequently sending Intelligence to study the databank.

Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy

entities.name: Assault on Coruscant
entities.description:
Around 3 ABY, to damage a statue of Galactic Emperor Sheev Palpatine: at that time, both Palpatine and Darth Vader were dealing with an anomaly in the Force, so the Alliance hoped the assault would rattle the pair, pushing them further off-balance, and also remind the galaxy that the Alliance continued to fight the Galactic Empire. By striking at the Imperial capital planet of Coruscant, the rebels hoped to show they were strong and unafraid. The plan for the assault was devised by General Leia Organa, who, along with Admiral Gial Ackbar, presented the plan to a group of elite rebel pilots.

A-wing pilots Nien Nunb, Freyta Smyth, and Bryen Rowne joined Lando Calrissian and Chewbacca for the mission. Although the mission resulted in the deaths of Smyth and Rowne, it was ultimately a success, as the target was taken out and news of the daring rebel attack reached the HoloNet.

entities.name: Duel on Coruscant
entities.description:
During the Clone Wars, a duel took place in the Senate Building on Coruscant between the bounty hunter Boba Fett and the Jedi Master Mace Windu.

After Jedi Master Mace Windu killed Jango Fett during the Battle of Geonosis, Fett's son Boba Fett desired to kill Windu in vengeance. Boba Fett arrived on Coruscant after arranging to give information vital to the survival of the Republic to Supreme Chancellor Palpatine. Fett was escorted to the Jedi Temple to await his appointment but not before agreeing to leave his weapons on his ship. Once he was left alone, Fett left the Temple and traveled to the lower levels of Coruscant. In his excursion, Fett received weapons from Hat Lo and a saberdart from Elan Sleazebaggano before returning to the Temple. After finding that Windu had already left for his own meeting with the Chancellor, Fett used his jetpack to fly to the Senate Building.

Boba Fett entered Palpatine's level of the Senate Building through a window after disabling its alarm. Fett proceeded directly to Palpatine's antechamber where he found Mace Windu. Fett fired almost immediately with his flechette pistol. After Windu dodged the first rounds Fett rushed him and shot Windu's shoulders. The Jedi then jumped over Fett while igniting his lightsaber. Windu swung the lightsaber twice, grazing Fett's armor and knocking the pistol from his hands. Fett then drew a dagger and rushed Windu again. The dagger only went through the Jedi's robes but Fett did manage to punch Windu's ribs. Windu countered by hitting his lightsaber against the hunter's shoulder.

At this point, the Jedi Master gave Fett a chance to surrender. Fett returned the dagger to his belt, but he was taking the opportunity to release his CryoBan grenade. Fett attempted to shoot Windu while he suffered the effects of the blast, and was hit on his arm and helmet when failed. After Fett refused to surrender again, Windu knocked the dagger away. Running out of options, Fett fired the saberdart which Windu merely caught between his fingers. Knowing he had been beaten and wanting to go down fighting, Fett refused the last offer of surrender and raised his flechette pistol to force Windu to kill him. Just before the last blow could be dealt, Chancellor Palpatine entered the room with his Red Guards who ended the fight.
entities.short_description: During the Clone Wars, a duel took place in the Senate Building on Coruscant between the bounty hunter Boba Fett and the Jedi Master Mace Windu.

entities.name: Liberation of Coruscant

entities.name: Military revolt on Coruscant
entities.description:
A military revolt was orchestrated on Coruscant by Headmaster Gentis during his attempted coup. Gentis successfully took control of Coruscant for a brief time, but was defeated shortly afterward.

Though the Clone Wars had ended, many Imperial soldiers kept dying because of the Emperor Palpatine's warmongering, a fact that led the Headmaster of the Imperial Academy, Gentis, to launch an coup, with the goal of killing the Sith Lord and stopping the endless killing that cost him all but one of his sons. Using his position, the Headmaster struck the night of the graduation of the first class of Imperial officers.

Explosions rocked the cityscape for kilometers around, eliminating seventy-two Imperial targets within minutes. The officer's club, various Stormtrooper garrisons, the Comm Towers, and a supply depot were all destroyed. Imperial Plaza became ground zero in the battle that erupted, as "terrorist" forces swarmed through the city streets, fighting with the Empire's clone forces. The stormtroopers were losing the battle until the "Warlock," Supreme Commander Darth Vader, appeared, rallying the troops and driving the enemy forces back. In the madness, Tohm had escaped from the prototype starfighter by engaging its ejection seat and landing in the midst of the battle. Tohm joined the stormtroopers in following Vader, but when one of the terrorists grabbed his ankle, he bent and removed the man's mask, revealing his friend Shens. Shens begged Tohm to help them kill Palpatine, the main target of their assassination attempts that night.

As Shens lay dying, he then asked Tohm to kill Vader, but Tohm told his friend that he should have included him earlier, and shot Shens in the head. The lieutenant then bowed to the Dark Lord of the Sith, who instantly respected his bravery and loyalty. As the pair made their way from the plaza, another explosion tore through the nearby buildings, unleashing a powerful necrotic virus known as Aorth-6. Dozens of Imperials, including Royal Guardsmen, were killed by the aerosolized virus, which liquified them from the inside out. Lieutenant Tohm donned a breathing device that he had taken from the TIE fighter when he ejected and followed Lord Vader inside. There they found a mortally infected Emperor Palpatine and Moff Trachta. Palpatine was using the dark side of the Force to keep the virus at bay, but was losing the battle even with his formidable powers. Vader accused Trachta of being part of the conspiracy, but the Moff vehemently denied it, saying they needed to get the Emperor into hiding; fear of his power was the only thing keeping the Empire together. The trio escorted the sovereign to secret hangar below the Imperial Palace, where they loaded him aboard a stealth transport.

entities.name: Scourge of Coruscant
entities.description:
The Scourge of Coruscant was an attack by the Scourge on the Galactic Empire's capital planet, the ecumenopolis of Coruscant, brought upon by the Sith Lord Darth Vader as part of a test for his Sith Master, Darth Sidious, known publicly as Galactic Emperor Sheev Palpatine. Vader decided to test Sidious and try to showcase the power he had acquired from his hatred. As part of his test, Vader collected a number of the Scourge's spider-droids, which it used to infect droids and cyborgs. Without context, it would even look as though Vader himself was leading the Scourge's invasion.

Arriving on Coruscant aboard his TIE Advanced x1 and speeding past and Imperial checkpoint looking for any sign of the Scourge, Vader was shot down but crashed into the Imperial Palace, where he was surrounded by a grouping of stormtroopers from a Lambda-class T-4a shuttle. Vader soon wiped out every trooper who was sent against him, including members of his own death trooper guard who were ordered to turn on Vader by the Emperor. Sidious used the battle to claim to Vader that, without his blessing, he had nothing to command, further questioning if he was in control of his own hate. Soon enough, the collected spider-droids escaped Vader's TIE Advanced x1 and infected the death trooper corpses as Vader struggled with Sidious. While Vader neck snapped each trooper and lifted them into the air to prevent their escape into the Lambda shuttle, he threw the spider-droids out into Imperial City, where the Scourge used them to find and infect droids to massacre the populace.

While Sidious struck down several droids with his Force lightning, taking several civilians with them, the infected droids made it out into the city, where they quickly killed up to one hundred citizens. To protect his capital, Sidious ordered Grand Vizier Mas Amedda—who, like Sub-Administrator Sly Moore, was disturbed by Sidious's casual execution of citizens along with the Scourged droids—to wipe out sector 35 and sector 36 under protocol 23. As laser weaponry destroyed both sectors, destroying any Scourged droids at great cost to the city, Sidious explained the source of his power: while Vader's hatred for Sidious did indeed increase his power in the dark side, Sidious himself thrived off such hate. As such, the more Vader or any of his other followers hated the Emperor, the more powerful the man became. Vader was allowed to leave Coruscant in silence aboard the Lambda, aboard which the Scourge used a surviving spider-droid to tell Vader that, by bonding with it, he would finally be powerful enough to defeat Sidious. Vader willingly allowed the Scourge to infect him but quickly separated his armor from the Scourge at large, protecting himself as he began to create a Scourge infection of his own on Mirgoshirax.

entities.name: Duel on Corvair II
entities.description:
By 42 BBY, a duel was fought on the astronomical object Corvair II after the Wookiee Jedi Initiate Krrsish attacked fellow Trandoshan Initiate Gheyr. When Gheyr's friend, the Togorian Jedi youngling Jak'zin, tried to stop Krrsish, he was harmed and punched by the Wookiee. The fight was eventually interrupted by Jedi Master Yoda.

The duel on Corvair II first appeared in the fifth issue of the Star Wars: Yoda comic series. The comic was authored by Jody Houser, illustrated by Luke Ross, and published by Marvel Comics Prior to the comic's release, it was first mentioned in a post published on January 17 of that year on StarWars.com that announced the future release of Yoda 6.

entities.name: Battle against Crimson Dawn
entities.description:
Between 3 ABY and 4 ABY, Vermillion and the Galactic Empire. After becoming aware that the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Sidious was hunting her, Crimson Dawn leader Lady Qi'ra activated her spies within the various major powers of the galaxy to create chaos in order to buy her time to follow through with her plans. Qi'ra hid with the Orphans on an astronomical object aboard their ship, the Siroto, where they were eventually discovered by the Imperial Navy. The Empire deployed an Interdictor-class to prevent Qi'ra and her flagship from escaping.

As Qi'ra spoke personally with Sidious and outlined her plans to destroy him, Qi'ra sent the Vermillion to attack the interdictor. The Vermillion was attacked by TIE fighters and TIE/IN interceptors, but they were unable to prevent the ship from crashing directly into the interdictor, destroying both. Escape pods were deployed from the Vermillion, and Sidious ordered they all be destroyed, allowing for no one to escape.

The destruction of the Vermillion allowed for Qi'ra and the Oprhans to escape from the Imperials aboard the Siroto and as they left, Chanath Cha asked Qi'ra if they should pick up any potential survivors from the escape pods, Qi'ra thought for a moment before declining, adding that they could honor their sacrifice by seeing her plans through to the end.

The fact that Qi'ra survived was later inadvertently revealed to Vader by Cha. When Cha confronted Vader, he informed her that she would not avenge Qi'ra's death, which surprised the hunter. Vader sensed this and realized that Qi'ra had actually survived, adding that his Master would be fascinated to learn of this.

entities.name: Skirmish with Crimson Dawn
entities.description:
In 3 ABY, a skirmish broke out between the Sith assassin Ochi and assassins of Crimson Dawn on an astronomical object when Ochi, whose loyalty was being tested by the Sith Lord Darth Vader, attempted to find out who the Grand Hutt Council member Bokku was working with to betray Jabba Desilijic Tiure. After he spotted two assassins under a carriage, Ochi killed one of them and told the other he wanted to speak with them. The assassin informed Ochi it would be difficult because if he messed with Bokku, he messed with Crimson Dawn, revealing her affiliation as several other assassins joined her. Ochi killed a number of the assassins as he attempted to escape but found himself surrounded again. In response, Ochi told them that if they messed with him, they messed with Darth Vader. The assassins laughed at Ochi's claims, and the female assassin pointed out that whilst Ochi could maybe kill a dozen of them, he could not take out all of Crimson Dawn, before telling Ochi to join Crimson Dawn.

Ochi saw that Vader had arrived and informed the assassins, and also warned them to surrender or die. Vader, however, flew over Ochi, and landed his shuttle nearby, much to Ochi's confusion. The female assassin then told Ochi that Vader had not arrived to save him, but to test him, and again told Ochi to join them. Ochi's response was to shoot the assassin, killing her, and to run to take cover behind a rock. Eventually Ochi killed the rest of the assassins before he saw Vader stood above him, and informed the Sith Lord that Bokku was working with Crimson Dawn, though he realized that the Vader had already known this fact. As he made his way atop a rock, Ochi assured Vader that his loyalty lied with the most powerful and the pair soon found themselves surrounded by more Crimson Dawn assassins. Vader confirmed he would always be the most powerful, and Ochi laughed as the two began to cut down the assassins.

entities.name: First Battle of Cyclor
entities.description:
The First Battle of Cyclor, also known as the attack on Cyclor, was a Nihil raid on the Cyclor Shipyards above Cyclor in the Mid Rim. Sarn Starbreaker, a Cloud of Pan Eyta's Tempest, wanted to make a strike against the Galactic Republic by destroying the Innovator, an Elite-class vessel being built at the shipyards which was to be a showpiece of the upcoming Valo Republic Fair. The Cyclorrian workers, alongside Jedi Knight Indeera Stokes and her Padawan Bell Zettifar, fought back against the attackers. After the Cyclorrians managed to get a signal for help past the Nihil's scrambler droids, a drift of Jedi Vectors led by Jedi Master Porter Engle arrived from Derra to reinforce them. Ultimately, Zettifar was able to destroy Sarn Starbreaker's Cloudship despite having been shot in the gut with a harpoon, killing the Cloud amidst the defeat of all his forces.

Star Wars: The High Republic: Chronicles of the Jedi

entities.name: Second Battle of Cyclor
entities.description:
The Second Battle of Cyclor, or as the Skirmish over Cyclor, was a Nihil attack on the Cyclor Shipyards in 231 BBY. It occurred not long after the Battle of Valo, where the Dowutin Tempest Runner Pan Eyta left his fellow Tempest Runner Lourna Dee for dead when Republic reinforcements arrived. Dee survived and returned to the Nihil base on Grizal, where she witnessed Eyta be poisoned by Marchion Ro, the Eye of the Nihil, for challenging his authority and for his previous failures. Dee seemingly saved Eyta with an injection of cypanid, a substance from Ryloth that did not cure him but instead prolonged his agony, and convinced him to launch a second attack on the Republic.

Eavesdropping on a communication from Senator Tia Toon to the Cyclor Shipyards, Eyta learned that the Jedi Order was withdrawing its forces to Hetzal Prime and Starlight Beacon, and so chose to attack the shipyards—only for him to find an entire battle fleet waiting for his cruiser, the Elegencia, when it arrived. The Republic had recently discovered that the Nihil were tapping into their communications and laid a false trail to ambush the Nihil forces, and Dee had also gone behind Eyta's back and convinced the majority of his Tempest to abandon him as he had done to them on Valo. Upon realizing that he was betrayed, the severely-ill Eyta fled the Elegencia a secret escape pod and left the rest of his forces to be wiped out by the Republic.

Star Wars: The High Republic Character Encyclopedia

entities.name: Battle of Dac City
entities.description:
The Battle of Dac City was a conflict that occurred one year after the rise of the Galactic Empire, when Darth Vader undertook a mission to the planet Mon Cala to determine if a Jedi was hiding there and advising the Mon Calamari king, Lee-Char, in negotiations with the Empire. Moff Wilhuff Tarkin aboard the Sovereign had previously sent down ambassador Telvar to make an trade deal with Lee-Char but the king continued to deny the man and he was forced to take leave for the time being.

At that moment, Vader arrived, along with three Inquisitors and a squad of elite Purge Troopers. They were confronted by the king's chief of security Gial Ackbar who denied the possibility of there being a threat on Mon Cala. However the Lambda-class T-4a shuttle carrying Telvar exploded, killing all on board. This prompted Tarkin to deploy his forces onto Mon Cala. Lee-Char informed the Jedi of this and the Jedi said he could handle the Inquisitors and that he knew the identify of the black armored individual Ackbar had failed to get the name of.

Mon Calamari and Quarren forces under King Lee-Char battled an Imperial battalion consisting of AT-AT walkers, AT-DP walkers, and TIE fighters. Meanwhile, Darth Vader, the Inquisitors Ninth Sister, Tenth Brother, and the Sixth Brother, and Purge Troopers secured the landing platform after killing many Mon Calamari and Quarren.

The Inquisitors headed towards the palace. The Ninth Sister thought that it was folly to believe that the Jedi fugitive would be hiding near the King. Vader responded that King Lee-Char knew how to contact the Jedi fugitive. The Tenth Brother thought that Lee-Char probably fled the moment that the Imperial battalion arrived. However, Vader sensed that the king was still there. Per his previous encounter with the king , Darth Vader reasoned that the king would not abandon his city utill the battle was done.

entities.name: Skirmish on Dac
entities.description:
The Skirmish on Dac took place in 137 ABY, and was a continuation of the genocide ordered by Emperor Darth Krayt to punish the Mon Calamari for the collaboration with the Galactic Alliance Remnant. In the waters of their homeworld Dac, a group of Mon Calamari refugees were ambushed by Krayt's Shark Squadron of subfighters, which deployed from the underwater battle station, Sea Lion. The Sharks began to kill every Mon Cal in sight under the belief that the natives had no defenses; however, they were surprised when a squad of Mon Calamari Rangers, led by a Mon Cal named Tanquar, arrived to assist their kinsmen. Battle immediately ensued, and a squad of Aquatic assault stormtroopers was sent into the depths to deal with the refugees by commander Sturves of the Sea Lion. Before the troopers could even begin their assault on the Mon Cals, they were unexpectedly attacked by Imperial Master Treis Sinde, who defeated them all in short order.

Sinde then infiltrated the Sea Lion and engaged the remaining crewmembers in battle. He managed to cause an explosion in the station which left it critically damaged, and many of the crew dead or wounded. Sinde was then confronted by chief Bor Alsek, with whom Sinde had served many years prior. After a brief exchange, Sinde was forced to kill Alsek in self-defense. The Imperial Master then exited the station, which was taking on massive amounts of water. Defeated, the Sea Lion and its remaining Sharks fled the scene, leaving the Mon Cal Rangers to revel in their victory. However, Master Sinde was less-than pleased with the Rangers' performance, and reminded them what they were truly fighting for—the survival of the Mon Calamari race.

The skirmish on Dac first appeared in the 2009 comic Legacy (2006) 32, which was written by John Ostrander with art by Omar Francia. It was the first issue of the Fight Another Day story arc of Star Wars: Legacy.

entities.name: Battle on Dagu
entities.description:
A battle took place on Dagu during the Clone Wars. It was between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems during which High General Shaak Ti battled a Dark Acolyte named Artel Darc.

Master Shaak Ti was accompanying a large group of clones when they were captured and imprisoned on the swamp world, Dagu. While one of Count Dooku's most cunning Dark Jedi Acolytes, Artel Darc, controlled the Separatist prison, Shaak Ti was able to disguise her identity as a Jedi and laid low amongst her fellow prisoners. In the depths of the prison, Ti began a revolt against the Separatists, aided by clones and the enslaved natives, the Rybet.

entities.name: Slaughter on Daivak
entities.description:
During the High Republic Era, the Drengir slaughtered many residents of the Outer Rim planet Daivak. The sentient carnivorous plants had emerged across the Galactic Frontier several months earlier, prompting an alliance between the Jedi Order and the Hutt Clan to combat them. Jedi Master Avar Kriss and the Hutt warrior Myarga Anjiliac Atirue led forces to Daivak to combat the plant monsters. After Kriss called for reinforcements from the Starlight Beacon, Jedi Knight Keeve Trennis and Master Sskeer were able to enter the Drengir Root Mind and discover the location of the Great Progenitor, the first Drengir, which pained the plant creatures and forced them to retreat. As a result, Kriss next planned an assault on the Drengir rootworld to bring an end to the threat.

entities.name: Destruction of Dalna
entities.description:
The Destruction of Dalna was a volcanic cataclysmic event on the planet Dalna in 230 BBY. It was triggered by the Nihil pirate organization and their scientist Zadina Mkampa using a crystal matrix built into the planet's crust that created groundquakes. Mkampa activated it after Jedi Knight Vernestra Rwoh attacked her as part of her mission to rescue her friend the child scientist Avon Starros. While some feared Dalna would never recover, Honesty Weft had faith that scientists would find a way to stablize the world.

entities.name: Battle of Daluuj
entities.description:
The Battle of Daluuj was a minor skirmish preceding the Evacuation of Yavin in 0 ABY. It occurred between a small Rebel Alliance team and Imperial forces under Commander Orlok.

Following the first Imperial invasion of Mon Calamari, Admiral Gial Ackbar and his loyal Mon Calamari forces fled to meet with the Alliance Fleet. En route, they were ambushed by Imperial warships over Daluuj and forced to evacuate to the planet below in escape pods.

The pods were later rescued by Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, and Leia Organa. Despite being heavily outmanned, Admiral Ackbar came up with a plan to lure the Imperial ground-skimmers over a mud lake with gigantic worms that had previously dragged the Millennium Falcon down to the bottom upon landing, reasoning that the worms would also be attracted to Imperial machinery as well and attack. Not only were all three ground-skimmers dragged to the bottom, but the Falcon was raised and the Rebel group was allowed to leave Daluuj.

entities.description:
The Dandoran Campaign was a military campaign of the Galactic Civil War. Following the Battle for Tatooine, Alliance High Command sought to understand why the Galactic Empire was interested in the planet Dandoran. Colonel Jennica Pierce was tasked with investigated, and as such dispatched her rebel forces to disrupt the Imperial operations. The campaign began with the destruction of multiple Imperial garrisons on the western continent, but eventually the conflict escalated. During the campaign, Imperial forces occasionally attacked rebel forces on Tatooine.

entities.name: Turf war with the Dank Graks
entities.description:
The turf war with the Dank Graks was a criminal conflict that took place during the High Republic Era. It saw the Force-sensitive outcasts of the Dank Graks attempt to wrest control of the planet Takodana from the pirate queen Maz Kanata and rid the world of the influence of the Jedi Order. The war had its origins decades earlier in a dispute between Kanata and Arkik Von, the Geonosian leader of the Graks, that saw the former con the latter out of control of the planet. Inspector Raf Thatchburn of the Galactic Antipiracy Command attempted to settle the conflict and bring both groups to justice, occasionally siding with Kanata's faction when their interests aligned.

entities.name: Battle of Dankayo
entities.description:
During the Galactic Civil War, the Galactic Empire discovered the location of an administrative base for the Alliance to Restore the Republic that was located on the planet Dankayo ordered the Star Destroyers Avenger, Devastator, and Relentless to bombard it. The Rebel Alliance learned of the impending assault and General Carlist Rieekan ordered the evacuation of the base. After this successful evacuation, Imperial Armored Transports Elusive and Timely recovered sensitive intelligence in the the ruins of the base. As the Imperial transports prepared to leave the Dankayo system, they were attacked by the Lambda-class shuttle Bonderium that had been stolen by the rebels. The Elusive escaped into hyperspace before it could be destroyed, dumping its garbage before it did so. Shortly, the Squib Momship Thrifty entered the star system to retrieve the rubbish. An Ugor battle-wagon soon appeared as well and engaged the Squibs over control of the garbage dump.

Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition

entities.name: Battle of Dantooine
entities.description:
The Battle of Dantooine occurred during the Imperial Period when an Imperial strike force attempted to find and kill Falon Grey, who was hiding on the planet. The clone X1 spearheaded the assault, but X2 joined the rebels inside, taking a different path from his brother.

The Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader sent X1, X2, and other troops to Dantooine to root out and destroy a Jedi that the local villagers had been harboring onplanet. While en route to Dantooine, X2 decided that siding with the Galactic Empire was wrong, and opposed the Empire, as well as his clone brother, X1.

X2 then arrived on the planet, defected, and helped the villagers repel the brutal Imperial invasion. During the battle, he encountered the Jedi Falon Grey, a veteran of the Clone Wars. Grey was revealed to be his and X1's genetic father.

With the initial Imperial invasion in full swing, clone stormtroopers were sent to villages known to harbor Rebel activists, and assaulted the locales using AT-RTs.

The Jedi Master Dar'Nala instigated a conspiracy to restart the Great Galactic War between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire after it was ended by the Treaty of Coruscant in 3653 BBY. She arranged for the Republic transport Envoy to attack an Imperial warship, and framed the Empire for the attack, and the conspiracy culminated in a bombing of the Senate Tower that almost restarted war. However, the conspiracy ended with Dar'Nala's death on Dantooine.

In the resulting chaos, Darga fled his palace and left for Bespin and the team succeeded in escaping, along with Denia.

entities.name: Duel in the Dark Temple
entities.description:
After gathering all the artifacts of Tulak Hord, Darth Zash's apprentice brought them before their master, who was preparing her ritual in the Dark Temple on Dromund Kaas. As it became apparent that Zash intended to use the ritual to acquire Kallig's body, a duel between Master and apprentice ensued.

Despite Kallig wearing Zash down, the powerful sorceress pushed her apprentice into submission and initiated the ritual. The timely intervention by Kallig's Dashade servant, Khem Val, interrupted the ritual, with bizarre consequences. The ritual of essence transfer was redirected into the Dashade, and due to the Force resistance found in his species, Khem survived and was forced to share his body with the angry Sith Lord.

With Zash appearing to be dead, Kallig became a Lord and inherited all her assets as well as the resentful relationship with Darth Thanaton, Zash's former superior.

entities.description:
The Darkon system was the host of a battle during 12 ABY's Orinda campaign, which was fought as part of the Galactic Civil War. Shortly after the formation of the Imperial Remnant, Head of State Gilad Pellaeon won a string of victories along the Entralla Route. The New Republic responded by sending the Executor-class Star Dreadnought Lusankya, and the two sides clashed at Darkon. Commanded by General Wedge Antilles and supported by Tycho Celchu's Rogue Squadron, the Lusankya defeated Pellaeon's own Executor-class Star Dreadnought, the Reaper, and Turr Phennir's 181st Imperial Fighter Group. The Imperials retreated, and further showdowns awaited.

entities.description:
The fight for the Darksaber was a duel between Paz Vizsla and Din Djarin that took place on the Mandalorian covert on Glavis Ringworld, in 9 ABY. Vizsla, who was a member of House Vizsla, challenged Djarin for a duel so he could regain the Darksaber, a weapon whose wielder could lead the Mandalorians, back to his Clan. Eventually the Armorer stopped the duel when Djarin held a knife near Vizsla's throat, and asked them if they removed their helmets. When Djarin admitted that he had, the Armorer replied that he was no longer a Mandalorian, and Vizsla told him to leave. Djarin left the covert with the Darksaber.

entities.name: Search for the Darksaber
entities.description:
After Moff Gideon of the Galactic Empire took possession of the Darksaber from Lady Bo-Katan Kryze during the Great Purge of Mandalore, Kryze launched a search for the mythical weapon to reclaim her lost station as the ruler of the planet Mandalore. Her suspicions that Gideon still held the weapon were confirmed during an assault on a Gozanti-class Assault Carrier in 9 ABY. During the second rescue of Grogu, however, Child of the Watch Din Djarin would duel and best Gideon, unknowingly claiming the Darksaber for himself. With the Darksaber out of her grasp, the Mandalorian warriors and fleet she had assembled abandoned her to become mercenaries.

entities.description:
Many years before 2000 BBY, the Sith Lord Darth Phobos was defeated by a joint force of Jedi and Sith.

The Jedi and Sith recognized Phobos and her cult as a threat to both factions, so they reluctantly joined forces against the cult in an attempt to stop the Theelin Sith. The battle ended in a Jedi/Sith victory, with Darth Phobos defeated. Her cult perpetuated for many years, only to become extinct by the time of the Fourth Great Schism in 2000 BBY.

Despite Phobos' supposed death, rumors of her survival continued for centuries, becoming a legend within the Jedi Order.

entities.name: Plot to assassinate Darth Vader
entities.description:
In 3 ABY, Imperial Sub-Administrator Sly Moore plotted with members of her court to assassinate the Sith Lord Darth Vader and have him replaced at the side of Emperor Sheev Palpatine with the rebel pilot Luke Skywalker.

In preparation for her first attempt, Moore, who had recently been demoted from Administrator to Sub-Administrator after she failed to destroy Vader at the request of Palpatine, acquired the specifications of Vader's armor and provided them to the bounty hunter IG-88, who then encountered Vader Zee-Nine City Seven in Hutt Space. IG-88 almost had the Sith Lord decapitate himself, though he was ultimately forced to shoot himself in the head after Vader used the Force to retrieve a controller the droid held that contained the code to Vader's armor and used it to control IG-88. Sometime later, IG-88, who had rebuilt himself, traveled to Coruscant to meet with Moore and her court and inform them that he planned to terminate his contract because he felt Vader could not be defeated.

Vader, however, had followed the bounty hunter, and struck down the droid for a second time. The court made way for a nearby temple, where Moore, in a simialr move to IG-88, used a remote to freeze Vader's armor so her court could kill Vader. The assassins were unsuccessful in their attempts as Vader had the vulnerability fixed. Vader knocked the remote out of her hand as he told her that she could not bend the will of a Sith. Moore responded that she had only wanted to see if Vader was plagued by fear, before adding that whilst he could easily kill her, it would not save him from him being replaced by Skywalker in the favor of Palpatine. Moore then proposed that she bid for the carbonite-frozen body of Han Solo at Crimson Dawn's upcoming auction, so that Vader could use Solo to lure Skywalker in and kill him, which Vader agreed upon, unaware of Moore's true intentions. Moore added that she would be delighted to bring together Vader and Skywalker, as the young rebel was the only one who could kill Vader.

Moore attended the auction, though she was ultimately outbid by and lost to Jabba Desilijic Tiure. Shortly after, Vader arrived and claimed Solo for himself, and eventually Jabba surrendered possession of Solo to Vader and the Empire. Vader then used Solo as bait to lure Skywalker in as planned, threatening to cut Solo in half if Skywalker did not go to him. Skywalker was unable to confront Vader and instead decided to distract Vader in his X-wing long enough for Leia Organa to recover Solo for the Rebel Alliance. Vader took the bait and began to chase him in his TIE Advanced. As the two were locked in pursuit above and in the skies of Jekara, Moore had the Droid Crush Pirates of Bestoon attempt to kill Vader so that Skywalker could escape. The act revealed her true intentions to Ochi, who after dueling with her, apprehended Moore, ending her plot to kill Vader.

entities.description:
This skirmish took place in 43.5 ABY when Monarg attempted steal R2-D2, restraining the droid in his shop, Monarg's Mechanic Works. Allana Solo, whose grandparents, Han and Leia Solo, were attending a conclave on Dathomir, decided to try and rescue R2-D2, but was met with hostilities from Monarg. After a short skirmish with Monarg, Allana fled the man's shop with C-3PO, R2-D2, and her pet nexu, Anji. They went back aboard the Millennium Falcon, and Allana took off in the ship, piloting it away and accidentally causing severe damage to the fence surrounding the spaceport.

entities.name: Second Battle of Dathomir
entities.description:
The Second Battle of Dathomir was a battle fought during the Clone Wars on Dathomir between the combined forces of the Sith and the Confederacy of Independent Systems; and the renegade Sith Lord Maul and Mother Talzin. The battle began after Maul brought the captive Sith Lord Count Dooku to Dathomir, so Talzin could drain the Count's life force and use it to return her previously-destroyed physical form. Darth Sidious was able to trace the location of Dooku, his apprentice, and traveled with General Grievous to Dathomir to rescue Dooku and defeat their enemies.

Sidious and Grievous arrived to confront Maul and Talzin, the latter of whom had used her magick to take control of Dooku's body. This led to a lightsaber duel, in which Sidious quickly gained the upper hand against the Talzin-controlled Dooku. Talzin appeared in the flesh, returned to her physical form, and held off a Force lightning assault from Sidious and, eventually, Dooku. Talzin sacrificed her own life to allow Maul to escape, as Grievous fatally stabbed the Dathomir witch through the chest while Maul fled from Dathomir. The Separatists, meanwhile, also attacked Maul's Black Sun and Pyke Syndicate allies, leading the mercenaries to end their alliance with Maul—effectively destroying the Shadow Collective. Though Maul escaped, Sidious believed his former apprentice's defeat eliminated his future, while securing the future of the Sith.

Sometime between 19 BBY and 5 BBY, when Maul explored planets in search of advantages, one led him to a Sith castle on the planet Damanos. He was approached by a vision of Grievous, who had been slain by their mutual enemy Obi-Wan Kenobi during the Battle of Utapau in 19 BBY. During their conversation, "Grievous" taunted Maul, asking if he remembered their last encounter: when he murdered his beloved mother.
